Source_Text_Yo: A di gàárì sílẹ́ ewúrẹ́ ńyọjú; ẹrù ìran rẹ́ ni?
Target_Text_En: We prepare the saddle, and the goat presents itself; is it a burden for the lineage of goats?
Cultural_Context: Goats that know their place do not offer their backs to be saddled.

Source_Text_Yo: A fi ọ́ jọba ò ńṣàwúre; o fẹ́ẹ́ jẹ Ọlọ́run ni?
Target_Text_En: You have been crowned a king, and yet you make good-luck charms; would you be crowned God?
Cultural_Context: Being crowned a king is about the best fortune a mortal could hope for.

Source_Text_Yo: A fijó gba Awà; a fìjà gba Awà; bí a ò bá jó, bí a ò bá jà, bí a bá ti gba Awà, kò tán bí?
Target_Text_En: By dancing we take possession of Awà; through fighting we take possession of Awà; if we neither dance nor fight but take possession of Awà anyway, is the result not the same?
Cultural_Context: Why make a huge production of a matter that is easily taken care of?

Source_Text_Yo: A gbé gàárì ọmọ ewúrẹ́ ńrojú; kì í ṣe ẹrù àgùntàn.
Target_Text_En: We lift a saddle and the goat scowls; it is no burden for a sheep.
Cultural_Context: The goat has no cause to scowl, because no one will condescend to ride it anyway.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í bá ọba pàlà kí ọkọ́ ọba má ṣàn-ánni lẹ́sẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not share a farm boundary with a king without getting one’s feet gashed by the king’s hoe.
Cultural_Context: One should be cautious in dealing with people in authority.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í bẹ̀rù ikú bẹ̀rù àrùn ká ní kí ọmọ ó kú sinni.
Target_Text_En: One does not so fear death and disease that one asks that one’s child die before one.
Cultural_Context: One should not be more concerned with saving oneself than with saving one’s dependents.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í bínú ààtàn ká dalẹ̀ sígbẹ̀ẹ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not get angry with the rubbish dump and discard one’s rubbish into the bush.
Cultural_Context: One should not act in unreasonable and harmful ways because of anger.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í bínú orí ká fi fìlà dé ìbàdí.
Target_Text_En: One does not get angry with one’s head and therefore use one’s cap to cover one’s buttocks.
Cultural_Context: Do not cut off your nose to spite your face.
Comments: Fix space in the target_text_en "but tucks"

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í bọ òrìṣà lójú ọ̀fọ́n-ọ̀n; bó bá dalẹ́ a máa tú pẹpẹ.
Target_Text_En: One does not sacrifice to a god in the pres ence of a house rat; otherwise, when night falls it invades the rafter shelves.
Cultural_Context: Do not do things that might constitute temptation to others.
Comments: Fix space in the target_text_en "pres ence"

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dàgbà má làáyà; ibi ayé bá báni là ńjẹ ẹ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not become an adult and yet lack courage; one lives life as it finds one.
Cultural_Context: One should do what is fitting for one’s station in life.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dá ọwọ́ lé ohun tí a ò lè gbé.
Target_Text_En: One does not lay hands on a load one can not lift.
Cultural_Context: One should not overreach.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dájọ́ orò ká yẹ̀ ẹ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not set the day for an orò rite and then ignore it.
Cultural_Context: One must not let important matters slide.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dákẹ́ ká ṣìwí; a kì í wò sùn-ùn ká dáràn.
Target_Text_En: One does not keep quiet and yet misspeak; one does not silently contemplate the world and yet get into trouble.
Cultural_Context: A careful and cautious person seldom gets into trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dé Màrọ́kọ́ sin ẹlẹ́jọ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not arrive at Màrọ́kọ́ ahead of the litigant.
Cultural_Context: One should not take charge of other people’s business.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi gbèsè sọ́rùn ṣọ̀ṣọ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not carry debt around one’s neck and live like a dandy.
Cultural_Context: One should discharge one’s obligations before indulging in extravagance.
Comments: Fix space in the cultural_context "dis charge"

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ìka ro etí, ká fi ro imú, ká wá tún fi ta ehín.
Target_Text_En: One does not use one’s finger to clean one’s ear passages, use it to pick one’s nose, and then use it to pick one’s teeth.
Cultural_Context: One should always behave with decorum.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi orí wé oríi Mokúṣiré; bí Mokú kú láàárọ̀ a jí lálẹ́
Target_Text_En: One does not liken one’s fortune to Mokúṣiré’s; if Mokú dies in the morning, he resurrects at night.
Cultural_Context: Never emulate people who know tricks you don’t.
Comments: Removed hyphen in the target_text_en "Mokú-ṣiré’s". it was absent in the original yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi pàtàkì bẹ́ èlùbọ́; ẹní bá níṣu ló ḿbẹ́ ẹ.
Target_Text_En: One does not come by yam flour because of one’s importance; only people who have yams can make yam flour.
Cultural_Context: One cannot eat importance.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fini joyè àwòdì ká má lè gbádìẹ.
Target_Text_En: One cannot be given the title ‘‘eagle’’ and yet be incapable of snatching chickens.
Cultural_Context: One should be able to live up to expectations.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbé sàráà kọjá-a mọ́ṣáláṣí.
Target_Text_En: One does not carry alms beyond the mosque.
Cultural_Context: Excess brings disgrace.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbọ́ ‘‘Lù ú’’ lẹ́nu àgbà.
Target_Text_En: One never hears ‘‘Beat him or her up’’ in the mouth of an elder.
Cultural_Context: Elders resolve disputes; they do not goad disputants on.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbọ́n ju ẹni tí a máa dÍfá fún.
Target_Text_En: One cannot be wiser than the person for whom one will consult the Ifá oracle.
Cultural_Context: It is better to listen to the supplicant rather than put words in his or her mouth.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbọ́n tó Báyìí-ni-ngó-ṣe-ǹkan-àn mi
Target_Text_En: One cannot be as wise as ‘‘Thus-will-I-do my-thing.’’
Cultural_Context: Never impose your preferences on other people in their own affairs.
Comments: in the yoruba text i can see "ngo" instead of "n o". This is an old way of wrting it. should it be retained or corrected?

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbọ́n tó ‘‘Èmi-lóni-í.’’
Target_Text_En: One cannot be as wise as ‘‘I-am-the-owner.’’
Cultural_Context: One should not presume to know as much about a thing as the owner of it.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbọ́n tó ẹni tí ńtannijẹ.
Target_Text_En: One is never as wise as the person deceiving one.
Cultural_Context: The deceiver always has the advantage of the dupe.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í jayé ọba ká ṣu sára.
Target_Text_En: One does not so luxuriate in one’s majesty that one shits on oneself.
Cultural_Context: Lack of moderation and decorum will bring disgrace to even the most elevated person.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í jẹ oyè ẹnu ọ̀nà kalẹ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not bear the title of gatekeeper even until nighttime.
Cultural_Context: As one advances in age, so should one’s responsibilities advance in gravity and importance.
Comments: Added "full stop" to the end of Source_Text_Yo

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í kó èlé ṣẹ̀ṣọ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not live fashionably on borrowed money.
Cultural_Context: Live within your means.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í kórira ọ̀fọ́n-ọ̀n ká finá bọ ahéré.
Target_Text_En: One does not so hate the bush rat that one sets one’s farm hut alight.
Cultural_Context: One should not destroy oneself simply to get at one’s enemy.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í kọ́ àgbàlagbà pé bó bá rún kó rún.
Target_Text_En: One does not teach an elder that, what has been crushed should remain crushed.
Cultural_Context: An elder should know when a matter should end.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í kọ ẹlẹ́ṣin ká tún lọ fẹ́ ẹlẹ́ṣẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not divorce a horse rider and go marry a pedestrian.
Cultural_Context: One should ever progress, never regress.
Comments: Added "full stop" to the end of Source_Text_Yo

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í lé èkúté ilé ẹni ká fọwọ́ ṣẹ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not shoo the mouse in one’s house and break one’s hand.
Cultural_Context: One should be safe from hazards in one’s own home.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mọ́ egbò fúnra ẹni ká sunkún.
Target_Text_En: One does not treat one’s own sore and yet cry from the pain.
Cultural_Context: One should know one’s own pain threshold.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mọ ìyá Òjó ju Òjó lọ.
Target_Text_En: One does not presume to know Òjó’s mother better than Òjó himself does.
Cultural_Context: Never claim to know a thing better than the people closest to it.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mọ ọ̀nà ọgbà ju ọlọ́gbà lọ; ẹní múni wá là ńtẹ̀lé.
Target_Text_En: Do not presume to know the way to or around a garden better than the owner of the garden; always follow the person who brought you.
Cultural_Context: Never presume to have a better knowledge of a matter than has the person most intimately involved.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mọ̀-ọ́ rò bí ẹlẹ́jọ́
Target_Text_En: One never knows how to present it like the owner of the case.
Cultural_Context: No one can know better than the person himself or herself where it hurts most and what relief is needed.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mú oko lọ́nà ká ṣèmẹ́lẹ́; tajá tẹran ní ḿbúni.
Target_Text_En: One does not farm a plot by the road and neglect its care; every dog and goat would ridicule one.
Cultural_Context: Never expose yourself to insult by behaving badly in public view.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ní agbára kékeré ṣe èkejì.
Target_Text_En: One does not offer to second a combatant in spite of one’s negligible strength.
Cultural_Context: Never attempt more than you have the power to accomplish.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ní ọ̀kánjúwà ká mọ̀; ará ilé ẹni ní ńsọ fúnni.
Target_Text_En: One does not know that one has covetousness; it is one’s kin who so inform one.
Cultural_Context: Often, only those close to one can recognize and point out one’s flaws.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í pe ìyàwó kó kan alárẹnà.
Target_Text_En: One does not summon the wife and so involve the go-between.
Cultural_Context: People should mind their own business.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í peni lákọ ẹran ká ṣorí bòró.
Target_Text_En: One does not enjoy the designation ‘‘He Goat’’ and yet sport a smooth [hornless] head.
Cultural_Context: A person should live up to his or her billing.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í pẹ̀lú ọ̀bọ jáko.
Target_Text_En: One does not join a monkey in roaming the bush.
Cultural_Context: Do not join others in their madness.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ṣíwájú ẹlẹ́ẹ̀ẹ́dẹ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not conclude for the person who says, ‘‘Ẹ̀ẹ́dẹ́ . . .’’
Cultural_Context: Never presume to know what someone else intends to say.
Comments: Added "full stop" to the end of Source_Text_Yo

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í yàgò fún ẹlẹ́ṣin àná.
Target_Text_En: One does not get out of the way for a person who rode a horse yesterday.
Cultural_Context: Past glory avails little in the present.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í yàgò fún ‘‘Mo gun ẹṣin rí o!’’
Target_Text_En: One does not get out of the way for ‘‘I used to ride a horse!’’
Cultural_Context: People should not expect to live on past glory.

Source_Text_Yo: A léṣu sílẹ̀ páńdọ̀rọ̀-ọ̀ já lù ú; èlé mbénì?
Target_Text_En: We group yams in lots, and the fruit of the sausage tree drops among them; does it count as complement to a lot, or as gratuity?
Cultural_Context: The fruit might look something like a yam, but it does not belong with yams.

Source_Text_Yo: À ḿbáni mú adìẹ à ńforúnkún bó; bọ́wọ́ bá ba òkókó, a ò ní fún aládìẹ?
Target_Text_En: One helps to catch a chicken and scrapes one’s knees; having laid hands on the chick, will one not hand it over to the owner?
Cultural_Context: One should not be overzealous in helping others, especially when no benefit will accrue to one from the effort.

Source_Text_Yo: À ḿbẹ̀rù alájá, ajá ṣebí òun là ḿbẹ̀rù.
Target_Text_En: One shows deference to the dog’s owner, and the dog thinks the deference is to it.
Cultural_Context: A person who has a powerful patron mistakenly believes that the respect he enjoys from others is due to his or her own qualities, whereas it is reflected from the patron.
Comments: Removes hyphen from cultural context "mis-takenly"

Source_Text_Yo: À ńgé e lọ́wọ́, ó ḿbọ òrùka.
Target_Text_En: His hand is being severed, yet he is slip ping on a ring.
Cultural_Context: The person has been judged undeserving of a hand; it is an affront, there fore, for him or her to adorn the fingers—an indication of heedlessness.
Comments: Removed space from "there fore" in cultural context

Source_Text_Yo: A ní ká wá ẹni tó lẹ́hìn ká fọmọ fún, abuké ní òun rèé; ti gànnàkù ẹ̀hìn-in rẹ̀ là ńwí?
Target_Text_En: One seeks a person with a prominent back as suitor for one’s daughter, and the hump back presents himself; who spoke of protruding back?
Cultural_Context: Since the expression that translates as ‘‘prominent back’’ is an idiom meaning a proud pedigree. the humpback makes a rather embarrassing mistake. Com pare 55.
Comments: Removed space from "there fore" in cultural context

Source_Text_Yo: A ní Tanlúkú ò mọ̀-ọ́ jó, Tàǹlukú wá gbè é lẹ́sẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: People say that Tanlúkú is a poor dancer, and Tanlùkù comes to his aid.
Cultural_Context: A person who is as helpless as the person in trouble should not offer to rescue him/her.

Source_Text_Yo: À ńjá ìbàǹtẹ́ ẹ̀ lẹ́hìn, ó ńjá tará iwájú.
Target_Text_En: His loincloth is being stripped from behind, yet he is stripping those of the people ahead of him.
Cultural_Context: Attacks on him do not stop him from belaboring his enemies.

Source_Text_Yo: À ńsọ̀rọ̀ olè, aboyún ńdáhùn; odiidi èèyàn ló gbé pamọ́.
Target_Text_En: We speak of stealing, and a pregnant woman intervenes; she herself is concealing a whole person.
Cultural_Context: Her condition makes her guilty of concealment.

Source_Text_Yo: À ńsunkún Awúgbó, Awúgbó ò sunkún ara-a ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: We lament Awúgbó’s plight; Awúgbó does not lament his own plight.
Cultural_Context: The person the proverb is aimed at is too daft to realize his or her sorry plight.

Source_Text_Yo: À ńwá ẹni tí a ó fọmọ fún, olòṣì ńyọjú.
Target_Text_En: We seek a person to give a child to [in marriage], and a worthless person presents him self.
Cultural_Context: People should know their place and not overrate themselves. This is a variant of 50.
Comments: Removed space in "mar riage" in Target_Text_En

Source_Text_Yo: À ńwọ́nà àti fi aṣiwèrè sílẹ̀, ó ní bí a bá dé òkè odò ká dúró de òun.
Target_Text_En: People are scheming to shake an imbecile from their company, and he asks that they wait for him on reaching the bank of the river.
Cultural_Context: If people are seeking ways of getting rid of a person, that person should not lay down his conditions for remaining with them.

Source_Text_Yo: A ò lóbìnrin à ńdá oóyọ́ sí; bí a bá dá oóyọ́ sí ewúrẹ́ ni yó jẹ ẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Without having a wife, a person spares oóyọ́ to grow; if it flourishes, it is destined to be food for goats.
Cultural_Context: The vegetable is used in stews, and stews are for wives to cook.
Comments: fix  "oóy 8" to "oóyọ́" in Target_Text_En

Source_Text_Yo: A ò mọ ohun tí Dárò-ó ní kó tó wí pé olè-é kó òun.
Target_Text_En: One does not know what Dárò owned before he claimed to have been robbed.
Cultural_Context: The poor person conveniently blames his poverty on thieves.

Source_Text_Yo: A ò mọ ohun tí eléwé-e gbégbé ńtà kó tó sọ pé ọjà ò tà.
Target_Text_En: One does not know what the seller of gbégbé leaves was selling before she started complaining about the slow market.
Cultural_Context: The seller of goods nobody wants blames her fortune on the slow market.

Source_Text_Yo: A pè ọ́ lọ́mọ erín-màgbọn ò ńyọ̀; ìwọ pàápàá ló mì í?
Target_Text_En: You are described as the child of the elephant that swallows coconuts, and you rejoice; are you the one who swallows coconuts?
Cultural_Context: The description honors the father, not the person being addressed.
Comments: Removed space from "coco nuts" and "ele phant" in Target_Text_En

Source_Text_Yo: A rí èyí rí ni tonílé; a ò rí èyí rí ni tàlejò; bónílé bá ní ká jẹ ẹ́ tán, àlejò a ní ká jẹ ẹ́ kù.
Target_Text_En: ‘‘Its like has been seen before’’ is what the host says; ‘‘No one has ever seen its like before’’ is what the guest says; if the host says that we should empty the plate, the guest should argue for leaving a little.
Cultural_Context: A host might minimize his hospitality, but the guest should praise it; if the host is lavish, the guest should not be greedy.

Source_Text_Yo: Aaka ò gbé ọ̀dàn; igbó ní ńgbé.
Target_Text_En: The hedgehog does not live in the grass land, only in the forest.
Cultural_Context: Certain things are proper; certain things are not.
Comments: fixed "dan" to "odan" in the source yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Àáyá yó níjọ́ kan, ó ní ká ká òun léhín ọ̀kánkán.
Target_Text_En: The colobus monkey ate its fill one day and asked that its front teeth be knocked out.
Cultural_Context: Excessive happiness made the animal careless.
Comments: fixed "nij" to "nijo", and "kankan" to "'okankan"

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbò dúdú kojá odò ó di funfun.
Target_Text_En: The black ram crosses the river and becomes white.
Cultural_Context: Propitious events can drastically change a person’s fortunes for the better.
Comments: too long to complete

Source_Text_Yo: Aáyán fẹ́rẹ́gẹṣin; adìẹ ni ò gbà fún un.
Target_Text_En: The cockroach would ride a horse; it is the chicken that does not allow.
Cultural_Context: A cockroach that stirs in the presence of a chicken is as good as dead.

Source_Text_Yo: Aáyán fẹ́ẹ́jó; adìẹ ni ò jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The cockroach would dance; it is the chicken that does not allow.
Cultural_Context: A cockroach that stirs in the presence of a chicken is as good as dead.

Source_Text_Yo: Aáyán kì í yán ẹsẹ̀ erin; èèyàn kì í yán ẹsẹ̀ irò
Target_Text_En: A cockroach does not trip an elephant; a human being does not trip a chimpanzee.
Cultural_Context: One should not take on adversaries one cannot match.
Comments: Added "ẹ̀" to ese twice

Source_Text_Yo: Àbá ni ikán ńdá; ikán ò lè mu òkúta.
Target_Text_En: The termite is only striving; it can never eat a rock.
Cultural_Context: Though termites may make their tunnels on a rock, the rock will be safe.

Source_Text_Yo: Abinú-fùfù ní ńwá oúnjẹ fún abínú wẹ́rẹ́ wẹ́rẹ́.
Target_Text_En: A volatile-tempered person secures food for a mild-tempered person.
Cultural_Context: Whatever good fortune might have been meant for the volatile person will wind up in the lot of the mild-mannered person.
Comments: fix "ororo" to "were were" in the yoruba proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Àbọ̀ ejò kì í gbé isà.
Target_Text_En: Half a snake does not live in a burrow.
Cultural_Context: One should act according to one’s circumstances.
Comments: fix  "ọ́" to ''Àbọ̀"

Source_Text_Yo: Abùléra ọ̀fọ́n-ọ̀n: ó ní ọjọ́ tí ológbò-ó ti bí òun ò ìtí-ì dá a ní báríkà.
Target_Text_En: Mouse-that-does-not-know-its-place: it says that since the day the cat delivered [a baby], it has not gone to offer congratula tions.
Cultural_Context: Never forget your vulnerabilities and limitations.
Comments: fixed multiple omission of "ọ́" in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Àbúrò kì í pa ẹ̀gbọ́n nítàn.
Target_Text_En: The younger person does not give the older person history lectures.
Cultural_Context: One should not exceed one’s station.

Source_Text_Yo: Àbúrò rẹ ńdáṣọ fún ọ, o ní o ò lo elékuru; ta ní ńlo alákàrà?
Target_Text_En: Your junior brother [or sister] buys clothing for you, and you say you will not wear anything with bean-grits patterns; who has the fright to opt for clothing with a bean-fritter pattern
Cultural_Context: One should act in accordance to one's station in life.
Comments: missing cultural context

Source_Text_Yo: A-dá-má-lè-ṣe àdàbà tí ńdún bẹ̀m̀bẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Start-something-it-cannot-finish dove makes bombastic noises.
Cultural_Context: Bombast often masks fickleness.

Source_Text_Yo: Adẹ́tẹ̀ẹ́ ni òun ò lè fún wàrà, ṣùgbọ́n òún lè yí i dànù.
Target_Text_En: The leper says he may not be able to squeeze out milk, but he can spill it.
Cultural_Context: Even feckless people can cause some damage.
Comments: fixed lots of missing "ẹ́" in t

Source_Text_Yo: Adarí wèrè, ó kán lógbò.
Target_Text_En: The leper sees a mad person and dashes into the bush.
Cultural_Context: A person who should be ostracized ostracizes others.

Source_Text_Yo: Adẹ́tẹ̀ẹ́ méjì, ó fìkan purọ́; ó ní nígbàtí òún lu ọmọ òun lábàrá, ó já à léékánná pàtì.
Target_Text_En: The leper said two things, one of them being a lie; he said after he had struck his child with his palm, he also pinched him severely with his nails.
Cultural_Context: One fools only oneself when one claims to have done the impossible.

Source_Text_Yo: Adìẹ́ tó ṣu tí kò tọ̀, ara-a rẹ̀ ló kù sí.
Target_Text_En: The chicken that shits and does not piss retains the rest in its body.
Cultural_Context: Self-deprivation hurts the person concerned, not anyone else.
Comments: can't make any sense of the Yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: A-dìtan-mọ́ èsúó; ó ní èkùlù ló bí ìyá òun.
Target_Text_En: The red-flanked duiker, desperate to claim relationship, says that its mother was born of a crested duiker.
Cultural_Context: Never make preposterous claims of kinship.

Source_Text_Yo: Adití ò gbọ́, ‘‘Yàgò!’’
Target_Text_En: The deaf do not hear, ‘‘Make way!’’
Cultural_Context: Cautionary words are lost on reckless people.

Source_Text_Yo: À-fà-tiiri ni tìyàwó; bí a bá fà á tí kò tiiri, ó ní ohun tó ńṣe é.
Target_Text_En: Resisting-while-being-pulled is the proper behavior for a bride; if she is pulled and does not resist, something is the matter with her.
Cultural_Context: However eager the bride, she must ap pear coy and shy; one should behave with decorum appropriate to one’s position.

Source_Text_Yo: Àfi ohun tí a kì í tà lọ́jà lẹrú kì í jẹ.
Target_Text_En: The only thing a slave cannot eat is some thing not available in the market.
Cultural_Context: A slave has no choice.

Source_Text_Yo: Afínjú wọ ọjà ó rìn gbẹndẹkẹ; ọ̀bún wọ ọjà ó rìn ṣù ṣù; ọ̀bùn ní ó rù ẹrù àfínjú relé
Target_Text_En: The fashionable person enters the market and walks in a leisurely manner; the filthy person enters the market and walks in a sluggish manner; it is the filthy person that will carry the fashionable person’s load to the house for him or her.
Cultural_Context: Good breeding confers great advantages.

Source_Text_Yo: Ahún ńre àjò, ó gbé ilé-e rẹ̀ dání.
Target_Text_En: Tortoise embarks on a journey and takes his house along.
Cultural_Context: One’s dearest possessions deserve the closest attention.
Comments: makes no sense together

Source_Text_Yo: Afínjú-u póńpólà, ogé kun osùn láìwẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Unusual-fashionable-person, the preener anoints herself with camwood without taking a bath.
Cultural_Context: Cleanliness should be more than a matter of appearance.

Source_Text_Yo: Àfòpiná tó fókúnpáná-a súyà; ẹrán pọ̀ sí i.
Target_Text_En: The moth tries to put out the barbecue fire; the meat becomes more plentiful.
Cultural_Context: A person who foolishly attempts dangerous tasks courts destruction. This is a variant of the following entry.
Comments: fixed space in cultural context and ọ́ in the yoruba proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Àfòpiná tó ní òun ó pa fìtílà, ara ẹ̀ ni yó pa.
Target_Text_En: The moth that attempts to kill [put out] the oil lamp will kill itself.
Cultural_Context: It is unwise to take on an adversary one knows can destroy one.
Comments: added ẹ̀ to the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Afọ́jú tó dijú, tó ní òún sùn, ìgbàtí kò sùn ta ló rí?
Target_Text_En: The blind person who shuts his eyes and says he is asleep, when he was not asleep, whom did he see?
Cultural_Context: The deceiver deceives himself or herself.
Comments: fixed "ọ́" in proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Àgó tó gbó ṣáṣá, bìtí pa á; áḿb sì olóósè a-bara-kù kù .
Target_Text_En: The nimble, sprightly rat fell victim to the trap; how much more the sluggish, sickly
Cultural_Context: Not Provided
Comments: makes no sense

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbẹ̀jẹ ò koro nílé ńlá.
Target_Text_En: Pumpkin is never bitter in a big household.
Cultural_Context: When one is in need, one cannot be too choosy.
Comments: makes no sense

Source_Text_Yo: Àgùnbánirọ̀ ní ńfojúdini.
Target_Text_En: It is the person taller than another who shows no respect for the other.
Cultural_Context: Even in a company, each person should know his or her relative station.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà ajá kì í bàwọ̀jẹ́
Target_Text_En: A grown dog does not deface its skin.
Cultural_Context: Decorum goes with age.
Comments: added ẹ́ and ọ́ to the Yoruba proverb. "ẹ́" was miswritten as "o"

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà ìmàle kì káṣọ kọ́rùn.
Target_Text_En: Muslim elder does not throw a sheet over his shoulder for clothing.
Cultural_Context: One should behave as is proper for one’s position.
Comments: swapped "lagbada" for "korun" in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà kán ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀ lÓgùn; Yemaja ló gbé e lọ.
Target_Text_En: An elderly person tried it [something] in the river Ògùn; the river goddess carried him away.
Cultural_Context: Thoughtless emulation of others could be disastrous.
Comments: Added "ẹ́ẹ̀" to ther yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà kì í ṣerée kí-ló-bá-yìí-wá?
Target_Text_En: An elderly person does not engage in the kind of play that provokes the comment, ‘‘What brought all this about?’’
Cultural_Context: Elders should show decorum.
Comments: Removed "See 126." from cultural context

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà kì í ṣorò bí èwe.
Target_Text_En: An elderly person does not perform ritu als like a youth.
Cultural_Context: The elder’s performance should be commensurate with his station and status.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbá òfìfo ní ńpariwo; àpò tó kún fówó kì í dún.
Target_Text_En: It is an empty barrel that is noisy; a sack full of money makes no sound.
Cultural_Context: Persons of little worth make the most noise.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà tí kò mọ ìwọ̀n ara-a rẹ̀ lodò ńgbé lọ́.
Target_Text_En: It is an elder who does not know his limita tions that is washed away by a river.
Cultural_Context: Elders who cannot swim will be cautious near rivers.
Comments: fixed "ọ́, ẹ̀" in the yoruba proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà tí kò nítìjú, ojú kan ni ìbá ní; ojú kan náà a wà lọ́gangan iwájú-u rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: An elder without self-respect might as well have only one eye, that one eye being in the center of his forehead.
Cultural_Context: Shamelessness does not become an elder.
Comments: fixed "ọ́, ẹ̀" in the yoruba proverb. "ẹ́" was miswritten as "o"

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà tí yó tẹ̀ẹ́, bó fárí tán, a ní ó ku járà ẹnu.
Target_Text_En: An elder courting disgrace, after his head has been shaved, says, ‘‘Now, how about shaving the beard [as a gratuity]?’’
Cultural_Context: One should know how far one may go before one suffers disgrace.
Comments: Removed "o" for "ẹ̀ẹ́" in the yoruba proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà tó bú ọmọdé fi èébú-u rẹ̀ tọrọ.
Target_Text_En: An elder who insults a youth makes a present of his own insult.
Cultural_Context: Only those who show respect for others may expect respect in return. Compare the preceding and following entries.
Comments: Added "ẹ̀" to the yoruba proverb. removed unnecessary space in the cultural context

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà tó fi ara-a rẹ̀ féwe lèwe ḿbú.
Target_Text_En: It is an elder who delivers himself unto youths that the youth will insult.
Cultural_Context: If one wants to be respected, one should respect oneself. Compare the preceding two entries.
Comments: Added "ẹ̀" to the yoruba proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà tó mọ ìtìjú kì í folè ṣeré.
Target_Text_En: An elder who is wary of disgrace will not play at stealing.
Cultural_Context: Anything that smacks of stealing will disgrace an elder.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà-ìyà tí ńmùkọ ọ̀níní: ó ní nítorí omi gbígbóná orí-i rẹ̀ ni.
Target_Text_En: Worthless elderly person who is eating corn gruel worth one-tenth of a penny: he says he only wants the hot water on top of it.
Cultural_Context: One should act according to the demands of one’s status.
Comments: added "ọ́" to the yoruba proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàlagbà akàn tó kó sí garawa; yègèdè, ojú tì í.
Target_Text_En: The elderly crab that enters into a bucket is thoroughly disgraced.
Cultural_Context: One should avoid potentially disgraceful actions.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàlagbà kì í ṣe lágbalàgba.
Target_Text_En: An elder should not behave in an unbecoming manner.
Cultural_Context: One should behave according to one’s status.
Comments: Removed space in target text_en

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàlagbà kì í yọ ayọ̀-ọ kí-ló-báyìí-wá?
Target_Text_En: An elder does not rejoice in a manner that would provoke, ‘‘What brought all this about?’’
Cultural_Context: Moderation and decorum in every thing.
Comments: Added "ọ́" to the yoruba proverb. removed " This is identical in intent with 108." from cultural context

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàlagbà tó ńgun ọ̀pẹ, bó bá já lulẹ̀ ó dọrun.
Target_Text_En: An elder who climbs palm trees: if he crashes from the tree, he will find himself in heaven.
Cultural_Context: An elder should know better than to climb palm trees; one should not court danger. Compare 223; see also 1500.
Comments: Added "ọ" thrice to the yoruba proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàlagbà tó wẹ́wù àṣejù, ẹ̀tẹ́ ni yó fi rí.
Target_Text_En: An elder who wears the garment of im moderation will find disgrace because of it.
Cultural_Context: Immoderation brings disgrace.
Comments: "ẹ̀tẹ́ ni yó" was omitted in the yoruba proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàrá ba ọ̀nà jẹ́, ó rò pé òún tún ọ̀nà ṣe.
Target_Text_En: The rain flood ruins the path believing that it is repairing it.
Cultural_Context: Ignorance or incompetence in tackling a task often leads to unintended results.
Comments: "ọ̀" x2 and "ẹ́" were omitted in the yoruba proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Agbára wo ló wà lọ́wọ́ igbá tó fẹ́ fí gbọ́n omi òkun.
Target_Text_En: What strength does the calabash have at its disposal that makes it attempt to scoop up all the water in the ocean?
Cultural_Context: People should not overreach.
Comments: "ọ̀" x3 was missing. also "ẹ́" was miswritten as "o"

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbéré laáyán gbé tó ní òun ó jòó láàárín adìẹ.
Target_Text_En: The cockroach overreaches itself when it says it will dance in the company of chick ens.
Cultural_Context: The chickens will eagerly peck it to death.
Comments: " Compare 67 and 68." was removed from the cultural context

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbéré lẹyẹ ńgbé; kò lè mu omi inú àgbọn.
Target_Text_En: The bird only attempts the impossible; it cannot drink the milk in a coconut.
Cultural_Context: One should know one’s limits.
Comments: Absent cultural context, target_text_en cut off halfway at "it"

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbéré-e ṣìgìdì tó ní ká gbé òun sójò: bí apá ti ńya nitan ńya; kidiri orí ò lè dá dúró.
Target_Text_En: The overreaching mud idol that asked to be put in the rain: as the arms fell off, so did the thighs; the rounded head could not support itself.
Cultural_Context: One should know one’s limitations.

Source_Text_Yo: Ahọ́n ni ìpínnlẹ̀ ẹnu.
Target_Text_En: The tongue is the border of the mouth.
Cultural_Context: There is a limit to everything.
Comments: "ẹ̀" and "ọ́" were absent in the yoruba proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Àì-kúkú-joyè, ó sàn ju, ‘‘Ẹnuù mi ò ká ìlú’’ lọ.
Target_Text_En: Not-assuming-the-position-of-ruler-at-all is far better than, ‘‘My word is not heeded by the people.’’
Cultural_Context: A person who does not assume a responsibility is better off than a person who takes it on and fails to fulfill it.

Source_Text_Yo: Àì-lápá làdá ò mú; bí a bá lápá, ọmọ owú tó-ó gégi.
Target_Text_En: It is a deficiency of biceps that blunts the machete; if one has strong biceps, one can cut trees with a cudgel.
Cultural_Context: One should not blame one’s deficiencies on one’s tools.

Source_Text_Yo: Àì-lè-jà ni à ńsọ pé, ‘‘Ojúde baba-à mi ò dé ìhín.’’
Target_Text_En: It is inability to fight that prompts one to say, ‘‘My father’s front yard does not extend this far
Cultural_Context: A coward will find any excuse to avoid a just fight.
Comments: Cultural context was excluded

Source_Text_Yo: Àì-mọ̀-kan, àì-mọ̀-kàn ní ḿmú èkúté-ilé pe ológbò níjà.
Target_Text_En: It is severe ignorance that prompts a mouse to challenge a cat to a fight.
Cultural_Context: Never taunt an adversary you cannot handle.
Comments: "ọ̀" was omitted twice in the Yoruba proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Àìsí èèyàn lóko là ḿbá ajá sọ̀rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is the absence of people on the farm that brings one to converse with a dog.
Cultural_Context: But for unfortunate circumstances, one would not deign to associate with certain people.
Comments: "ọ̀" was omitted twice in the Yoruba proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Àìsí-ńlé ẹkùn, ajá ńgbó.
Target_Text_En: The leopard being away from home, the dog barks.
Cultural_Context: When the master is away, the minion will strut.
Comments: Removed "See the following entry, and also 146." from cultural context

Source_Text_Yo: Àìsí-ńlé ológbò, ilé dilé èkúté.
Target_Text_En: The cat being away from home, the house becomes a domain for mice.
Cultural_Context: People will take advantage of any relaxation of supervision.
Comments: Removed "See the previous entry." from cultural context. Also removed a space

Source_Text_Yo: Àìso àbà ló mẹ́yẹ wá jẹ̀gbá; ẹyẹ kì í jẹ̀gbá
Target_Text_En: The failure of the àbà tree to produce fruit brought the bird to eating garden egg; ordinarily, birds would not eat bitter tomato.
Cultural_Context: But for unavoidable misfortune, one would not have been reduced to the demeaning circum stance in which one finds oneself.
Comments: "ẹ̀" was omitted x3 in the yoruba proverb.  Also, i fixed a grammatical error in the target_text. The sentence was lacking "produce" which is an error from the source material

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá kì í gbó níbojì ẹkùn.
Target_Text_En: A dog does not bark in the leopard’s lair.
Cultural_Context: One must defer to one’s superiors.
Comments: Mismatch order. context was in yoruba, proverb and direct translation were in the translation column

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá kì í lọ ságinjù lọ ṣọdẹ ẹkùn
Target_Text_En: A dog does not go into the wild to hunt a leopard.
Cultural_Context: One should not attempt feats one is unqualified to accomplish.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá kì í rorò kó ṣọ́ ojúlé méjì
Target_Text_En: A dog is never so fierce that it can guard two doorways.
Cultural_Context: One cannot serve two masters simultaneously.
Comments: "ọ́" was missing in the yoruba proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá mọ ìgbẹ́; ẹlẹ́dẹ̀-ẹ́ mọ àfọ̀; tòlótòló mọ ẹni tí yó yìnbọn ìdí sí
Target_Text_En: A dog knows excrement; a pig knows a mud pit; a turkey knows to whom to direct its fart.
Cultural_Context: People should know who are their peers and who are not.
Comments: "ò" was omitted, "ẹ́" was omitted thrice and elede was miswritten as eludu

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá rí epo kò lá; ìyá-a rẹ̀ẹ́ àṣe ihá bí?
Target_Text_En: The dog sees palm oil but does not lick it; did its mother excrete palm-nut pericarp?
Cultural_Context: One should not be unreasonably squeamish.
Comments: "a rẹ̀ẹ́" was omitted in the yoruba proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá tó ńlépa ẹkùn, ìyọnu ló ńwá
Target_Text_En: A dog that chases a leopard is seeking trouble.
Cultural_Context: One should not overreach oneself.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá tún padà sí èébì-i rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The dog returns to its vomit.
Cultural_Context: To accept what one has once rejected is to lose face.
Comments: Added "ẹ̀"

Source_Text_Yo: Àjàpá ní kò sí oun tó dà bí oun tí a mọ̀ ọ́ ṣe; ó ní bí òún bá ju ẹyìn sínu, òun a tu èkùrọ́ sílẹ̀
Target_Text_En: Tortoise says there is nothing quite like expertise in one’s calling; it says if it puts a palm fruit into its mouth, it spits out a palm nut.
Cultural_Context: Nothing succeeds like expertise.
Comments: Removed space in "expertise" in the target_text_en, cut off from "tu..." in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Àjàpá ní òun tí ìbá só ló sùn yí, bẹ̀ẹ́ni ẹní bá sùn kì í só.
Target_Text_En: Tortoise argues that it that might have farted but was sound asleep, and, surely, those that sleep do not fart!
Cultural_Context: Some defenses are so transparent as to be frivolous.
Comments: mis-parsed ''ẹ́ẹ́" as "o "

Source_Text_Yo: Àjàpá ńlọ sájò, wọ́n ní ìgbà wo ni yó dèé, ó ní ó dìgbàtí òún bá tẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Tortoise set out on a journey and, asked when it would return, replied that it would be after it had earned disgrace.
Cultural_Context: Certain people will not change course until they are disgraced.
Comments: Omitted "ọ́" in the Yoruba text, replaced "o gba" with "ẹ́"

Source_Text_Yo: Àjátì àwọn ní ńkọ́ òrofó lógbón
Target_Text_En: It is a loosely hung net that teaches the fruit pigeon a lesson.
Cultural_Context: Careless, imprudent persons have their nemesis waiting for them.
Comments: "ọ́" was omitted twice in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: À-jẹ-ì-kúrò ní ńpa ẹmọ́n; à-jẹ-ì-kúrò ní ńpa àfè; à-jẹ-ì-kúrò ní ńpa máláàjú.
Target_Text_En: Feeding-without-leaving kills the Tull berg’s rat; feeding-without-departing kills the spotted grass mouse; feeding-without departing kills the máláàjú rat.
Cultural_Context: Lack of moderation leads to death.
Comments: ẹ & ọ́ were omitted in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: À-jẹ-pọ̀ ni tàdán.
Target_Text_En: Eating-until-vomiting is the trait of the bat. On humility 53
Cultural_Context: This observation on a being with no self restraint could also be a wish that a person not benefit from something he or she has appropriated.
Comments: "ọ̀" was omitted

Source_Text_Yo: À-jẹ-tán, à-jẹ-ì-mọra, ká fi ọwọ́ mẹ́wẹ̀ẹ̀wá jẹun ò yẹ ọmọ èèyàn.
Target_Text_En: Eating-absolutely-everything, eating-with abandon, eating with all ten fingers is un worthy of human beings.
Cultural_Context: People should not be slaves to food.
Comments: ẹ & ọ́ were omitted in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: À-jókòó-àì-dùde, à-sọ̀rọ̀-àì-gbèsì, ká sinni títí ká má padà sílé: àì-sunwọn ní ńgbèhìn-in rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Sitting-without-getting-up, speaking without-waiting-for-responses, walking people on their way and not turning back: unpleasantness is what they breed.
Cultural_Context: Excess and self-forgetfulness in anything bring unpleasant results.
Comments: m was omitted in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Àkàtàmpò ò tó ìjà-á jà; ta ní tó mú igi wá kò ó lójú?
Target_Text_En: The bow cannot fight, but who dares con front it with a stick?
Cultural_Context: A stick is no match for a bow.
Comments: ẹ & ọ́ were omitted in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Àkîijé mú òrìṣà níyì.
Target_Text_En: Refusal-to-acknowledge-salutations en hances the god’s dignity.
Cultural_Context: Distancing oneself from ordinary people lends one prestige.
Comments: "Àkîijé mu" was replaced with "kójọmú"

Source_Text_Yo: Àkísà-á mọ̀ ìwọn ara-a rẹ̀, ó gbé párá jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The rag knows its place; it remains quietly on the rafters.
Cultural_Context: A person of low stand ing should not call attention to himself or herself.
Comments: ẹ, ọ́ & a were omitted in the yoruba text. cutoff from "...weave cloth." till the cultural context, givint not_provided

Source_Text_Yo: Àkókó inú igbó ní àwọn lè gbé odó; òpòlò lódò ní àwọn lè lọ ìlèkè; awúrebé ní àwọn lè hun aṣọ.
Target_Text_En: Woodpeckers in the forest say they can carve mortars; frogs in the stream say they can string beads; and awúrebe say they can weave cloth
Cultural_Context: Misplaced self-confidence leads the creatures into empty boasts.
Comments: ẹ & a were omitted in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Akórira ò ní ǹkan; ọ̀dùn ò sunwò fún ṣòkòtò.
Target_Text_En: An overly squeamish person owns nothing; raffia cloth is no good for trousers.
Cultural_Context: Exces sive squeamishness renders one helpless and destitute.
Comments: "ǹ" & "ọ́" were omitted in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Akú, nkò ní omitooro-o rẹ̀ ẹ́ lá; àìkú, nkò níì pè é rán níṣẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Dead, I will not eat its broth; alive, I will not send it on an errand.
Cultural_Context: One need pay no mind to a person who can in no way affect one’s fortune. Compare 2188.
Comments: o & ẹ́ were missing from the Yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Àkùkọ adìẹ́ fi dídájí ṣàgbà; ó fi ṣísụ-sílẹ̀ ṣèwe.
Target_Text_En: The rooster shows its maturity by its early rising; it shows its lack of maturity by defe cating on the floor.
Cultural_Context: Nobody is free of some blemish.
Comments: "adìfò" instead of "adie fi"

Source_Text_Yo: Aláàńtètè: ó jí ní kùtùkùtù ó ní òun ó dàá yànpòn-yànpòn sílẹ̀
Target_Text_En: The cricket arises in the morning and vows to perform wonders.
Cultural_Context: The puny person’s boasts are always empty.
Comments: ẹ, ọ́ & a were omitted in the yoruba text.

Source_Text_Yo: Aláìnítìjú lọ kú sílé àna-a rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: A shameless person goes to die in his in-laws’ house.
Cultural_Context: One should never demean oneself with unbecoming actions.
Comments: "ẹ̀." was omitted in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Alákòró kì í sá fógun.
Target_Text_En: A wearer of a battle helmet does not flee from war.
Cultural_Context: A warrior does not run from battle.

Source_Text_Yo: Aláǹgbá kì í lérí àti pa ejò.
Target_Text_En: A lizard does not boast that it will kill a snake.
Cultural_Context: People should not propose what they cannot accomplish.
Comments: "ǹ" was missing in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Aláṣejù ajá ní ńlépa ẹkùn.
Target_Text_En: It is an overreaching dog that chases leopards.
Cultural_Context: One should not challenge people one cannot match.
Comments: removed space in "leo pards"

Source_Text_Yo: Aláṣejù, baba ojo.
Target_Text_En: The immoderate person, greatest of cowards.
Cultural_Context: Immoderation is a cloak for cowardice.

Source_Text_Yo: Aláṣejù, pẹ̀rẹ̀ ní ńtẹ́; àṣéjù, baba àṣetẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The immoderate person easily finds disgrace; immoderation is the father of disgrace.
Cultural_Context: Immoderation brings disgrace.
Comments: total mixup in the order

Source_Text_Yo: Aláṣejù tí ńpọkọ ní baba.
Target_Text_En: Overzealous wife calls her husband ‘‘father.’’
Cultural_Context: The wife who calls her husband ‘‘father’’ carries respect beyond reasonable limits; one should not be overzealous observing proprieties.

Source_Text_Yo: Aláṣọ àlà kì í jókòó sísọ̀ elépo
Target_Text_En: A person dressed in white does not sit at the stall of a palm-oil seller.
Cultural_Context: One should not expose oneself to abuse or danger.
Comments: "ọ̀" was missing in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Aláṣọ-kan kì í ná ànárẹ
Target_Text_En: A person who has only one set of clothing does not bargain until he is wet.
Cultural_Context: A person with meager resources should husband them judiciously.
Comments: removed "See also the following entry." from cultural context

Source_Text_Yo: Aláṣọ-kan kì í ṣeré òjò.
Target_Text_En: A person who has only one set of clothing does not play in the rain.
Cultural_Context: A person with meager resources should husband them judiciously.

Source_Text_Yo: Alátiṣe ní ḿmọ àtiṣe ara-a rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The person who must settle his or her affair knows best how to plan to go about doing so.
Cultural_Context: One should not second-guess others or try to make their decisions for them.
Comments: "ẹ̀" was misssing in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Àlejò kì í lọ kó mú onílé dání.
Target_Text_En: The visitor does not take his or her leave and take the host along.
Cultural_Context: Each person must confront his or her destiny alone.

Source_Text_Yo: Àlejò kì í pìtàn ìlú fónílé.
Target_Text_En: The visitor does not recount the history of the town for the host.
Cultural_Context: Never presume to know more than the custodian of knowledge.
Comments: removed space from "know ledge" in cultural knowledge

Source_Text_Yo: Àlémú ò yẹ àgbà; àgbà kì í ṣe ohun àlémú.
Target_Text_En: To be pursued does not become an elder; an elder does not cause himself to be pursued. On humility 55
Cultural_Context: Elders should always behave in ways that would cause them no disgrace.

Source_Text_Yo: Amùrín ò sunwọ̀n, ó yí sáró
Target_Text_En: The lizard is not good-looking to start with, and it slips into indigo dye.
Cultural_Context: A person who has enough flaws should not seek ways to add to them.
Comments: "ọ̀" was missing from the yoruba context

Source_Text_Yo: Ànán-mánàán ẹtu jìnfìn; oní-mónìí ẹtu jìnfìn; ẹran mìíràn ò sí nígbó lẹ́hìn ẹtu?
Target_Text_En: Yesterday the antelope was caught in a pit trap; today the antelope is caught in a pit trap; is there no other animal in the forest besides the antelope?
Cultural_Context: If the same person repeatedly finds himself or herself in difficulties others are able to avoid, one should look to the person’s character for the expla nation.

Source_Text_Yo: Apá èkúté-ilé ò ká awùsá; kìkìi yíyíkiri ló mọ.
Target_Text_En: The mouse cannot get a grip on the awùsá nut; all it can do is roll it around.
Cultural_Context: Some people are beyond any schemes by their enemies.

Source_Text_Yo: Àpárá ńlá, ìjà ní ńdà.
Target_Text_En: Excessive ribbing unfailingly leads to a fight.
Cultural_Context: Jokes should have limits.

Source_Text_Yo: Àpárá ńlá ni iná ńdá; iná ò lè rí omi gbéṣe.
Target_Text_En: The fire is being most overbearing; there is nothing fire can do to water.
Cultural_Context: This entry has the same application as the following one.

Source_Text_Yo: Àpárá ńlá nikán ńdá; ikán ò lè mu òkúta.
Target_Text_En: The termite is being most overbearing; a ter mite cannot eat a rock.
Cultural_Context: Certain people do not know their place; certain people are beyond the reach of their adversaries.

Source_Text_Yo: Àpọ́nle ni ‘‘Iyá-a Káà’’; ìyá kan ò sí níkàn tí kò lórúkọ.
Target_Text_En: Calling a person ‘‘Mother of the Compound’’ is only a mark of respect; there is no mother in the compound who does not have a name.
Cultural_Context: People in a position of re spect should not forget that respect can be withdrawn. See the preceding entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ará okó ní òún gbọ́ fínrín fínrín; ta ló sọ fun bí kò ṣe ará ile?
Target_Text_En: The bush dweller says he heard a rumor; who told him, if it was not a town dweller?
Cultural_Context: People should not presume to instruct those who know better than they.
Comments: "ọ́" was absent in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Ara-àìbalẹ̀, olórí àrùn.
Target_Text_En: Restlessness, father of all diseases.
Cultural_Context: No disease is greater than hyperactivity.

Source_Text_Yo: Àrífín ilé ó jọkà jẹ òròmọ adìẹ.
Target_Text_En: Fear of losing face within one’s home dis suades one from eating day-old chicks.
Cultural_Context: A person who would retain esteem among his or her peers must not act beneath himself or herself.

Source_Text_Yo: À-rí-ì-gbọdọ̀-wí: baálé ilé ṣu sápẹ.
Target_Text_En: Something-seen-but-unmentionable: the man of the house shits in the saucepan.
Cultural_Context: When an illustrious person does the un mentionable, no one dares speak. See the following entry also.

Source_Text_Yo: Àrí-ì-gbọdọ̀-wí, baálé ilé yọkun lémú.
Target_Text_En: Something-seen-but-unmentionable: the man of the house walks around with mucus dripping from his nose.
Cultural_Context: When a venerable person acts like a fool, few dare tell him so.
Comments: "ọ̀" was missing in the yoruba text. "See the preceding entry." was removed from the cultural context

Source_Text_Yo: Arọ̀lẹ̀kẹ̀ ò rọ bàtà; gbẹ̀dó-gbẹ̀dó ò rọ ojúgun.
Target_Text_En: The bead maker cannot fashion a shoe; the mortar carver cannot manufacture a shin bone.
Cultural_Context: People should stick to what they are qualified to do.
Comments: "Aré ló kò" instead of "Arọ̀lẹ̀kẹ̀"

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣá kì í rà kádìẹ gbé kòkòrò dání.
Target_Text_En: When a kite hovers, a chicken does not hang on to an insect.
Cultural_Context: When a great danger threatens, one does not wait for small favors.

Source_Text_Yo: A-ṣe-bọ̀rọ̀kìnní-má-kìíyè-sábíyá, gbogbo abíyá dọ́ṣẹ.
Target_Text_En: He-who-lives-in-style-but-pays-no attention-to-his-armpits: both armpits are taken over with foamy filth.
Cultural_Context: Attention to detail is integral to good character or breeding.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣejù baba àṣetẹ́; ẹ̀tẹ́ ní ńgbèhìn àṣejù; àgbàlagbà tó wẹ̀wù àṣejù ẹ̀tẹ́ ni yó fi rí.
Target_Text_En: Lack of moderation is the father of disgrace; disgrace comes of immoderation; a grown person who clothes himself in immodera tion will find disgrace.
Cultural_Context: Immoderation leads to disgrace.
Comments: removed "This is a more elaborate form of 179." from cultural context and "àsejì;" instead of "àṣetẹ́"

Source_Text_Yo: À-ṣé-kú làgbàlagbà ńsíràn.
Target_Text_En: Denying-until-death is the way an old per son denies a matter.
Cultural_Context: One must never admit to doing something unworthy of one’s position.
Comments: "Àsìkú" instead of"À-ṣé-kú"

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀yọ màrìwò, ó ní òun ó kan ọ̀run; àwọn aṣáájúu rẹ̀-ẹ́ ṣè bẹ́ẹ̀ rí?
Target_Text_En: The newly emerged palm frond says it will touch the sky; did those that came before it do so?
Cultural_Context: Ambition should be tempered with realism.
Comments: "See the following entry" was removed from cultural context, "Àṣ ṣ yọ" innstead of "Àṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀yọ"

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣiwèrè èèyàn ní ńsọ pé irú òun ò sí; irúu rẹ̀-ẹ́ pọ̀ ó ju ẹgbàágbèje lọ.
Target_Text_En: Only an imbecile says there is no one else like himself; the likes of him are many more than several thousands.
Cultural_Context: There is no one the likes of whom the world has never seen.
Comments: "ró" instead of "rẹ̀-ẹ́ pọ̀ ó"

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣọ à-fọ̀-fún ò jẹ́ ká mọ olówó.
Target_Text_En: Clothes washed clean make identifying the rich person impossible.
Cultural_Context: A poor person who looks to his or her appearance appears rich.
Comments: "àfẹ́ fún ò jẹ́" instead of "à-fọ̀-fún ò jẹ́ ká"

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣọ tó kuni kù ní ńjẹ gọgọwú.
Target_Text_En: Whatever clothing one is left with is one’s best.
Cultural_Context: One makes the most of what one has.

Source_Text_Yo: A-ṣúra-mú ò tẹ́ bọ̀rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: A person who is mindful of his or her image is not easily disgraced.
Cultural_Context: People take one as On humility one presents oneself.
Comments: removed "Compare the following entry." from cultural context

Source_Text_Yo: À-tẹ́-ẹ̀-ká ni ìyì ọlọ́lá; sàlúbàtà ni ìyì ọlọ́tọ̀; bá a bá gbérawá lágbeéjù ọba ni wọ́n ńfini íṣe.
Target_Text_En: Spreading-the-mat-without-rolling-it-back up is the mark of the wealthy; sandals are the mark of the illustrious; if one sings one’s praise too loudly, one is liable to be made a king.
Cultural_Context: People take one as one presents oneself.
Comments: ẹ & ọ́ were omitted in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: À-wín-ná-wó ò yẹni; à-gbà-bọ̀-ọ ṣòkòtò ò yẹ ọmọ èèyàn; bí kò fúnni lẹ́sẹ̀ a dọ̀rọ̀gì; ohun ẹni ní nyẹni.
Target_Text_En: Borrowing-money-to-spend does not speak well of one; borrowed trousers do not be come a person: if they are not tight around the legs, they are difficult to remove; it is one’s own things that fit.
Cultural_Context: One should not live beyond one’s means.
Comments: cut off in yoruba text at "biko funni l'... "

Source_Text_Yo: Àwòrò tí a ò bá lù kì í luni
Target_Text_En: A priest you do not hit does not hit you.
Cultural_Context: A person who wants to be respected must respect others.

Source_Text_Yo: A-wọ̀lú-má-tẹ̀ẹ́, ìwọ̀n ara-a rẹ̀ ló mọ̀.
Target_Text_En: One-who-enters-a-town-and-maintains his-or-her-reputation does so because he or she knows his or her place.
Cultural_Context: Self-knowledge guarantees one’s reputation.
Comments: totally different text were extravcted from the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Ayọ̀ àyọ̀jù làkèré fi ńṣẹ́ nítan.
Target_Text_En: It is excessive rejoicing that breaks the frog’s thigh.
Cultural_Context: Immoderate happiness breeds unhappiness.
Comments: "ńṣọràn." instead of "ńṣẹ́ nítan" in yoruba text. "ọ̀" was missing twice and was even replaced with "o"

Source_Text_Yo: Àyọ̀-yó ni bàtá à-jó-fẹ-ehín
Target_Text_En: Dancing to bàtá music and exposing one’s teeth is excessive happiness.
Cultural_Context: Happiness should know moderation.
Comments: "[?]B" was removed from the target_text_en

Source_Text_Yo: Bẹbẹlúbẹ ò ì tíì débẹ̀, ibẹ̀ ló ḿbọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The busybody is not there yet, but he is on his way.
Cultural_Context: There is no keeping a nosy person out of others’ affairs.
Comments: ẹ & ọ́ were replced with e and o by the parser

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá dàgbà à yé ogun-ún jà.
Target_Text_En: When one becomes old, one stops warring.
Cultural_Context: An elder should leave off things that are a mark of youth.
Comments: "Compare 128 and 1500." was removed from cultural context

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá fi inú wénú, iwọ là ńjẹ.
Target_Text_En: If we compare notes with others, we wind up eating bile.
Cultural_Context: Comparing fortunes with others is likely to leave a bitter taste in one’s mouth.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá ḿbá ọmọdé jẹun lóko, gànmù ganmu imú ẹni ní ńwò.
Target_Text_En: If one eats with a youth on the farm, he stares at the protrusion of one’s nose.
Cultural_Context: Too much familiarity with youth breeds con tempt.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá ńgúnyán, kòmẹsẹ́ á yọ.
Target_Text_En: If one prepares pounded yams, the uninvited should depart.
Cultural_Context: The well-bred visitor should make an exit when the hosts turn to intimate affairs.
Comments: "ẹ́" was omiktted once in the yoruba text

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá ti lè ṣe là ńwí; a kì í yan àna ẹni lódì.
Target_Text_En: One admits to one’s limits; one does not cease speaking to one’s relatives-in-law.
Cultural_Context: One should not let an inability to fulfill a formal obligation prevent one from fulfilling essential obligations.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá ti mọ là ńdé; a-láì-léṣin kì í dé wò̟nwò̟n.
Target_Text_En: One arrives according to one’s worth; a horseless person does not arrive with the noise of hoofs and stirrups.
Cultural_Context: One should act according to one’s worth.
Comments: "See also the following entry." was removed from cultural context. ẹ́ and "ọ" was omitted once and twice respectively

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá ti mọ là ńkú; olongo kì í kú tìyàntìyàn.
Target_Text_En: One dies according to one’s weight; the robin does not die and make a resounding noise [on hitting the ground].
Cultural_Context: One acts ac cording to one’s worth.
Comments: "See also the previous entry." was removed rrom cultural context

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá tọ̀ sílé, onípò a mọ ipò.
Target_Text_En: If someone wets the bed, each person should know where he or she slept.
Cultural_Context: In the event of a crime, the guilty should not attempt to shift the blame to others.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá wí pé ó dọwọ́-ọ babaláwo, babaláwo a ló dọwọ́ Ifá; bí a bá ní ó dọwọ́ àgbà ìṣègùn, àgbà ìṣègùn a ló dọwọ́ sanyìn; bí a bá ní ó dọwọ́ ààfáà tó gbójú, a ní ó dọwọ́ Ọlọ́run gá ògo.
Target_Text_En: If one says that a matter now lies in the hands of the Ifá priest, the Ifá priest says it lies in the hands of Ifá; if one says that it[?]lies in the hands of the venerable medicine man, the venerable medicine man says it rests in the hands of the god of herbs; if one says it rests in the hands of the formidable. Muslim priest, he says it is in the hands of God the most glorious.
Cultural_Context: All achievements are creditable to the powers that make them possible, not to the agents.
Comments: "ọ́" was omitted 6 times

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá dáṣọ lé aṣọ, a kì í pe ọ̀kan lákìísà.
Target_Text_En: If one has not acquired one garment after another, one does not call the first one a rag.
Cultural_Context: One may not disdain an old tool until one is able to replace it.
Comments: "ọ̀" was omitted once

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá lè dá Tápà, Tápà kì í dáni.
Target_Text_En: If one cannot throw a Nupe man in a wrestling match, he should not throw one.
Cultural_Context: If one fails, one should at least avoid disgrace.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá lọ sóko irọ̀, a kì í pa á mọ̀ni.
Target_Text_En: If one does not go to the farm of lies, lies are not told against one.
Cultural_Context: If one does not lay oneself open to lies, one is not lied about.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá ṣèké, a kì í fi ẹ̀tẹ́ kú.
Target_Text_En: If one has not been false, one does not die in disgrace.
Cultural_Context: One’s honesty is one’s vindication.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá tí ì jókòó, a kì í nasẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: If one has not yet sat down, one does not stretch one’s legs out.
Cultural_Context: Until one has thor oughly secured one’s position, relaxation is premature.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá tí ì lè kọ́lé àgọ́ là ńpa.
Target_Text_En: If one is yet unable to build a house, one makes a tent.
Cultural_Context: One should neither overreach oneself nor refrain from striving.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá tó baba ọmọ ṣe, a kì í pe alákàrà.
Target_Text_En: If one lacks the wherewithal to act like a father to a child, one does not summon the seller of bean fritters.
Cultural_Context: If one has no means of offering hospitality, one should not invite visitors.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá tó ìyà-á kọ̀ tí à ńkọ̀ ọ́, àjẹkún ìyà là ńjẹ.
Target_Text_En: If one lacks the means to reject suffering and attempts to reject it, one’s suffering simply multiplies.
Cultural_Context: Whoever cannot defend himself or herself must learn forbearance.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a ó ti tó kì í jẹ́ ká hùwà búburú; bí a ó ti mọ kì í jẹ́ ká hùwà rere.
Target_Text_En: The heights one will reach keep one from evil deeds; the ordained limit to one’s greatness keeps one from doing good deeds.
Cultural_Context: A person’s achievements are enhanced or limited by the person’s character.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí àgbà kò bá ṣe ohun ẹ̀rù, ọmọdé kì í sá.
Target_Text_En: If an elder does not do something fearful, the youth do not flee.
Cultural_Context: Youth responds to age according to how age acts.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ajá rójú ẹkùn, a pa rọ́rọ́.
Target_Text_En: When the dog sees the eyes of the leopard, it keeps very still.
Cultural_Context: In the presence of one’s betters, one keeps one’s place.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí àjànàkú ò bá rí ohun gbémì, kì í ṣe inú gbẹndu sọ́dẹ.
Target_Text_En: Unless an elephant had swallowed some thing, it would not turn its bloated stomach to the hunter.
Cultural_Context: Unless a person has some resource to rely on, he or she does not tempt fate.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ayá bá mojú ọkọ, alárìnnà a yẹsẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: When the wife has got to know the husband, the marriage broker makes way.
Cultural_Context: Once one’s task is done, one removes oneself.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ayé bá ńyẹni, ìwà ìbàjẹ́ là ńhù.
Target_Text_En: If life is being good to one, one is likely to act disgracefully.
Cultural_Context: Prosperity breeds temptations to misbehave.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí baálẹ̀-é bá ńtàkìtì, òrógi là ḿbá ẹmẹsẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: If the chief is turning somersaults, the messenger should be found standing erect.
Cultural_Context: The great may indulge themselves, but the lowly must keep their heads.
Comments: "é" was omitted once

Source_Text_Yo: Bí eegbọ́n bá so mọ́ ajá lẹ́nu, akátá là ńní kó já a?
Target_Text_En: If a tick fastens onto a dog’s mouth, does one ask a jackal to dislodge it?
Cultural_Context: A person of great substance is not asked to minister to a person of no substance.
Comments: "ẹ́" was omitted once

Source_Text_Yo: Bí eegbọ́n bá so ayínrín nímú, adìẹ kọ́ ni yó ja.
Target_Text_En: If a tick clings to a fox’s nose, it is not a chicken that will remove it.
Cultural_Context: The prey is not sent to minister to a predator.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí èèyán bá ní kò sí irú òun, àwọn ọlọgbọ́n a máa wòye.
Target_Text_En: If a person says there is no one like him or her, wise people maintain a contemplative silence.
Cultural_Context: A person who thinks he or she is peerless fools no one but himself or herself.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ẹkùn ò bá fẹ, èse là ńpè é.
Target_Text_En: If a leopard does not act mighty, one refers to it as a cat.
Cultural_Context: A person who acts beneath his station loses some respect.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ẹlẹ́bọ ò bá pe ẹni, àṣefín ò yẹni.
Target_Text_En: If the person offering a sacrifice does not invite one, intruding is not proper.
Cultural_Context: It is bad form to intrude into other people’s affairs.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ìlàrí bá fẹ́ẹ́ tẹ́, a ní kí lọba ó ṣe?
Target_Text_En: When a courtier seeks disgrace, he asks, ‘‘What can the king do?’’
Cultural_Context: If one does not show respect for one’s patron, one courts disgrace.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí iná bá dun ọbẹ̀, a dá ọ̀rọ̀ sọ.
Target_Text_En: If the fire gets at the stew, the stew will burst into speech.
Cultural_Context: If the excitement is strong enough, coyness disappears.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí kò sí àkópọ̀, kí lewúrẹ́ wá dé ìsọ̀ adìẹ?
Target_Text_En: Were it not for the fact that they were transported together, what would a goat want in the chicken’s stall? .
Cultural_Context: Necessity brings together people who would otherwise have nothing to do one with another

Source_Text_Yo: Bí kò sí tọ̀bùn èèyàn, ta ni ìbá jí lówùúrọ̀ tí kò bọ́jú ṣáṣá?
Target_Text_En: But for a person of filthy habits, who would wake in the morning and not wash his or her face clean?
Cultural_Context: Antisocial people betray themselves by their habits.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ó di ọdún mẹ́ta tí ẹkùn-ún ti ńṣe òjòjò, olugbe la ó ha rán lọ bẹ̀ ẹ́ wò?
Target_Text_En: If it has been three years since the leopard took ill, is it a monkey that one sends to ask its condition
Cultural_Context: Even though one may be down on one’s luck, there are yet certain propositions one would consider insulting.
Comments: "ẹ́" was missing once

Source_Text_Yo: Bí òfé ti ńfò la ti ḿmọ̀ ọ́ lákọ ẹyẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is by its flight that the parrot proves itself a formidable bird.
Cultural_Context: One shows one’s quality through one’s accomplishments.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ojú bá rí, ẹnu a dákẹ́.
Target_Text_En: When the eyes see, the mouth remains quiet.
Cultural_Context: The mouth does not reveal everything the eyes see.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ojú kò bá rí, ẹnu kì í sọ nǹkan.
Target_Text_En: If the eye does not see, the mouth says nothing.
Cultural_Context: The mouth can tell only what the eye sees.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ojú kò bá ti olè, a ti ará ilé ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: If the thief feels no shame, members of his household should.
Cultural_Context: A person’s disgrace must concern his relatives.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ojú onílé bá mọ tíntín, tí ojú àlejòó tó gbòǹgbò, onílé ní ńṣe ọkọ àlejò.
Target_Text_En: Even though the host’s eyes are tiny, and the guest’s eyes are huge, it is the host who holds sway over the guest.
Cultural_Context: The host is lord over the guest.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí òkú fẹ, bí kò fẹ, ká bi ọmọ olókùú léèrè.
Target_Text_En: Whether the funeral is grand or is not, one should ask the heir of the dead.
Cultural_Context: Only those most intimately concerned know the close truths of an affair and should be asked about them.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí olóde ò kú, òdee rẹ̀ kì í hu gbẹ́gi.
Target_Text_En: If the owner of a yard does not die, his yard is not overgrown with wild grass.
Cultural_Context: If one does not die, one is able to look after one’s affairs.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí olóúnjẹẹ́ bá rojú à fi àìjẹ tẹ́ ẹ.
Target_Text_En: If the owner of the food is reluctant to share, one disgraces him by refusing to eat.
Cultural_Context: The best way to treat a miser is to refuse anything from him.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọdún bá dún, bọnnọnbọnnọn a pàwọ̀ dà
Target_Text_En: When the year is done, the bọnnọnbọnnọn tree changes its color.
Cultural_Context: When the seasons change, one changes one’s habits.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọjàá bá tú tán, a ku olórí-i pàtẹpàtẹ, a ku àgbààgbà sà-ǹkò sà-ǹkò lọ́jà; bÍfá bá pẹ̀dí tán, ìwọ̀-ǹwọ̀ a dìde

Target_Text_En: Ash mixed with water likens itself to indigo dye, but it cannot do what the dye can do; the large red bean likens itself to corn.
Cultural_Context: One should know better than to attempt to overreach one’s capabilities
Comments: "ǹ" was missing in the Yoruba context. cutoff from the target_text till the cultural context

Source_Text_Yo: Láká-ǹláká ò ṣéé fi làjà; ọmọ eégún ò ṣéé gbé ṣeré.
Target_Text_En: A limp is no great asset for a person wish ing to stop a fight; a masquerader’s child is no easy playmate.
Cultural_Context: One should know one’s limits and also what one would be ill advised to attempt.
Comments: "ǹ" was missing in the Yoruba context.

Source_Text_Yo: Lékèélékèé ò yé ẹyin dúdú; funfun ni wọ́n ńyé ẹyin wọn.
Target_Text_En: Cattle egrets never lay black eggs; only white eggs do they lay.
Cultural_Context: Ony certain types of be havior are suitable for people in certain positions.
Comments: "ọ́" was missing once

Source_Text_Yo: Má tẹ̀ẹ́ lọ́wọ́ oníle, má tẹ̀ẹ́ lọ́wọ́ àlejò; lọ́wọ́ ara ẹni la ti ńtẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Save face with members of your household, and save face with complete strangers, such a person loses face with himself or herself.
Cultural_Context: A person too careful about his or her reputation will end up losing regard for himself or herself. Some situations call for doing away with decorum.
Comments: gross misparsing of the yoruba proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Màlúù ò lè lérí níwájú ẹṣin.
Target_Text_En: A cow may not boast in the presence of a horse.
Cultural_Context: One should acknowledge and defer to those better able than oneself.

Source_Text_Yo: Mélòó lÈjìgbò tí ọ̀kan ẹ̀ ńjẹ́ Ayé-gbogbo.
Target_Text_En: How large a community is Ejigbo that one of its settlements is named Ayegbogbo [the whole world]?
Cultural_Context: One should be modest in one’s claims.

Source_Text_Yo: Mo dàgbà mo dàgó, aré ọmọdé ò tán lójúù mi.
Target_Text_En: I have become old and wise, but childish play has not ceased to appeal to me.
Cultural_Context: There is something of the youth that lingers even in age
Comments: cultural context was placed as tartget text en while cultural context itself was empty

Source_Text_Yo: Mo dàgbà tán èwé wù mí.
Target_Text_En: Having grown old, I miss youthfulness.
Cultural_Context: One does not appreciate one’s youth until one has lost it.
Comments: removed trailing text from cultural context

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Mo dára, mo dára,’’ àìdára ní ńpẹ̀kun ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: ‘I am beautiful, I am beautiful’’ has ugliness as its conclusion.
Cultural_Context: Whoever is infatuated with his or her attractiveness will end up being despised by all.
Comments: "ẹ̀" was mising twice

Source_Text_Yo: Mo mọ̀Bàrà mo mọ̀Fún” ti kì í jẹ́ kí àwòko kó ọ̀pẹ́ẹ̀rẹ́ níFá.
Target_Text_En: ‘I am versed in ọ̀bàrà and versed in ọ̀fún,’’ the boast that discourages àwòko from teaching ọ̀pẹ́ẹ̀rẹ́ Ifá verses.
Cultural_Context: Disdain for advice or instruction leaves a person in ignorance
Comments: gross mismatch in the 3 columns

Source_Text_Yo: "Mo mọ̀-ọ́ gùn" lẹṣin ńdà.
Target_Text_En: ‘‘I am an expert horseman’’ is usually the one thrown by a horse.
Cultural_Context: Assuming that one knows it all causes one grief.
Comments: gross mismatch in the 3 columns

Source_Text_Yo: “Mo mọ̀wọ̀n ara-à mi” kì í ṣẹ̀rẹ̀kẹ́ èébú.
Target_Text_En: ‘‘I am jealous of my dignity’’ does not hurl insults at others.
Cultural_Context: A person who wishes to maintain his or her dignity must not by his or her actions invite insults.
Comments: "ẹ́" & "ọ̀" were missing multiple times in the yoruba context

Source_Text_Yo: “Mo yó” ńjẹ́ “mo yó,” “mo kọ̀” ńjẹ́ “mo kọ̀”; jẹun ǹṣó, àgbà ọ̀kánjúwà ni.
Target_Text_En: ‘‘I am full’’ means ‘‘I am full’’; ‘‘I decline’’ means ‘‘I decline’’; eating with abandon, that is the father of all greediness.
Cultural_Context: One should not accept every invitation to the table.
Comments: "ẹ́" & "ọ̀" were missing multiple times in the yoruba context

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Ng óò gba owó-ò mi lára ṣòkòtò yìí’’; ìdí làgbàlagbà ńṣí sílẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: ‘I will get my money’s worth out of these trousers’’; the grown man only winds up exposing his bare buttocks to the world.
Cultural_Context: One should not insist on squeezing every last ounce of use out of a perishable article.

Source_Text_Yo: Nígbàtí à ńto ọkà a ò to ti ẹmọ́ si.
Target_Text_En: When we were stacking the corn, we did not stack some for the brown rat.
Cultural_Context: People should keep their hands off other people’s property unless they have been asked to help themselves.
Comments: cut off halfwAY IN TARGET TEXT EN

Source_Text_Yo: Nígbàtí o mọ̀-ọ́ gùn, ẹṣin e-ẹ́ ṣẹ ṣé orókún?
Target_Text_En: Since you claim to be a seasoned rider, why has your horse gone lame?
Cultural_Context: An expert does not produce flawed goods.

Source_Text_Yo: Nígbàwo làpò ẹkùn-ún di ìkálá fọ́mọdé?
Target_Text_En: Since when did a tiger-hide sack become a thing a child uses to harvest okro?
Cultural_Context: People should not presume to lay claim to things or functions that are far beyond their station.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó bọ́ lọ́wọ́ oṣù ó dàràn-mọ́jú.
Target_Text_En: The moon loses its esteem and shines all night long.
Cultural_Context: A person who overstays his or her welcome ceases to be valued.

Source_Text_Yo: O dájú dánú, o ò mọ ẹ̀sán mẹ́sàn-án.
Target_Text_En: Your eyes flinch not and your mouth is unstoppable, but you do not know nine times nine.
Cultural_Context: Too much mouth often indicates too little substance.
Comments: Many letters were and misparsed in the yoruba text. the target text en was cutoff midway

Source_Text_Yo: Ó di àwùjọ ṣòkòtò kí ládugbó tó mọ ara rẹ̀ Lábèṣè
Target_Text_En: Not until the gathering of trousers will Ládugbo know itself as a miscreant.
Cultural_Context: Some people will not learn the truth about themselves until they are openly disgraced.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó di ọjọ́ alẹ́ kábuké tó mọ̀ pé iké kì í ṣọmọ.
Target_Text_En: Not until the end of days will the humpback realize that a hump is not a child.
Cultural_Context: People seldom learn wisdom until it is too late.
Comments: "ẹ́" & "ọ̀" were missing multiple times in the yoruba context

Source_Text_Yo: Ò ńjàgbọ̀nrín èṣín lọ́bẹ̀, o ní o ti tó tán.
Target_Text_En: You are reduced to eating last year’s antelope in your stew, and yet you claim to have attained the height of good fortune.
Cultural_Context: A hard-up person who claims to be prosperous deceives himself or herself.
Comments: "ẹ́" & "ọ̀" were missing multiple times in the yoruba context

Source_Text_Yo: O ru ládugbó ò ńrera; kí ni ká sọ fẹ́ni tó ru Òrìṣà-a Yemọja.
Target_Text_En: Because you are carrying a huge pot, you strut; what would one say to the person carrying the divinity Yemoja?
Cultural_Context: Never assume to be more important than you are, espe cially when there are really more important people around.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó tọ́ kí eégún léni lóko àgbàdo, èwo ni ti Pákọ̀kọ̀ láàrin ìlú?
Target_Text_En: It might be seemly for a masquerader tochase one off a corn farm, but it is not seemly for Pák k to chase one in the middle of town.
Cultural_Context: A person who is in no position to exercise authority over another should not presume to do so.
Comments: cutoff during the target text en and the cultural context was lost as well

Source_Text_Yo: Ó yẹ ẹni gbogbo kó dínwó aró, kò yẹ atọ̀ọ́lé.
Target_Text_En: It is fitting for everybody to bargain to re duce the cost of dyeing clothes, but not the bed wetter.
Cultural_Context: The person in desperate need of a thing cannot afford to be finicky.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó yẹ ẹni gbogbo kó sọ pé ‘‘Ọlọ́run aṣèkan-má-kù,’’ kò yẹ akúkó.
Target_Text_En: Everyone can justifiably say, ‘‘God, who has left nothing undone,’’ but not a eunuch.
Cultural_Context: People should not act as though they are unaware of their flaws.

Source_Text_Yo: Odò kékeré lalákàn-án ti lè fọ́ epo; bó bá di àgàdàm̀gbá tán, odò a gbé alákàn lọ.
Target_Text_En: It is only in a small stream that the crab can make its oil; when it becomes huge and swift, the river sweeps the crab away.
Cultural_Context: When times are easy, there is little one cannot attempt.

Source_Text_Yo: Ogun tí olójúméjìí rí sá ni olójúkan-án ní òún ńlọ jà.
Target_Text_En: The war that the two-eyed person saw and fled is the same the one-eyed person vows he will join.
Cultural_Context: A comment on overreaching people who attempt feats that have defeated their betters.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun méjì ló yẹ Ẹ̀ṣọ́: Ẹ̀ṣọ́ jà, ó lé ogun; Ẹ̀ṣọ́ jà ó kú sógun.
Target_Text_En: Only two things are proper for a warrior: the warrior goes to war and drives the enemy off; the warrior goes to war and dies in battle.
Cultural_Context: One should not act in a way that is not proper or becoming.
Comments: "Ẹ̀" & "ọ́" were missing from the yoruba proverb

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí à ńtà là ńjẹ; kì í ṣe ọ̀rọ̀ oníkẹrosíìnì.
Target_Text_En: What one sells is what one eats; that does not apply to the kerosene seller.
Cultural_Context: One should be mindful of the peculiarities of one’s situation.
Comments: "ẹ́" & "ọ̀" were missing multiple times in the yoruba context

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí eèrá bá lè gbé ní ńpè ní ìgànnìkó.
Target_Text_En: Whatever the ant is able to carry is what it says is its full measure.
Cultural_Context: One should match one’s desires to what one can afford.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí kò tó okòó kì í jẹ àgbà níyà.
Target_Text_En: A thing that is not worth the least amount of money should not prove a hardship for an elder.
Cultural_Context: One should not be defeated by insignificant problems.
Comments: cutoff from target text en till cultural context

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó yẹni ló yẹni; okùn ọrùn ò yẹ adìẹ.
Target_Text_En: Whatever is becoming for a person is what is becoming; a noose is not becoming for a chicken.
Cultural_Context: One should always confine one’s actions to those that are proper and becoming.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí wẹ̀rẹ́ fi ńṣe ara , ó pọ̀ ju ohun tó fi ńṣe ọmọ ẹlòmíràn lọ.
Target_Text_En: What the imbecile does to himself is far worse than what he does to others.
Cultural_Context: Said when a person intending to injure others in fact does himself or herself greater injury.
Comments: "ẹ́" & "ọ̀" were missing multiple times in the yoruba context

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó ṣeé faga là ńfaga sí; èwo ni, ‘‘Ìwòyí àná mo ti na ànaà mi fága-fàga’’?
Target_Text_En: One boasts only about things proper to boast about; whoever heard of the boast, ‘‘By this time yesterday I had given my parent in-law the beating of his life’’?
Cultural_Context: One should not cheerfully and boastfully embrace disgrace.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú àlejò la ti ńjẹ gbèsè; ẹ̀hìn-in ẹ̀ là ńsan án.
Target_Text_En: It is in a visitor’s presence that one gets into debt; it is in her absence that one repays the debt.
Cultural_Context: One does not estimate how much hospitality is costing until one’s visitor has departed. Compare 3454.
Comments: "ẹ́" was missing multiple times in the yoruba context

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú baba ara: a-wọ́n-bí-ojú; a-ṣòró-dà bí-àgbà.
Target_Text_En: The eye, father of the body: nothing is as valuable as the eye; nothing is as difficult to achieve as the status of elder.
Cultural_Context: What is most precious is most difficult to achieve.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú iná kọ́ lewùrà ńhurun.
Target_Text_En: It is not in the presence of the flame that water yam grows hair.
Cultural_Context: One dares not strut when one’s bane is around.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í pọ́n baálé ilé kó fọwọ́ gbálẹ̀ ilé ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: A head of a household is never so hard up that he sweeps his compound with his bare hands.
Cultural_Context: However desperate one might be, there are certain things one must not stoop to do.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í pọ́n babaláwo kó bèrè ẹbọ àná
Target_Text_En: An Ifá diviner-priest is never so hard up that he asks for yesterday’s sacrifice.
Cultural_Context: One should not permit hardship to lead one to demeaning behavior.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í pọ́n ẹdun kó dẹni ilẹ̀; ìṣẹ́ kì í ṣẹ́ igún kó di ojúgbà adìẹ.
Target_Text_En: The colobus monkey is never so reduced in circumstances that it becomes a land hugging creature; the vulture is never so badly off that it becomes the equal of a chicken.
Cultural_Context: No matter what one’s misfortune, one should maintain one’s dignity.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í pọ́n òkú ọ̀run kó ní kí ará ayé gba òun.
Target_Text_En: A dead person cannot be so desperate as to appeal to a living person for deliverance.
Cultural_Context: However bad one’s circumstances might be, one should use good sense in determining where to turn for help.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í pọ́nni ká fàbúrò ẹni ṣaya.
Target_Text_En: One should not become so desperate that one takes one’s younger sister as wife.
Cultural_Context: Desperation should not preempt propriety.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í pọ́nni ká fàkísà bora.
Target_Text_En: One should never be so benighted that one covers oneself in rags.
Cultural_Context: Despite adverse circumstances, one should strive to maintain one’s dignity.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í pọ́nni ká pọ́n léhín.
Target_Text_En: One’s circumstances do not so deteriorate that one becomes red in teeth.
Cultural_Context: Adverse circumstances should not keep one from attending to essential matters.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú ò ti oníṣègùn, ó ní àna òun ńkú lọ.
Target_Text_En: The medicine man lacks all shame, he announces that his parent-in-law is dying.
Cultural_Context: If one cannot do what is expected, one should at least not broadcast one’s shame.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkété pẹ̀lú ọmọ ẹ̀-ẹ́ di ọgbọọgba sínú ihò; nígbà tí ìyá ńfehín pàkùrọ́, ọmọ náà ńfehín pa pèlú.
Target_Text_En: The giant bush rat and its child become equals in their hole; the mother cracks palm nuts with her teeth, and the child does the same thing.
Cultural_Context: Too much familiarity makes comrades of people who are quite distant from each other in standing.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkùnkùn ò mẹni ọ̀wọ̀; ó dÍfá fún ‘‘Ìwọ́ tá nìyẹn’’?
Target_Text_En: Darkness does not know who deserves deference; it consulted the oracle Ifá for ‘‘ Who might you be?’’
Cultural_Context: People who wander about in darkness cannot expect to be treated with deference

Source_Text_Yo: Olóbìnrin kan kì í pagbo ìja.
Target_Text_En: A person who has only one wife does not form a circle for a fight.
Cultural_Context: A person who does not have enough helping hands should not embark on ventures that are too ambitious.

Source_Text_Yo: Olójúkan kì í tàkìtì òró.
Target_Text_En: A one-eyed person does not attempt standing somersaults.
Cultural_Context: One should limit one’s ambition to one’s capability.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó jẹun jẹjẹ; òtòṣì jẹun tìpà-tìjàn; òtòṣì tí ḿbá ọlọ́rọ̀ rìn, akọ ojú ló ńyá.
Target_Text_En: The rich man eats slowly and at leisure; the poor person eats fast and with anxiety; the poor man who keeps company with a wealthy man is exceeding his station.
Cultural_Context: One should keep to comrades whose station is similar to one’s own.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó ní ḿbá ọlọ́rọ̀-ọ́ rìn; ẹgbẹ́ ní ḿbá ẹgbẹ́ ṣeré.
Target_Text_En: It is a rich person that keeps company with a wealthy person; only people of equal standing play together.
Cultural_Context: One should associate with one’s equals.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó ní ńjẹ iyán ẹgbàá.
Target_Text_En: It is a rich person that eats pounded yams worth 2,000 cowries.
Cultural_Context: One’s level of con sumption reflects the depth of one’s pocket.

Source_Text_Yo: Olóyè kékeré kì í ṣe fáàárí níwájú ọba
Target_Text_En: A minor chief should not act garrulously in the presence of a king.
Cultural_Context: One should know one’s station and act accordingly.

Source_Text_Yo: Òní, ẹtú jìnfìn, ọ̀la, ẹtú jìnfìn; ẹtu nìkan lẹran tó wà nígbó?
Target_Text_En: Today, the antelope falls into the ditch; tomorrow, the antelope falls into the ditch; is the antelope the only animal in the forest?
Cultural_Context: If a person is the only one misfortune always visits, there is probably something the person is doing to invite it.

Source_Text_Yo: Oníbàjẹ́ ò mọra; oníbàjẹ́ ńlọ sóko olè ó mú obìnrin lọ; ọkọ́ kó akọṣu, ìyàwó kó ewùrà.
Target_Text_En: The shameless person does not know what is fitting; the shameless person is off to raid a farm, and he takes his wife along; the husband steals staple yams, and the wife steals water yams.
Cultural_Context: A man who involves his family in his questionable ventures has sunk to the lowest depths.

Source_Text_Yo: Onífunra àlejò tí ńtètè se onílé pẹ̀lẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The excessively attentive visitor extends hospitality greetings to the host.
Cultural_Context: One should not assume other people’s functions.
