Source_Text_Yo: Onígẹ̀gẹ́ filẹ̀kẹ̀ dọ́pọ̀; onílẹ̀kẹ̀ ìbá gbowó, kò rọ́rùn fìlẹ̀kẹ̀ so.
Target_Text_En: The person with a goiter offers a ridiculously low price for beads; were the beads seller to accept her offer, she would have no neck to string the beads around.
Cultural_Context: One can always find a ruse to get one out of embarrassing situations.

Source_Text_Yo: Onílé ńjẹ èso gbìngbindò; àlejò-ó ní kí wọ́n ṣe òun lọ́wọ́ kan ẹ̀wà.
Target_Text_En: The host is eating the fruits of the gbìngbindò tree; the visitor asks to be treated to some black-eyed peas.
Cultural_Context: When one’s benefactor is experiencing hardship, one should be realistic in one’s requests of him.

Source_Text_Yo: OníṢàngó tó jó tí kò tàpá, àbùkù ara ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The Ṣango worshiper who dances and does not kick his legs disgraces himself.
Cultural_Context: A person who skimps on what is expected of him disgraces himself.

Source_Text_Yo: On-íṣẹ́pẹ́-igí bímọ ó sọ ní Ayọ̀-ọ́kúnlé; ayọ̀ wo ló wà lára ìṣẹ́pẹ́-igíi.
Target_Text_En: The seller of twigs for firewood has a child and names him Ayọ̀ọ́kúnle [Joy-fills-this home]; what sort of joy is to be found in firewood twigs?
Cultural_Context: One should not make too much of nothing.

Source_Text_Yo: O ǹpè ní ńfa ọlá; òjípè kì í fa ọlá.
Target_Text_En: It is the person who does the summoning that assumes airs; the person subject to summons does not assume airs.
Cultural_Context: One should know one’s place, especially in the company of more illustrious people.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí-i kí ní ńyá àpọ́n tó ńsúfèé? Nítorí pé yó gùn-ún-yán fúnra ẹ̀ yó níkan jẹ.
Target_Text_En: What is the cause of the bachelor’s elation that makes him whistle? That he will make pounded yams for himself and eat it by himself?
Cultural_Context: A bachelor with no one to share his life and his meals has nothing to be cheerful about.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Òru ò molówó’’ nIfá tí à ńdá fún "Ìwọ ta nìyẹn?"
Target_Text_En: ‘‘ The dark of night knows not who is a wealthy person’’ is the oracle one delivers to ‘‘Who might that be?’’
Cultural_Context: Nighttime wanderers should be prepared for indignities.

Source_Text_Yo: Orogún ìyá ẹ-ẹ́ dáṣọ fún ọ o ní kò balẹ̀; mélòó nìyá ẹ-ẹ́ dá fún ọ tó fi kú?
Target_Text_En: Your mother’s co-wife made a garment for you, and you complain that it is not long enough; how many did your mother make for you before she died?
Cultural_Context: People dependent on charity should be grateful rather than difficult to please

Source_Text_Yo: Òtòlò-ó jẹ, òtòlò-ó mu, òtòlò-ó fẹsẹ̀ wé ẹsẹ̀ erin.
Target_Text_En: The water buck ate, the water buck drank, the water buck compared its limbs to an elephant’s.
Cultural_Context: Satiation leads to excess.

Source_Text_Yo: Oúnjẹ ọmọ kékeré a máa wọ àgbà nínú; òrùka ọmọ kékeré ni kì í wọ ágbá lọ́wọ́
Target_Text_En: A youth’s food can enter the stomach of an elder; it is only a youth’s ring that cannot slip onto an elder’s finger.
Cultural_Context: An elder may take advantage of the youth in certain respects, but in some others an elder must respect his status.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó ẹ̀yẹ ò sú ẹni-í san; tọ̀ràn ni ò súnwọ̀n.
Target_Text_En: People have no difficulty paying the money for glorious events; it is the money for trouble that is unpleasant to pay.
Cultural_Context: The troubles one goes into for honorable purposes are really a pleasure; not so the trouble to extricate oneself from problems.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọbẹ̀ kì í gbé inú àgbà mì.
Target_Text_En: A stew does not slosh around once inside an elder.
Cultural_Context: An elder should know how to keep confidences.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀bún ríkú ọkọ tìrànmọ́; ó ní ọjọ́ tí ọkọ òún ti kú òun ò fi omi kan ara.
Target_Text_En: The filthy person takes advantage of her husband’s death for blame; she says since her husband died, she has not violated her person with water.
Cultural_Context: Shiftless people will latch on to any excuse to shirk duties.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀gà-ǹ-gà lọmọ-ọ̀ mi ńjẹ́, ẹ má pe ọmọ-ọ̀ mi ní Ògò-ǹ-gò mọ́! Èwo lorúkọ rere níbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: My child’s name is Ọ̀gàǹgà; don’t you call mychild Ògòǹgò any more! Which of the two is a good name?
Cultural_Context: A choice between two bad things is no choice at all.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀gẹ̀gẹ́ ò lẹ́ wà; láyán ló fara wéṣu.
Target_Text_En: The poisonous cassava has no attraction; it resembles a yam only in vain.
Cultural_Context: No imitation can be as good as the real thing.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ àgbà-á kú sàn ju ọjọ́ ágbà-á tẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The day an elder dies is far better than the day an elder is disgraced.
Cultural_Context: Death is prefer able to disgrace.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ kan là ńbàjẹ́, ọjọ́ gbogbo lara ntì.
Target_Text_En: Only one day brings disgrace to a person; the shame is felt every day.
Cultural_Context: The thoughtless act of a moment mars one’s reputation for a long time.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ kan ṣoṣo là ńtẹ́; ojoojúmọ́ lojú ńtini.
Target_Text_En: It takes only one day to disgrace oneself; the shame is a daily affair.
Cultural_Context: Fleeting indiscre tions have lasting effects.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ tí alákàn-án ti ńṣepo, kò kún orùbà.
Target_Text_En: In all the days the crab has been making oil, it has not filled a pot.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who have labored long but have nothing to show for all their effort.

Source_Text_Yo: "Ọjọ́ tí mo ti ńbọ̀ ng ò rírú ẹ̀ rí"; olúwa ẹ̀-ẹ́ mọ ìwọ̀n ara ẹ̀ ni.
Target_Text_En: In all the days I have walked this earth, I have never seen the like’’: that person knows his place.
Cultural_Context: If one knows one’s place, one will be spared humiliation.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kánjúwà àgbà ní ńsọ ara ẹ̀ dèwe.
Target_Text_En: It is an avaricious elder that turns himself into a child.
Cultural_Context: An elder who cannot control his appetite asks to be treated like a child.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kánjúwà alágbaà ní ńgarùn wo eégún.
Target_Text_En: It is an insatiable chief of the masqueraders’ cult that stands on tiptoe to watch a performing masquerader.
Cultural_Context: It is unseemly to be too greedy, especially when everything is at one’s disposal anyway.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọkùnrin kì í ké, akọ igi kì í ṣoje.
Target_Text_En: A man does not cry; hardwood does not ooze sap.
Cultural_Context: Fortitude is the mark of a man.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlọgbọ́n kan ò ta kókó omi sáṣọ; ọ̀mọ̀ràn kan ò mọ oye erùpẹ̀ ilẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: No wise man ever ties water in a knot in his cloth; no knowledgeable person can tell the number of grains of sand on the earth.
Cultural_Context: There are certain feats that are beyond even the most accomplished of men.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlọgbọ́n ò tẹ ara ẹ̀ nÍfá; ọ̀mọ̀ràn ò fi ara ẹ̀ joyè; abẹ tó mú ò lè gbẹ́ èkù ara ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The wise person does not consult the Ifá oracle for himself; the knowledgeable person does not install himself as chief; the sharp knife does not carve its own handle.
Cultural_Context: The strongest and wisest of men still would need the service of other people at some time.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ àì-jọbẹ̀-rí tí ńja epo sáyà.
Target_Text_En: A child new to eating stews: he shows himself by dripping palm oil on his chest.
Cultural_Context: Upstarts will betray themselves by their misuse of their new-found fortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ onílẹ̀ á tẹ̀ ẹ́ jẹ́jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The owner of the earth treads gently on it.
Cultural_Context: Responsible people do not always do as they can, but behave as is proper.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀mùtí gbàgbé ìṣẹ́; alákọrí gbàgbé ọ̀la.
Target_Text_En: The drunkard ignores his misery; the ill-fated person forgets tomorrow.
Cultural_Context: Irresponsible people often indulge themselves instead of taking care of their pressing problems.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀nà ọ̀fun ò gba egungun ẹja.
Target_Text_En: The throat cannot accommodate fish bones.
Cultural_Context: Everybody and everything have some limitation.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn ò dun ọmọ ẹṣin; a mú ìyá ẹ̀ so, ó ńjẹ oko kiri.
Target_Text_En: Problems make hardly any impression on the foal of a horse; its mother is tied down, but it grazes nonchalantly about.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who show no concern for the afflictions of those close to them.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rọ̀ bọ̀tí-bọ̀tí ò yẹ àgbàlagbà.
Target_Text_En: Speech like drunken babble does not befit a venerable person.
Cultural_Context: Responsible adults should be very careful about what they say.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rọ̀ ò dùn lẹ́nu ìyá olè.
Target_Text_En: Speech is not pleasant in the mouth of the mother of a thief.
Cultural_Context: There is little a miscreant can say that will impress people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rọ̀ wo ló wà lẹ́nu alaṣọ pípọ́n.
Target_Text_En: What sort of speech can there be in the mouth of the person whose clothes are brown from dirt?
Cultural_Context: People with blemishes should keep a low profile.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ṣọ́ ọlọ́ṣọ̀ọ́ ò yẹni; ṣòkòtò àgbàbọ̀ ò yẹ ọmọ èèyàn.
Target_Text_En: One never looks good in other people’s finery; borrowed trousers do not fit the borrower.
Cultural_Context: One should not be a habitual borrower.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọwọ́ àìdilẹ̀ ní ńyọ koríko lójú àna ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Idle hands are the ones obliged to remove grass specks from their in-law’s eyes.
Cultural_Context: People who are unemployed can expect to be asked to perform all sorts of belittling tasks.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀wón là ńra ògo, ọ̀pọ̀ là ńra ọ̀bùn, iyekíye là ńra imẹ́lẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Honor is always bought dear, filthiness cheap, and idleness at an indifferent price.
Cultural_Context: Nothing is more difficult to come by than honor.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀yájú-u baálé ní ńpàdé ìbòsí lọ́nà.
Target_Text_En: It is a reckless homeowner who is met with alarms when he ventures outside.
Cultural_Context: A patriarch who misbehaves earns disgrace.

Source_Text_Yo: Pamí-nkú obìnrín ṣorí bẹmbẹ sọ́kọ
Target_Text_En: A masochistic woman hardens her head against her husband.
Cultural_Context: Obstinacy only invites harsh punishment.

Source_Text_Yo: Pátápátá alágbẹ̀dẹ ò ju ilé àrọ lọ.
Target_Text_En: The most one can expect of the blacksmith is confined to the smithy.
Cultural_Context: There is a limit to a person’s bragging.

Source_Text_Yo: Pẹ̀lẹ́ larewà ńrìn; jẹ́jẹ́ lomo ọlọ́jà ńyan.
Target_Text_En: Carefully is the manner in which a beautiful person walks; gently is the manner in which a prince steps.
Cultural_Context: Gently and carefully are the best ways to take life.

Source_Text_Yo: Pẹ̀lẹ́-pẹ̀lẹ́ nijó àgbà; ara gbogbo ló di àkísà tán.
Target_Text_En: An elderly person’s manner of dancing must be very gentle, because the whole body has become worn to a rag.
Cultural_Context: Elderly people should not overexert themselves.

Source_Text_Yo: San là ńrìn; ajé ní ḿmúni pá kọ̀rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Straight and upright is the way one would walk; it is money that forces one to sneak about.
Cultural_Context: When one is in debt, one’s freedom of movement is compromised.

Source_Text_Yo: Sesere ńdá gọ́ọ́bú; oníkàmẹ́sàn-án ńgbé ṣíbí.
Target_Text_En: The insignificant thing is attempting an earth-shaking feat; the person with only nine fingers is lifting a spoon.
Cultural_Context: Said of a person overreaching.

Source_Text_Yo: Sún mọ ọ̀hún, sún mọ́ ìhín! Bí a bá kan ògiri ilé-e baba ẹni, ṣe là ńdúró gbọin-gbọin
Target_Text_En: Move away, move over here! When one moves until one is against the walls of one’s father’s house, one stands steadfast.
Cultural_Context: There must be a limit to how much one will back down before enemies.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣàgbà-ṣàgbà ò níí ṣé àgbà títí láí.
Target_Text_En: The elderly person who acts his proper part will always be respected as an elder.
Cultural_Context: If responsible people wish to be retain other people’s respect, they must always act like elders.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣágo ḿbúgò, ó ló ṣẹnu gbáṣọ́rọ́.
Target_Text_En: The demijohn insults the bottle, saying the latter has a long snout.
Cultural_Context: It is silly to pick a blemish one shares as the basis for insulting others; the pot should not call the kettle black.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣàkì ńṣe bí ọ̀rá, egungun ńṣe bí ẹran.
Target_Text_En: The tripe presents itself as fat; the bone presents itself as meat.
Cultural_Context: One should not pretend to be what one is not.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣáláporẹ́ ò mọ ẹgbẹ́ ẹ̀ nínú omi
Target_Text_En: Ṣáláporẹ́ [a tiny fish] does not know its peer inside water.
Cultural_Context: One should know who one’s peers are and not overstep one’s bounds.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣe bóo ti mọ, ẹlẹ́wà-a Ṣàpón.
Target_Text_En: Moderate your preening and strutting, beautiful woman of [the town of] Ṣàpn.
Cultural_Context: Do not overreach, and do not be too full of yourself.

Source_Text_Yo: “Ta ní mbẹ níbẹ̀?” làgbẹ̀ fi ńsán ìbàntẹ́ wọ̀lú.
Target_Text_En: Who is there whose opinion matters?’’ is the attitude that makes the farmer come into town dressed only in a loincloth.
Cultural_Context: People who make a spectacle of themselves show no regard for others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ta ní ńjájá ní mọ́ṣáláṣí?
Target_Text_En: What would a dog be doing in a mosque?
Cultural_Context: Said to tell off people who are not wanted in a company.

Source_Text_Yo: Ta ní ńjẹun tájá ńjùrù.
Target_Text_En: At whose dinner table is the dog wagging its tail?
Cultural_Context: Said to tell off people who make their presence felt when they should rather make themselves scarce.

Source_Text_Yo: Tòlótòló mọ ẹni tó ńyìnbọn ìdí sí.
Target_Text_En: The turkey knows toward whom it farts.
Cultural_Context: People must be careful in choosing the people they presume to approach with familiarity.

Source_Text_Yo: Wèrè èèyàn ní ńwípé irú òun ò sí; irú ẹ̀ẹ́ pọ̀ ó ju ẹgbàágbèje lọ.
Target_Text_En: Only an imbecile asserts that there is none like him or her; his or her like numbersmore than millions.
Cultural_Context: No one is incomparable.

Source_Text_Yo: Tẹ̀tẹ̀ kì í tẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Spinach is never disgraced.
Cultural_Context: May one never knowdisgrace.

Source_Text_Yo: Wón ń pé gbẹ́nàgbẹ́nà ẹyẹ àkókó ńyọjú.
Target_Text_En: The call goes out for a carpenter, and the woodpecker presents itself.
Cultural_Context: One should not think too much of one’s capabilities.

Source_Text_Yo: "Yan àkàrà fún mi wá ká jìjọ jẹ ẹ́": Àìtó èèyàn-án rán níṣẹ́ ní ńjẹ́ bẹ́ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: ‘Go buy bean fritters for me so we can eat them together’’: that spells uncertainty about one’s right to send the person ad dressed on an errand.
Cultural_Context: People in authority should not be tentative in asserting their authority.

Source_Text_Yo: Yíyẹ́ là ńyẹ́ Òkóró sí tí à ńpè é nígi obì; obì tí ì bá so lórí ẹ̀ ní ńya abidún.
Target_Text_En: It is only a mark of respect when one calls Òkóró a kola-nut tree; any kola nut that might grow on his head would turn out to be slimy.
Cultural_Context: People who enjoy the respect of others should not make the mistake of overestimating their importance.

Source_Text_Yo: A fọwọ́ mú ajá o lọ, a ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀ ńfi ìka méjì pè é.
Target_Text_En: We grab a dog with the hands and it escapes; thereafter we beckon it with two fingers.
Cultural_Context: If both hands cannot detain a dog, two fingers from a distance will not bring it back.

Source_Text_Yo: A dẹ́bọ fún igúnnugún, ó ní òun kò rú; a dẹ́bọ fún àkàlà, ó ní òun kò rú; a dẹ́bọ fún ẹyẹlé, ẹyẹlé gbẹ́bọ, ó rúbọ.
Target_Text_En: A sacrifice was prescribed for the vulture, but it refused to sacrifice; a sacrifice was prescribed for the ground hornbill, but it declined to sacrifice; a sacrifice was prescribed for the pigeon, and it gathered the prescribed materials and made the sacrif ice.
Cultural_Context: The vulture and the ground hornbill were unfortunate in comparison with the pigeon, because they did not carry out the prescribed sacrifice

Source_Text_Yo: A fún ọ lọ́ bẹ̀ o tami si; o gbọ́n ju ọlọ́bẹ̀ lọ.
Target_Text_En: You are given some stew and you add water; you must be wiser than the cook.
Cultural_Context: Adding water is a means of stretching stew. A person who thus stretches the stew he or she is given would seem to know better than the person who served it how much would suffice for the meal.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í bọ́ sínú omi tán ká máa sá fún òtútù.
Target_Text_En: One does not enter into the water and then run from the cold.
Cultural_Context: Precautions are useful only before the event.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dá aró nÍṣokùn; àlà là ńlò.
Target_Text_En: One does not engage in a dyeing trade in Ìṣokùn; people there wear only white.
Cultural_Context: Wherever one might be, one should respect the manners and habits of the place.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dá ẹrù ikùn pa orí.
Target_Text_En: One does not weigh the head down with a load that belongs to the belly.
Cultural_Context: Responsibilities should rest where they belong.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í du orí olórí kí àwòdì gbé tẹni lọ.
Target_Text_En: One does not fight to save another person’s head only to have a kite carry one’s own away.
Cultural_Context: One should not save others at the cost of one’s own safety.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í duni lóyè ká fọ̀nà ilé-e Baálẹ̀ hanni.
Target_Text_En: One does not compete with another for a chieftaincy title and also show the competitor the way to the king’s house.
Cultural_Context: A person should be treated either as an adversary or as an ally, not as both.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fá orí lẹ́hìn olórí.
Target_Text_En: One does not shave a head in the absence of the owner.
Cultural_Context: One does not settle a matter in the absence of the person most concerned.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi àgbà sílẹ̀ sin àgbà.
Target_Text_En: One does not leave one elder sitting to walk another elder part of his way.
Cultural_Context: One should not slight one person in order to humor another.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi àì-mọ̀-wẹ̀ mòòkùn.
Target_Text_En: One does not dive under water without knowing how to swim.
Cultural_Context: Never engage in a project for which you lack the requisite skills.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ara ẹni ṣe oògùn àlọ̀kúnná.
Target_Text_En: One does not use oneself as an ingredient in a medicine requiring that the ingredients be pulverized.
Cultural_Context: Self-preservation is a compulsory project for all.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi aṣọ ṣèdìdí yọwó.
Target_Text_En: One does not leave cloth in a bundle while bargaining over it.
Cultural_Context: It is wise to know what one is negotiating to buy.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ejò sórí òrùlé sùn.
Target_Text_En: One does not go to bed while a snake is on the roof.
Cultural_Context: Never let down your guard while danger still lurks.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ẹ̀jẹ̀ ìbálé pa tírà; alákoto ò bí abo ọmọ.
Target_Text_En: One does not smear blood [from a woman’s deflowering] on a Muslim charm; a devirgined woman does not give birth to a "female" child.
Cultural_Context: One must not do the forbidden if one does not expect trouble

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ẹran ikún gbọn ti àgbọ̀nrín nù.
Target_Text_En: One does not brush off antelope meat with squirrel meat.
Cultural_Context: Never prefer something of little value to something of great value.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ẹ̀tẹ́ sílẹ̀ pa làpálàpá.
Target_Text_En: One does not ignore leprosy to treat a rash.
Cultural_Context: More serious problems deserve more im mediate attention.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi idà pa ìgbín.
Target_Text_En: One does not use a sword to kill a snail.
Cultural_Context: Remedies should be commensurate with the problem.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ìgbín sọ́kò sórìṣà.
Target_Text_En: One does not throw a snail at a god.
Cultural_Context: vice to the worthy should be performed with decorum, not with insult.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi iná sórí òrùlé sùn.
Target_Text_En: One does not go to bed while there is a fire on one’s roof.
Cultural_Context: Better take care of problems before relaxing.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ìtìjú kárùn.
Target_Text_En: One does not because of shyness expose oneself to a disease.
Cultural_Context: Never be too shy to speak out on your own behalf.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ìyá ẹní dákú ṣeré.
Target_Text_En: One does not as a joke say one’s mother has collapsed.
Cultural_Context: Never trifle with serious matters.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ogun dán ẹ̀ṣọ́ wò.
Target_Text_En: One does not tease a warrior by saying there is a war [or an invasion].
Cultural_Context: Do not play with a loaded and primed gun.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ohun sọ́wọ́ búra.
Target_Text_En: One does not hide something in one’s hand and yet swear [that one knows nothing about it].
Cultural_Context: It is foolish to tempt fate; the dis honest person exposes himself or herself to the possibility of discovery.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ohun-olóhun tọrẹ bí kò ṣe tẹni.
Target_Text_En: One does not make a gift of property that is not one’s own.
Cultural_Context: Never be too free with other people’s property.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi oko sin fún ìwọ̀fà.
Target_Text_En: One does not hide the farm from the pawned worker.
Cultural_Context: It does not make sense to prevent a servant one has hired from doing what one hired him to do.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi olórí ogun ṣe ìfagun.
Target_Text_En: One does not position the commander of the army at the rear of the column.
Cultural_Context: The best foot is the one to put forward.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi oníjà sílẹ̀ ká gbájúmọ́ alápẹpẹ.
Target_Text_En: One does not leave the person one has a quarrel with and face his lackey.
Cultural_Context: Focus rather on your main problem, not a side show.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi owó du oyè-e alágbára.
Target_Text_En: One does not rely on money to contest a chieftaincy reserved for the strong.
Cultural_Context: Money won’t buy everything.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ọlá jẹ iyọ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not consume salt according to one’s greatness.
Cultural_Context: Too much of a good thing can be dangerous.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ọ̀nà ikùn han ọ̀fun.
Target_Text_En: One does not show the throat the way to the stomach.
Cultural_Context: Do not presume to know better than the expert.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi nà odò han ikún.
Target_Text_En: One does not show the squirrel the way to the river.
Cultural_Context: Telling someone what he or she already knows is silly.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ọ̀rọ̀ sílẹ̀ gbọ̀rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not ignore one matter to attend to another matter.
Cultural_Context: Every obligation deserves attention.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbá ẹni tó yọ̀bẹ mú.
Target_Text_En: One does not grab hold of a person who has pulled a knife.
Cultural_Context: Prudence and caution are imperative in dealing with dangerous people.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbé àwòrán gàgàrà ká má fi ọwọ́ ẹ ti nǹkan.
Target_Text_En: One does not carve a tall statue without resting its hand on something.
Cultural_Context: Everybody needs some support.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbé ẹran erin lérí ká máa fẹsẹ̀ wa ihò ìrẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not carry elephant meat on one’s head and dig cricket holes with one’s big toe.
Cultural_Context: If one is blessed with plenty, one should not keep chasing after trifles.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbé odò jiyàn-an ọṣẹ́ hó tàbí kò hó.
Target_Text_En: One does not sit by a river and argue whether the soap will foam or will not foam.
Cultural_Context: Where the claim can be put to the test, verbal argument is foolish.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbé ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ sọnù ká tún bèrè-e jàǹto.
Target_Text_En: One does not throw a toad away and inquire after its young.
Cultural_Context: Commiseration after injury is hypocritical.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbójú-u fífò lé adìẹ àgàgà; a kì í gbójú-u yíyan lé alágẹmọ.
Target_Text_En: One should not expect flight from the flight-less chicken; one should not expect striding from a chameleon.
Cultural_Context: To expect the impossible is to delude oneself.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbọ́ ẹjọ́ ẹnìkan dájọ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not deliver a verdict after hearing only one side.
Cultural_Context: Justice requires impartiality and a full hearing.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ka igún mọ́ ẹran jíjẹ.
Target_Text_En: One does not list vultures among edible meats.
Cultural_Context: Certain things one does not stoop to do.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ka ilé òrìṣà kún ìlú.
Target_Text_En: One does not count a god’s grove as part of the town.
Cultural_Context: Do not list questionable items as part of your wealth.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ka oyún inú kún ọmọ ilẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not count a fetus among living children.
Cultural_Context: Never count your chickens before they are hatched.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ka ọmọ fún òbí.
Target_Text_En: One does not enumerate children for the parents.
Cultural_Context: Do not presume to know better than those most intimately involved.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í kọ ọmọ-ọ́ bí ká sọ ọ́ ní Èwolódé?
Target_Text_En: One does not so resent having a child that one names it What-is-this-that-has happened?
Cultural_Context: Childbirth is always a happy event.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í léku méjì ká má pòfo.
Target_Text_En: One does not chase two rats and avoid coming up with nothing.
Cultural_Context: Never try to go in two directions at once.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mú ọmọ òṣì lọ sí Ìlọ́rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not take a child destined for poverty to Ìlọ́rọ̀.
Cultural_Context: A person cannot transcend his or her destiny.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í lọ́mọ léhin kọ oúnjẹ.
Target_Text_En: One does not have children at one’s rear and yet refuse food.
Cultural_Context: No amount of anger or distress should keep one from looking after one’s dependents.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mọ ọkọ ọmọ ká tún mọ àlè-e rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not acknowledge the husband for one’s child and also acknowledge her illicit lover.
Cultural_Context: Never betray trust or connive at betraying it.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mú ìbọn tetere.
Target_Text_En: One does not hold a gun carelessly.
Cultural_Context: Always be careful in handling dangerous matters.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mú oko mú ẹjọ́ kí ọ̀kan má yẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not opt to work on the farm and also opt to go argue one’s case and avoid neglecting one or the other.
Cultural_Context: One cannot do two mind-absorbing tasks at once.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mú ọmọ oǹdọ́pọ̀ dè.
Target_Text_En: One does not chain the child of a person who offers too low a price for one’s wares.
Cultural_Context: It is not a crime to make an offer that might be unacceptable.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í múlé móko kọ̀kan má yẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not devote oneself to the home and devote oneself to the farm and not wind up neglecting one of them.
Cultural_Context: One cannot go in two opposite directions at once.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ní ẹgbàá nílé wá ẹgbàá ròde.
Target_Text_En: One does not have 1,000 cowries (or six pence) at home and go chasing abroad for 1,000 cowries.
Cultural_Context: Only the promise of a greater fortune should tempt one to neglect what one already has.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í pa asínwín ilé, nítorí ọjọ́ tí tòde yó bàá wá sílé.
Target_Text_En: One does not kill the imbecile within one’s home, because of the day when the one from outside might visit.
Cultural_Context: One should cultivate one’s own madness; one might need it to combat others’ madness.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í pa igún, a kì í jẹ igún, a kì í fi igún bọrí.
Target_Text_En: One does not kill the vulture; one does not eat the vulture; one does not offer the vulture as a sacrifice to one’s head.
Cultural_Context: Certain behaviors are beyond the pale.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í pé kí òṣìkà ṣe é ká wò ó.
Target_Text_En: One does not dare a wicked person to do his worst.
Cultural_Context: Never tempt evil people to do their evil.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í peni lólè ká máa gbé ọmọ ẹran jó.
Target_Text_En: One does not suffer the reputation of being a thief and yet go seeking to dance with kids [baby goats].
Cultural_Context: It is foolish to behave in ways that will confirm people’s evil opinion of one.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í rán ọ̀lẹ wo ojú ọjọ́ àárọ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not send a shirker to go see what the morning looks like outside.
Cultural_Context: Never rely on the advice of people who have a vested interest in the matter being considered.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í re nísun lọ dà síbú.
Target_Text_En: One does not collect water from a spring to dump in the deep.
Cultural_Context: Do not rob the poor to further enrich the wealthy.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í rí adìẹ nílẹ̀ ká da àgbàdo fún ajá.
Target_Text_En: One does not see chickens about and throw one’s corn to the dog.
Cultural_Context: Always direct help where it will be appreciated and where it will do some good.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í rí àjẹkù orò.
Target_Text_En: No one ever sees the leavings of the god Orò.
Cultural_Context: What must be consumed must be completely consumed.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í rí bàtá nílẹ̀ ká fẹnu sín in jẹ.
Target_Text_En: One does not see a bàtá drum on the ground and use one’s mouth to mimic its sound.
Cultural_Context: Too much talk about a problem is useless when a practical solution has presented itself. One should not make a person’s case for him or her when that person is present

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í rí ewé nílẹ̀ ká fọwọ́ fámí.
Target_Text_En: One does not see leaves lying about and scoop up feces with one’s bare hand.
Cultural_Context: Take advantage of whatever aids are available to you.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í rí ẹni ranni lérù ká yọkẹ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not find helpers willing to help with one’s load and yet sprout a hump on one’s back [from carrying too heavy a load].
Cultural_Context: Always avail yourself of offered help.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í rí ojú ẹkùn ká tọ́ ẹkùn.
Target_Text_En: One does not see the look on a leopard’s face and then taunt the leopard.
Cultural_Context: It is foolish to invite disaster needlessly on one’s own head.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í sá fún àjíà ká dìgbò lu eégún.
Target_Text_En: One does not run from the herald of the masquerader and collide with the masquerader himself.
Cultural_Context: Never court a greater disaster in an attempt to avert a minor one.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í sin àlè kọjá odò; ohun tí ńṣe ọṣẹ́ ò tó ǹkan.
Target_Text_En: One does not walk one’s secret lover across a river; the causes of huge disasters are usually insignificant in themselves.
Cultural_Context: If one is engaged in a dangerous venture, one should not also cast discretion to the wind.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í sọ pé abẹ Ọ̀yọ́ mú; nígbà náà ni yó sọ pé bẹ́ẹ̀ ni òun ò n ò tíì pọn.
Target_Text_En: One does not tell an Ọ̀yọ́ person that his knife is sharp, for only then will he say he has not even honed it yet.
Cultural_Context: Offer no braggart any opportunity to resume his bragging.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í sọrọ ìkọ̀kọ̀ lójú olófòófó.
Target_Text_En: One does not discuss secret matters in the presence of a tattler.
Cultural_Context: Be careful with your secrets.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ṣe fáàárí ẹ́ṣẹ̀ dídì sọ́mọ adétẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not flaunt one’s ability to make a fist in the face of a leper’s child.
Cultural_Context: Never make fun of people because of their affliction.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ṣe fáàárí itọ́ dídà sọ́mọ a-kú-wárápá.
Target_Text_En: One does not drool in jest in the presence of the child of an epileptic.
Cultural_Context: Never make fun of afflicted people by mimicking their affliction.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ṣoore tán ká lóṣòó tì í.
Target_Text_En: One does not do a favor and then camp by it
Cultural_Context: Having done some good, do not hang around to compel gratitude.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í sùn jẹ́rìí ìdí.
Target_Text_En: One cannot be asleep and also be able to vouch for one’s anus.
Cultural_Context: Assert only those things you know for certain.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ṣòwò méjì kẹ́ran má jẹ ọ̀kan.
Target_Text_En: One does not engage in two trades without having one consumed by goats.
Cultural_Context: One cannot effectively manage two enterprises at once.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ti ojú on-íka-mẹ́sàn-án kà á.
Target_Text_En: One does not count the fingers of a person who has only nine in his or her presence.
Cultural_Context: One must be discreet in speaking about other people’s flaws and deformities.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í wá aláṣọ-àlà nísọ̀ elépo.
Target_Text_En: One should not look for a white-clad person in the stall of palm-oil sellers.
Cultural_Context: One should know the likely places to look for whatever one seeks.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í wà nínú ìṣẹ́ ká perin tọrẹ.
Target_Text_En: One does not wallow in poverty and yet kill an elephant for public distribution.
Cultural_Context: Always live according to your circumstances.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í wíjọ́ ọ wíwò ká jàre.
Target_Text_En: One does not complain about being looked at and be vindicated.
Cultural_Context: One should not complain that other people are doing what one is also doing.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í tijú bá baálé ilé jẹ akátá; bó bá mú, ìwọ náà a mú tìẹ.
Target_Text_En: One should not be too embarrassed to eat a jackal with one’s host; as he helps himself, one also helps oneself.
Cultural_Context: Never be too bashful to adopt the ways of the people among whom you find yourself.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í yin ọmọdé lójú ara ẹ̀; ìfàsẹhìn ní ńkángún ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not praise a child in his presence; only backsliding results.
Cultural_Context: Children should not be praised too highly; they should always be made aware that they can be even better.

Source_Text_Yo: A lé tẹ̀m̀bẹ̀lẹ̀kun jìnnà bí ẹnipé kó bọ́jù sígbó.
Target_Text_En: One chases conspiracy away, as though one would have it disappear into the bush.
Cultural_Context: No one should want anything to do with conspiracy.

Source_Text_Yo: À ńgba òròmọ adìẹ lọ́wọ́ ikú, ó ní wọn ó jẹkí òun jẹ̀ láàtàn.
Target_Text_En: One struggles to save the chick from certain death, and it complains that one is preventing it from foraging at the dump.
Cultural_Context: Chicks foraging at the dump are easy prey for kites.

Source_Text_Yo: A ní kọ́mọ má kùú, o ní kò jọ bàbá kò jọ ìyá.
Target_Text_En: We strive to keep a child from dying, and you say he resembles neither the father nor the mother.
Cultural_Context: The person addressed has his or her priorities reversed.

Source_Text_Yo: A ní kí olókùnrùn ṣe tó, ó ní òun ò lè ṣe tó, tò, tó.
Target_Text_En: The invalid is asked to say, ‘‘Tó,’’ and he complains that he cannot keep saying, ‘‘Tó, tò, tó.’’
Cultural_Context: He has expended more effort in his refusal than he would have in complying.

Source_Text_Yo: "À ńjùwọ́n" ò ṣéé wí lẹ́jọ́; ìjà ìlara ò tán bọ̀rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: "We are driven by envy of them" is a bad case to make; a quarrel spawned by jealousy is not easy to settle.
Cultural_Context: Quarrels whose causes cannot be openly admitted will not readily end.

Source_Text_Yo: À ńkì í, à ńsà á, ó ní òun ò mọ ẹni tó kú; a ní, ‘‘Alákàá ẹgbàá, a-biṣu-wọ̀rọ̀-wọ̀rọ̀-lóko, a-bàgbàdo-tàkì-tàkì-lẹ́gàn”; ó ní, “Ọlọ́dẹ ló kú, tàbí ìnájà?”
Target_Text_En: We recite someone’s praise names, we intone his attributes, and a person says he does not know who died; we say, ‘‘He of the two hundred granaries, he whose yams are plentiful on the farm, he whose corn is abundant in the fields,’’ and the person asks, ‘‘Is the dead person a hunter or a trader?’’
Cultural_Context: A person for whom everything must be spelled out, a person who cannot make deductions from the most obvious hints, is daft indeed.

Source_Text_Yo: À ńkì í, à ńsà á, ó ní òun ò mọ ẹni tó kú; ó ńgb, “Ikú mẹ́rù, Ọ̀pàgá, a-biṣu-ú-ta-bí-òdòdó, a-lábà-ọkà, a-roko-fẹ́yẹ-jẹ”; ó ní, “Àgbẹ̀ ló kú, tàbí ọ̀nájà?”
Target_Text_En: We recite someone’s praise names, we intone his attributes, and a person says he does not know who died; he hears, ‘‘Death takes a renowned man, a titled man, whose yams spread like petals, who possesses barns of corn, whose fields are a bounty for birds,’’ and he asks, ‘‘Is the dead man a farmer or a trader?’’
Cultural_Context: A person for whom everything must be spelled out, a person who cannot make deductions from the most obvious hints, is daft indeed

Source_Text_Yo: À ńsọ̀rọ̀ elégédé, obìnrín ḿbèrè ohun tí à ńsọ, a ní ọ̀rọ̀ ọkùnrin ni; bí a bá kó elégédé jọ, ta ni yó sè é?
Target_Text_En: We are discussing pumpkins; a woman asks what we are discussing, and we respond that it is men’s talk; after we have gathered the pumpkins, who will cook them?
Cultural_Context: There is no point in excluding the woman from a matter that will eventually involve her anyway.

Source_Text_Yo: A rí i lójú, a mọ̀ ọ́ lẹ́nu; òṣòwò oṣẹ kì í pọ́n-wọ́-lá.
Target_Text_En: One can tell by looking, and one can tell by taste; a soap seller does not lick her fingers.
Cultural_Context: Soap is recognizable as soap, and anyone who has ever tasted it knows that one does not lick fingers caked with soap. Each trade has its don’ts.

Source_Text_Yo: A ta bàbà a fowó-o bàbà ra bàbà.
Target_Text_En: We sell guinea corn, and with the guinea corn money we buy guinea corn.
Cultural_Context: For all one’s efforts and exertions, one has not significantly altered one’s circumstances.

Source_Text_Yo: Àáyá bọ́ sílẹ̀, ó bọ́ sílé.
Target_Text_En: The colobus monkey jumps to the ground; it runs for home.
Cultural_Context: When danger lurks, the wisest course is to run for safety.

Source_Text_Yo: Àáyá gbọ́n, Ògúngbẹ̀-ẹ́ sì gbọ́n; bí Ògúngbẹ̀-ẹ́ ti ḿbẹ̀rẹ̀ ni àáyá ńtiro.
Target_Text_En: The colobus monkey is wily, but so is Ogungbẹ; as Ogungbẹ crouches, so the monkey tiptoes.
Cultural_Context: The prey that knows its stalker’s tricks is safe.

Source_Text_Yo: Àbá kì í di òtítọ́; ojo ni kì í jẹ́ ká dá a.
Target_Text_En: Plans do not automatically bear fruit; only the fainthearted do not make plans.
Cultural_Context: Although plans may never bear fruit, people should still make them.

Source_Text_Yo: Àbá ní ńdi òtítọ́; ojo ni kì í jẹ́ ká da.
Target_Text_En: Attempts result in achievement; it is faint heartedness that keeps one from making an effort.
Cultural_Context: Without striving, one accomplishes nothing

Source_Text_Yo: Àbàtì àlàpà: a bà á tì, a bá à rẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Unfinished, abandoned wall: unable to master it, one befriends it.
Cultural_Context: One reconciles oneself to matters one cannot control.

Source_Text_Yo: A-bayé-jẹ́ kò ṣéé fìdí ọ̀ràn hàn.
Target_Text_En: A treacherous person is not someone to tell profound matters to.
Cultural_Context: One should keep one’s secrets from treacherous people.

Source_Text_Yo: Abẹ́rẹ́ ò ṣéé gúnyán.
Target_Text_En: A needle cannot be used to make pounded yams.
Cultural_Context: Some tools are inadequate for some tasks.

Source_Text_Yo: Abẹ́rẹ́ tó wọnú òkun ò ṣéé wá.
Target_Text_En: A needle that drops into the ocean defies finding.
Cultural_Context: Some tasks are hopelessly impossible to accomplish.

Source_Text_Yo: Abiyamọ, kàgbo wàrà; ọjọ́ ńlọ.
Target_Text_En: Nursing mother, make the herbal decoction in good time; the day is waning.
Cultural_Context: Attend to duties on time.

Source_Text_Yo: Abiyamọ́ purọ́ mọ́mọ-ọ rẹ̀ jẹun.
Target_Text_En: The nursing mother lies against her child to secure food.
Cultural_Context: One uses every ruse available in the interest of one’s well-being.

Source_Text_Yo: Abiyamọ́ ṣọwọ́ kòtò lu ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: A nursing mother cups her palm to strike her child.
Cultural_Context: Discretion is the better part of discipline.

Source_Text_Yo: Àbọ̀ṣẹ́ kì í ṣe iṣẹ́ òòjọ́; iṣẹ́-ẹ baba ẹni ní ńgbani lọ́jọ́ gan-an.
Target_Text_En: Spare-time work is no profession; it is an assignment from one’s father that takes all of one’s day.
Cultural_Context: One does not waste one’s time on trifles or hobbies.

Source_Text_Yo: Àbùkún layé gbà.
Target_Text_En: The world accepts only adding on.
Cultural_Context: Supplement rather than deplete.

Source_Text_Yo: Adánilóró fagbára kọ́ni.
Target_Text_En: He who disappoints teaches one to be more resourceful.
Cultural_Context: Once disappointed or injured, one learns to be self-reliant.

Source_Text_Yo: Adẹ́tẹ̀-ẹ́ ní òún ṣẹ́ ọ̀ràn kan de àwọn ará ilé òun; ó ní bí òun bá lọ sídàálẹ̀, wọn ò jẹ́ fi kàn-ìn-kàn-ìn òun wẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The leper says that he trusts his relatives on a certain matter; he says when he goes on a journey, they would not dare use his sponge to wash themselves.
Cultural_Context: People have a knack for skirting dangerous or distasteful situations.

Source_Text_Yo: Adìẹ ò lè ti ìwòyí sunkún ehín.
Target_Text_En: A chicken cannot at this late date bemoan its lack of teeth.
Cultural_Context: Everything at its proper time.

Source_Text_Yo: A-fásé-gbèjò ńtan ara-a rẹ̀ jẹ.
Target_Text_En: He-who-would-collect-rainwater-in-a-sieve deceives himself.
Cultural_Context: The shiftless person hurts himself more than others.

Source_Text_Yo: Afẹ́fẹ́ ndá ológìì láàmú; oníyẹ̀fun rọra.
Target_Text_En: The wind is making life difficult for the seller of liquid cornstarch; corn-flour seller, you had better watch out!
Cultural_Context: When even those better situated are defeated, one must be prepared for tough times.

Source_Text_Yo: A-fi-tiẹ̀-sílẹ̀-gbọ́-tẹni-ẹlẹ́ni: ògànjọ́ ni wọn ńsìnkú-u rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: He-who-neglects-his-own-affairs-to-care for-others’-affairs: it is in the middle of the night that his burial is carried out.
Cultural_Context: Do not sacrifice your self-interest to take care of others.

Source_Text_Yo: Àfòmọ́ ńṣe ara-a rẹ̀, ó ní òún ńṣe igi.
Target_Text_En: The creeper is destroying itself, but it thinks it is destroying its host.
Cultural_Context: The host’s death will also be the parasite’s death.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgádágodo ò finú han ara-a wọn.
Target_Text_En: Padlocks do not share their secrets with one another.
Cultural_Context: Some secrets one should not divulge to others.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgùntàn ò jí ní kùtùkùtù ṣe ẹnu bọbọ.
Target_Text_En: A sheep does not wake in the morning and droop its mouth.
Cultural_Context: One should not dawdle in the morning.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà òṣìkà ńgbin ìyà sílẹ̀ de ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: A wicked elder sows suffering for his children.
Cultural_Context: One’s character often affects the for tunes of one’s children.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà ṣoore má wo bẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Elder, do a favor and remove your eyes from it.
Cultural_Context: Do not advertise your acts of kindness or pointedly await acknowledgment of them.

Source_Text_Yo: À-gbà-bọ́ ò di tẹnì.
Target_Text_En: A foster child does not become one’s own child.
Cultural_Context: There is nothing like having one’s own.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàdo kì í ṣe èèyàn; ta ní ńrí ọmọ lẹ́hìn eèsún?
Target_Text_En: The maize plant is not a human being; who ever saw children on the back of elephant grass?
Cultural_Context: One should not overestimate the value of things.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàká labiyamọ ńgbàjá mọ́ ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is completely and securely that a mother [bearing her child on her back] supports the child with a strip of cloth.
Cultural_Context: One must be thorough in discharging one’s responsibility.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbìgbò, rọra fò, ọdẹ́ ti dé sóko; àgbìgbò tí ò bá rọra fò á bọ́ sápò ọdẹ
Target_Text_En: Big-headed bird àgbìgbò, fly warily, for the hunter has arrived in the forest; any àgbìgbò that does not fly warily will wind up in the hunter’s bag.
Cultural_Context: Conditions are hazardous; it behooves everyone to take care.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbokan là ńrọ́ Ifá adití.
Target_Text_En: It is with full voice volume that one recites divination verses for the deaf.
Cultural_Context: One cannot be too subtle with the daft.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbọn kì í ṣe oúnjẹ ẹyẹ.
Target_Text_En: Coconut is no food for birds.
Cultural_Context: Some things and some people are immune to some types of danger; one should not attempt the impossible.

Source_Text_Yo: Ahún dùn; kò tóó jẹ fúnni.
Target_Text_En: Tortoise meat is delicious, but there is not enough of it to make a meal.
Cultural_Context: One should husband one’s resources wisely.

Source_Text_Yo: Ahún wọnú orù, ó ku àtiyọ.
Target_Text_En: Tortoise has entered into a narrow-necked pot; now, getting out is a problem.
Cultural_Context: One should consider the possible consequences of one’s actions before acting.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìgb n ni yó pa Iṣikan; a ní ìyáa rẹ̀-ẹ́ kú, ó ní nígbàtí òún gbọ́, ṣe ni òún ńdárò; bíyàá ẹní bá kú àárò là ńdá?
Target_Text_En: Foolishness will be the death of Iṣikan; he is told that his mother has died, and he says that when he heard the news, he sorely la mented the tragedy; if one’s mother dies, is it lamentation that is called for?
Cultural_Context: The well bred person is always mindful of his or her obligations.

Source_Text_Yo: Àì-gbọ́n-léwe ni à-dàgbà-di-wèrè.
Target_Text_En: Lack-of-wisdom-in-youth is imbecility in adulthood.
Cultural_Context: The man turns out just as the child was; the grown person acquires his traits in childhood.

Source_Text_Yo: Àì-mọ́-ọ́-gbé-kalẹ̀ leégún fi ńgba ọtí.
Target_Text_En: It is ineptitude-in-setting-it-down that makes the wine a spoil for the eégún [i.e., that causes the wine to be spilled].
Cultural_Context: Ineptitude makes an impossible job of the easiest tasks.

Source_Text_Yo: Àì-roko, àì-rodò tí ńṣápẹ́ fún eégún jó.
Target_Text_En: Not-going-to-the-farm, not-going-to-the river claps for masqueraders to dance.
Cultural_Context: It is an idler who makes music for masqueraders to dance.

Source_Text_Yo: Àì-sọ̀rọ̀ ní ńmú ẹnu rùn.
Target_Text_En: It is abstention from speaking that makes the mouth smell.
Cultural_Context: One should always say one’s piece in a discussion.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá èṣín ò mọdẹ.
Target_Text_En: A dog born a year ago does not know how to hunt.
Cultural_Context: One learns from experience and maturity.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá là bá kí; èse ò pẹran fúnni jẹ.
Target_Text_En: One should rather commend the dog; the cat does not kill meat for one to eat.
Cultural_Context: Assign commensurate values to your assets.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá ti eré-e rẹ̀ bá dánilójú là ńdẹ sí ehoro.
Target_Text_En: It is a dog in whose speed one has faith that one sics at a hare.
Cultural_Context: One entrusts important tasks only to those one can trust.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá tí ò létí ò ṣé-é dẹ̀gbẹ́.
Target_Text_En: A dog without ears is no good for stalking prey.
Cultural_Context: A person who cannot be instructed is useless.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá tó gbé iyọ̀, kí ni yó fi ṣe?
Target_Text_En: A dog that swipes salt, what will it do with it?
Cultural_Context: Do not expend your effort on senseless ventures.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá tó lè sáré là ńdẹ sí egbin.
Target_Text_En: It is a swift dog that one sends after a Kobe antelope.
Cultural_Context: One entrusts important tasks only to those one can trust

Source_Text_Yo: Ajàkàṣù ò mọ̀ bí ìyàn-án mú.
Target_Text_En: The person who eats large helpings does not care that there is a famine.
Cultural_Context: Greed knows no thrift.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjànàkú kúrò lẹ́ràn à ńgọ dè.
Target_Text_En: The elephant is not among the ranks of animals one lies in ambush for.
Cultural_Context: The wise person puts some distance between himself and a formidable adversary.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjànàkú ò ṣéé rù.
Target_Text_En: The elephant is impossible to carry.
Cultural_Context: Some tasks are impossible to accomplish.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèyàn-án ní òun ó bà ọ́ jẹ́ o ní kò tó bẹ́ẹ̀; bí ó bá ní o ò nùdí, ẹni mélòó lo máa fẹ fùrọ̀ hàn?  A person vows to disgrace you, and you respond that there is no way he can suc ceed; if he spreads the word that you did not clean yourself after defecating, to how many people will you display your anus? ( .)
Target_Text_En: A person vows to disgrace you, and you respond that there is no way he can suc ceed; if he spreads the word that you did not clean yourself after defecating, to how many people will you display your anus?
Cultural_Context: No one is immune to malicious defamation

Source_Text_Yo: Èké tan-ni síjà ẹkùn, ó fi ọrán síṣẹ́ sápó ẹni.
Target_Text_En: The devious person goads one to confront a leopard and fills one’s quiver with broken arrows.
Cultural_Context: It is dangerous to follow a devious person’s counsel.

Source_Text_Yo: Eku ò gbọdọ̀ ná ọjà tí ológìnní dá.
Target_Text_En: A mouse dares not visit a market established by a cat.
Cultural_Context: One should not deliberately court disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Eku tí yó pa ológìnní ò níí dúró láyé.
Target_Text_En: The mouse that attempts to kill a cat will not live long on this earth.
Cultural_Context: It is foolhardy to take on powers that can destroy you.

Source_Text_Yo: Èmi ló lòní, èmi ló ló lọ̀la, lọmọdé fi ńdígbèsè.
Target_Text_En: Today belongs to me; tomorrow belongs to me’’ is the attitude that pushes a youth into debt. .
Cultural_Context: Lack of foresight leads to disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Èmi ò wá ikún inú agbè fi jiyán; ṣùgbọ́n bíkún bá yí sínú agbè mi mo lè fi jiyán
Target_Text_En: I will not go looking for a squirrel in my gourd to eat with pounded yam; but if a squirrel falls into my gourd, I will eat it with pounded yam.
Cultural_Context: I will not steal, but neither will I refuse a lucky find.

Source_Text_Yo: Èpè-é pọ̀ ju ohun tó nù; abẹ́rẹ́ sọnù wọ́n lọ gbé Ṣàngó.
Target_Text_En: The cursing is far in excess of what is lost: a needle goes missing, and the owners invoke Ṣango.
Cultural_Context: One’s reaction to a situation should be commensurate to it.

Source_Text_Yo: Èpè-é pọ̀ ju ohun tó nù lọ; abẹ́rẹ́ sọnù a gbé ṣẹ́ẹ́rẹ́ sita.
Target_Text_En: The curse is out of all proportion to the lost article: a needle is lost and [the owner] brings out a magic wand.
Cultural_Context: One should not overreact to events.

Source_Text_Yo: Eré-e kí lajá ḿbá ẹkùn ṣe?
Target_Text_En: What sort of sport is it that the dog engages in with the leopard?
Cultural_Context: One should know better than to court disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Èrò kì í jẹ́wọ́-ọ ‘Mo tà tán.’
Target_Text_En: The trader never confesses, ‘‘I sold all my wares.’’
Cultural_Context: People are ever loath to disclose the extent of their good fortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Eṣinṣin ò mọkú; jíjẹ ni tirẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The fly does not heed death; all it cares to do is eat.
Cultural_Context: The fly will persist in attacking an open sore, heedless of death; nothing will keep an addict from the thing he or she is addicted to.

Source_Text_Yo: Èṣù ò ṣejò; ẹni tó tẹ ejò mọ́lẹ̀ lẹ̀bá ḿbá.
Target_Text_En: There is no disaster stalking the snake; it is whoever steps on a snake that is in trouble.
Cultural_Context: It is not the snake inadvertently stepped on that is in peril; it is the person who inadver tently steps on the snake.

Source_Text_Yo: Ètì mẹ́ta ò yẹ orí; èèyàn mẹ́ta ò dúró ní méjì-méjì.
Target_Text_En: Three ears are unbecoming for the head; three people cannot stand in twos.
Cultural_Context: Good things are not good in all situations; one can have too much of a good thing.

Source_Text_Yo: Ewúrẹ́ jẹ ó relé; àgùntán jẹ ó relé; à-jẹ-ì-wálé ló ba ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The goat forages and returns home; the sheep forages and returns home; the pig’s flaw is its habit of not returning home after foraging.
Cultural_Context: There is nothing wrong with traveling, as long as one knows when to go home.

Source_Text_Yo: Ewúrẹ́ kì í wọlé tọ ìkokò.
Target_Text_En: A goat does not venture into the lair of a wolf.
Cultural_Context: Never knowingly put yourself in harm’s way.

Source_Text_Yo: Èyí ayé ńṣe ng kà ṣàì ṣe; bádìẹ-ẹ́ màa wọ ọ̀ọ̀dẹ̀ a bẹ̀rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Whatever the rest of the world does, I will not forswear; when a chicken wants to enter the porch, it stoops.
Cultural_Context: One should not violate established custom.

Source_Text_Yo: Èyí ò tófò, èyí ò tófò: fìlà ìmàle-é kù pàtàkí.
Target_Text_En: This is no great loss; this is no great loss’’: the Muslim’s cap dwindles to almost nothing.
Cultural_Context: If one keeps dispensing one’s property only a little at a time, soon little will be left.

Source_Text_Yo: Ewú logbó; irùngbọ̀n làgbà; máamú làfojúdi.
Target_Text_En: Gray hair shows age; a beard shows maturity; a mustache shows impudence.
Cultural_Context: One’s appearance in a group sometimes indicates one’s attitude toward the group

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ pa Ayéjẹ́nkú, ẹ pa Ìyálóde Aníwúrà; ìgbà tí ẹ pa Ìyápọ̀ ẹ gbàgbé ogun.
Target_Text_En: You killed Ayéjẹnkú and killed Ìyálóde Aníwúrà; but when you killed Ìyápọ̀, you forgot about wars.
Cultural_Context: Past misbehaviors might have gone unpunished, but the latest will have dire repercussions

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀bi alábaun kì í gbèé dẹ̀bi àna-a rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Tortoise’s guilt is not long in becoming its parent-in-law’s.
Cultural_Context: Incommensurate retalia tion soon transfers public sympathy from the aggrieved person to the culprit.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀bìtì ò peèrà tó sè pẹ̀lẹ́pẹ̀lẹ́; ènu ẹni ní ńpàni.
Target_Text_En: A trap does not kill an ant that is cautious; it is one’s mouth that turns out to be one’s death.
Cultural_Context: The cautious will live long on the earth; the incautious engineers his or her own death.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀bìtì tí ò kún ẹmọ́ lójú, òun ní ńyí i lẹ́pọ̀n sẹ́hìn.
Target_Text_En: It is a trap that the giant rat disdains that wrenches its testicles backward.
Cultural_Context: Dangers that one belittles are likely to cause great havoc.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀ẹ̀kan ṣoṣo lọmọ ńsín tí à ńní ‘‘à-sín-gbó, à-sín-tọ́.’’
Target_Text_En: It is when a child sneezes only once that one wishes for the child ‘‘Sneeze and grow old, sneeze and live long.’’
Cultural_Context: Casual responses are appropriate only for minor difficulties; if the difficulties grow serious, more appropriate measures must be adopted.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀gbá mọ̀dí Ọbà; ẹni tó gbéniṣánlẹ̀-ẹ́ lè pani.
Target_Text_En: The Ẹ̀gbá know the secrets of Ọbà town; whoever throws a person has the ability to kill the person.
Cultural_Context: Whoever holds a person’s secret has some power over that person, just as the wrestler who can throw his opponents can probably also kill him.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹgbẹ́ ẹja lẹja ńwẹ̀ tọ̀; ẹgbẹ́ ẹyẹ lẹyẹ ńwọ́ lé.
Target_Text_En: Fish swim in a school of their own kind; birds fly in a flock of their own kind.
Cultural_Context: One should seek and keep the company of people of one’s own station.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀hìn àjànàkú là ńyọ ogbó; ta ní jẹyọ agada lójú erin.
Target_Text_En: It is after the demise of the elephant that one brandishes a cudgel; who dares draw a scimitar in the face of an elephant?
Cultural_Context: One can be brave after the danger has been removed.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀hìn ní ńdun ol-ókùú-àdá sí.
Target_Text_En: It is the back of the man with a blunt cutlass that suffers.
Cultural_Context: A person who does not make adequate preparations for a task or test will rue his or her negligence.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀kọ tí kò bá léwé làgbà ńgbà.
Target_Text_En: It is corn loaf with no leaf wrapping that the elder takes
Cultural_Context: One who is careless with one's property is likely to lose it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹkùn kì í yan kí ajá yan.
Target_Text_En: A leopard that struts is not answered by strutting from a dog.
Cultural_Context: One should recognize danger and avoid it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ tó kú légbodò ló ní ká fòun jẹyán.
Target_Text_En: It is a pig that dies at the time of the harvesting of new yams that asks to be eaten with pounded yam.
Cultural_Context: If one puts oneself in harm’s way, one deserves what one gets.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹlẹ́jọ́ kú sílé, aláròyé kú sí tà gbàngbà.
Target_Text_En: The person involved in an affair dies at home; the spokesperson dies out in the open.
Cultural_Context: The busybody’s fate is worse than that of the person involved in the affair.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹlẹ́kún sunkún ó bá tirẹ̀ lọ; aláròpa ìbá sunkún kò dákẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The person with a cause to cry cries and de parts; a person whose mind never leaves a problem will never stop crying.
Cultural_Context: One should not keep harping on one’s injuries.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹlẹrù ní ńgbé ẹrù ká tó ba ké ọfẹ.
Target_Text_En: The owner of the load must first lift it before one lends one’s encouragement.
Cultural_Context: Only those who make an effort on their own behalf deserve help from others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀lúlùú, ìwọ ló fòjò pa ara-à rẹ.
Target_Text_En: Lark-heeled Cuckoo, it was you that got yourself drenched in the rain.
Cultural_Context: Whatever your difficulty is, you brought it on your self.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni àjò ò pé kó múra ilé.
Target_Text_En: The person for whom a journey has not been profitable should prepare to return home
Cultural_Context: One should know when it's time to return home.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni bá mọ iṣin-ín jẹ a mọ ikú ojú-u rẹ̀-ẹ́ yọ.
Target_Text_En: Whoever knows how to eat Akee apple must know how to remove its deadly raphe.
Cultural_Context: One should be sure of one's capabilities before attempting dangerous feats.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá fẹ́ àbuké ni yó ru ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀ dàgbà.
Target_Text_En: Whoever marries a humpbacked woman will carry her child on his back until the child is weaned.
Cultural_Context: One who knowingly gets himself or herself into a difficulty will bear the consequences.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá fẹ́ àràgbó gbẹ̀hìn ni yó sìnkú-u rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The last spouse of an old person will bury him or her.
Cultural_Context: One should weigh the obligations an enterprise will entail before embarking on it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá mọ ayé-é jẹ kì í gun àgbọn.
Target_Text_En: Whoever knows what makes for a good life never climbs coconut palms.
Cultural_Context: Whoever cares about his or her welfare does not live dangerously.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá mọ ayé-é jẹ kì í jà.
Target_Text_En: Whoever knows how to enjoy life does not enter into a fight.
Cultural_Context: The best way to enjoy life is to avoid conflict.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá na Ọ̀yẹ̀kú á ríjà Ogbè.
Target_Text_En: Whoever whips Ọ̀yẹ̀kú will have Ogbè to answer to
Cultural_Context: If one assaults a protected person, one should be prepared to answer to his or her protector.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá pé kí àkàlà má jòkú, ojú-u rẹ̀ lẹyẹ ńkọ́kọ́ yọ jẹ.
Target_Text_En: Whoever says the ground hornbill should not eat carrion will be the first to lose his or her eyes to the bird.
Cultural_Context: Whoever tries to prevent the inevitable will be trampled in the process of its occurring.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá rọra pa eèrà á rí ìfun inú-u rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Whoever takes great care in killing an ant will see its innards.
Cultural_Context: One must handle delicate matters carefully.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá sọ púpọ̀ á ṣìsọ.
Target_Text_En: Whoever talks a lot will misspeak.
Cultural_Context: It is best to be a person of few words.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní dáríjiní ṣẹ̀tẹ́ ẹjọ.
Target_Text_En: The one who forgives defuses the dispute.
Cultural_Context: Once the aggrieved person is pacified, there is no further point in pursuing the case.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní dúró de erín dúró dekú; ẹni tó dúró dẹfọ̀n-ọ́n dúró dèjà; ẹni dúró de eégún alá-gangan, ọ̀run ló fẹ́-ẹ́ lọ.
Target_Text_En: Whoever waits in a charging elephant’s path waits for death; whoever waits in a buffalo’s path waits for an attack; whoever tarries before a fleet-footed masquerader hankers for a trip to heaven.
Cultural_Context: Whoever sees trouble approaching and does not flee courts disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní gúnyán kalẹ́ yóò júbà ọbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: A person who has made pounded yams must pay homage to the stew.
Cultural_Context: The prudent person cultivates the source of what he or she needs.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní gbé adíẹ òtòṣì-í gbé ti aláròyé.
Target_Text_En: Whoever steals a poor person’s chicken steals from an incessant complainer.
Cultural_Context: One should choose one’s adversaries with prudence.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní kánjú jayé á kánjú lọ sọ́run.
Target_Text_En: Whoever is in a hurry to enjoy life will go to heaven in a hurry.
Cultural_Context: Patience is what life calls for.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni méjì kì í bínú egbinrin.
Target_Text_En: Two people do not hold a grudge and refuse reconciliation.
Cultural_Context: If there is to be any hope of ending a quarrel, at least one of the parties must be willing to make up.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni òyìnbó fẹ́ràn ní ńtì mọ́lé.
Target_Text_En: It is the person the white man likes that the white man incarcerates.
Cultural_Context: Whoever becomes too friendly with a white man deserves what the white man does to him. A favorite, being more likely to take liberties with his or her benefactor, is more likely to get in trouble than the unfavored.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a bá ńbá ṣíṣẹ́kí í ṣí lẹ; bórí bá túnni ṣe a kì í tẹ́ bọ̀rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The person being lent a hand does not malinger; one whom Providence favors is not easily disgraced.
Cultural_Context: One should make the most of unexpected good fortune and not squander the opportunity it presents.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a bá ḿmú ìyàwó bọ̀ wá fún kì í garùn.
Target_Text_En: The person to whom a bride is being brought does not strain his neck [to see her from a distance].
Cultural_Context: One should not be unduly impatient for what is coming toward one anyway.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a bá ti rí kì í tún ba mọ́lẹ̀ mọ́.
Target_Text_En: A person who has been seen has no further need of hiding.
Cultural_Context: Once the damage is done, prevention comes too late.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a fẹ́-ẹ́ sunjẹ kì í fepo para lọ jókòó sídìí iná
Target_Text_En: A person being eyed for barbecuing does not baste himself with oil and sit by the fire.
Cultural_Context: One should not facilitate one's own undoing.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a ò lè mú, a kì í gọ dè é.
Target_Text_En: One does not lie in ambush for an adversary one is no match for.
Cultural_Context: Pick fights only with those over whom you can prevail.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a ò lè mú, Ọlọ́run là ńfi lé lọ́wọ́.
Target_Text_En: An adversary over whom one cannot prevail one leaves to God’s judgment.
Cultural_Context: If your adversary is too much for you, let God attend to him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ńsáré kiri nínú-u pápá ńwá nà àti jìn sí kòtò.
Target_Text_En: The person who runs about in the bush courts the danger of falling into a ditch.
Cultural_Context: Reckless action can lead to disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó bá mu ọtí ogójì á sọ̀rọ̀ okòó.
Target_Text_En: Whoever drinks 40 cowries’ worth of wine will talk 20 cowries’ worth of talk.
Cultural_Context: A little wine opens the way for even less information.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó bá obìnrin kó lọ sílé-e rẹ̀ yó sùn nínú ẹ̀rù.
Target_Text_En: A man who goes with a woman to her house will sleep in fear.
Cultural_Context: Illicit acts carried on indiscreetly are attended by great anxiety.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó ba ogún-ún baba rẹ̀ jẹ́, ó ja òkú ọ̀run lólè, yó sì di ẹni ìfìbù.
Target_Text_En: Whoever ruins his or her father’s bequest robs the dead and becomes a person of reproach.
Cultural_Context: We must keep faith with our ancestral heritage.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó bá wọ odò ni àyà ńkò, àyà ò fo odò.
Target_Text_En: It is the person who enters a river who is terrified, not the river.
Cultural_Context: It is the person who takes on an invincible adversary, not the adversary, who has a problem.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó fẹ́ẹ́ wọ àkísà kì í bá ajá ṣe eré-e géle.
Target_Text_En: A person who does not wish to wear rags should not engage in rough play with a dog.
Cultural_Context: People should avoid situations that might earn them disgrace.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó jìn sí kòtò-ó kọ́ ará ìyókù lọ́gbọ́n.
Target_Text_En: The person who falls into a ditch teaches others a lesson.
Cultural_Context: One learns from the experi ences of those who have gone before.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó mú u lórí ní ó kú, ìwọ tí o mú u lẹ́sẹ̀-ẹ́ ní ó ńjòwèrè.
Target_Text_En: The person holding it by the head says it is dead; you who are holding it by the feet say it is going through death throes.
Cultural_Context: Novices should not presume to be more knowledge able than the experts.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ò tóni-í nà ò gbọdọ̀ ṣe kọ́-ń-dú síni.
Target_Text_En: A person who is not strong enough to beat you up should not adopt a threatening pose toward you.
Cultural_Context: People should not challenge forces they cannot withstand.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó yá ẹgbàafà tí kò san án, ó bẹ́gi dí ọ̀nà egbèje.
Target_Text_En: The person who borrows 1,200 cowries and does not pay them back blocks the path of 1,400 cowries.
Cultural_Context: A person who defaults in little things does himself or herself out of the opportunity for larger benefits.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí Orò-ó máa mú ḿba wọn ṣe àìsùn Orò
Target_Text_En: The person who will be the sacrificial victim of Orò is joining in the revelry on the eve of the sacrifice.
Cultural_Context: The intended victim innocently helps in making preparations for his or her own demise; if there is the slightest possibility of peril, one should not act carelessly.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu ẹyẹ ní ńpẹyẹ; ènu òrofó ní ńpòrofó; òrofó bímọ mẹ́fà, ó ní ilé òun-ún kún ṣọ́ṣọ́ṣọ́.
Target_Text_En: The bird’s mouth is its death; the green fruit pigeon’s mouth is its death; the pigeon hatches six chicks and boasts that its house is bursting at the seams.
Cultural_Context: To boast about good fortune is to invite predators.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu òfòrò ní ńpa òfòrò; òfòrò-ó bímọ méjì, ó kó wọn wá sẹ́bàá ọ̀nà, ó ní “Ọmọ-ọ̀ mí yè koro-koro.”
Target_Text_En: The squirrel’s mouth summons its death; the squirrel has two children, takes them to the edge of the path, and says, ‘‘My children are hale and well indeed.’’
Cultural_Context: Excessive boasting about one’s good fortune invites predators.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu-ù mi kọ́ ni wọ́n ti máa gbọ́ pé ìyá ọba-á lájẹ̀ẹ́.
Target_Text_En: It is not from my mouth that people will learn that the king’s mother is a witch.
Cultural_Context: I will not place myself in jeopardy by speaking dangerous truths; one should not acknowledge or comment on everything one sees.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹṣin iwájú ni ti ẹ̀hìn ńwò sáré.
Target_Text_En: The leading horse is the one by which the followers set their pace.
Cultural_Context: One takes example from those that have gone before.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀sọ̀ ẹ̀sọ̀ la fi ńlá ọbẹ̀ tó gbóná.
Target_Text_En: Slowly, slowly is the way to eat soup that is scalding hot.
Cultural_Context: The more dangerous the task, the greater the care required.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀tẹ́ ní ńgbẹ̀hìn aláṣejù.
Target_Text_En: Disgrace is the reward of excess.
Cultural_Context: Lack of moderation results in disgrace.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹyin adìẹ ò gbọdọ̀ forí sọ àpáta.
Target_Text_En: A chicken egg should not strike its head against a rock.
Cultural_Context: It is unwise to take on forces one cannot withstand.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹyin lọ̀rọ̀; bó bá balẹ̀ fífọ́ ní ńfọ́.
Target_Text_En: Words are eggs; when they drop on the floor, they shatter into pieces.
Cultural_Context: Words are delicate things; once spoken, they cannot be retrieved.

Source_Text_Yo: Fáàárí àṣejù, oko olówó ní ḿmú ọmọ lọ.
Target_Text_En: Intemperate dandyism lands a youth on a creditor’s farm as a pawn.
Cultural_Context: Squandered resources bring destitution.

Source_Text_Yo: Fẹ̀hìntì kí o rí ìṣe èké; farapamọ́ kí o gbọ́ bí aṣeni-í ti ńsọ.
Target_Text_En: Sit back and you will see how a devious person operates; conceal yourself and you will hear how those who seek others’ destruction speak.
Cultural_Context: One must be cagey in order to learn the truth about unreliable people.

Source_Text_Yo: Fi ohun wé ohun, fi ọ̀ràn wé ọ̀ràn; fi ọ̀ràn jì ká yìn ọ́.
Target_Text_En: Liken one thing to another, liken one matter to another; forgive and forget and earn people’s praise.
Cultural_Context: Rather than permit an offense to recall earlier ones, one should forgive and forget.

Source_Text_Yo: Gùdùgudu ò túra sílẹ̀ lẹ́ẹ̀kan.
Target_Text_En: Poisonous yam has never lost its skin.
Cultural_Context: A certain person has never been known to be off his or her guard.

Source_Text_Yo: Fi ọ̀ràn sínú pète ẹ̀rín; fi ebi sínú sunkún ayo.
Target_Text_En: Keep your troubles inside and laugh heartily; keep your hunger hidden and pretend to weep from satiation.
Cultural_Context: One should keep one’s woes to oneself and show a happy face to the world.

Source_Text_Yo: Fò síhìn-ín fò sọ́hùn-ún làkèré fi ńṣẹ́ nítan.
Target_Text_En: Jump this way, jump that way is how a frog breaks its thigh.
Cultural_Context: Restlessness lands people in trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: Ganganran ò ṣéé kì mọ́lẹ̀; a-gúnni-lọ́wọ́-bíi-ṣọṣọrọ.
Target_Text_En: A sharp object is not something to grab for; [it is] a-thing-that-pierces-one’s-hand like-a-sharp-instrument.
Cultural_Context: Dangerous things must be handled very carefully.

Source_Text_Yo: Gìdì-gìdì ò mọ́là; ká ṣiṣẹ́ bí ẹrú ò da nǹkan.
Target_Text_En: Scurrying around does not ensure prosperity; working like a slave results in nothing.
Cultural_Context: One does not necessarily prosper by working oneself to death.

Source_Text_Yo: Gùdùgudu-ú kan légbò kán-ín-kán-ín.
Target_Text_En: Poisonous yam’s roots are sour indeed.
Cultural_Context: The subject is something one must stay away from, for encounter with it is unpleasant.

Source_Text_Yo: "Gbà sókè" ni "Gbà sọ́kọ̀"; ohun tó a bá sọ síwájú là ń bá.
Target_Text_En: Put this above [ashore]’’ equals ‘‘Put this in the boat’’; it is what one throws ahead that one finds in one’s path.
Cultural_Context: One reaps the rewards of the good one sows.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbéjò-gbéjò ò gbé ọká.
Target_Text_En: No snake dancer dances with a cobra.
Cultural_Context: There are some perils even the bravest of people should not court.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbẹ́ran-gbẹ́ran ò gbé ẹkùn.
Target_Text_En: No animal pilferer ever pilfers a leopard.
Cultural_Context: There are some risks even the most brazen risk taker would be wise to avoid.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbígbòòrò là ńṣe ọ̀nà igi.
Target_Text_En: The path along which a log will be rolled must be made wide enough.
Cultural_Context: One should make provisions adequate for the task ahead.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbogbo ajá ní ńjẹ imí: èyí tó bá jẹ tiẹ̀ bẹ́nu laráyé ńpè ní dìgbòlugi.
Target_Text_En: All dogs eat excrement, but only those that smear their mouths with it are described as rabid.
Cultural_Context: No one is without blemish, but one must keep one’s flaws within reasonable bounds.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbogbo ìjà nìjà; bóo gbémi lulẹ̀ mà mọ́ ẹ lójú lákọ lákọ.
Target_Text_En: Every way of fighting is a legitimate way of fighting. If you are strong enough to throw me, I will fight back by looking at you with absolute disdain.
Cultural_Context: One must know one’s limitations, especially when up against insurmountable odds.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbogbo obìnrin ló ńgbéṣẹ́, èyí tó bá ṣe tiẹ̀ láṣejù laráyé ńpè láṣewó.
Target_Text_En: All women are unfaithful; only those who know no moderation are put down as whores.
Cultural_Context: Nobody is without blemishes; the important thing is to keep them from getting out of hand.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbólóhùn kan la bi elépo; elépo ńṣe ìrànrán.
Target_Text_En: One asks only one question of the palm oil seller, but she rambles endlessly on.
Cultural_Context: A person plagued by a bad conscience makes endless excuses when asked simple questions.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbólóhùn kan-án ba ọ̀rọ̀ jé; gbólóhùn kan-án tún ọ̀rọ̀ ṣe.
Target_Text_En: One solitary statement muddies an entire affair; one solitary statement clears all the confusion. I
Cultural_Context: A single sentence can cause irreparable damage; a single sentence can also repair the greatest relational damage.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ òṣì bí ọmọ ọlọ́rọ̀ là ńrí.
Target_Text_En: At the beginning of one’s penury one seems like the child of most prosperous parents.
Cultural_Context: A course of action that will lead to disaster often has a pleasant beginning.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi ìṣáná la ti ńkíyè sóògùn.
Target_Text_En: From the time one makes one’s boasts, one should begin to mind one’s charms [or juju].
Cultural_Context: One should always match one’s vows with adequate preparation to effectuate them.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi rere làkàsọ̀-ọ̀ ńgbé sọlẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The ladder always rests on a propitious spot.
Cultural_Context: A prayer that one may always land at a fortunate place.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi tí a gbọ́n mọ là ńṣòwò-o màlúù mọ.
Target_Text_En: One should limit the depth of one’s involvement in cattle trading to the extent of one’s astuteness.
Cultural_Context: Be careful not to put at risk more than you can afford, or to get in over your head.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi tí à ńlọ là ńwò, a kì í wo ibi tí a ti ṣubú.
Target_Text_En: One should keep one’s eyes on where one is going, not where one stumbled.
Cultural_Context: The best course of action is not to dwell on setbacks but to face the future resolutely.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi tí a ti ńwo olókùnrùn la ti ńwo ara ẹni.
Target_Text_En: Just as one cares for the sick, one should also care for oneself.
Cultural_Context: One should be as solicitous of one’s own welfare as of others’.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi tí akátá ba sí, adìẹ ò gbọdọ̀ débẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Wherever the jackal lurks, the chicken must give the place a wide berth.
Cultural_Context: Keep as clear of known dangers as possible.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi tí inú ṣíbẹ́ asẹ́ tó, inú ò gbọdọ̀ bí ìkòkò débẹ̀; bínú bá bí ìkòkò débẹ̀, ẹlẹ́kọ ò ní-í rí dá.
Target_Text_En: The cooking pot must never harbor a grudge to the same extent that the sieve does; if the pot does so, the corn-meal trader will have nothing to sell.
Cultural_Context: The more power one has, the more one should exercise restraint.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbínú baba òṣì.
Target_Text_En: Anger [is the] father of hopelessness.
Cultural_Context: Anger achieves no good but may backfire on who ever expresses it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbínú lọbá fi ńyọ idà; ìtìjú ló fi ńbẹ́ ẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is in anger that the king draws his sword; it is shame that makes him go through with the beheading.
Cultural_Context: Once one begins an injudicious action on impulse, one may have to carry it through to avoid embarrassment.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbínú ò da nǹkan; sùúrù baba ìwà; àgbà tó ní sùúrù ohun gbogbo ló ní.
Target_Text_En: Anger accomplishes nothing; forbearance is the father of character traits; an elder who has forbearance has everything.
Cultural_Context: Forbearance will avail one everything, whereas anger will always prove futile.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbínú ò m pé olúwa òun ò lẹ́sẹ̀ ńlẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Anger does not know that its owner has no legs to stand on.
Cultural_Context: Anger does not know prudence.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbísẹ́hin àgbò kì í ṣojo.
Target_Text_En: A ram’s stepping backward is not indicative of cowardice.
Cultural_Context: One should not mistake for indecisiveness a person’s deliberateness before acting.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbà tí a bá ní kí Ègùn má jà ní ńyọ̀bẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is only when one pleads with the Ègùn person [from Porto Novo or Àjàṣ in present-day Benin Republic] that he draws his knife.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who redouble their efforts belatedly, just when they are supposed to break off.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbọn-ọ́n ní apátí kò lápátí, tání jẹ́ jẹ́ kà kọjú ìbọn kọ òun.
Target_Text_En: Whether a gun has a trigger or not, who would calmly permit it to be pointed at him or her?
Cultural_Context: One should not take foolish chances.

Source_Text_Yo: Ì-dún-kídùn-ún òyo ni w n fi ńsọ òyo nígi; ì-fọ̀-kúfọ̀ ògbìgbì ni w n fi ńta ògbìgbì lókò; ì-jẹ-kújẹ àdán ní ńfi-í tẹnu pọ̀ fẹnu ṣu.
Target_Text_En: It is the incessant chattering of the Pataguenon monkey that causes people to belabor it with sticks; it is the annoying sounds of the ògbìgbì bird that causes people to throw stones at it; it is indiscriminate feeding that causes the bat to ingest food and excrete with the same mouth.
Cultural_Context: A person’s mouth may be his or her death.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìfẹ́ àfẹ́jù lewúrẹ́ fi ń bá ọko-ọ rẹ̀ írúngbọ̀n.
Target_Text_En: It is excessive love that induces the goat to grow a beard in sympathy with her mate.
Cultural_Context: In all things, moderation is advisable.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìfi ohun wé ohun, ìfi ràn wé ràn, kò jọkí ràn ó tán.
Target_Text_En: Citing comparable things and recalling simi lar occurences [in the past] make ending a quarrel impossible.
Cultural_Context: Refusal to forget the past prevents reconciliation.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìfunra loògùn àgbà.
Target_Text_En: Wariness is the elders’ most efficacious juju.
Cultural_Context: The person who is always wary will avoid much grief.

Source_Text_Yo: Igi ganganran má gùn-ún mi lójú, òkèèrè la ti ńwò ó wá.
Target_Text_En: ‘Protruding twig, do not poke me in the eye’’; one must keep one’s eyes on the twig from a distance.
Cultural_Context: Don’t wait until problems arise before preparing to deal with them.

Source_Text_Yo: Igi tó bá bá Ṣàngó lérí, gbígbẹ ní ńgbẹ.
Target_Text_En: Whatever tree engages in a contest of threats with Ṣango will suffer the fate of drying up.
Cultural_Context: Never take on an adversary too tough for you to handle.

Source_Text_Yo: Igúnnugún gbọ́n sínú.
Target_Text_En: The vulture conceals a lot of wisdom in itself.
Cultural_Context: Even a person who appears foolish may be quite astute.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbà ara ḿbẹ lára là ḿbù ú tà.
Target_Text_En: It is when there is a surfeit of flesh on the body that one cuts some of it for sale.
Cultural_Context: One makes a gift only of one’s surplus.

Source_Text_Yo: Igbá dojúdé ò jọ ti òṣónú, tinú igbá nigbá ńṣe.
Target_Text_En: That a calabash faces downward is no anti-social sign; the calabash is only acting ac cording to its nature.
Cultural_Context: One should not read evil intent into others’ innocent actions.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbà tí a bá perí àparò ní ńjáko.
Target_Text_En: Just as the talk turns to the partridge, it shows up to raid the farm.
Cultural_Context: Said of a person who plays into his or her adversary’s hand just when the adversary most wants to injure him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: Igbá tó fọ́ ní ńgba kasẹ létí; ìkòkò tó fọ́ ní ńgba okùn lọ́rùn.
Target_Text_En: It is the broken calabash that has iron staples driven into its edges; it is the cracked pot that has its neck tied with a rope.
Cultural_Context: It is the person who makes trouble who is visited with repercussions.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbẹ̀hìn ní ńyé olókùúàdá.
Target_Text_En: It is only at the end that the person with a blunt cutlass realizes his error.
Cultural_Context: Some times wisdom comes too late to salvage lost opportunities.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbín ńràjò ó filé ẹ̀ ṣẹrù.
Target_Text_En: The snail sets out on a journey and makes a load of its house.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who are overly possessive of their goods or turf.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbín tó ńjẹ̀ ní màfọ̀n, tí ò kúrò ní màfọ̀n, ewé àfọ̀n ni wọn ó fi dì í dele.
Target_Text_En: A snail that forages at the base of the African breadfruit tree and never leaves the base of the African breadfruit tree will be taken home wrapped in the leaf of the African breadfruit tree.
Cultural_Context: One should know when to quit, or else one will wind up in trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìhàlẹ̀-ẹ́ ba ọ̀ṣọ́ èèyàn jẹ.
Target_Text_En: Empty boasts ruin a person’s reputation.
Cultural_Context: One’s mouth should not be more powerful than one’s arms.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìjẹǹjẹ àná dùn méhoro; ehoró rebi ìjẹ àná kò dẹ̀hìn bọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Yesterday’s food find so delighted the hare that it went to the spot of yesterday’s feeding and never returned.
Cultural_Context: Persistence in risky ventures leads to disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìjímèrè tó lóun ò ní-í sá fájá, ojú ajá ni òì tí-ì to.
Target_Text_En: The brown monkey vows it will not run from a dog, only because the dog has not caught a glimpse of it.
Cultural_Context: The coward may boast as much as he or she wishes, until the real test materializes.

Source_Text_Yo: Ijó àjójù ní ńmú kí okó eégún yọ jáde.
Target_Text_En: Unrestrained dancing is what causes the masquerader’s penis to become exposed.
Cultural_Context: One should exercise restraint in performing even pleasurable activities.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkánjú òun pẹ̀lẹ́, ọgbọọgba.
Target_Text_En: Haste and patience end up the same.
Cultural_Context: Great haste offers no advantage over patience.
