Source_Text_Yo: Ìkekere ńfọ̀rọ̀ ikú ṣẹ̀rín.
Target_Text_En: Ikekere [a type of fish] is treating a deadly thing as something to laugh about.
Cultural_Context: One should not take serious or deadly matters lightly.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkóeruku èèwọ̀ Ifẹ̀; ajá kì í gbó níbòji ẹkùn.
Target_Text_En: Carrying dust is taboo in Ifẹ; no dog dares bark in the shadow of the leopard.
Cultural_Context: One should not engage in forbidden or dangerous acts.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkòkò ńseṣu ẹnìkan ò gbọ́; iṣú dénú odó ariwó ta.
Target_Text_En: Yams cook in a pot and nobody knows, but when the yams get into the mortar, alarms sound.
Cultural_Context: Matters disclosed only to prudent people can be contained, but once they leak to irresponsible persons, they become broadcast.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkókó ọmọ tó tọwọ́ bọ eérú ni yó mọ̀ bó gbóná.
Target_Text_En: The newborn child who thrusts its hand into ashes will find out for itself if they are hot.
Cultural_Context: Experience best teaches that one should avoid dangerous ventures.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikún ńjọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ ikún ńrèdí; ikún ò mọ̀ pé ohun tó dùn ní ńpani.
Target_Text_En: The squirrel is eating a banana, and the squirrel is wagging its tail; the squirrel does not know that it is what is sweet that kills.
Cultural_Context: Overindulgence in good things can result in serious problems.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìlara àlàjù ní ḿmúni gbàjẹ́, ní ḿmúni ṣẹ́ṣó.
Target_Text_En: Excessive envy of others causes one to take on witching and makes one become a wizard.
Cultural_Context: Too much envy leads to antisocial behavior.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé nÌjèṣà-á ti ńmúná lọ sóko.
Target_Text_En: It is from the home that the Ìjèṣà person takes fire to the farm.
Cultural_Context: The wise person assembles all the materials needed before embarking on a venture.

Source_Text_Yo: Iná kì í wọ odò kó rójú ṣayé.
Target_Text_En: Fire does not enter into a stream and yet retain the opportunity to live.
Cultural_Context: Whoever ventures into dangerous situations deserves the repercussions.

Source_Text_Yo: Iná ò ṣé-é bò máṣọ.
Target_Text_En: Fire is not something one conceals under one’s clothing.
Cultural_Context: One should not hide one’s pressing problems but seek help.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìnàkí kì í ránṣẹ̀ ìjà sẹ́kùn.
Target_Text_En: The baboon does not send an ultimatum to the leopard
Cultural_Context: People should not challenge forces they are no match for.

Source_Text_Yo: Inú ẹni lorúkọ tí a ó sọ ọmọ ẹni ńgbé.
Target_Text_En: It is inside oneself that the name one will name one’s child resides.
Cultural_Context: One should not broadcast one’s secrets to the whole world.

Source_Text_Yo: Inúure àníjù, ìfunra atèébú ní ḿmù wá báni.
Target_Text_En: Too much good will toward others engenders suspicion and attracts insults.
Cultural_Context: One can be too good to others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìpàkọ́ là ńdà sẹ́hìn ká tó da yangan sẹ́nu.
Target_Text_En: One throws back the head first before throwing corn into the mouth.
Cultural_Context: One should not put the cart before the horse.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìpàkọ́ ò gbọ́ ṣùtì, ìpẹ̀hìndà ò mọ yẹ̀gẹ̀ yíyẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The occiput does not recognize contempt; a turned back does not see a disdainful gesture.
Cultural_Context: The best response to insults is to disregard them.

Source_Text_Yo: Isà tí ò lójú Alalantorí ńdẹ ẹ́, áḿbọ̀ǹtorí àgbá ikún.
Target_Text_En: Alalantori watches a hole without a visible opening, how much more a squirrel’s burrow.
Cultural_Context: A person who watches his or her pennies is not likely to be careless with dollars.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣẹ kì í pani; ayọ̀ ní ńpani.
Target_Text_En: Misfortune does not kill; it is indulgent happiness that kills.
Cultural_Context: Indulgence kills more surely than want.

Source_Text_Yo: Iṣẹ́ tí a kò ránni, òun ìyà ló jọ ńrìn.
Target_Text_En: A task one was not asked to do usually travels in the company of punishment.
Cultural_Context: One usually rues doing things one has no business doing.

Source_Text_Yo: Itọ́ tí a tu sílẹ̀ kì í tún padà re ẹnu ẹni mọ́.
Target_Text_En: The saliva one has spat out does not return to one’s mouth.
Cultural_Context: Once one has said something, one cannot take it back.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìtọ́jú ló yẹ abẹ́rẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Safekeeping is what is appropriate for a needle.
Cultural_Context: One should pay special attention to matters that are very delicate.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìtọsẹ̀ ló nìlú.
Target_Text_En: Close investigation keeps the affairs of the town in order.
Cultural_Context: Investigating matters well before acting helps maintain harmony in a group.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìwà òní, ẹjọ́ ọ̀la.
Target_Text_En: Today’s behavior [causes] tomorrow’s problem.
Cultural_Context: The foolish behavior of the present sows the seeds of difficulties for the future.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyá là bá bú; bí a bú baba ìjà ní ńdà.
Target_Text_En: One would be wiser to insult [another person’s] mother; if one insults the father, a fight would certainly ensue.
Cultural_Context: One should measure one’s insults in order to avoid a fight; a father is valued well over a mother.

Source_Text_Yo: Iyán àmọ́dún bá ọbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Next year’s pounded yam will still find some stew.
Cultural_Context: Whenever one’s good fortune comes will be time enough to enjoy it.

Source_Text_Yo: Iyán mú, ìrẹ́ yó; ìyàn-án rọ̀, ìrẹ́ rù.
Target_Text_En: A famine rages and the grasshopper grows fat; the famine subsides and the grasshopper grows lean.
Cultural_Context: One should husband one’s resources wisely and save for lean times in times of plenty.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyàwó la bá sùn; ọkọ ló lóyún.
Target_Text_En: The wife was the one made love to, but it is the husband who got pregnant.
Cultural_Context: The person directly involved in a matter does not make as much fuss as the person only tangentially involved.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyàwó ò fọhùn ó fọ́jú.
Target_Text_En: The bride does not speak, and she is also blind.
Cultural_Context: Persons newly arrived in a place or a company should shut their mouths and open their eyes so that they learn the customs before speaking.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyẹ̀wù kan ṣoṣo ò lè gba olókùnrùn méjì.
Target_Text_En: One single room will not do for two invalids.
Cultural_Context: Make adequate provisions for what ever one contemplates doing.

Source_Text_Yo: Jayé-jayé fi ẹ̀lẹ̀ jayé; báyé bá já kò ní àmúso.
Target_Text_En: You reveler, do things in moderation; if the string of life is cut, there is no retying it.
Cultural_Context: One should observe moderation in all things.

Source_Text_Yo: Jẹ kí o yó oògùn ni kò ṣunwọn.
Target_Text_En: Eat-your-fill-of-it medicine is no good.
Cultural_Context: Anything without measure is dangerous.

Source_Text_Yo: Jẹ kí ọmọ ó ti ọwọ́ ìyá ẹ̀ kú wá.
Target_Text_En: Let a child die at his or her own mother’s hands.
Cultural_Context: One should not become involved in the affairs of a person intent on his or her own ruin.

Source_Text_Yo: Kàkà kí ó sàn lára ìyá àjẹ́, ó fi gbogbo ọmọ bí obìnrin; ẹye ńgorí ẹyẹ.
Target_Text_En: Instead of mother witch’s affairs improving, all the children she bears turn out to be female; birds climb upon birds.
Cultural_Context: Despite all efforts, the fortunes of a person may continue to be bad.

Source_Text_Yo: Kàkà kí ọmọ ó bẹ̀bẹ̀ ọ̀ràn, òmíràn ni kò ní-í ṣe mọ́.
Target_Text_En: Instead of apologizing for past misbehavior, a child should rather guard against a repeti tion.
Cultural_Context: One should look to the future and not dwell on past mistakes.

Source_Text_Yo: Kékeré ejò, má foore ṣe é.
Target_Text_En: However small the snake, show it no mercy.
Cultural_Context: Better to be safe than sorry.

Source_Text_Yo: Kékeré la ti ńpa ẹkàn ìrókò; bó bá dàgbà ọw kì í ká a mọ́.
Target_Text_En: One kills the roots of the ìrókò tree while it is still a sapling; when it matures it is out of control.
Cultural_Context: One should take care of problems before they become unmanageable.

Source_Text_Yo: Kèrègbè tí kò lọ́rùn ni yóò júwe bí àgbẹ̀ ó ti so òun kọ́.
Target_Text_En: The neckless gourd will itself indicate to the farmer how to tie it up.
Cultural_Context: A difficult person prompts others as to the best way to handle him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: Kèrègbè tó fọ́ á padà lẹ́hìn odò.
Target_Text_En: The broken gourd ceases plying the river.
Cultural_Context: One should know when to stop pursuing an adversary.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí á fọn fèrè, ká jámú sí-i, ọ̀kan yóò gbélẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Between blowing a flute and wriggling the nose, one [action] will have to go.
Cultural_Context: No one can hope to perform two conflicting activities at the same time.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí á jìnnà séjò tí a ó bẹ́ lórí; ikú tí yó panni a jìnnà síni.
Target_Text_En: One should stand far back from a snake that has not been beheaded; the death that would kill deserves a wide berth.
Cultural_Context: One should recognize dangerous situations and keep away from them.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí á lé akátá jìnnà ká tó bá adìẹ wí.
Target_Text_En: One should first chase the jackal away before reprimanding the chicken.
Cultural_Context: Get rid of the immediate danger before reprimanding those who caused it.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí a máa re tábà ká máa wòkè, kọ́jọ́ tó kanrí ká wo oye ìka tí yó kù.
Target_Text_En: Let us keep on cutting tobacco leaves to pieces while looking up, and let us see at day’s end how many fingers will be left.
Cultural_Context: One should pay close attention when one is engaged in dangerous work.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí á ṣíṣẹ́ lówó lọ́wọ́ ò dàbí-i ká mọ̀-ọ ná.
Target_Text_En: To work and make a great deal of money is nothing like knowing how to spend it.
Cultural_Context: Riches are nothing if one does not know how to use the wealth.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí á tan iná pa agbọ́nrán, ká fọ̀pá gbọọrọ pejò, ká dìtùfù ká fi gbọ̀wẹ̀ lọ́wọ́-ọ Ṣàngó; ní ìṣojú-u Mádiyàn lagará ṣe ńdáni.
Target_Text_En: Let us light a lamp to kill the wasp; let us use a long stick to kill the snake; let us light a torch to secure the help of Ṣango; when one is face-to-face with Mádiyàn [enter-into no-dispute], one runs out of patience.
Cultural_Context: One should adopt the appropriate solution for every problem instead of engaging in long disputes.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí á tó mọ̀ pé kíjìpá kì í ṣe awọ, ó di ọdún mẹ́ta.
Target_Text_En: Before one realizes that tough hand-woven cloth is not leather, three years will have passed.
Cultural_Context: It may take time, but one will even tually realize that no one is invulnerable to misfortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Kì í ṣe ojú-u kọ̀lọ̀kọ̀lọ̀ ladìẹ́ ti ńjẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is not in the presence of the fox that the chicken forages nonchalantly.
Cultural_Context: One would be foolish to let down oné guard when one knows that danger is nearby.

Source_Text_Yo: Kì í tán nígbá osùn kó má ba àlà jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The calabash of camwood is never so empty that it cannot soil white cloth.
Cultural_Context: Some people or conditions are so unredeemable that no matter what one does, they persist in being evil.

Source_Text_Yo: Kì í tètè yé oníbúrẹ́dì; ó dìgbà tó bá di mẹ́ta kọ́bọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The bread seller never learns in time, not until his ware has become three a penny.
Cultural_Context: People rarely learn to mend their ways until they have suffered some reverses.

Source_Text_Yo: Kì í tètè yéni: òwe ńlá ni.
Target_Text_En: One never learns in good time: that is a profound proverb.
Cultural_Context: People tend always to learn wisdom too late.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí ni ológìní ńwá tó fi jóna mọ́le? Ṣòkòtò ló fẹ́ẹ́ mú ni, tàbí ẹrù ní ńdì?
Target_Text_En: What was the cat doing that caused it to be burnt in a house fire? Was it looking for its trousers or gathering its property?
Cultural_Context: One should not put oneself in the path of avoidable dangers.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí oníkálùkù rọra ṣe é; ìfẹjú òbò ò lè fa aṣọ ya.
Target_Text_En: Let everybody take matters easy; the vagina cannot tear a cloth by gaping at it.
Cultural_Context: Over excitement accomplishes little; it is far better to take life easy.

Source_Text_Yo: Kìtì ò mọ́là; ká ṣíṣẹ́ bí ẹrú ò da nǹkan.
Target_Text_En: Sudden pouncing does not capture greatness; working like a slave does not ensure anything.
Cultural_Context: One does not guarantee greatness for oneself by slaving.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ajá tí kì í gbó; àgbójù ajá là ńpè ní dìgbòlugi.
Target_Text_En: There is no dog that does not bark; excessive barking by a dog is what makes people say it is rabid.
Cultural_Context: No person is without a flaw; unbounded flaws are what give people a bad reputation.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ìgbà tí a dá aṣọ tí a ó rílẹ̀ fi wọ́.
Target_Text_En: There is no time one makes a dress that one lacks opportunities to wear it casually.
Cultural_Context: There will always be time to enjoy what one has worked for; one should not be unduly impatient.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ohun tí ńle tí kì í rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: There is nothing that gets hard that does not eventually become soft.
Cultural_Context: Every problem eventually becomes solved somehow.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ohun tí sùúrù-ú sè tí kò jinná.
Target_Text_En: There is nothing that patience cooks that is not well cooked.
Cultural_Context: Forbearance overcomes all things.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ohun tó lọ sókè tí kò ní padà wá sílẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: There is nothing that goes up that will not eventually come down.
Cultural_Context: One should not be too impatient in anticipating the inevitable.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ohun tó yára pa ẹni bí ọ̀rọ̀ àsọjù.
Target_Text_En: There is nothing that kills faster than talking too much.
Cultural_Context: One should govern one’s mouth.

Source_Text_Yo: Kọkọ-kọkọ ò jẹ́ kó mọ ẹni tí rọ̀àn ńdùn.
Target_Text_En: The woman who divorces husbands at the least provocation does not allow one to know when a matter really hurts.
Cultural_Context: Habitual overreaction defuses real alarms.

Source_Text_Yo: Kọ́kọ́rọ́ àṣejù, ilẹ̀kùn ẹ̀tẹ́ la fi ńṣí.
Target_Text_En: The key of excess is usually good only to open the door of disgrace.
Cultural_Context: Excess brings disgrace.

Source_Text_Yo: Kòkòrò tó jẹ̀fọ́ jàre ẹ̀fọ́; ìwọ̀n lewéko ńdára mọ.
Target_Text_En: The insect that eats the vegetable wins the case against the vegetable; leaves should observe moderation in their attractiveness.
Cultural_Context: A person enticed to a crime is not as guilty as the person who did the enticing.

Source_Text_Yo: Kùkùté kan kì í fọ́ni lépọ̀n lẹ́ẹ̀mejì.
Target_Text_En: No one stump can break one’s oil pot twice.
Cultural_Context: The same disaster should not befall a person twice; one usually learns from experience.

Source_Text_Yo: Kùn yún, kùn wá bí ikọ̀ eèrà.
Target_Text_En: Hurry forth and hurry back like a messenger ant.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who are too restless to stay still.

Source_Text_Yo: Làákàyè baba ìwà; bí o ní sùúrù, ohun gbogbo lo ní.
Target_Text_En: Common sense [is] the father of good character; whoever has patience has everything.
Cultural_Context: Common sense and patience are the chief qualities one must have.

Source_Text_Yo: Làálàá tó ròkè, ilẹ̀ ní ḿbọ̀.
Target_Text_En: A worrisome problem that soars to the heavens must eventually come down.
Cultural_Context: No difficulty is without its end.

Source_Text_Yo: Labalábá tó dìgbò lẹ̀gún, aṣọ ẹ̀ á fàya.
Target_Text_En: The butterfly that collides with a thorn will have its cloth shredded.
Cultural_Context: One should be wise enough to know one’s nemesis and avoid it.

Source_Text_Yo: Lù mí pẹ́, lù mí pẹ́ làpọ́n fi ńlu ọmọ ẹ̀ pa.
Target_Text_En: It is by gentle but persistent beating that the bachelor beats his child to death.
Cultural_Context: People not used to caring for delicate articles soon destroy them by mishandling.

Source_Text_Yo: Màá jẹ iṣu; màá jẹ èrú; ibi ayo ló mọ.
Target_Text_En: I will eat a whole yam; I will also eat a slice of yam; satiation ends it all.
Cultural_Context: The greediest appetite will not survive satiation.

Source_Text_Yo: Má bàá mi ṣeré tí kèrègbé fi gba okùn lọ́rùn.
Target_Text_En: Do not ask me to play the sort of game the gourd played and got a rope around its neck.
Cultural_Context: Do not ask me to endanger myself needlessly.

Source_Text_Yo: Má fi iyán ewùrà gbọ́n mi lọ́bẹ̀ lọ sóko ẹgàn.
Target_Text_En: Do not eat up my stew with pounded yam made from water yams before your trip to the forest farm.
Cultural_Context: Do not use up my meager resources on your way to a place of plenty.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Má fi okoò mi dá ọ̀nà,’’ ọjọ́ kan là ńkọ̀ ọ́.‘‘
Target_Text_En: Do not cut a path through my farm’’ is a protest one must make some day.
Cultural_Context: Whoever does not take a stand to protest the violation of his or her rights will continue to have them violated.

Source_Text_Yo: Má fi tìrẹ kí mi lọ́rùn là ńdá fún apènà àti òwú.
Target_Text_En: Do not hang your trouble around my neck’’ is the oracle delivered to the shuttle and the weft thread.
Cultural_Context: Do not involve me in your problems as the weft thread got the shuttle entangled.

Source_Text_Yo: Má fìkánjú jayé, awo ilé Alárá; má fi wàà-wàà joyè, awo Òkè Ìjerò; ayé kan ḿbẹ lẹ́hìn, ó dùn bí ẹní ńlá oyin
Target_Text_En: Do not go impatiently about enjoying life: the oracle delivered to the [royal] Alárá household; do not rush into chieftaincy: the oracle for the people of Òkè Ìjerò; there comes another life in the future that is as delicious as licking honey.
Cultural_Context: Whoever goes about life with patience will reap untold enjoyment from it.

Source_Text_Yo: Má ṣe jáfara; àfara fírí ló pa Bíálà; ara yíyá ló pa Abídogun.
Target_Text_En: Never be sluggish; sluggishness killed Bíálà, but then overeagerness killed Abídogun.
Cultural_Context: One should avoid extremes in all things.

Source_Text_Yo: Mábàjẹ́ ò jẹ́ fi aṣọ ẹ̀ fún ọ̀lẹ bora.
Target_Text_En: Mábàjẹ́ will never think of giving his covering cloth ro a shiftless person to use.
Cultural_Context: Whoever values his or her property will not entrust it to worthless people.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Méè-wáyé-ẹjọ́’’ fọmọ ẹ̀ fọ́kọ mẹ́fà.
Target_Text_En: Méèwáyéẹjọ́ [‘‘I did not come to live a life of litigation’’] gave his daughter to six suitors all at once.
Cultural_Context: If one wishes to avoid trouble, one should avoid actions certain to result in trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: Méjì-i gbẹ̀du ò ṣé-é so kọ́.
Target_Text_En: Two gbẹ̀du drums are too much to hang on one’s shoulders.
Cultural_Context: Some propositions are simply too much for anyone to tackle.

Source_Text_Yo: "Ng óò wọ́ ọ kágbó" ẹ̀hìn-in r ni yó fi lànà.
Target_Text_En: ‘‘I will drag you through the bush’’ will have to clear a path with his own back.
Cultural_Context: (Whoever is determined to make trouble for others must be prepared to take some trouble himself.

Source_Text_Yo: Nítorí ará ilé la ṣe ńdá ṣòkòtò ará oko dára.
Target_Text_En: It is with the town dweller in mind that one makes the bush person’s trousers well.
Cultural_Context: One’s products are one’s advertisement, regardless of whether the recipient knows their quality.

Source_Text_Yo: Nítorí-i ká lè simi la ṣe ńṣe àì-simi.
Target_Text_En: It is to be able to rest that one forgoes rest.
Cultural_Context: One labors in the present to provide for one’s future.

Source_Text_Yo: Nítorí ọjọ́ tí ó bá máa dáràn la ṣe ńsọmọ lórúkọ.
Target_Text_En: It is in anticipation of the day a child will get into trouble that one gives it a name.
Cultural_Context: Each individual has a name and is therefore an independent agent responsible for his or her own actions.

Source_Text_Yo: Nítorí ọ̀la la ṣe ńṣòní lóore.
Target_Text_En: It is with tomorrow in mind that we do favors for today.
Cultural_Context: What one sows determines what one reaps.

Source_Text_Yo: Nítorí ọlọgbọ́n la ṣe ńdá ẹ̀wù aṣiwèrè kanlẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is with the wise person in mind that one makes the idiot’s garment full length.
Cultural_Context: One who cares about his or her reputation will perform obligations well even when the recipient has no power over him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: Nǹkan mẹ́ta la kì í pè ní kékeré: a kì í pe iná ní kékeré; a kì í pe ìjà ní kékeré; a kì í pe àìsàn ní kékeré.
Target_Text_En: Three things one must never treat as of little consequence: one must never treat fire as of little consequence; one must never treat a quarrel as of little consequence; and one must never treat an illness as of little conse quence.
Cultural_Context: Attend to every potential problem early before it gets out of hand.

Source_Text_Yo: O bá ẹfọ̀n lábàtà o yọ̀bẹ sí i; o mọ ibi ẹfọ̀n-ọ́n ti wá?
Target_Text_En: You come upon the carcass of a buffalo in the marshes and you pull out your butcher ing knife; do you know where the bush cow came from?
Cultural_Context: People should not lay claim to things whose procurement they know nothing about.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó dé orí akáhín àkàràá deegun.
Target_Text_En: In the mouth of a toothless person, bean fritters become like bones.
Cultural_Context: To the shiftless person even the easiest task is onerous.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó dé ọwọ́ aláròóbọ̀ ó di níná.
Target_Text_En: When goods get into the hands of the retailer, they become objects to haggle about.
Cultural_Context: A shopkeeper is a difficult person to obtain a good bargain from.

Source_Text_Yo: O kò rí àkàṣù ò ńpata a sẹ́fọ̀ọ́.
Target_Text_En: You have not found corn loaf and yet you are readying the vegetable stew.
Cultural_Context: Said of a person too eagerly anticipating a favor that might not materialize.

Source_Text_Yo: Ò ḿbá obìnrin ẹ jà ò ńkanrí mọ́nú; o máa nà á lóògùn ni?
Target_Text_En: You quarrel with your wife and you put on a baleful look; do you propose to use an evil charm on her?
Cultural_Context: One should moderate one’s response to annoyances.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Ó ḿbọ̀, ó ḿbọ̀!’’ ẹ̀wọ̀n là ńso sílẹ̀ dè é.‘‘
Target_Text_En: Watch out, watch out, for here it comes!’’ For such a thing one would best prepare a snare.
Cultural_Context: If the thought of something fills one with apprehension, one should plot to defeat it.

Source_Text_Yo: O lọ sÍjẹ̀bú kan, o ru igbá àṣẹ bọ̀ wálé.
Target_Text_En: You made only one trip to Ìjèbú and you returned with a calabash of charms.
Cultural_Context: Said of a person on whom the impact of an experience is all out of proportion

Source_Text_Yo: Ó ní ibi tí tànpẹ́pẹ́ ńgbèjà ẹyìn mọ.
Target_Text_En: There is a limit to the protection that black stinging ants can offer palm fruits.
Cultural_Context: There is a limit to the help one can expect from others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó ní ohun tí àgbá jẹ tẹ́lẹ̀ ikùn kò tó sọ pé èyí yó òun.
Target_Text_En: The elder ate something to line his stomach before he said that what [little] was before him would suffice to sate his hunger.
Cultural_Context: The prudent person prepares himself or herself for all eventualities.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó ní ohun tí àgbá jẹ tẹ́lẹ̀ ikùn kò tó sọ pé ìyà-á yó òun.
Target_Text_En: The elder ate something to line his stomach before he said his suffering was enough food for him.
Cultural_Context: Even when one is prostrated by grief, one does not ignore one’s need to survive.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó ní ohun tí ìbòsí ràn nínú ìjà.
Target_Text_En: Raising an alarm or calling for help goes only so far to aid someone in a fight.
Cultural_Context: No matter what help a person in trouble re ceives, he or she will still be in for some grief.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó pẹ́ títí aboyún, oṣù mẹsàn-án.
Target_Text_En: The longest respite for the pregnant woman is nine months.
Cultural_Context: Sooner rather than later, the day will arrive when one must fulfill one’s obligation or pay one’s debt.

Source_Text_Yo: O rí àgbébọ̀ adìẹ lọ́jà ò ńta geere sí i; ìba ṣe rere olúwa rẹ̀ ò jẹ́ tà á.
Target_Text_En: You see an adult chicken at the market and you eagerly go for it; if it was of any value, would the owner sell it?
Cultural_Context: People should think carefully before they assume obligations.

Source_Text_Yo: O só pa mí mo pọ́nnu lá, o bojúwẹ̀hín mo dọ̀bálẹ̀, o tíwọ́ bọ̀gbẹ́. gbogbo; o fẹ́ẹ́ mí ni?
Target_Text_En: You foul the air in my face and I lick my lips; you glance back and I prostrate myself before you and yet you stretch your hand into the bush; would you tie me up?
Cultural_Context: Said by a long-suffering person who has quietly taken a great deal of abuse, when the abuser persists in his or her ill treatment.

Source_Text_Yo: O wà lọ́rùn ọ̀pẹ ò ḿbá Ọlọ́run ṣèlérí.
Target_Text_En: You are perched at the lofty neck of the palm tree and you are bandying words with God.
Cultural_Context: Said of a person who taunts more powerful adversaries even when he or she is in a vulnerable position.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrin bẹẹrẹ: òṣì bẹẹrẹ.
Target_Text_En: Innumerable wives, innumerable prob lems.
Cultural_Context: Whoever adds wives to wives adds problems to problems.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrin tó gégi nígbó Orò, ó gé àgémọ
Target_Text_En: A woman who cuts wood in the grove of Orò has cut her last.
Cultural_Context: Whoever tempts a fate that is known to strike unfailingly has tempted her last.

Source_Text_Yo: Òbò-ó ní ìtìjú ló mú òun sápamọ́ sábẹ́ inú, ṣùgbọ́n bí okó bá dé, òun á sínà fún un.
Target_Text_En: The vagina says it is coyness that caused it to hide below the belly, but if a penis shows up, it will open the way for it.
Cultural_Context: Modesty does not indicate a lack of ability or willingness to act decisively.

Source_Text_Yo: Odídẹrẹ́ ni wọn ò lè tí ojú òun yan òun mọ́ ẹbọ; bí wọ́n bá ńdífá, òun a sá wọlé.
Target_Text_En: The parrot says no one will prescribe it as a sacrifice in its presence; when it sees people consulting the oracle, it will go hide in its closet.
Cultural_Context: The smart person should always distance himself or herself from disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Odídẹrẹ́ ńwolé hóró-hóró bí ẹnipé yó kòó sílé; àgbìgbò nọ̀wọ̀ràn ńwohò igi bí ẹnipé kò tibẹ̀ jáde.
Target_Text_En: The parrot eyes the cramped house as though it would enter; the big-headed bird ágbìgbò eyes the hole in the tree as though it did not emerge from there.
Cultural_Context: Some people fail to appreciate their assets, while others envy them what they have.

Source_Text_Yo: Òfèèrèfé ò ṣé-é fẹ̀hín tì.
Target_Text_En: A chasm is nothing to lean on.
Cultural_Context: One should not trust in emptiness.

Source_Text_Yo: Ogun àgbọ́tẹ́lẹ̀ kì í pa arọ.
Target_Text_En: A long-foreseen war does not kill a cripple.
Cultural_Context: One must take advantage of foreknowledge to protect oneself.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun gbogbo, ìwọn ló dùn mọ.
Target_Text_En: All things are good or pleasing only to a point.
Cultural_Context: One should observe moderation in all things.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun gbogbo kì í pẹ́ jọ olóhun lójú.
Target_Text_En: It is never long before a thing becomes invaluable to the owner.
Cultural_Context: A person always attaches excessive value to his or her possessions. Trust a person to exaggerate their value, especially when they are damaged or coveted by others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun gbogbo kì í tó olè.
Target_Text_En: Nothing ever satisfies a thief.
Cultural_Context: Greed and covetousness are the marks of a thief.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun gbogbo là ńdiyelé; ṣùgbón kò sẹ́ni tó moye ara-a rẹ̀; ẹ̀jẹ̀ ò fojú rere jáde.
Target_Text_En: Everything has its price, but no one knows his or her own worth; bloodshed never has a good cause.
Cultural_Context: People should not devalue their own lives by exposing themselves to unnecessary danger.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí a bá máa jẹ a kì í fi runmú.
Target_Text_En: One does not sniff at what one will even tually eat anyway.
Cultural_Context: Don’t sneer at what you will eventually embrace.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí à bá ṣe pẹ̀sẹ̀, ká má fi ṣe ikánjú; bó pẹ́ títí ohun gbogbo a tó ọwọ ẹni.
Target_Text_En: That which one should do slowly and carefully one should not do in a hurry; sooner or later everything comes within one’s reach.
Cultural_Context: One should not shirk present responsibilities in the pursuit of a distant goal.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí a bá tẹjúmọ́ kì í jóná.
Target_Text_En: Whatever one trains one’s eyes upon will not get charred.
Cultural_Context: Matters to which one devotes one’s undivided attention will not go awry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí a fi ẹ̀sọ̀ mú kì í bàjẹ̀; ohun tí a fagbára mú ní ńníni lára.
Target_Text_En: Whatever one handles gently will not be ruined; it is what one attempts with force that causes grief.
Cultural_Context: A gentle approach will accomplish much, whereas a forceful approach is likely to complicate matters.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí a fún ẹlẹ́mọ̀ṣọ́ ní ńṣọ́.
Target_Text_En: It is what one gives to a caretaker to look after that he looks after.
Cultural_Context: One would best focus only on the task assigned.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí a ó pé yó dẹrù ní ńdiṣẹ́.
Target_Text_En: It is always something one does not expect to be a load that eventually becomes a huge task.
Cultural_Context: Matters that one considers of little sig nificance have a way of becoming insoluble problems.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí a rí la fi ḿbọ párá ẹni; bí igi tíná ḿbẹ lẹ́nu ẹ̀ kọ́.
Target_Text_En: One uses whatever one can find to fill gaps in one’s roof; that does not apply to a faggot spewing flames.
Cultural_Context: Every seemingly sensible generalization has exceptions.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí ajá rí tó fi ńgbó ò tó èyí tí àgùntán fi ńṣèran wò.
Target_Text_En: That which a dog sees and barks at is nothing compared to what the sheep contemplates in silence.
Cultural_Context: Some people make mountains out of other people’s molehills.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó bá wu olókùnrùn ní ńpa á.
Target_Text_En: Whatever the invalid craves is what spells his or her death.
Cultural_Context: Whatever one is addicted to is likely to prove one’s undoing.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó bá wu ọmọ-ọ́ jẹ kì í run ọmọ nínú.
Target_Text_En: Whatever a child craves will not give him or her a stomachache.
Cultural_Context: One is always willing to endure sacrifices in order to have whatever one craves.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjijì là ńrọ́mọ lọ́wọ́ alákẹdun.
Target_Text_En: It is all of a sudden that one sees a baby in the arms of the colobus monkey.
Cultural_Context: One need not announce ahead of time what feat one will perform.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò kan kì í báni lábà ká jìjàdù ọ̀rọ̀-ọ́ sọ; bí ẹ̀gbọ́n bá sọ tán, àbúrò á sọ.
Target_Text_En: When people are trapped in a hut by a downpour, there is no sense in fighting to get a word into the discussion; after the older person has spoken, the younger per son will speak.
Cultural_Context: When there is a surfeit of a commodity, there is no sense in scrambling to get some of it.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò ńrọ̀, Orò ńké; atọ́kùn àlùgbè tí ò láṣọ méjì a ṣe ògèdèǹgbé sùn.
Target_Text_En: The rain is falling, and the call of the secret cult is sounding loudly outside; the shuttle that lacks a change of clothing will sleep naked.
Cultural_Context: If one has not made provisions for rainy days, when they come one must suffer the attendant hardship.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú abẹ ò ṣé-é pọ́nlá.
Target_Text_En: The edge of a razor is not a thing to lick.
Cultural_Context: Never engage in dangerous behavior.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú àwòdì kọ́ ladìẹ ńre àpáta.
Target_Text_En: It is not in the watchful presence of a kite that a chicken strolls to a rock.
Cultural_Context: One does not engage in culpable activity in the presence of those charged with upholding discipline.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kan làdá ńní.
Target_Text_En: A machete can have only one edge.
Cultural_Context: One should be true to one calling or relationship and not philander.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kan náà lèwe ńbágbà.
Target_Text_En: It is at the same place that the youth will come up on the elder.
Cultural_Context: Sooner or later the youth becomes an elder; patience is all.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú ní ńkán ọkọlóbìnrin; àlè méjì á jà dandan.
Target_Text_En: The husband of the wife is only being unduly hasty; in time two concubines will inevitably quarrel.
Cultural_Context: One should not be overly anxious for results that are inevitable anyway.

Source_Text_Yo: "Ojú ó fẹ́rakù" tó ta ajá ẹ̀ lókòó; ó ní bó bá jẹ́ bẹ́ẹ̀ ni wọn ńtà á wọn a máa tún ara wọn rí.
Target_Text_En: We-might-see-each-other-again’’ sold his dog for 20 cowries; he said if that is how things are sold, they might well see each other again.
Cultural_Context: If someone sells you an item at a ridiculously low price, you may expect to see that person again

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú ológbò lèkúté ò gbọdọ̀ yan.
Target_Text_En: In the presence of the cat the mouse must not saunter.
Cultural_Context: One cannot afford to be careless in the presence of powerful enemies.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú tí kì í wo iná, tí kì í wo òòrùn; ojú tí ḿbáni dalẹ́ kọ́.
Target_Text_En: Eyes that cannot stand lamplight and that cannot stand sunlight are not eyes that will last until the twilight of one’s life.
Cultural_Context: From early indications, one can tell what friendships or possessions will prove lasting.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú tí yóò báni dalẹ́ kì í tàárọ̀ ṣepin.
Target_Text_En: The eyes that will last one until nighttime will not start oozing matter at the dawn.
Cultural_Context: Relationships that will last will not become onerous right at the start.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojúkòkòrò baba ọ̀kánjúà.
Target_Text_En: Covetousness [is] the father of envy.
Cultural_Context: The envious and the covetous are similar.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkèlè gbò-ǹ-gbò-ó fẹ ọmọ lójú toto.
Target_Text_En: A huge morsel forces the child’s eyes wide open.
Cultural_Context: Aperson who bites off more than he can chew will suffer in the process of trying.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkèlè kan ní ńpa àgbà.
Target_Text_En: Only one morsel kills an elder.
Cultural_Context: The smallest thing, if not accorded the proper attention, can be the death of even the most powerful person.

Source_Text_Yo: Òketè baba ogun: bí a ṣígun, olúkúlùkù ní ńdi òketè-e lọ́wọ́.
Target_Text_En: Large bundle, father of all wars: when preparing for war, each person prepares his bundle to take along.
Cultural_Context: For all tasks, adequate preparations are mandatory.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkété tó bọ́ ìrù-ú mọ̀ pé ìpéjú ọjà ọrún òun ló sún.
Target_Text_En: The giant bush rat that has its tail stripped by a trap knows that it is its visit to the fifth-day market that was postponed.
Cultural_Context: One should take a near-disaster as a warning.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkìpa ajá la fi ḿbọ Ògún.
Target_Text_En: It is a mature and sizable dog that one sacrifices to Ògún.
Cultural_Context: One should use material proper for the occasion.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkò àbínújù kì í pẹyẹ
Target_Text_En: A stone thrown in anger does not kill a bird.
Cultural_Context: Whatever one does in anger is likely to go awry.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkò tí ẹyẹ́ bá rí kì í pẹyẹ.
Target_Text_En: A missile that a bird sees will not kill the bird.
Cultural_Context: If one sees danger approaching, one will take precautions.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkóbó ò lè fi alátọ̀sí ṣẹ̀sín.
Target_Text_En: The eunuch cannot make fun of the person with gonorrhea.
Cultural_Context: A person who has a blemish should not make fun of other people’s blemishes.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkú àjànàkú là ńyọ ogbó sí; ta ní jẹ́ yọ agada séerin.
Target_Text_En: It is a dead elephant one approaches with a cutlass; who would dare draw a machete to attack an elephant [that is alive]?
Cultural_Context: One dares taunt a powerful adversary only when he has been neutralized.

Source_Text_Yo: Okùn àgbò kì í gbèé dorí ìwo.
Target_Text_En: It is never long before a ram’s tethering rope slips to its horns.
Cultural_Context: Seemingly minor difficulties soon become unmanageable problems.

Source_Text_Yo: Olójútì logun ńpa.
Target_Text_En: It is those who worry about their image who die in war.
Cultural_Context: Discretion and a thick skin are sometimes much better than valor.

Source_Text_Yo: Olóògbé ó jẹ́wọ; atannijẹ bí orun.
Target_Text_En: The dozing person does not confess; nothing deceives like sleep.
Cultural_Context: One can always feign sleep to avoid engaging in discussions.

Source_Text_Yo: Olóòlà kì í kọ àfín.
Target_Text_En: The facial scarifier does not scarify an albino’s face.
Cultural_Context: There are some tasks that are beyond the scope of experts.

Source_Text_Yo: Olórìṣá gbé ààjà sókè, wọ́n ní ire ni; bí ire ni, bí ibi ni, wọn ò mọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The cult priest raises his divining wand and the worshipers proclaim the omen good; whether it is good or bad they do not know.
Cultural_Context: It is foolhardy to presume to know what is in other people’s minds.

Source_Text_Yo: Olè kì í gbé gbẹ̀du.
Target_Text_En: No thief steals a gbẹ̀du drum.
Cultural_Context: One should not attempt a risky business one has no hope of pulling off.

Source_Text_Yo: Omi là ńkọ́-ọ́ tẹ̀ ká tó tẹ iyanrìn.
Target_Text_En: Water is the first thing one’s foot encounters before it encounters the sand.
Cultural_Context: One should attend to the most urgent matters first.

Source_Text_Yo: Òní, adìẹ mí ṣìwọ̀; ọ̀la, adìẹ mí ṣìwọ̀; ọjọ́ kan la óò fẹ́ áìwọlé adìẹ kù.
Target_Text_En: Today, my chicken has gone to roost in the wrong place; tomorrow, my chicken has gone to roost in the wrong place; someday soon the errant chicken will disappear permanently.
Cultural_Context: Little errors, if not checked, will result in a major blunder.

Source_Text_Yo: Òní, babá dákú; ọ̀la, babá dáku; ọjọ́ kan ni ikú yóò dà baba sígbè.
Target_Text_En: One day, the patriarch collapsed; the next day the patriarch collapsed; one day death will throw the patriarch.
Cultural_Context: Frequent close calls with death will eventually lead to real death.

Source_Text_Yo: Òní, ẹṣín dá baba; ọ̀la, ẹṣín dá baba; bí baba ò bá yé ẹṣin-ín gùn, ọjọ́ kan lẹṣin óò dá baba pa.
Target_Text_En: One day, the horse threw the patriarch; the next day the horse threw the patriarch; if the patriarch does not stop riding the horse, one day the horse will throw him to his death.
Cultural_Context: One should take warning from little disasters.

Source_Text_Yo: Onígbàjámọ̀ ńfárí fún ọ, ò ńfọwọ́ kàn án wò; èwo ló máa kù fún ọ níbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The hair scraper is scraping your head, and you are feeling your scalp with your hand; what do you expect will be left for you there?
Cultural_Context: Once the end is clear, one should stop being anxious about developments.

Source_Text_Yo: Onílé ńrelé wọ́n ní oǹdè ńsá; oǹdè ò sá, ilé ẹ̀ ló lọ.
Target_Text_En: The homeowner heads for home and they say the guard is on the run; the guard is not on the run but merely heading home.
Cultural_Context: A strategic retreat to regroup is not the same as giving up the fight.

Source_Text_Yo: Ònímónìí, ẹtú jìnfìn; ọ̀lamọ́la, ẹtú jìnfìn; ẹran mìíràn ò sí nígbó ni?
Target_Text_En: Today, the antelope falls into a ditch; tomorrow, the antelope falls into the ditch; is there no other animal in the forest?
Cultural_Context: If the same person gets into trouble every time, the person needs to look to himself or herself.

Source_Text_Yo: Onínúfùfù ní ńwá oúnjẹ fún onínúwòròwòrò.
Target_Text_En: Always it is the hot-tempered person that finds food for the even-tempered person.
Cultural_Context: The even-tempered person will always have the advantage of the hot-tempered person.

Source_Text_Yo: Oníṣu ní ḿmọ ibi iṣú gbé ta sí.
Target_Text_En: The owner of the yams is the one who knows where the mature yams are.
Cultural_Context: One should not presume to know more about an affair than the person most intimately involved.

Source_Text_Yo: Onísùúrù ní ńṣe ọkọ ọmọ Aláhúsá.
Target_Text_En: Only the patient person will win the daughter of the Hausa man.
Cultural_Context: Patience overcomes all obstacles.

Source_Text_Yo: Oókan ni wọ́n ńta ẹṣin lọ́run; ẹni tí yó lọ ò wọ́n; ṣùgbọ́n ẹni tí yó bọ̀ ló kù.
Target_Text_En: Horses sell for only one cowrie in heaven; there is no shortage of people who will go there, but who ever returns from there?
Cultural_Context: Setting out on dangerous ventures is the easiest thing in the world, but their repercussions prove to be unspeakable.

Source_Text_Yo: Oókan-án sọni dahun; eéjì-í sọni dàpà.
Target_Text_En: One cowrie makes one a miser; two cowries make one a spendthrift.
Cultural_Context: One who has little seems a miser; one who has plenty becomes careless with money.

Source_Text_Yo: Oore ọ̀fẹ́ gùn jùwàásù.
Target_Text_En: The benediction is longer than the sermon.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who are long-winded.

Source_Text_Yo: Oore tí Agbé ṣe lọ́fà, ó dagbe
Target_Text_En: The favor Agbe did in ọ̀fà town reduced him to begging.
Cultural_Context: One should learn from Agbe’s example and be prudent in doing favors.

Source_Text_Yo: Oore tí igúnnugún ṣe tó fi pá lórí, tí àkàlá ṣe tó fi yọ gẹ̀gẹ̀, a kì í ṣe irú ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The sort of favor the vulture did by going bald, the sort of favor the ground hornbill did by developing a goiter, one does not do it
Cultural_Context: One should not do favors that will result in one's own ruin.

Source_Text_Yo: Ooré pọ̀, a fìkà san án.
Target_Text_En: The favor was excessive; it was repaid with wickedness.
Cultural_Context: Too great a favor provokes enmity.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí ejò ò ṣé-é họ imú.
Target_Text_En: The head of a snake is nothing to scratch one’s nose with.
Cultural_Context: Never expose yourself to unnecessary danger.

Source_Text_Yo: Orin ní ńṣíwájú ọ̀tẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Singing goes before plotting.
Cultural_Context: People about to engage in a plot will first spar to sound one another out.

Source_Text_Yo: Orin tí a kọ lánàá, tí a ò sùn, tí a ò wo, a kì í tún jí kọ láàárọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The song that we sang yesterday, without sleep, without respite, we do not resume singing in the morning.
Cultural_Context: Yesterday’s problems should be gone with yesterday.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrìṣà kékeré ò ṣé-é há ní párá.
Target_Text_En: A small god is not a thing to hang from the rafters.
Cultural_Context: Some things may seem insignificant yet must not be taken lightly.

Source_Text_Yo: Òròmọ-adìẹ ò màwòdì; ìyá ẹ̀ ló màṣá.
Target_Text_En: The young chick does not know the eagle; it is its mother that knows the kite.
Cultural_Context: The young are neither as experienced nor as careful as the old.

Source_Text_Yo: Òṣé ní ńṣíwájú ẹkún; àbámọ̀ ní ńgbẹ̀hìn ọ̀ràn; gbogbo àgbà ìlú pé, wọn ò rí oògùn àbámọ̀ ṣe.
Target_Text_En: Hissing goes before crying, and had-one but-known comes at the conclusion of an unfortunate matter; all the elders in the town assembled, but they could find no antidote for had-we-but-known.
Cultural_Context: One can only regret an error once it has been committed; there is no undoing it.

Source_Text_Yo: Oúnjẹ tí a ó jẹ pẹ́, a kì í bu òkèlè-e rẹ̀ tóbi.
Target_Text_En: Food that one expects to last one does not eat in huge handfuls.
Cultural_Context: Wise husbandry is the medicine for lasting prosperity.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó ò bá olè gbé.
Target_Text_En: Money does not live with a thief.
Cultural_Context: A thief and money are incompatible neighbors; never trust a thief with money.

Source_Text_Yo: Òwúyẹ́ a-ṣòrò-ó-sọ bí ọ̀rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: A hush-hush matter [is] difficult to utter as speech.
Cultural_Context: The matter under reference is so delicate it almost does not bear speech.

Source_Text_Yo: Oyún inú: a kì í kà á kún ọmọ-ọ tilẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not count a pregnancy as a child already delivered.
Cultural_Context: One should not treat anything hoped for as though it were already in hand.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀bánijà ní ḿmọ ìjagun ẹni.
Target_Text_En: Only those we struggle with know our strategies.
Cultural_Context: Only through close association does one know other people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀bàyéjẹ́, tí ńrú gángán wọ̀lú.
Target_Text_En: Purveyor of general disaster, who carries a gángan drum into town.
Cultural_Context: Apostrophe addressed to trouble makers.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Ọbẹ̀ lọmú àgbà’’ ló pa onígbaǹso Ògòdò.
Target_Text_En: ‘Stew is the breast milk of adults’’ is what killed the calabash repairer of Ògòdò town.
Cultural_Context: Addiction kills.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀bẹ ṣìlò-ó ḿbáni ṣeré a ní kò mú, bí eré bí eré ó ńpani lọ́wọ́.
Target_Text_En: The ṣìlò knife is playing with one, and one says it is not sharp, just as in play it slashes one’s hand.
Cultural_Context: Be careful not to underestimate people who do not advertise themselves; otherwise, they will have you prostrate before you know what is happening.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọbẹ̀ tóo sè tílé fi jóná wàá sọ ọ́.
Target_Text_En: The sort of stew you cooked and set the house on fire, you will explain.
Cultural_Context: You must explain the unheard-of behavior that resulted in such a disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀bẹlẹ̀wò bẹlẹ̀wò; bí ewúrẹ́ yó bàá dùbúlẹ̀ a bẹ ilẹ̀ ibẹ̀ wò.
Target_Text_En: Inspector of the ground inspects the ground; if a goat wishes to lie down, it first inspects the ground.
Cultural_Context: Look well at the lay of the land before engaging in any new venture.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀daràn ẹyẹ tí ńmusàn.
Target_Text_En: Habitual criminal bird eats oranges.
Cultural_Context: Addressed to any person whose actions are likely to lead to a disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀dárayá tí ńfi ẹ̀gbẹ́ na igi.
Target_Text_En: Sprightly person hurls himself sidewise against a tree.
Cultural_Context: Said of a too-cheerful person whose excess energy is getting on others’ nerves.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọdẹ a-fi-fìlà-pa-erin: ọjọ́ kan ni òkìkí-i rẹ̀ ḿmọ.
Target_Text_En: The hunter who would kill elephants with his cap: his fame lasts only one day.
Cultural_Context: Whoever promises to do the impossible enjoys fame only as long as it takes for the impossibility to be manifest.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀gá-a má fi ẹsẹ̀ yí ẹrẹ̀ , gbogbo ara ní ńfi yí i.
Target_Text_En: The never-soil-your-foot-with-mud dandy eventually soils his whole body.
Cultural_Context: Too much squeamishness is its own undoing.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀gán ìmàdò ò ṣéé kò lójú.
Target_Text_En: A full-grown warthog is not something to confront.
Cultural_Context: One would be wise to avoid dangerous people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ ḿbàjẹ́; a ní ó ńpọ́n.
Target_Text_En: The banana is rotting; people say it is ripening.
Cultural_Context: It does not help to rationalize a brat’s behavior with silly explanations.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀gọ̀ ńgbé ọ̀gọ rù.
Target_Text_En: A fool carries a cudgel around.
Cultural_Context: A person is cultivating the means to his or her own ruin.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀gbágbá wọlẹ̀, ó ku àtiyọ.
Target_Text_En: The iron stake has been driven into the ground; the problem now is how to pull it out.
Cultural_Context: Some ventures that are easy at the start prove mightily intractable down the line.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọgbọ́n àgbọ́njù ní ńpa òdù ọ̀yà.
Target_Text_En: It is excessive cunning that kills the mature cane rat.
Cultural_Context: Too much cleverness brings trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọgbọ́n àgbọ́njù ní ńsọ ẹni diwin; bí oògún bá pọ̀ lápọ̀jù a sọni di wèrè; bóbìnrín bá gbọ́n àgbọ́njù, péńpé laṣọ ọkọ ẹ̀ ḿmọ.
Target_Text_En: Excessive cleverness turns one into a phantom; too much magical charm turns the owner into an imbecile; if a woman is too cunning, her husband’s clothes wind up ill-fitting.
Cultural_Context: People who are too cunning are headed for trouble; a man who marries too cunning a woman is headed for trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọgbọ́n ọdúnnìí, wèrè ẹ̀míì.
Target_Text_En: Today’s wisdom, next year’s madness.
Cultural_Context: What seems wise now may appear like lunacy in hindsight.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọgbọ́n pẹ̀lú-u sùúrù la fi ḿmú erin wọ̀lú.
Target_Text_En: It is with cunning and patience that one brings an elephant into town.
Cultural_Context: The most difficult tasks can be accomplished with wisdom and patience.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ tí a ó bàá nù, gágá lara ńyáni.
Target_Text_En: The day one is destined to be lost one is never able to contain one’s excitement.
Cultural_Context: Disaster attends overenthusiasm.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ tí a to ọkà a ò to ti èkúté mọ́ ọ.
Target_Text_En: The day one arranged the corn in the granary, one did not think in terms of the rat.
Cultural_Context: One hardly ever plans for trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ tí àgbẹ̀ ṣíṣe-é bá di kíyèsílẹ̀, ká ṣíwọ́ oko ríro.
Target_Text_En: The day farming entails being careful not to hurt the soil, one should stop farming.
Cultural_Context: If the basic condition for a trade is interdicted, one should no longer engage in that trade.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ tí elétutu-ú bá máa fò, ìjà pere kì í rìn.
Target_Text_En: On the day the white flying ants wish to swarm, the worms that prey on them keep still.
Cultural_Context: Only cunning will deliver one’s prey into one’s hands.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kánjúwà baba àrùn.
Target_Text_En: Covetousness, father of all diseases.
Cultural_Context: There is no disease like greed.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kánjúwà baba olè; àwòròǹṣoṣò-ó wo ohun olóhun má ṣẹ̀ẹ́jú.
Target_Text_En: Covetousness, father of thievery; bug-eyed greedy person stares at another person’s property without blinking.
Cultural_Context: Covetousness leads to stealing.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kánjúwà èèyàn-án dé àwùjọ, ó wòkè yàn-yàn-àn-yàn.
Target_Text_En: The covetous person arrives in a gathering, and his eyes dart about restlessly.
Cultural_Context: The covetous person is always on the lookout for something.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kánjúwà kì í mu ẹ̀jẹ̀ ẹlòmíràn; ẹ̀jẹ̀ ara ẹ̀ náà ní ḿmu.
Target_Text_En: The greedy person does not drink other people’s blood; he drinks only his own.
Cultural_Context: Greed recoils on the greedy.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kánjúwà ò ṣéé fi wá nǹkan.
Target_Text_En: Impatient envy is not a good state in which to seek anything.
Cultural_Context: One should be patient in seeking one's own fortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kánjúwà pẹ̀lú olè, déédé ni wọ́n jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Covetousness and thievery are similar to each other.
Cultural_Context: Covetousness is as bad as stealing.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kánjúwà-á pín ẹgbàafà nínú ẹgbàaje; ó ní kí wọ́n pín ẹgbàá kan tó kù, bóyá igbiwó tún lè kan òun.
Target_Text_En: The insatiable person receives 12,000 cowries out of 14,000; he asks that the remaining 2,000 be shared, [so] perhaps 200 of them will come to him.
Cultural_Context: Greed knows no limits.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọkọ̀ ńjò, ọkọ̀ ńjò! Ìgbà tó bá rì, kò parí ná?
Target_Text_En: The boat is leaking, the boat is leaking! After it sinks, won’t matters end?
Cultural_Context: There is little one can do about a problem whose outcome is inevitable.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan lọwọ́ ńyọ.
Target_Text_En: Broomstraws drop off one by one.
Cultural_Context: Huge problems usually build up gradually.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọkùnrin tó fẹ́ òjòwú méjì sílé ò rẹ́ni fi ṣọ́le.
Target_Text_En: A man who marries two jealous women has no one to tend his home in his absence.
Cultural_Context: Jealousy is a terrible quality in a spouse.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kùn-ún mọ̀nà tẹ́lẹ̀ kójú ẹ̀ tó fọ́.
Target_Text_En: The millipede knew the way before it went blind.
Cultural_Context: The old knew how to live before they became frail.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Ọ̀la ni mò ńlọ,’’ tí ńfi koto ṣe àmù. ‘‘
Target_Text_En: "Tomorrow I take my leave" uses a shallow pot as his water jar.
Cultural_Context: Shortsighted people make little provision for the future.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Ọlá ò jẹ́ kí nríran’’; ọmọ Èwí Adó tí ńtanná rìn lọ́sàn-án
Target_Text_En: ‘Greatness won’t let me see’’: the son of the Èwí, king of Adó, lights a lamp to walk with in broad daylight.
Cultural_Context: One should not allow one’s good fortune to go to one’s head.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀làjà ní ńfi orí gbọgbẹ́.
Target_Text_En: It is the person who separates two fighters who gets gashed on the head.
Cultural_Context: The peacemaker is likely to suffer for his pains.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlọ́dẹ kì í torí atẹ́gùn yìnbọn.
Target_Text_En: A hunter does not fire off his gun because of the wind.
Cultural_Context: One should be deliberate and attentive in pursuing one’s profession.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlọgbọ́n bẹẹrẹ-ẹ́ pète ìgárá.
Target_Text_En: The excessively cunning person is trying his hand at stealing.
Cultural_Context: Too much cunning is like thievery.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ adìẹ́ fò, a ní ‘‘Ẹrán lọ àkẹ́ẹ̀!’’
Target_Text_En: A chick flies up, and we exclaim, ‘‘A game animal has escaped, alas!’’
Cultural_Context: Do not blow matters out of all credible proportion.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ inú ayò ò ṣéé bá bínú.
Target_Text_En: The seeds in an ayò game are not things to be angry at.
Cultural_Context: One should not blame one’s misfortune on innocent people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ orogún ẹ-ẹ́ kú, o ní ẹní rí ẹ lọ́run ò purọ́; bí tìẹ́ bá kú ńkọ́.
Target_Text_En: The child of your rival wife dies, and you say the person who saw you in heaven did not lie; what if your own child dies?
Cultural_Context: One should not go overboard in sharing other people’s sorrow.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọrí odó pani lọ́tọ̀, ká tó wí pé ká kùn ún lóògùn.
Target_Text_En: A pestle is a lethal weapon in itself, let alone after rubbing poison on it.
Cultural_Context: Overkill is pointless; if a situation is dangerous enough as it is, one should not aggravate it by acting provocatively.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀mùtí ò mu agbè já.
Target_Text_En: The drunkard does not drink the gourd through.
Cultural_Context: There is a limit to the pleasure a drunk can get from a bottle.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀nà ẹ̀bùrú dá ọwọ́ olúwa-a rẹ̀ tẹlẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: A shortcut causes a person to land on his palms.
Cultural_Context: There are perils to taking paths one is not familiar with.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀nà ìgbàlẹ̀ a máa já sọ́run.
Target_Text_En: The road to the secret grove of the egúngún cult may lead to heaven.
Cultural_Context: People who do the forbidden may pay dearly for their temerity.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀nà là ńṣì mọ̀nà; bí a ò bá ṣubú, a kì í mọ ẹrù-ú dì.
Target_Text_En: It is by missing one’s way that one learns the way; if one does not fall, one does not learn how to tie one's load properly.
Cultural_Context: Errors and failures are opportunities to learn.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ ò tó ohun tí à ńyọ àdá sí.
Target_Text_En: The problem posed by the banana tree is nothing that calls for a machete.
Cultural_Context: Do not make too much of a minorcrisis.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀nà ni yó mùú olè; ahéré ni yó mùú olóko.
Target_Text_En: The road will eventually expose the thief; the farm hut will eventually expose the farmer.
Cultural_Context: When the habitual wrongdoer comes to grief, it will be in the course of his wrong doing.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀nà ọ̀fun, ọ̀nà ọ̀run: méjèèjì bákannáà ni wọ́n rí.
Target_Text_En: The pathway of the throat, the pathway to heaven: the two are very much alike.
Cultural_Context: One’s throat may lead to one’s death.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pá àgbéléjìká, a-tẹ́hìn-lójú.
Target_Text_En: The walking stick that is carried on the shoulder has its eye pointed backward.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who pay no attention to their future.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pọ̀ oògùn ní ńru ọmọ gàle-gàle.
Target_Text_En: It is a great deal of medicine that possesses a child and robs it of all self-control.
Cultural_Context: A person who lacks moderation is like someone overpowered by bad medicine.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ lejò ḿbùjẹ, tí à ńwí pé ilẹ̀-ẹ́ rorò?
Target_Text_En: Is it because a snake is biting a toad that one says the earth portends disaster?
Cultural_Context: Do not make too much of insignificant events.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn ńlá-ńlá ní ḿbá àpá; ọ̀ràn ṣẹ́kú ṣẹ́kú ní ḿbá oṣè.
Target_Text_En: Only huge problems befall the mahogany bean tree; only minor problems befall the baobab tree.
Cultural_Context: Different people have different levels of vulnerability.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn ò dun gbọ̀ọ̀rọ̀; a dá a láàárọ̀, ó yọ lálẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Problems have hardly any effect at all on the pumpkin shoot; broken off in the morning, it reappears the following night.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who are unimpressed by correction or punishment.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn ọkà-á ní ìba; ayé ní òṣùwọ̀n.
Target_Text_En: A matter pertaining to corn has a limit; life has its measure.
Cultural_Context: To everything there is a proper limit.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rọ̀ ò pọ̀, àkàwé-e rẹ̀ ló pọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The matter in question is not overwhelming; it is the elaboration of it that is almost forbidding.
Cultural_Context: Creating a problem is easy; explaining it is not quite as easy.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rọ̀ púpọ̀ ò kún agbọ̀n; irọ́ ní ḿmú wá.
Target_Text_En: A lot of words will not fill a basket; they will only lead to lies.
Cultural_Context: Brevity is wise in discussions; wordiness leads to invention.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí ò ní ohùn fífọ̀, dídá kó yẹ ẹ́.
Target_Text_En: A matter that does not have a means to voice itself had better be silent.
Cultural_Context: Matters that should not be mentioned should be left unbroached.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ṣọ́ oníbùjé ò pé isán; ọ̀ṣọ́ onínàbì ò ju ọdún lọ.
Target_Text_En: The beauty bestowed by tattooing with the juice of the bùjé plant does not last nine days; a prostitute’s beauty does not last more than a year.
Cultural_Context: Fast living plays havoc with people’s looks.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀tọ̀ọ̀tọ̀ là ńtẹ ẹrẹ̀; ọ̀tọ̀ọ̀tọ̀ là ńtẹ eruku.
Target_Text_En: One step after the other is the manner to walk through mire; one step after the other is how one walks through dust.
Cultural_Context: With great care, one can extricate oneself safely from any problem.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀wọ́n yúnlé, ọ̀pọ̀-ọ́ yúnjà.
Target_Text_En: Expensive commodities come to the home; inexpensive ones go to the market.
Cultural_Context: If one overprices one’s goods, one will find no takers.

Source_Text_Yo: Pala-pálà kì í ṣe ẹran àjẹgbé; ẹ ṣáà máa mu àgúnmu.
Target_Text_En: Stockfish is not a meat one eats without repercussions; keep on drinking herbal remedies.
Cultural_Context: One pays for one’s indiscretions by and by.

Source_Text_Yo: Paramọ́lẹ̀-ẹ́ kọ ọ̀ràn àfojúdi.
Target_Text_En: The serpent refuses to betrifled with.
Cultural_Context: Certain situations are not to be taken lightly, lest they result in painful repercussions.

Source_Text_Yo: Pẹ̀lẹ́-pẹ̀lẹ́ léjò-ó fi ńgun àgbọn.
Target_Text_En: It is very carefully and patiently that a snake climbs the coconut palm.
Cultural_Context: Dangerous and difficult tasks should be attempted with care and patience.

Source_Text_Yo: Pẹ̀tẹ̀ pẹ̀tẹ̀ ọ̀rọ̀, àtà-sí-ní-lára-má-wọ̀n-ọ́n.
Target_Text_En: The soiling caused by speech stains a person and cannot be removed.
Cultural_Context: Injury once spoken cannot be recalled.

Source_Text_Yo: Pípẹ́ ni yó pẹ̀ẹ́, agbọ̀n á bo adìẹ.
Target_Text_En: It may take long, but the coop will eventually cover the chicken.
Cultural_Context: One may put it off a while, but one cannot avoid one's fate.

Source_Text_Yo: Pípẹ́ ni yó pẹ̀ẹ́ akólòlò á pe baba.
Target_Text_En: It may take long, but the stammerer will eventually manage to say ‘‘Papa.’’
Cultural_Context: With perseverance the most difficult task will be accomplished.

Source_Text_Yo: Pípẹ́ ni yó pẹ̀ẹ́, akọ̀pẹ yó wàá sílẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It may take a while, but the palm-wine tapster will descend from atop the palm tree.
Cultural_Context: With patience, what one desires will eventually happen.

Source_Text_Yo: Pípẹ́ ni yó pẹ̀ẹ́, amòòkùn yó jàáde nínú odò.
Target_Text_En: It may take a while, but the underwater swimmer will eventually surface.
Cultural_Context: If one is patient, what is bound to happen will eventually happen.

Source_Text_Yo: Pípẹ́ ni yó pẹ̀ẹ́, èké ò mú rá.
Target_Text_En: It may take a while, but the deceitful person will not be undiscovered.
Cultural_Context: Truth will unfailingly triumph in the end.

Source_Text_Yo: Pípẹ́ ni yó pẹ̀ẹ́, ẹní lọ sódò á bọ̀ wálé.
Target_Text_En: It may take a while, but the person who went to the stream will return home.
Cultural_Context: There is no journey that does not end sometime.

Source_Text_Yo: Pípẹ́ ni yó pẹ̀ẹ́, Ọ̀rúnmìlà yó jẹ àgbàdò dandan.
Target_Text_En: It may take a while but Ọ̀rúnmìlà will surely eat corn.
Cultural_Context: What one deserves will unfailingly come one’s way in the end.

Source_Text_Yo: Rò ó kóo tó ṣe é; ó sàn ju kóo ṣé kóo tó rò ó.
Target_Text_En: Think it through before you do it; that is better than doing it before you think it through.
Cultural_Context: Plan ahead.

Source_Text_Yo: Rọra dì, ká lè bá ọ sá.
Target_Text_En: Pack judiciously that we may accompany you while you escape.
Cultural_Context: A person who wants other people’s help must lighten his or her baggage.

Source_Text_Yo: Sà á bí olóògùn-ún ti wí.
Target_Text_En: Invoke it exactly as the maker of the charm instructed.
Cultural_Context: Always follow instructions, and do not presume to know better than your instructor.

Source_Text_Yo: Sùúrù loògùn ayé.
Target_Text_En: Patience is the talisman for living.
Cultural_Context: Patience solves all problems.

Source_Text_Yo: Sùúrù ò lópin.
Target_Text_En: There is no end to the need for patience.
Cultural_Context: One must never tire of exercising patience.

Source_Text_Yo: Sùúrù-ú lérè.
Target_Text_En: Patience has its profits.
Cultural_Context: Patience is a useful quality to cultivate.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣà ǹgbákó ró, a ní kò róo re, Ṣàǹgbàkù-ú gbè é lẹ́sẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Ṣàǹgbákó makes a sound and we say the sound is foul, and then Ṣàǹgbàkù lends its voice in its support.
Cultural_Context: Do not choose to do things that others before you have been condemned for doing.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣe-ká-rí-mi, alájá tó so ẹ̀gi mọ́rùn.
Target_Text_En: Exhibitionist: a dog owner who ties a sheep’s mane around his own neck.
Cultural_Context: Do not go to too great lengths to call people's attention to yourself.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Ṣé kí nfìdí hẹ?’’ làfòmọ́ fi ńdi onílé.
Target_Text_En: "May I perch here awhile?" is the ruse by which the climber-parasite becomes a permanent resident.
Cultural_Context: Give people an inch, and they are likely to take several miles.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣe-ǹ-ṣe dìwọ̀fà, bó ṣe é yó dẹrú-u wọn.
Target_Text_En: The habit that made a person a pawn,] if the person persists in it, will make him or her a slave.
Cultural_Context: One should desist from pursuits that have proved unprofitable.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣe-ǹ-ṣe ewúrẹ́ làgùntàn ńfiyè sí.
Target_Text_En: The habit of the goat is what the sheep pays attention to.
Cultural_Context: One would be wise to learn from the behavior and plight of fools.

Source_Text_Yo: "Ta á sí i" kì í bá ni wá ọfà.
Target_Text_En: "Shoot at it" does not help one find arrows.
Cultural_Context: People are ever eager to goad one to action but never to help one carry out the task.

Source_Text_Yo: Ta ní rán Abẹ́lù wọ ọkọ̀, tó ní ọkọ̀ọ́ ri òun?
Target_Text_En: Who sent Abẹ́lu into a boat, as a result of which action he says he was drowned?
Cultural_Context: People who get into trouble by their own actions should complain to no one.

Source_Text_Yo: "Tàná là ńjà lé lórí" ló pa Baálẹ̀ẹ Kòmọ̀kan.
Target_Text_En: It is yesterday’s matter that we are fighting over’’ is what killed Chief Know-Nothing.
Cultural_Context: It is wise to let the past alone.

Source_Text_Yo: Tantabùlù, aṣòróówọ̀ bí ẹ̀wù àṣejù.
Target_Text_En: An unbecoming thing is as unpleasant to wear as a garment of disgrace.
Cultural_Context: Disgrace is not a pleasant thing to live with.

Source_Text_Yo: Wẹ́rẹ́ wẹ́rẹ́ nikán ńjẹlé.
Target_Text_En: Slowly, slowly is the manner in which termites consume a house.
Cultural_Context: Inconspicuous and imperceptible problems in time become huge disasters.

Source_Text_Yo: Tìjà tìjà ní ńṣe ará Ọ̀pọ́ndá.
Target_Text_En: Incessant proneness to fighting is the affliction of Ọ̀pọ́ndá people.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who are always out for a fight.

Source_Text_Yo: Tọ̀sán tọ̀sán ní ńpọ́n ìtalẹ̀ lójú; bílẹ̀-ẹ́ bá ṣú yó di olóńjẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is the persistence of daylight that imposes suffering on the mud-floor worm; when night falls, it will find food.
Cultural_Context: Patience will bring what one lacks.

Source_Text_Yo: Wàrà ò sí lónìí, wàrà-á wà l la.
Target_Text_En: No cheese today, but there will be cheese tomorrow.
Cultural_Context: Today’s want will be followed by tomorrow’s plenty.

Source_Text_Yo: Wòròwórònikán ńjẹlé.
Target_Text_En: Slowly, slowly is the manner in which ter mites consume a house.
Cultural_Context: Inconspicuous and imperceptible problems in time become huge disasters.

Source_Text_Yo: Wíwò-ó tó ìran.
Target_Text_En: Watching is enough for a spectacle.
Cultural_Context: One would do well just to watch spectacles and avoid becoming part of them.

Source_Text_Yo: Wó ilé ẹ kí mba ọ kọ, ẹrù ikàn kan ní ńpa fún ní.
Target_Text_En: Demolish your house and I will help you rebuild it’’: he will give one only one bundle of thatching grass.
Cultural_Context: Never trust people who goad you into trouble with promises of help down the road.

Source_Text_Yo: Wò bìà-á yọ́ tán, ó pe ẹgbẹ́ ẹ̀ wá.
Target_Text_En: The greedy person fed to satiation, and he summons his friends.
Cultural_Context: The freeloader always seeks opportunities to take as much as possible from his or her benefactor.

Source_Text_Yo: Wọ́n ní, ‘‘Ìbàrìbá, ọmọ ẹ-ẹ́ jálè.’’ Ó ní ‘‘A gbọ́ tolè tó jà; èwo lokùn ọrùn-un ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: People said, "‘Ìbàrìbá person, your child stole something" She responded, ‘‘That he stole something I can understand, but I can not understand the rope around his neck.’’
Cultural_Context: Punishment should fit the offense, not be disproportionate.

Source_Text_Yo: Wọ́n purọ́ fún ọ, o ò gbà; o lè dé ìdí òótọ́?
Target_Text_En: People lie to you and you do not accept the lie; can you ever know what the truth is?
Cultural_Context: Since one can seldom be sure what the truth is, one would save oneself a great deal of grief by not always insisting on it.

Source_Text_Yo: Wọ́n torí ajá ńlóṣòó lọ fowó rọ̀bọ.
Target_Text_En: Because the dog sits on its haunches, they went and spent their money on purchasing a monkey.
Cultural_Context: One should not pass up something useful for something useless simply because the latter looks better.

Source_Text_Yo: Yíyọ́ ẹkùn, tojo kọ́; ohun tí yó jẹ ní ńwá.
Target_Text_En: The leopard’s stealthy gait is not a result of cowardice; it is simply stalking a prey.
Cultural_Context: Do not mistake people’s gentle nature for spinelessness.

Source_Text_Yo: Yọkọlú-yọkọlú, kò ha tán bí? Ìyàwó gbọ́kọ ṣánlẹ̀, ọkọ́ yọké.
Target_Text_En: All your strutting and bragging, where is it now? The wife threw the husband down so hard that he grew a hump on his back.
Cultural_Context: Said of braggarts who have been taken down a few notches.

Source_Text_Yo: A hán ìkokò lọ́wọ́ ọ̀tún, a hán ìkokò lẹ́sẹ̀ òsì; ó ku ẹni tí yó kò ó lójú.
Target_Text_En: We lop off the hyena’s right forelimb; we lop off the hyena’s left hind limb; the question is, who will face it now?
Cultural_Context: Inflicting such injuries on the hyena is no victory; it only makes the animal more dangerous.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dá ẹ̀rù okó ńlá ba arúgbó.
Target_Text_En: One should not attempt to scare an old [woman] with a huge penis.
Cultural_Context: A person who has seen everything is not easily frightened.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dùbúlẹ̀ ṣubú.
Target_Text_En: One does not fall from a prone position.
Cultural_Context: Hunger cannot make one faint and fall if one goes to sleep.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ojoojúmọ́ rí olè jà kó dà bí-i tọwọ́ ẹni.
Target_Text_En: One is never so fortunate at daily thievery that it matches owning one’s own things.
Cultural_Context: Self-sufficiency is far better than fortunate opportunism.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ojú olójú ṣòwò ká jèrè.
Target_Text_En: One never trades with other people’s eyes and profit.
Cultural_Context: There is nothing like attending to one’s business oneself.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ojúbọ̀rọ̀ gba ọmọ lọ́wọ́ èkùrọ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not easily or casually take the child from the palm nut
Cultural_Context: It takes effort to accomplish a good end.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mọ ibi tí à ńlọ kí ọrùn ó wọ ẹni.
Target_Text_En: One does not, despite knowing where one is going, suffer a constricted neck from one’s heavy load.
Cultural_Context: If one knows the size of the task, one should regulate one’s effort accordingly.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í sọ pé ọjà-á nígbà; bó bá nígbà, kíníṣe tí wọ́n tún ńná a?
Target_Text_En: One does not say there is a time for the market; if it were so, why would people con tinuously patronize it?
Cultural_Context: Any time is a good time to trade.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ṣe ọ̀tẹ̀ ẹranko gán-ń-gán; bí a bá he ìgbín àdá là ńnà á.
Target_Text_En: One does not conduct one’s feud with an animal in a halfhearted manner; if one finds a snail, one hits it with a machete.
Cultural_Context: Give your all to every enterprise you embark upon.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í walẹ̀ fún adìẹ jẹ.
Target_Text_En: One does not scratch the ground for the chicken to find food.
Cultural_Context: Each person is responsible for his or her own welfare.

Source_Text_Yo: À ńpa ẹ̀kukù, ẹ̀kukù ńrúwé; à ńyan nínú aṣẹro, aṣẹro ńdàgbà; à ńkébòsí Ògún, ara Ògún ńle.
Target_Text_En: The more one weeds kukù, the more it sprouts leaves; the more one tramples aṣẹro, the more it grows; the more one rails against Ògún, the more he thrives.
Cultural_Context: Because the two plants are hardy and virtually indestructible, and Ògún is the formidable god of metals and war, the proverb bespeaks resilience and invulnerability.

Source_Text_Yo: "A ò mọ̀yí Ọlọ́run yó ṣe" kò jẹ́ ká bínú kú.
Target_Text_En: We know not what God will do’’ keeps one from committing suicide.
Cultural_Context: Often it is hope that keeps people going.

Source_Text_Yo: A pa ẹmọ́ lóko ilá, a jù ú sí ọ̀kẹ́ ílasa; ilé ẹmọ́ lẹmọ́ lọ.
Target_Text_En: A giant rat is killed on an okra farm and thrown into a sack containing okra leaves; the giant rat has arrived at its home.
Cultural_Context: The resourceful person will find a way to adapt to any situation.

Source_Text_Yo: Ààrẹ àgòrò tó bá gbójú, tòun tolúwa-a rẹ̀ lẹgbẹ́ra.
Target_Text_En: A subordinate military officer who is audacious is the equal of his superior.
Cultural_Context: Audaciousness will get one one’s way.

Source_Text_Yo: Abẹ́rẹ́ á lọ kí ọ̀nà okùn tó dí.
Target_Text_En: The needle will pass before the way of the thread is blocked.
Cultural_Context: Unlike the thread’s, the passage of the needle through the cloth is ever smooth.

Source_Text_Yo: Abiyamọ ọ̀tá àgàn; ẹní ńṣiṣẹ́ ọ̀tá ọ̀lẹ.
Target_Text_En: Nursing mother, enemy of the barren woman; working person, enemy of the idler.
Cultural_Context: The mother incurs the envy of a barren woman; the hard worker incurs the hatred of the idler.

Source_Text_Yo: Aboyún bí, ìhá tù ú.
Target_Text_En: The pregnant woman delivered; her sides are much eased.
Cultural_Context: Relief comes in time to the persevering sufferer.

Source_Text_Yo: Abẹ̀wẹ̀ ńwá ọ̀tá fúnra ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: He who summons others to render him communal help seeks enemies.
Cultural_Context: It is best to be self-sufficient.

Source_Text_Yo: Àdán tó sùn sídìí ọsàn ò rí he, áḿbọ̀sì oódẹ tó ní òún jí dé.
Target_Text_En: Bat, who slept by the orange tree, found no orange to pick, let alone the parrot which said it came over very early at dawn.
Cultural_Context: The more persistent person will surely be re warded before the less persistent.

Source_Text_Yo: A-fàkàrà-jẹ̀kọ́ ò mọ iyì ọbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: He-who-eats-corn-meal-with-bean-fritters does not know the virtues of stew.
Cultural_Context: Whoever leads a sheltered life misses out on some great experiences.

Source_Text_Yo: Afẹ́fẹ́ kí í fẹ́ kí omi inú àgbọn dànù.
Target_Text_En: The wind does not blow against the liquid inside a coconut and cause it to spill.
Cultural_Context: Certain people are not susceptible to certain disasters.

Source_Text_Yo: Àfẹjútoto ò mọ ọkùnrin.
Target_Text_En: Glaring wildly does not bespeak manliness.
Cultural_Context: Action is more persuasive than appearance.

Source_Text_Yo: Àfẹ́ká là ńfẹ́ iná.
Target_Text_En: Blowing from all directions is how one blows at a fire [to kindle it].
Cultural_Context: One should apply one’s best effort to any task.

Source_Text_Yo: Agẹmọ ò ṣé-é jẹ lẹ́nu.
Target_Text_En: The chameleon is not a thing to eat in one’s mouth.
Cultural_Context: Certain propositions are beyond the pale.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgùdà ò jẹ lábẹ̀-ẹ Gẹ̀ẹ́sì.
Target_Text_En: The Catholic missionary is not in the pay of the British administration.
Cultural_Context: An assertion of nondependence on a supposedly higher authority.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà tí kò tó ọmọdé-é rán níṣẹ́ ní ńsọ pé kó bu omi wá ká jọ mu.
Target_Text_En: It is an elder who lacks the authority to send a child on an errand who tells the child to go fetch water so they can drink it together.
Cultural_Context: One who is sure of his or her authority does not need to sweeten orders with incentives.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàbọ́ ò di tẹni
Target_Text_En: A foster child does not become one’s own child.
Cultural_Context: There is nothing like having one’s own.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàbọ́-ọ ṣòkòtò, bí kò fúnni lẹ́sẹ̀ a ṣoni; rẹ́mú-rẹ́mú ni ohun ẹni ḿbáni mu.
Target_Text_En: Borrowed trousers, if they are not too tight around the legs, will be too loose; one’s own things fit one exactly.
Cultural_Context: Borrowed articles are never like one’s own.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàká lèéfí ńgba igbó.
Target_Text_En: It is completely that smoke fills the forest.
Cultural_Context: Whatever is worth doing is worth doing diligently and thoroughly.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàká lẹsẹ̀ ńgba ọ̀nà.
Target_Text_En: It is completely that the feet take over a path.
Cultural_Context: Indulge not in half measures.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbaǹgbá ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀, ó làwo lórí san-san.
Target_Text_En: Despite all difficulties, the animal àgbaǹgbá sprouts prominent horns on its head.
Cultural_Context: Perseverance overcomes all difficulties.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàrá kọ́ ni yó gbèé omi lọ.
Target_Text_En: It is not the flood that will make away with the river.
Cultural_Context: The upstart cannot prevail against the well-established person.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàtán ni gẹ̀gẹ̀ ńgba ọ̀fun.
Target_Text_En: It is completely that goiter takes over the neck.
Cultural_Context: One cannot stop matters from run ning their course.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbẹ̀ gbóko róṣù.
Target_Text_En: A farmer remains on the farm and sees the moon.
Cultural_Context: The conscientious farmer spends long periods on the farm; persistence is the key to success.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbinsínú legbin ńgbin; àkùnsínú lẹkùn ńkùn; hùn hùn hùn ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ ínú ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ ní ńgbé.
Target_Text_En: Groaning internally is how an antelope groans; rumbling internally is how a leopard rumbles; the grunts of a pig stay inside the pig.
Cultural_Context: People may grumble, but they dare not voice their complaints openly.

Source_Text_Yo: Agbójúlógún fi ara-a rẹ̀ fóṣì ta.
Target_Text_En: He-who-places-his-hopes-on-inheritance delivers himself to destitution.
Cultural_Context: One should secure one’s own living.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbólà ni tàgbọ̀nrín; ọjọ́ tí àgbọ̀nrín bá gbó ni ọjọ́ ikú-u rẹ̀ ńyẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Baying-and-surviving is the fate of the deer; whenever a deer bays, on that day its death is averted.
Cultural_Context: Every reverse portends good fortune in the end.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìdúró là ńpè níjó.
Target_Text_En: Not standing still is what is described as dancing.
Cultural_Context: Continuous striving deserves praise, whatever the outcome.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìtó ehín-ín ká ni à ńfọwọ́ bò ó.
Target_Text_En: It is not-having-attained-the-age-for-losing one’s-teeth that makes one cover [the mouth] with one’s hand.
Cultural_Context: One should not be reticient in asserting oneself.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá ilé ó mọdẹ-ẹ́ ṣe.
Target_Text_En: A domesticated dog does not know how to hunt.
Cultural_Context: Pampering kills initiative.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjà kì í jìn mọ́ ológbò lẹ́sẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The snare does not snare a cat’s paw.
Cultural_Context: Some people are immune to certain perils.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá wéré-wéré ní ńpa ikún.
Target_Text_En: It is an agile dog that kills a squirrel.
Cultural_Context: The world belongs to the quick.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá wo ẹyẹ láwòmọ́jú.
Target_Text_En: The dog looks at birds with eyes full of disdain.
Cultural_Context: Against adversaries beyond one’s powers, one must be satisfied with futile gestures.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajé sọ ọmọ nù bí òkò.
Target_Text_En: Wealth throws a person away like a stone.
Cultural_Context: The search for wealth takes one into distant lands.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjẹgbé nigún ńjẹbọ.
Target_Text_En: Eating without adverse effects is the vulture’s way of consuming sacrificial offerings.
Cultural_Context: Some people can engage in daring and dangerous behavior with impunity.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajìnfìn, má ta ojú ilé; ọ̀pọ̀lọ̀ jìnfìn má ta ojú àtijáde.
Target_Text_En: You who have fallen into the dungeon, do not be impatient to arrive home; when the toad drops into a pit, it cannot be impatient to get out.
Cultural_Context: Certain predicaments one does not get out of in a hurry.

Source_Text_Yo: A-jókò-ó-kunkun ò jẹ́ kí a-jókòó-jẹ́jẹ́ ó-jókòo.
Target_Text_En: The sit-tight person denies the tentative sitter a place.
Cultural_Context: The meek will not inherit the earth.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjùmọ̀bí ò kan ti àrùn; kí alápá mú apá-a rẹ̀ kó le.
Target_Text_En: Familial obligations do not extend to diseases; let each person look well to his or her arms.
Cultural_Context: Relatives will not bear your disease for you.

Source_Text_Yo: A-ká-ìgbá-tà-á náwó ikú.
Target_Text_En: He-who-plucks-the-African-locust-bean tree-seeds-to-sell spends death’s money.
Cultural_Context: Whoever engages in a dangerous venture more than earns his or her pay.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkànṣe lọfà ìmàdò; jagan oró ò ran èse.
Target_Text_En: The arrow for a warthog is a major project; an ordinary poison has no effect on the cat.
Cultural_Context: Certain tasks call for deliberate and extraordinary efforts.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkèekèé ní òún kúrò ní kòkòrò-o kí nìyí?
Target_Text_En: Scorpion says that its status transcends what-type-of-insect-is-this?
Cultural_Context: Stature and importance are not always commensurate; some people should not be underestimated.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkèekèé rìn tapó-tapó.
Target_Text_En: The scorpion travels accompanied by venom.
Cultural_Context: The stalwart is never unprepared to answer a call.

Source_Text_Yo: Akíkanjú-kankan, ogun ní ńlọ; abù wàwà, ọjà ní ńná; àkànní òbúkọ, bó bá tòṣì a máa rí jẹ.
Target_Text_En: For the exceptionally brave person the proper profession is warring; for the gregarious person, trading; the illustrious he-goat, even when it is poor, finds enough to eat.
Cultural_Context: Proper application of one’s talent makes one prosper.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkótán ni gẹ̀gẹ̀ ńkó ọ̀fun.
Target_Text_En: It is completely that goiter takes over the throat.
Cultural_Context: Calamities give no quarter.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkùkọ-ọ́ kọ, ọ̀lẹ́ pòṣé.
Target_Text_En: The cock crows, and the lazy person hisses.
Cultural_Context: The coming of the morning is an annoyance to the lazy person.

Source_Text_Yo: Alágẹmọ-ọ́ ti bímọ-ọ rẹ̀ ná; àìmọ̀-ọ̀jó kù sọ́wọ́-ọ rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The chameleon has given birth to its young; inability to dance is the responsibility of the child.
Cultural_Context: A parent has done his or her part by having a child; the child’s fortunes are the child’s responsibility.

Source_Text_Yo: Alágbàró ò yege; aláṣọ á gbà á bó dọ̀la.
Target_Text_En: She who borrows a wrapper skirt to wear is not home free; the owner of the cloth will take it back tomorrow.
Cultural_Context: There is nothing like having one’s own.

Source_Text_Yo: Alákatam̀pò ojú ò lè ta ẹran pa.
Target_Text_En: A person with crossbows in his eyes cannot kill an animal.
Cultural_Context: Even the most vicious of looks cannot kill.

Source_Text_Yo: Aláǹgbá tó já látorí ìrókò tí kò fẹsẹ̀ ṣẹ́, ó ní bẹ́nìkan ò yìn un òun ó yinra òun.
Target_Text_En: The lizard that fell from atop the ìrókò tree without breaking its limbs says if no one admires his feat, he will do the admiring himself.
Cultural_Context: One should be self-confident enough not to need validation by others.

Source_Text_Yo: Alára ní ńgbára-á ga; bádíẹ́ bá máa wọ̀ọ̀dẹ̀ a bẹ̀rẹ̀.
