Target_Text_En: It is the owner of the body that elevates the body; when a chicken wishes to enter the porch, it stoops.
Cultural_Context: One should sound one’s own trumpet and not be unduly humble.

Source_Text_Yo: A-lèjà-má-lè-jà-pẹ́: ẹlẹgbẹ́ ojo.
Target_Text_En: He-who-can-fight-but-cannot-fight-for long: the equal of a coward.
Cultural_Context: Ability to start a fight is nothing like the ability to see it through.

Source_Text_Yo: Àlejò orí ni kókó.
Target_Text_En: The lump is only the head’s visitor.
Cultural_Context: One should learn to live with afflictions.

Source_Text_Yo: Apá lará; ìgbọ̀nwọ́ niyèkan.
Target_Text_En: One’s arms are one’s relatives; one’s elbows are one’s siblings by the same mother.
Cultural_Context: Even more reliable than one’s relatives and siblings are one’s own resources.

Source_Text_Yo: Àpáàdì-í gbóko kò rà.
Target_Text_En: The potsherd lives on the farm but does not decay.
Cultural_Context: Resilience is a fortunate quality to have.

Source_Text_Yo: Àpagbé lOrò ńpagi
Target_Text_En: Killing-without-recourse is Orò’s way of killing trees.
Cultural_Context: When unanswerable disaster befalls a person, there is neither recourse nor response.

Source_Text_Yo: Apárí ní ńfojú di abẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is a bald person who may be disdainful of the razor.
Cultural_Context: The bald person has no use for razors.

Source_Text_Yo: Apẹ́ẹ́jẹ kì í jẹ ìbàjẹ.
Target_Text_En: A person who waits patiently for a long time before eating will not eat unwholesome food.
Cultural_Context: Those who are patient will have the best of things.

Source_Text_Yo: Àpọntán kò wí pé kí odò má sun.
Target_Text_En: Scooping a spring dry does not stop more water from collecting.
Cultural_Context: If one’s resources are limitless, some use will not exhaust them.

Source_Text_Yo: Ara kì í wúwo kí alára má lè gbe.
Target_Text_En: A body cannot be too heavy for the owner to lift.
Cultural_Context: Whatever others might feel, a person is never put off by himself or his own habits.

Source_Text_Yo: Ara-à mí gba òtútù, ó gba ọ̀nini.
Target_Text_En: My body can endure chills and can endure coldness.
Cultural_Context: I am long-suffering.

Source_Text_Yo: Àràbà ńlá fojú di àáké.
Target_Text_En: The huge silk-cotton tree belittles the axe.
Cultural_Context: It takes a mighty person to defy a powerful force.

Source_Text_Yo: Ariwo àjìjà ní ńdọ́run.
Target_Text_En: It is only the noise of the whirlwind that reaches heaven.
Cultural_Context: One’s enemies may be clamorous, but all they are capable of is noise.

Source_Text_Yo: Asúrétete ní ńwojú ọjọ́.
Target_Text_En: It is the person in a hurry who studies the complexion of the day.
Cultural_Context: When one has important tasks at hand, one pays particular attention to impinging conditions.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣá ò gbádìẹ níkọ̀kọ̀; gbangba làṣá ńgbádìẹ.
Target_Text_En: The kite does not snatch chicks in secret; it snatches them openly.
Cultural_Context: What one dare do, one does openly.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣá ò lè balẹ̀ kó gbéwúrẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The kite cannot swoop down and carry off a goat.
Cultural_Context: Whoever attempts the impossible deceives himself or herself.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣá wo ìgbín kọ̀rọ̀; ìkaraun-un rẹ̀ ò jẹ́ kó gbé e.
Target_Text_En: The kite looks slyly at the snail, but its shell stops the bird from snatching it.
Cultural_Context: When the prey’s defenses are impenetrable, the predator can only glare.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣá wọ̀bọ kò rọ́wọ́ gbé e.
Target_Text_En: The kite watches the monkey but has no hands to carry it off.
Cultural_Context: A monkey is no prey to a kite.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣírí ìkokò, ajá k ni yó tùú u.
Target_Text_En: The secrets of the hyena’s being will not be revealed through the actions of the dog.
Cultural_Context: The stalwart’s comeuppance will not happen at the hands of a no-account person.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtẹ́lẹwọ́ ẹni kì í tanni.
Target_Text_En: One’s palm does not deceive one.
Cultural_Context: One’s trust is best placed in one’s own resources.

Source_Text_Yo: Àyè kì í há adìẹ kó má dèé ìdí àba-a rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The space is never so tight that a chicken will not be able to reach its incubating nest.
Cultural_Context: No obstacle should keep one from one’s duty.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá ńpa èpo oṣè, ṣe ní ḿmáaá sanra sí i.
Target_Text_En: The more one peels the bark of the baobab, the fatter it becomes.
Cultural_Context: The more a certain person is misused, the more successful he or she becomes.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá jìyà tó kún agbọ̀n; a ò lè jẹ oore tó kún ahá.
Target_Text_En: If one does not experience enough suffering to fill a basket, one cannot enjoy enough good to fill a cup.
Cultural_Context: Suffering precedes pleasures.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ebí bá ńpa ọ̀lẹ, à jẹ́ kó kú.
Target_Text_En: If a lazy person is suffering from hunger, he or she should be left to die.
Cultural_Context: Shiftless people deserve no sympathy.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ẹnìkan ò kíni ‘‘Kú-ù-jokòó,’’ kíkí Ọlọ́run-ún ju ti igba èèyàn lọ.
Target_Text_En: If a person does not extend greetings to you, God’s greetings are worth more than those of two hundred people.
Cultural_Context: Being snubbed by people matters nothing, as long as God does not snub you.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ẹrú yó bàá jẹ ìfun, ibi ẹ̀dọ̀ ní-í tí ḿbẹ̀rẹ̀
Target_Text_En: A slave that would eat intestines must begin with the liver
Cultural_Context: One must endure unpleasantness before achieveing one's ends.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ẹkẹ́-ẹ tálákà ò tó lówùúrọ̀, á tó lálẹ́.
Target_Text_En: If a poor person’s forked stake is not long enough in the morning, it will be long enough at night.
Cultural_Context: The things one rejects when the choice is abundant will become acceptable when there is no choice.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá ṣe bí ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ lọ́nà Ìkòròdú, a ò lè ṣe bí Adégbọrọ̀ lọ́jà ọba.
Target_Text_En: If one does not act like a pig on the way to Ikòròdú, one cannot act like Adégbọr at the king’s market.
Cultural_Context: Before one can live in luxury, one must soil one’s hands with work.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ẹ̀yá bá dẹkùn, ẹran ní ńpajẹ.
Target_Text_En: When the cub becomes a grown leopard, it kills animals for food.
Cultural_Context: When the child becomes an adult, he adopts adult ways.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ìbí bá tẹ̀, bí ìbí bá wọ́, oníkálukú a máa ṣe baba nílé ara-a rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: If the pedigree is bent, if the pedigree is crooked, each person will play the father in his own home.
Cultural_Context: In difficult times, each per son has the solace and security of his own home.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ilẹ̀-ẹ́ bá mọ́, ojú orun lọ̀lẹ ńwà.
Target_Text_En: When day breaks, the lazy person will still be asleep.
Cultural_Context: Lazy people will not rouse themselves to do an honest day’s work.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí iná kò bá tán láṣọ, ẹ̀jẹ̀ kì í tán léèékánná.
Target_Text_En: If lice are not completely gone from one’s clothing, one’s nails will not be free of blood.
Cultural_Context: If the causes of one’s problems are not removed, the problems will persist.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ìṣẹ́ bá ńṣẹ́ d láṣẹ̀ẹ́jù, kó lọ sígbó erin: bó bá pa erin ìṣẹ́-ẹ rẹ̀ a tán; bí erín bá pá a, ìṣẹ́-ẹ rẹ̀ a tán.
Target_Text_En: If a youth is in the grip of excessive privation, he should go after an elephant: if he kills an elephant, his privation will be over; if an elephant kills him, his privation will be over.
Cultural_Context: People in desperate straits should resort to desperate remedies; whatever the outcome, they will be no worse off than before.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí iwájú ò bá ṣeé lọ sí, ẹ̀hìn a ṣeé padà sí.
Target_Text_En: If one cannot go forward, one will be able to retreat.
Cultural_Context: If a goal proves impossible of achievement, one can at least abandon it.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí màlúù-ú tó màlúù, ọ̀pá kan ni Fúlàní fi ńdà wọ́n.
Target_Text_En: However numerous the cattle might be, it is with only one staff that the Fulbe man herds them.
Cultural_Context: The good worker needs no elaborate tools.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Bí mo lè kú ma kú’’ lọmọkùrín fi ńlágbára; ‘‘Ng ò lè wáá kú’’ lọmọkùnrín fi ńlẹ.‘‘
Target_Text_En: If I must die, let me die’’ is what makes a man strong; ‘‘I simply will not court death’’ is what makes a man lazy or cowardly.
Cultural_Context: Daring makes the man; caution unmakes the man.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ó pẹ́ títí, akólòlò á pe baba.
Target_Text_En: However long it may take, the stammerer will eventually say, ‘‘Father.’’
Cultural_Context: With perseverance, the most difficult task will eventually be accomplished.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ó pẹ́ títí, àlejò á di onílé.
Target_Text_En: In time, a sojourner becomes a native.
Cultural_Context: Persistence leads to success.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ó ti wuni là ńṣe imàle ẹni; bó wu Lèmámù a fẹlẹ́dẹ̀ jẹ sààrì.
Target_Text_En: One practices one’s Islam as one pleases; if the imam wishes, he may break his fast with pork.
Cultural_Context: One lives one’s life as one sees fit.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí Ògún ẹní bá dánilójú, à fi gbárí.
Target_Text_En: If one is sure of one’s Ògún cult object, one taps one’s head with it.
Cultural_Context: If one is sure of one’s position, one confidently swears by anything.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ojú kò pọ́nni bí osùn, a kì í he ohun pupa bí idẹ.
Target_Text_En: If one’s eyes do not become as red as cam wood stain, one does not come by some thing as red as brass.
Cultural_Context: Unless one endures some hardship, one does not reap great benefits.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ojú owó ẹni ò yóni, ènì ò lè yóni.
Target_Text_En: If what one bought for money does not fill one, neither will a little extra thrown into the bargain.
Cultural_Context: A person who cannot survive on his main occupation cannot survive on his sideline.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ojúmọ́ mọ́ lékèélékèé a yalé ẹlẹ́fun, agbe a yalé aláró, àlùkò a yalé olósùn.
Target_Text_En: When day dawns, the cattle egret makes for the home of the dealer in chalk; the blue touraco heads for the home of the indigo dealer; the purple àlúkò bird seeks out the dealer in camwood resin.
Cultural_Context: Diligent people never dally in pursuing their trade.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọwọ́ kò sin ilẹ̀, tí kò sin ẹnu, ayo ní ńjẹ.
Target_Text_En: If the hand does not cease going down and going to the mouth, satiation results.
Cultural_Context: If one keeps at a task, it will eventually be accomplished.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí Ṣàǹgó bá ńpa àràbà, tó ńpa ìrókò, bíi tigi ńlá kọ́.
Target_Text_En: Even though Ṣango kills the silk-cotton tree and kills the ìrókò tree, no such fate can be fall the huge tree.
Cultural_Context: A boast that the person being referred to is mightier than even the mightiest other person around.

Source_Text_Yo: Dàńdógó kì í ṣe ẹ̀wù ọmọdé.
Target_Text_En: Dàńdógo is not a garment for the young.
Cultural_Context: Certain feats are beyond certain people.

Source_Text_Yo: Dídán là ńdán ọ̀ràn wò; bí olówó ẹní kú, à lọ ṣúpó.
Target_Text_En: One should give everything a try; if one’s owner dies, one goes to claim his wife.
Cultural_Context: One should attempt even the impossible.

Source_Text_Yo: Dídán lẹyẹlé ńdán kú
Target_Text_En: A perpetually shining appearance is what characterizes the pigeon even until death.
Cultural_Context: Either an observation that a person’s reputation cannot be tarnished or a wish that it never become tarnished.

Source_Text_Yo: Díẹ̀-díẹ̀ leku ńjawọ.
Target_Text_En: It is bit by bit that rats eat leather.
Cultural_Context: With slow and steady application, even a difficult task will be done.

Source_Text_Yo: Díẹ̀-díẹ̀ lẹyẹ ńmu ọsàn.
Target_Text_En: It is bit by bit that a bird eats an orange.
Cultural_Context: Easy does it.

Source_Text_Yo: Díẹ̀ díẹ̀ ní ńtànṣẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Gradual efforts complete a task.
Cultural_Context: The biggest task is accomplished with gradual and steady attention.

Source_Text_Yo: Ebè kan ṣoṣo àkùrọ́ kúrò ní Mo fẹ́rẹ̀ẹ́ ṣíwọ́.
Target_Text_En: A single heap on the farm does not warrant ‘‘I am just about done.’’
Cultural_Context: The first step is not nearly the completion of a long journey.

Source_Text_Yo: Ebi ni yó kọ̀ọ́ wèrè lọ́gbọ́n.
Target_Text_En: It is hunger that will force sense into the imbecile.
Cultural_Context: Even an imbecile must heed hunger.

Source_Text_Yo: Dùndún fọ̀ràn gbogbo ṣàpamọ́ra.
Target_Text_En: The talking drum endures all matters without complaint.
Cultural_Context: It is best to be stoically resilient.

Source_Text_Yo: Ebí ńpa ejò, ahún ńyan.
Target_Text_En: The snake is hungry, and the tortoise saunters by.
Cultural_Context: If one is invulnerable, one may strut.

Source_Text_Yo: Ebi ò jẹ́ ká pa ọwọ́ mọ́; ebí ṣẹnú papala.
Target_Text_En: Hunger keeps one from folding one’s hands; hunger causes the mouth [or cheeks] to shrink.
Cultural_Context: One must work in order to eat.

Source_Text_Yo: Èdì kì í mú ọjọ́ kó má là.
Target_Text_En: No charm can act upon the day and keep it from dawning.
Cultural_Context: What is inevitable will come to pass, willy-nilly.

Source_Text_Yo: Èébú kì í so.
Target_Text_En: Insults do not attach to one’s body like pods.
Cultural_Context: Insult ignored is insult defused.

Source_Text_Yo: Eégún tí ńjẹ orí ẹṣin, orí àgbò ò lè kò ó láyà.
Target_Text_En: The masquerader who is accustomed to eating horse heads will not be daunted by ram heads.
Cultural_Context: A person who has faced down serious challenges will not be defeated by a slight inconvenience.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèwọ̀ ni tọwọ̀; a kì í figi ọwọ̀ dáná.
Target_Text_En: As far as the broom is concerned, it is taboo; one does not make kindling of broom sticks.
Cultural_Context: Come what may, a threatening or threatened disaster will not happen.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèyàn ìbáà kúrú, ìbáà búrẹ́wà, gbèsè ò sí, ìtìjú ò sí.
Target_Text_En: Whether a person be short or ugly, if there is no debt, there can be no disgrace.
Cultural_Context: As long as one is debt-free, other details of one’s personal circumstances are of little consequence.

Source_Text_Yo: Èkó ilá gba ara ẹ̀ lọ́wọ́ ọ̀bẹ.
Target_Text_En: Okro that has gone fibrous has delivered itself from the knife.
Cultural_Context: At some point, one outgrows some dangers.

Source_Text_Yo: Èminrin ńjẹni, ò tó ìyà.
Target_Text_En: Being bothered by sandflies is no misfortune.
Cultural_Context: Whatever one’s problems, they can always be worse.

Source_Text_Yo: Èpè ìbínú ò pa odì.
Target_Text_En: An angry curse does not kill an enemy.
Cultural_Context: One gets only psychological satisfaction from cursing one’s enemy.

Source_Text_Yo: Èpò ìbúlẹ̀ kì í pa irẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Creeping weeds cannot kill the silk-rubber tree.
Cultural_Context: A puny person is no threat to a mighty person.

Source_Text_Yo: Erín jẹ̀ jẹ̀ jẹ̀ kò fọwọ́ kọ́ aṣá; ẹfọ̀n-ọ́n jẹ̀ jẹ̀ jẹ̀ kò ki ẹsẹ̀ wọ pòòlò; ẹyẹ kékèké ńfò lókè wọn ò forí gbági.
Target_Text_En: The elephant forages a long time without cutting its hand on a spear; the buffalo forages a long time without falling into a trap; numerous small birds fly across the sky without colliding with trees.
Cultural_Context: Despite the ubiquitousness of danger, one can be safe.

Source_Text_Yo: Eṣinṣín ńpọntí; ekòló ńṣú ọ̀lẹ̀lẹ̀; kantí kantí ní ká wá kan dí agbè lẹ́nu kí ǹkankan má kòó sí i.
Target_Text_En: The fly is procuring wine while the worm is cooking bean meal, and the sugar fly asks them to find something to cork the gourd so nothing will enter into it.
Cultural_Context: The idler seeks to find more work for those already fully and usefully employed.

Source_Text_Yo: Eṣú jẹ oko tán eṣú lọ; eṣú lọ Wata, ilé-e rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The locusts are done feeding; the locusts have departed; the locusts have gone to Wata, their home.
Cultural_Context: When one’s task is com pleted, one returns to one’s home. Or, the marauder has done his damage and has gone back where he came from.

Source_Text_Yo: Ewúrẹ́ ńṣọdún; àgùtán gbàlù sẹ́hìn; òbúkọ-ọ́ ní ká sin òun lọ sílé àna òun.
Target_Text_En: The goat is celebrating an event; the sheep is in a procession with drums; and the he goat asks to be accompanied to its in-law’s home.
Cultural_Context: A person who has made no investment should not expect to reap the benefits of the venture.

Source_Text_Yo: Ewúrẹ́ ò lè rí ewé ọdán òkè fi ṣe nǹkan.
Target_Text_En: A goat can in no wise take the fig tree’s leaves aloft for any purpose.
Cultural_Context: Certain people are beyond the reach of othjer people's machination.

Source_Text_Yo: Ewúro ò fi tojo korò.
Target_Text_En: The bitterleaf did not become bitter as a result of cowardice.
Cultural_Context: One does what one must, regardless of the actions or wishes of others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹbọ jíjẹ kì í pa igún.
Target_Text_En: The consumption of sacrificial offerings will not kill the vulture.
Cultural_Context: One cannot be hurt by one’s natural calling.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹgbẹ̀rún eèrà ò lè gbé ṣúgà; wọ́n ó kàn tò yí i ká lásán ni.
Target_Text_En: A thousand ants cannot lift [a cube of ] sugar; they can only mill around it in vain.
Cultural_Context: Some tasks are beyond certain people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ègbèrún ẹja ó lè dẹ́rù pa odò.
Target_Text_En: A thousand fishes will not overload a river.
Cultural_Context: It is futile to attempt to overwhelm an invincible person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹjọ́ ẹlẹ́jọ́, lọ́yà ńrò ó, ámbọ̀ǹtorí ẹjọ́ ara-a rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The lawyer argues other people’s cases, much more his own.
Cultural_Context: One who is conscientious on behalf of others can be expected to be even more conscientious on his or her own behalf.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹlẹmùnún ò mú eégún.
Target_Text_En: An apprehender does not apprehend a masquerader.
Cultural_Context: Certain people are beyond anyone’s control.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀lúlùú ní kàkà kí òun má dun ọbẹ̀, òun á rúnwọ rúnsẹ̀ sí i.
Target_Text_En: The lark-heeled cuckoo vows that rather than not being delicious in the stew, it will crush its arms and legs in pursuit of that end.
Cultural_Context: One vows that even up to the cost of one’s life, one will give everything one has to achieve an end.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá ńjẹ òbúkọ tó gbójú, yó jẹ àgùtàn tó yọ̀ wo.
Target_Text_En: Whoever is used to eating full-grown he-goats will eat lambs that have sprouted horns.
Cultural_Context: A person known for daring deeds can always be expected to defy custom; one cannot cure people of ingrained habits.

Source_Text_Yo: Èní bá ńṣiṣẹ́ kì í ṣọ̀lẹ; bórí bá túnniṣe a kì í tẹ́ bọ̀rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Whoever has a job should not malinger; if Providence smiles, one can hardly fail.
Cultural_Context: Dili gence in one’s pursuit will certainly result in prosperity.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá yẹ ọ̀nà Ìjẹ̀bú tì ni yó yẹ̀ ẹ́ tán.
Target_Text_En: The same person who weeds the road to Ìjẹ̀bú without carrying off the weeds will eventually remove them.
Cultural_Context: The shirker will sooner or later be forced to do his or her duty; one should do a thing efficiently, not halfheartedly.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni èèyàn ò kí kó yọ̀; ẹni Ọlọ́run ò kí kó ṣọ́ra.
Target_Text_En: Whoever is shunned by people should rejoice; whoever is shunned by God should look out.
Cultural_Context: God’s favor is preferable to that of other people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní máa jẹ oyin inú àpáta kìí wo ẹnu àáké.
Target_Text_En: Whoever will eat the honey in a rock does not worry about the edge of the axe.
Cultural_Context: One should be prepared to make the sacrifices necessary to achieve a worthy goal.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní máa jẹun kunkun a tìlẹ̀kùn kun-kun.
Target_Text_En: Whoever wishes to eat heartily must lock his door firmly.
Cultural_Context: To prevent intrusion into one’s affairs, one should keep them well guarded.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní máa rí àtisùn akàn á pẹ́ létí isà.
Target_Text_En: Whoever wishes to see a crab go to sleep will stay long by its hole.
Cultural_Context: Whoever seeks the impossibe will wait forever.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní máa rí àtisùn-un pẹ́pẹ́yẹ á jẹ gbèsè àdín.
Target_Text_En: Whoever wishes to see ducks go to sleep will go into debt paying for [fuel] oil.
Cultural_Context: Whoever awaits the impossible will wait forever.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni ọ̀lẹ́ pá re ọ̀run òṣì; ẹni iṣẹ́ pa-á re run ẹ̀yẹ.
Target_Text_En: Whoever dies from poverty dies a miserable death; whoever dies from work dies a noble death.
Cultural_Context: Better to die on one’s feet than to give in to reverses.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí à ḿbọ́ ò mọ̀ pé ìyàn-án mú.
Target_Text_En: A person fed by others is never aware that there is famine.
Cultural_Context: A person who has no responsibilities does not appreciate the efforts of those who do.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí iṣẹ́ ńpa-á yá ju ẹni tí ìṣẹ́ ńpa.
Target_Text_En: A person dying fom overwork is better than a person dying of destitution.
Cultural_Context: Better to suc cumb to overwork or occupational hazards than to succumb to poverty.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí kíkí-i rẹ̀ ò yóni, àìkí-i rẹ̀ ò lè pani lébi.
Target_Text_En: A person whose greetings do not fill one’s stomach cannot cause one to starve by with holding the greetings.
Cultural_Context: A person whose benevolence has little effect on one’s fortune cannot affect one with malevolence.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ńgbẹ́lẹ̀ ní ńsìnkú; ẹni tí ńsunkún ariwo ló ńpa.
Target_Text_En: The person digging a grave is the one performing his or her funerary duties; the person crying is merely making a noise.
Cultural_Context: Tangible help is better than useless sympathetic gestures.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó bá pẹ́ lẹ́hìn ni à ńyọ́ omi ọbẹ̀ dè.
Target_Text_En: Those who arrive late are the ones who find the watery residue of the stew awaiting them.
Cultural_Context: Timeliness earns one the best choice, tardiness the worst.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó bá wo ojú ìyàwó ní ńmọ̀ pé ìyàwó ńsunkún.
Target_Text_En: Only a person who looks at the bride’s face knows that the bride is crying.
Cultural_Context: It is futile to seek sympathy when no one is paying attention.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó fò sókè-é bẹ́ ijó lórí.
Target_Text_En: Whoever leaps up decapitates dance.
Cultural_Context: Nothing more can be expected from a person who has given the ultimate effort.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó forí sọlẹ̀-ẹ́ gbìyànjú ikú.
Target_Text_En: Whoever dives headfirst to the ground has made a creditable attempt at suicide.
Cultural_Context: One should acknowledge people’s sincere efforts.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó gbálẹ̀ ni ilẹ̀ ḿmọ́ fún.
Target_Text_En: It is for the person who sweeps the floor that the floor is clean.
Cultural_Context: Those who exert themselves are the ones who reap rewards

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ọ̀ṣọ́ bá wù kó ṣòwò; ẹni ajé yalé-e rẹ̀ ló gbọ́n.
Target_Text_En: Whoever likes fineries should engage in a trade; it is the person blessed by riches who is wise.
Cultural_Context: Good things come only to the industrious.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní yára lÒgún ńgbè
Target_Text_En: Ògún is on the side of the swift.
Cultural_Context: The swift are justified in taking advantage of the tardy.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnú dùn-ún ròf ; agada ọwọ́ dùn-ún ṣánko.
Target_Text_En: The mouth cooks vegetable stew most expertly; the hand emulating a machete cuts a field most effortlessly.
Cultural_Context: A person's mouth may boast of anything, and his or her hand may claim to be able to do anything until put to the test.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu iṣẹ́ ẹni ni a ti ḿmọ ẹni lọ́lẹ́.
Target_Text_En: It is at one’s occupation that one proves oneself an idler.
Cultural_Context: One reveals one’s mettle at one’s place of employment.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu òfìfo kì í dún yànmù-yànmù.
Target_Text_En: Empty mouths do not make chewing noises.
Cultural_Context: If one has not filled others’ mouths with food, one cannot expect them to be full of one’s praise.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀rù kì í ba igbó, bẹ́ẹ̀ni kì í ba odò; ẹ̀rù kì í ba ọlọ lójú ata.
Target_Text_En: The forest knows no fear, and neither does the river know fear; the grindstone never shows fear in the face of pepper.
Cultural_Context: A worthy person should not give way to fear.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀rù kì í ba orí kó sá wọnú.
Target_Text_En: The head is never so frightened that it disappears into the shoulder.
Cultural_Context: One should be brave enough to meet one’s fate.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀rù ogun kì í ba jagun-jagun.
Target_Text_En: Fear of battle never afflicts a warrior.
Cultural_Context: One should be bold in pursuing one’s goals.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹsẹ̀ kì í wúwo kí ẹlésẹ̀ má lè gbé e.
Target_Text_En: The feet are never so heavy that the owner cannot lift them.
Cultural_Context: Each person must live with his or her own peculiarities.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹṣin kì í dani kí á má tún gùn ún.
Target_Text_En: Do not refrain from mounting a horse that has thrown you.
Cultural_Context: A failure should not stop you from making further attempts.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹṣin kì í já kó já èkejì-i rẹ̀
Target_Text_En: A horse does not get loose and stop to free its companion.
Cultural_Context: Each person must look to his or her own salvation.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀sọ̀ ẹ̀sọ̀ ni ìgbín fi ńgbà gun igi.
Target_Text_En: Slowly, slowly is the way a snail climbs a tree.
Cultural_Context: With dogged persistence, one accomplishes the most difficult of tasks.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀tẹ́ bá ọ̀lẹ.
Target_Text_En: Disgrace comes upon the shiftless.
Cultural_Context: Disgrace attends shiftlessness.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹyẹ ò sọ fún ẹyẹ pé òkò ḿbọ̀
Target_Text_En: A bird does not tell a bird that a stone is on its way.
Cultural_Context: Each person looks out for his or her own safety.

Source_Text_Yo: Fi gọ̀gọ̀ sílẹ̀ fún ọ̀dáwé; fi ọkọ sílẹ̀ fún onílara.
Target_Text_En: Leave the hooked stick alone for the leaf plucker; leave the husband alone for the jealous woman.
Cultural_Context: One should simply shun persons who will not share what they have.

Source_Text_Yo: Fífẹ́ la fẹ́ ẹ̀fọ́ tí à ńpè-é ní ọ̀rẹ́ ẹ̀kọ; ti ilé ogè-é tó ogè-é jẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is only because one loves spinach that one calls it a friend of corn loaf; what the dandy has at home is enough food for him or her.
Cultural_Context: That one delights in another person’s company is not to say that one cannot do without it.

Source_Text_Yo: "Fọ ẹ̀kọ ká jọ mu ú," kò tó ọkọlóbínrin-ín ṣe ni.
Target_Text_En: "Prepare the corn pap and let us eat it together" is an indication that the speaker lacks what it takes to be a husband.
Cultural_Context: One should not be tentative in exercising one’s authority.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbẹ́dó-gbẹ́dó kan ò lè fi ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ ṣe nǹkan.
Target_Text_En: No carver of mortars can do a thing to the banana stem. I
Cultural_Context: Certain people and certain objects have nothing to fear from certain types of adversaries.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbẹ̀rù ejò ó jẹkà tẹ ọmọ ejò mọ́lẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Fear of the snake keeps one from stepping on the young of the snake.
Cultural_Context: One usually benefits from the stature or position of one’s parents or protector.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi tí a ní kí gbégbé má gbèé, ib ní ńgbé.
Target_Text_En: The spot one cautions the gbégbé plant not to inhabit, there it will surely inhabit.
Cultural_Context: One will fulfill one’s destiny, whatever others might do to prevent it.

Source_Text_Yo: Idà kì í lọ kídà má bọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The sword never departs without returning.
Cultural_Context: Said in the context of a prayer that a person departing on a journey might return safely.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìdẹra ò kan àgbà.
Target_Text_En: Ease has nothing to do with age.
Cultural_Context: Industry pays off more surely than longevity.

Source_Text_Yo: Igi kì í dá lóko kó pa ará ilé.
Target_Text_En: A tree does not snap in the forest and kill a person at home.
Cultural_Context: Disaster cannot befall a person who is not in an exposed position.

Source_Text_Yo: Igúnnugún pa guuru mádìẹ; kò leè gbe.
Target_Text_En: The vulture rushes at the chicken, but it cannot carry it off.
Cultural_Context: One should not attempt what one knows one cannot accomplish.

Source_Text_Yo: Igba ẹranko kì í dènà de ẹkùn.
Target_Text_En: Two hundred animals will not lie in ambush for a leopard.
Cultural_Context: Exercise prudence and recognize an adversary that is more than your match.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbà yí làárọ̀? Arúgbó ńkọgba.
Target_Text_En: Is it just morning now? The old man is striv ing to make two hundred heaps a day.
Cultural_Context: The efforts that would have been commendable if timely are now worthless.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbà yí làárọ̀? Arúgbó ńṣoge.
Target_Text_En: Is it just morning now? The old person is grooming himself or herself.
Cultural_Context: Never wait until it is too late before you look to your well-being.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbé a gbé ìyàwó kò ṣéé gbé owó.
Target_Text_En: The strategy one adopts in acquiring a wife will not do with regard to money.
Cultural_Context: What suffices in one situation may not be applicable in another.

Source_Text_Yo: Igbe kí-ni-ngó-jẹ-sùn ní ḿpọ̀lẹ.
Target_Text_En: The cry ‘‘What shall I eat for supper?’’ is what kills the lazy person.
Cultural_Context: The lazy person would rather put effort into lamenting his or her fate than into gainful employment.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbín kì í tẹnu mọ́gi kó má gùn ún.
Target_Text_En: The snail will not fasten onto a tree and fail to climb it.
Cultural_Context: Once one takes on a job, one should see it through.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbín kọ mímì ejò.
Target_Text_En: The snail rejects the fate of being swallowed by a snake.
Cultural_Context: There are some perils to which one is immune.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìjà ò mọ ẹ̀gbọ́n, ó sọ àbúrò dakin.
Target_Text_En: Fighting knows not who is the elder; it makes a hero of the younger.
Cultural_Context: In certain situations, prowess is more important than age.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìje òun oore ní mú ọmọ siṣẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Competition and reward are the inducements for a child to work hard.
Cultural_Context: It is the wish to at least keep up with others or the hope for a reward that makes one work hard.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìjẹkújẹ kì í pa ahanrandi.
Target_Text_En: Careless eating does not kill the worm ahanrandi.
Cultural_Context: One can do what one pleases without fear of repercussion.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikán ò lè rí ṣe lára ìgànná.
Target_Text_En: The termite can have no adverse effect on a wall.
Cultural_Context: Certain things are invulnerable to certain disasters.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikọ̀ tí ò mọ iṣẹ́-ẹ́ jẹ́ nÍ ńjẹ́ ẹ lẹ́ẹ̀mejèe.
Target_Text_En: It is the messenger who does not know how to deliver a message properly that delivers it seven times over.
Cultural_Context: Incompetence imposes additional burdens on a person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkòkò tí yó jẹ ata, ìdí ẹ̀ á gbóná.
Target_Text_En: The pot that wishes to eat pepper [stew] will first endure scalded bottoms.
Cultural_Context: Good things come only after great labor or suffering.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilá kì í ga ju akórè lọ kó má tẹ̀ ẹ́ ká.
Target_Text_En: The okro plant is never so much taller than the harvester that he or she cannot bend it to harvest.
Cultural_Context: The conscientious worker will always find the means to complete the task.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé tí a tó lọ sùn lọ́sàn-án, a kì í tó òru lọ sùn ún.
Target_Text_En: A house one has the right to sleep in during the day, one does not wait for the cover of night to go sleep in it.
Cultural_Context: One should not be coy about doing what one has the right to do.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé tí a tóó kun, a kì í bo ìtùfù-u rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: A house one is in a position to burn, one does not conceal the torch to set it ablaze.
Cultural_Context: One need not be coy in doing what one has the authority or standing to do.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ò yí olè lójú.
Target_Text_En: Frogs’ eggs do not attract the attention of the thief.
Cultural_Context: If one has nothing for others to covet, one is safe from envy.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìlẹ̀kẹ̀-ẹ́ gbé orí àtẹ wú ọ̀lẹ.
Target_Text_En: Beads remain on the display tray and from there attract the admiration of the feckless person.
Cultural_Context: The feckless person can admire desirable things but will not have the means to purchase them.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìlérí adìẹ, asán ni lójú àwòdì.
Target_Text_En: The chicken’s boasts are unavailing before the kite.
Cultural_Context: The puny person who threatens a formidable person fools himself or herself.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìlọrin ò lóòṣà; ẹnu lòòṣà Ìlọrin
Target_Text_En: The Ìlórin person has no god; his or her mouth is his or her god.
Cultural_Context: The person under reference is all mouth and no substance.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìmúmúnàá abìdí sembé-sembé; ìmúmú nàá ò dáná rí, tiná-tiná ní ḿbá kiri.
Target_Text_En: Firefly with its rear ablaze: the firefly has never kindled a fire but carries fire with it wherever it goes.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who want results without making any effort.

Source_Text_Yo: Iná kì í jó kí ògiri sá.
Target_Text_En: Fire does not rage and cause a wall to flee.
Cultural_Context: Certain entities are invulnerable to certain dangers.

Source_Text_Yo: Iná kì í jó kó wọlé akàn.
Target_Text_En: A fire does not rage and enter the home of the crab.
Cultural_Context: An incantatory observation invoking immunity for a person from some danger.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìpa à ńpoṣè ara ló fi ńsan.
Target_Text_En: Our attempt to kill the oṣè tree only makes it fatter.
Cultural_Context: Some people prosper in spite of their enemies’ machinations.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìpẹ̀ta lọṣẹ àpọ́n.
Target_Text_En: The sap of the violet tree is what the bache lor uses for soap.
Cultural_Context: A person who lacks the means to provide properly for himself or herself must be resourceful at making do.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìpilẹ̀ ọrọ̀-ọ́ lẹ́gbín.
Target_Text_En: The beginning of wealth is chock-full of filth.
Cultural_Context: Success comes after great effort and much headache.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìpọ́njú lọmọdé fi ńkọ́Fá, ìgbẹ̀hìn-in rẹ̀ a dẹni.
Target_Text_En: A child’s learning of Ifá is full of privations, but the outcome is a life of ease.
Cultural_Context: The ease that comes in the end makes up for the effort to achieve one's goal.

Source_Text_Yo: Ire tí ọwọ́-ọ̀ mi ò tó, ma fi gọ̀gọ̀ fà á.
Target_Text_En: The good my hand cannot reach, I will pull down with a hooked stick.
Cultural_Context: I will spare no effort in pursuit of my goals.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìríkúrìí kì í fọ́ ojú.
Target_Text_En: Evil sights do not make the eyes go blind.
Cultural_Context: There is nothing in the offing that one cannot withstand.

Source_Text_Yo: Irínwó ẹfọ̀n, ẹgbẹ̀rin ìwo; ogún-un Fúlàní, ójì-i bàtà: Ògídíolú ò wẹ̀hìn tó fi lé Adalo lùgbẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Four hundred buffaloes with eight hundred horns; twenty Fulbe men and forty shoes: Ògídíolú did not look back until he had chased Adalo into the bush.
Cultural_Context: Comment on aformidable man who does not flinch before any enemy.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìròjú baba ọ̀lẹ.
Target_Text_En: Shirking work [is the] father of laziness.
Cultural_Context: The person who will not work is worse than a lazy person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìrókò o-nígun-mẹ́rìn-dín-lógún ò tó erin-ín gbémì, áḿbọ̀ǹtorí ìtóò a-lára-bóró bóró
Cultural_Context: A person not defeated by a formidable obstacle will certainly not be stopped by a minor irritant.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìrònú ìkokò ní yó pa ajá.
Target_Text_En: Worrying about the wolf is what will kill the dog.
Cultural_Context: Some people are already vanquished by the mere anticipation of a struggle.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìrọ́jú ni ohun gbogbo; ojoojúmọ́ ní ńrẹni.
Target_Text_En: Perseverance is everything; one gets tired daily.
Cultural_Context: One should not fold up in the face of the first trial.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìsàlẹ̀ ọrọ̀ l'ẹ́gbín.
Target_Text_En: The dregs of wealth are filthy.
Cultural_Context: Wealth comes only after one has endured a great deal of rubbish.

Source_Text_Yo: Isán ḿbọ́jú, ìtàlá ńwẹsẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Nine days wash the face, thirteen days wash the feet.
Cultural_Context: Said of a person who takes an eternity to do simple things.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣẹ́ kí í ṣe ohun àmúṣeré; ìyà kì í ṣe ohun àmúṣàwàdà.
Target_Text_En: Destitution is not something to treat with levity; mysery is nothing to joke about.
Cultural_Context: One should not trifle with one’s problems.

Source_Text_Yo: Iṣẹ́ loògùn ìṣẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Work is the antidote for destitution.
Cultural_Context: One must work in order to better one’s condition.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣẹ́ ní òun ó kòówó; ìyà-á ní òun ó sìngbà; réderède-é ní òun ó ṣe onígbọ̀wọ́: ta ní jẹ́ rere nínú-u wọn?
Target_Text_En: Destitution proposes to trade its services for money; suffering proposes to pawn itself for money; wretchedness proposes to stand surety for them: which of them has anything going for it?
Cultural_Context: In a community of losers no one person can be expected to turn the situation around.

Source_Text_Yo: Iṣẹ́ ajé le, ó tó ọpa.
Target_Text_En: Gainful employment is tough, as tough as a supple pole.
Cultural_Context: Gainful work is not easy.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣẹ́ ńṣẹ́ ọ ò ńrojú; ta ni yó fùn-ún ọ ni oògùn-un rẹ̀?
Target_Text_En: Destitution grips you and you sit scowling; who will give you the antidote?
Cultural_Context: One should take practical steps to solve one’s problem rather than sit around moping.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣẹ́ ò gbẹ́kún, ebí jàre ọ̀lẹ.
Target_Text_En: Destitution does not yield to tears; hunger has a claim on the shiftless.
Cultural_Context: One does not end destitution by simple lamentation; whoever does not work is a fair victim to hunger.

Source_Text_Yo: Iṣẹ́ ọ̀gẹrọ̀ lọ̀lẹ́; kò jẹ́ wá iṣẹ́ agbára.
Target_Text_En: The lazy person knows how to do only things that call for little effort; he or she never seeks out work that demands strength.
Cultural_Context: Said of those who always look for the easiest way out of a dilemma.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣẹ́ tó ṣẹ́ ọmọ lógún ọdún, ìyà tó jẹ ọmọ lọ́gbọ̀n oṣù, bí kò pa ọmọ, a sÍ lẹ́hìn ọmọ.
Target_Text_En: The poverty that has plagued a child for twenty years, the suffering that has been the fate of a child for thirty months, if it does not kill the child should leave the child in peace.
Cultural_Context: Perseverance puts an eventual end to all suffering.

Source_Text_Yo: Iṣẹ́-ajé-ò-gbé-bòjì, ọmọ ẹ̀ Òjíkùtù.
Target_Text_En: Gainful-work-does-not-keep-to-the-shade; his or her child is named First-up-at-dawn.
Cultural_Context: Success in life calls for self-sacrifice.

Source_Text_Yo: Iṣu àtẹnumọ́ kì í jóná; ọ̀kà àtẹnumọ́ kì í mẹrẹ; àwòdì kì í gbé adìẹ à-tẹnu-kunkun-mọ́.
Target_Text_En: The yam one does not stop speaking about will not get burned; the corn meal one speaks constantly about does not become too well done; a chicken that is the subject of constant caution does not get snatched up by a hawk.
Cultural_Context: Anything that is the subject of constant attention will not be ruined.

Source_Text_Yo: Iṣu ẹni kì í fini pe ọmọdé kó má ta.
Target_Text_En: One’s yam will not, because one is only a youth, refuse to grow to maturity.
Cultural_Context: Even a youth can accomplish much if he or she makes an effort.

Source_Text_Yo: Iṣú wà lọ́wọ́ ẹ; ọ̀bẹ́ wà lọ́wọ́ ẹ.
Target_Text_En: The yam is in your hand, and the knife is in your hand.
Cultural_Context: Said to encourage one to do what he or she has to do without further delay, especially when all requisite conditions have been met.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìwà ọ̀lẹ ḿba ọ̀lẹ lẹ́rù; ọ̀lẹ́ pàdánù, ó ní aráyé ò fẹ́ràn òun.
Target_Text_En: The lazy person’s character fills him or her with fear; the lazy person loses all and complains that the world hates him or her.
Cultural_Context: Each person is more the architect of his or her own fortune than the victim of others’ machinations.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìwòyí èṣí ewùrà-a baba-à mí ti ta: ìrègún rere ò sí ní bẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: By this time last year my father’s water-yam had grown huge’’: that is nothing good to reminisce about.
Cultural_Context: One should look to the present instead of dwelling on past achievements, and others’ at that.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyà tó ńjẹ ọ̀lẹ ò kéré: a-lápá-má-ṣiṣẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The malaise that afflicts the lazy person is not trifling: [it is] one-who-has-arms-that-will-not-work.
Cultural_Context: Laziness is a great affliction.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyànjú là ńgbà; bí a ò gbìyànjú, bí lẹ là ńrí; ojoojúm ní ńrẹni.
Target_Text_En: One simply makes an effort; if one does not make an effort one seems like a shiftless person; one copes with weariness daily.
Cultural_Context: In spite of weariness, one must still make a decent effort at one’s calling.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyáwọ́, ìyásẹ̀ lajá fi ńpa ehoro; wàrà wàrà lẹkùn ńgùn.
Target_Text_En: Nimble hands and nimble feet make it possible for a dog to kill a rabbit; the leopard attacks its prey with lightning speed.
Cultural_Context: One should be brisk about what one has to do.

Source_Text_Yo: Jagajìgì ò mọ ogun; ogun ńpa elégbèje àdó.
Target_Text_En: Loading the body down with charms has no effect in a war; war kills even the per son carrying 1,400 juju gourdlets. K
Cultural_Context: One should trust in one’s arms rather than in one’s charms.

Source_Text_Yo: Kàkà kí ilẹ̀ kú, ṣíṣá ni yó ṣàá.
Target_Text_En: Rather than die, the earth will only become bare.
Cultural_Context: One may be inconvenienced by one’s enemies’ machinations, but one will not be destroyed by them.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí á gbé ọkọ́ so sájà ká pète imẹ́lẹ́, ojúgun-ún yó tán ó fíkùn sẹ́hín.
Target_Text_En: Hiding the hoe in the loft and contriving to shirk work, the shin ate its fill and developed a stomach at its back.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who shirk work but eagerly partake of the rewards.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí á ránni níṣẹ́ ò tó ká mọ̀ ọ́ jọ́.
Target_Text_En: To be sent on an errand is nothing compared to knowing how to carry it out.
Cultural_Context: The good servant is the one who can perform his or her tasks well.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí a re odò ká sùn; kí ni ará ilé yó mu?
Target_Text_En: If we go to the river and sleep there, what will the people left at home drink?
Cultural_Context: We must not fail those who depend on us.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí á tó bí ọmọdé, ẹnìkan là ḿbá ṣeré.
Target_Text_En: Before the child was born, one had someone as a playmate.
Cultural_Context: Message to someone that before he or she came around, one got along rather well and would do so again if that person were to disappear from the scene.

Source_Text_Yo: Kì í kan ẹni ká yẹrí.
Target_Text_En: When a duty is one’s turn, one does not duck it.
Cultural_Context: One must step up and carry out one’s responsibility when the time comes.

Source_Text_Yo: Kì í rẹ òòrẹ̀ kó rẹ sinsin ìdí ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The porcupine may tire, but never the quills at its rear.
Cultural_Context: One can never be so tired that one will leave oneself defenseless.

Source_Text_Yo: Kì í tán nígbá osùn ká má rìí fi pa ọmọ lára.
Target_Text_En: The calabash of camwood is never so empty that one does not find enough in it to rub on a baby.
Cultural_Context: One may lack many things but never the means to fulfill one’s obligations.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí ni eégún ńwò tí kò fi òwúrọ̀ jó?
Target_Text_En: What was the masquerader looking at that he did not take advantage of the morning to dance?
Cultural_Context: One should not dawdle but rather do things at the mosyt opportune moment

Source_Text_Yo: Kí ní ḿbẹ nínú isà tí yó ba òkú lẹ́rù.
Target_Text_En: What is there in the grave to frighten a corpse?
Cultural_Context: There is nothing in the offing that one cannot cope with.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí ni ọmọ ẹyẹ ó ṣe fún ìyá ẹ̀ ju pé kó dàgbà kó fò lọ?
Target_Text_En: What will a nestling do for its mother other than become mature and fly away?
Cultural_Context: People who are powerless to help one cannot hurt one by witholding their support.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí òyìnbó tó dé la ti ńwọ aṣọ.
Target_Text_En: Long before the white man came, we were wearing clothes.
Cultural_Context: One got along pretty well before a certain person came on the scene.

Source_Text_Yo: Kíkú ajá, ng kò ní omitooro ẹ̀-ẹ́ lá; àìkú ẹ̀ ng kò ní pè é rán níṣẹ́.
Target_Text_En: When the dog dies, I will not lick the stew made with it; alive, I will not send it on an errand.
Cultural_Context: One has absolutely no use for the person at whom the proverb is directed.

Source_Text_Yo: Kìnìún ò níí ṣàgbákò ẹkùn.
Target_Text_En: A lion does not face peril from a leopard.
Cultural_Context: The stronger person has nothing to fear from the weaker.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò ka ikú, àdàbà sùú-sùú tí ńj láàrin àṣá.
Target_Text_En: It fears not death, the pigeon that forages among hawks.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who habitually court danger.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí alápatà tí ńpa igún.
Target_Text_En: There is no butcher who slaughters the vulture for sale.
Cultural_Context: Certain actions are forbidden. Or, one is beyond the power of one’s enemies.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí bí igbó ṣe lè ta kókó tó, erin óò kọjá.
Target_Text_En: No matter how knotty the bush might be, the elephant will find a way through it.
Cultural_Context: No obstacle can stop a resourceful and formi dable person.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí èrè nínú-u ‘‘Gba owó kà.’’
Target_Text_En: There is no profit in ‘‘Take this money and count it [for me].’’
Cultural_Context: One cannot depend on profiting from others’ industry.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ewu lóko, àfi gìrì àparò.
Target_Text_En: There is no danger on the farm except for the sudden noise of partridges taking to the air.
Cultural_Context: An incantatory wish that all dangers will stay well away from oneself or some subject of one’s wishes.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ẹni tí Ọlọ́run ò ṣe fún, àfi ẹni tó bá ní tòun ò tó.
Target_Text_En: There is no one to whom God has not been generous, only those who will say he has not been generous enough.
Cultural_Context: Everyone has something to be thankful for.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ibi tí kò gba ọ̀gọ̀; ọ̀lẹ layé ò gbà.
Target_Text_En: There is no place where a fool is not welcome; the world rejects only shiftless people.
Cultural_Context: People may be foolish, but they had better not be shiftless.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ibi tí ọwọ́-ọ̀jà erin ò tó.
Target_Text_En: There is no place an elephant’s trunk cannot reach.
Cultural_Context: There is no place beyond a person’s reach or influence.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ikú tí kò rọ adìẹ lọ́rùn
Target_Text_En: There is no manner of death that is inconvenient for the chicken.
Cultural_Context: One is game for whatever propositions another might make.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ohun tí ńti òkè bọ̀ tí ilẹ̀ ò gbà.
Target_Text_En: There is nothing dropping from above that the earth cannot withstand.
Cultural_Context: There is no eventuality that one cannot cope with.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí oúnjẹ tí ḿmú ara lókun bí èyí tí a jẹ sẹ́nu ẹni lọ.
Target_Text_En: There is no food that nourishes one’s body like what one puts in one’s own mouth.
Cultural_Context: The only thing one can be sure of is what one has in one’s possession.

Source_Text_Yo: Kùtù-kùtù kì í jíni lẹ́ẹ̀méjì; kùtù-kùtù ní ńjẹ́ òwúrọ̀;; biri ní ńjẹ́ álẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Early dawn does not wake one twice; early dawn is the morning; deep darkness is night.
Cultural_Context: The morning comes only once; whoever wastes it will discover too late that night has fallen.

Source_Text_Yo: Labẹ́-labẹ́ ò bá tìjà wá odò; kanna kánná ò bá ti ẹ̀kọ wá oko.
Target_Text_En: The labẹ́-labẹ́ plant did not come to the river looking for a fight; the crow did not come to the farm in search of corn gruel.
Cultural_Context: One may be minding one’s business when one is provoked but should nevertheless be prepared to respond.

Source_Text_Yo: Labẹ́-labẹ́ ò bẹ̀rù ìjà.
Target_Text_En: The labẹ́-labẹ́ plant is not afraid of a fight.
Cultural_Context: One is prepared for whatever trouble might come one's way.

Source_Text_Yo: Lékèélékèé gbàràdá, ó gba tẹlòmíràn mọ.
Target_Text_En: The cattle egret borrows wonders to per form and performs enough for itself and others.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who have done far more than anyone expected of them.

Source_Text_Yo: Lójú-lójú là ńwo ẹni tí a óò kéwì fún.
Target_Text_En: It is directly in the eyes that one looks at the subject of the praise poem one is performing.
Cultural_Context: One should squarely face the person with whom one has business.

Source_Text_Yo: "Má kọjá mi Olùgbàlà" kì í ṣe orin àkúnlẹ̀kọ.
Target_Text_En: "Pass me not by, dear Redeemer" is not a song one sings on one’s knees.
Cultural_Context: The Redeemer helps only those who make an effort on their own behalf.

Source_Text_Yo: Máà gbíyè lógún; ti ọwọ́ ẹni ní ńtóni.
Target_Text_En: Place not your hopes in inheritance; the product of one's hand labor is what sustains one.
Cultural_Context: Whoever trusts in inheritance courts disasater.

Source_Text_Yo: Ní teere, ní tèèrè, Ṣàngó ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀ ó jó wọjà.
Target_Text_En: Erratically, with almost imperceptible forward movement, just so Ṣango danced until he was at the market.
Cultural_Context: If unimpeded or unattended to, a seemingly negligible development will eventually assume proportions one cannot ignore.

Source_Text_Yo: Màrìwò ò wí fúnra wọn tẹ́lẹ̀ tí wọ́n fi ńyọ.
Target_Text_En: Palm fronds do not consult with one another before they sprout.
Cultural_Context: Each person is responsible for his or her own decisions.

Source_Text_Yo: Màrìwò ò wojú ẹnìkan, àfi Ọlọ́run.
Target_Text_En: Palm fronds look up to no one except God.
Cultural_Context: One’s trust is in God only.

Source_Text_Yo: Mo di arúgbó ọdẹ tí ńtu olú, mo di àgbàlagbà ọdẹ tí ńwa ògò gò láàtàn; mo di ògbólógbòó akítì tí ńgba ìbọn lọ́wọ́ ọdẹ.
Target_Text_En: I have become an aged hunter reduced to gathering mushrooms; I have become an old hunter good only for digging palm weevils; I have become an aged monkey that snatches the gun from the hunter’s grip.
Cultural_Context: A helpless person pushed to the wall will somehow find the means to put up a fight.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Mo kúgbé’’ lehoro ńdún lóko; ‘‘Mo mówó rá’’ làparò ńdún lábà-a bàbà.
Target_Text_En: ‘‘I have perished!’’ is the cry of the hare in the bush; ‘‘I have destroyed things worth a lot of money!’’ is the cry of the partridge in the guinea-corn field.
Cultural_Context: A worthless person can also be counted upon to destroy things of value.

Source_Text_Yo: Mo ṣe é tán ló níyì; a kì í dúpẹ́ aláṣekù.
Target_Text_En: ‘I have completed the job’’ is what deserves praise; one does not thank people who leave a job only half done.
Cultural_Context: Whatever one embarks upon, one should see it through.

Source_Text_Yo: Múlele múlèle: ilá tí ò mú lele ò léè so; ikàn tí ò mú lele ò léè wẹ̀wù ẹ̀jẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: High potency upon high potency: the okro that lacks high potency cannot fruit; the bitter tomato that lacks high potency cannot achieve the blood-red complexion.
Cultural_Context: Sharpness is a requisite quality for success.

Source_Text_Yo: Ngó lọ, ngó lọ! Lòbìnrín fi ńdẹ́rù ba ọkùnrin; "Bóo lè lọ o lọ" lòkùnrín fi ńdẹ́rù ba obìnrin.
Target_Text_En: If you have a mind to leave, go ahead and leave!’’ is the retort a man throws at a woman.
Cultural_Context: Every person in a relationship has something he or she can hold over the others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ní inú ẹ̀gún, ní inú-u gọ̀gọ̀, ọmọ ayò a ṣara bòró.
Target_Text_En: In the midst of thorns, in the midst of crooked twigs, the ayò seeds remain smooth.
Cultural_Context: A person who will thrive will do so in spite of adversities.

Source_Text_Yo: Ní inú òfÍÌ àti ọ̀láà, ọmọ páńdọ̀rọ̀ ńgbó.
Target_Text_En: Despite being blown hither and thither in the gale, the fruits of the sausage tree survive to maturity.
Cultural_Context: Some people will thrive despite adversities.

Source_Text_Yo: Ní inú òwú la ti ḿbù ṣènì òwú.
Target_Text_En: It is out of one’s stock of cotton that one takes some for makeweight.
Cultural_Context: It is to one’s treasury that one resorts for investments to build the treasury further.

Source_Text_Yo: Ní ọjọ́ eré nìyà ńdun ọ̀lẹ; kàkà kó wọlé kó jáde a fọwọ́ rọ igi, a pòṣé ṣàrà.
Target_Text_En: It is on the day of festivities that the lazy person is miserable; instead of going inside his room and emerging again [in other words, fetching gifts for the revelers], he leans his arms against a tree and hisses incessantly.
Cultural_Context: Shiftless people eventually reap the disgrace of their laziness when they are unable to do what is socially expected of them.

Source_Text_Yo: Ò báà kúrú, ò báà párí, gbèsè ò sí, ẹ̀sín ò sí; onígbèsè ló lè fini ṣẹ̀sín.
Target_Text_En: One may be diminutive, and one may be bald, but without debt one has not earned ridicule; only one’s creditor has grounds to poke fun.
Cultural_Context: However much one might be devoid of accomplishments, as long as one stays out of debt, one’s dignity is intact.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó gbọ́ tiyán sògìrì mọ́dìí; ó gbọ́ toko sọ àdá nù.
Target_Text_En: On hearing about pounded yam he girded himself with cooked melon seeds for stew seasoning; on hearing about farm work he threw his cutlass away.
Cultural_Context: The lazy person will eagerly heedthe summons to eat but not to work.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó di ọjọ́ tí àkàrà ìyá kùtà ká tó mọ ọmọ tó lè jẹ̀kọ.
Target_Text_En: It is only on the day when the mother’s bean fritters do not sell that one knows which child can consume large quantities of corn meal.
Cultural_Context: One knows the good worker not at the time of boasting but when there is work to be done.

Source_Text_Yo: O kò gun ẹṣin lọ́sàn-án, o ò gun èèyàn lóru, o ò du n kan kàrà-kàrà; báwo lo ṣe lè ní káyé má fọ̀ọ́?
Target_Text_En: You do not ride a horse by day; you do not ride people by night; and you do not make great exertions to achieve any goal. How could you have a say in saving the world from disaster?
Cultural_Context: A person who makes no effort cannot affect human affairs.

Source_Text_Yo: O kò ṣá igi lọ́gbẹ́, o o ò sọ ògùrọ̀ lọ́fà, o dédìí ọ̀pẹ o gbẹ́nu sókè ò ńrẹtí; ọ̀fẹ́ ní ńro?
Target_Text_En: You did not slash the trunk with a cutlass; you did not shoot an arrow at the top of the palm-wine-producing palm tree; you come to the foot of the palm tree and raise your open mouth. Does it drip all by itself ?
Cultural_Context: Said of people who expect to reap benefits where they have not made any effort.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Ó kù díẹ̀ kí nwí’’: ojo ní ńsọni da.
Target_Text_En: ‘I was just on the verge of speaking my mind’’: it only makes one into a coward.
Cultural_Context: One should either engage or refrain from making excuses.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó ní ibi tí ó ńdé, itọ́-dídámì nínú ààwẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It goes some way [in assuaging hunger], saliva swallowing during a fast.
Cultural_Context: Every little effort helps.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó pa obì, ó yọ abidún-un rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: He split the kola-nut pod open and also removed the bad among the seeds.
Cultural_Context: Said of a person who has fulfilled an obligation to the utmost.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrin tẹ́ẹ́rẹ́ yẹ ọkọ ẹ̀ níjọ́ ijó, obìnrin tí gídÌgbá yẹ ọkọ ẹ̀ níjọ́ èbù; bó bá ru ọgọ́rùn-ún èbù tán a kó kébé-kébé níwájú ọkọ.
Target_Text_En: A slender woman is the joy of her husband on a day of dancing, but a hefty woman is her husband’s joy on the day of yams quartered for planting; after she has toted a hundred yam pieces, she walks smartly [toward the farm] ahead of her husband.
Cultural_Context: Good looks are not all that make a good wife.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrin tí yó fẹ̀ẹ́ alágbára, ọkàn kan ní ḿmú.
Target_Text_En: A woman who would marry a formidable man must have an unwavering mind.
Cultural_Context: Once one has made a decision on an important matter, one should remain resolute.

Source_Text_Yo: Òbúrẹ́wà ẹni, tòrìṣà ni; àìràṣọlò, tolúwarẹ̀ ni.
Target_Text_En: A person’s ugliness is the god’s doing; the person’s lack of clothing is his or her own fault.
Cultural_Context: One must take responsibility for some conditions, but cannot be blamed for others.

Source_Text_Yo: Odídẹrẹ́ kì í kú sóko ìwájẹ.
Target_Text_En: The parrot never dies in the grazing field.
Cultural_Context: A prayer that just as the parrot always returns home from grazing, the subject of the prayer will return safely from a business venture away from home.

Source_Text_Yo: Odò kì í kún bo ẹja lójú.
Target_Text_En: A river does not so swell as to be over the head of the fish.
Cultural_Context: A statement that an adversary at his most powerful can never pose a threat.

Source_Text_Yo: Odò tí a bá mọ orísun ẹ̀ kì í gbéni lọ.
Target_Text_En: A river whose source one knows does not carry one away.
Cultural_Context: A person whose beginning one knows cannot pose a great threat.

Source_Text_Yo: Odó tó bá tojú ẹni kún kì í gbéni lọ
Target_Text_En: A river that swells in one’s presence does not carry one away.
Cultural_Context: A danger that one sees in the making can be avoided.

Source_Text_Yo: Ogun kì í rí ẹ̀hìn ogun.
Target_Text_En: An army does not see the rear of an(other) army.
Cultural_Context: One should face one’s adversary squarely.

Source_Text_Yo: Ogún ọdún tí ebí ti ńpa ọ̀gà, ìrìn-in fàájì ó padà lẹ́sẹ̀-ẹ rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: In all the twenty years that the chameleon has been in the throes of hunger, its dignified gait has not deserted it.
Cultural_Context: The dignified person never allows himself or herself to be ruffled by adversity.

Source_Text_Yo: Ògbógbó àwọ̀n ní ḿbi ajáko.
Target_Text_En: It is a mighty net that can trip the civet cat.
Cultural_Context: It takes extraordinary efforts or capabilities to accomplish extraordinary tasks.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun kan ladìẹ ńjẹ kágbàdo tó dé.
Target_Text_En: The chicken had something to eat before there was corn.
Cultural_Context: A statement that one does not depend on somebody else since one survived before his or her arrival

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí a bá gbìn la ó kàá.
Target_Text_En: What one plants is what one reaps.
Cultural_Context: Every action has its proper reward.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí a bá gbín sẹ́hÌn la ó padà bá.
Target_Text_En: Whatever one sows behind one is what one will return to find.
Cultural_Context: One reaps whatever one sows.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí a fún ẹ̀ṣọ́ ṣọ́ ni ẹ̀ṣọ́ ńṣọ́.
Target_Text_En: Whatever one hands to a warrior to look after is what he looks after.
Cultural_Context: One should concentrate on the duty entrusted to one.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun títán lọdún eégún.
Target_Text_En: The annual egúngún festival is not endless.
Cultural_Context: Every condition ends sometime.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó ṣe ìjímèrè tó fi gungi ẹ̀gẹ̀, bí kò bá rí ohun tó jù bẹ́ẹ̀l ọ kò ní sọ̀kalẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Whatever it was that sent the brown monkey climbing to the top of the thorny acacia tree, unless it sees something even more terrifying, it will not climb down.
Cultural_Context: It takes a threatened catastrophe to make one look kindly on minor inconveniences.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó ṣe ìwọ̀fà tí kò fi wá sóko olówó, bójú bá kan ojú yó sọ fún olówó-o rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Whatever caused the pawned worker to stay away from the creditor’s farm, when the two come face to face, he or she will have some explaining to do.
Cultural_Context: Whoever shirks his or her duty will eventually have to explain why.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjìji ò bẹ̀rù ọ̀fìn.
Target_Text_En: The shadow has no fear of the gully.
Cultural_Context: One has no need to fear a harmless adversary.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjìjí ṣe lẹ́gẹ́-lẹ́gẹ́ má wòó.
Target_Text_En: The shadow lacks substance but it never crashes.
Cultural_Context: Apparent fragility may mask real resilience.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò ìbá rọ̀, kí ladẹ́tẹ̀ ìbá gbìn? Ọwọ́ adẹ́tẹ̀ ò ká ẹyọ àgbàdo mẹ́wàá.
Target_Text_En: Were it to rain, what would the leper have planted? A leper’s palm cannot scoop ten grains of corn.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who blame their deficiencies on flaws in Nature.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjó jìyà gbé; alágbára-á bú u, ó gun àjà; a tọ̀ ọ́.
Target_Text_En: Òjó is victimized without recourse; a bully insults him, he goes to hide in the rafters, and his nemesis follows him there.
Cultural_Context: Said of poeple who are powerless to stop being victimized.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò pamí, òjò pa ère-è mi; òjò ò pa ẹwà ara-à mi dànù.
Target_Text_En: The rain may beat me, and the rain may beat my statue; the rain cannot wash away my good looks.
Cultural_Context: Adversity will not get the better of me.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjòjò ọ̀lẹ ò tán bọ̀rọ̀, ọ̀lẹ́ bà á tì ó dáná orí.
Target_Text_En: A lazy person’s illness is not soon over; the lazy person finds no way out and prepares a fire to warm his head.
Cultural_Context: A lazy person will use every excuse to avoid any obligation, and when he cannot avoid it, his fulfillment of it is always pitiable.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò-ó pa odídẹ àlùkò ńyọ̀, àlùkò-ó rò pé ìkó bàjẹ́; òjó mú ìkó wọṣọ.
Target_Text_En: Rain beats the parrot and the touraco re joices, thinking that the parrot’s tail feather is ruined; the rain only makes the tail feather brighter.
Cultural_Context: The occurrence one’s adversaries hoped would destroy one only improved one’s fortunes.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò-ó pọnmi fún ọ̀lẹ, kò ṣẹ́gi fún ọ̀lẹ.
Target_Text_En: The rain provides water for the lazy person, but it does not fetch firewood for the lazy person.
Cultural_Context: Parasites can have only so much done for them, never everything.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú abaníjẹ́ pọ́n, kò lè tan fítílà.
Target_Text_En: The detractor’s eyes glow red, but they cannot light a lamp.
Cultural_Context: A detractor’s slanderous efforts are in vain.

Source_Text_Yo: "Ojú àna-à mi ò sunwọ̀n"; kò ju kó gba ọmọ ẹ̀ lọ.
Target_Text_En: "The look on my parent-in-law’s face is baleful"; the worst he or she can do is take his or her daughter back.
Cultural_Context: There is a limit to which a benefactor’s withdrawal of his or her beneficence can hurt one.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í pọ́n iṣin ká má bàá wóró nínú ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The Akee apple is never so blighted that one does not find a seed in it.
Cultural_Context: Whatever befalls, one will be left with some residual property.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í pọ́n iṣin kó má là.
Target_Text_En: The Akee apple is never so blighted that it does not eventually split open.
Cultural_Context: Whatever misfortune might befall, one would be able to do those things that are second nature.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú là ńrọ́; ògó ṣòro-ó ṣe.
Target_Text_En: One only tries one’s best; heroic deeds do not come easy.
Cultural_Context: One’s best is enough.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú lakàn-án fi ńṣọ́ orí.
Target_Text_En: The crab watches after its head with its eyes.
Cultural_Context: One should have one’s eyes open to protect one’s interests.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú mẹ́wàá kò jọ ojú ẹni.
Target_Text_En: Ten eyes are not like one’s own.
Cultural_Context: Seeing something oneself is far better than hearing a report of it from ten people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú olójú kì í gba ọ̀ràn fúnni wò.
Target_Text_En: Other people’s eyes will not look after matters for you.
Cultural_Context: No one else will take care of your affairs.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú olójú ò jọ ojú ẹni; a-ṣọ̀ràn-deni ò wọ́pọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Other people’s eyes are nothing like one’s own; minders of other people’s business are few.
Cultural_Context: No one can look after one’s affairs as one would oneself.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú pọ́n koko má fọ̀ọ́; ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ pọ́n koko má rọ̀; ọ̀rán fini dùgbẹ̀-dùgbẹ̀ yunni nù; ọ̀ràn tí ńfinni ò leè pani.
Target_Text_En: The eyes go red but do not go blind; the banana goes brilliant yellow but does not rot; a problem rattles one to the foundations and lets one go; a problem that rattles one will not kill one.
Cultural_Context: Every problem soon comes to an end in time.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú rẹ̀gbin kò fọ́, a-jọ̀-pọ̀-Ìyà-má-rù.
Target_Text_En: The eye looks on a filthy sight and does not go blind, [like] one who sustains a succession of sufferings without wasting away.
Cultural_Context: With resilience one will overcome all problems.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú ti kókó, ojú ti eéwo; ojú ti aáràgbá ìdí pẹ̀lú.
Target_Text_En: The lump that attacks the head is shamed, the boil is shamed, and the hardened tissue on the buttocks is shamed also.
Cultural_Context: An assertion of defiance in the face of adversity.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú tó ti rókun ò níí rọ́sà kó bẹ́rù.
Target_Text_En: The eyes that have seen the ocean will not tremble at the sight of the lagoon.
Cultural_Context: Once one has survived a grave peril, small incon veniences will not be unduly impressive.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojúmọ́ kì í mọ́ kí ọwọ́ má yùn-ún ẹnu.
Target_Text_En: Never a day dawns that the hand does not make a trip to the mouth.
Cultural_Context: Certain obligations are unavoidable.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkè lẹyẹ ńfọhùn.
Target_Text_En: It is from aloft that the bird sounds off.
Cultural_Context: It is time for one to rise up.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkè méjì kì í bínú ẹni; bí a bá gun ọ̀kan, à sì máa rọ ọ̀kan.
Target_Text_En: One cannot be bedeviled by two hills; if one ascends a hill, one descends a hill.
Cultural_Context: Every hill one must climb has a descent on the other side.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojúoró ní ńlékè omi; òṣíbàtà ní ńlékè odò.
Target_Text_En: The water lettuce always winds up on the surface of the water; the waterlily always winds up on the surface of the stream.
Cultural_Context: Just as those plants remain on top of their habitats, so one will remain triumphant over one’s adversaries.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkìkí ajá kì í pa oṣù
Target_Text_En: A dog’s howling will not kill the moon.
Cultural_Context: The threats of ineffectual enemies amount to nothing.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkìkí ò poṣù; ariwo ò pagún; ibi ẹ rí ẹ kíbòsí-ì mi lọ.
Target_Text_En: Being widely reputed does not kill the moon; being noised about does not kill the vulture; wherever you please, make a noise about me.
Cultural_Context: A statement that one is not bothered by people who spread stories about one.

Source_Text_Yo: Oko etílé ladìẹ́ lè rò.
Target_Text_En: The chicken is good at cultivating only the soil close by the home.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who boast when in the safety of their rooms but can do nothing once outside.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkò kan igi; Òkò padà sẹ́hìn kí o rebi o ti wá.
Target_Text_En: Stone, hit a tree; stone, retrace your steps and return to whence you came.
Cultural_Context: Something of an incantation to send evil wishes back toward those who sent them.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkú ò moye à ńràgọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The corpse does not know the cost of the shroud.
Cultural_Context: The person who does not have to pay the bills does not care how expensive the things he wastes are.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkú ọ̀lẹ ó ní pósí.
Target_Text_En: A lazy person’s corpse does not merit a coffin.
Cultural_Context: One does not receive in death a treatment one’s life has not earned. Or, one reaps what one sows.

Source_Text_Yo: Olójú kì í fojú sílẹ̀ kí tàlùbọ́ kó wọ̀ ọ́.
Target_Text_En: The owner of the eyes will not neglect them and watch foreign matter lodge in them.
Cultural_Context: One does not simply look on as one’s interests are jeopardized.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó kì í fi owó ẹ̀ fún abòṣì na.
Target_Text_En: The rich person will not give his or her money to a poor person to spend.
Cultural_Context: Generosity has its limits.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó mọ òwò.
Target_Text_En: The rich person is an expert at trading.
Cultural_Context: Success comes from expertise.

Source_Text_Yo: Omi adágún ò lè gbé màlúù lọ
Target_Text_En: A stagnant pool cannot carry off a cow.
Cultural_Context: Some adverse situations are annoyances only and pose no danger.

Source_Text_Yo: Omi ló dànù, agbè ò fọ́.
Target_Text_En: It is the water that is spilled; the water gourd is not broken.
Cultural_Context: A proverb usually used to console parents who have lost a child: the child is likened to the water, and the mother to the vessel.

Source_Text_Yo: Omi ḿbẹ látọ́.
Target_Text_En: There is water in the long-necked calabash.
Cultural_Context: One has resources that others may not know about.

Source_Text_Yo: Olúmọ Ẹ̀gbá ò ṣéé gbé.
Target_Text_En: The Olúmọ of the Ẹ̀gbá territory is impossible to carry.
Cultural_Context: Some tasks are absolutely impossible.

Source_Text_Yo: Omi ṣẹ́lẹ̀rú ò mu akèrègbè.
Target_Text_En: The water from a new spring will not cover a gourd to the top.
Cultural_Context: An upstart cannot defeat a veteran.

Source_Text_Yo: Omí wọ́ yanrìn gbẹrẹrẹ, bẹ́ẹ̀ni omi ò lọ́wọ́, omi ò lẹ́sẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Water drags the sand about, and yet water lacks hands and lacks legs.
Cultural_Context: One may not have a great deal but can nevertheless perform wonders.

Source_Text_Yo: Oní ló ḿmọ, ìjà ọ̀lẹ.
Target_Text_En: It will all end sometime today’’: a lazy person’s motto in a fight.
Cultural_Context: The idler or shirker forced to perform some task is always eager for the day’s end.

Source_Text_Yo: Oníbàjẹ́ ó lódó; ẹnu gbogbo lodó-o wọn.
Target_Text_En: Detractors of others have no pestles; their mouths are their pestles.
Cultural_Context: Detractors have no weapons other thanb their mouths.

Source_Text_Yo: Oníbànà ní ńtjú òrobó; onídẹ ní ńtọ́jú awẹde.
Target_Text_En: It is he who has copper ornaments who must procure oranges; whoever has brass ornaments must procure the herb awẹdẹ.
Cultural_Context: Each person must see to procuring whatever he or she needs.

Source_Text_Yo: Onígbèsè èèyàn-án ti kú; a ò tÍÌ sìnkú ẹ̀ ni.
Target_Text_En: The habitual debtor is already dead, except that he has not yet been buried.
Cultural_Context: Someone always in debt is no better than a dead person.

Source_Text_Yo: OníṢàngó ò mẹni tí òún ńwà lóògì dànù.
Target_Text_En: The Ṣango worshiper knows not whose ground corn he is spilling.
Cultural_Context: One does not care who is affected by one’s actions.

Source_Text_Yo: Oníṣe kì í fìṣe ẹ̀ sílẹ̀ re ibi; ó ńre àjò ó mú ìṣe ẹ̀ lọ́wọ́ gírígírí.
Target_Text_En: The owner of a habit will not go on a journey and leave his habit at home; when he goes, he takes his habit along with him.
Cultural_Context: One cannot escape from one’s character.

Source_Text_Yo: Oníṣòwó wà lóòrùn; náwónáwó wà níbòji.
Target_Text_En: The person who does the trading is in the sun; the person who spends the money is in the shade.
Cultural_Context: A criticism of people who ex pend no effort but take advantage of other people’s exertions.

Source_Text_Yo: Oníṣú fiṣu ẹ se ẹ̀bẹ; ojú ti atèèpojẹ.
Target_Text_En: The owner of the yams makes yam pottage out of the yams; the person who eats the yam scrapings off the peels is shamed.
Cultural_Context: The parasite is shamed when the host finds a way to shut him out.

Source_Text_Yo: Oògùn kì í gbé inú àdó jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: A magical charm does not work from within its gourdlet.
Cultural_Context: One cannot expect any benefit from one’s resources without deploying them.

Source_Text_Yo: Oòrùn ò kan àtàrí, ọwọ́ ò dá.
Target_Text_En: The sun has not risen directly above the head; working hands cannot cease their toil.
Cultural_Context: The day is for working.

Source_Text_Yo: Oòrùn ò pa ọ́, òjò ò pa ọ́, o ní ò ńṣiṣẹ́ ajé.
Target_Text_En: The sun does not beat you; the rain does not beat you; yet you say you are engaged in a gainful pursuit.
Cultural_Context: Profitable labor is seldom pleasurable.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí adẹ́tù ńpète àrán; orí adáràn-án ńpète àtijọba.
Target_Text_En: The head that wears a cloth cap strives to wear a velvet cap; the one that wears a velvet cap strives to become a king.
Cultural_Context: Everyone hopes for a better tomorrow.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí iṣẹ́ laago ńkú lé.
Target_Text_En: It is while at work that a clock dies.
Cultural_Context: A vow never to stop working until death.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí kì í tóbi kólórí má lè gbé e.
Target_Text_En: A head is never so heavy that the owner cannot carry it.
Cultural_Context: One should always be capable of taking care of one’s affairs.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí ńlá kì í pá tán.
Target_Text_En: A huge head does not go completely bald.
Cultural_Context: The more one has in abundance, the more cushion one has against reverses.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí olórí kì í báni gbẹ́rù.
Target_Text_En: Other people’s heads will not carry one’s load.
Cultural_Context: Each person must bear his own burden.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrìṣà tí ńgbọ̀lẹ ò sí; apá ẹni ní ńgbeni.
Target_Text_En: No god comes to the aid of shiftless people; only their arms aid them.
Cultural_Context: One’s well-being is in the muscular strength of one’s arms.

Source_Text_Yo: Òru ni ìnàhìn àgbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Nighttime is a farmer’s time to stretch the back.
Cultural_Context: As long as the day lasts, there will be work to do.

Source_Text_Yo: Òṣìṣẹ́ lọ̀tá ọ̀lẹ.
Target_Text_En: The industrious person is the enemy of the shiftless person.
Cultural_Context: People with flaws hate those who might show them up.

Source_Text_Yo: Òṣìṣẹ́ wà lóòrùn; ẹní máa jẹ́ wà níbòji.
Target_Text_En: The laborer is in the sun; the person who will reap the fruit is in the shade.
Cultural_Context: Quite often those who do the work are not the ones who gain the benefits of the labor.

Source_Text_Yo: Òwò àdá kì í pa àdá; òwò ọkọ́ kì í yọ ọkọ́ lẹ́nu.
Target_Text_En: A machete’s trade does not kill the machete; a hoe’s trade does not cause problems for the hoe.
Cultural_Context: A person’s forte does not constitute a problem for him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó ò mọ ẹ̀gbọ́n, ó sọ àbúrò dàgbà.
Target_Text_En: Wealth does not know who is the elder; it makes a senior of the younger person.
Cultural_Context: Suc cess does not depend on age or maturity.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó ò níran àfi ẹni tí kò bá ṣiṣẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Money has no lineage, except for the person who will not work.
Cultural_Context: Money does not restrict itself to certain families; only the shiftless are shunned by money.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó olówó leégún ńná.
Target_Text_En: Other people’s money is what the masquerader spends.
Cultural_Context: The parasitic person always relies on other people’s largesse.

Source_Text_Yo: Òwò tí a bá máa ṣe àṣelà, a kì í rí àpá lára ẹni.
Target_Text_En: The trade that one will pursue and that will make one prosper does not leave scars.
Cultural_Context: A pursuit that is destined to make one prosperous will not cause unbearable hardship.

Source_Text_Yo: Òwò tí a fowó rà, owó la fi ńpa.
Target_Text_En: Merchandise that one buys with money, one earns money for.
Cultural_Context: One does not give away merchandise for which one paid money.

Source_Text_Yo: Òwò tí a ó ṣe là ńtọ́jú; Òjí fabẹ họra.
Target_Text_En: The trade one will pursue is the one one protects; Òjí scratches his body with a razor.
Cultural_Context: The gadgets people favor give away their trade.

Source_Text_Yo: Òyìnbó baba ọ̀nájà; ajé baba téní-téní.
Target_Text_En: The white man is the past master of trading; money is the guarantee of fashionableness.
Cultural_Context: Without money one cannot be fashionable.

Source_Text_Yo: Òyìnbó ta ọjà ta orúkọ; Ègún tajà ta èdìdì.
Target_Text_En: The white man sells merchandise with the name brand still attached; the Ègún person sells cloth still in its bundle.
Cultural_Context: One deals with matters wholesale, as it were, not retail.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọba tó fi iyùn bọlẹ̀, ọba tó wú u, àwọn méjèèjì la ó máa sọ orúkọ-ọ wọn.
Target_Text_En: The king who buries coral beads, the king who digs them up: both will have their names remembered by posterity.
Cultural_Context: Whoever performs an unprecedented feat, whatever it might be, will be remembered by posterity.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọba tó sọ ẹgàn di erùfù, ọba tó sọ erùfù dẹgàn: àwọn méjèèjì la ó máa sọ orúkọ-ọ wọn.
Target_Text_En: The king who turned a forest into a sandy plain, the king who turned a sandy plain into a forest: both their names will be re membered by posterity.
Cultural_Context: Whoever performs a great feat will be remembered.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọbẹ̀ tó dùn, owó ló pa á.
Target_Text_En: A delicious stew was procured with money.
Cultural_Context: Nothing good happens without money.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọbẹ̀-ẹ́ tutù tán, a dawọ́ bù ú lá.
Target_Text_En: The stew having cooled, one hollows one’s palm to eat it.
Cultural_Context: When the back of a difficult task has been broken, people are eager to tackle it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀dájú ló bí owó; ìtìjú ló bí gbèsè.
Target_Text_En: It is brazenness that gives birth to wealth; it is excessive reticence that gives birth to poverty.
Cultural_Context: Nothing succeeds without some audaciousness.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọdọọdún làgbẹ̀ ńníyì.
Target_Text_En: It is every year that the farmer receives praise.
Cultural_Context: Statement or prayer that some person will receive perennial praise, just as the annual harvest brings praise to the farmer.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọdúnnìí ọdẹ́ pa erin; ẹ̀ẹ̀míràn ọdẹ́ pa ẹfúọ̀, ọdún mẹ́fà ọdẹ́ p òló; ọlá ńrewájú, tàbí ọlá ńrẹ̀hìn?
Target_Text_En: This year the hunter kills an elephant; the next year the hunter kills a buffalo; two years hence the hunter kills a grass mouse: is his glory increasing or decreasing?
Cultural_Context: One should always strive for greater accomplishments, not lesser.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ dúdú ò ṣéé bùṣán; ọmọ burúkú ò ṣéé lù pa.
Target_Text_En: An unripe plaintain is not something to eat; a useless child is not something to beat to death.
Cultural_Context: Certain problems one simply has to live with.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjà tí a fowó rà, owó la fi ńpa.
Target_Text_En: One makes money from goods one purchased with money.
Cultural_Context: Do not make gifts of commodities purchased for trade.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀-jẹ-wọ̀mù wọ̀mù-kú-wọ̀mù wọ̀mù lorúkọ tí àpà ńjẹ́.
Target_Text_En: One-who-eats-recklessly-and-dies-recklessly is the name one calls a wonderful person.
Cultural_Context: Wasteful people will never learn the value of things.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọgbọ́n òyìnbó ti ojú òkun là wá; aṣọ kí ni ó borí akẹsẹ?
Target_Text_En: The white man’s wisdom shines even across the seas; what cloth, though, is better than akẹsẹ cloth?
Cultural_Context: Despite the appeal of foreign goods, local wares are preferable.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ a bá kọ́ ọ̀lẹ là ńkọ́ inú rírọ́.
Target_Text_En: The day one learns laziness is the day one should learn how to endure a painfully empty stomach.
Cultural_Context: The lazy person should not expect to be fed by others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ a bá rí ìbí nìbí ńwọlẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The day one sees the afterbirth is the day it enters the earth.
Cultural_Context: Once one perceives a threat, one can deal decisively with it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ eré lọ̀ràn ńdun ọ̀lẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is on the day of relaxation that the lazy person experiences regret.
Cultural_Context: People who did not save for a rainy day will be sorry when those who did save enjoy the benefits of their foresight.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ tí a dóko là ńjìjà ilẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The day one gets to the farm is the day one fights over boundaries.
Cultural_Context: Do not procrastinate.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ tí a ńkọ́ṣẹ́ là ńkọ́ ìyára.
Target_Text_En: The day one learns a trade is the day one learns to be quick at it.
Cultural_Context: Whatever one does should be done thoroughly and expertly.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlẹ́ bà á tì, ó kó sílé Ifá.
Target_Text_En: The lazy person fails at everything, whereupon he becomes an Ifá acolyte.
Cultural_Context: The lazy person finds easy tasks to do.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀lẹ, baba àrùn.
Target_Text_En: Laziness, father of all diseases.
Cultural_Context: Laziness is worse than any disease.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀lẹ èèyàn ò rí ayé wá.
Target_Text_En: A lazy person has found no world to come to.
Cultural_Context: The lot of a lazy person in this world is misery.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀lẹ fẹ́ àrùn kù, ó bú pùrù sẹ́kún.
Target_Text_En: [If] the lazy person cannot find a disease to contract, he bursts into tears.
Cultural_Context: A lazy person would rather catch a disease than submit to work.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀lẹ fi ọ̀ràn gbogbo ṣe "hòo."
Target_Text_En: The lazy person replies ‘‘yes’’ to all propositions.
Cultural_Context: You will get no argument from a lazy person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀lẹ́ jogún ìbànújẹ́, ó ní òún jogún ìran òun.
Target_Text_En: The lazy person inherits unhappiness; he says he has inherited the fate of his lineage.
Cultural_Context: The lazy person has himself to blame, not his destiny.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀lẹ́ jogún ìbáwí.
Target_Text_En: The lazy person inherits recriminations.
