Cultural_Context: The lazy person is a tempting scapegoat.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀lẹ́ kákò,, ó di òjòjò.
Target_Text_En: The lazy person curls up, and his condition becomes a serious ailment.
Cultural_Context: The simplest tasks become impossible undertakings for the lazy person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀lẹ́ kún àárẹ̀ lọ́wọ́.
Target_Text_En: Laziness lends weariness a hand.
Cultural_Context: Laziness is often a contributor to weariness.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀lẹ́ mọ èèwọ̀ ìjà: ó ní bàbá òún ní kóun má jà lọ́nà oko.
Target_Text_En: The coward knows the preventive for fighting: he says his father has ordered him not to fight on the way to the farm.
Cultural_Context: The coward will use every excuse to get out of a fight.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀lẹ́ ní ọjọ́ tí ikú bá pa òun, inú òhun á dùn. Ikú ní òun ó jẹ̀ẹ́ kí ojú ẹ̀ rí màbo.
Target_Text_En: The lazy person says on the day he dies, he will be happy. Death says he will visit him [the lazy person] with suffering that is out of this world.
Cultural_Context: There is no way for the lazy person to avoid suffering.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀lẹ́ ní ọjọ́ tí òún bá kú òun ó yọ̀; ohun tí ojú ọ̀lẹ́ máa rí kó tó kú ńkọ́?
Target_Text_En: The coward says he will rejoice on the day he dies, but what about the woes he will experience before he dies?
Cultural_Context: Death may offer the coward a respite, but he will suffer before death comes.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀lẹ́ ò yẹẹ́ nì lọ́mọ.
Target_Text_En: A lazy person is not something one wants as a child.
Cultural_Context: Who wants a lazy child?

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀lẹ́ wáṣẹ́ rírọ̀ ṣe.
Target_Text_En: The lazy person seeks out an easy task to do.
Cultural_Context: Trust the lazy person to find the easiest tasks.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlọgbọ́n kì í kú sóko ọ̀lẹ; bí ọlọgbọ́n bá kú sóko ọ̀lẹ, ọ̀ràn náà-á nídìí.
Target_Text_En: The wise will not die on a farm for the lazy; if a wise person dies on a farm for the lazy, there must be some explanation.
Cultural_Context: The resourceful person will always find a way out of a predicament.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlọ́mú dá ọmú ìyá ẹ̀ gbé.
Target_Text_En: Each child must lift its mother’s breast by itself.
Cultural_Context: Every person to his or her own resources.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlọ́run yó pèsè; kì í ṣe bí èsè oríta.
Target_Text_En: The Lord will give alms, but not the sort one comes upon at crossroads.
Cultural_Context: One wishes for good gifts from God, not just any sort of leavings.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ tí yó jẹ̀ẹ́ àṣàmú, kékeré ní ńtií ṣẹnu ṣámú-ṣámú
Target_Text_En: A person who will become exemplary begins showing precociousness from childhood.
Cultural_Context: Childhood shows the adult.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ tó káwọ́ sókè ló fẹ́ ká gbé òun.
Target_Text_En: It is the child who raises its arms that induces people to lift it.
Cultural_Context: If you want people to come to your aid, first lift a finger on your own behalf.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ tó ṣípá fúnni là ńgbé jó.
Target_Text_En: It is the child who lifts its arms that one picks up and dances with.
Cultural_Context: One makes friends with people who offer friendship.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọdé ò mọ ibi tí à ńpọn òun rè.
Target_Text_En: A child does not know where the person who carries it on her back is headed.
Cultural_Context: People who depend on others do not know what those others have in mind for them.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀mu ní ńgbé ọ̀mu mì.
Target_Text_En: It is drunkenness that swallows [or drowns] a champion drinker.
Cultural_Context: Only an intrepid contestant can match another intrepid contestant.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀nà kì í dí mọ́ aládàá.
Target_Text_En: The path does not close on a man carrying a machete.
Cultural_Context: No problem is insoluble for a resourceful person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn búburú kì í bá ikún nílé.
Target_Text_En: An evil event never finds the squirrel at home.
Cultural_Context: A statement that one will never be around when disaster occurs.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn fini dùgbẹ̀-dùgbẹ̀ yinni nù; ọ̀ràn fini dùgbẹ̀-dùgbẹ̀ bí ẹnipé kò ní í tán; ọ̀ràn ṣe wá tán; ojú á tẹlẹ́gàn, a sì ti ẹni tí ńyọnusọ.
Target_Text_En: A problem shakes one up vigorously and lets one go; a problem shakes one up vigorously as though it will never end; the trouble will end, deflating the ill wishers and also those who will not mind their own business.
Cultural_Context: However terrible one’s problems, they will cease and leave one in better shape than one’s enemies would like.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọrùn kì í wọ òṣùká; ẹlẹ́rù lọrùn ńwọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The pad placed on the head to soften the friction of the load on the head does not suffer from the weight; the person carrying the load is the one whose neck suffers under the weight.
Cultural_Context: Commiserators and people lending a hand do not suffer the troubled person’s pain; the troubled person is the one who bears it all.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọwọ́ atẹ́gùn ò ká gẹdú.
Target_Text_En: The wind is no match for timber.
Cultural_Context: Even powerful forces come up against objects they cannot move.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọwọ́ ẹni la fi ńtú ìwà ara ẹni ṣe.
Target_Text_En: One’s own hands are what one uses to mend one’s fortune.
Cultural_Context: Each person’s fortune is in his or her own hands.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọwọ́ ẹni ni yó yòóni.
Target_Text_En: One hands are what feed one to satiation.
Cultural_Context: Your hands are your best resources.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọwọ́ ní ńtún ara ṣe.
Target_Text_En: The hands are the agents for grooming the body.
Cultural_Context: One’s well-being is in one’s hands.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọwọ́ tó dilẹ̀ là ńfi lérán.
Target_Text_En: It is on an idle hand that one rests one’s chin.
Cultural_Context: It is when one has nothing to do that one engages in mischief.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọyẹ́ ni yó kìlọ̀ fún onítòbí.
Target_Text_En: It is the harmattan that will teach the person who has only a loincloth a lesson.
Cultural_Context: People who do not provide for the rainy day will pay when the storm does come.

Source_Text_Yo: Pa á ní ńjẹ́ ọgbẹ́, tiiri ní ńjẹ ọfà; bí a bá ta á ṣe là ńwá a; bí a ò bá wá a a dẹran Ìdin.
Target_Text_En: A sharp report is what accompanies a machete wound; a flying motion is the characteristic of an arrow; if you hit your prey, you should go in search of it; if not, it becomes meat for maggots.
Cultural_Context: Always follow through in your pursuits.

Source_Text_Yo: Páńdọ̀rọ́-ọ́ já, ará rọ ìyá ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The fruit of the sausage tree drops, [and] its mother knows relief.
Cultural_Context: Relief is sweet after one’s burden has been lifted.

Source_Text_Yo: Pà-pà lójú lẹ́ẹ̀kínní, pà-pà lójú lẹ́ẹ̀kejì: bójú náà ó bá fọ́, bàì-bàì ní ńdà.
Target_Text_En: A blow to the eye the first time and a blow to the eye a second time: if the eye does not go blind, it will see only dimly.
Cultural_Context: Continual attacks will eventually leave their mark on the victim.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣàngó ò lè pa igi ńlá.
Target_Text_En: Ṣango cannot destroy a huge tree.
Cultural_Context: The substantial and well-established peron is better able to withstand adversity than weaklings.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣe kóo ní; àbá ò di tẹni; èèyàn ò ṣoògùn ọrọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Work in order to have; intentions do not be come possessions; no one makes money by magic.
Cultural_Context: Labor, not idle thought, produces wealth.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣiṣe-é rorò, jíjẹ ọ̀fẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Working is difficult; one would rather free load.
Cultural_Context: Few people enjoy labor; all would like to live the good life for free.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣòkòtò gbọọrọ ò dọlà; abíni lÉkòó ò dowó.
Target_Text_En: Long trousers do not amount to wealth; being born in Lagos does not ensure riches.
Cultural_Context: Wealth does not come from dressing well or living in a big city.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣòkòtò tí ńṣiṣẹ́ àràn, oko ní ńgbé.
Target_Text_En: The pants that do the work that purchases the velvet fabric stay on the farm.
Cultural_Context: The real workers and producers of wealth are likely to be less in the public eye than their beneficiaries.

Source_Text_Yo: Tàkúté tí yó pa Aláginjù á pẹ́ lóko kí wọ́n tó gbé e wálé.
Target_Text_En: The snare that will capture the lord of the wilderness will stay long in the bush before returning home.
Cultural_Context: Whoever attempts the impossible is in for long frustration.

Source_Text_Yo: Tàpò-tàpò là ńyọ jìgá; tewé-tewé là ńyan ẹ̀kọ.
Target_Text_En: With their sac and all is how to remove chiggers; with its wrapping-leaves is the way to buy corn meal.
Cultural_Context: One must do things thoroughly, not by halves.

Source_Text_Yo: Tẹ̀tẹ̀ ẹ̀gún ti lómi tẹ́lẹ̀ kójò tó rọ̀ sí i.
Target_Text_En: The prickly spinach was succulent before the rain fell on it.
Cultural_Context: A statement that one does not depend on largesse from other people.

Source_Text_Yo: Títa ríro là ńkọlà, bó bá jinná a di tẹni.
Target_Text_En: Facial scarification causes with a great deal of pain; when it heals, its beauty becomes one’s pride.
Cultural_Context: Good things come with some pain.

Source_Text_Yo: Tojú tìyẹ́ làparò-ó fi ńríran.
Target_Text_En: It is with both its eyes and its feathers that the partridge sees.
Cultural_Context: A statement that someone is all eyes.

Source_Text_Yo: Tọ̀sán tóru, imú ò gbélẹ̀; bó bá dákẹ́, à jẹ́ pé ó pín.
Target_Text_En: Day or night, the nose does not rest; if it stops, that means the end.
Cultural_Context: Some things are so reliable that they never fail.

Source_Text_Yo: Wàhálà ló bí ìrọra; òṣì ló bí wàhálà.
Target_Text_En: Struggle gives birth to ease; destitution gives birth to struggle.
Cultural_Context: He who exerts himself will find ease in the end; he who avoids exertions is doomed to struggle in the end.

Source_Text_Yo: Wèrè èèyàn ní ńru ẹrù wòran; ẹní ru ẹrù wòran ni wèrè èèyàn ńwò.
Target_Text_En: Only an imbecile carries a heavy load and stops to watch a spectacle; such a heavily laden spectacle watcher is the sort of spec tacle that attracts the attention of imbeciles.
Cultural_Context: Only a fool neglects pressing duties to dawdle.

Source_Text_Yo: Wíwẹ̀ là ńwẹ̀ ká tó jàre ọyẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Only by taking a cold shower can one shake off the chill of the harmattan.
Cultural_Context: The solution to a problem may require some initial unpleasantness.

Source_Text_Yo: Wọ́n ní, Àparò aṣọ ẹẹ́ ṣe pọ́n báyìí? Ó ní ìgbà wo laṣọ òun ò níí pọ́n. Kóun kọ igba láàárọ̀, kóun tó họ ilẹ̀ kùrẹ̀-kùrẹ̀ lábùsùndájí. Ìgbà wo lòun ó ràáàyè fọṣọ?
Target_Text_En: People asked the partridge, ‘‘Why is your clothing so dirty?’’ He responded, ‘‘Why would my clothing not be dirty? Given the time it takes me to make a hundred heaps in the morning, and the time I need to scratch the ground at dawn, what time is left for me to wash my clothes?’’
Cultural_Context: The shiftless can always find excuses to explain their predicament.

Source_Text_Yo: Yán sí i, yán sí i ní ńpa alákàrà lẹ́rÌn ín.
Target_Text_En: "Sell more to me, sell more to me" is what brings smiles to the face of the bean-fritters seller.
Cultural_Context: Good fortune always makes people happy.

Source_Text_Yo: Yànmù-yanmu là ńjọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Gracelessly is the way one eats bananas.
Cultural_Context: Certain activities do not permit gracefulness.

Source_Text_Yo: Yànmùyánmú ńṣe fújà láìlápa.
Target_Text_En: The mosquito brags despite its lack of arms.
Cultural_Context: Insignificant pests can still be the source of considerable annoyance.

Source_Text_Yo: Yí mi sébè, kí nyí ọ sí póró oko.
Target_Text_En: Throw me on the heaps, and I will throw you into the furrows.
Cultural_Context: To whatever attack you mount against me, I will respond in kind.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í pè lẹ́rú, ká pè é lóbí.
Target_Text_En: One does not call it a slave and also call it a child of the house.
Cultural_Context: One must be clear about one’s attitude toward a thing or person; ambivalence causes trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í pè é lẹ́rù ká pè é lọ́ṣọ̀ọ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not call it a burden and also call it an adornment.
Cultural_Context: An event is either a boon or a disaster, never both.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í rí ẹṣin ní ìso.
Target_Text_En: One does not find a horse on tether.
Cultural_Context: Too easy and too convenient a find suggests stealing.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í rí i ká tún sọ pé a ò ri mọ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not see a thing and then say one does not see it.
Cultural_Context: Always stand by your word.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ró aṣọ ajé sídìí ká dájọ́ òdòdò lẹ́bi.
Target_Text_En: One does not wear the ritual loincloth for presiding over a trial-by-ordeal and judge the righteous guilty.
Cultural_Context: One must not violate the oath one is sworn to observe.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í so ẹran mẹ́ran kó kàn án pa.
Target_Text_En: One does not tie a goat with another goat and keep one from butting the other to death.
Cultural_Context: One must not injure a person committed to one’s protection.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í sọ̀rọ̀ ìkọ̀kọ̀ kó má diyàn ní gba-n gba.
Target_Text_En: One does not conspire in secret without having the matter eventually cause a public argument.
Cultural_Context: Whatever is done in secret soon becomes exposed.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ṣe ẹlẹ́jọ́ ní "Ngbọ́"?
Target_Text_En: One does not ask the main litigant, ‘‘How about it?’’
Cultural_Context: Do not expect impartial witnessing from an interested party.

Source_Text_Yo: Àbàtá pani; àbàtá pani; ká ṣá sọ pé odò-ó gbéni lọ.
Target_Text_En: He died in the mire, he died in the mire; let us simply say that the person drowned.
Cultural_Context: One should prefer plain talk to euphemisms.

Source_Text_Yo: Àbẹ̀tẹ́lẹ̀ n ńfọ́jú onídàájọ́.
Target_Text_En: It is bribery that blinds a judge.
Cultural_Context: Bribery beclouds judgment.

Source_Text_Yo: Adánu tí ńjẹ ilá: ó ní ‘‘Ẹ ò rí ilẹ̀ báyìí?’’
Target_Text_En: Cleft-lipped person eating okro complains, ‘‘Can you believe what a mess the floor is?’’
Cultural_Context: The culprit complains about a condition as though he or she had nothing to do with it.

Source_Text_Yo: Àdàpè olè ní ńjẹ́ àfọwọ́rá
Target_Text_En: It is simply a euphemism for theft to say àfọwọ́rá [literally, causing to disappear through the operations of the hand].
Cultural_Context: The use of a euphemism does not change the nature of a thing.

Source_Text_Yo: Àdàpè olè ní ńjẹ́ ọmọ-mi ńfẹ́wọ́.
Target_Text_En: It is a euphemistic description of stealing to say, ‘‘My child’s hands are uncontrollably nimble.’’
Cultural_Context: One should face facts and not skirt them.

Source_Text_Yo: Adẹ́tẹ̀ẹ́ sọ́rọ̀ méjì, o fìkan purọ́; ó ní nígbàtí òún lu ọmọ òun lábàrá, òún ja léèékánná pàtì.
Target_Text_En: The leper said two things, one of them being a lie; he said after he had struck his child with his palm, he also pinched him severely with his fingernails.
Cultural_Context: One fools only oneself when one claims to have done the impossible.

Source_Text_Yo: Afasẹ́gbèjò ńtan ara-a rẹ̀ jẹ.
Target_Text_En: He who would collect rainwater in a sieve deceives himself.
Cultural_Context: The shiftless person hurts himself more than others.

Source_Text_Yo: Afatarẹ́nilójú, alè-e baále.
Target_Text_En: One-who-smears-one’s-eyes-with-pepper: one’s husband’s concubine.
Cultural_Context: The illicit lover of a woman’s husband is no friend of hers.

Source_Text_Yo: Afẹ́nilóbìnrin ò ro ire síni.
Target_Text_En: He-who-has-an-affair-with-one’s-wife harbors no good will toward one.
Cultural_Context: One knows one’s friends by their behavior.

Source_Text_Yo: Afìkọ̀kọ̀jalè, bí ọba ayé ò rí ọ; tọ̀rún rí ọ.
Target_Text_En: You-who-steal-in-secret, if an earthly king does not see you, the heavenly king sees you.
Cultural_Context: Nothing is hidden from God.

Source_Text_Yo: Afọ́jú àjànàkú, kò mọ igi, kò mọ èèyàn.
Target_Text_En: A blind elephant does not know a man from a tree.
Cultural_Context: Fate is no respecter of persons.

Source_Text_Yo: Àfọwọ́rá ní ńjẹ́ olè.
Target_Text_En: Employing-the-hands-to-make-things disappear is called stealing.
Cultural_Context: Euphemistic circumlocution does not relieve a crime of its true nature.

Source_Text_Yo: Agada ò morí alágbẹ̀dẹ.
Target_Text_En: The sword cannot tell the smith’s head from others.
Cultural_Context: Natural justice does not play favorites.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàká lodi ńgba ìlú.
Target_Text_En: It is completely that a fortification wall encircles a town.
Cultural_Context: Brook no half measures.

Source_Text_Yo: A-gbẹ́jọ́ ẹnìkan-dájọ́, òṣìkà èèyàn.
Target_Text_En: He-who-decides-a-case-after-hearing-only one-side [is] the dean of wicked persons.
Cultural_Context: Justice requires considering both sides of a case.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbọ́ìgbọ́tán Ègùn, ìjà ní ńdá sílẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Imperfect understanding of Ègùn [a language spoken to the west of Yoruba] brings nothing but dissension.
Cultural_Context: Half-knowledge is a bad thing.

Source_Text_Yo: Àì-fẹ́-àlejòó-ṣe là ńwí pé "Ọ̀rẹ́ ọ̀rẹ́-ẹ̀ mí dé"; ká ṣáà ti wí pé, "Ọ̀rẹ́-ẹ̀ mí dé."
Target_Text_En: Reluctance-to-extend-hospitality makes one say, ‘‘My friend’s friend has arrived’’; one should simply say, ‘‘My friend has arrived.’’
Cultural_Context: If one’s friend’s friend is one’s friend, one should not stress that the friend is once removed; one should avoid doubletalk.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìfẹ̀sọ̀ké ìbòsí ni kò ṣéé gbè.
Target_Text_En: It is an alarm that is raised without moderation that finds no helpers.
Cultural_Context: If the person who raises an alarm puts people off by his or her methd, they will not come to his or her aid

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbẹ̀ gbóko róṣù.
Target_Text_En: A farmer stays on the farm and sees the moon.
Cultural_Context: The conscientious farmer spends long periods on the farm; persistence is the key to success.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá ní òun ìba má dèé oko rí òun ìbá sọ pé ọ̀run ni wọ́n ti ńkálá wá.
Target_Text_En: The dog says that if it had never been to a farm, it would have thought that okra came from heaven.
Cultural_Context: People are inclined to hoodwink the innocent or the ignorant.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá ti erée rẹ̀ẹ́ bá dánilójú là ńdẹ sí ehoro.
Target_Text_En: It is a dog in whose speed one has faith that one sics on a hare.
Cultural_Context: One entrusts important tasks only to those one can trust.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjàlá, ta ní nà ọ́? Ìwọ náà kọ́ un?
Target_Text_En: Àjàlá, who whipped you? It is none other than you, isn’t it?
Cultural_Context: An evildoer is often also a dissembler.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjànàkú kúro ni ‘‘A rí ǹkan fìrí’’; bí a bá rérin ká wí.
Target_Text_En: The elephant is more than something of which one says, ‘‘I caught a fleeting glimpse of something’’; if one saw an elephant, one should say so.
Cultural_Context: Don’t hedge when discussing the obvious.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjò àìwuniíyún là ńdÍfá sí.
Target_Text_En: It is about a journey one does not want to make that one consults the oracle.
Cultural_Context: Where there is no desire, excuses are easy to find.

Source_Text_Yo: A-kápò-má-ṣọdẹ: ọ̀tá ẹranko, ọ̀tá èèyàn.
Target_Text_En: He-who-carries-a-hunting-bag-but-does not-hunt: enemy alike of man and beast.
Cultural_Context: Be not a dog in the manger.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkàsọ̀ faratilẹ̀ faratilé; bí ẹni tí a fẹ̀hìntì ó bàá yẹni a wí fúnni.
Target_Text_En: A ladder rests on the ground and leans on the house; if the person one leans on must remove his support, he should give warning.
Cultural_Context: A person one trusts should be completely trustworthy.

Source_Text_Yo: Akọ asín kì í gbọ́ ohùn ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀ kó dúró; abiyamọ kì í gbọ́ ẹkún ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀ kó má tara ṣàṣà
Target_Text_En: A male asín rat does not hear the cry of its young and remain still; a nursing mother does not hear the cry of her baby without responding anxiously.
Cultural_Context: One must take one’s chief responsibilities seriously.

Source_Text_Yo: Alákatam̀pò ò mọ irú ẹran.
Target_Text_En: The user of a crossbow does not know what sort of game he shoots at.
Cultural_Context: Some people lack a sense of discrimination.

Source_Text_Yo: Alápatà ò mọ irú ẹran.
Target_Text_En: The butcher does not know what the animal is.
Cultural_Context: A butcher is indifferent to the type of animal he butchers.

Source_Text_Yo: Amọ̀rànbini Ọ̀yọ́, bí o bá gbé kete lérí, wọn a ní oko lò ńlọ tàbí odò.
Target_Text_En: People-who-know-the-answer-yet-ask-the question, natgives of Ọ̀yọ́: if they see you carrying a water pot, they ask whether you are on your way to the farm or the stream.
Cultural_Context: If the answer is plain to see, one does not ask the question.

Source_Text_Yo: Apajájẹ-ẹ́ nÍ ẹ̀rù adìẹ ḿba òun.
Target_Text_En: The-person-who-kills-and-eats-dogs claims to be afraid of chickens.
Cultural_Context: A hardened criminal pretends to have scruples about mere peccadilloes.

Source_Text_Yo: Apani kì í jẹ́ mú idà kọjá nípàkọ́ òun.
Target_Text_En: A murderer never permits the passage of a sword behind his skull.
Cultural_Context: The criminal is ever suspicious of other people’s intentions.

Source_Text_Yo: Àpèjúwe lalágbẹ̀dẹ ńrọ.
Target_Text_En: The blacksmith manufactures from a description.
Cultural_Context: Unless a person speaks his or her mind, others cannot know what the person has in it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ará Ìbàdàn kì í ságun; à ó rìn sẹ́hín ni wọ́n ńwí.
Target_Text_En: Ibadan people do not run from war; what they say is, ‘‘We will fall back a little.’’
Cultural_Context: There are ways of avoiding battle without seeming to do so.

Source_Text_Yo: Arítẹnimọ̀ọ́wí, ó fi àpáàdì ràbàtà bo tirẹ̀ mọ́lẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: He-who-eagerly-speaks-of-one’s-problems covers his own with a huge potsherd.
Cultural_Context: People will talk about others’ problems while carefully hiding their own.

Source_Text_Yo: Àrókanlẹ̀ laṣọ ayaba; àwàkanlẹ̀ ni ti yàrà.
Target_Text_En: Wrapping-from-waist-to-the-floor is the style of the queen’s wrapper; digging-down to-the-deepest-bottom is the requirement of yàrà, the dry moat.
Cultural_Context: Whatever one has to do, one must be thorough and not satsified with half measures.

Source_Text_Yo: Arúgbó oǹdágbèsè, ó ní mélòó ni òun ó dùúró san níbẹ̀?
Target_Text_En: The old person who incurs debt says, how much of it will he be around to repay?
Cultural_Context: A person whose days are numbered can afford to take on long-term obligations.

Source_Text_Yo: Asárélówó ḿbẹ lọ́nà ogun; Apọ̀ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀ m̀bẹ lọ́nà èrò; Bó-pẹ́-títí-ng-ó-lá ḿbẹlábà, ó ńjẹ ẹ̀sun iṣu.
Target_Text_En: He-who-hurries-after-riches is on his way to battle; He-who-has-in-abundance is off on his travels; By-and-by-‘‘I-will-be-rich’’ is back in his hut, eating roasted yams.
Cultural_Context: Wealth comes to those who exert themselves, not to those who wait for it to find them.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣeburúkú tẹsẹ̀ mọ́nà.
Target_Text_En: The evildoer makes a brisk exit.
Cultural_Context: The evildoer would not wait for his nature to catch up with him.

Source_Text_Yo: A-ṣọ̀tún-ṣòsì-má-ba-ibìkan-jẹ́, irọ́ la ó bàá níbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One-who-is-tight-with-the-right-and-tight with-the-left-without-alienating-either: what one will find in that characterization is a lie.
Cultural_Context: There is no way to support both sides of a quarrel without betraying one side.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwárí lobìnrin ńwá nǹkan ọbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Seeking-until-finding is how a woman looks for ingredients for stew.
Cultural_Context: The dutiful person does not permit difficulties to keep her from accomplishing her duty.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá ká okó mọ́ obìnrin nídìí á ní kùkú ni.
Target_Text_En: If one catches a penis in a woman’s vagina, she will argue that it is only a corncob.
Cultural_Context: Trust a woman to deny even the obvious.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá ńyọ́lẹ̀ dà, ohun abẹ́nú a máa yọ́ni ṣe.
Target_Text_En: If one engages secretly in treachery, secret disasters come.
Cultural_Context: Crimes committed in secret do not go unrequited.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí abẹ́rẹ́ bí abẹ́rẹ́ lèèyàn ńṣèké; ọj tó bá tóbi tó ọkọ́ tí a fi ńroko ní ńpani.
Target_Text_En: Like a needle, like a needle, one compiles falsehood; the day it is as big as the hoe one uses on a farm, that is the day it kills one.
Cultural_Context: Small falsehoods eventually grow into a habit powerful enough to kill.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ẹnú bá jẹ, ojú á tì.
Target_Text_En: If the mouth has eaten, the eyes shut down.
Cultural_Context: If one has received some favor from a person, one’s eyes will be closed to the person’s faults.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ìgbín ńfà, ìkaraun a tẹ̀lé e.
Target_Text_En: When the snail crawls, its shell follows.
Cultural_Context: The dependent person always sticks close to his or her support.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ìkà-á bá ńrojọ́, ìkà kọ́ ni yó da.
Target_Text_En: If the wicked person states a case, it is not the wicked person who will judge it.
Cultural_Context: The wicked will not prevail in the face of impartial judges.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí o finú ṣìkà tí o fòde ṣòótọ́, ọba séríkí á rín ọ rín ọ.
Target_Text_En: If you hide wickedness inside you while displaying a kindly disposition, God above will laugh hard at you.
Cultural_Context: No secret act of wickedness is concealed from God.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí o rí i, wà pé o ò rí; ọkọ́ fún ọ lówó, àlé gbà á ná.
Target_Text_En: If you saw it, you would say you did not; your husband gave you money and your lover spends it.
Cultural_Context: An unfaithful woman deserves no trust.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ó ti wù kó pẹ́ tó, olóòótọ́ ò níí sùn sípò ìkà.
Target_Text_En: However long it takes, a truthful person will not wind up in the bed made for the wicked.
Cultural_Context: Whatever happens in the short run, in the long run the truthful person will be vindicated.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí obìnrín bá máa dán èké wò, a da aṣọ dúdú bora.
Target_Text_En: When a woman wishes to engage in mischief, she wears dark clothing.
Cultural_Context: A woman’s furtiveness portends mischief.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ojú bá sé ojú; kí ohùn má yẹ ohùn.
Target_Text_En: If eyes no longer see eyes, let the voice not miss the voice.
Cultural_Context: Though separated by distances, people should keep agreements they made.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí olókùnrùn yó bàá kú, kó má purọ́ mọ́ àlapà; omitooro kì í korò.
Target_Text_En: If an invalid is approaching death, he should not lie about the melon-seed loaf; stew is never bitter.
Cultural_Context: If one must make excuses for one's flaw,s, one should make them plausible.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí o ní ọ̀pọ̀ oògùn, tí o ní èké, kò níí jẹ́; orí ẹní jẹ́ ó ju ewé lọ; ìpín jà ó ju oògùn lọ.
Target_Text_En: .If you have a great deal of medicine and you are false, it will not work; one’s head works better than any herb; one’s destiny is far more effective than any medicine.
Cultural_Context: Evil intentions make one’s medicine ineffective; the best hope lies in one’s head and one’s destiny.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí òru bí òru ní ńṣe aláṣọdúdú.
Target_Text_En: Longing for nighttime, longing for night time is the tendency of the person in dark clothing.
Cultural_Context: A person engaged in secret business is always secretive.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọgbọ́n bá tán nínú, a tún òmíràn dá.
Target_Text_En: When an elder has exhausted all his wisdom, he turns to another’s wisdom.
Cultural_Context: An elder is never at a loss for what to do.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọmọdé bá mọ igbá-di-ogóje, kò lè mọ èrò-kò-wájà.
Target_Text_En: If a youth knows two-hundred-becomes one-hundred-forty, he cannot know traders refuse-to-come-to-the-market.
Cultural_Context: A person who knows how to cheat those who deal with him will not know how to win them back when they refuse to deal with him.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọmọdé bá ri oyin, a ju àkàrà nù.
Target_Text_En: When a child sees honey, he throws away bean fritters.
Cultural_Context: The inconstant person’s concern is limited to the latest attraction.

Source_Text_Yo: Dúkìa tí a fi èrú kójọ kò mú ká dolówó.
Target_Text_En: The treasure one gathers by foul means will not make one rich.
Cultural_Context: Wealth garnered unfairly does not last.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Ebí ńpa mí’’ ò ṣéé fìfé wí.
Target_Text_En: ‘‘I am hungry’’ is not a message that whistling can convey.
Cultural_Context: A person in need of help must not be coy or cryptic in asking for it.

Source_Text_Yo: Eegun tí a bá so m ajá l rùn, kì í ṣán an.
Target_Text_En: A dog does not eat a bone tied to its neck.
Cultural_Context: One may not take advantage of a person or thing entrusted to one’s care.

Source_Text_Yo: Èké lojú ó tì bó dọ̀la.
Target_Text_En: The devious will reap shame in the future.
Cultural_Context: Wickedness will receive its just deserts in due time.

Source_Text_Yo: Èké mọ ilé-e rẹ̀ ó wó; ọ̀dàlẹ́ mọ tirẹ̀ ó bì dànù.
Target_Text_En: The devious person builds a house, and it collapses; the treacherous person builds one, and it tumbles in ruins.
Cultural_Context: Evil people will not profit from their enterprises.

Source_Text_Yo: Elékèé lèké ńyé; oun a bá ṣe ní ńyéni.
Target_Text_En: Only a devious person knows what he or she is about; each person alone is privy to what he or she has done.
Cultural_Context: One can never be sure about a devious person.

Source_Text_Yo: Eléwe-é ní iyènú; àìní mọ ìwà-á hù.
Target_Text_En: A person who has children must be responsible; one who does not must know how to behave.
Cultural_Context: One should live up to one’s responsibilities.

Source_Text_Yo: Èlùbọ́ lo wáá rà; ọmọ ẹrán ṣe dénú igbá?
Target_Text_En: You came to buy yam flour; how did a kid find its way into your calabash?
Cultural_Context: The alibi offered by a culprit [subject of the proverb] is full of holes.

Source_Text_Yo: Èké Ìbídùn, tí ńkí eégún ‘‘Kú àtijọ́.’’
Target_Text_En: [It is a] lying Ìbídùn who greets a masquerader with ‘‘It’s been quite a while!’’
Cultural_Context: The subject of the comment [here named Ìbídùn] is prone to telling blatant lies.

Source_Text_Yo: Èrò ò kí baálẹ̀, baálé ló ńkí.
Target_Text_En: The guest does not pay homage to the chief, only to the host.
Cultural_Context: One’s first obligation is to one’s immediate benefactor, not to a remote authority, however great.

Source_Text_Yo: Etí, gbọ́ èkejì kí o tó dájọ́.
Target_Text_En: Ear, hear the other side before passing judgment.
Cultural_Context: One should not form an opinion after hearing only one side of an argument.

Source_Text_Yo: Etí tó gbọ́ àlọ ni yó gbọ̀ọ́ àbọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The same ears that heard about the departure will hear about the return.
Cultural_Context: Whoever is privy to the genesis of an affair will [must] be privy to its conclusion.

Source_Text_Yo: Ewúrẹ́ nÍ òun ò mọlé odì; ẹni Òún bá ṣẹ̀ kó bi Òun.
Target_Text_En: The goat says it does not set aside any house as an enemy’s; whoever it has offended should ask it why.
Cultural_Context: One wants no enemies; if one has offended anyone, that person should ask why.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹgẹ́ ò ṣákìí; ẹní bá bọ́ sábẹ́-ẹ rẹ̀, a pa á kú pátá-pátá.
Target_Text_En: The ẹgẹ́ trap never misses; whatever passes beneath it, it strikes dead.
Cultural_Context: A certain person, or thing, can be relied upon to do what is expected of him, her, or it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀ẹ̀mejì letí ọlọ́jà ńgbọ́rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The ears of the king hear everything twice.
Cultural_Context: Whoever will judge a case must hear it twice from both sides of the dispute.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ-kòÌ-fẹ́-mi kù, tó tà ajá-a rẹ̀ lókòó.
Target_Text_En: You-have-not-seen-the-last-of-me, who sold his dog for 20 cowries.
Cultural_Context: A person duped without his or her knowledge will be back for redress once the fact dawns on him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀là lọ̀rọ̀; bí a ò bá là á rírú ní ńrú.
Target_Text_En: Statements must be clarified; if they are not, they become muddy.
Cultural_Context: One must always be clear in one's speeches or intentions.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀là lọ̀rọ̀; bóbìnrín bá jókòó a laṣọ bòbò.
Target_Text_En: Statements must always be clarified; when a woman sits, she covers her genitals with her wrapper.
Cultural_Context: One must always be clear in one's speeches or intentions.

Source_Text_Yo: Èlérìí ní ńyanjú ẹjọ́; èlérìí kì í ṣe elégbè.
Target_Text_En: It is a witness that clears up a case; a witness is not a partisan.
Cultural_Context: People called to bear witness in a case should be impartial.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni a kò fẹ́ nilé-e rẹ̀ ńjìnna lójú ẹni.
Target_Text_En: It is a person one does not love whose house is distant in one’s estimation.
Cultural_Context: One can always find an excuse for not doing what one does not wish to do.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá sùn là ńjí, a kì í jí apirọrọ.
Target_Text_En: One wakes only those that sleep, not those pretending to sleep.
Cultural_Context: Deal with people who are in earnest, not with gamesters.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní gbé àrùn pamọ́ kọjá ore oníṣègùn.
Target_Text_En: Whoever conceals a disease is beyond help from a doctor.
Cultural_Context: People in need of help should not conceal the fact.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a nà ní kùm̀mọ̀ mẹ́fà, tó ní kan ṣoṣo ló ba òun, níbo nìyókùú sọnù sí?
Target_Text_En: [If] a person is hit six times with a club and says only one blow landed, where did the other blows disappear?
Cultural_Context: A person who tries to minimize obvious misfortune deceives no one.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó bá mọ ìṣe òkùnkùn, kó má dàá òṣùpá lóró; ohun a ṣe ní ńmúni-í rìnde òru; òkùnkùn ò yẹ ọmọ èèyàn.
Target_Text_En: Whoever knows what darkness can do must not antagonize the moon, [since] one’s actions [sometimes] send one abroad at night; roaming around in the dark is not a becoming habit.
Cultural_Context: It is best to cultivate those forces that might serve one well in the future.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó fẹ́ẹ́ kúure, kó hùwà rere.
Target_Text_En: Whoever wishes to die a decent death, let him or her live decently.
Cultural_Context: As one lives, so one dies, and so one is remembered.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó gbépo lájà ò jalè bí ẹni tó gbà á sílẹ̀ fún un.
Target_Text_En: The person who removes oil from the rafter is less a thief than the person who helps him set it on the floor.
Cultural_Context: The abettor is more a culprit than the perpetrator.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó gbọ́n tó ńpurọ́; ẹni tó mọ̀ràn tó ńṣèké; ẹni tó mọ̀ pé nǹkan ò sí tó ńtọrọ; èwo ló sàn nínú àwọn mẹ́tẹ́ẹ̀ta?
Target_Text_En: The person who is wise and yet lies, the person who knows the truth and yet dissembles, the person who knows one has nothing and yet asks for something: which is any good among the three?
Cultural_Context: The liar, the dissembler, and the one who would embarrass you are all equally evil.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó ṣe ojú kò da bí ẹni tó ṣe ẹ̀hìn.
Target_Text_En: The person who honors one in one’s presence is nothing like the person who honors one in one’s absence.
Cultural_Context: It is what people say of you or do on your behalf in your absence that matters.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnìkan kì í yọ̀ kí ilẹ̀ ó sẹ́.
Target_Text_En: When a person slips, the earth may not deny responsibility or knowledge.
Cultural_Context: For whatever one does, one should be willing to accept responsibility.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu òpùrọ́ kì í ṣẹ̀jẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The liar’s mouth does not bleed.
Cultural_Context: Lies have no telltale labels attached.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu-u rẹ̀ ní ńdá igba, tí ńdá ọ̀dúnrún.
Target_Text_En: His or her mouth is the same one that proposes two hundred and proposes three hundred.
Cultural_Context: An unreliable person’s mouth is ever running, and what comes out of it is not to be trusted.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹran tí a kì í jẹ, a kì í fi ehín pín in.
Target_Text_En: Meat that one does not eat, one does not bite into with one’s teeth.
Cultural_Context: One should be unequivocal in one’s commitments or avoidances.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀tàn kì í ṣe ọgbọ́n.
Target_Text_En: Deceit is no wisdom.
Cultural_Context: Deceit is not a reliable strategy to count on.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀wà yí kò dùn, ẹ̀wà yí kò dùn, àáṣó ìpàkọ́ ḿmì tìtì.
Target_Text_En: These beans are not delicious, these beans are not delicious, yet the coiffure at the occiput is shaking vigorously.
Cultural_Context: A person’s actions toward a person or thing belie his or her detracting comments; if one claims to dislike something or someone, one’s actions should not say the opposite.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹyẹlé ní òun ò lè bá olúwa òun jẹ, kí òun bá a mu, kí ó di ọjọ́ ikú-u rẹ̀ kí òun yẹrí.
Target_Text_En: The pigeon says it cannot share its owner’s food and drink, and then, when the day of his death arrives, ducks its head.
Cultural_Context: If one shares the good times with a person, one should be prepared to share the bad times also.

Source_Text_Yo: Fi inú ṣìkà, fi òde ṣòótọ́; ẹni tí ḿbini kò níí ṣàì bini.
Target_Text_En: Hide wickedness in you and affect a benevolent comportment; the one who calls people to account will not forget.
Cultural_Context: God sees all hidden acts of wickedness and metes out punishment to their perpetrators.

Source_Text_Yo: Gba-n-gba là ńṣe gbàǹgbà; bẹ́ṣín bá kú, ìta gbangba là ńsin Í sí.
Target_Text_En: One performs one’s great feats in the open; if a horse dies, one buries it in a wide-open space.
Cultural_Context: One should not attempt to keep weighty matters under wraps.

Source_Text_Yo: Gba-n-gba làṣá ńta.
Target_Text_En: The hawk always spreads its wings to the fullest.
Cultural_Context: Whatever one has in mind, one should lay it out fully in the open.

Source_Text_Yo: Gba-n-gba lÒgèdègbé ńṣawo.
Target_Text_En: Ògèdègbé always performs his rituals in the open.
Cultural_Context: A great person need not hesitate to do whatever he or she has a mind to do.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbáà tínrín, okùn òtítọ́ kì í já; bí irọ́ tó ìrókò, wíwó ní ńwó.
Target_Text_En: Even if it is flimsy, the thread of truth never snaps; even though a lie might have the girth of an ìrókò tree, it inevitably crashes.
Cultural_Context: Truth will inevitably triumph over lies.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi tí a ti na ọmọ ọba là ḿbèrè, a kì í bèrè ibi tí ọmọ ọbá ti pọ́n lẹ́gbẹ̀ẹ́.
Target_Text_En: What one should ask is where the prince was attacked and flogged; one does not ask where the prince got the welts on his side.
Cultural_Context: When matters require urgent attention, one should not speak in riddles or prevaricate.

Source_Text_Yo: Igbó kannáà lọdẹ ńdẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is in the same forest that a hunter hunts [or all hunters hunt].
Cultural_Context: One should stick to that which one knows. Or, the manners and behaviors of members of a fraternity should be consistent and uniform.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìjòkó là ḿbá eèbà.
Target_Text_En: The oil pot is ever found in a sitting position.
Cultural_Context: The constancy of the pot is worth emulating.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkòkò kì í ṣelé ìgbín; ṣe ló dè ìgbín mọ́lẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The pot is no shelter for the snail; all it does is trap the snail.
Cultural_Context: One should not try to pass off as a favor an injury one is causing a person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìlú tí a bá rè là ḿbá pé.
Target_Text_En: The citizens one goes abroad with are those in whose ranks one remains.
Cultural_Context: One should not desert one’s colleagues midway through an enterprise.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìmàlé gbààwẹ̀ ó lóun ò gbétọ́ mì; ta ní ńṣe ẹlẹ́rìí fún un?
Target_Text_En: The Muslim fasts and swears he did not swallow his saliva; who is to corroborate his story?
Cultural_Context: There is no point is paying attention to a claim that cannot be verified.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìmàlé sọ̀rọ̀ òjó kù, ó ní Ọlúrun-ún jẹrìí òun.
Target_Text_En: The Muslim says something and thunder rumbles; he says the Almighty is corrobo rating his statement.
Cultural_Context: Said of someone who claims a neutral occurrence as evidence support for his or her position.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìmùlẹ̀ ò gbọdọ̀ tan ara wọn jẹ; ìmọ̀ ẹnìkan ò yàn.
Target_Text_En: Those who enter into a covenant must not betray one another; one person’s counsel is not enough by itself.
Cultural_Context: One must not break covenants.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìpẹ́pẹ́rẹ́ ìgò méje; bí kò bá pé méje ara kì í gbà á.
Target_Text_En: Seven trifling bottles; fewer than seven and one cannot endure the thought.
Cultural_Context: If a matter is really of no importance, one should not dwell on it.

Source_Text_Yo: Irọ́ ni "Má jọgunìkan ó gbọ́"; òótọ́ ni "Ẹni o rí o bí."
Target_Text_En: "Breathe not a word of it to anyone" denotes a lie; "Ask anyone you please" indicates the truth.
Cultural_Context: It is a only a lie that one wants no witness to; one will gladly proclaim the truth.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìrókò tó bá gbàbọ̀dè, bíbẹ́ ni.
Target_Text_En: Whichever ìrókò tree becomes involved in treachery gets felled.
Cultural_Context: Whoever engages in treachery will be destroyed, no matter his or her status.

Source_Text_Yo: 'Jẹ́ kí nfìdí hẹ́ ẹ" -ẹ́ gbàjókó; àfòmọ́ di onílé.
Target_Text_En: "Permit me to perch by you" takes the whole seat; the parasite becomes the host.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who take over by wiles what belongs to others.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí a baà lè pẹ́ níbẹ̀, abuké ní bí òún bá kú, kí wọ́n ti ẹ̀hìn tú ìfun òun.
Target_Text_En: Just to delay people deliberately, the hump back says when he dies his intestines should be removed from the back.
Cultural_Context: Said of people resorting to transparent delaying tactics.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí á gà, kí á gò, èdè ni ò yédè.
Target_Text_En: Sitting and refusing to budge from one’s position results from lack of communication.
Cultural_Context: It is when people fail to compromise that problems defy solution.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí á rí ká rà, ká rà ká má san: à-rà-àì san èkejì olè.
Target_Text_En: To see and buy, to buy and not pay: buying without paying [is] the twin of stealing.
Cultural_Context: One should pay for whatever one buys.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí olówó wá, kí aláwìn wá; à-rà-àì-san ni ò sunwọ̀n.
Target_Text_En: Let the purchaser with cash come, and let the purchaser on credit come; only buying without [eventually] paying is bad.
Cultural_Context: What is important is not so much when but that one fulfill one’s obligation.

Source_Text_Yo: "Kò dùn mí, kò dùn mí"; àgbàlagbà ḿbú ọpa lẹ́ẹ̀mẹfà nítorí iyán àná.
Target_Text_En: ‘‘I am not upset, I am not upset!’’ Yet a grown man swears angrily six times because of last night’s pounded yam.
Cultural_Context: A person’s protestation of indifference is belied by agitated behavior.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ohun tí a ò lè fi òru ṣe; ẹ̀rù ọ̀sán là ḿbà.
Target_Text_En: There is nothing one cannot do in the dead of night; the light of day alone is what one fears.
Cultural_Context: The cover of darkness is a perfect protection for any sort of enterprise.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò ṣeku kò ṣẹyẹ ò jẹ́ kí àjàò sanwó òde.
Target_Text_En: Being neither a rat nor a bird keeps àjàò (a birdlike animal) from having to pay poll tax.
Cultural_Context: It is impossible to be really sure of a person who will not commit to any side in a dispute.

Source_Text_Yo: Má sẹ̀ẹ́ kí ọ̀ràn má pọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Do not deny your responsibility; that way the problem will be minimized.
Cultural_Context: Refusing to accept one’s responsibility only aggravates one’s difficulties.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Mo kò ó’’ kì í ṣe àìní àpèjúwe.
Target_Text_En: ‘‘I met him’’ is an incomplete statement without further elaboration.
Cultural_Context: One should say enough to make one’s message understood.

Source_Text_Yo: Nì palaba, ní wonko, ẹ̀rẹ̀kẹ́ á ṣèkan.
Target_Text_En: Either sunken or swollen, the cheeks will be one or the other.
Cultural_Context: If one is not one way, one must be the other way; one cannot be no way at all.

Source_Text_Yo: Nígbàtí ọwọ́ ò tẹ ìjàdù là ńní kò sí ohun tí à ńjẹ tí kì í tán.
Target_Text_En: It is when one has come up empty in a scramble for food that one says there is nothing one eats that is not finished sooner or later.
Cultural_Context: An affectation of indifference is often disguised disappointment.

Source_Text_Yo: "Ó fò sókè ó pẹ́títí," irọ́ ló ńpa.
Target_Text_En: "He jumped up and stayed aloft almost for ever": that is a lie.
Cultural_Context: One should control the urge to exaggerate.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó jọ gàtè, kò jọ gàtè, ó fẹsẹ̀ méjèèjì tiro rìn.
Target_Text_En: It may seem like staggering, and it may not seem like staggering, but he is tipping forward on tiptoes.
Cultural_Context: A euphemism does not make an action anything other than what it is.

Source_Text_Yo: O kò pọ̀ ọ́, bẹ́ẹ̀ni oò gbé e mì.
Target_Text_En: You do not spit it out, and yet you do not swallow it.
Cultural_Context: Said of a person who will neither accept nor reject a proposition.

Source_Text_Yo: "Ó mọ́ mi lọ́wọ́" ní ńdi olè.
Target_Text_En: "It is an exact fit for my hand" leads to thievery.
Cultural_Context: One should not grow too attached to other people’s possessions.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó ńṣe apá kúlú-kúlú bí ẹni ká gbé e jó, ó sì ńṣẹnu hàmù-hàmù bí èyí tí yó gbèéni mì.
Target_Text_En: It wiggles its arms as though it would have one dance with it, and yet it is working its mouth as though it would swallow one.
Cultural_Context: Said of a person who mixes friendly gestures with threatening ones.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó pẹ́ títí ni "A-bẹnu-bí-ẹnu-ọ̀bọ"; ká ṣá sọ pé, "Ìwọ Lámọnrín, ọ̀bọ ni ọ́."
Target_Text_En: It is mere circumlocution to say, ‘‘A person has a mouth like a fool’s’’; one should rather say, ‘‘You, so-and-so, you are a fool.’’
Cultural_Context: Be confident enough to speak without hedging.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó ta ọfà sókè, ó ṣí odó borí.
Target_Text_En: He shot an arrow toward the sky and covered his head with a mortar.
Cultural_Context: Said of a person who causes problems and goes into hiding, leaving others to suffer the consequences.

Source_Text_Yo: Obì-í bọ́ lọ́wọ́ alákẹdun ó ní òún fún ará ilẹ̀; bí kò fún ará ilẹ̀, yó sọ̀kalẹ̀ wá mú u?
Target_Text_En: Kola nut drops from the grip of a monkey, which says it makes a gift of the nut to ground dwellers; if it does not make a gift of it to ground dwellers, would it come down to fetch it?
Cultural_Context: One can tell when necessity is being disguised as virtue.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrin abàlèmẹ́fà: àlè mẹ́fà ò mọ ara wọn.
Target_Text_En: A woman who has six lovers: the six lovers never know about one another.
Cultural_Context: Women are past mistresses of deceit.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrín bímọ fúnni kò pé kó má pani; obìnrin ò bímọ fúnni kò pé kó má pani.
Target_Text_En: That a woman has had your child does not mean she cannot kill you; that a woman has not had your child does not mean she may not kill you.
Cultural_Context: Intimacy is no protection against a woman.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrín pẹ́ lọ́jà ó fìgbójú wọlé.
Target_Text_En: A woman who tarried too long at the market returns home with a brazen face.
Cultural_Context: An offender will try to ward off criticism by first going on the offensive.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrín re ilé àlè, ó fi ilé ìyá ẹ̀ tan ọkọ jẹ
Target_Text_En: A woman goes to her lover’s house and uses her mother’s home to deceive her husband.
Cultural_Context: Legitimate pursuits ofen serve as cover for illegitimate ones.

Source_Text_Yo: Odídẹrẹ́ ẹyẹ òkun, àlùkò ẹyẹ ọ̀sà; bí a bá jẹun gbé, ká má jẹ̀ẹ́ùn gbé.
Target_Text_En: The parrot is a bird of the sea, and the king fisher a bird of the lagoon; even though we may forget that we once partook of the food, let us never forget what we covenanted.
Cultural_Context: However far we may roam, and however long, we should never forget promises made.

Source_Text_Yo: Òfìífìí là ńrí, a ò rí òkodoro; òkodoro ḿbọ̀, baba gba-n-gba.
Target_Text_En: All we see is shadows, not clarity; but clarity will come, father of all openness.
Cultural_Context: The truth may be long hidden, but in the end it will emerge into the open.

Source_Text_Yo: Ògèdèm̀gbé irọ́ kì í dáni síyẹ̀wù; gba-n gba ní ńdáni sí.
Target_Text_En: An audacious lie does not trip one in one’s closet; it exposes one in a public place.
Cultural_Context: One’s transgressions are likely to catch up with one in the most embarrassing circumstances.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí a ó fẹ́ kéèyàn ó mọ̀ là ńṣe lábẹ́lẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is what one wishes to keep a secret that one does in private.
Cultural_Context: One who has nothing to hide should not do things in secret.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojo díẹ̀, akin díẹ̀; ìyà ní ńkó jẹni.
Target_Text_En: A little cowardice [or] a little bravery: all it brings one is trouble.
Cultural_Context: One should decide whether one will be bold or cowardly; inconsistency in such matters results in suffering.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò ọ̀gànjọ́ ò pa ẹni rere; bí kò pa jalè jalè a pa yíde-yíde.
Target_Text_En: A midnight rain does not beat a decent person; if the person it beats is not a habitual thief, he or she will be a habitual [night] wanderer.
Cultural_Context: Honest people are seldom caught in compromising positions.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú gba-n-gba là ńta awọ gbà-ǹ-gbà.
Target_Text_En: It is out in the open that one spreads a huge skin.
Cultural_Context: A matter that is of great consequence to all should be discussed in the presence of all.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í fẹ́nikù kó hu ibi.
Target_Text_En: The eyes do not, because they do not see one, engage in evil against one.
Cultural_Context: Never take advantage of people’s absence to do them ill.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú lobìnrín mọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Women know only the face.
Cultural_Context: The only time one can rely on women is when one is present.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú lọ̀rọ̀-ọ́ wà.
Target_Text_En: Discourse is in the eyes.
Cultural_Context: Look the person with whom one is holding a dialogue in the eyes.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú olóbì la ti ńjèrè obì
Target_Text_En: It is in the presence and with the knowledge of the kola-nut seller that one receives a gratuitous addition to one’s purchase.
Cultural_Context: If one has a right to something, one should not take it surreptitiously.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú tó ti mọni rí kì í wípé òun ò mọni mọ́.
Target_Text_En: The eyes that used to recognize us cannot say they no longer recognize us.
Cultural_Context: Whatever happens, one should not refuse to acknowledge one’s friends.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkété ní ọjọ́ gbogbo lòún mọ̀, òun ò mọ ọjọ́ mìíràn.
Target_Text_En: The large bush rat says it knows every day but not some other day.
Cultural_Context: If one makes a promise, it should be firm and definite, not vague.

Source_Text_Yo: Olófòófó ò gbẹ́gbàá; ibi ọpẹ́ nì ḿmọ.
Target_Text_En: The tattler does not earn six pence; thanks are all he gets.
Cultural_Context: Tattling is not a profitable or appreciated habit.

Source_Text_Yo: Olóòótọ́ ìlú nìkà ìlú.
Target_Text_En: The honest person in a town is the ogre of the town.
Cultural_Context: Honesty seldom makes one popular.

Source_Text_Yo: Olóòótọ́ kì í sùn sípò ìkà.
Target_Text_En: The honest person will not sleep in the place prepared for the wicked person.
Cultural_Context: The honest person will in the end be vindicated.

Source_Text_Yo: Òǹrorò lẹ̀gbọ́n òfófó.
Target_Text_En: Lack of compassion is the elder of backbiting.
Cultural_Context: A person who lacks compassion will think nothing of spreading false news about others.

Source_Text_Yo: Òtítọ́ dọ́jà ó kùtà; owó lọ́wọ́ là ńra èké.
Target_Text_En: Truth arrives at the market but finds no buy]er; it is with ready cash, though, that people buy falsehood.
Cultural_Context: People appreciate falsehood more than truthfulness.

Source_Text_Yo: Òtítọ́ kì í kú ká fi irọ́ jọba.
Target_Text_En: The truth does not die to be replaced as king by the lie.
Cultural_Context: The lie cannot match the truth in esteem.

Source_Text_Yo: Òtítọ́ kì í ṣìnà; irọ́ ní ńfòrí gbọgbẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Truth never goes awry; it is falsehood that earns a gash on the head.
Cultural_Context: Truth will not bring misfortune; falsehood leads to trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: Òtítọ́ korò; bí omi tooro nirọ́ rí.
Target_Text_En: Truth is bitter; falsehood is like meat stew.
Cultural_Context: It is more difficult to be truthful than to lie.

Source_Text_Yo: Òtítọ́ lolórí ìwà.
Target_Text_En: Truthfulness is the chief of attributes.
Cultural_Context: There is no better attribute than truthfulness.

Source_Text_Yo: Òtítọ́ ní ńtú ẹrù ìkà palẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is truth that unpacks the load of the wicked for all to see.
Cultural_Context: Truth will triumph over the wicked.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó lobìnrín mọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Women care only about money.
Cultural_Context: Whatever women do, they do only for money.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọbẹ̀-ẹ́ dún, ọbẹ̀ ò dùn, iyán tán nígbá.
Target_Text_En: The stew is delicious, the stew is not delicious; the pounded-yam meal is completely gone from the dish.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who complain about something yet will not let go of it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kánkán là ńṣe ìbí; ìkọ̀kọ̀ là ńṣe ìmùlẹ̀; bí a tọ́jú ìmùlẹ̀ tán, ká tọ́jú ìbí pẹ̀lú; bí a bá kú ará ẹni ní ńsinni.
Target_Text_En: One conducts affairs with one’s kin with forthrightness; one enters into covenants [with nonrelatives] in secret; as one attends to one’s secret compacts, one should also attend to affairs with one’s kin; on the day one dies, it is one’s kin who attend to the funeral.
Cultural_Context: Never neglect your relatives in favor of others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀mọ̀rán bèèrè ọ̀ràn wò; Àjàpá ní, "Ẹni tí wọ́n pa lánàá, kàà kú tán?"
Target_Text_En: The sage asks for information; Àjàpá the trickster asks, ‘‘About the person who was killed yesterday, is he already dead?’’
Cultural_Context: If you know the answer to a question already, don’t ask it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀nà irọ́ kì í pẹ́ẹ́ pin.
Target_Text_En: The path of deceit soon ends.
Cultural_Context: Deceit is soon exposed.

Source_Text_Yo: "Ọ̀ràn yí ò dùn mí": ẹ̀ẹ̀kanṣoṣo là ńwí i.
Target_Text_En: "This matter does not hurt me": stating it only once suffices.
Cultural_Context: If one is indifferent to something, it should not dominate one’s conversations.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rọ̀ ìkọ̀kọ̀, ní gba-n-gba ní ḿbọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Secret matters have open exposure as their ultimate destination.
Cultural_Context: Whatever is done in secret will eventually be brought to light.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rọ̀ ò pariwo.
Target_Text_En: The matter in question does not make a noise.
Cultural_Context: The matter under discussion poses little problem.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀tá ẹni kì í pòdù ọ̀yà.
Target_Text_En: One’s enemy never kills a huge cane rat.
Cultural_Context: One is always tempted to minimize the accomplishments of one’s enemies.

Source_Text_Yo: Pátá-pátá là ńfọ́jú, kùm̀bọ̀-kumbọ là ńdẹ́tẹ́; ojú à-fọ́-ì-fọ́-tán ìjà ní ńdá sílẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One’s blindness should be absolute, and one’s leprosy should pervade the whole body; half-blindness only brings dissension.
Cultural_Context: One’s condition should be definite, not ambiguous or undetermined.

Source_Text_Yo: Pátá-pátá leégún ńfaṣọ borí.
Target_Text_En: It is completely that the masquerader covers his head with his shroud.
Cultural_Context: One must be thoroughgoing in whatever one does.

Source_Text_Yo: Pẹ̀hìndà kí o ríṣe èké, fara pamọ́ kí o rí bí aṣení ti ńsọ.
Target_Text_En: Turn your back, and you will discover how the deceitful person behaves; hide, and you will find out what the detractor is saying.
Cultural_Context: If one could surprise them, one would discover the true nature of one’s enemies.

Source_Text_Yo: Pípọn niyì idẹ; ẹ̀jẹ̀ niyì oògun.
Target_Text_En: Redness is the glory of brass; efficaciousness is the glory of medicine.
Cultural_Context: Truth to one’s nature and fulfillment of one’s obligations are the determinants of one’s worth.

Source_Text_Yo: Pọ̀ǹgbà-pọngba là ḿbá odi.
Target_Text_En: Firmly planted and unshakable is the way one finds the city fortification.
Cultural_Context: An injunction to be firm and unshakable.

Source_Text_Yo: Purọ kóo níyì; bí a bá jáni tán, ẹ̀tẹ́ nÍ ńdà.
Target_Text_En: Lie and become renowned; once you have been found out, the result is disgrace.
Cultural_Context: The glory that results from deceit does not last.

Source_Text_Yo: Rìkíṣí pa wọ́n pọ̀ wọ́n dọ̀rẹ̀; kò lọ́jọ́ kò lóṣù ọ̀rẹ́ bàjẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Intrigue brought them together and they became friends; it did not take days, let alone months, before the friendship ended.
Cultural_Context: People united in friendship by intrigue soon become enemies.

Source_Text_Yo: Rìkíṣí pin, alábòsí lọ.
Target_Text_En: When the intrigue is terminated, the devious person takes his leave.
Cultural_Context: When the intrigue is exposed, the career of the devious person is over.

Source_Text_Yo: Sàráà baba ẹbọ.
Target_Text_En: Alms are the ultimate sacrifice.
Cultural_Context: It is blessed to give alms.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣìgìdì ò l nu fọhùn; ir ńpur fúnr.
Target_Text_En: Ṣìgìdì ò lẹ́nu fọhùn; irọ́ ńpurọ́ fúnrọ́.
Cultural_Context: The earthen idol has no mouth to speak; lies are lying to lies.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣìgìdì tí ò sọ̀rọ̀, a ò mẹni tí ńgbè.
Target_Text_En: [Since] the earthen idol does not speak, no one knows whose side it is on. T
Cultural_Context: No one can ascribe any position to a person who is cagey.

Source_Text_Yo: Ta la domi sí lára? Ta lòrìṣà ńgùn?
Target_Text_En: Who is the one on whom water was poured? Who is the one being mounted by the god?
Cultural_Context: The person receiving all the attention can not pretend not to be the one in need of attention.

Source_Text_Yo: Ta leṣinṣin ìbá gbè bí kò ṣe elégbò?
Target_Text_En: Who else will the flies flock after if not the person with open sores?
Cultural_Context: Opportunistic people can be expected to stick with those who offer them the most benefits.

Source_Text_Yo: Ta ló dè ọ́ tí ò ńkakọ?
Target_Text_En: Who has tied you down and thus forced you to confess your guilt?
Cultural_Context: Said to stop the mouths of people who protest too much as a result of a guilty conscience.

Source_Text_Yo: Wá jẹun. n ò jẹ. Ó fọgọ́rùn-ún okèlè tọ́ ọbẹ̀ wò.
Target_Text_En: Come join me at my meal.’’ ‘‘Thank you, but no.’’ Still he eats a hundred mouthfuls, just to taste the stew.
Cultural_Context: If you intend to decline an invitation, match your action to your words.

Source_Text_Yo: Wọ́n ní, ‘‘Àwòko, o bú ọba.’’ Ó ní ìgbà wo lòún ráàye bú ọba, kóun tó kọ igba lówùúrọ̀, igba lọ́sàn-án, igba lálẹ́, kóun tó fi àyìndà-yindà lù ú?
Target_Text_En: They said, ‘‘Mockingbird, you are accused of insulting the king.’’ It asked, when would it have time to insult the king, seeing that it must sing two hundred songs in the morning, two hundred in the afternoon, and two hundred at night, mixing it all up with some frolicsome notes?
Cultural_Context: The person in trouble will resort to ludicrous alibis to escape punishment.

Source_Text_Yo: Wọ́n ní kárúgbó gba ọmọ pọ̀n, ó ní ṣe bí wọ́n mọ̀ pé òun ò léhín; wọ́n ní kó pa ọmọ jẹ ni?
Target_Text_En: The old woman is asked to carry a child on her back, and she says but they know she has no teeth; was she asked to eat the child?
Cultural_Context: Said of people whose comment on a proposition is wildly irrelevant.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi àìmọ̀nà dá pàdé-m̀-pàdé.
Target_Text_En: One does not play the rendezvous game without knowing one’s way.
Cultural_Context: One should not enter into competition handicapped by ignorance.

Source_Text_Yo: Abúni ò tó abẹ̀rín; bẹ́ẹ̀ni abẹ̀rín ò mọ ẹ̀hìn ọ̀la.
Target_Text_En: The person who insults one is not as bad as the person who derides one; yet the person who derides one does not know what the future may bring.
Cultural_Context: Fortunes and circumstances may be reversed in time.

Source_Text_Yo: Adìẹ́ yẹ̀gẹ̀; a ṣe bí ó ṣubú.
Target_Text_En: The chicken lists to one side; we think it has fallen.
Cultural_Context: Never be too quick to celebrate the demise of a nemesis.

Source_Text_Yo: Àfẹ́ẹ̀rí kan ò ju ká rí igbó ńlá bọ́ sí lọ; ẹbọ kan ò ju ọ̀pọ̀ èèyàn lọ; "Òrìṣá gbé mi lé àtète" kan ò ju orí ẹṣin lọ.
Target_Text_En: There is no disappearing trick better than the availability of a dense forest to disappear into; there is no sacrifice more efficacious than having many people on one’s side; there is no ‘‘The gods have elevated me’’ that is higher than the back of a horse.
Cultural_Context: Practical and realistic moves are more reliable than mysterious expectations.

Source_Text_Yo: A-fi-tirẹ̀-sílẹ̀-gbọ́ tẹniẹlẹ́ni: Ọlọ́run ní mba gbọ́ tirẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: He-who-neglects-his-affairs-to-care-for others’-affairs: it is God that takes care of his affairs.
Cultural_Context: God takes care of the benevolent.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbò ò ṣéé mú; ọ̀dá ò ṣéé mú; ohun gbogbo ní ńtóbi lójú ahun.
Target_Text_En: A ram is too much to give; a gelded animal is too much to give; everything is excessive in the sight of a miser.
Cultural_Context: Expect no favor from a miser.

Source_Text_Yo: Àì-fi-kan-pe-kan ní ḿba kan jẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is failure-to-count-anything-as-significant that ruins things.
Cultural_Context: Minimizing problems results in disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìmète, àìmèrò, lọmọ ìyá mẹ́fà-á fi ńkú sóko ẹgbàafà.
Target_Text_En: Lack of resourcefulness and lack of thoughtfulness cause six siblings to die as pawns for only 12,000 cowries.
Cultural_Context: Pooling resources and wisdom ensures better results than going alone.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjẹ́gbà ni ti kọ̀ǹkọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Croaking-in-relays is the mark of frogs.
Cultural_Context: It is in the nature of sheep to follow and to lack initiative.

Source_Text_Yo: Akẹ́yinjẹ ò mọ̀ pé ìdí ńro adìẹ.
Target_Text_En: The person who gathers eggs to eat does not know that the chicken’s orifice hurts.
Cultural_Context: One should never be so preoccupied with one’s own pleasures that one does not care what they cost others.

Source_Text_Yo: A-lágbára-má-mèrò, baba ọ̀lẹ́.
Target_Text_En: He-who-has-strength-but-lacks-discretion [is the] father of laziness.
Cultural_Context: A powerful but thoughtless person is worse than the laziest person.

Source_Text_Yo: A-láì-mète-mèrò ọkọ tó fi adìẹ ìyàwó bọ orí ìyálé; bí baálé bá jẹ́ Ìkà, èwo ni tòrìṣà?
Target_Text_En: The shiftless, thoughtless husband makes the junior wife’s chicken a sacrifice to the senior wife’s head; if the husband is wicked, what about the god?
Cultural_Context: God will not accept offerings or prayers tainted with wickedness.

Source_Text_Yo: Aláràjẹ ò mọ ọdún; a-biṣu-úta-bí-igi.
Target_Text_En: He who purchases the food he eats cares not what the season is; his yams always flourish like trees.
Cultural_Context: The consumer does not know what the producer goes through.

Source_Text_Yo: Arúgbó ṣoge rí; àkísà-á lògbà rí.
Target_Text_En: The old person was once a dandy; the rag was once in fashion.
Cultural_Context: Those who are favored should remember that times and circumstances do change.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣírí-i náwó-náwó kì í tú lójú ahun.
Target_Text_En: The big spender is never disgraced in the presence of the miser.
Cultural_Context: The free spender will always be honored in the community.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣiwèrè ló bí ìyá ọ̀bọ.
Target_Text_En: It was an imbecile that gave birth to the mother of the monkey.
Cultural_Context: The fool belongs in the same lineage as the imbecile.

Source_Text_Yo: A-ti-ara-ẹni-roni, ajá ọdẹ.
Target_Text_En: A-creature-that-applies-another’s circumstances-to-itself: a hunter’s dog.
Cultural_Context: The hunter’s dog would do well to place itself in the shoes of the animals it hunts.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayídóborí tafà sókè: ojú Olúwaá tó wọn.
Target_Text_En: Those who cover their heads with mortars and shoot arrows into the sky: God’s eyes encompass them all.
Cultural_Context: God sees all acts of selfishness and wickedness toward others.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá rí òkú ìkà nílẹ̀, tí a fi ẹsẹ̀ ta á; ìkà-á di méji.
Target_Text_En: If one sees the corpse of a wicked person on the ground and one kicks it, there are then two wicked people.
Cultural_Context: If one returns evil for evil, one joins the ranks of the evil.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí o ṣe rere yó yọ sí ọ lára; bí o kò ṣe rere yó yọ sílẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: If your deeds are good, the benefits return to you; if your deeds are not good, they will be apparent to all.
Cultural_Context: Neither good nor evil goes for nought.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ó ti ńdun ọmọ ẹyẹ, bẹ́ẹ̀ ló ńdun ọmọ èèyàn.
Target_Text_En: As the young of birds know pain, so do the young of humans.
Cultural_Context: Others feel hurt, just as we do.

Source_Text_Yo: "Èrò tètè jí;" "Èrò jẹ́ ilẹ̀ ó mọ̀": tèrò là ńrò.
Target_Text_En: Traveler, get up early’’; ‘‘Traveler, wait until light’’: it’s all out of solicitousness for the traveler’s welfare.
Cultural_Context: Good intention does not guarantee good reception; the person of whose welfare one is being solicitous may resent one’s attention.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ ní ká má tafà; kí ni a ó fi lé ogun? Kànnà-kànnà la fi lé Boko.
Target_Text_En: You forbid us to shoot arrows, so with what shall we repell invaders? In the past the Boko were repelled with catapults.
Cultural_Context: It is unhelpful to deprive people of the tools they need for what they must do.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní fowó lògbà ló káyé já.
Target_Text_En: It is the person who uses his or her money to enjoy life who lives well.
Cultural_Context: Money is to be used to enjoy life.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní lówó kó ṣe bí ọba; àrà wo lahún fẹ́ẹ́ fi owó dá.
Target_Text_En: Whoever has riches should act like a king; what kind of feat can a miser perform with money?
Cultural_Context: The best thing to do with wealth is use it to live well.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní mọ owó-ó lò lowó ḿbá gbé.
Target_Text_En: It is the person who knows how to use wealth that wealth attaches to.
Cultural_Context: Wealth follows only those who know how to use it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a ṣe lóore tí kò dúpẹ́, bí ọlọ́ṣà-á kóni lẹ́rù ni.
Target_Text_En: A person for whom one does a favor but who shows no gratitude is like a robber who has stolen one’s goods.
Cultural_Context: Ingratitude is comparable to robbery.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó bá máa bímọ á yọ̀ fọ́lọ́mọ.
Target_Text_En: Whoever would have children of her own must rejoice with those who already have.
Cultural_Context: Those who seek good fortune must not begrudge those who are already fortunate.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó bèèrè ọ̀rọ̀ fẹ́ ìdí-i rẹ̀ ẹ́gbọ́.
Target_Text_En: Whoever asks about a matter genuinely wishes to know its causes.
Cultural_Context: If a person asks for help with a problem, one should appreciate the gesture and comply.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó gòkè, kó fa ọ̀rẹ́-ẹ rẹ̀ lọ́wọ́; ẹni tó rí jẹ, kó fún ọ̀rẹ́-ẹ rẹ̀ jẹ.
Target_Text_En: Whoever has reached the top, let him or her pull a friend by the hand; whoever has food to eat, let him or her share it with a friend.
Cultural_Context: If one has succeeded, one should give aid to those still struggling.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó so Ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ parí ọ̀ṣọ́; ẹni tó fúnni lọ́mọ-ọ́ parí oore.
Target_Text_En: The person who adorns herself with beads has done the ultimate in self-beautifying; the person who gives one a child [in marriage] has done the ultimate in favor.
Cultural_Context: There are certain gestures that cannot be surpassed.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ó ṣe ìbàjẹ́ èèyàn-án ṣe ìbàjẹ́ ara-a rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Whoever defames others defames himself or herself.
Cultural_Context: The evil one does to others reflects on oneself.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹyẹlé fi ẹ̀sín-in rẹ̀ pamọ́, ó ńṣe ẹ̀sín adìẹ.
Target_Text_En: The pigeon hides its own disgrace and goes ridiculing the chicken.
Cultural_Context: A person full of flaws insists on finding fault with others.

Source_Text_Yo: Igbá olóore kì í fọ́; àwo olóore kì í fàya; towó tọmọ ní ńya ilé olóore.
Target_Text_En: The calabash of a kindhearted person never breaks; the china plate of a kindhearted person never cracks; both riches and children ever converge in the home of a kindhearted person.
Cultural_Context: Good always attends those who are good.

Source_Text_Yo: Igba onípẹ̀lẹ́ kì Í fọ́; àwo onípẹ̀lẹ́ kì Í fàya.
Target_Text_En: The calabash belonging to a patient person never breaks; the china plate belonging to a patient person never cracks.
Cultural_Context: Patient people never come to grief.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé olóore kì í wó tán; tìkà kì í wó kù.
Target_Text_En: The home of a kindhearted person never collapses completely; the home of a wicked person always collapses, leaving nothing standing.
Cultural_Context: Good will attract good, and evil will attract evil.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé ọ̀ṣọnú àyàyó; ta ní jẹ́ yalé ahun káhun.
Target_Text_En: To visit the home of a generous person is to be plied with food aplenty; who would think of visiting a miser?
Cultural_Context: One’s generosity or miserliness makes one friends or loses one friends.

Source_Text_Yo: Inú búburú, oògùn òṣì.
Target_Text_En: Ill will [is the] medicine that ensures misfortune.
Cultural_Context: Misfortune will surely attend a person who harbors ill will toward others.

Source_Text_Yo: Inúure kì í pani, wàhálà ní ńkó báni.
Target_Text_En: Good will toward others does not kill; it only gets one into trouble.
Cultural_Context: One should be wary of kindness to others.

Source_Text_Yo: "Iyán dára, ọbẹ̀-ẹ́ dùn" ló pa Akíndélé lóko Ìgbájọ; "Òrìṣà, nkò fún ọ ní èdì jẹ" ló pa abọrìṣà Ìkirè.
Target_Text_En: "The pounded yam is good and the stew is delicious" killed Akíndélé on his farm at Ìgbájọ; ‘‘God, I will not give you some food to eat" is what killed the priest at Ìkiré.
Cultural_Context: Closed-fistedness and stinginess bring people nothing but misfortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyàwó jẹ ọkà jẹ igbá.
Target_Text_En: The wife ate the yam-flour meal and ate the calabash with it.
Cultural_Context: One should show consideration and exercise care in using others’ property.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí á ṣá a ṣá a, kí á gbọ̀n ọ́n gbọ̀n ọ́n; ká fi oko eéran sílẹ̀ ló dá eéran lára.
Target_Text_En: One may slash at it and slash at it, and one may shake the sand from its roots forever, but nothing affects the eéran grass like being abandoned.
Cultural_Context: The best treatment for a recalcitrant person is to shun him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: "Kí ní yìí ò pọ̀"; n ò lè fún ọ níbẹ̀; olúwarẹ̀ ahùn ni.
Target_Text_En: "This thing is not plentiful; I cannot give you any of it": the person is a miser.
Cultural_Context: However little one has, one should be willing to spare some for others.

Source_Text_Yo: "Kiní yìí tí o fún mi ò pọ̀": ahun ní ńjẹ́bẹ́.
Target_Text_En: "This thing that you have given me is not plentiful": that statement indicates a greedy person.
Cultural_Context: One should not be too demanding of one’s benefactors.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò mú ti ọwọ́ ẹ̀ wá ò gba tọwọ́ ẹni.
Target_Text_En: He-will-not-bring-what-he-has will not have what one has
Cultural_Context: A person who will not share what he or she has will not have a share of others' possessions either.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí kò sí; bẹ́ẹ̀ní ọmọ wọn ńyó.
Target_Text_En: "We have nothing, we have nothing!" Yet their children always have full stomachs.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who are too tightfisted to help others.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò tó ǹkan ní ńsọni dàhùn.
Target_Text_En: "There is not much of it" is what turns one into a miser.
Cultural_Context: Only a miser does not have enough to share with others.

Source_Text_Yo: Náwó-náwó kì í ṣàpà.
Target_Text_En: The big spender is not a prodigal.
Cultural_Context: There is nothing wrong with spending one’s money.

Source_Text_Yo: O jẹbẹ, o mubẹ, o babẹ̀ jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: There you ate, there you drank, and there you fouled.
Cultural_Context: Don’t besmirch a place that has been good to you.

Source_Text_Yo: "O kú iṣẹ́" ò lè bí aráyé nínú.
Target_Text_En: "Greetings to you at work" cannot invite people’s anger.
Cultural_Context: A courteous act does not expose one to trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: "Ó kún mi lójú," ẹ̀kọ Arogun; ọ̀kan ṣoṣo ni mo rà, igba ènì ló fi sí i.
Target_Text_En: "Its impression on me is tremendous’’: such is Arogun’s corn meal; I bought only one, but she gave me two hundred as makeweight [or extra measure].
Cultural_Context: Said of people who have gone well beyond the call of duty.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Mú wá, mú wá’’ lapá ẹyẹlé ńké.
Target_Text_En: ‘‘Bring! Bring!’’ is the sound of the pigeon’s wings.
Cultural_Context: Some people know only how to take, never how to give.

Source_Text_Yo: Obì kékeré kọjá òkúta ńlá.
Target_Text_En: A small kola nut is superior to a large stone.
Cultural_Context: A small gift is better than none at all.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrin tó bímọ tó bí olómitútù, wàhálà ọkọ ẹ̀-ẹ́ dínkù; kò ní já ewé mọ́, bẹ́ẹ̀ ni kò ní wa egbò.
Target_Text_En: A woman who bears a child that requires only cold water for all cures has saved her husband much worry; he will never again go searching for medicinal leaves, nor will he go digging roots.
Cultural_Context: A considerate woman is the joy of her husband.

Source_Text_Yo: Obínrin-ín bímọ fún ọ o ní o ò rínú ẹ̀; o fẹ́ẹ́ kó o nífun ni?
Target_Text_En: A woman has a child by you, and you still say you do not see her inside [know her mind]; would you have her expose her intestines?
Cultural_Context: People’s actions are enough, without accompanying words, to prove the extent of their commitment.

Source_Text_Yo: Ògún ò rọ ike; àgbẹ̀dẹ ò rọ bàtà; oko ò ṣòro-ó ro, àgbẹ̀dẹ ò pa ọkọ́ tà.
Target_Text_En: Ògún [god of metals] does not fashion ivory; the blacksmith does not make shoes; were farming not a difficult pursuit, the blacksmith would not manufacture hoes for sale.
Cultural_Context: One should appreciate people for their efforts and not belittle their accomplishments.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí ḿbá ahun náwó ḿbẹ lápò-o ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: What will help a miser spend his money is right there in his or her pocket.
Cultural_Context: The person who does not willingly share what he or she has will somehow find himself or herself being deprived of it.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò pa ewé-e kòkò; bó lè ya kó ya.
Target_Text_En: The rain beats the coco-yam leaf; if it will tear, let it tear.
Cultural_Context: When one has no invest ment in a property, one is likely to be care less in using it. Also, one will do what one pleases, and damn the consequences.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú la rí là ńkọrin òkú, òkú ò forin sáyé kó tó lọ.
Target_Text_En: It is out of regard for onlookers that one sings in praise of the dead; the dead did not prescribe a song before departing this life.
Cultural_Context: One does certain things out of a sense of propriety, not because one must.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú ní ńrójú ṣàánú.
Target_Text_En: Eyes are what look on eyes and fill with kindness.
Cultural_Context: When the eyes actually see suffering, they cannot avoid compassion.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú ọba ayé ló fọ́; tọ̀rún là kedere, ó ńwo aṣebi.
Target_Text_En: Only the king of this earth is blind; that of heaven is wide-eyed, watching evildoers.
Cultural_Context: God sees all acts of wickedness that may be hidden from earthly authorities.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkúlú ní tà ni ó ro tóun fún? Òkúlú tì wá ro tiẹ̀ fun Òkulú.
Target_Text_En: Òkulu asks with whom should he lodge his complaint? Did anybody lodge his complaint with Òkulu?
Cultural_Context: If one has been unhelpful to others, one should not expect any help from them.

Source_Text_Yo: Onígẹ̀gẹ̀ ìṣájú ba tìkẹhin jẹ.
Target_Text_En: The goitered person going in front ruins the fortunes of the one coming behind.
Cultural_Context: A person’s misdeeds compromise those coming after him.

Source_Text_Yo: Oore kì í gbé; ìkà kì í dànù; à-ṣoore jindò ní mmúni pàdánù oore.
Target_Text_En: A good deed does not go for nought; a wicked deed is never lost; drowning while doing a favor is what makes the good person lose out on the rewards for his goodness.
Cultural_Context: Every kindness, like every wickedness, is rewarded; one should be prudent, though, in doing favors.

Source_Text_Yo: Oore tí a ṣe fádìẹ ò gbé; bó pẹ́títí a ṣomi tooro síni lẹ́nu.
Target_Text_En: The favor that one does a chicken is not for nought; in due course it will make stew to delight one’s mouth.
Cultural_Context: There will always be a return for whatever favor one does for others.

Source_Text_Yo: Òṣónú ò bí èjìrẹ́; onínúure ní ḿbí ẹdun.
Target_Text_En: An ill-natured woman will not give birth to twins; only good-natured people give birth
Cultural_Context: Only good people are fortunate enough to have twins.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó ló ńpe ìná owó.
Target_Text_En: Money is what calls for spending money.
Cultural_Context: The availability of money creates the need to spend it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀gá Ìwátà, eṣú ò mọ olóòótọ́; eṣú dé, eṣú jẹ oko olóore.
Target_Text_En: Big shot of Ìwátà town; the locusts do not know who is honest; the locusts arrive and the locusts eat up the good person's farm.
Cultural_Context: Vandals care not wjhich property belongs to good people and which to bad people

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀mùtí kì í ṣàpà; owó ẹ̀ ló ńná.
Target_Text_En: The drunkard is not a prodigal; it is his money that he is spending.
Cultural_Context: One can spend one’s money as one wishes.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn-an-yàn ò sí nínúu iyánrán.
Target_Text_En: There is no compulsion in voluntary work.
Cultural_Context: Volunteering is not an obligation.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọtí gbélé ahun ó kan.
Target_Text_En: Wine stays in the home of the miser until it goes sour.
Cultural_Context: The miser would rather see things go bad than share them.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀tọ̀ niṣẹ́ olókùnrùn.
Target_Text_En: The assignment for an invalid must be different from everybody else’s.
Cultural_Context: People should be employed only according to their capabilities.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọwọ́ híhá àhájù ní ńdínà ire mọ́ ni.
Target_Text_En: Excessive stinginess is what slams the door of fortune in one’s face.
Cultural_Context: Miserliness will divert good fortune away from the miser.

Source_Text_Yo: Pẹ̀gàn-pẹ̀gàn-án bọ́ sóde kò ní láárí; ẹni tí ò rówó ṣe fújà ní ńpẹ̀gàn ẹni.
Target_Text_En: He who derides others steps outside and does not amount to much; it is he who has no basis for bragging that derides others.
Cultural_Context: People who belittle others are themselves worthless.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣe sílẹ̀: ẹrù-u rẹ̀ kì í pẹ́ níbodè.
Target_Text_En: He who extends kindness beforehand: his goods will not stay long at the frontier.
Cultural_Context: Thegenerous person will always find helpers to ease his passage.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣẹ̀gàn-ṣẹ̀gàn ò láṣọ méjì; pé-ń-pé laṣọ abúni ḿmọ.
Target_Text_En: The detractor of others does not possess a change of clothing; the garment of the in sulter of people is always skimpy.
Cultural_Context: People who make a habit of cutting others down never prosper either.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣìkà-ṣìkà-á fi díẹ̀ ṣe ara ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The wicked person does a little wickedness to himself or herself.
Cultural_Context: Wickedness has some adverse effect on the perpetrator.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣìkà-ṣìkà-á gbàgbé àjọbí, adánilóró gbàgbé ọ̀la.
Target_Text_En: The wicked forget kinship; the person who hurts others forgets tomorrow.
Cultural_Context: People who inflict injury on others forget that the gods of kinship will inflict punishment on them and that they themselves may be at the receiving end in the future.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣìkà-ṣìkà ò jẹ́ pe ara ẹ̀ níkà.
Target_Text_En: The wicked person will never describe himself as wicked.
Cultural_Context: The wicked always strive to appear as decent, kind people.

Source_Text_Yo: Tewé tegbò ní ńṣàánú àfòmọ́.
Target_Text_En: Both the leaf and the root take pity on the climbing parasite.
Cultural_Context: A plea for consideration from all and sundry.

Source_Text_Yo: Tigi tọ̀pẹ̀ ní ńṣàánú àfòmọ́.
Target_Text_En: Both trees and palms take pity on the climbing plant.
Cultural_Context: A plea for mercy from all and sundry.

Source_Text_Yo: Tigi tọ̀pẹ̀ ní ńsàánú ìyèré lóko.
Target_Text_En: Both trees and palms extend kindness to the African black pepper plant.
Cultural_Context: A plea for kind ness from others.

Source_Text_Yo: Tìkà toore, ọ̀kan kì í gbé.
Target_Text_En: Wickedness or kindness, neither goes for nought.
Cultural_Context: Wickedness and kindness will be rewarded unfailingly.

Source_Text_Yo: Tútù ní ńtẹnu ẹja wá.
Target_Text_En: Only coolness come out of the fish’s mouth.
Cultural_Context: Permit your mouth to say only soothing things.

Source_Text_Yo: Àì-lóbìnrin kò ṣé-é dákẹ́ lásán; ó tó ká pe gbogbo ayé kó bá ni gbọ́ ọ̀rọ̀ náà.
Target_Text_En: Not-having-a-woman is not a problem to keep secret; it merits appealing to the whole world to intervene in the matter.
