Cultural_Context: A man without a woman needs drastic measures to resolve his problem.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkẹ́bàjẹ́, ọmọ àgan-án-dáríjọ-bí.
Target_Text_En: Spoiled rotten, child-collectively-mothered by-barren-women.
Cultural_Context: Infertile women make poor mothers.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkẹ́jù tí ḿba ọmọ olówó jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Excessive pampering ruins the child of a wealthy person.
Cultural_Context: Children of wealthy parents are likely to be spoiled with too much pampering.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣèbàjẹ́ ńwá ẹni rere kúnra.
Target_Text_En: The evildoer seeks good people to associate with.
Cultural_Context: Evil people always seek the company of good people to burnish their image.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwòdì òkè ò mọ̀ pé ará ilẹ̀ ńwo òun.
Target_Text_En: The hawk in the sky does not know that ground dwellers are watching it.
Cultural_Context: One may be unaware, but one’s machinations are not hidden.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí eégún bá jóore, orí a yá àtọ́kùn-un rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: If a masquerader dances well, his attendant is filled with pride.
Cultural_Context: The accomplishments of one’s relatives give one cause for pride.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí eégún ẹní bá jóore, orí a yáni.
Target_Text_En: If one’s masquerader dances well, one is proud.
Cultural_Context: The accomplishments of one’s relatives give one cause for pride.

Source_Text_Yo: Bíbí ire ò ṣé-é fowó rà.
Target_Text_En: A good pedigree is not something one can buy with money.
Cultural_Context: Money cannot improve the circumstances of one’s birth.

Source_Text_Yo: Dídùn dídùn nilé olóyin; kíkorò nilé agbọ́n.
Target_Text_En: Sweetness is the constant characteristic of the honey seller’s home; bitterness is the permanent characteristic of the wasp’s home.
Cultural_Context: The good person will always be at tended by goodness, the wicked person by wickedness.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèyàn-án dára ó ku ìwà; ilé dára ó ku ìgbé.
Target_Text_En: A person may be attractive, but character still matters; a home may be gorgeous, but what matters is its livability.
Cultural_Context: Looks are not everything.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèyàn-án rìn, òjìjí tẹ̀ lé e; kò ṣé-é mú, kò ṣé-é jù sápò.
Target_Text_En: A person walks along, and his or her shadow follows; it cannot be grabbed, and it cannot be slipped into the pocket.
Cultural_Context: No one can hide his or her character.

Source_Text_Yo: Ehín funfun lẹ̀ṣọ́ ẹ̀rín; ìwà rere l ṣ èèyàn.
Target_Text_En: The adornment of a smile is white teeth; the adornment of a person is good character.
Cultural_Context: Good character is more valuable than good looks.

Source_Text_Yo: Ehín ọ̀kánkán obìnrín kán; olórí ẹwà-á lọ.
Target_Text_En: A woman’s front teeth break; the main stay of [her] beauty is demolished.
Cultural_Context: When one’s main asset is gone, one is as good as finished.

Source_Text_Yo: Èké kú, a gbẹ́lẹ̀ ó kan òkúta.
Target_Text_En: The devious person dies, and while digging his or her grave one strikes a rock.
Cultural_Context: Even the earth bears witness against the wicked.

Source_Text_Yo: Èké ṣíṣe ò ní ká má lòówó; ìkà ṣíṣe ò ní ká má dàgbà; ṣùgbọ́n ọjọ́ àtisùn lẹbọ.
Target_Text_En: Being devious does not prevent one from prospering; being evil does not prevent one from living long; but it is one’s dying day that one needs to worry about.
Cultural_Context: The devious and the evil may prosper and live long, but their end will be terrible.

Source_Text_Yo: Epo kì í tẹ́; iyọ̀ kì í tẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Palm oil never goes stale; salt never goes stale.
Cultural_Context: Certain things never go out of season or favor. Also, this is a prayer that a person may never be disgraced.

Source_Text_Yo: Èṣù ò níwà, a kọ́lé-e rẹ̀ síta.
Target_Text_En: Èṣù lacks good character; therefore, his house is built outdoors.
Cultural_Context: Also, this is a prayer that a person may never be disgraced.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹgbàá ọ̀bùn ò tó ọ̀kan ṣoṣo ọ̀gá.
Target_Text_En: Two hundred filthy persons are no match for one person of good repute.
Cultural_Context: One decent individual is worth more than two hundred tasteless people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀hìn ò sunwọ̀n: ajá mú awọ ẹkùn tẹ́ sùn.
Target_Text_En: The end is inauspicious: a dog sleeps on the hide of a leopard.
Cultural_Context: The way one is remem bered after death is a good indication of whether or not one lived and died well.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá ṣẹ̀ jalè lẹ́ẹ̀kàn, bó bá fàrán ogún ọ̀kẹ́ bora, aṣọ olè ló wọ.
Target_Text_En: Whoever stole once, if he or she later drapes himself or herself in expensive velvet cloth, is draped in stolen goods.
Cultural_Context: A reputation once ruined is impossible to mend.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bú ẹṣin lọ́bùn-ún jàre ẹṣin: ẹṣin ò bọ́jú lálẹ́; kò wẹsẹ̀ lówùúrọ̀; pẹ̀tẹ̀-pẹ́tẹ̀ èṣí ḿbẹ látẹ̀ẹ́lẹsẹ̀-ẹ ẹṣin.
Target_Text_En: Whoever calls the horse filthy is justified: the horse does not rinse its face at night; the horse does not wash its feet at night; there is year-old caked mud on the hooves of the horse.
Cultural_Context: If one does not look well to one’s behavior, one deserves the contempt of others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní fi ẹnu ra iyì, ẹ̀tẹ́ ẹ̀ ḿbọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The disgrace of the person who bought glory with his or her mouth is near at hand.
Cultural_Context: Underserved glory is soon exposed.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní mọ ẹni ò dàbí ẹni a mọ̀.
Target_Text_En: A person who knows one is not like a person one knows.
Cultural_Context: One can vouch for the character of a person one knows, not of a person who knows one.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni rere kì í kú sípò ìkà.
Target_Text_En: A good person does not die the death of an evil person.
Cultural_Context: Each person will be recompensed according to his or her character.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó lórí rere tí kò níwà, ìwà-a rẹ̀ ni yó ba orí-i rẹ̀ jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: A person who is blessed with good fortune but lacks good character: his character will ruin his or her good fortune.
Cultural_Context: Evil character ruins good destiny.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó lówó tí kò níwà, owó olówó ló ní.
Target_Text_En: The person who has riches but lacks good character has other people’s riches.
Cultural_Context: A rich person without good character soon loses his or her riches to others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó pẹ́ lóko ọ̀pẹ ló ní ká dá àbá kábàá.
Target_Text_En: The person who stayed too long on the palm-wine farm is the one who encouraged all sorts of speculation about what he was up to.
Cultural_Context: If one’s behavior is devious, people are justified in wondering about one’s character.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹsẹ̀ igúnnugún tí mọ ọbẹ̀ jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The legs of vultures, which ruin the stew.
Cultural_Context: An abomination [is] like the legs of a vulture in a stew.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹsẹ̀-ẹ́ pọ̀ lẹ́hìn-in kòrikò.
Target_Text_En: There is a multitude of feet in the wake of the wolf.
Cultural_Context: An illustrious person attracts a great following.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú yá ju ẹ̀sín.
Target_Text_En: Death is preferable to disgrace.
Cultural_Context: One should die rather than besmirch one’s name.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé dára ó ku ẹkẹ́; èèyàn-án dára ó ku ìwà.
Target_Text_En: The house is beautiful but for its pillars; a person is handsome, but what of character?
Cultural_Context: Bad character nullifies any charm a person might have.

Source_Text_Yo: "Ìṣe ẹ̀ ni" ó jẹ́ ká mọ ikú àbíkú.
Target_Text_En: "That is his or her habit" keeps one from knowing when an àbíkú is really dying.
Cultural_Context: One who cries "wolf" too many times will attract no one in times of trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìwà kì í fi oníwà sílẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Character will not forsake its owner.
Cultural_Context: One cannot shed one’s character.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìwà lẹ̀sìn.
Target_Text_En: Character is worship.
Cultural_Context: One’s worship and prayers are only as efficacious as one’s character is good.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìwà lòrìṣà; bí a ti hù ú sí ní ńgbeni sí.
Target_Text_En: Character is a god; just as one lives it, so it succors one.
Cultural_Context: One’s fortune depends on one’s character.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìwà rere lẹ̀ṣọ́ èèyàn; ehín funfun lẹ̀ṣọ́ ẹ̀rín.
Target_Text_En: Good character is a person’s [best] adorn ment; white teeth are the adornment of a smile.
Cultural_Context: A person’s most desirable trait is good character, just as a smile’s best aspect is white teeth.

Source_Text_Yo: Ká ròhìn ẹni ò tó ká bá ẹni bẹ́ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: To have people say good things about one is nothing like being found to vindicate the report.
Cultural_Context: One’s real character is more important than what others say.

Source_Text_Yo: "Kítìjú pa mí" ààrẹ èpè ni.
Target_Text_En: "May I die of shame": that is the chief of all curses.
Cultural_Context: No fate is worse than disgrace.

Source_Text_Yo: Màá-ṣe-é-màá-lọ obìnrin, ojú-u pópó lòrìṣà-a rẹ̀ ńgbé
Target_Text_En: I-will-do-as-I-wish-and-go-my-way woman: the memorial shrine to her goddess belongs by the roadside.
Cultural_Context: A wife who cares not about her character is not worth keeping.

Source_Text_Yo: Méjì là ńwé èèyàn; bí ò ṣe yíyìn a ṣe bíbú.
Target_Text_En: There are two ways of speaking about people; if it is not in praise, it will be in castigation.
Cultural_Context: One has either a good reputation or bad, never neutral.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Mo bí, mo bí’’ kì í ṣe ọmọ rere.
Target_Text_En: "I have just had a baby; I have just had a baby!" does not make for good breeding.
Cultural_Context: Frequent births are less desirable than painstaking child rearing.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó di orí ẹni ó bàjẹ́, àì-mọ̀wà-á-hù ni.
Target_Text_En: [If] all was ruined during one’s watch, that spells a defect in character.
Cultural_Context: A person of good character will not be responsible for social disasters.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrin tí kò níwà, ìyá ẹ̀ ní ḿbá ṣorogún.
Target_Text_En: A woman without good character will have only her mother as co-wife.
Cultural_Context: A woman without good character is unlikely to find a husband.

Source_Text_Yo: Obínrin tó bímọ tí ò gbọ́n fabẹ́ jóná.
Target_Text_En: A woman who gives birth to a child that lacks wisdom only singed her genitals.
Cultural_Context: A child who grows up lacking wisdom is the bane of his or her mother.

Source_Text_Yo: Òbúkọ-ọ́ dé, òórùn-ún dé.
Target_Text_En: The he-goat has arrived; stink has arrived.
Cultural_Context: When evil people arrive at a gathering, dissension ensues.

Source_Text_Yo: Odò gbẹ má gbẹ́ orúkọ.
Target_Text_En: Rivers dry up but not their names.
Cultural_Context: One’s deeds will survive one.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú ìkà la ti ńfi ọmọ olóore jọba.
Target_Text_En: It is in the presence of the wicked person that the son of the good person is crowned king.
Cultural_Context: The wicked will live long enough to see the good prosper.

Source_Text_Yo: Olè kì í gbọ́ orúkọ ẹ̀ kó dúró.
Target_Text_En: A thief does not hear his name and stand in place.
Cultural_Context: A person who has something to hide is always worried about being exposed.

Source_Text_Yo: Oníwàpẹ̀lẹ́: a-báni-gbé-tuni-lára.
Target_Text_En: A mild-mannered person [is] one with whom cohabitation envelops one in ease.
Cultural_Context: A mild-mannered person is a joy to live with.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrìṣà nìwà; bí a ti hù ú ló ṣe ńgbeni.
Target_Text_En: Character is a god; it aids one according to how one uses it.
Cultural_Context: One’s character determines one’s fortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Orúkọ ẹni ní ńjẹ́rìí ẹni lókèèrè.
Target_Text_En: One’s name is one’s most effective advocate abroad.
Cultural_Context: Your reputation determines what people who do not know you go by.

Source_Text_Yo: Orúkọ lẹ̀gbọn oyè
Target_Text_En: A name is the elder of a chieftaincy title.
Cultural_Context: A good name is better than an important position.

Source_Text_Yo: Orúkọ tí a sọ ọmọ ní ḿmọ́mọ lára.
Target_Text_En: It is the name a child is given that sticks to the child.
Cultural_Context: People behave later in life the way they were brought up.

Source_Text_Yo: Òyìnbó ńlọ ó ṣu sága.
Target_Text_En: The white man takes his leave; he shits on the chair.
Cultural_Context: Said of persons who leave a mess of problems behind when they depart a place.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ́ tán lára ọmọ tí ńjẹ eérú.
Target_Text_En: There is no longer anything worth calling a child in a child that eats ashes.
Cultural_Context: A youth whose habits are filthy and bestial is worthless.

Source_Text_Yo: Pála-pàla nilé ìgbín, igbó rere nilé ahun.
Target_Text_En: The home of the snail is ever disorganized, but the home of the tortoise is a tidy bush.
Cultural_Context: One can always expect to find certain people in an orderly state.

Source_Text_Yo: Sán ọ̀bẹ sùn, fi apó rọrí; ìwà ọmọ ní ṣe ọmọ jẹ òkígbẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Tie a knife on you before you sleep; use a quiver as your pillow: your character forces you to resort to charms for rendering cut lasses harmless against your flesh.
Cultural_Context: People whose characters are evil have good reason to fear attack from others.

Source_Text_Yo: Tìwà tìwà là ńràjò.
Target_Text_En: It is in the company of one’s character that one goes on a journey.
Cultural_Context: No one leaves his or her character at home when venturing abroad.

Source_Text_Yo: Yíyẹ ní ńyẹ ẹyẹlé; dídẹ̀ ní ńdẹ àdàbà lọ́rùn.
Target_Text_En: The fate of the pigeon is always to enjoy good report; the fate of the dove is always to be at peace.
Cultural_Context: A way of wishing people peace and good regard.

Source_Text_Yo: TẸ̀gbá tẸ̀sà ló mọ Láfì lágẹmọ; gbogbo ayé ló mọ Tẹlẹ̀mú lólè.
Target_Text_En: Both the Ẹ̀gbá and the Ẹ̀sà people know that Láfì is like the chameleon; the whole world knows Tẹlmú as a thief.
Cultural_Context: Said of aperson whose bad character is common knowledge.

Source_Text_Yo: Akíríboto kì í lójú awẹ́; ẹ̀là ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ kì í lójú àtókùnbọ̀.
Target_Text_En: One-piece kola nut has no cleavage lines; a split bead has no string hole.
Cultural_Context: A defective thing or person is not as well off as a whole thing or person.

Source_Text_Yo: Àlàáfíà baba ẹ̀ṣọ́; ojúrírí baba ara líle.
Target_Text_En: Well-being, father of commanding presence; peace of mind, father of well-being.
Cultural_Context: Without well-being there is no good impression; without peace of mind there is no well-being.

Source_Text_Yo: Àlàáfíà baba ọ̀rẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Well-being, father of friendship.
Cultural_Context: Nothing conduces to friendship like well-being.

Source_Text_Yo: Anìkànrìn ejò là ńfàdá pa.
Target_Text_En: It is a snake that travels alone that one kills with a machete.
Cultural_Context: The lone traveler is vul nerable to opportunistic attacks.

Source_Text_Yo: Ara líle loògùn ọrọ̀.
Target_Text_En: A healthy body is the medicine for wealth.
Cultural_Context: Health is wealth.

Source_Text_Yo: Aràrá kì í yin Ọlọ́run, àfi bó bá rárọ tí ńrákò.
Target_Text_En: A dwarf does not show gratitude to God until he sees a crawling cripple.
Cultural_Context: Until seeing people who are worse off, one does not appreciate one’s own good fortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣunú ò mọ̀-ọ́ láyọ̀; ó dìgbà tó bá rí ẹni tí kò lè ṣu.
Target_Text_En: The person who has diarrhea does not know his or her good fortune until seeing some one who cannot relieve himself or herself.
Cultural_Context: Until seeing others who are worse off, one makes too much of one’s misfortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Bírí lolongo ńyí; a kì í bá òkùnrùn ẹyẹ lórí ìtẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The orange waxbill is always sprightly; one never finds an invalid bird in a nest.
Cultural_Context: The person addressed is ever healthy or will ever be healthy.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun à ńjẹ kọ́ là ńtà.
Target_Text_En: What one eats is not what one sells.
Cultural_Context: One should satisfy one’s needs before thinking about disposing of the excess.

Source_Text_Yo: Olókùnrùn ẹ̀ṣọ́ kì í ru ẹkù; kí alára tún ara mú
Target_Text_En: A sickly warrior does not carry rope snares; everyone should prepare properly for the task at hand.
Cultural_Context: People who have important duties to perform should gird up their loins accordingly.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í nìkan gbé agán kẹ́sẹ́-ẹ rẹ̀ má wọ̀ọ́lẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not carry a masquerader’s shroud by oneself and succeed in keeping its train off the ground.
Cultural_Context: One can succeed in certain ventures only with the aid of others.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í nìkan jayé.
Target_Text_En: One does not enjoy life alone.
Cultural_Context: A person without other people is nothing.

Source_Text_Yo: Abẹ́rẹ́ kí í nù tòun tòwú nídìí.
Target_Text_En: A needle is never lost with a thread in its eye.
Cultural_Context: As the thread will reveal where the needle is, a person with relatives will always have people interested in his or her fate.

Source_Text_Yo: Abímitán ò da n kan; ara la fi ńré.
Target_Text_En: "I am well born" guarantees nothing; all it permits is flaunting.
Cultural_Context: It is personal qualities, not birth, that determine one’s fortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Abiyamọ, a-bẹ̀hìn-jíjà.
Target_Text_En: Nursing mother with a fighting back.
Cultural_Context: The child she carries fights, and fights for her

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà ò lówó a ní kò gbọ́n; olówó ńṣe bí ọba lóko.
Target_Text_En: An elderly man has no money, and we say he lacks wisdom; the rich man is like a king on his farm.
Cultural_Context: Money is everything.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà tí ńfọ̀ ní káà láìlówólọ́wọ́, akọ ajá ní ńgbó.
Target_Text_En: An elder sounding off in the back yard with out money in his possession is like a barking male dog.
Cultural_Context: Money makes the person.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàtọ́ ò jọ obí; ọmọ-ọlọ́mọ ò jọ tẹni.
Target_Text_En: A foster child is not like a child one gave birth to; other people’s children are not the same as one’s own.
Cultural_Context: There is no substitute for one’s own possession.

Source_Text_Yo: Agbọ̀ràndùn bí ìyá ò sí; ẹni tó ní baba ló tó ara-á ré.
Target_Text_En: There is no commiserator like one’s mother; only those who have fathers dare to be im pudent.
Cultural_Context: With the backing of a powerful patron, one can attempt anything.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìkọ́wọ́rìn ejò l m aráyé fi ńfàdá pa wọ́n.
Target_Text_En: The failure-to-travel-in-groups habit of snakes makes it easy for humans to kill them with machetes.
Cultural_Context: Those who hang together will not hang separately.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìlẹ́bíyéye làìní aáwọ̀ lọ́rùn.
Target_Text_En: Not-having-numerous-relatives explains not having quarrels to attend to.
Cultural_Context: Many relatives make many quarrels.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìlówó ló sí; bí a bá lówó ló w, tajá tẹran ní ọmọ bá ni tan.
Target_Text_En: Lack of money is lack of friends; if you have money at your disposal, every dog and every goat will claim to be related to you.
Cultural_Context: Money makes the person, socially.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìlówólọ́wọ́ kì í ṣàìsàn; àìníṣẹ́ lọ́ràn.
Target_Text_En: Lack of money is no disease; it is lack of work that is a disaster.
Cultural_Context: As long as one has a job, one has hope.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìmọ èèyàn lọjà ò tà.
Target_Text_En: It is not-knowing-people that makes one unable to sell one’s wares.
Cultural_Context: To know people is to be a successful trader.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìsí ẹnìkẹta ni ẹni méjì-í fi ńja àjàkú.
Target_Text_En: It is the absence of a third person that makes it possible for two people to fight to the death.
Cultural_Context: Communal living minimizes the effects of personal conflicts.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá tó lẹ́ni lẹ́hìn á pbọ; èèyàn tó lẹ́ni lẹ́hìn á jàre ẹjọ́.
Target_Text_En: A dog that has people behind it will kill a monkey; a person with people behind him will win lawsuits.
Cultural_Context: With people behind one, one can accomplish the impossible.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajániláyà bí àì-lówó-lọ́wọ́, àìlówó baba ìjayà, owó ní ńtúniṣe.
Target_Text_En: Frightful-thing-like-lack-of-ready-money, lack-of-money [is] father of frights; it is money that repairs a person’s fortunes.
Cultural_Context: Lack of money is a frightful condition.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajé nìyá ògo.
Target_Text_En: Wealth is the mother of glory.
Cultural_Context: Money makes all things possible.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajé tún ọmọ bí.
Target_Text_En: Wealth brings rebirth.
Cultural_Context: However one was born, wealth makes one over.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjòjì ó rẹ́ni jẹ́rìí-i rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The stranger has no one to bear witness for him or her.
Cultural_Context: A stranger cannot hope for vindication against an indigene.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjọrìn ní ńyẹ èrò.
Target_Text_En: Traveling in company best suits the wayfarer.
Cultural_Context: There is glory in numbers.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkọ́bí ẹni ní ńrọni.
Target_Text_En: It is one’s firstborn that is one’s support.
Cultural_Context: One’s heir is also one’s security in old age.

Source_Text_Yo: A-kọrin-láì-lélégbè, bí ẹní lu agogo lásán.
Target_Text_En: He-who-sings-and-lacks-a-supporting chorus [is] the same as one who merely beats a gong.
Cultural_Context: A chorus enhances a solo performance.

Source_Text_Yo: Alááyan ní ńjẹun ogun.
Target_Text_En: It is the industrious person who enjoys the bounty of war.
Cultural_Context: To the valiant belong the spoils.

Source_Text_Yo: Alágẹmọ ò rẹ́ni wá wòran òun; ẹní bá gbọ́ ṣẹ́ṣẹ́, èèyàn ní nsáré.
Target_Text_En: The chameleon has no audience to watch it; if one hears footsteps, it is people that are running.
Cultural_Context: People should know the limits of their capability and act accordingly.

Source_Text_Yo: Ará ilé ẹni ò ṣeun; èèyàn ẹni ò sunwọ̀n; a ò lè fi wé àlejò lásán.
Target_Text_En: The members of one’s household have not done well by one; one’s relatives are not good-natured; yet one cannot liken them to mere strangers.
Cultural_Context: Whatever one may have against one’s own people, they are still pref erable to strangers.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtàm̀pàkò ni oníkìmí ìka; baba ọmọ-ọ́ kú ọmọ-ọ́ dẹyọ.
Target_Text_En: The thumb is the pillar among fingers; a father dies and the children are disunited.
Cultural_Context: As thumb to fingers, so is a father to his children: remove the one and the others are dispersed.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtàm̀pàkò ò sí ìká dẹ̀tú; baba ọmọ́ kú ọmọ́ dẹyọ.
Target_Text_En: The thumb is missing and the fingers be come unbunched; the father dies and the children become individuals.
Cultural_Context: Without the thumb, the fingers cannot be bunched; with out a father the children are dispersed.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtàrí ni ó jẹkóòrùn ó pa àgbọ̀n ìsàlẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is the skull that keeps the sun off the chin below.
Cultural_Context: As the chin is beholden to the skull, one is beholden to one’s benefactor.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtẹ́wọ́ lará; ìgbọ̀nwọ́ niyèkan.
Target_Text_En: One’s palms are one’s relatives; one’s elbows are one’s siblings of the same mother.
Cultural_Context: The most reliable things are one’s own resources.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá mú iná kúrò lóko, àfi àgbẹ̀ tí yó jọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀; bí a bá mú ti Ìbíkúnlé Olókè kúrò, Balógun Ògbóríẹfọ̀n, à di agíraṣe.
Target_Text_En: If one removed fire from the farm, only farmers satisfied with a diet of bananas would be unconcerned; but for Ìbíkúnlé Olókè, General Ògbórí Ẹfọ̀n, we could achieve nothing.
Cultural_Context: Deprived of their founts of power, people are ineffective.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá ní ohun àgbà, bí èwe là ńrí.
Target_Text_En: If one does not have the accouterments of elders, one seems a mere youth.
Cultural_Context: An elder is not an elder without the means to be one.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá rẹ́ni fẹ̀hìntì bí ọ̀lẹ là ńrí; bí a kò bá rẹ́ni gbójúlé, à tẹra mọ́ṣẹ́ ẹni.
Target_Text_En: With no one to lean on, one seems a lazy person; with no one to rely on, one faces one’s duties with devotion.
Cultural_Context: The person with powerful support seems better than his or her peers; lacking such support, one should redouble one’s efforts.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò lówó, à léèyàn; bí a kò léèyàn à lóhùn rere lòrun.
Target_Text_En: If one lacks money, one should have people; if one lacks people, one should be pleasant in one’s speech.
Cultural_Context: If you lack a social as set, make up for it in other ways.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ebí bá kúrò nínú ìsẹ́, ìsẹ́ bùṣe.
Target_Text_En: If hunger is removed from poverty, poverty comes to an end.
Cultural_Context: Whoever has food to eat is not poor.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí eégún ò bá mọ Òdèré, tí kò m Àṣàkẹ́, atọ́kùn-ún rẹ̀ ní ńwi.
Target_Text_En: If a masquerader cannot recognize Òdèré and cannot recognize Àṣàkẹ́, his attendant has to tell him.
Cultural_Context: One’s aides are there to make up for one’s deficiencies.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí eégún yó lọ, a di ìròjú fún atọ́kùn.
Target_Text_En: When the time comes for the masquerader to depart, the attendant begins to grieve.
Cultural_Context: One is saddened at losing one’s benefactor and patron.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ẹni ńlá ò bá tán, ọ̀ràn ńlá ò lè pani.
Target_Text_En: If there is no scarcity of great people, a great problem cannot kill one.
Cultural_Context: As long as one has powerful patrons, difficult problems will not defeat one.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ìbí ò tẹ̀, bí ìbí ò wọ́, ẹni tí a bá níwájú tó baba-á ṣe fúnni.
Target_Text_En: If the pedigree is not bent, if the pedigree is not crooked, the person ahead of one is enough to play the role of father.
Cultural_Context: Unless there is dissension in the family, the elders in it exercise responsibility over the youth.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ìtì ò wó, ọwọ́ kì í ba ìṣẹ́pẹ́.
Target_Text_En: If the trunk does not fall, the twigs are not endangered.
Cultural_Context: One is safe as long as one’s protector is around.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ìyá ò sí, ta ní jẹ́ ṣe ọmọ ọlọmọ lóore.
Target_Text_En: If there is no mother, who would show kindness to another person’s child?
Cultural_Context: A child can look only to its mother for protection.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ìyàwó ọ̀lẹ́ bá dàgbà, olówó ni yó gbé e.
Target_Text_En: When the woman betrothed to a lazy person matures, the rich man marries her.
Cultural_Context: The idle will be left empty-handed.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí kò bá sí owó, baba ẹnìkan ò ju baba ẹnìkan lọ.
Target_Text_En: In the absence of money, one person’s father is no greater than another person’s father.
Cultural_Context: Money determines status.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí kò sí igi lẹ́hìn ọgbà ọgbà á wó; bí kò sí akọ nínú-u bàtá bàtá ò níí le.
Target_Text_En: Without a post behind the fence, the fence will collapse; without masculine forces in bàtá drumming, the music is not gripping.
Cultural_Context: Without his or her main support, a person is nothing.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí kò sí towó, kí la ó fòwò ṣe?
Target_Text_En: Were it not for the matter of money, what would one want with trading?
Cultural_Context: The need for money gets one into a trade.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí kò sí tỌya, ogun a ti kó Irá, bí kò sí tOlúfọ̀n, ogun a ti kó Ifọ̀n lọ.
Target_Text_En: But for the goddess Ọya, Irá would have been sacked in a war; but for the god Olúfọ̀n, Ifọ́n would have been destroyed.
Cultural_Context: Thanks to one’s protector, one survives.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ó ku òní ku ọ̀la kí òùngbẹ pa awọ́nrínwọ́n, òjò yó rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: If it is only a matter of days before the iguana dies of thirst, rain will fall.
Cultural_Context: For those the gods favor, rescue will come before disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ó ku òní ku lá kí ọmọ olódò-ó kú fún òùngbẹ, ọ̀ṣọ̀rọ̀ òjò á rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: If it is only a matter of days before the child of the river goddess dies of thirst, a torrential rain will fall.
Cultural_Context: The favored of the gods will always be rescued before disaster falls.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí òkété bá dàgbà, ọmú ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀ ní ḿmu.
Target_Text_En: When the giant rat becomes old, it sucks from its child’s breast.
Cultural_Context: In one’s old age, one depends on one’s children.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí olówó sọ̀rọ̀, tó ṣèké, ajé a ní kò purọ́.
Target_Text_En: If a rich person speaks and lies, money will say he or she has not lied.
Cultural_Context: A rich person can get away with any lie.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí òtútù ńpa ìwọ̀fà wọn a ní ó kó ìṣe-e rẹ̀ dé; bí ó ńpa olówó wọn a ní kó rọ́jú kó ata sẹ́nu.
Target_Text_En: When the pawn has a fever, people say he is up to his usual tricks; when the owner is thus afflicted, they urge him to make an effort to eat.
Cultural_Context: The poor cannot expect the consideration the rich enjoy.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí owó bá sì nínú ọ̀rọ̀, a súni pa.
Target_Text_En: If money is removed from a matter, it bores one to death.
Cultural_Context: Money gives weight to matters.

Source_Text_Yo: Bíọ́-bíọ́ tí apó ńdá, ọrán ló gbójúlé.
Target_Text_En: The quiver’s boasting is due to its confidence in the backing of the bow.
Cultural_Context: A person who is sure of his backers can boast as much as he likes.

Source_Text_Yo: Bọ̀rọ̀kìnní ju ọlọ́rọ̀ lọ.
Target_Text_En: The popular rich man is superior to the merely wealthy.
Cultural_Context: To be well regarded is better than to be rich.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbí-ì rẹ-ẹ́ sẹ nù ò ńyọ̀; o ò mọ̀ pé irú ẹ ló ńrá.
Target_Text_En: Your pregnancy aborts and you rejoice; you are not aware that it is your kind that is perishing.
Cultural_Context: What in the short run is a boon might turn out in the long run to be a disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Ire kì í dé ká má gbọ̀ọ́ ohùn-un gudu gudu.
Target_Text_En: Good fortune does not arrive without being trailed by the sound of the gudugudu drum.
Cultural_Context: Good fortune must be greeted with rejoicing.

Source_Text_Yo: Òwúsúwusù-ú mú ojú ọ̀run bàjẹ̀; gùdẹ̀ gùdẹ̀ ò jẹ́ kóòrùn ó ràn.
Target_Text_En: The fog besmirches the face of the sky; the clouds keep the sun from shining.
Cultural_Context: An unfortunate matter keeps happiness or cheerfulness at bay.

Source_Text_Yo: Wẹ̀ níwọ̀n; ajé ní ńwẹni.
Target_Text_En: Limit how often you take a bath; it is wealth that grooms a person.
Cultural_Context: Wealth beautifies more efficiently than a lot of grooming.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í délé ayò ká má bàá ọmọ.
Target_Text_En: One never arrives at the home of the ayò game without finding children.
Cultural_Context: A prayer for a blessing of children in abundance.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà ló tó Orò-ó lọ̀; ọba ló tó ehín erin-ín fun.
Target_Text_En: Only a [male] elder is qualified to invoke Orò; only a king is qualified to blow a horn carved out of elephant tusk.
Cultural_Context: Certain tasks are for august people only.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà mẹ́ta ní ḿmọ ìdí ẹẹ́ta.
Target_Text_En: It takes three elders to know the mystery behind three.
Cultural_Context: It takes the pooled wisdom of many elders to resolve deep matters.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà ní ńkọ́ àpò àgbà.
Target_Text_En: Only an elder may hang the satchel of an elder [on his shoulder].
Cultural_Context: Certain privileges are restricted to elders.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà ó sí ìlú bàjẹ́; baálé ilé kú ilé dahoro.
Target_Text_En: Without elders a town is ruined; the patri]arch of the compound dies, and the household becomes an empty shell.
Cultural_Context: Elders hold a community together.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò kú, a ó jẹ ẹran tó tó erin.
Target_Text_En: If one does not die, one will eat as much as an elephant's meat.
Cultural_Context: Whoever has life has things to accomplish.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò kú, ìṣe ò tán.
Target_Text_En: If one does not die, one’s accomplishments are not over.
Cultural_Context: As long as one has life, one has feats to accomplish.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí orí pọẹ́ nílẹ̀, á di ire.
Target_Text_En: If a head remains long on earth, it becomes fortunate.
Cultural_Context: If one lives long enough, one will prosper.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọmọdé ò kú, àgbà ní ńdà.
Target_Text_En: If a youth does not die, he becomes an elder.
Cultural_Context: In time even a youth assumes the mantle of an elder.

Source_Text_Yo: Iná kú feérú bojú; ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ kú fọmọ ẹ̀ rọ́pò; olóyè-é kú foyè sílẹ̀ lọ.
Target_Text_En: The fire dies and covers its face with ashes; the banana tree dies and replaces itself with an offshoot; a chief dies and leaves his title behind.
Cultural_Context: When a person dies, survivors inherit his or her place and property.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyàwó dùn-ún gbé; ọm dùn-ún kó jáde.
Target_Text_En: Marriage is a pleasurable activity, and so is christening a child.
Cultural_Context: Marrying and christening are pleasures.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrin tó jí ní kùtùkùtù tó ní Ọlọ́run ni yó mọ oye ọmọ òun, ó gbégbá ìrégbè.
Target_Text_En: A woman who at the dawn of her life vows that only God will know how many children she will bear has placed a load of trouble on her own head.
Cultural_Context: Children are not an unmixed blessing for women.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ tí a bá kú, ọwọ́ ò gba okòó; ọmọ ẹni ní ńjogún ẹni.
Target_Text_En: The day one dies one’s hand cannot hold a coin; one’s children inherit one’s property.
Cultural_Context: One cannot take earthly possessions into the grave but must leave them to one’s survivors.

Source_Text_Yo: Ólọ́mọ́ kúrò ní "kí ló bí?"
Target_Text_En: A person who has a child is not a person who can be asked, "What did you sire?"
Cultural_Context: A child is a child; whoever has one cannot be taunted with childlessness.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ bẹẹrẹ, òṣì bẹẹrẹ
Target_Text_En: A multitude of children, a multitude of misery
Cultural_Context: Children are desirable but not in excess.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ ẹni kì í di méjì kínu kanni.
Target_Text_En: One’s mind does not become sour because one has had a second child.
Cultural_Context: People always rejoice at having children.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ ẹni là ḿbí; ẹrú ẹni là ńrà lọ́jà.
Target_Text_En: One gives birth to one’s children; one buys one’s slave in the market.
Cultural_Context: No one can buy children in the market.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ kì í nù bí ẹranko.
Target_Text_En: A child does not become lost like an animal.
Cultural_Context: One must place great value on one’s children.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ́ mọ ìyá ẹ̀; talágbàtọ́ nìyà.
Target_Text_En: A child knows its mother; the foster mother’s lot is misery.
Cultural_Context: A child will never treasure a foster mother as much as a natural mother.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ ò láyọ̀lé; ẹni ọmọ́ sin ló bímọ.
Target_Text_En: Children are not to be rejoiced over; only those whose children bury them really have children.
Cultural_Context: The most valuable service one may expect from one’s children is that they attend to one’s funeral.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ ọlọ́mọ-ṣòro-ó pè rán níṣẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Another person’s child is not easy to send on an errand.
Cultural_Context: There is nothing like having one’s own children.

Source_Text_Yo: "Ọmọ- mí kú" yá ju "Ọmọ mí nù" lọ.
Target_Text_En: "My child is dead" is far better than "My child is lost."
Cultural_Context: One may lose a child to death, but it is unspeakable parental irresponsibility simply to lose a child.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí aboyún bá sọ, ẹni méjì ló sọ ọ́.
Target_Text_En: Whatever a pregnant woman says is said by two people.
Cultural_Context: A pregnant woman’s words should not be taken lightly.

Source_Text_Yo: Tọmọ tó máa kú, tọmọ tó máa yè, ká yọ̀ fọ́lọ́mọ.
Target_Text_En: Whether the child will survive or not, let us rejoice with a person who has a baby.
Cultural_Context: Childbirth is always an occasion for joy.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi eku kan rẹ ọmọ méji.
Target_Text_En: One does not placate two children with one rat.
Cultural_Context: An otherwise sufficient commodity divided too many ways satisfies no one.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ẹ̀jẹ̀ dúdú sínú tutọ́ funfun jáde.
Target_Text_En: One does not leave red blood inside and spit out white saliva.
Cultural_Context: Never let people think you love them when in fact you wish them ill.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í láhun níyì.
Target_Text_En: One cannot be both stingy and respected.
Cultural_Context: Only generosity earns respect.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìsí owó là ńpa ọ̀ọ́dúnrún mọ́; kí ni irínwó baba ìgbiwó tó-ó ṣe?
Target_Text_En: It is lack of money that makes one hoard 300 cowries; what can 400 cowries, the father of 200 cowries, accomplish?
Cultural_Context: Those who have little make too much of little things.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìsí owó là ńtìlẹ̀kùn m dúnrún; kí ni irínwó baba ìgbiwó tó-ó ṣe?
Target_Text_En: It is lack of money that makes one keep 300 cowries under lock; what can 400 cowries, father of 200 cowries, accomplish?
Cultural_Context: The im port is the same as that of the preceding entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìsí owó ni, "Jẹ́ kílẹ̀ ó mọ́"; ajé kì í gbowó ká ní ó dọ̀la.
Target_Text_En: It is lack of money that makes one say, "Wait until morning"; if the terms are agreeable, one does not wait until morning.
Cultural_Context: Lack of money makes one temporize even when the market is in one’s favor.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjẹ́kù là ńmayo.
Target_Text_En: Leaving remnants is the indicator of satiation.
Cultural_Context: How one lives will show how well off one is.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajé-ṣàlúgà! Ó fi ẹni iwájú sílẹ̀ ṣe ẹni ẹ̀hìn ní pẹ̀lẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Almighty wealth! It skips over the person in front to offer salutations to the person behind.
Cultural_Context: Wealth is no respecter of age.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajíjìfà ní ńní tìtì ìpàkọ́.
Target_Text_En: It is a person who wakes to free booty that develops an overhanging nape.
Cultural_Context: Those who labor for their food are not plagued with obesity.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkẹ̀hìnsí ọlá ò sunwọ̀n.
Target_Text_En: The reverse side of greatness is unattractive.
Cultural_Context: A fall from greatness, or turning one’s back on greatness, is unfortunate.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkísà-á ba ẹni rere jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Rags demean illustrious people.
Cultural_Context: A ragged attire overrides innate qualities.

Source_Text_Yo: A-kó-èésú-má-dàá, ẹrùngbà olè.
Target_Text_En: He-who-collects-the-pool-in-turn-but-does-not-make-a-contribution: same as a thief.
Cultural_Context: Reaping without sowing is akin to stealing.

Source_Text_Yo: A-pèèpò-lẹ́hìn-àgbà, àgbà ḿbọ̀ wá.
Target_Text_En: You-who-clear-the-weeds-behind-an-elder, your old age approaches.
Cultural_Context: Those who do favors for old people should be reminded that they too will some day grow old.

Source_Text_Yo: Àrùn tí ńjẹ́ rnárun ò sí; ebi ní ńmú ara-á yi.
Target_Text_En: There is no sickness called nettle rash; it is hunger that makes one develop welts.
Cultural_Context: Hunger is a disease not to be belittled.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣírí ẹ̀kọ kì í tú lójú ewé.
Target_Text_En: The secrets of corn meal’s being will not be exposed in the presence of leaves.
Cultural_Context: As long as one has champions, one will not be disgraced.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtètèdáyé ò kan tàgbà; orí ẹni ní ńgbéni ga.
Target_Text_En: Primogeniture has nothing to do with elderliness; it is the head that elevates one.
Cultural_Context: Age is no guarantee of status.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá lówó lọ́wọ́ tó tó ti ṣẹ̀kẹ̀rẹ̀, ìwà rere ni nǹkan.
Target_Text_En: Even if one has as much money as the beaded gourd, it is good character that matters.
Cultural_Context: Character is more important than wealth.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí òtútù ńpa ọ̀lẹ à jẹ́ kó kú; kíkú tàìkú ọ̀lẹ ò ṣe n kan fúnni.
Target_Text_En: If a lazy person has a fever, one lets him die; neither a live nor a dead lazy person does anything for one.
Cultural_Context: A lazy person is not worth troubling over.

Source_Text_Yo: Bóomọ́ yọ láàrin bàbà.
Target_Text_En: Red corn shows amid guinea corn.
Cultural_Context: A good person sticks out among bad people.

Source_Text_Yo: Èkó ò dùn lójú ẹni tí ò lówó lọ́wọ́.
Target_Text_En: The city of Lagos offers no pleasures in the view of a penniless person.
Cultural_Context: Without money, one is shut out of many pleasures.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni ajé ya ilé-e rẹ̀ ló gbọ́n.
Target_Text_En: It is the person whose home riches have found that is wise.
Cultural_Context: Whoever has prospered may boast that he or she is wise.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣẹ́-ẹ bàtà kì í ṣẹ́ òyìnbó.
Target_Text_En: The dearth of shoes never afflicts the white man.
Cultural_Context: One never lacks a thing for which one is the source.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣẹ́ owó kì í ṣẹ́ Dàda, Dàda olówó ẹyọ.
Target_Text_En: The dearth of money never afflicts Dàda, Dàda who is blessed with coins.
Cultural_Context: One will never lack whatever is part of one's essence.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣẹ́ ò mú ọkọláyà kó má ran ọmọ; akúṣẹ̀ẹ́ kì í ní ará.
Target_Text_En: Destitution does not afflict the husband and spare his children; the poverty-ridden person does not have relatives.
Cultural_Context: The destitution of the head of the household affects all members of the household; on the other hand, the poor person does not have many friends.

Source_Text_Yo: Náwó-náwó ò ná sẹ́gi; òtòṣì ò ná erèé dàgbà; Ìràtà tí ńṣẹ́gi tà nínú ìgbẹ́ : owó ni gbogbo wọ́n jọ ńná.
Target_Text_En: The big spender does not use beads for money; the poor person did not grow up spending peas; the person who gathers fire wood from the forest for sale: all of them spend money.
Cultural_Context: Rich or poor, no one can do without money.

Source_Text_Yo: Òde ò sú aláṣọ-ọ́ lọ.
Target_Text_En: Public functions do not faze a person with many clothes.
Cultural_Context: No eventuality can overwhelm a person with abundant resources.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkú tó bá láṣọ, Ifẹ̀ ní ńsin ín.
Target_Text_En: A dead person who owns a wealth of clothes is buried by Ifẹ̀ itself.
Cultural_Context: The community itself sees to the funeral of an illustrious person; the problems of a popular person arouse the concern of everyone.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó lará mọ̀; ará ò mọ ìṣẹ́, èrò tí ò lówó, ará fa ìwé ẹ̀ ya.
Target_Text_En: Kin acknowledges only the rich; no kin claims a poverty-ridden person; the way farer who has no money for kin rips up his papers.
Cultural_Context: Everybody associates with a rich person, but nobody knows a poor person

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó layé mọ̀
Target_Text_En: Humankind knows only the rich.
Cultural_Context: The poor do not count in this world.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó lọba lÉkòó.
Target_Text_En: The rich man is king in Lagos.
Cultural_Context: Lagos is an ideal playground for the rich.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó sòkè dilẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The rich person turns a hill into a plain.
Cultural_Context: Nothing is beyond a rich person, not even drastically altering the face of Nature.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrìṣà bí ajé ò sí; ajé ní ńgbéni ga.
Target_Text_En: There is no god like money; it is money that makes people great.
Cultural_Context: Money can accomplish anything.

Source_Text_Yo: Òṣì ní ńjẹ "Ta ní mọ̀ ọ́ rí?" Owó ní ńjẹ "Mo bá ọ tán."
Target_Text_En: Poverty is what explains "Who knows you?" Wealth explains, "I am related to you."
Cultural_Context: No one knows a poor person, but everybody claims kinship to a rich person.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó ilé yọ, gbèsè ḿbínú.
Target_Text_En: The household money makes its appearance, and debt becomes angry.
Cultural_Context: One’s enemies are never happy to see one escape misfortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó lẹ́gbọ́n; ọmọ làbúrò.
Target_Text_En: Money is the elder sibling; a child is the younger sibling.
Cultural_Context: Having wealth makes having children easier.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó ló wọ́n, ìyàwó ò wọ́n.
Target_Text_En: Only money is hard to come by; a wife is not hard to come by.
Cultural_Context: If one has money, finding a wife is a simple matter.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó ní nígbà tí òun ò sí nílé, ta ní ńdámọ̀ràn lẹ́hìn òun.
Target_Text_En: Money asked, when it was not at home, who dared to make plans in its absence?
Cultural_Context: Without money, all plans are useless.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó ò sí, èèyàn ò sun wón.
Target_Text_En: [If] money is lacking, a person is unattractive.
Cultural_Context: Wealth is beauty.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó òtòṣì ní ńgbé òkè ẹrù; tolówó a máa gbé ìsàlẹ̀ igbá.
Target_Text_En: It is a poor man’s money that stays at the top of the load; the rich person’s money rests at the bottom of the calabash.
Cultural_Context: A poor man wants to be able easily to see and reach his money, but the rich person can afford to be more carefree.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó yẹ ilé, Ògún yẹ odò.
Target_Text_En: Money fits a home quite well; Ògún is at home by the river.
Cultural_Context: Money is a desirable thing in a home.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọbẹ̀ lọmú àgbà.
Target_Text_En: Stew is the breast milk of adults.
Cultural_Context: Adults have their own nourishment, even if it differs from children’s.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjà tí ò tà, owó ló ńwá.
Target_Text_En: Goods that will not sell are only in need of money.
Cultural_Context: All things are possible if there is money.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ ẹwà kan ò sí; ọmọ aṣọ ní ḿbẹ.
Target_Text_En: There is no such thing as a child that is a creation of beauty, but there is something like a child that is a creation of clothing.
Cultural_Context: Clothing, rather than facial beauty, determines the impression one makes on others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pọ̀ irú kì í ba ọbẹ̀ jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: A surfeit of locust-bean seasoning does not ruin a stew.
Cultural_Context: One cannot have too much of a good thing.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn tí ẹgbà-á wọ̀, ó kúrò láwàdà
Target_Text_En: A problem complicated by as much money as 2,000 cowries is no longer a joking matter. T
Cultural_Context: Matters that involve significant amounts of money are not to be trifled with.

Source_Text_Yo: Ta la gbé gẹṣin tí kò ṣèpàkọ́ lùkẹ?
Target_Text_En: Who would be placed on the horse and not cock his head haughtily?
Cultural_Context: One should forgive the arrogance of fortunate people.

Source_Text_Yo: Tí alágbádá ó fi kú, yíyan ni yó máa yan.
Target_Text_En: Until the time the owner of elaborate garments dies, he will keep strutting.
Cultural_Context: One should not be bashful about displaying one’s wealth.

Source_Text_Yo: Wọ́n ṣe bí òtòṣì ò gbọ́n bí ọlọ́rọ̀; wọ́n ní ì bá gbọ́n ì bá lówó lọ́wọ́.
Target_Text_En: People think the poor person lacks the wisdom the wealthy person has; they say if one had wisdom, one would be rich.
Cultural_Context: It is folly to equate wealth with wisdom.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀mí gígùn lèrè ayé.
Target_Text_En: Longevity is the reward of living.
Cultural_Context: Longevity is most to be desired by all.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀mí gígùn ní ńsànyà.
Target_Text_En: It is longevity that makes up for suffering.
Cultural_Context: Longevity makes all suffering worthwhile.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí èèm ó mọ ní Ìbèṣè, kó má ṣe dé Ìjánà.
Target_Text_En: May the disaster stop at Ìbèṣè and not get to Ìjánà.
Cultural_Context: May trouble stop before it reaches our frontier.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ alẹ́ là ńtọrọ.
Target_Text_En: It is nighttime [i.e., old age] that one should pray for.
Cultural_Context: Old age is everybody’s desire.

Source_Text_Yo: Pípẹ́ láyé lèrè ayé.
Target_Text_En: Longevity is the profit of living.
Cultural_Context: Longevity is the reward for having lived a good life.

Source_Text_Yo: Agẹmọ kì í kú ní kékeré.
Target_Text_En: The chameleon does not die young.
Cultural_Context: A prayer for longevity.

Source_Text_Yo: Àfòm ò légbò; igi gbogbo ní ḿbá tan.
Target_Text_En: The climbing plant has no roots; it claims relationship with every tree. B
Cultural_Context: A feckless person is ever in search of benefactors.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ilé kan ilé, tí ọ̀dẹ̀dẹ̀- kan ọ̀dẹ̀dẹ̀, bí a kò fẹ́ni níbẹ̀, a ò tó abẹ́rẹ́.
Target_Text_En: If houses adjoin and living rooms abut, if one is not wanted there, one is not worth so much as a needle.
Cultural_Context: Being neighbors amounts to nothing if there is no mutual regard.

Source_Text_Yo: Elègbè [or elégbè] ní ḿmú orin dùn.
Target_Text_En: It takes a chorus to make a song melodious.
Cultural_Context: It is good to have backers.

Source_Text_Yo: Eṣinṣin tí ḿbá ọdẹ rìn á mu j yó
Target_Text_En: A fly that keeps a hunter company will drink blood to its fill.
Cultural_Context: The fortunes and misfortunes of one’s associates will surely rub off on one.

Source_Text_Yo: Ètí-i baba nílé, ètí-i baba lóko, èèyàn ní ńjẹbọrọ.
Target_Text_En: "Father’s ears encompass the house, father’s ears reach to the farm" spells "people"’
Cultural_Context: A person who is privy to what goes on every where has people everywhere.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀mí àbàtà ní ḿmú odò ṣàn; ọlá-a baba ní ḿmú ọmọ yan.
Target_Text_En: It is due to the life in the marshes that the river flows; it is owing to the greatness of the father that the son struts about.
Cultural_Context: The successful person has some backing that must be acknowledged.

Source_Text_Yo: Èni tí a bú lẹ́hìn tó gbọ́, a-betí-í-lu lára-bí-ajere.
Target_Text_En: A person who is insulted in absentia but hears about the insult anyway: his or her entire body is all ears, as a sieve is all holes.
Cultural_Context: If one cannot be everywhere, one should make sure one has people everywhere.

Source_Text_Yo: Èní tí kò lówó a léèyàn; èyí tí kò léèyàn ẹni tí kò léèyàn a láápọn.
Target_Text_En: A person who lacks money should have people; a person who lacks people should be gregarious.
Cultural_Context: Good connections can make up for lack of money; but if one also lacks good connections, one had better be gregarious or personable.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí kò ní adèsọ̀ kì í pàtẹ.
Target_Text_En: A person who has no one to watch a stall should not display his or her wares there.
Cultural_Context: If one lacks helpers, one should be judicious in the extent of one’s undertakings.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí kò ní "Ẹ bá mi pè é!" kì í dákú.
Target_Text_En: A person who does not have "Help me revive him!" does not faint.
Cultural_Context: If one does not have a champion, one should stay out of trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó fi ilé sílẹ̀-ẹ́ sọ àpò ìyà kọ́; ẹni tí ó sọ ọkọ́ nù-ú kọ́ àpò ebi.
Target_Text_En: Whoever moves away from home drapes the satchel of suffering on his or her shoulder; whoever loses a hoe drapes the satchel of hunger.
Cultural_Context: To move from one’s home is to expose oneself to hardship; to lose the means of making a living is to expose oneself to hunger.

Source_Text_Yo: Fóró-fóró imú ìyàwó, ó sàn ju yàrá òfìfo lọ.
Target_Text_En: A bride with a gaping nose is better than an empty bedroom.
Cultural_Context: To have something blemished is much better than to have nothing at all.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìhín ilé, ọ̀hún ilé; òjò kì í rọ̀ kó pa ọmọ adìẹ.
Target_Text_En: Here a home, there a home; the rain does not fall and drench a chick.
Cultural_Context: One should not submit to suffering when relief is everywhere around.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú tí kò níí pani ní ńgbé aláwo rere koni.
Target_Text_En: It is the death that has no intention of killing one that brings an expert diviner man one’s way.
Cultural_Context: One should be grateful if one has people to warn one about impending dangers.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìlẹ̀kùn tí kò ní alùgbàgbà, kó jókòó ẹ̀ jẹ́jẹ́; ẹni tí ò ní baba kì í jìjà ẹ̀bi.
Target_Text_En: A door without a knocker should keep its peace; a fatherless child does not fight an unjust fight.
Cultural_Context: People who have no strong backing should not court trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìràwọ̀ sán sán sán, a-lọ́mọ lẹ́hìn-bí òṣùpá.
Target_Text_En: Brilliantly twinkling star, with a multitude of followers like the moon.
Cultural_Context: Comment on an illustrious person who has a huge following.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyàwó dùn lọ́sìngín.
Target_Text_En: Marriage is pleasant when it is new.
Cultural_Context: No pleasure compares to that of a honeymoon.

Source_Text_Yo: Jọ̀jọ̀ àgbò ní ḿmú àgbò níyì; ọlá-a baba ní ḿmú ọmọ yan.
Target_Text_En: It is the ram’s dewlap that lends it dignity; it is the father’s greatness that gives the son reason to strut.
Cultural_Context: One who has good grounds for doing so may walk proudly.

Source_Text_Yo: Ká jà ká re Ọ̀yọ́, ká mọ ẹni tó lọba.
Target_Text_En: Let us quarrel and go to Ọ̀yọ́, and we will see on whose side the king is.
Cultural_Context: Boast that one would have the powers-that-be on one’s side in any quarrel.

Source_Text_Yo: Ká ríni lókèèrè ká ṣàríyá, ó yóni ó ju oúnjẹ lọ.
Target_Text_En: To see one from afar and greet one cheer fully satisfies far better than food ever could.
Cultural_Context: Fellowship is far better than material gifts.

Source_Text_Yo: Ká ṣíni létí ò jẹ́ kágbà ó ṣìṣe láàrin ilé.
Target_Text_En: Being quietly advised keeps an elder from committing a blunder within his household.
Cultural_Context: Even elders will do well to heed advice.

Source_Text_Yo: Kàkà kí gbajúmọ̀ ó jẹ ọ̀pọ̀lọ́, ẹni tí yó pa kọ̀ǹkọ̀ fun yó jàáde.
Target_Text_En: Rather than the popular person finding himself reduced to eating a toad, someone will emerge to kill a frog for him.
Cultural_Context: The well regarded person will always have people to come to his or her aid in times of need.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ohun tó dàbí-i ká wáni wálé.
Target_Text_En: There is nothing that compares with being visited at home.
Cultural_Context: It is a great honor to be visited in one’s home.

Source_Text_Yo: Lára èèyàn lowó wà.
Target_Text_En: Riches are inseparable from people.
Cultural_Context: Whoever has people around him is rich indeed.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí olókìkí ò jẹ́ asán; wọ́n ńkígbe ẹ̀ nílé, wọ́n ńkígbe ẹ̀ lógun.
Target_Text_En: The lot of a valorous person is not simple; he is called upon at home, and he is called upon in battle.
Cultural_Context: A great person is subject to demands from all sides.

Source_Text_Yo: Oṣùpá gbókè mỌ̀yọ́; ọbá gbélé mọ ará oko.
Target_Text_En: The moon remains on the firmament and knows all about Ọ̀yọ́; the king remains at home but knows all about the farm dweller.
Cultural_Context: An influential person does not have to be present at a place to know what goes on there.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó fífún ò tó èèyàn.
Target_Text_En: A gift of money is not equal in value to a [gift of a] person.
Cultural_Context: Human presence or company is worth more than money.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó kan ò ró ṣẹkẹ; èèyàn mẹ́ta ò dúró ní méjì méjì
Target_Text_En: A solitary coin does not clink; three people cannot stand in twos.
Cultural_Context: One cannot make sufficiency out of deficiency.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlọ́rọ̀-ọ́ kú, ẹ̀hìn-in rẹ̀-ẹ́ kún.
Target_Text_En: The wealthy person dies and his wake is congested.
Cultural_Context: A wealthy person has many mourners.

Source_Text_Yo: Wèrèpè-é gba ara ẹ̀ gba igi oko.
Target_Text_En: The cow-itch protects itself and protects other trees in the forest.
Cultural_Context: Closeness to a powerful person is good protection.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ba Ọlọ́run ṣòwò ká pàdánù.
Target_Text_En: One does not trade with God and come up a loser.
Cultural_Context: Any venture that takes God into account will surely prosper.

Source_Text_Yo: A kọ́lé bíríkótó, a ní kí òrìṣà gbà á; bí kò bá gbà á, kó lọ sígbẹ̀ẹ́ kó lọ ṣá ẹkẹ́, kó lọ sọ́dàn lọ họ okùn, kó mọ bí agara-á ti ńdáni.
Target_Text_En: We build a modest shrine and implore the god to accept it; if he does not accept it, let him go into the forest to cut stakes, let him go into the grassland for vines, so that he might appreciate the pains we have taken.
Cultural_Context: A god must not be too demanding of his worshipers, for if pushed too far they will rebel.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtidádé Olókun ò ṣẹ̀hìn òkun; àtidádé Ọlọ́sà ò ṣẹ̀hìn ọ̀sà; àti dádée kìnnìún ò ṣẹ̀hìn Olúigbó.
Target_Text_En: The crowning of the Olókun, goddess of the sea, will not be in the absence of the sea; the crowning of the Ọlọ́sà, goddess of the lagoon, will not be in the absence of the lagoon; the crowning of the lion will not be in the absence of the deity of the forests.
Cultural_Context: Nothing can be accomplished without God’s help.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayé ó fẹ́ kà rẹrù ká sọ̀; orí ẹni ní ńsọni.
Target_Text_En: The world would not wish to see one set down one’s heavy burden; only one’s head relieves one of the burden.
Cultural_Context: One cannot count on the good will of the world; one can count only on one’s protective spirit.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí alàgbà-á bá júbà fÓlúwa, Ọ̀nà á là.
Target_Text_En: If the elder pays homage to God, the path opens.
Cultural_Context: Nothing is possible without God, and nothing is impossible with God.

Source_Text_Yo: Eégún ṣé-é jó; òòṣà-á ṣé-é jó; ti Olódùmarè-é yàtọ̀.
Target_Text_En: A masquerader can be set alight; a god [or idol] can be set alight; God, though, is a different matter.
Cultural_Context: Only God is beyond peril at the hands of humans.

Source_Text_Yo: Igba ẹkẹ́ ní ńfọwọ́ tilé; igba alámù ní ńfọwọ́ ti ògiri; Olú-fọwọ́-tì ni Ṣàngó; gbogbo ayé ní ńfọwọ́ ti ọba.
Target_Text_En: Two hundred poles hold up a house; two hundred lizards support a wall with their hands; Chief-lends-support is Ṣango’s name; the whole world lends support to the king.
Cultural_Context: Used in the context of prayer or incantation to invoke the support of the powers that control the universe.

Source_Text_Yo: Kàkà kí ebí pa ọmọ awo kú, ìpèsè ni yó yòó o.
Target_Text_En: Rather than the child of the priest dying of hunger, he or she will feed to satisfaction on goods provided for sacrifice.
Cultural_Context: Providence will not permit the referent to suffer want.

Source_Text_Yo: Kọ̀lọ̀kọ̀lọ̀ ìbá kú, adìẹ ò sunkún; kọ̀lọ̀kọ̀lọ̀ ò gba adìẹ sìn.
Target_Text_En: Were the fox to die, the chicken would not shed a tear; the fox never fostered a chick.
Cultural_Context: One does not mourn an enemy’s disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Múni-múni ò lè mú Olódùmarè.
Target_Text_En: The professional arrester cannot arrest the Almighty.
Cultural_Context: God is beyond human punishment.

Source_Text_Yo: "N ò níí sin Olúwa, n ò níí sin Ànábì"; ohun tí olúwarẹ̀ ó sìn ò níí tó èkùrọ́.
Target_Text_En: "I will not worship God, and I will not worship Allah"; what such a person will worship will not be so large as a palm kernel.
Cultural_Context: A person who is too picky will wind up having no pick at all.

Source_Text_Yo: Nítorí Ọlọ́run nìmàlé fi ńjẹ mọ́sà.
Target_Text_En: It is in deference to God that the Muslim eats fried corn cake.
Cultural_Context: Necessity obliges one to do things one would not do otherwise.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí babá ṣe sílẹ̀ nìrègún ọmọ.
Target_Text_En: What the father provided is what the children inherit.
Cultural_Context: Children benefit from the industry of their father.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú ilẹ̀ la ṣe dá a tí a ṣe rú u; bí ẹbọ́ bá máa jẹ́kí ilẹ̀ ó jẹ́rìí.
Target_Text_En: It is in the presence of Earth that one consulted the oracle and offered the prescribed sacrifice; if the sacrifice will yield the promised result, let Earth bear witness.
Cultural_Context: The Earth will monitor and enforce oaths sworn in her presence.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkùtù ọ̀pẹ kì í wo ojú ẹlòmíràn bí kò ṣe ojú Ọlọ́run.
Target_Text_En: Young palm leaves do not raise their eyes to anyone other than God.
Cultural_Context: All affairs are best left to God.

Source_Text_Yo: Oore wo lòrìṣá ṣe fún abuké tó sọ ọmọ ẹ̀ ní Òrìṣá-gbè-mí?
Target_Text_En: What favor have the gods granted the humpback who names his child Òrìṣágbèmí [The gods have come to my aid]?
Cultural_Context: There is no point in offering gratitude in a direction from which no help has come.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrìṣà, bí o ò le gbè mí, ṣe mí bí o ti bá mi.
Target_Text_En: God, if you will not save me, leave me as you found me!
Cultural_Context: If the person one looks to for help does not help, he or she at least should not leave one worse off than before.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrìṣà ní ńpeni wá jẹ ọkà; a kì í gbọ́ ọwọ́ orógùn lẹ́hìnkùlé.
Target_Text_En: It is the gods that summon one to come eat yam-flour meal; one does not hear the sound of the stirring stick from the back yard.
Cultural_Context: If one chances on good fortune, one should give thanks to the gods.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrìṣà tí a kẹ́, kẹ́, kẹ́, tí kò gbọ, tí a gẹ̀, gẹ̀, gẹ̀, tí kò gbà; ojú-u pópó ní ńgbé.
Target_Text_En: The god that one praises, praises, and praises but who does not listen, that one worships, worships, and worships but who refuses to heed, ends up in the streets. Ọ
Cultural_Context: If a supposed savior consistently fails you, discard it and find yourself another.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlọ́run la kì í sú.
Target_Text_En: Only God never gets fed up with us.
Cultural_Context: Unlike people, God is infinitely patient.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlọ́run ní ńṣèdájọ́ a-fehín-pínran.
Target_Text_En: Only God can render justice to the person who uses his teeth to share out meat.
Cultural_Context: God alone sees, and can reward, what people do in secret.

Source_Text_Yo: Ta ni tàkúté Olúwa ò leè mú?
Target_Text_En: Who is beyond being caught in God’s trap?
Cultural_Context: No one is beyond God’s judgment.

Source_Text_Yo: Tinú tẹ̀hìn ni labalábá fi ńyin Ọlọ́run.
Target_Text_En: It is with both its belly and its back that the butterfly praises the Lord.
Cultural_Context: One should glorify God with all one has.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dúró nílùú ká fara hẹ.
Target_Text_En: One does not stay for long in a town and remain uninvolved.
Cultural_Context: One must live as a part of one’s community.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mọ alájá ká nà á lọ́pa.
Target_Text_En: One does not know a dog’s owner and yet rain blows on it with a rod.
Cultural_Context: One’s regard for a person should extend to that person’s interests. Compare the two following entries.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mọ alájá ká pè é ní títà.
Target_Text_En: One does not know the owner of a dog and yet announce that it is for sale.
Cultural_Context: One should safeguard the interests of those one knows, even in their absence.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mọ alájá ká pé kẹ́kùn ó pa á jẹ.
Target_Text_En: One does not know the owner of a dog and yet wish that a leopard would eat it.
Cultural_Context: One should invoke no ill on things dear to people one knows.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í sọ pé ó di ọjọ́ tí a bá bímọ ká tó sọ ọmọ níkòó.
Target_Text_En: One does not say it will not be until one has fathered a child that one raps a child on the head with one’s knuckles.
Cultural_Context: Every adult shares the responsibility for disciplining all children, not only his or her own.

Source_Text_Yo: Abánigúnwà ní ḿmọ ìjagun ẹni.
Target_Text_En: It is he who shares one’s throne that knows one’s strategy in battle.
Cultural_Context: Only soulmates know each other’s minds.

Source_Text_Yo: Abánigbé ní ḿmọ ìṣe ẹni.
Target_Text_En: Whoever one lives with knows one’s habits.
Cultural_Context: The public image is not reliable.

Source_Text_Yo: A-bánigbé-má-mọ́wà-ẹni, ọ̀tá ẹni ni.
Target_Text_En: He-who-lives-with-one-without-knowing one’s-habits: he is one’s enemy.
Cultural_Context: A housemate who does not know one’s ways cannot be trusted.

Source_Text_Yo: Abíni ò tó atọ́ni.
Target_Text_En: The parent is no match for the rearer.
Cultural_Context: Raising a child is more important than giving birth to a child.

Source_Text_Yo: A-dáko-má-gbin-ọkà-á ní òún dá ikún lára; bíkún ò bá rí jẹ lóko-o rẹ̀, áá rí jẹ lóko ẹlòmíràn.
Target_Text_En: He-who-prepares-a-farm-and-does-not plant-corn says he is denying something to the squirrel;if squirrel finds nothing to eat on his farm, it will find something on an other person’s farm.
Cultural_Context: Obsessive attempts to injure others can and do backfire.

Source_Text_Yo: Adámú ò lè wà nílé ká má gbọdọ̀ ṣe han-han.
Target_Text_En: One does not stop saying han-han simply because there is a person with a nasal speech defect in the home.
Cultural_Context: There is a limit to the concessions one can make to those one lives with.

Source_Text_Yo: Àì-fojú-kan-ara-ẹni ó jẹ́ kí ọ̀tẹ̀ tán.
Target_Text_En: Not-seeing-each-other-face-to-face perpetuates a conspiracy.
Cultural_Context: Lack of personal contact prevents the ending of a feud.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá tó ti ńríni yọ̀ kì í tún ríni gbó
Target_Text_En: A dog that once rejoiced on seeing one does not switch to barking on seeing one.
Cultural_Context: Radi cal changes in other people’s attitude to one are developments not to be wished for.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjànàkú yáwó tán kò singbà mọ́; erin-ín gbówó olówó wọgbó lọ.
Target_Text_En: The elephant pawned itself for money but did not serve as promised; the elephant took others’ money and disappeared into the bush.
Cultural_Context: The mighty person can get away with anything.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajé ló mọ bí òun ó ti ṣe ọlọ́jà Odògbo, tí a pa ẹ̀kìrì ká fi wójò, tó nìkan kun ún tà.
Target_Text_En: Only the demon of prosperity knows what it will do with the chief of Odògbo; we killed a wild goat as an offering for rain, and he cut it for sale for himself.
Cultural_Context: A powerful person who betrays his trust must be left to the gods to deal with.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjèjé ọwọ́ kan ò gbégbá karí.
Target_Text_En: Asingle hand does not lift a calabash to the head [to be carried].
Cultural_Context: It takes two hands to lift a heavy load. Cooperation is best.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajẹ̀bimágbà ní ńkógun wọ̀lú.
Target_Text_En: It is he-who-is-guilty-but-refuses-to-accept the-guilt that brings warfare into a town.
Cultural_Context: Refusal to accept one’s guilt ruins communal harmony.

Source_Text_Yo: Aládùúgbò ẹni ni ọmọ ìyá ẹni.
Target_Text_En: One’s neighbor is one’s same-mother relative.
Cultural_Context: A neighbor is as close as any sibling.

Source_Text_Yo: Aláìláyà ò lè gbé ilé ńlá; bí a bá láyà ihòrò ní ńsinnií lọ
Target_Text_En: A fainthearted person cannot live in a large house; if one has a lion heart, it leads one to the grave.
Cultural_Context: Whatever the inconvenience, one must learn to get along with people or else live as a hermit.

Source_Text_Yo: Alájọbí ò sí mọ́, alájọgbé ló kù.
Target_Text_En: Kin is no longer to be found; only cohabitors remain.
Cultural_Context: Kinship is no longer in fashion, only neighborliness.

Source_Text_Yo: Ànìkànjẹ ayé kì í dùn; jíjọjẹ ní ńdára.
Target_Text_En: Going through life by oneself is unpleasant; living life in company is pleasant.
Cultural_Context: Having riches is nothing like having people.

Source_Text_Yo: Àńtètè, ó dá yànpọ̀n-yànpọ̀n sílẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The cricket sows confusion among others. With the family 301
Cultural_Context: When people like the cricket depart a place, they leave dissension and confusion in their wake.

Source_Text_Yo: Àpésan kì í tú ìlú.
Target_Text_En: Contributing to a common purse does not ruin a town.
Cultural_Context: A town that acts together stays together.

Source_Text_Yo: Àpọ́n yan ìyà ó ní òún yan ìyá; ta là bá kó iṣu méjì fún tí kò gúnyán konko fúnni?
Target_Text_En: A bachelor chooses suffering but says he chose his mother; to what person would one give two yams but would not make pounded yam?
Cultural_Context: Whatever a mother can do for a man, a wife can do, and more.

Source_Text_Yo: Ará òde ò mọni lọrú; ará ilé ẹni ní ńnawọ́ ẹrú síni.
Target_Text_En: Outsiders do not know that one is a slave; people of one’s household are the ones who point one out as a slave.
Cultural_Context: If those of one’s household do not dishonor one, outsiders will not.

Source_Text_Yo: Aríjàmálàjà, ọ̀tá Ọlọ́run.
Target_Text_En: One-who-sees-a-fight-and-does-not-try-to stop-it: an enemy of God.
Cultural_Context: To fail to stop a fight is to offend God.

Source_Text_Yo: Àrò mẹ́ta kì í da ọbẹ̀ nù
Target_Text_En: A trident cooking hearth does not spill stew.
Cultural_Context: Many hands ensure success.

Source_Text_Yo: Àsopọ̀ ní ńmú ewúrẹ́ wẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is being-tied-together that forces goats to
Cultural_Context: Many hands ensure success.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwáyó fara ẹ̀ gbodì.
Target_Text_En: We-are-full makes enemies for himself.
Cultural_Context: A person who refuses favors on behalf of others makes enemies of those others.

Source_Text_Yo: Awo ní ńgbe awo nígbọnwọ́; bí awo ò bá gbe awo nígbọnwọ́ awo á tẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Initiates of mysteries must rally round other initiates; if initiates do not rally round one another, they suffer disgrace.
Cultural_Context: Cooperation among group members protects their collective image.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá bu ìgbẹ́ lábùká, a ó rìí ẹran inú-u rẹ̀ pa.
Target_Text_En: If hunters encircle the bush, they will suc ceed in killing the animals therein.
Cultural_Context: If all available hands converge on a task, it will be accomplished.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá fa gbùùrù, gbùùrù a fagbó.
Target_Text_En: If one pulls the vine, the vine pulls the bush.
Cultural_Context: If one goes after an offender, one becomes entangled with his or her patron.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá ḿbú ẹtù, orí a máa f awó.
Target_Text_En: If one insults the guinea fowl, the guinea fowl gets a headache.
Cultural_Context: When one hears one’s close relative insulted, one feels insulted.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí àṣá kò bá fẹ́ẹ́ fẹ́ àṣá níràn, ojú-u sánmà-á tó-ó fò fẹ́yẹ láì fara gbúnra.
Target_Text_En: If an eagle does not want to provoke an eagle, the sky is wide enough for birds to fly without bumping one another.
Cultural_Context: If one is spoiling for a fight, any excuse will do.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ẹjọ́ ò sunwọ̀n, ẹlẹ́jó là ńfún dá.
Target_Text_En: If a case is hopeless, one asks the owner to judge it.
Cultural_Context: If guilt is obvious, the guilty should be made to declare it.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ẹrú bá jọ ara-a wọn, à mọ̀ pé ilé kannáà ni wọ́n ti wá.
Target_Text_En: If slaves resemble one another, one surmises that they came from the same household.
Cultural_Context: People who share similar traits deserve to be lumped together.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ìbágbé ò bá wọ̀, ká yàgò fúnra.
Target_Text_En: If cohabitation does not work, let us give each other some space.
Cultural_Context: If people cannot be friends or husband and wife, they should part amicably.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ilé kò dùn, bí ìgbẹ̀ nìlú ńrí.
Target_Text_En: If the home is not pleasant, the town seems like a jungle.
Cultural_Context: The tone of the town depends on the condition of the homes in it.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí obìnrín bá di méjì, imú ọkọ a di odó, a ní wọn ò tún yí imú lu òun mọ́.
Target_Text_En: When women number two, the husband’s nose becomes a mortar; she [the first wife] says that he no longer rolls his nose in her direction.
Cultural_Context: The erstwhile favorite never takes kindly to being supplanted by a new favorite.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ojú bá ko ojú, àlà yó tọ̀ọ́ nídìí ìgbá.
Target_Text_En: If eyes meet eyes, the boundary line will be straight at the base of the locust tree.
Cultural_Context: When all parties participate in dividing something among them, no one is cheated.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọmọ ò jọ ṣòkòtò a jọ kíjìpá.
Target_Text_En: If a child does not resemble the trousers, he should resemble the wrapper.
Cultural_Context: If a child does not take after his father, he should take after his mother.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọmọdé bá pa eku, a dá a jẹ, bó bá pa ẹyẹ, a dá a jẹ, ṣùgbọ́n ọjọ́ tó bá dáràn gòdògbà, a fà á wá sọ́dọ́ ọ bàbá-a r .
Target_Text_En: When a youth kills a rat, he eats it alone; when he kills a bird, he eats it alone; but when he is in serious trouble, he drags it home to his father.
Cultural_Context: A youth does not re member his parents until he needs their help.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèyàn bí ìyá ò sí; ta ní jẹ́ ṣe ọmọ-ọlọmọ lóore.
Target_Text_En: There is no being like a mother; whoever did another person’s child a favor?
Cultural_Context: A mother is the surest support a person can ever hope for.

Source_Text_Yo: Ehín tó tayọ, wàhálà ẹnu ni.
Target_Text_En: A bucktooth is trouble for the mouth.
Cultural_Context: One pays one way or another for one’s shortcomings. Or, the shortcomings of one’s relatives spell problems for one also.

Source_Text_Yo: Èkó ilá gba ara-a rẹ̀ lọ́wọ́ ọbẹ̀: ilá táa kókìkí ò so; gbọ̀ọ̀rọ̀ táa gbkẹ́lé ò fà; ọmọ ìf táa gbkẹ́lé ò ṣe bí a ti rò
Target_Text_En: Okro that goes to seed saves itself from being stewed: the okro one boasted about fails to fruit; the pumpkin one placed one’s hopes on sends out no trailers; the beloved child one relied on fails to do as one hoped.
Cultural_Context: One can hope for no rewards for one’s pains from an ungrateful child.

Source_Text_Yo: Èyí wù mí kò wù lọmọ ìyá méjì-í fi ńjẹun lótọ̀ọ̀tó
Target_Text_En: This appeals to me but not to you’’ is the reason why two children of the same mother eat separately. Ẹ
Cultural_Context: Even the closest of relatives may differ in taste.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀ ńgbàdúrà kẹ́ṣin ilé kú; ẹ ò níí lẹ́ṣin mìíràn níran yín mọ́.
Target_Text_En: You pray for the death of the household horse; there will never be another horse in your lineage. 304 relationships
Cultural_Context: Any household that wishes for the destruction of its most illustrious mem ber will never again be blessed with a worthy member.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀ẹ̀tán lelégbè ẹyìn; ọmọ bíbí inú ẹni lelégbè ẹni.
Target_Text_En: Young palm fruits are the support of ripe ones; one’s children are one’s support.
Cultural_Context: In their old age parents have their children to lean on.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀là ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ ò lójú àtokùnbọ̀; alágbẹ̀dẹ ò rójú ará
Target_Text_En: A split bead lacks a hole for a thread; the blacksmith has no time for relatives.
Cultural_Context: Some occupations leave no room for the obser vance of courtesies.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹlẹbí ò sinmi; ẹni à bí ire ò ráyè
Target_Text_En: A person with a large family does not rest; a person of good birth has no time to himself or herself.
Cultural_Context: Whoever has a large family or is very popular has many obligations and great demands on his or her time.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni a bí wọn bí kì í wù wọ́n; ẹni ẹlẹ́ni ní ńyá wọn lára.
Target_Text_En: Their blood relatives never find favor with them; only strangers evoke their enthusiasm.
Cultural_Context: People always appreciate what is remote more than what is near at hand.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bímọ ọ̀ràn ní ńpọ̀n ọ́n dàgbà.
Target_Text_En: Whoever mothers a problem child will bear it on her back until it is weaned.
Cultural_Context: Oneself, and no one else, bears the consequences of one’s own actions.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí yó kùú kì í la odó yáná
Target_Text_En: A dying person does not split the mortar to kindle a fire to warm himself or herself.
Cultural_Context: However desperate one’s circumstances, one should respect the interests of others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó bá yọ ará ilé-re lẹ́nu yó jogún òfo.
Target_Text_En: Whoever makes himself or herself a nui sance to those of his or her household in herits nothing. F G
Cultural_Context: It pays to look well to one’s relations with one’s family.

Source_Text_Yo: Gángán ló báni tan; kò ṣéé fi bẹ rẹ́.
Target_Text_En: His relationship to one is very slight; even so it cannot be severed with a knife. I
Cultural_Context: The most distant relative still deserves to be acknowledged and treated as such.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìfẹ́ ní kókó ìpàkọ́; a kì í fi aṣọ kọ́ ọ.
Target_Text_En: The knot at the occiput is something one tolerates out of love; one cannot hang clothes on it.
Cultural_Context: One does or endures certain things without expecting material benefits from them.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbà ò lè di ìgbà òyìnbó ká fi àbúrò ẹni ṣaya.
Target_Text_En: No matter to what extent the era has become a white man’s era, one cannot take one’s own sister as a wife
Cultural_Context: There are some values and habits that will survive the strongest foreign influences. Compare the next entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó gbogbo èdè àti ìtàn ti o jẹ́ ẹni tó gbogbo èdè àti ìtàn ti o jẹ́ ẹni tó gbogbo èd
Target_Text_En: There are some values and habits that will survive the strong est foreign influences.
Cultural_Context: Compare the next entry.)

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbà ò lè di ìgbà òyìnbó kọ́mọ ẹní sọnù ká má wàá a.
Target_Text_En: However strong the white man’s influence, if one’s child is lost, one will go searching for him or her.
Cultural_Context: A people’s values must survive the strongest foreign influences.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú òde ní ńpa ọmọdé fún ìyá ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is death from outside that kills a child for his or her mother.
Cultural_Context: A child not properly instructed at home will learn a lesson from strangers outside the home.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìlasa ò sunwọ̀n; ta ló bí ilá?
Target_Text_En: Okro leaf is no good; who gave birth to the okro?
Cultural_Context: However great the offspring, he or she must yet acknowledge his or her parents.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé là ńwò ká tó sọmọ lórúkọ.
Target_Text_En: One considers the home before giving a child [from it] a name.
Cultural_Context: A child’s character is a good indication of the sort of home he or she comes from.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé la ti ńkẹsọ̀ọ́ ròde.
Target_Text_En: One adorns oneself with finery in one’s home before stepping outside.
Cultural_Context: One’s char acter follows one from home into the world outside.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé làbọ̀sinmi oko.
Target_Text_En: The home is where one returns for rest after the farm.
Cultural_Context: However long one wanders, one eventually returns home.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé ni bọ̀yí máa bọ̀ sí
Target_Text_En: The home is the place the houseboy returns With the family 305 to in the end.
Cultural_Context: One may try, but one cannot escape one’s destiny.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé ọkọ lobìnrín ti ńtún ìpín yàn.
Target_Text_En: It is in the marital home that a woman’s destiny is revised.
Cultural_Context: A woman’s destiny be gins anew when she goes to her husband’s home.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilénikúwà ẹran Àjàyí; Àyànmọ́-ìpín ẹran Olúgbòde
Target_Text_En: The-home-is-where-death-lurks, the name of Àjàyí’s goat; One’s-fate-is-set-at-one’s creation, the name of Olúgbòde’s goat.
Cultural_Context: If one’s home base is secure, one is safe from disaster; yet no one can avert his or her fate.

Source_Text_Yo: Ipin lójú, ikun nímú, ará ilé ẹní mọ̀dí ẹ̀: àrùn lará ìta ńpè é.
Target_Text_En: Eyes oozing matter, mucus in the nose: those of one’s household know the cause, but strangers attribute them to disease.
Cultural_Context: Only those really close to a person know the real reasons for his or her condition.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣẹ̀ àpọ́n ò lórí; tabiyamọ ló sàn dí.
Target_Text_En: The bachelor’s privations are to no pur pose; those of a mother are somewhat better.
Cultural_Context: Suffering is tolerable as long as it is not purposeless.

Source_Text_Yo: Iṣẹ́ ḿbẹ lóko òkú tí a pè tí kò dáhùn
Target_Text_En: There is work to be done on the farm of the dead person, who is called but does not re spond.
Cultural_Context: When a person becomes incapable of performing his or her duties, the relatives inherit the obligation to take them up.

Source_Text_Yo: Iṣu kì í ta kó gbàgbé ewé; àgbàdo kì í yọmọ kó gbàgbé ìrùkẹ̀rẹ̀; kí ni ngó jẹ gbàgbé ọmọ-ọ̀ mi?
Target_Text_En: The yam does not mature and forget the leaves; the corn does not ripen and forget the tassels; what would I eat that would make me forget my children?
Cultural_Context: However successful one might be, ones’s children would still be uppermost in one’s mind.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìtàkùn ní ńṣe ikú pa ọ̀kẹ́rẹ́; obìnrin ní ńṣe ikú pa ọkùnrin.
Target_Text_En: Vines are the death of squirrels; women are the death of men.
Cultural_Context: As dangerous as vines are to the squirrels, so dangerous are women to men.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìtàkùn tó so igbá, tó so agbè, ló so elégéde.
Target_Text_En: The same vine that grew a calabash and grew a gourd also grew a pumpkin.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who are of the same stock but harbor enmity toward one another.

Source_Text_Yo: Iwájú la ti ńjogún; ẹ̀hìn la ti ńṣàgbà.
Target_Text_En: One inherits from one’s front, and one sets an example at one’s back.
Cultural_Context: Deriving benefits from one’s elders, one is obligated to pass on some benefits to those who are younger.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyá là bá ní; ará ò ṣe nǹkan fúnni.
Target_Text_En: One whould rather have a mother; relatives hardly do one any favor.
Cultural_Context: A mother is to be preferred over other kin.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyá ni wúrà, baba ni jígí; ọjọ́ ìyá kú ni wúrà-á bájẹ́; ọjọ́ tì bàbá kú ni jígí lọ.
Target_Text_En: Mother is gold, father is glass; the day the mother dies is the day the gold is ruined; the day the father dies is the day the glass is gone. J
Cultural_Context: One’s parents are of great value, but the mother is more precious than the father.

Source_Text_Yo: Jọ mí jọ mí,’’ òkú òǹrorò ní ńsọni dà.
Target_Text_En: Be just like me, be just like me!’’ makes one an intolerable tyrant.
Cultural_Context: One should allow others to be themselves.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí adití baà gbọ́rọ̀ la ti ńsọ lójú ọmọ ẹ́.
