Target_Text_En: It is so that a deaf person might hear some thing that one says it in his or her child’s presence.
Cultural_Context: One way of making one’s opin ion known to a person one cannot or dares not speak to is to say it in the hearing of someone close to that person.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí ni a ó ṣe fún ọmọ àlè tí yó peni ní baba?
Target_Text_En: What could one do for a bastard that would induce him or her to call one ‘‘father’’?
Cultural_Context: A favor done for unworthy and ungrateful people is a favor done in vain.

Source_Text_Yo: Kòbánitan ò jogún ẹni.
Target_Text_En: He-[or-she]-is-not-related-to-one does not inherit from one. M
Cultural_Context: Those one has nothing to do with have no rights in one’s affairs.

Source_Text_Yo: Má ṣe fìwà jọ mí; ọmọ olè lolè ńjọ.
Target_Text_En: Do not take after me; a thief takes after a thief ’s offspring [or a thief ’s offspring takes after his parents].
Cultural_Context: One should take after one’s parents in character.

Source_Text_Yo: "Ng ó ṣe iyá" ò lè jọ iyá; "Ng ó ṣe baba" ò lè jọ baba; "Wòsọ̀ dè mí" ò lè jọ onísọ̀; ojú mẹ́wàá ò lè jọ ojú ẹni.
Target_Text_En: Watch the store for me’’ is not the same as the owner of the store; ten eyes are not like one’s own.
Cultural_Context: A substitute is never as good as the real thing.

Source_Text_Yo: Nínù là ńnu ọmọ ẹyẹ dàgbà.
Target_Text_En: Until it matures, the young bird is fed by having food placed in its mouth.
Cultural_Context: People have the responsibility to care for their dependents until they are able to care for themselves.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrín délé ọkọ ó gbàgbé ọ̀rẹ.
Target_Text_En: On arriving at her marital home, a woman forgets her suitors.
Cultural_Context: On leaving a stage in one’s life, one should abandon the habits of that stage

Source_Text_Yo: Obínrin tí kòì lórogún ò tíì màrùn tí ńṣèun
Target_Text_En: A woman who does not yet have a co-wife does not yet know what disease she has.
Cultural_Context: Until one has enemies, one seldom knows one’s flaws.

Source_Text_Yo: Òde là ńṣàgbà, ilé kan bí ìbó; bó pẹ́ títí, àtilé àtòde ní ḿbọ̀ wáá kàn
Target_Text_En: When one is abroad, one acts the venerable sage, even though one’s homestead is as sour as the sap of the ìbó plant; but sooner or later both the homestead and the outside become sour.
Cultural_Context: One cannot conceal one’s secret shame forever.

Source_Text_Yo: Odò kì í ṣàn kó gbàgbé ìsun
Target_Text_En: A river does not flow and forget its source.
Cultural_Context: However far you may roam, always remem ber where you came from.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkò lọmọ: Ọlọ́run ní ńwí pé ká sọ síbi tó dára.
Target_Text_En: A child is [like] a stone: only God’s grace guides one to throw it to a propitious place.
Cultural_Context: It takes Providence to help one do right by one’s children.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkú ọlọ́mọ kì í sun à-sùn-gbàgbé.
Target_Text_En: The corpse of a person who left children behind does not forget itself in sleep.
Cultural_Context: An expression of the belief that dead people survived by young children will continue to care for them from their new abode.

Source_Text_Yo: Oǹsìn ní ḿmọ ìwà.
Target_Text_En: The servant is best placed to know [the mas ter’s] character.
Cultural_Context: Those dependent on you can best tell what sort of person you are.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí kì í pọ̀ lọ́jà ká má mọ tìyá ẹni.
Target_Text_En: Heads are never so plentiful in the market place that one does not recognize one’s mother’s.
Cultural_Context: One must always favor one’s kin.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrìṣà ilé ẹni kì í hunni.
Target_Text_En: One’s household god never turns on one.
Cultural_Context: One should always be able to count on succor, not betrayal, from one’s own house hold.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrìṣà ò níkà; ará ilé ẹni ní ńroni pa.
Target_Text_En: The gods are not wicked; it is people from one’s household who kill one with defama tion.
Cultural_Context: One’s greatest enemies often come from one’s own household.

Source_Text_Yo: Orogún kì í jogún orogún.
Target_Text_En: Co-wives do not inherit from co-wives.
Cultural_Context: People with distinct interests should keep them distinct.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọkọ ẹni lodì ẹni.
Target_Text_En: One’s husband is one’s closest kin.
Cultural_Context: There should be no relationship more intimate than that between spouses.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlá àbàtà ní ḿmú odò-ó ṣàn; ọlá-a baba ní ḿmú ọmọ yan.
Target_Text_En: It is the by the grace of the marshy land that a river flows; it is by the grace of the father that the son struts.
Cultural_Context: The person who has strong backers can afford to strut.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlanfẹ ni baba ẹyẹ, iyùn ni baba ìlẹ̀kẹ̀; ẹni tí a bá fẹ́ ìyá ẹ̀ lọmọ ẹ̀ ńwunni
Target_Text_En: The ọlanfẹ bird is the father of all birds; the coral bead is the father of all beads; it is the offspring of the person whose mother one loves that are attractive.
Cultural_Context: One’s love for a woman affects one’s feelings toward her children.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ àlè, ilé ní ńtú
Target_Text_En: A bastard does nothing but disrupt the household.
Cultural_Context: Illegitimate children ruin fami lies.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ́ bọ́ lọ́wọ́-ọ nínà, ó di à-wò-mọ́jú.
Target_Text_En: When a child outgrows whipping, he be comes a person one looks at and rolls one’s eyes in disgust.
Cultural_Context: When a child becomes an adult and still has not learned to behave well, one can only throw up one’s hands in resignation.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ ẹni ò ṣèdí bẹ̀bẹ̀rẹ̀, ká sòlẹ̀kẹ̀ mọ́ ọmọ ẹlòmíràn nídìí.
Target_Text_En: One does not, because one’s child’s waist is too fat, put waist beads around the waist of another person’s child.
Cultural_Context: One always loves one’s own children best, despite their flaws.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ olúgelegele-é pa ìdí m búúbú
Target_Text_En: The olúgelegelé plant tidies up its base dili
Cultural_Context: Not Provided

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ ọlọ́mọ là ńrán níṣẹjẹ ‘‘dé tòru-tòru.’’
Target_Text_En: It is only another person’s child that one sends on a return-unfailingly-even-after nightfall errand.
Cultural_Context: One always feels more free to misuse other people’s property than one’s own.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ ọlọ́mọ ní ńpa baba oníbaba.
Target_Text_En: It is another person’s child that kills another person’s father.
Cultural_Context: Both the perpetrator and the victim of an evil deed have relatives to whom they relate differently. People often do evil to other, unrelated, people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ tí ó ní ẹlẹrù yó bàjẹ́
Target_Text_En: A child who fears no one will be rotten.
Cultural_Context: Any person who refuses to be disciplined is worth nothing.

Source_Text_Yo: Alébíowú means ‘‘one who lies contentedly like festering jealousy’’; Ajíb ládé means ‘‘one who rises ac companied with prosperity.’’
Target_Text_En: The two are to be pictured as in their characteristic morning poses.
Cultural_Context: Not Provided

Source_Text_Yo: Abéégúndé means ‘‘One who arrives during the annual eégún festival.’’
Target_Text_En: Only those who belong to the cult may give such a name to their children; the sense of the proverb seems to be that those who do not be long to the cult may not give their own children such a name.
Cultural_Context: With the family 309

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ tí ò níyàá kì í dégbò hìn.
Target_Text_En: A motherless child should not get a sore on his back.
Cultural_Context: Unless you have people to help you out, do not get into trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ tó bu ìyá lẹ́hìn jẹ, ẹni tí yó pọ̀n ọ̀n á ṣíṣẹ.
Target_Text_En: A child that bit its mother’s back: whoever will carry it on her back has her work cut out for her.
Cultural_Context: Children who cannot be dis ciplined by their parents pose even greater problems for their caretakers.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ tó bu ìyá ẹ̀ lẹ̀hìn jẹ, kò sí alágbàpọ̀n tó jẹ́ pọ̀n ọ́n.
Target_Text_En: The child that bit its mother’s back, no surrogate carrier will carry on her back.
Cultural_Context: Children that cannot be controlled by their parents will not easily find caretakers. Compare the preceding entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ tó dára ti bàbá ẹ̀ ni; ọmọ burúkú tìyá ẹ̀ ni
Target_Text_En: A well-disciplined child is the father’s child; an ill-bred child is the mother’s.
Cultural_Context: It is up to the father to discipline the child; it is up to the mother to see that the child accepts the discipline.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ tó ní kíyàá òun má sùn, òun náà ò níí fójú kàn orun.
Target_Text_En: A child that is determined to keep its mother awake will itself not catch a glimpse of sleep
Cultural_Context: People intent on making trouble for others will not themselves remain untroubled.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ yìí ṣe gbọ́n báyìí? Ó ní baba nísàlẹ̀ ni
Target_Text_En: How did this child come to be so wise?’’ It is only because he has a father somewhere. 310 relationships
Cultural_Context: A well-bred child is evidence of his father’s good influence.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọdé tó yá tọ́rò lóde, owó ilé ló ná
Target_Text_En: A child who borrows three pence on the streets is actually spending household money.
Cultural_Context: Members of the household will ulti mately be held responsible for the actions of the minors in the household.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn tó bá bá ojú á bá imú.
Target_Text_En: The trouble that befalls the eyes will also af fect the nose.
Cultural_Context: Whatever afflicts those close to one afflicts oneself also.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rẹ́ ẹni ní ḿbáni pilẹ̀ ọ̀rọ̀, ará ilé ẹni ní ḿbani kó o
Target_Text_En: It is a friend that helps one lay the foun dation of a venture; kinfolk help one carry it to fruition.
Cultural_Context: Kin are more valuable than friends.

Source_Text_Yo: Órẹ́ kítí-kítí, iyèkan kàtà-kàtà: bọ́rẹ̀ẹ́ kítí-kítí bá kú, iyèkan kàtà-kàtà ní ńgbé e sin
Target_Text_En: The closest of friends, the most distant of relatives: when the closest friend dies, the most distant relatives are the ones who ar range the funeral.
Cultural_Context: The closest friend is not as important as even distant relatives.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rọ̀ àgbà, bí kò bá ta ẹ̀dẹ́, ogun ní ńta.
Target_Text_En: The word that issues out of the mouth of an elder, if it does not hit at hunting, will hit at war.
Cultural_Context: There is always considerable substance and weight in what an elder says.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣe igbá ilé jẹ́jẹ́; a ò mọ ìwà tí toko yó hù.
Target_Text_En: Handle the home calabash with care; no one knows how the farm calabash will behave. T
Cultural_Context: Be good to the things and people you al ready have; you can never be sure what you might end up with if you were to trade them for new ones.

Source_Text_Yo: Tímọ́-tímọ́ letí ḿmọ́ orí, tìmọ́-tìmọ́ lalámọ̀ ńgún amọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Closely is the manner of the ear’s attachment to the head; smoothly is the way the clay worker pounds his clay. W
Cultural_Context: An admonition to people to remain intimate.

Source_Text_Yo: Wo isè dè mi kì í jọ onísọ̀; Ng ó sè baba fún ọ ó lè jọ baba.
Target_Text_En: Watch the stall for me’’ cannot be like the store owner; ‘‘I will be like a father to you’’ can never be like a father. With the family 311 On relationships within the community A
Cultural_Context: Where kinship is concerned, substitutes can never be like the real thing.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í bá ẹni gbé ká má mọ ojú ẹni.
Target_Text_En: One does not live with a person and yet not know how to deal with him or her.
Cultural_Context: To know a person well is to know that person’s habits and tastes.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í bá ẹni tan ká tún fani nítan ya.
Target_Text_En: One does not claim kinship with a person and yet split the person’s thighs.
Cultural_Context: Sexual activities between blood relatives are taboo.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í bá ọmọ ẹni ṣeré kó doko ẹgba.
Target_Text_En: One does not play with one’s child and then head for the bush of whips.
Cultural_Context: One should keep the play in playing and not turn it into a quarrel.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í tóó bánigbé ká má tòó ọ̀rọ̀-ọ́ bánisọ.
Target_Text_En: One does not qualify to live with a person without also qualifying to talk to the person.
Cultural_Context: Friends and relatives have every right to counsel with a person.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í yan àna ẹni lódì.
Target_Text_En: One does not refuse to speak to one’s family in-law.
Cultural_Context: Certain obligations must never be neglected out of pique.

Source_Text_Yo: Ààyè ọmọ là ńfẹ́; a kì í fẹ́ ókú ọmọ.
Target_Text_En: One courts a live person; one does not court a dead person.
Cultural_Context: One should spare no effort to keep one’s child alive.

Source_Text_Yo: Adásínilọ́rùn, obìnrin ọ̀dọ̀gọ: ẹlérú ńwá ẹrú, ó ní kí wò n jẹkí ọkọ òun ti oko dẹ́ ná
Target_Text_En: Person-who-involves-one-in-trouble, idiotic woman: a slave owner comes searching for his missing slave, and she says he should wait until her husband returns from the farm.
Cultural_Context: A loose mouth is a dangerous thing for the owner and his or her kin.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkèekèe òjògán fìdí jà; ará ilé ẹni-í fojúdini.
Target_Text_En: The formidable scorpion fights with its tail; members of one’s household belittle one.
Cultural_Context: Those most familiar with you are likely to show you disrespect. The scorpion’s fighting with its tail, rather than its arms, is here construedasasignofcontemptforthe adversary.

Source_Text_Yo: Amúnibúni ẹran Ìbíyẹ; Ìbíyẹ-ẹ́ fọ́jú ọ̀tún, ẹran-an rẹ̀-ẹ́ fọ́ tòsì.
Target_Text_En: A-creature-that-makes-one-insult-anotherperson, Ìbíyẹ’s goat; Ìbíyẹ is blind in the right eye,and her goat is blind in the left
Cultural_Context: If the parent and the child share the same trait, one risks provoking the parent by remarking on the trait in the child

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣenilóde ò tó tilé; ilé ni wọ́n ti ńṣeni.
Target_Text_En: The-enemy-outside is no match for the enemy at home; one is done in in one’s own home.
Cultural_Context: The enemy at home is more formidable than the enemy abroad.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣiwèrè èèyàn ní ńkọṣẹ́ àbọ̀ ọjà.
Target_Text_En: Only an imbecile refuses to run an errand he or she can do on the way from the market.
Cultural_Context: One should not refuse to do a favor that entails no hardship or inconvenience.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣusọ́nà ní ńfi ìyá-a rẹ̀ gbèpè
Target_Text_En: A child who shits on the path brings down curses on its mother. B
Cultural_Context: A child’s behavior is a reflection on its mother; a child’s misbehav ior exposes its parents to castigation.

Source_Text_Yo: Bàbá laláàbò; ìyá lonírànwọ́; orogún nikú
Target_Text_En: A father is a protector; a mother is a helper; a co-wife is death.
Cultural_Context: Two women who share the same husband are deadly enemies.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá wí pé kí ará ilé ẹni má lòówó, ará òdé ní ńyáni lọ́fà.
Target_Text_En: If one schemes so that one’s relatives may not prosper, outsiders eventually receive one as a pawn.
Cultural_Context: One who works to ensure that one’s people do not succeed becomes fair game for outsiders.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá fi oògùn pa ọmọ ìyá ẹni, ọmọ bàbá ẹni kì í sá fúnni.
Target_Text_En: If one did not kill one’s sibling by the same mother with poison, one’s sibling by the same father does not flee.
Cultural_Context: If one has done nothing to encourage them to do so, one’s close relatives will not avoid one.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá lè dijú kan ọmọ ẹni níkòó, ojú là ńlà sílẹ̀ tí wọ́n fi ńkàn án lọ́mọríodó lórí.
Target_Text_En: If one cannot close one’s eyes to rap one’s child on the head, one will watch with wide open eyes as others hit him on the head with a pestle.
Cultural_Context: If one will not discipline one’s child, others will, and much more mercilessly.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá sọ fún ọmọdé pé èèyàn lọkọ ìyá-a rẹ̀, a ní ta ní ńwá gba ìyá òun lẹ́kọ jẹ lójoojúm yìí?
Target_Text_En: If a child is not told that a certain person is its mother’s husband, the child asks who this person is who comes everyday to take food from its mother.
Cultural_Context: Without knowing the re lationship between two people, one cannot understand their actions.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí àkùkọ́ bá kọ láyé, àwọn ẹgbẹ́ ẹ̀ á gbè é lọ́run.
Target_Text_En: If a cock crows on earth, its peers respond in heaven.
Cultural_Context: A company always backs up its leader.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ará ilé ẹní bá ńjẹ kòkòrò tí kò sunwọ̀n, tí a kò sọ fún un, hùrùhẹ̀rẹ-ẹ rẹ̀ ọ níí j ká sùn lóru.
Target_Text_En: If a member of one’s household is eating bad insects and is not cautioned, his or her hacking cough will not permit one any sleep during the night.
Cultural_Context: If one does not counsel one’s brother, one will share in his misfortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ẹni ẹní bá kú lókèèrè, à pẹta-a r wálé.
Target_Text_En: If one’s relative dies far away from home, the dead person’s relic is sent home.
Cultural_Context: How ever far a person wanders, something of that person must eventually return home.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ikú ilé ò pani, tòde ò lè pani.
Target_Text_En: If the death at home does not kill one, the death outside will not.
Cultural_Context: If one is secure at home, one will be secure abroad.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ó bá bá ojú, á bá imú pẹ́lú.
Target_Text_En: Whatever disaster befalls the eye will also befall the nose.
Cultural_Context: One shares in the fate of people close to one.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí orí kan-án bá sunwọ̀n á ran igba.
Target_Text_En: If a head is blessed with good fortune, it will affect a hundred others.
Cultural_Context: To be associated with success is to benefit from the success.

Source_Text_Yo: Binisí-binisí: ọ̀tá ilé ò rí kòtò bini sí.
Target_Text_En: Push-one-into, push-one-into: one’s house hold enemy can find no ditch to push one into. E
Cultural_Context: The enemy in your own home cannot openly hurt you.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèyàn ẹni là ńfi ààyè ọmọ hàn; nígbà tó bá dòkú gbogbo ayé ní ńyọrí-i rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One presents one’s live child only to one’s kin; when it dies, the world makes itself scarce.
Cultural_Context: One shares good fortune only with those who will stand by in times of need.

Source_Text_Yo: Egbò-ó kẹ̀, iná kẹ̀, ohùn èèyàn-án kẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The ulcer grows bigger, the fire glows redder, and one’s voice grows hoarse.
Cultural_Context: The unrelenting misbehavior of others necessitates one’s continuous admonition.

Source_Text_Yo: Èkúté ilé tó fàkọ̀ sílẹ̀ tó ńjọ̀bẹ, tẹnu ẹni ló fẹ́ẹ́ gbọ́.
Target_Text_En: The house mouse that spares the sheath but eats the knife is bent on provoking one.
Cultural_Context: A person who deliberately provokes another is spoiling for a fight.

Source_Text_Yo: Ení tere, èjì tere lọjà-á fi ńkún.
Target_Text_En: The first solitary person, then the second solitary person: thus is the market filled.
Cultural_Context: A collection of solitary individuals makes a multitude. See the next entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ení tere, èjì tere, ọ̀pọ̀ wọ̀mù.
Target_Text_En: The first solitary person, then the second solitary person, eventually a multitude.
Cultural_Context: This a variant of the preceding entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Èpìpà ńpa ara-a rẹ̀ ó ní òun ńpa ajá.
Target_Text_En: The hard tick is committing suicide but be lieves it is killing the dog. Ẹ
Cultural_Context: The host’s death is the parasite’s also; one destroys oneself if one destroys one’s only support. A vul nerable person who does not lie low invites disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni ẹlẹni ní ńkọlé fún ikán.
Target_Text_En: It is other people who build homes for the termite.
Cultural_Context: One may benefit from other people’s labors.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní ní ìlú ò dùn, kó kẹ́rù kó gba oko lọ.
Target_Text_En: Whoever says the town is not pleasant should pack his or her luggage and head for the bush.
Cultural_Context: Antisocial people deserve to live by themselves in the forest.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó ba ọmọ ọlọ́mọ lórí jẹ, òrìṣà inú ilé yó ba tirẹ̀ náà jẹ.
Target_Text_En: Whoever ruins the lot of an innocent person will have his own lot ruined by the god of the hearth.
Cultural_Context: The gods visit retribution on those who do evil to others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnìkan ní ńkésẹ̀ nílùú, tí a fi ńsọ wípé à ńlọ sílùú akésẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Onlyonepersoninatownhastohavehis or her leg amputated before people will say they are on their way to the amputee’s town.
Cultural_Context: One person’s blight rubs off on all associated with him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbódó rù mí kí ngbé àlàpà ru ọmọ-ọ̀ rẹ.
Target_Text_En: Burden me with a mortar, and I will burden your child with a denuded wall.
Cultural_Context: A vow to pay like with like.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbogbo ìká fojú ṣe ọ̀kan, àtàm̀pàkò-ó ṣe tiẹ̀ lọ́tọ̀.
Target_Text_En: All fingers face in one direction; the thumb alone goes its own way.
Cultural_Context: In a consensual assembly, there is the loner who must go it independently.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbàdàn kì í gbe onílé bí àjèjì.
Target_Text_En: The city Ibadan is never as hospitable to its natives as to strangers.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who are kinder to strangers than to their friends or relatives.

Source_Text_Yo: Ifá ní ká jọ wò ó; mo ní ká jọ wò ó; ohun tí a bá jọ wò gigún ní ńgún.
Target_Text_En: Ifá says we should mind it together; I say we should mind it together; whatever all mind together will come out just right.
Cultural_Context: (When all people pool their resources, everything comes out right.

Source_Text_Yo: Igi wọ́rọ́kú daná rú; èèyàn burúkú bàsè jẹ́
Target_Text_En: A crooked piece of wood scatters the fire; an evil person ruins a feast.
Cultural_Context: The presence of a contrary person in a group robs the group of any harmony.

Source_Text_Yo: Igún pá lórí, kò kan alábẹ.
Target_Text_En: The vulture’s baldness has nothing to do with a barber.
Cultural_Context: Said of a certain person’s troubles which are not of others’ making.

Source_Text_Yo: Igbó etílé òun ẹ̀gbin, àdàpọ̀ òwò òun ìyà; yàrá à-jùmọ̀ -gbé ìtalẹ̀ ni nínú.
Target_Text_En: The forest close by the town is doomed to cope with filth; a trading partnership ex poses one to suffering; a shared bedroom is a breeding ground for mud-earth-dwelling biting worms.
Cultural_Context: All relationships entail irri tants and require some capacity for accom modation.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìríni ni ìkíni; ìkíni ni ìjẹ́ni.
Target_Text_En: To see a person is to greet the person; to be greeted is to respond.
Cultural_Context: The well-bred person greets people when he or she sees them, and the well-bred person responds to greetings.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí àdàbà sùú-sùú wí fú jẹdíẹdíẹ; kíyẹ ó wí fẹ́yẹ.
Target_Text_En: Let the pigeon talk to the woodpecker; let bird speak to another bird.
Cultural_Context: Each person should spread a matter under discussion to as many ears as possible.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò-gbélé-kò-gbọ́nà ní ńsìnkú àbíkú
Target_Text_En: He-does-not-live-in-the-home-and-he does-not-live-on-the-path is the one who buries the àbíkú.
Cultural_Context: The footloose stranger will always be called upon to help do things no one else wants to do.

Source_Text_Yo: Kọ̀ǹkọ̀ṣọ̀ ò dá ku èlùbọ́.
Target_Text_En: The sieve does not sift yam flour on its own.
Cultural_Context: No individual is self-sufficient.

Source_Text_Yo: Lọ́jọ́ ikú ọ̀tà, gbogbo tà ní ńpé jọ.
Target_Text_En: On the day a merchant dies, all merchants gather.
Cultural_Context: It is right and fitting to do one’s duty by one’s comrades.

Source_Text_Yo: Má ta omi sí mi lára kì í dé odò; má fàrá kàn mi kì í wá ọjà.
Target_Text_En: Do not splash water on me’’ should stay away from the river; ‘‘Do not touch my per son’’ should stay away from the market.
Cultural_Context: People who would rather be alone should avoid gathering places.

Source_Text_Yo: Mo ni "Ajowò," wọ́n ni "Ajowò"; ohun ti a ba jo wo gugun ni ńgún.
Target_Text_En: Let us mind it together,’’ and they responded, ‘‘Let us mind it together’’; what ever has everyone’s attention and care comes out straight.
Cultural_Context: Pooling resources ensures success.

Source_Text_Yo: "Mo ti wi?" "Bẹ́ẹ̀ lo wi!" Ẹ̀ẹ̀kannáà làwon méjèèji ngbonu sókè.
Target_Text_En: What did I say?’’ ‘‘So you said!’’ Both mouths speak in unison. N
Cultural_Context: Unanimous agree ment leaves no room for dispute.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Ng ò lè jẹ ìjẹkújè’’ kì í gbé àwùjọ ọ̀pọ̀ èèyàn
Target_Text_En: ‘I will not eat rubbish’’ does not live in a crowd.
Cultural_Context: One must have a thick skin if one wishes to be part of a crowd.

Source_Text_Yo: "Ng ò níí fẹ́, ng ò níí gbà": ibi tó sùn sí lánàá, kò níí sùn síb lónìí
Target_Text_En: ‘‘I will never agree, and I will never con cede’’: wherever he slept last night, he will not sleep there today. O
Cultural_Context: A disagreeable per son is not welcome company anywhere for long.

Source_Text_Yo: Ò ńwòmí, mò ńwò ọ́; ta ní ṣeun nínú u wa?
Target_Text_En: All you do is look at me, and all I do is look at you; which of us is any use to the other?
Cultural_Context: A person who does not lift a hand to help another deserves no help from that other in return.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó pa wọ́n tán nínú ọmọ ataare; kí là bá tún fèèpo ṣe?
Target_Text_En: He has removed all the seeds from the alli gator pepper; what now can one do with the shell?
Cultural_Context: Said of a person who has taken the best of some communal property, leaving others with little that is of any use.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú ẹni là ḿbi aṣeni lóhun.
Target_Text_En: It is in the presence of witnesses that one challenges the person who caused one in jury.
Cultural_Context: One should make a point of exposing one’s detractor or injurer to the public.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojúlùmò níí jẹ́ kà na ìyá ọ̀gbà ẹni.
Target_Text_En: The community will not let one flog the mother of one’s comrade.
Cultural_Context: Communal sanctions prevent outrageous behavior. See the following proverb for comparison.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojúlùmò níí jẹ káhun ó sun ìgbẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The community will not let the miser sleep in the wild.
Cultural_Context: Even the antisocial person will benefit from communal solicitousness. Compare the preceding proverb.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkò là ńsọ sígúnnugún níyà míràn; ibi a gbé mọgún la ti ńṣegún lóore.
Target_Text_En: It is with stone missiles that the vulture is greeted in foreign lands; only where the vulture is known does it receive favorable treatment.
Cultural_Context: Only where people know one’s stature does one receive the respect one deserves.

Source_Text_Yo: Onílù-ú ò fẹ́ kó tú; abánigbé ló ńṣe é bẹ́ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The native of the town does not wish it to break up; it is the doing of the sojourner.
Cultural_Context: People with no stake in a venture might wish to destroy; not so those with a stake in it.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí kìí burú lọ́wọ̀ọ́.
Target_Text_En: One head is never [individually] unfortunate in a large company.
Cultural_Context: Misfortune does not single out a person from among a group.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Òun ló mọ̀’’ kì í mọ ní òun nìkan. ‘‘
Target_Text_En: That is his business’’ never confines itself to him. Ọ
Cultural_Context: A matter that concerns one person inevitably comes to concern others also.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọba ní ńgba a-láì-lárá.
Target_Text_En: The king is the defense of the person who has no kin.
Cultural_Context: The king is the ultimate protec tor of his people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọbẹ̀ tó dànù, òfò onílé, òfò àlejò.
Target_Text_En: The stew that spilled [is] a loss to the host and a loss to the visitor.
Cultural_Context: The destruction of anything valuable is a loss to everybody.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọkọ́ kú, ọmọ ọba mẹ́ta-á pètè; Ọbẹ̀ẹ̀ mú epo, Lálá mú íyọ̀; Àjùwọ́n mú atà.
Target_Text_En: The husband died, and three princesses made their contribution [to the feast]; Ọb brought palm oil, Lálá brought salt, and Àjùwn brought pepper.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who are supposed to carry out a project but who cannot effectively coordinate their efforts.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọdé gbọ́n, Ààrẹ́ gbọ̀n, la fi ńtẹ ilẹ. ifẹ̀
Target_Text_En: A youth is wise, and the chief is wise: that is the principle by which people go about at Ifẹ̀.
Cultural_Context: A youth’s counsel is as worth entertain ing as a chief ’s.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọdé ò jobì, àgbà ò joyè.
Target_Text_En: The youth does not eat kola nuts; the elder does not win the chieftaincy title.
Cultural_Context: If you do not cultivate others, even those lesser than yourself, then you cannot expect any consideration from them.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pẹ tó darí, igbà-á kọ̀ ọ́.
Target_Text_En: The palm tree whose top is bent to the ground is rejected by the climbing rope.
Cultural_Context: If you pose no challenge, people won’t expend any effort in dealing with you.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pọ̀ èèyàn kì í wọ Orò kí Orò gbé wọn
Target_Text_En: A multitude of people cannot enter the Orò grove and be carried away by Orò.
Cultural_Context: There is strength and security in numbers.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pọ̀ èèyàn ní ńjẹ́ jànmáà.
Target_Text_En: It is a multitude of people that is called a congregation.
Cultural_Context: No one person can be a multitude.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pọ̀ leṣú fi ya igi lóko.
Target_Text_En: It is by means of their numbers that locusts tear down a branch on the farm.
Cultural_Context: There is strength in numbers.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn tó bá ṣe ojú ìlú ò fara sin.
Target_Text_En: Whatever happened in the presence of the whole town cannot be kept secret.
Cultural_Context: It is pointless to be secretive about something everybody already knows about.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀run ńya bọ̀, kì í ṣọ̀ràn ẹnìkan.
Target_Text_En: The sky falling down is not any one per son’s problem.
Cultural_Context: One should not be overly concerned at the threat of a danger that is general. See the following entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀run ńya bọ̀, ò ńyẹrí; ìwọ nìkan ni?
Target_Text_En: The sky is falling and you are ducking your head; are you the only one [in danger]?
Cultural_Context: There is no sense in trying to avoid a dan ger that is general. See the previous entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ṣín mọ ìwẹ̀, inú ḿbí ẹyẹ oko.
Target_Text_En: The fish eagle knows how to swim; the other birds of the forest seethe with anger.
Cultural_Context: People are ever jealous of others’ accomplishments.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ́tọ̀ọ̀tọ̀ èyí làna ìgbín? Ìpére-é kú o ò sunkún, ìlákọ̀ṣẹ-ẹ́ kú o ò gbààwẹ̀, o bá ẹlẹ́tẹ lónà o tẹ̀ ẹ́ rẹ́, odò ńgbé ìṣáwùrú lọ o ní ‘‘Dẹ̀ẹ̀, dẹ̀ẹ̀, máa rà’’; ta lò ńṣe àna fún?
Target_Text_En: What sort of in-law are you to the snail? A small snail dies and you do not cry; tiny snails die and you do not abstain from eating; you see the grasshopper on the path and you step on it; the stream is carrying rounded small snails away and you say ‘‘Float gently away!’’ To whom do you perform in-law obligations?
Cultural_Context: Said of people who display no fellow feeling with anyone.

Source_Text_Yo: Float gently away!’’ To whom do you per form in-law obligations?
Target_Text_En: The expression hánnìyàn (or, better, hàn- -yàn for han èèyàn) literally means ‘‘show people.’’[?]small snail dies and you do not cry; tiny snails die and you do not abstain from eat ing; you see the grasshopper on the path and you step on it; the stream is carry ing rounded small snails away and you say ‘‘
Cultural_Context: Said of people who display no fellow feeling with anyone.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀tùn ì bá pọ̀ tó Ìbàdàn, à-múró-yaró ni ó jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Ibadan but for the addiction of its people to vengeance.
Cultural_Context: Insistence on vengeance will disperse a community.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀tún wẹ òsì, òsì wẹ tún lọw fi ḿmọ́.
Target_Text_En: The right washing the left and the left wash ing the right is the way to get the hands clean.
Cultural_Context: Success in a venture depends on cooperation.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọwọ́ epo layé ḿbáni lá, ayé kì í báni láwọ́ ẹ̀jẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The world will join one in licking fingers dripping with palm oil but not in licking fingers dripping with blood.
Cultural_Context: People will share your good fortune with you, but not your misfortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀wọ́ ni ọ̀wọ́ ikán, ọ̀pọ̀ ni ọ̀pọ̀ èèrùn.
Target_Text_En: The orderliness is the orderliness of termites; the multiplicity is the multiplicity of the swarming brown ants.
Cultural_Context: Said in describing a great multitude attending an event.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọwọ́ ọmọdé ò tó pẹpẹ, ọwọ́ àgbà ò wọ kèrègbè; iṣẹ́ tí àgbà-á bá bẹ ọmọdé kó máṣe kọ̀ó; gbogbo wa la ní ohun tí a lè ṣe fúnra-a wa.
Target_Text_En: The youth’s hand cannot reach the rafters, and the elder’s hand cannot enter the gourd; the youth should not refuse to run the errand on which the elder sends him or her; each one of us can do something for the other.
Cultural_Context: Everybody needs someone some time; therefore, one should not refuse to aid others, even those one thinks one will never need.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọwọ́ púpọ̀ ní ńpa osùn.
Target_Text_En: Many hands are required to rub camwood powder on the body.
Cultural_Context: Many hands cooperat ing ensure that a task is thoroughly done.

Source_Text_Yo: Pípé là ńpé gbọ́n, a kì í pé gọ̀.
Target_Text_En: People assemble to seek wisdom collectively; people do not assemble in order to become stupid.
Cultural_Context: If people are willing to talk, others will be willing to listen.

Source_Text_Yo: Sọ̀ọ̀r-sọ̀rọ̀-ọ̀ wà, bẹ́ẹ̀ ni ẹní máa gbọ́ ḿbẹ.
Target_Text_En: There is the loquacious person, and so also there is the person willing to listen.
Cultural_Context: If people are willing to talk, others will be willing to listen.

Source_Text_Yo: Tẹ̀ mí ntẹ̀ ọ́, layé gbà.
Target_Text_En: Step on me and I will step on you is what life takes.
Cultural_Context: In life we must act toward others as they act toward us. Compare 3188.

Source_Text_Yo: Tijú fún mi kí ntijú fún ọ; ẹni tó tijú fúnni là ńtijú fún.
Target_Text_En: Behave with decorum toward me, and I will behave with decorum toward you; only those who approach one with decorum earn decorum in return. 320 relationships
Cultural_Context: Act toward people the way you would like them to act toward you.

Source_Text_Yo: Túlùú-túlùú, ẹyẹ Elém̀pe
Target_Text_En: Town disperser, the Elé pe bird.[?]Y
Cultural_Context: A person who carries rumors from people to people will cause dissension in the community.

Source_Text_Yo: Yánníbo-ó mú erèé rún; gbẹ̀gìrì-í ṣàn
Target_Text_En: Yánníbo chewed up the black-eyed peas; the black-eyed-pea stew is watery.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who ruin or deplete what was set aside for the benefit of a whole group.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Yó bàá ọ,’’ kì í ba ẹnìkan mọ
Target_Text_En: ‘A pox on you!’’ does not limit its effect to only one person.
Cultural_Context: Ill fortune invoked for specific people affects others close to them.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í tán fún ẹni ilé jókòó.
Target_Text_En: One does not spread a mat for a member of the household to sit on.
Cultural_Context: Acquaintances should not insist on being waited upon like strangers.

Source_Text_Yo: A-bániṣe-mábàániṣe-mọ́: à bùṣà fáláṣejù kété-kété.
Target_Text_En: He-that-once-fraternized-with-one-but stops-doing-so: one would do well to give such a person a wide berth.
Cultural_Context: A friend turned enemy is a danger to be avoided.

Source_Text_Yo: A-bániwọ́ràn-bá-ò-rídá; ó fúnni léyìí tí kò wuni; ó pa ọmọ tún ọmọ rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: He-who-helps-one-find-trouble-when-one has-none gives what one does not want; he kills a child and returns to soothe the child.
Cultural_Context: A person who involves one in difficulties by his actions is no friend, however much he might pretend to be. See the following entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Àdàpọ̀ owó ní ḿmú ìjà wá.
Target_Text_En: Saving money in joint accounts results in quarrels.
Cultural_Context: Certain things should not be a part of friendship.

Source_Text_Yo: Adébipani kì í ṣọ̀rẹ́ ẹni.
Target_Text_En: He who inflicts hunger on one is no friend.
Cultural_Context: Know your enemy.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajé ní ḿba ojú ọ̀rẹ́ jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: It is money that brings a frown to the brow of friendship.
Cultural_Context: Nothing ruins a friendship more surely than the intrusion of money.

Source_Text_Yo: Àpá kì í jọ̀lọ̀ kó dà bí ara ẹni; ká jà ká rẹ́ ọ̀ dà bí ọ̀rẹ́ ìpilẹ̀ṣẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: However smooth a scar is, it is never the same as the original skin; a mended quarrel is not like original friendship.
Cultural_Context: Relationships may be mended, but it is better if they never need mending.

Source_Text_Yo: A-ríre-báni-jẹ, àgbọ̀n ìsàlẹ̀; òkú kú láàárọ̀, àgbọ̀n-ọ́n yà kó tó dàlẹ́.
Target_Text_En: A-thing-that-shares-only-good-things-withone, the lower jaw; a person dies in the morning, and the jaw separates before nightfall.
Cultural_Context: Fair-weather friends are like the lower jaw that separates from the head as soon as the owner dies.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá gbá ilé gbá ọ̀nà, ọ̀dọ̀ ààtàn là ńdà á sí.
Target_Text_En: After one has swept the house and the path ways, one dumps the dirt at the rubbish heap.
Cultural_Context: However long a matter is discussed, its resolution devolves to the proper agent. Compare 4857.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ijó bá di ijó àgbà, ìlù a yípadà.
Target_Text_En: When the dance becomes a dance of elders, the drumming should change.
Cultural_Context: One must match one’s behavior to one’s circum stances.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọmọdé láṣọ bí àgbà, kò lè lákìísà bí àgbà
Target_Text_En: A youth may have as many clothes as an elder, but he will not have as many rags as an elder.
Cultural_Context: Though a youth may enjoy the same rank as an elder, he cannot match the elder in experience.

Source_Text_Yo: Ègbé ni fún ọmọ tó ní bàbá òún kéré.
Target_Text_En: Woe betide the child who says his or her father is insignificant.
Cultural_Context: Children who belittle their father deserve the worst fate possible.

Source_Text_Yo: Ègbọ́n iwájú: alugbọn baba.
Target_Text_En: One’s older brother [is a suitable] substitute father.
Cultural_Context: Respect others of your elders as you would your parents.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a bá dé ìlú ò tó ẹni tí a dé ìlú mọ̀
Target_Text_En: The person with whom one came to a town is not as important as the person one came to know after arriving in the town. 322 relationships
Cultural_Context: A cur rent friend or benefactor is more important than a sometime friend or benefactor.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a bá nídìí àbà ní ńjẹ baba.
Target_Text_En: The person one finds settled at the granary is the lord of the place.
Cultural_Context: One should give due ragard to those who have been to places, or accomplished things, before one’s time. Compare 3326 and 3456.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìjà ò mẹ̀gbọ́n
Target_Text_En: A quarrel does not know who is the elder.
Cultural_Context: In a quarrel one is likely to forget all pro prieties.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkonkoso-ó tiiri pa eku, ìwọ̀- tiiri pa ẹja, ọkàa bàbà-á tiiri wo olóko; bí ọmọdé ó bàá àgbà jẹun títiiri ní ńtiiri.
Target_Text_En: The mousetrap leans to one side to kill the mouse; the hook bends in order to kill the fish; the guinea corn leans sideways to watch the farmer; if a child will eat with an elder, it is proper for the child to lean to the side.
Cultural_Context: One must defer to one’s elders and superiors and not be too forward in their company.

Source_Text_Yo: Ipa àbálẹ́ lọkùn ńtò.
Target_Text_En: It is the path blazed by the needle that the thread follows.
Cultural_Context: One should emulate one’s elders.

Source_Text_Yo: "Ó ḿbọ!" ló yẹ baba; bí baba bá dé, rán tán.
Target_Text_En: Watch out, here he comes’’ is what befits the patriarch; after he has arrived, there is no more threat. Ọ
Cultural_Context: Fear of what a person might do is often a more powerful deterrent than what the person is actually capable of doing.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọdé fẹ́ẹ́ kú, o ní ẹnu àgbà ńrùn.
Target_Text_En: A child seeks death [when] he says the mouth of an elder stinks.
Cultural_Context: Disrespect for elders is a death wish.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọdé kì í wò ṣọ̀ṣọ̀ níbùjókòó àgbà
Target_Text_En: A youth does not stare when in the com pany of elders.
Cultural_Context: Etiquette demands that youth avert its eyes from age, or at least look deferentially at it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀-pani-nítàn ní ńfi ojúlé ẹni hanni.
Target_Text_En: It is the person who tells one one’s own his tory that shows one the doorway to one’s own home.
Cultural_Context: We would do well to pay at tention to the words of the sages who know more than we do about our own lineage.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí a pé kí baba má gbọ̀ọ́, baba ní ńparí ẹ̀
Target_Text_En: A matter that one tries to keep from the ears of the patriarch will eventually come before the patriarch for resolution.
Cultural_Context: The elders have a right to be privy to all important matters, because keeping order and peace is their responsibility.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí ọbá bá sọ, abẹ́ gé e.
Target_Text_En: Whatever the king says is severed by a razor.
Cultural_Context: The king’s word is final. See the previous entry.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í bá ẹrú mulẹ̀, ká bá olúwa mulẹ̀, ká má da ẹnìkan.
Target_Text_En: One cannot make a pact with the slave and make a pact with the master and not betray one of them.
Cultural_Context: One cannot enter into alliance with people whose interests are in conflict.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dúpẹ́ ara ènì.
Target_Text_En: One does not give thanks to oneself.
Cultural_Context: Grati tude is superfluous among close friends or relatives.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ibi sú olóore.
Target_Text_En: One does not return evil to one’s benefactor.
Cultural_Context: Never render evil for good.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi òtítọ́ sínú gbàwìn ìkà.
Target_Text_En: One does not leave truthfulness inside to purchase wickedness on credit.
Cultural_Context: Never go out of your way to injure others.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ràn-an pápá lọ ẹja; a kì í fi ọ̀ràn-an odò lọ àfè.
Target_Text_En: One does not invite a fish to the grassland; one does not entice the field mouse to the stream.
Cultural_Context: Do not expect people to destroy themselves at your bidding.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gba àkàkà lọ́wọ́ akítì; a kì ígba ilée baba ẹni lọ́wọ́ ẹni.
Target_Text_En: One does not deny the monkey the habit of squatting; one does not wrest a person’s father’s home from him.
Cultural_Context: Respect others’ rights.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbà lọ́wọ́-ọ ‘‘Mé rì í.’’
Target_Text_En: One does not take from ‘‘I do not have.’’
Cultural_Context: Never seek to take from the destitute the little they do have.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í rí a-rẹ́-má-jà; a kì í rí a-jà-má-rèẹ́.
Target_Text_En: No one ever sees friends who do not quarrel; no one ever sees people who quarrel and never make up.
Cultural_Context: Friendship and quarrels cannot go on forever, unbroken.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ṣe ọ̀rẹ́ èrò ká yọ̀; èrò yó relé bó dọ̀la.
Target_Text_En: One does not befriend a sojourner and re joice; the sojourner will leave for home come tomorrow.
Cultural_Context: Permanent ties are to be preferred to fleeting ones.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ṣìpẹ̀-ẹ ‘‘Nàró’’ fábuké.
Target_Text_En: One does not give the advice ‘‘Stand up straight’’ to a humpback.
Cultural_Context: Do not impose impossible conditions on others.

Source_Text_Yo: À ńdáhùn sí gbèsè; góńgó orí ẹ̀ la kì í kán.
Target_Text_En: One may intervene in the discussion of a debt, but one does not break its spike.
Cultural_Context: Though one may discuss others’ debts, one has no obligation to settle them.

Source_Text_Yo: Abanijẹ́ ba ara ẹ̀ jẹ́
Target_Text_En: A detractor injures his own reputation.
Cultural_Context: A person who maligns other people re-flects badly on his own character.

Source_Text_Yo: Abanijó níí gbayì.
Target_Text_En: A detractor will not earn a good reputation.
Cultural_Context: This is a variant of the previous entry.

Source_Text_Yo: A-báni-jẹ-má-bàáni-ṣe, ìfà èèyàn; ẹní jẹ dídùn ní ńjẹ kíkan.
Target_Text_En: He-who-shares-one’s-food-but-does-not share-one’s-tasks [is a] freeloader; he who eats the sweet should also eat the sour.
Cultural_Context: People should not be fair-weather friends.

Source_Text_Yo: Abánikú rọṣẹ wón; abánikú, ogun ní ḿbani lọ.
Target_Text_En: A friend who would die with one is rare; he who would do so accompanies one even to war.
Cultural_Context: Few friends will risk death by ac companying one to a war that they have no interest in.

Source_Text_Yo: Abánirẹ́ fi àfo ìjà sílẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: A person who befriends another should make allowances for quarrels.
Cultural_Context: It is realis tic to expect that a friendship will not be without occasional quarrels.

Source_Text_Yo: Àdánù ńláńlá ni fún ẹni tó fẹ́ni, tí a ò fẹ́.
Target_Text_En: What a great loss it is for a person who loves you but that you do not love.
Cultural_Context: Unrequited love is a painful thing.

Source_Text_Yo: Àdàpọ̀mọ́ obìnrin ò ṣéé yanjú
Target_Text_En: A congress of women [or with women] is not easy to unravel.
Cultural_Context: Problems in cer tain relationships defy intervention from outside.

Source_Text_Yo: Adáríjini ní ńṣẹ̀tẹ́ ẹjọ́.
Target_Text_En: He who forgives takes the wind out of the case’s sails.
Cultural_Context: To forgive is to be magnani mous.

Source_Text_Yo: Adìẹ́ dà mí lóògùn nù; mo fọ́ ọ lẹ́yin.
Target_Text_En: The chicken spilled my medicine; I broke its eggs.
Cultural_Context: One pays back tit for tat.

Source_Text_Yo: A-dùn-ún-jẹ bí àjẹpọ̀.
Target_Text_En: A delight to eat, like something one shares with others.
Cultural_Context: It is more delightful to share food than to eat alone.

Source_Text_Yo: Afiniṣẹ̀sín àlè, ó ní òun ó jẹ ibàpẹ.
Target_Text_En: Concubine-who-would-disgrace-one says she would like some papaya.
Cultural_Context: True love and true friendship make no impossible demands. This is a variant of 3322.

Source_Text_Yo: Afínjú méjì kì í wo òjìji wọn nínú agada.
Target_Text_En: Two fops will not share the same mirror.
Cultural_Context: Arrogance leaves no room for rivalry.

Source_Text_Yo: Àfiohunwéohun, àfọ̀rànwéọ̀ràn; fi ràn jì ká lè yinni.
Target_Text_En: Recalling-similar-matters-of-the-past, recalling-similar-problems-of-the-past, for give an offense and earn praise.
Cultural_Context: One should forgive and not keep recalling past offenses.

Source_Text_Yo: À-fi-ọ̀rọ̀-wé-ọ̀rọ̀ ò jẹ́ kí ọ̀rọ̀ tán bọ̀rọ̀ .
Target_Text_En: Allowing-a-current-matter-to-remind-one of-similar-matters-in-the-past prevents a quarrel from ending easily.
Cultural_Context: This is similar to the previous entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgùntàn tó bá ajá rìn á jẹ̀gbẹ́
Target_Text_En: A sheep that fraternizes with dogs will eat excrement
Cultural_Context: One inevitably assumes the habits of one’s constant company.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà ò sí nílùú ọ̀kẹ́rẹ́.
Target_Text_En: There are no elders in the town of squirrels.
Cultural_Context: Some cultures lack proper regard for age.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà tí kò fọ̀ mọ́ni níkùn kì í fọ̀ mọ́ni lórí.
Target_Text_En: An elder who does not make an impression on one’s stomach does not make an impres sion on one’s mind.
Cultural_Context: If a venerable elder cannot feed you, he may not command you, either.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà tí kò yáni lẹ́gbàá ìkọ̀kọ̀, bó bá dáṣẹ́ ilẹ́ sílẹ̀ a kì í lọ.
Target_Text_En: An elder who does not secretly lend one six pence: if he embarks on building a house, one does not show up to help.
Cultural_Context: One returns favor for favor.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà tó bú èwe lèwe ḿbú.
Target_Text_En: It is an elder who insults a youth that a youth insults.
Cultural_Context: Elders earn respect only if they respect others.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà tó gba gbàdù, ó gba ìtùnú.
Target_Text_En: An elder who has experienced a disaster has earned commiseration.
Cultural_Context: Be sensitive to other people’s difficulties.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà tó gbin èbù ìkà, orí ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀ ni yó hù sí.
Target_Text_En: An elder who plants yams of wickedness will see them sprout on the head of his child.
Cultural_Context: The wickedness of the father will be visited on the children. Compare 702 and 1306.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà tó jẹ à-jẹ-ì-wẹ̀hìn ni yó ru ẹrù-u r délé
Target_Text_En: The elder who eats with abandon will carry his own load to the house.
Cultural_Context: If an elder offers no food to the youth around him, he cannot expect any help from them.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàlagbà kì í méku dání kó di amùn rín.
Target_Text_En: An elder does not hold a rat and see it turn into a lizard.
Cultural_Context: One should be able to rely on an elder.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbàlagbà ńfìbínú lọ sÍlọrin, a ní kó ra tìróò bọ̀.
Target_Text_En: An elder is on his way to Ìlọrin in anger, and we ask him to bring back galena for us.3
Cultural_Context: One should be sensitive to other people’s predicaments. This is a variant of the preceding entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjẹìw hìn literally means ‘‘eating without look ing back’’: in other words, eating without considering what is proper.
Target_Text_En: What is proper is for elders to leave a little of their food for the young people.
Cultural_Context: That gesture is rewarded by the youths, who will stop the elder from doing any task and do it themselves. If the elder omits this gesture, he loses the consideration and respect of the youth.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbẹ̀jẹ-ẹ́ gbà wọ́n là tán, wọ́n ní ká pa á ní páńṣá.
Target_Text_En: After the pumpkin had saved them , they ordered that it be cut into ordinary calabash.
Cultural_Context: in a famine Never forget those who stick by you in your times of difficulty.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìfinipèni, àìfèèyànpèèyàn lará oko-ó fi ńsán ìbàǹtẹ́ wọ̀lú.
Target_Text_En: Lack-of-regard-for-anyone, lack-of-regard for-people makes the bush dweller enter the town in his loincloth.
Cultural_Context: Self-respect implies respect for others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá kì í gbàgbé olóore
Target_Text_En: A dog never forgets a benefactor.
Cultural_Context: One will, or should, always remember one’s benefac tor.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá kọ imí ẹlẹ́dẹ̀; ẹlẹ́dẹ̀-ẹ̀ kọ imí ajá.
Target_Text_En: The dog snubs the pig’s excrement; the pig snubs the dog’s excrement.
Cultural_Context: Neither party in a relationship will accept disrespect from the other.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá tó yó kì í bá àìyó ṣeré
Target_Text_En: A satiated dog does not frolic with a hun gry dog.
Cultural_Context: Avoid levity in the company of benighted people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajègbodò ńwá ẹni kúnra.
Target_Text_En: The-eater-of-new-yams seeks people to join him.
Cultural_Context: A culprit always wants company.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjọjẹ ò dùn bí ẹnìkan ò ní; bí a bá ní là ńṣe àjọjẹ.
Target_Text_En: Sharing of food is not pleasant if one par ticipant has nothing; it is when one has something that one shares.
Cultural_Context: Those who share expect something in return.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjọsùn ní ḿmú iná wá sáṣọ.
Target_Text_En: Sleeping together infects clothes with lice.
Cultural_Context: One takes on some of the blemishes of one’s associates.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkàṣù bàm̀bà lóṣù àgà, iṣu gbọọrọ lẹ́jọ̀dún
Target_Text_En: A sizable corn loaf in the month before the harvest, a long yam in the month of the har vest.
Cultural_Context: A good turn when it is needed will be repaid with accretion.

Source_Text_Yo: Àlè tí yó fini ṣẹ̀sín ní ńbèrè ibẹ́pẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is a concubine who wishes to disgrace one that demands pawpaw.
Cultural_Context: Those who deliber ately force one into compromising behavior seek to disgrace one.

Source_Text_Yo: À-múró-yaro ó jẹ́ kí ọ̀rọ̀ ó tán.
Target_Text_En: Repaying-injury-with-injury prevents the settlement of disputes.
Cultural_Context: As long as a wronged person insists on revenge, a quarrel will not be settled.

Source_Text_Yo: A-pọ́n-ori-kéré ò gbọ́n bí a-yọwó-má-rà.
Target_Text_En: The-person-who-skimps-on-his-or-her merchandise is not as clever as the would be-customer-who-prices-the-merchandise but-resists-buying.
Cultural_Context: The seller may attempt to scalp, but the buyer may refuse to buy.

Source_Text_Yo: Àràbà ni bàbá; ẹni a bá lábà ni baba.
Target_Text_En: The silk-cotton tree is the father; the person one finds at the hut is the lord.
Cultural_Context: Just as the silk-cotton tree sways over all other trees, the person who is first in a place holds sway over all others.

Source_Text_Yo: Àpá tètè is a game children on an errand play when there are alternate routes to their destination.
Target_Text_En: The children split into two groups, each party taking one route and trying to arrive first.
Cultural_Context: With friends and acquaintances 327

Source_Text_Yo: Àrífín ilé-ìgbẹ́, tí ḿmú ọmọdé wo ìhòòhò àgbà.
Target_Text_En: The disgrace that comes of using a commu nal latrine exposes an elder’s nakedness to the young.
Cultural_Context: The contingencies of living in a group sometimes expose one to insults one would otherwise avoid.

Source_Text_Yo: Àrífín tí ejò-ó fi yán ahun.
Target_Text_En: Lack of proper regard makes a snake bite a tortoise.
Cultural_Context: It is adding insult to injury for a person to be belittled by someone far below him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: À-rí-ìgbọdọ̀-wí, ẹran ilé tí ńfojú dọdẹ.
Target_Text_En: Something-seen-but-unmentionable: a do mestic animal that disdains a hunter.
Cultural_Context: The domestic animal may strut with impunity before a hunter.

Source_Text_Yo: À-ríni-mọ́ni ni à-kíni-mọ́ni.
Target_Text_En: Seeing-one-with-a-person is greeting-one with-a-person.
Cultural_Context: The sort of reception one receives depends on the sort of company one is in.

Source_Text_Yo: A-rojú-fúnni-láwìn-ọjà-á sàn ju a-rojú sinni-lówó lọ.
Target_Text_En: One-who-reluctantly-sells-to-one-on-credit is preferable to one-who-reluctantly-asks for-his-money.
Cultural_Context: Someone who reluctantly gives one something increases one’s stock nonetheless; someone who reluctantly takes from one decreases one’s stock. See the next entry also.

Source_Text_Yo: A-rọ́jú-fúnni-lóhun-ún sàn ju a-rọ́jú gbà-á lọ.
Target_Text_En: One-who-reluctantly-gives-one-something is preferable to one-who-reluctantly-takes it-back.
Cultural_Context: See the preceding entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Asínwín Ìká, aṣiwèrè Ìlúká, wọ́n dáríjọ, wọ́ ní àwọn ńṣọ̀rẹ́
Target_Text_En: The mad people of Ìká and the imbeciles 328 relationships[?]of Ìlúká got together and said they were all friends.
Cultural_Context: Like people keep like company.

Source_Text_Yo: Àsọtọẹ́lẹ̀ kò jẹ́ kí ìwọ̀fà di ẹrú olówó
Target_Text_En: A standing arrangement keeps the pawn from becoming a slave of the creditor.
Cultural_Context: To agree beforehand is to prevent misunder standings later.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣiwèrè èèyàn ní ńwípé ẹ̀gbọ́n ò tó; ẹni a bá níwájú ní ńṣe baba fúnni.
Target_Text_En: Only an imbecile says that those older than he or she are of no account; those who came before one can fill the role of father.
Cultural_Context: Never disdain an elder.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣọ kan-án kángun sára eégún ju ọ̀kan lọ.
Target_Text_En: One cloth is closer to the masquerader’s body than others.
Cultural_Context: Some friends or relatives are dearer than others.

Source_Text_Yo: A-tọ̀run-wáá-dọbẹ̀-síná, eégún-un sálà.
Target_Text_En: One-who-comes-all-the-way-from-heaven to-upset-stew-on-the-fire: masquerader of the Muslim day of worship.
Cultural_Context: The mas querader who disrupts one’s projects is an unwelcome visitor from heaven.

Source_Text_Yo: Awo ní ńperí awo.
Target_Text_En: Only mysteries can communicate with mys teries.
Cultural_Context: Only the initiate can gain access to mysteries and their import.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá ńdíje níbi iṣẹ, ọwà máa yán.
Target_Text_En: If people compete at a task, the task is soon done.
Cultural_Context: Competition promotes efficiency.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá torí igi gba odì, a ṣe iná fúnni yá.
Target_Text_En: If one makes enemies because of wood, it should make fire for one to warm oneself.
Cultural_Context: One should have something to show for one’s pains.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá fìjà pàdé, a kì í fìjà túká.
Target_Text_En: If people did not come together in a quarrel, they should not part in a quarrel.
Cultural_Context: Friend ship should not be permitted to turn to enmity.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá jà a kì í rẹ́.
Target_Text_En: If we have not quarreled, we cannot be friends.
Cultural_Context: Friends do not appreciate each other until after a quarrel.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá pàdé lókè, a ó pàdé lódò.
Target_Text_En: If we do not meet up on high, we will meet down below.
Cultural_Context: Paths that have crossed will somewhere, somehow, cross again.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá rí ohun fún òrìṣà èrò, a kì í gba torí-i r
Target_Text_En: If one has nothing to offer the god-
Cultural_Context: Not Provided

Source_Text_Yo: Bí àgbàlagbà kò bá ríbi jókòó, gbédìí gbédìí a gbé ọmọdé.
Target_Text_En: If an elder can find no place to sit, lift bottom-lift-bottom lifts the youth.
Cultural_Context: If a youth does not voluntarily show respect to elders, forces beyond his control will compel him.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí àgbàlagbà-á bá ńsòrí, tómọdé ò yájú, bó pẹ́ títí á mọ ohun tí wọn ńṣe.
Target_Text_En: If elders confer and the youth does not exceed his station, sooner or later he will know what they conferred about.
Cultural_Context: The well behaved youth will learn the way of the elders.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ará ilé ẹní bá forísọ, tí a kò bá mọ̀ ọ́ kí, ìjà ní ńdà.
Target_Text_En: If a member of one’s household bumps his or her head and one is careless in expressing one’s sympathy, a quarrel results.
Cultural_Context: Sympathy extended the wrong way leads to quarrels.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí aṣáájú ò bá mọ̀ọ́ rìn, ìgbẹ́ lára ẹ̀hìn ńwọ̀.
Target_Text_En: If the leader does not know his way, the follower winds up in the bush.
Cultural_Context: The incom petence of the leader spells disaster for the followers.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí èèyàn-án bá ṣeun ká sọ pé ó ṣeun; bí èèyàn-án bá ṣèèyàn ká sọ pé ó ṣèèyàn; nítorípé, ohun tí a ṣe, ó yẹ kó gbeni.
Target_Text_En: If a person deserves gratitude, we should say that he deserves gratitude; if a person is kindly, we should say that he is kindly, be cause one should reap the rewards of one’s actions. With friends and acquaintances 329
Cultural_Context: A person’s goodness should be publicly acknowledged.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ekòló bá júbà ilẹ̀, ilẹ̀ á lanu.
Target_Text_En: If the worm pays homage to the earth, the earth opens for it.
Cultural_Context: The proper approach will open any door.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ẹ̀bìtì ò pa eku, a kó ẹyìn fẹ́lẹ́yìn.
Target_Text_En: If the snare does not kill the rat, it returns the kernel bait to the owner.
Cultural_Context: If a performer will not carry out a task for which he or she has received payment, he or she returns the payment.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ẹlẹ́dá-é bá pàfọ̀ tán, ẹni rere ní ḿmáa-á wá fi yí lára.
Target_Text_En: After a pig has wallowed in the mud, it seeks a good person to soil with the mud.
Cultural_Context: Evil people always look for virtuous people to implicate.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí iná bá wọlé, òkùnkùn a paradà.
Target_Text_En: When light enters the house, darkness re moves itself.
Cultural_Context: When one’s superiors arrive, one yields authority to them.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí kò tó ẹ̀rù, kò tó ìsájú?
Target_Text_En: If it does not strike fear, does it not merit deference?
Cultural_Context: If one would not do a thing out of fear, could one not do it out of respect or as a favor?

Source_Text_Yo: "Bí o bá ṣe mí má ṣe ọ́" nigi oko ó fi ńdádé.
Target_Text_En: If you injure me, I will injure you in re turn’’; it is thus that trees in the forest sprout crowns.
Cultural_Context: Rivalry or antagonism is often the spur for glorious achievements.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ó ti ńṣe iṣu bẹ ló yé; bí ó ti ńṣèyàwó ọkọ-ọ rẹ̀ ló mọ̀; bí o ti ńṣe mí ẹ bi ọ̀rẹ́-ẹ̀ mi.
Target_Text_En: How the yam feels is known only to the knife; how the wife feels is known only to the husband; for how I feel, ask my friend.
Cultural_Context: The people closest to a person know best that person’s condition.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ó ti wù kí ọmọdé tètè jí tó, ọ̀nà ni yó bàá kùkùté.
Target_Text_En: However early the youth may rise from the bed, he will find the stump already on the road.
Cultural_Context: In some respects, the youth cannot compete with his elders.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí orí kan-án sunwọ̀n, a ran igba.
Target_Text_En: If one head is fortunate, it will affect others.
Cultural_Context: One person’s good fortune spills over to his or her associates.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí orogún ìyá ẹní bá ju ìyá ẹni lọ, ìyá là ńpè é.
Target_Text_En: If one’s mother’s co-wife is older than one’s mother, one calls her mother.
Cultural_Context: One shows the same respect to all elders as one would show to one’s parents.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí owó bá pọ̀ ọ̀rẹ́ àtèrò a pọ̀; bówó bá tán gbogbo wọn a wábi gbà lọ.
Target_Text_En: If money is plentiful, friends and guests are plentiful; when the money is gone, all of them will find other places to go.
Cultural_Context: People will swarm around the rich but disappear when reverses occur.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọmọdé bá máa só, a wo iwájú; bí àgbàá bá máa só, a wo ẹ̀hìn.
Target_Text_En: If a youth wants to fart, he looks ahead; if an elder wants to fart, he looks behind.
Cultural_Context: The youth should consider what his elders will make of his actions, whereas the elder should consider what example his actions set for the youth.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọmọdé bá ḿbá àgbà jẹun, títiiri ní ḿmáaá tiiri.
Target_Text_En: If a youth eats with an elder, he must show great diffidence.
Cultural_Context: In the company of elders, the youth must be well-behaved.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọmọdé bá ní baba òun ò tó ẹni tí à ńsáré bá, bàbá-a rẹ̀ a ní ọmọ òun ò tó ẹni tí à ńdúró dè.
Target_Text_En: If a youth says that his father is not worth catching up with, the father will say that his son is not worth waiting for.
Cultural_Context: A person who rejects his or her parents deserves to be disowned by them.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọmọdé bá ṣu imí búburú, èsìsì la fi ńnù ú nídìí.
Target_Text_En: If a youth expels foul excrement, one wipes his anus with nettle leaves.
Cultural_Context: A grievous offense deserves adequate punishment.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọtí bá ńpani, ṣé òorùn ńpa bọ̀tí; oró táa dá ọkà lọkà ńdáni san.
Target_Text_En: If wine intoxicates one, the fermented corn was beaten by the sun also; it is the pain one inflicted on the corn that is being avenged.
Cultural_Context: If one is wronged by the person one has wronged, one has no ground for complaint.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí yó ṣe èmi, bí yó ṣe ìwọ, kì í jẹ́ ká ṣu sóko a-láì-rójú.
Target_Text_En: It-might-happen-to-me, it-might-happen to-you stops one from defecating on the farm of the person who has no time to tend it.
Cultural_Context: One does not take advantage of the weak, for one does not know what might happen to one in the future.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Bùn mi mbùn ọ’’ lọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ńké. ‘‘
Target_Text_En: Give to me and I will give to you’’ is the cry of the toad.
Cultural_Context: Reciprocity is best in human relations.

Source_Text_Yo: Búni-búni, a-bèébú-wọ̀ntì-wọ̀ntì.
Target_Text_En: The person who insults others: a-person whose-nature-deserves-many-insults. D
Cultural_Context: The person with many flaws is typically the most ready to insult others.

Source_Text_Yo: Dídùn ló dùn tí à mọrẹ́jú kọ; tilé oge-é to oge-é jẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is because a relationship is pleasant that one eats corn loaf with one’s friend; what each dandy has at home is enough food for him. E
Cultural_Context: If a friendship sours, each friend will survive without the other. Compare 2103.

Target_Text_En: The person born of the same parents with one might betray one, let alone one’s friends.
Cultural_Context: Trust no one, neither relatives nor friends.

Target_Text_En: The person whose snuff one shares should be happy; all one gets from it is stained teeth.
Cultural_Context: He whose favor one accepts should know that even the acceptance of the favor has its burdens.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni à ḿbárìn là ńfìwà jọ.
Target_Text_En: It is the person whose company one keeps that one emulates.
Cultural_Context: One should match one’s comportment to one’s company.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni bí akàn ní ńhe akàn.

Target_Text_En: One returns home with the person one went out with; the dog departs with the person it came with.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a bá sùn tì là ńjarunpá lù.

Cultural_Context: One should confine one’s affairs to people with whom one keeps company.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ajá bá wá sóde lajá ḿbá relé.
Target_Text_En: Whoever the dog came out with is the per son the dog returns home with.
Cultural_Context: One should remain faithful to one’s companions. This is a variant of 3391.

Source_Text_Yo: Èran ní ńmúni jẹ ìdin; ọ̀rẹ́ ẹni ní ńmúni ru ẹrù ọ̀tá ẹni.
Target_Text_En: It is meat that makes one eat maggots; it is one’s friend that makes one carry an enemy’s load.
Cultural_Context: To please those one likes and re spects, one often has to do things one finds distasteful.

Target_Text_En: Asingle slave causes one to insult two hundred slaves.
Cultural_Context: The misbehavior of one member of a group brings dishonor to all members of the group.

Cultural_Context: A statement that someone is all but impossible to see or find.

Target_Text_En: The tree one would lean on has thorns; the person one would confide in is spreading evil stories about one.
Cultural_Context: There is no one to trust but oneself.

Cultural_Context: One should seek a worthy enough person to rely on.

Target_Text_En: The king’s mother is worthy of the designation ‘‘mother of mysteries’’; the chief’s mother is worthy of the appellation ‘‘mother of witches’’; Olúṣ ye [He who makes merry] can also be named Olúfàya [He who tears things apart].

Target_Text_En: My friend engaged in some deviousness, and I responded with my own deviousness; my friend told me to help myself to the arm of a snake on his rafters, and I asked him to help himself to the thigh of a fish on my shelf. P

Source_Text_Yo: Omi àjèjì tó wọ̀lú, píparẹ́ ní ńparẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Whatever strange water enters a town in evitably disappears. S
Cultural_Context: A newcomer to a community must adapt to its ways or face disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Sún mọ́hùn-ún, a féẹ́ ṣorò ilé-e wa, kì í jẹ́ kálejò di onílé.
Target_Text_En: ‘Move aside; we are about to perform some secret rites of our lineage’’ keeps a sojourner from becoming a member of the house hold.
Cultural_Context: Exclusion from intimate affairs will remind the visitor that he or she does not belong.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í bá baba ta ifọ̀n tán ká tún ba ọmọ ta eṣinṣin kúrò.
Target_Text_En: One does not lance an abscess for a father and then help the son chase flies away [from open wounds].
Cultural_Context: One should not be expected to be a benefactor to one generation and to the next one also.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dá ọmọ òkú lóró; a kì í ṣe ìkà fún ọmọ òrukàn.
Target_Text_En: One does not misuse an orphan; one does not act cruelly to one’s blood brother.
Cultural_Context: One should be considerate of those in need and also of one’s relatives.

Source_Text_Yo: Afúnijẹ kì í fúni tà.
Target_Text_En: The person who will give one food to eat will not give one food to sell.
Cultural_Context: There is a limit to charity.

Source_Text_Yo: Àì-dúpẹ́-oorè-ànà mú ooré súnií ṣe.
Target_Text_En: Failure-to-show-gratitude-for-yesterday’s favor dissuades benefactors from extending favors.
Cultural_Context: If one shows no gratitude for previous kindnesses, one stops receiving favors.

Source_Text_Yo: Ara ò ni ìwọ̀fà bí onígbọ̀wọ́; a-bánikówó lara ńni.
Target_Text_En: The pawn is never as troubled as his guaran tor; it is the person who stands for another who is apprehensive.
Cultural_Context: The guarantor has more reason to worry than the debtor.

Source_Text_Yo: Àríṣe làríkà; àríkà baba ìrègún.
Target_Text_En: What-one-is-able-to-do is what-one-has-to list; what-one-has-to-list gives one ground for recrimination.
Cultural_Context: If one does another a favor, one has some ground to reproach the recipient if he deserves it.

Source_Text_Yo: À-wín-ì-san ò rí owó wín.
Target_Text_En: The-borrower-who-does-not-repay finds no money to borrow.
Cultural_Context: He who defaults on a loan forfeits his opportunities for other loans.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí aṣiwèrè-é bá se àsè, ọlọgbọn a jẹ ẹ́.
Target_Text_En: If an imbecile prepares a feast, the wise per son will eat it. 342 relationships E
Cultural_Context: The fool is there for the wise to take advantage of.

Source_Text_Yo: Èkúté ilé ní tẹni tó pa òun ò dun òun bí ẹni tó gbé òun ṣánlẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The house mouse says he is not as hurt by the person who killed him as by the per son who dashed him on the floor. four Human Nature
Cultural_Context: I may forgive the person who vanquished me but not the person who took advantage of me afterward.

Source_Text_Yo: À báà ṣẹbọ; à báà ṣoògùn; bí a ti pé a ó rìí láyé là ńrí.
Target_Text_En: Even though one makes sacrifices, and even though one procures charms, however one is covenanted to turn out on earth is how one will turn out.
Cultural_Context: Neither sacrifices nor charms will alter a person’s destiny.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í pé kí ọmọdé má fẹ ehín gan-gan ran bó bá tù ú; ètè ni kò rí fi bò ó.
Target_Text_En: One does not order a child not to expose his buckteeth if doing so soothes him; what he lacks are enough lips to cover them.
Cultural_Context: Do not force people to act against their nature.

Source_Text_Yo: Òwu is an ancient gbá
Target_Text_En: Yoruba town. lacks are enough lips to cover them.
Cultural_Context: Do not force people to act against their nature.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í rí ọmọ ọba ká má rìí àmì ọba lára ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One never sees a prince or princess without seeing his or her mark of royalty.
Cultural_Context: People show their worth and breeding by their comportment. Also, a person from an illus trious lineage should not be seen going about in rags or in bad company.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í yin ará Ìjẹ́mù pé ó mọ asẹ́-ẹ́ hún; a ní ‘Àmònímàná alẹ́ àná ni mo fi pètè ìdí ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not praise an Ìj m person as an expert at weaving sieves, for then he will boast, ‘‘Only last night did I start on it!’’

Source_Text_Yo: "A ò mọ eyí tí Ọlọ́run ó ṣe" ó jẹ bínú kú.
Target_Text_En: We know not what God will do’’ stops one from committing suicide.
Cultural_Context: As long as one lives, one may hope.

Source_Text_Yo: A sé ẹtu, a ò sé ẹtu, ọparún gbá a nídìí; ọ̀ràn ẹtu ni bí?
Target_Text_En: We shot and missed the antelope; we shot and did not miss the antelope, and the bam boo hits its rear; is the antelope at fault?
Cultural_Context: One cannot always determine one’s own fate.

Source_Text_Yo: A sọ ọmọ ní Ṣódé, ó lọ síbi ó dé; a sọ ọmọ ní Ṣóbọ̀, ó lọ sájò ó bọ; a wá sọ ọmọ ní Ṣórìnlọ, ó lọ sájò kò dé mọ́, à ńsọ̀ Ta ni kò mọ̀ pé ilé lọmọ-ọ́ ti mú orúkọ ànù lọ?
Target_Text_En: A child named Ṣódé goes on a journey and returns; a child named Ṣób travels afar and returns; then a child named Ṣórìnlọ travels away and does not return, and people wonder why. Who does not know that the child left home with a name that assures his loss?
Cultural_Context: An expression of the belief that people act according to their names. Give a dog a bad name

Source_Text_Yo: Ààfáà-á sọ̀rọ̀ òjò-ó kù; ó ní Ọlọ́runún jẹ́rìí òun.
Target_Text_En: The Muslim priest makes a statement, and thunder rumbles; he says God is bearing him witness
Cultural_Context: The opportunist will turn everything to his or her advantage.

Source_Text_Yo: A ṣe àlapà lọ́ṣọ̀ọ́ kò yẹ ẹ́; a ṣe ohun gbogbo fúngi, o yẹ igi.
Target_Text_En: We decorate a bare, freestanding wall; the result is not pleasing, but whatever decoration a tree receives becomes it.
Cultural_Context: Efforts at improvement are wasted on some people

Source_Text_Yo: Àbíjọ là ḿmọ ìtan.
Target_Text_En: It is through resemblance that one knows those who are related.
Cultural_Context: People show their affinity by their similar behavior or appear ance.

Source_Text_Yo: Àdàbà ò wá oúnjẹ sẹ́nu òrofó; oníkálukú ní ńwá oúnjẹ sẹ́nu ara-a rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The dove does not put food into the mouth of the fruit pigeon; each person finds food for his or her own mouth.
Cultural_Context: Each person is responsible for his or her own welfare.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbìgbò ló mórí ìyà wáyé; orí tó máa gbeni ò dẹ́rù pani.
Target_Text_En: It is àgbìgbò that chose an evil destiny for itself; the head that will be one’s succor will not weigh one down.
Cultural_Context: A thing that will be one’s salvation will not also torment one.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìdé ikú là ńso ààjà m rùn; bíkú bá dé a já ààjà síl a gbé aláàjà lọ.
Target_Text_En: It is when death has not come calling that one ties charms around one’s neck; when death comes calling, it rips the charm away and carries its wearer off.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjíbọ̀wábá là ḿbá ilà àtólẹwọ́; a ò mọ ẹni tó kọ ; àjíbọ̀wábá lowó àdásan; a ò mọ ẹni tó jẹ ẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The lines of the palm are things that pre exist the owner’s awareness; no one knows who made them; a debt the whole commu nity must contribute to repay is an ageless debt; no one knows who incurred it.
Cultural_Context: Cer tain things defy human knowledge, and the sins of fathers are sometimes visited on their offspring generations later. Compare 3503.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkèré pèsè ìyẹ́; ìyá olódò ni ò gbà fún un.
Target_Text_En: The frog tried for wings; it was the river mother that refused her consent.
Cultural_Context: But for the forces of Nature, frogs would fly.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkọ́dá oró ò dàbí àdágbẹ̀hìn.
Target_Text_En: The first injury is nothing like the last.
Cultural_Context: The injury one inflicts is nothing compared to the injury one will receive in retaliation.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkúnlẹ̀yàn làdáyébá; a kúnlẹ̀ a yan ìpín; a dáyé tán ojú ńroni
Target_Text_En: What-was-chosen-on-the-knees is what is-encountered-on-earth; one kneels and chooses a destiny, but on reaching earth one is disconsolate.
Cultural_Context: A person’s fortunes on earth result from the person’s choices at his or her creation; however much one might la ment one’s fortunes on earth, they are one’s choice and responsibility. Compare 3481.

Source_Text_Yo: Àlùmọ́nì: ó ní ẹni tí òún bá wà lọ́wọ́-ọ rẹ̀ ló ni òun.
Target_Text_En: Prosperity: it says that the person in whose possession it is found is its owner.
Cultural_Context: Good fortune is no respecter of persons; it stays with whoever gets his or her hands on it.

Source_Text_Yo: Àníyàn ladìẹ́ fi imú ṣe; adìẹ kì í fọnkun.
Target_Text_En: A chicken’s nose is merely obligatory; a chicken does not blow its nose.
Cultural_Context: Certain things one endures as a matter of obligation; one can easily do without them.

Source_Text_Yo: Àránsí Ọlùrun ò séni; ọkàn ibàjẹ́ ò sélẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Whatever God sends in your direction will not miss you; a vehicle destined for disaster will not escape it.
Cultural_Context: One cannot escape one’s destiny.

Source_Text_Yo: Asùngbè-oyún lọmọ ńjọ.
Target_Text_En: It is the person who sleeps next to a preg nant woman that her child resembles.
Cultural_Context: A person will inevitably manifest the traits of his or her pedigree.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣẹgí-í ṣe wẹ́rẹ́-wẹ́rẹ́ wọ igbó; wàwà lọdẹ ńṣe tọ okùn nà; kò sóhun tórí ò lè fini ṣe; orí ẹni ní ḿmú ni jọba.
Target_Text_En: The wood gatherer walks stealthily into the bush; the hunter stalks briskly through the bush path; there is nothing one’s head cannot make one do; it is one’s head that makes one a king.
Cultural_Context: One’s destiny may lead one astray, and one’s destiny may bring one good fortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣọ pupa kì í bá òkú rọ̀run.
Target_Text_En: Purple cloth never accompanies the dead to heaven.
Cultural_Context: One individual has no part in another individual’s fate.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtẹ́wọ́ la bá ilà; a ó mọ eni tó kọ ọ́.
Target_Text_En: The lines of the palm were always there; no one knows who drew them.
Cultural_Context: One’s des tiny is hidden from one.

Source_Text_Yo: Àti kékeré làràmàjà-á ti ńlalé kọ́.
Target_Text_En: It is from its youth that the crab learns to build its house.
Cultural_Context: The nature of the adult is apparent in the child.

Source_Text_Yo: Àyànmọ́ ò gbóògùn.
Target_Text_En: Destiny does not respond to medicine.
Cultural_Context: No medicine can cure fate.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayésanmí ò se gbẹ̀du; èèyàn lásán ò ní làárì; ọba ni làárì ẹni.
Target_Text_En: Being prosperous does not entitle one to gb du drums; an ordinary person has no regality; it is in a king that regality resides.
Cultural_Context: Certain qualities are congenital, not to be acquired in life.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayọ̀ ò rúbọ.
Target_Text_En: Happiness offers no sacrifices. B
Cultural_Context: When one is happy and contented, one has no need of sacrifice.

Source_Text_Yo: Bániwí kì í báni débẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The counselor does not share the conse quences [of one’s choices] with one.
Cultural_Context: The adviser has no responsibility; only the doer does.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá bẹ oṣó oṣó á gbọ́; bí a bá bẹ àjẹ́  àjẹ́ à gbọ́ ṣùgbọ́n kí-ni-ngó-jẹ kì í gbọ́
Target_Text_En: If one pleads with a wizard, the wizard should be appeased; if one pleads with a witch, the witch should be appeased; but what-will-I-eat is never appeased.
Cultural_Context: One does not assuage hunger with pleas.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá ńfí èèpò ẹ̀pà sù ọtí, ènì máa yó á yó.
Target_Text_En: [Even] were one to sell wine by the peanut shell measure, those who will be intoxicated will be intoxicated. 348 human nature
Cultural_Context: Even in the midst of dearth, those who are destined to prosper will prosper.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá ńgúnyán nínú ewé, tí à ńsebẹ̀ nínú èèpo ẹ̀pà, ẹní máa yó á yó.
Target_Text_En: Even though one makes pounded yams in a leaf and cooks stew in a peanut shell, who will be full will be full.
Cultural_Context: Even in the midst of dearth, those destined to prosper will prosper.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí adìẹ́ bá ṣe ogún, tó ṣe ọgbọ̀n, àgò ni yó dè é.
Target_Text_En: Whether chickens number twenty or thirty, they will yield to being covered by the coop.
Cultural_Context: Certain fates cannot be averted by numbers alone.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí alẹ́ ẹni yó ti rí, òwúrọ̀ ẹni ni yó fi hàn.
Target_Text_En: How a person’s night will be is revealed by the person’s morning.
Cultural_Context: A person’s nature reveals itself from youth.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ológbòó bá pámi pámi, yó wọ̀ ọ́
Target_Text_En: A cat may skirt the water for a long time, but in the end it will enter the water.
Cultural_Context: An inevitability may be delayed but will not be avoided.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí Ọlọ́run ńṣe rere, à ní Ó ńṣe ibi.
Target_Text_En: When God is doing good, someone says he is doing evil.
Cultural_Context: Those who do not under stand God’s grand design fault some of his actions.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí Ọlọ́run ò pani, ẹnìkan ò lè pani.
Target_Text_En: If God does not kill one, nobody can kill one. (Only God can order people’s fates.
Cultural_Context: Only God can order people’s fates. A variant is Bí Ọl run ò pani ọba ò lè pani:

Source_Text_Yo: Eṣú á jẹ, eṣú á mu, eṣú á lọ; níbo ni alátampoko ó wọ̀?
Target_Text_En: The locusts will eat, the locusts will drink, and the locusts will depart; where will the grasshopper hide?
Cultural_Context: After the despoiler has done his or her damage, will the heirs not reap the consequences?

Source_Text_Yo: Ewúrò tó jẹ ṣílè kan pèe eèrí jẹ àdùbáǹsì ọjọ mẹ́ta.
Target_Text_En: The goat that eats a shilling along with corn bran has eaten for three days in advance. Ẹ
Cultural_Context: Whoever squanders valuable resources will pay with privation.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀dá ńlùlù ìbàjẹ; Ọlúrun ni ó jẹ kó dún.
Target_Text_En: Humans beat the drum of disgrace, but God prevents it from making a sound.
Cultural_Context: Others seek one’s disgrace, but God has foiled their plan.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀hìn-in kete lòfò ńṣe.
Target_Text_En: It is the back of the calabash that loses out on all good things.
Cultural_Context: It is some people’s fate always to get the short end of things.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí yó bájẹ́ ti bájẹ́ tàn; ẹni tí yó bálùmọ̀ ló kù.
Target_Text_En: The person whose lot it is to be spoiled is spoiled already; only the person whose lot is to rot remains to be seen.
