Cultural_Context: One wastes one’s effort in attempting to improve an incorrigible person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó ńrínni ò ní ìbáwí; orí ẹni ní ńpé ká rínni.
Target_Text_En: Those who laugh at one have no blame; it is destiny that places one in a position of being laughed at.
Cultural_Context: One should blame not others but one’s own fortune for whatever fate one suffers.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀rẹ̀kẹ́ òlókùnrùn: á wú kó tó bẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The cheeks of the diseased person will swell before they burst.
Cultural_Context: Things will get a great deal more painful before there is any relief.

Source_Text_Yo: Fínná fún mi! Ngò fínná fún ọ! Ní ńdájà sílẹ̀ làrọ.
Target_Text_En: Blow the furnace for me!’’ ‘‘I will not blow the furnace for you!’’ results in a fight at the forge. Gb
Cultural_Context: If responsibilities are not clearly specified among friends, quarrels result.

Source_Text_Yo: "Gba àkàṣù bàm̀bà" lóṣù agà ni "Gba iṣu gbọọrọ" lẹ́ẹ̀jọ̀dún.
Target_Text_En: Have a huge loaf [of corn meal] in May’’ translates to ‘‘Have a long yam’’ after the harvest.
Cultural_Context: A favor one does a person who is in difficulty is not forgotten.

Source_Text_Yo: Gba àkàṣù ní àbọjà ni Gba iṣu bọ̀ọ̀kù’’ ní àmọ́dún
Target_Text_En: Take a loaf [of corn meal]’’ on returning from the market translates to ‘‘Take a huge yam’’ a year hence.
Cultural_Context: A good turn will attract a good turn in return. The preceding two and following two entries are variants.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Gba iṣu fún Ọmọlàńkẹ́’’ nílé ni ‘‘Gba iyọ̀ fún Òṣoko’’ lóko.
Target_Text_En: ‘‘Take this yam for Ọmọlàńkẹ́'' at home translates to ‘‘Take this salt for Òṣoko’’ on the farm.
Cultural_Context: A favor one does when one has the advantage will be rewarded when one is in need. The preceding three entries and the following entry are variants.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbà mí lójò kí ngbà ọ lẹ́ẹ̀run.
Target_Text_En: Aid me in times of rain so I can aid you in times of drought. I
Cultural_Context: A person who extends aid to those in difficulty will receive aid from them when he or she is in difficulty.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi tí a ti jẹun ogójì, ka sọ̀rọ̀ okòó.
Target_Text_En: Where one eats food worth 40 cowries, one should make a speech worth 20 cowries.
Cultural_Context: One should make some effort to earn one’s keep.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi tí àgbà-á bá pin sí lọmọdé ti ḿbá a.
Target_Text_En: Wherever age comes to rest, there youth will catch up with it.
Cultural_Context: Sooner or later the youth of today will put on the mantle of the elders and become just like them.

Source_Text_Yo: Igí gbẹ níjù ó dègbé.
Target_Text_En: The tree dries up in the forest and it be comes worthless.
Cultural_Context: When one has lost the qualities that make one desirable, one is done for.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkà kì í fi oníkà sílẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Wickedness never leaves the wicked.
Cultural_Context: The wicked person can never change his or her nature.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé ni aláṣọ- jókòó sí tí òkùkù-ú wọlé tọ̀ọ́.
Target_Text_En: The weaver was at home when the woof entered to seek him or her out.
Cultural_Context: The good destined to come one’s way will find one even if one does not venture out of the house.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé tó bá máa wó kì í gbọ́ ti igi ayẹ̀gẹ̀rẹ̀; ohun tó bá máa ṣeni kì í ní àkókò kan
Target_Text_En: A house that is destined to collapse will not be saved by slipping posts; disaster that is destined to befall one is not daunted by what season it is.
Cultural_Context: No one can deflect fate.

Source_Text_Yo: Iná ilé lẹranko ńyá gbẹ̀hìn, àfi èyí tó bá ringbó kú.
Target_Text_En: It is the household fire that warms [or roasts] an animal in the end, except for those that die wandering in the bush.
Cultural_Context: The person who besmirches the good name of his or her community when he or she is abroad must return home eventually to give an account.

Source_Text_Yo: Inú ẹ-ẹ́ dára ò ńyọ̀; orí ẹ-ẹ́ dára ná?
Target_Text_En: Because you harbor good will toward others, you are happy; has good fortune come your way?
Cultural_Context: One is not necessarily fortu nate simply because one harbors good will toward others.

Source_Text_Yo: Inú rere ò jọ orí rere.
Target_Text_En: Good nature is not the same as good fortune.
Cultural_Context: The good person is not necessarily safe from misfor tune.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìpín ògo kì í tẹ́; baarú lórí rere nínú ẹṣin
Target_Text_En: A person destined for glory will not suffer disgrace; an exceptionally powerful horse is fortunate among horses.
Cultural_Context: A person destined to shine will not fail to do so

Source_Text_Yo: Ìpín ọ̀jẹun kì í jẹ́ kíná kú.
Target_Text_En: The destiny of the person who will eat will keep the fire from going out.
Cultural_Context: Providence will take care of one’s needs.

Source_Text_Yo: Ire ẹni kì í kọjá ẹni.
Target_Text_En: The good fortune destined for one will not pass one by.
Cultural_Context: One’s destined good fortune will not be deflected.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìrìn Àṣàkẹ́ ò papọ̀ mọ́ ti Ọwọ́olú; Àṣàkẹ́ ńlọ ilé ọkọ, Ọwọ́olú ńre ọ̀run
Target_Text_En: Àṣàkẹ́’s path is not the same as Ọw olú’s path; Àṣàk is bound for her spouse’s home, whereas Ọwọ́olú is bound for heaven.
Cultural_Context: Different people have different destinies.

Source_Text_Yo: Irú tó bà lé ẹni nípàkọ́ ò ní òun ò ní gbéni mì; Ọlùrun ọba ni ó jẹkí ipá ẹ̀ ká a.
Target_Text_En: God Almighty denied it the power to do so.
Cultural_Context: One’s enemies are unrelenting in their effort to do harm; only God has thwarted them.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣe tí ẹ̀fúùfù-lẹ̀lẹ̀ ńṣe ọ̀run, bí kò wó, bí kò ya, Ọlùrun ọba ni kò jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The way the wind belabors the sky, that the sky does not collapse or tear into pieces is thanks to God Almighty.
Cultural_Context: Only the gods have kept one from falling into the hands of one’s enemies.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣe mojú; ìyà máwọ̀; èbì pa àlejò, ójú tó ilé, ójú à tóko.
Target_Text_En: Poverty cares not who owns which eyes; suffering does not pay attention to skin complexion; when hunger grips the stranger, the eyes that have seen the house will see the farm. On fate 351
Cultural_Context: Hard times do not spare anyone; every person must gird himself or herself.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìwò tí à ńwo àparò bíi ká fi dálá, orí ẹyẹ ni ò pẹyẹ.
Target_Text_En: The way one eyes a partridge betrays one’s wish to cook it in okro stew; it is the bird’s head [or providence] that kept death from the bird.
Cultural_Context: One’s enemies would like to see one dead, but one’s destiny will not let them have their way.

Source_Text_Yo: Ká fi ẹfun t ile aje, ká fosùn tọ́lé ìlẹ̀kẹ̀; àkọ́dá orí kì í gbé ìsàlẹ̀ ọjà.
Target_Text_En: Let us whitewash the house of riches and paint that of beads with camwood; the head created at the beginning of time does not languish at the marketplace.
Cultural_Context: Whoever is destined to prosper will not fail to do so.

Source_Text_Yo: Kì í ṣe ẹjọ́ eléhín gan-gan-ran; òrìṣà ló dá a tí kò fi awọ bò ó.
Target_Text_En: The blame does not belong to the per son with protruding teeth; it was the god who created him or her that failed to cover them with enough skin.
Cultural_Context: One should not be faulted for things over which one has no control.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí alábàárò tó ju orí ẹni.
Target_Text_En: There is no commiserator that surpasses
Cultural_Context: The best support one has is one’s own head, one’s protective spirit

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ìgbà tí ọmọ awo ò níí ṣawo.
Target_Text_En: There is no escaping the time when a per son born into a cult must become initiated into its mysteries.
Cultural_Context: One cannot avoid one’s ordained calling.

Source_Text_Yo: Kọṣẹ́-kọṣẹ́ kan kì í kọ iṣẹ́ Ọlọ́run.
Target_Text_En: No recalcitrant person ever refuses God’s errand. L
Cultural_Context: No one can refuse to do God’s bidding.

Source_Text_Yo: Lílọ ní ńkẹ́hin-in bọ̀í.
Target_Text_En: Departure is the inevitable fate of the house boy. M
Cultural_Context: However much a servant may be made to feel like family, he should know that his eventual separation is inevitable.

Source_Text_Yo: Màkàn-màkàn loyè ńkàn.
Target_Text_En: Chieftaincy titles go around in turns.
Cultural_Context: One’s good fortune will come one’s way in due time.

Source_Text_Yo: Ní inú ilẹ̀kú lOrò ńjẹ
Target_Text_En: Where the dead are buried, there Orò feeds.
Cultural_Context: Some people’s misfortune is other people’s good fortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Níní owó kàdárà ni; àìní owó kàdárà ni.
Target_Text_En: Being blessed with money is a matter of des tiny; not having money is also a matter of destiny. O
Cultural_Context: One’s earthly fortune is a matter of destiny beyond one’s control.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó wu àgùàlà kó mọ́lẹ̀ bí òṣùpá, Ọlọrun ọba ni ó jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The planet Venus would like to be as bright as the moon, but God the King would not permit it to be.
Cultural_Context: Everyone wishes to be as great as the greatest person, but each indi vidual’s destiny is decisive. The following three entries are variants.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó wu aṣiwèrè kó ru igbá-a rę dọ́jà, ará ilé ẹ̀ ni ó jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The mad person would wish to carry her calabash as far as the market, except that the members of her household would not let her.
Cultural_Context: Communal constraints are to be thanked for curbing people’s propensity to indulge in licentious behavior. The pre ceding entry and the following two are variants.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó wu ewúrẹ́ kó bímọ ẹ̀ ní òbúkọ, Ọlùrun ọba ni ò fun; ó wu àgùntàn bọ̀lọ̀jọ̀ kó bímọ lágbò, Ọlọ́run ọba ni ò fún un; ó wu adìẹ òkòkó kó bímọ ẹ̀ lákùkọ, Ọlọ́run ọba ni ò fún un.
Target_Text_En: The goat would wish that its kid was a hegoat, only God the King did not consent; the robust sheep would wish its lamb was a ram, only God the King would not agree; the big hen would wish its chick was a cock, only God the King would not grant her wish.
Cultural_Context: Everybody wishes for great things, but God does not grant all wishes.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó wu ẹtu kó gbé ogún ọdún nígbó, ṣùgbọ́n ó wu onípàkúté kó dọ́jà lọ́la.
Target_Text_En: The antelope would like to live for twenty years in the bush, but the setter of snares would like it to reach the market on the morrow.
Cultural_Context: Different people’s interests often conflict. The preceding three entries are variants.

Source_Text_Yo: Òfò ò jẹ́ kí ọlórò ó pọ.
Target_Text_En: Gainless ventures limit the ranks of the rich.
Cultural_Context: Everybody craves success, but not all are favored by fortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkèté ní tòun ló bá òun tí oun-ún fẹ̀hìn tiná.
Target_Text_En: The giant bush rat says a misfortune befell it and caused it to sit warming itself by the fire.
Cultural_Context: It was a grave disaster that caused one to be found in disgraceful or embarrassing circumstances.

Source_Text_Yo: Olóríburúkú kì í re oko ikàn; bó bá re oko ikàn, ilá ní ńká wálé.
Target_Text_En: An ill-fated person does not go to a locust bean farm; if he should go to a locust-bean farm, he will return home with okra.
Cultural_Context: A per son destined to fail will always find a way to fail.

Source_Text_Yo: Omi lèèyàn; bó bá ṣàn wá a tún ṣàn padà.
Target_Text_En: Humans are streams; they flow forth and flow back.
Cultural_Context: People are not fixed in one loca tion; no one knows where he or she will find himself or herself in the future.

Source_Text_Yo: Omi tí a máa mu kì í ṣàn kọjá ẹni
Target_Text_En: The water one is destined to drink will On fate 353 not flow past.
Cultural_Context: One’s destiny will not pass one by.

Source_Text_Yo: Òmùgòó lè ṣìṣe kó dọgbón; orí yàt sórí.
Target_Text_En: The fool may commit a blunder that comes to seem as wisdom; heads differ from one another.
Cultural_Context: Although some pay dearly for their mistakes, others benefit from mistakes that fortuitously prove fortunate; it is all a matter of chance.

Source_Text_Yo: Òní la rí, kò sẹ́ni tó mọla.
Target_Text_En: Today is all we see; nobody knows tomor row.
Cultural_Context: No one knows what the future will bring.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí inú kì í jẹ́ kí tòde sunwọ̀n.
Target_Text_En: The unseen head prevents the visible head from prospering.
Cultural_Context: A person’s chosen [evil] destiny will always keep him from prosper ing.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí la fi mòran láwo.
Target_Text_En: It is one’s luck that determines the piece of meat one takes from a plate
Cultural_Context: How one fares in life depends on luck.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí ló mọ ibi ẹsẹ̀ ńrè.
Target_Text_En: The head alone knows where the feet will go.
Cultural_Context: One never knows where one’s destiny will lead.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí loníṣe; ẹ̀dá lèrè.
Target_Text_En: The head acts; one’s nature determines one’s reward.
Cultural_Context: People act as their heads direct them; their reward is according to their nature.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí tí kò níí rún àgbàdo sùn ní ńgbéni ko èlérù iṣu kan
Target_Text_En: A head [destiny] that will not chew corn for supper brings a certain bearer of yams one’s way.
Cultural_Context: When matters seem hopeless, a way out will surely materialize for the fortunate person.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí tí yó gbeni kì í pàn lẹ́rù
Target_Text_En: A head that will make one prosper will not prove too heavy for one to carry.
Cultural_Context: Whatever is destined to make one prosper will not cause inconvenience.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí tó máa dádé, nínú agoroodẹ ní ńti í yọ wá; ọrùn tí yó lo èjìgbà ìlẹ̀kẹ̀, nínú agoroodẹ ní ńti-íyọ ọ́ wá; bèbè-ìdí tí yó lo mọ́sàajì, aṣọ ọba tó kóná yanran-yanran, nínú agoroodẹ ní ńti-í yọ ọ́ wá
Target_Text_En: The head that will wear a crown is so des tined from before the birth of the gods; the neck that will be adorned with beads is so destined from before the birth of the gods;[?]the waist that will wear m sàajì, the cloth of kings that is soft and shiny, is so destined from before the birth of the gods.
Cultural_Context: One only lives a course that was predetermined before one’s birth.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí tó máa jẹ ògẹ̀dẹ̀ sùn kì í gbọ́; bí wọ́n bá ńgbéyán bọ̀ wá fun, yó fọ̀ọ́ ni dandan
Target_Text_En: A head destined to eat plantains for supper will not escape that destiny; if pounded yam is being brought, it [the dish] will unfail ingly break.
Cultural_Context: There is no antidote or cure for ill luck.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrìṣà tí Ṣàngó ò bá lè mú, eré ló lè sá.
Target_Text_En: Whatever god Ṣango cannot catch must in deed be fleet of foot.
Cultural_Context: Only extraordinarily good fortune can save people from fate.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrìṣà tó dá ẹnu níbùú mọ ohun tí òun ó fi sí i.
Target_Text_En: The god who made the mouth horizontal knows what [food] he will put in it.
Cultural_Context: The gods have a plan and a reason for whatever they have created.

Source_Text_Yo: Òwú tí ìyá gbọ̀n lọmọ ńran.
Target_Text_En: It is the cotton that the mother fluffs that the daughter spins. Ọ
Cultural_Context: Children take after their parents.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọkàn ẹni làlùfáà ẹni.
Target_Text_En: One’s heart is one’s priest.
Cultural_Context: The quality of one’s heart determines how good one’s fortune will be.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ aráyé ó fẹ́ ká rẹrù ká sọ̀; orí ẹni ní ńsọni.
Target_Text_En: The people of this world never want to see one carry a load and later set it down; only one’s guardian spirit helps one set the load down.
Cultural_Context: People do not offer to help others out of difficulties; only providence does.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pá ò lè pa agogo; abínú ẹni ò lè pa kádàrá dà
Target_Text_En: A stick cannot kill a bell; ill wishers cannot alter a person’s destiny.
Cultural_Context: No amount of ill will by others will change God’s plan for a person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀tá ńlùlù ìbàjẹ́, Ọlòrun ò jẹ́ kó dún.
Target_Text_En: One’s enemy is beating the drum of defa mation, but God won’t let it make a sound. R
Cultural_Context: God has frustrated the schemes of one’s enemies.

Source_Text_Yo: Rìkíṣí ò gbọ́ oògùn; Ọlọ́run ní ḿbáni sẹ̀tẹ̀-ẹ rìkíṣí.
Target_Text_En: Intrigue cannot be combatted with medi cine; only God can help one conquer in trigue. S
Cultural_Context: Only God can help one overcome one’e enemies.

Source_Text_Yo: Sa orí má sa oògùn; oògùn ní ọj ìpọ́njú, orí lọ́jọ́ gbogbo.
Target_Text_En: Trust in your head and not in medicine; medicine is for the day of hardship, but your head is for every day.
Cultural_Context: It is better to trust in one’s genius than in medicinal charms

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣátánì ló mú àtọ̀sí ààfáà wá; ẹlẹ́hàá kì í jáde, ààfáà kì í yànlè
Target_Text_En: Satan is to blame for the imam’s gonorrhea; the wife confined in the harem does not ven ture outdoors, and the imam does not keep an illicit lover. T
Cultural_Context: One has to be most inventive to explain away a problem for which there can be no one else to blame.

Source_Text_Yo: Ta ní ńfẹ́ ká jí? Aráyé ò fẹ́ni fọ́rọ̀, àforí ẹni.
Target_Text_En: Who ever wants one to wake up? People never wish wealth for one, only one’s head does.
Cultural_Context: People seldom wish that others pros per.

Source_Text_Yo: Tẹní máa sunwọ̀n kì í gbọ́.
Target_Text_En: No one can block the path of good fortune for someone destined to prosper. 356 human nature W
Cultural_Context: No one can stop another’s destiny.

Source_Text_Yo: Wíwò téwúrẹ́ alápatà bíi kó kú; orí ẹni ni ó pàní.
Target_Text_En: The look the goat gives the butcher wishes death for the latter; only one’s head does not deliver one to death.
Cultural_Context: Those adversely affected by year lawful duties may hate you, but your head will protect you from their machinations. Compare the following entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Wíwò tí à ńwàparò, bíi ká fi dálá, orí ẹyẹ ni ò pẹyẹ.
Target_Text_En: The way one eyes a partridge betrays a desire to cook it in okro stew; only the bird’s head says no to death.
Cultural_Context: One’s enemies look at one with death in their eyes, but one’s des tiny says no to their desires.

Source_Text_Yo: Wọ́n ní ọ̀nà-á wà níbìkan, o ò bèèrè lọ́wọ́ orí.
Target_Text_En: They say a path is open somewhere, and you did not ask your head [guiding spirit]. On human vulnerability and limitations A
Cultural_Context: Always seek the guidance of your guiding power.

Source_Text_Yo: A fẹ́ ẹ nílé, a fẹ́ ẹ lóko; bọ́mọ́ bá ti lóyún, kò parí ná?
Target_Text_En: She is courted at home; she is courted on the farm; once the girl becomes pregnant, will there not be an end to courting?
Cultural_Context: However attractive and desirable a woman may be, once she becomes pregnant, she no longer attracts suitors.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbé àárín ojì èèyàn ká má ṣì wí.
Target_Text_En: One cannot live amid forty people and never misspeak.
Cultural_Context: It is impossible to live in a group and never cause offense.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mọ ilẹ̀ ọjà-á gbá.
Target_Text_En: One never knows how to sweep a market.
Cultural_Context: If there is a multitude to please, one will always leave some people disgruntled.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mọ̀ọ́ gún mòọ́ tẹ̀ kíyán ewùrà má lẹ̀ẹ́mọ
Target_Text_En: One is never so good at pounding and smoothing that the pounded yams one makes with ewùrà yams [also water yams] will not be lumpy.
Cultural_Context: Certain tasks defeat even the experts.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mọ̀ọ́ w ká káyéjá; bọ̀rọ̀kìnní kan ò wà á já; báa ṣoore títí á kù síbìkan.
Target_Text_En: One is never so expert a swimmer that one swims the whole world; no great man ever swam it; no matter how much good one does there will be some omission.
Cultural_Context: No one can be all-wise in worldly matters.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í nàró ká ọdún.
Target_Text_En: One cannot stand upright year-round.
Cultural_Context: Everybody falls sometime.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í wáyé ká máà lárùn kan lára; ìjà-ìgboro làrùn Ìbàdàn.
Target_Text_En: One does not come into this world and not have a disease; street fighting is the disease of Ibadan people.
Cultural_Context: Ibadan people cannot help street fighting; other people have other peculiar second natures.

Source_Text_Yo: A lè gbé omi léná de elégbò, ṣùgbọ́n a ò lè wẹ ẹsẹ̀ dè é.
Target_Text_En: One may heat water in preparation for the person with an ulcer, but one cannot clean the ulcer until he or she arrives.
Cultural_Context: There is a limit to the help one can render another per son, especially a person who will not make an effort on his or her own behalf.

Source_Text_Yo: A ní kó múwá, ó ní kò sí; ahun ni lójú alágbe.
Target_Text_En: He is asked for alms and says he has nothing to give; to the beggar he appears as a miser.
Cultural_Context: People are often unmindful of the fact that other people have their own problems.

Source_Text_Yo: À ńkọ́lé ikin, à ńyọ̀dẹ̀dẹ̀ imọ̀, hòrò ni ilé àgbékẹ́hin.
Target_Text_En: Though we build houses of thatch, though we make corridors of palm leaves, it is to a grave that we will retire in the end.
Cultural_Context: What ever a person’s riches, in the end he or she winds up in a grave.

Source_Text_Yo: A pé ẹlẹ́fọọ́-ọ ni, Tààtàn kọ́.
Target_Text_En: We hail a spinach seller, and she protests that her spinach is not from the dung heap. 358 human nature
Cultural_Context: The evildoer’s conscience will betray him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: A rìn fàà lójú agbàgàn; a yan kàṣà lójú abúni; abúni ò ní okòó nílé.
Target_Text_En: One strolls nonchalantly before a detrac tor; one struts proudly before a slanderer; the slanderer has not 20 cowries at home.
Cultural_Context: One need not pay a worthless detractor any mind.

Source_Text_Yo: A ṣe ohun gbogbo tán; ti ẹlenu ló kù.
Target_Text_En: We have done all we can do; what detractors will say is another matter.
Cultural_Context: Even after doing one’s best, one cannot control what critics will say.

Source_Text_Yo: Ààlà-á tó, ìmàle ò dúró de ara-a wọn.
Target_Text_En: The time for ablutions arrives; Muslims do not wait for one another.
Cultural_Context: Each person bears his or her own responsibility.

Source_Text_Yo: Àáyá ṣẹ́jú, ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀-ẹ́ kí ọwò bọ̀ ọ́.
Target_Text_En: The colobus monkey blinks, and its child pokes its fingers into the monkey’s eyes.
Cultural_Context: Children are a handful for their parents, who cannot always be quick enough to stop their mischief.

Source_Text_Yo: Abarapá ti gbogbo èèyàn; òkùnrùn tẹnìkan ṣoṣo.
Target_Text_En: Sprightliness is everybody’s; indisposition is one person’s alone.
Cultural_Context: People will fraternize with a lively person; nobody fraternizes with a sickly person.

Source_Text_Yo: Àbàtá ta kété bí ẹnipé kò bá odò tan.
Target_Text_En: The marsh stands apart as though it is not related to the river.
Cultural_Context: It is futile to deny re sponsibility for, or knowledge of, an event when the evidence of the truth is obvious and incontrovertible. Some people some times find it expedient to deny any relation ship with relatives.

Source_Text_Yo: Abẹ́rẹ́ jádìí, àkísà ńyọ̀ ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀; ó rò pé òyìnbó ò gún mọ́.
Target_Text_En: The needle’s eye breaks, and the cloth re joices; it thinks the white man has ceased making needles.
Cultural_Context: Do not rejoice at your formidable adversary’s temporary discomfi ture.

Source_Text_Yo: Àbíkú sọ olóògùn dèkè.
Target_Text_En: No amount of effort to the contrary will prevent what is ordained.
Cultural_Context: One who cries ‘‘wolf ’’ too many times will attract no one in times of real trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: Abínúẹni kò sẹ́ ọ̀ràn deni.
Target_Text_En: He who wants no good for one does not plead one’s innocence in one’s absence.
Cultural_Context: Expect no kindness from an enemy.

Source_Text_Yo: Àbọ̀ là ńya ilé ọ̀rẹ́ tì kò wuni.
Target_Text_En: It is on one’s way back home from a trip that one stops at the home of a friend one does not like.
Cultural_Context: One will always find ways to temporize on an unpalatable obliga tion.

Source_Text_Yo: A bọ eégún ò réégún; abọ̀rìṣà ò rórìṣà; ìmàlé fòríbálẹ̀ kò rÓlọ́run.
Target_Text_En: Muslim bows to the ground [at prayer] but does not see the High God.
Cultural_Context: One often does not see the person one serves.

Source_Text_Yo: A-bojú-gòdògbà kì í ríran l nà méjì
Target_Text_En: A person with huge eyes does not see in two directions at once.
Cultural_Context: The size of the eyes offers no special advantage.

Source_Text_Yo: Abuké ló ru ẹrù òrìṣà má s
Target_Text_En: A humpback carries a god-imposed bur den that cannot be laid down.
Cultural_Context: Congenital conditions cannot be easily vacated.

Source_Text_Yo: Abuké sùnkákà bí ẹní ta síná.
Target_Text_En: The humpback sleeps all spread out like one bloated in a fire.
Cultural_Context: Deformity prevents graceful sleeping postures.

Source_Text_Yo: A-búni-l lẹ ò mọ ohun tí ńṣeni.
Target_Text_En: The person who calls one a lazy person does not know what one’s problem is.
Cultural_Context: No one knows others’ private woes.

Source_Text_Yo: Àdábá nìjà; ẹni tí ìjà ò bá ní ńpera-a rẹ̀ lọ́kùnrin.
Target_Text_En: Fights are uninvited plagues; it is he who is not visited by a fight that boasts about his manhood.
Cultural_Context: Manliness is sometimes a matter of good fortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Àdàbà ò náání à ńkùngbẹ́; iná jó, ẹyẹ́ fò lọ.
Target_Text_En: The dove is not bothered that one sets fire to the brush; the fire rages, and the bird flies away.
Cultural_Context: One cannot be hurt by eventualities to which one is immune.

Source_Text_Yo: Adánilóró ò ṣéé fẹ̀hìntì
Target_Text_En: A person who habitually causes others pain is no one to trust.
Cultural_Context: Know your enemy.

Source_Text_Yo: Adìẹ́ bà lókùn; ara ò rọ okùn, ara ò rọ adíẹ.
Target_Text_En: The chicken alighted on a rope; the rope cannot relax, and the chicken cannot relax.
Cultural_Context: One person’s problems are problems also for those close to him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: Adìẹ ńlàágùn; ìhùùhù ni ó jẹ́ ká mọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The chicken sweats, but its down prevents us from knowing.
Cultural_Context: Everybody has his or her problems, although strangers may not guess. Compare 4041.

Source_Text_Yo: Adìẹ òpìpì kì í rápá gun orílé.
Target_Text_En: The flightless chicken never has the wings to fly to the top of the roof.
Cultural_Context: One’s enemies will not have the means to injure one; or, a person will never have the means to thrive.

Source_Text_Yo: Adití woni lẹ́nu sùn-ùn.
Target_Text_En: The deaf person stares fixedly at people’s mouths.
Cultural_Context: One acts according to one’s capa bilities.

Source_Text_Yo: Afẹ́fẹ́ ńgbá eruku lálá; ẹ̀fúùfù ńmi ewé àgbọ́n jìjà-jìà.
Target_Text_En: The wind whips the dust into a storm; the strong breeze whips the coconut leaves to a frenzy.
Cultural_Context: Everyone is beset with problems.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgádá mádìẹ dọ̀lẹ.
Target_Text_En: The grass shelter makes the chicken lazy.
Cultural_Context: Too much ease discourages resourceful ness.

Source_Text_Yo: Agílítí, a-bara-yíyi.
Target_Text_En: Lizard, thick-skinned creature.
Cultural_Context: To each his or her flaws.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgùntàn ò ìtíì kú à ńwì í níná; bóbá wá kú ńkọ́?
Target_Text_En: The sheep is not yet dead, and it is already being massaged with fire to burn the hair off its skin; what will happen then after its death?
Cultural_Context: If people do evil to a person when the person is present, what can one expect them to do when the person is not?

Source_Text_Yo: Àgùntàn ò pa aṣọ èṣí dà.
Target_Text_En: The sheep does not change its clothing from year to year.
Cultural_Context: Old habits die hard.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgùntàn pòpó ṣe ońdè lọ́rùn: oníkálukú a-bi-tiẹ̀-lára.
Target_Text_En: Sacrificial sheep with leather charms around its neck: each person has his or her own problems.
Cultural_Context: To each his or her problems.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà Ìjèṣà ò lè ṣàìjobì
Target_Text_En: An Ìjèṣà elder cannot refrain from chewing kola nuts.
Cultural_Context: Do not begrudge people what they crave.

Source_Text_Yo: Agbádá ya lọ́rún, ó bájẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The grand traditional garment rips around the neck and becomes ruined.
Cultural_Context: An object that loses its utility loses it value.

Source_Text_Yo: A-gbáhéré-yáná ni a-gbénú-oko-yá òòrùn.
Target_Text_En: Person-who-sits-by-the-fire-inside-the hut is one-who-suns-himself-on-the-farm.
Cultural_Context: One’s habits follow one, whether at home or on the farm.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbẹ̀ roko roko, wọn kà ṣàì gbàgbé ewé kan sébè.
Target_Text_En: However thoroughly a farmer might weed his farm, he will not fail to overlook some leaf on a mound.
Cultural_Context: No one can achieve per fection.

Source_Text_Yo: Agbọ́nmi ní ńwólé ẹja; apàjùbà ní ńwólé àparò; òlùgbóńgbó tìǹlà ni wọ́n fi ńṣẹ́gun ògúlùtu.
Target_Text_En: Who drains the stream destroys the home of the fish; who clears the forest for farm ing destroys the home of the partridge; a huge cudgel is the weapon for conquering what is left of a wall.
Cultural_Context: Each situation has its proper medicine, and each person his or her nemesis.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìmọ̀ kì í pa ọmọ.
Target_Text_En: Ignorance does not kill a child.
Cultural_Context: There are worse things in a child than ignorance.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìmọ̀-ọ́jọ́ ni kì í jẹ́ kí àlejò ó jó.
Target_Text_En: It is ignorance about dancing that keeps a stranger from dancing.
Cultural_Context: Ignorance about the customs of a place keeps the outsider from full integration.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìtètèjí inú ọ̀tá ńdùn, a jí tán inú ḿbí wọn.
Target_Text_En: One’s lateness in getting up in the morning makes one’s enemies happy; once one is up and about, they become angry.
Cultural_Context: One’s enemies always rejoice at the prospect of one’s demise.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá ẹgbrún ò gbọ́ orúkọ.
Target_Text_En: A dog bought for 1,000 cowries does not recognize or heed its name
Cultural_Context: One cannot teach a cheap dog anything. One gets what one pays for

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá ní ńlá omi lọbàálọbàá; eṣinṣin ò kún àtẹ ilé; ọmọrí igbá ò fìdí kal
Target_Text_En: It is a dog that licks water with its tongue; flies will not fill a tray for beads; the lid of a calabash cannot sit straight upright.
Cultural_Context: Certain things are characteristic of certain people; each has his or her limitations.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá òyìnbó dára, ó ku àtiṣọdẹ.
Target_Text_En: The white man’s dog is beautiful, but it lacks the ability to hunt.
Cultural_Context: A beautiful thing that has no use is nothing to be desired

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá tó pa ikún lónìí ḿbọ̀ wá pa ọ̀yà lọ́la; ká má fìbínú pajá
Target_Text_En: Adog that kills a squirrel today will kill a cane rat tomorrow; one should, therefore, not kill the dog in anger. (
Cultural_Context: One should not write anybody off because the person has suffered one setback.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjàpá ní bí òún bá jẹ, tí òún mu, tí òún yó, ara òun a yá; ṣùgbọ́n ìgbà tí òún bá rántí irán ìdí òun, òun a bú sẹ́kún pẹ̀rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Tortoise says when it has eaten and drunk to its fill, it becomes cheerful, but when it remembers its coccyx, it breaks into tears.
Cultural_Context: Even in the best of circumstances one is left with some blemish.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjẹ́ lè jẹ okú.
Target_Text_En: A witch cannot eat the dead.
Cultural_Context: A person dies only once and, once dead, is safe from witches and enemies.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajédéjẹ kì í jẹ ọ̀kan mọ
Target_Text_En: A-person-who-sneakily-eats-shrimps does not stop after eating only one.
Cultural_Context: Small trans gressions tend to become a habit.

Source_Text_Yo: Akáyín ò mọ efùrù-ú pè
Target_Text_En: A person with a missing tooth does not know how to pronounce efùrù.
Cultural_Context: One is limited by one’s nature.

Source_Text_Yo: Akọ́kọ́dájọ́ lọ̀tá ẹlẹ́jọ.
Target_Text_En: The first judge is the enemy of the litigant.
Cultural_Context: Few people take criticism kindly.

Source_Text_Yo: A-kọ́ni-ká-bàjẹ́ ò ṣe tiẹ̀ bẹ́ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: He-who-coaches-one-into-ruin does not manage his own affairs the same way.
Cultural_Context: People who will preside over the destruction of others know how to protect themselves.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkùkọ́ kì í pamọ
Target_Text_En: A rooster does not hatch eggs.
Cultural_Context: There is a limit to what one can expect of people; certain things are contrary to nature.

Source_Text_Yo: Alágbẹ̀dẹ́ ò fẹ́ kí ogun tán láyé.
Target_Text_En: The blacksmith [who makes weapons] does not wish for an end of wars on earth.
Cultural_Context: Self interest is paramount.

Source_Text_Yo: Alákàrà kì í fẹ́ kí ẹnìkejì gbé agbada.
Target_Text_En: The seller of bean fritters does not wish that another person acquire a deep-frying pot.
Cultural_Context: No trader wants competition.

Source_Text_Yo: Alákàṣù ó fẹ́ kí ẹni tó rà á yó.
Target_Text_En: The seller of corn-meal loaves does not wish buyers to be full.
Cultural_Context: Self-interest is paramount.

Source_Text_Yo: Àpọ́n tọrọ ọbẹ̀; kò mọ oye à ńkólá.
Target_Text_En: The bachelor begs for stew; he does not know how much okro costs.
Cultural_Context: A person ignorant of a trade does not appreciate its difficulties.

Source_Text_Yo: Àròyé niṣẹ́ ìbakà; kí niṣẹ́ ẹyẹ lóko?
Target_Text_En: Chattering is the burden of the Senegal canary; what is the trait of the birds on the farm?
Cultural_Context: Said of a talkative or idle person.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣá ò kú, ara ńta ẹtù; àwòdì á wo ìgbín kọ̀rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The kite does not die, and the partridge is anxious; the eagle watches the snail from the corner of its eye.
Cultural_Context: If one’s nemesis thrives, one is anxious, especially when one has no means of defense or retaliation.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣọ èṣín ò yẹni, bíi ti aṣọ ẹ̀wọ̀n kọ́.
Target_Text_En: Last year’s clothing is not proper for people, but that does not apply to prison uniforms.
Cultural_Context: Adverse circumstances may force peopl

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣọ tuntun ní ńṣe olúwa-a rẹ̀ tòde-tòde
Target_Text_En: A new dress impels its owner to roam out doors.
Cultural_Context: One is ever eager to show off one’s new acquisitions.

Source_Text_Yo: A-ti-kékeré-ṣẹrú ò mọyì ọmọlúwàbí.
Target_Text_En: One-who-has-been-a-slave-since-childhood does not appreciate being a freeborn.
Cultural_Context: A stranger to freedom does not appreciate it.

Source_Text_Yo: À-tọ̀-ìṣíwọ́ là ḿmòkóbó.
Target_Text_En: Urinating-without-ceasing is what betrays the eunuch.
Cultural_Context: One’s secret flaws have ways of making themselves public.

Source_Text_Yo: Awo Eégún lobìnrín lè ṣe, awo Gẹ̀lẹ̀dẹ́ lobìnrín lè wò; bóbìnrín bá fojú kan Orò, Orò á gbé e
Target_Text_En: Only the mystery of Eégun is accessible to women; it is only the mystery of G l d[?]that women may watch; if a woman catches a glimpse of Orò, Orò will make an end of her.
Cultural_Context: Only certain rites are allowed to certain people; the rest are proscribed.

Source_Text_Yo: A-wọ̀n-bí-ọgbọ́n, aṣòroódà bí àgbà.
Target_Text_En: Scarce-as-wisdom, difficult-to-become as-an-elder.
Cultural_Context: Wisdom is not common; achieving the traits of a sage is not easy.

Source_Text_Yo: Àyè ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ ò sí nídìí adìẹ.
Target_Text_En: There is no room for beads on the waist of a chicken.
Cultural_Context: Not every person can wear finery to good effect.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayé lè pa fìtílà yẹ.
Target_Text_En: The world is capable of snuffing one’s lamp of glory. B
Cultural_Context: People are capable of damaging one’s good reputation.

Source_Text_Yo: Baálé di mẹ́ta, itan adìẹ́ dàròyé.
Target_Text_En: Husbands number three; a chicken’s thigh becomes a bone of contention.
Cultural_Context: Too many claims on meager resources result in dissen sion.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá máa gbàwìn là ńṣe ojú àánú; bí a bá yó tán à di ọmọ ọba.
Target_Text_En: When one wants to make a purchase on credit, one wears a friendly look; after one has satisfied oneself, one becomes a prince.
Cultural_Context: Pleasantness lasts no longer than one’s need for favors.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá forí sọ, a kì í mọ ìrẹ̀-ẹ́ bẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: If one has not butted one’s head against a beam, one does not learn to stoop.
Cultural_Context: Nothing teaches caution like a mishap.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá pa ìjí han ìjí, ẹ̀rù kì í ba ìjí.
Target_Text_En: Unless one kills a brown monkey and shows it to a brown monkey, the brown monkey does not learn fear. permits the wearer to see but remain unidentifiable by spectators. 364 human nature
Cultural_Context: People seldom learn caution until danger has brushed by them.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá ṣubú, a kì í mọ ẹrù-ú dì.
Target_Text_En: If one has not fallen, one does not learn how best to pack one’s load.
Cultural_Context: One learns only after one has erred.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí àwòdì ò kú, adìẹ ò lè sinmi.
Target_Text_En: If the kite does not die, the chickens cannot relax.
Cultural_Context: As long as danger persists, one must be vigilant.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí Básè ò sè, kí ni Bálá ó làá?
Target_Text_En: If Help-Cook does not cook, what will Help Lick lick?
Cultural_Context: If nothing is available, one cannot expect anything.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ebí bá ńpa ejò, ahun kì í yan; àtahun àtejò, ẹran jíjẹ.
Target_Text_En: If a snake is hungry, a tortoise should not go strutting by; both snake and tortoise are edible meat.
Cultural_Context: One should always be vigilant and stay away from dangerous situations.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí eṣú bá jẹ oko tán eṣú á lọ, a ku alátanpopo.
Target_Text_En: Having devoured the farm, the locusts will depart, leaving the cricket behind.
Cultural_Context: When one has surmounted one’s greatest obstacle, the little ones will remain to claim one’s attention.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí etí kò gbọ́ yínkín, inú kì í bájẹ́.
Target_Text_En: If the ears do not hear bad news, the mind does not become unhappy.
Cultural_Context: Depression does not occur for no reason; it follows bad tidings.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ìgbá ò so kúdu-kùdu, kí lọmọ ẹrankó ó jẹ?
Target_Text_En: If the bitter tomato does not fruit abundantly, what will young animals eat?
Cultural_Context: If the provider does not provide, the dependents suffer.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ikú bá tilẹ̀kùn, ebi ní ńṣí i.
Target_Text_En: If death locks a door, hunger will open it.
Cultural_Context: The disconsolate mourner will sooner or later yield to hunger.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ilé kò bá kan ilé, wọn kì í jó àjóràn.
Target_Text_En: If houses do not abut, they do not catch fire from one another.
Cultural_Context: Unless one is associated with a person in trouble, one does not share in it.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ilé ńjó, bí olè ńjà, ẹni ebi ńpa yó máa wí.
Target_Text_En: If the house is on fire, if a burglar is at work, the hungry person will say his or her piece.
Cultural_Context: One’s private woes take precedence over public disasters.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ìrònú bá pọ̀, bí ikú ò tẹ̀le, àrùn ńkọ́?
Target_Text_En: If brooding is excessive, and if death does not result, what about disease?
Cultural_Context: Excessive brooding is not healthy.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ìyà ńlá bá gbéni ṣánlẹ̀, ké-kè-ké a máa gorí ẹni.
Target_Text_En: When a great misfortune floors us, small ones climb on us.
Cultural_Context: People who would other wise not dare to will take advantage of a person who is down.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí kò sí tọ̀mọ̀, kí là ńwá ní fùrọ̀ onífùrọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Were it not on account of children, what business would one have with another per son’s genitals?
Cultural_Context: Necessity imposes obligations.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ó bá di ibi yíyan, ògòǹgò a súnkì.
Target_Text_En: When it comes to frying, the palm weevil will contract.
Cultural_Context: If the disaster is big enough, the strongest person feels the effect.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí o bá fẹ́ bọ̀rọ̀kìnní-í tẹ́, jí relé-e rẹ̀ láfẹ̀ẹ̀mọ́júmọ́; wo ẹní tó tẹ́ sùn; wo aṣọ tó fi ḿbora.
Target_Text_En: If you wish to deflate a dandy, go to his home in the early dawn; look at the mat he sleeps on, and look at the sheet he covers himself with.
Cultural_Context: The dandy abroad is often filthy at home.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ó ti wù ká ṣe Ìbàdàn tó, apá kan ìlú là ńrí.
Target_Text_En: However long one lives in Ibadan, one sees only one part of the city.
Cultural_Context: No one can know all about the affairs of a city or person.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí òjò ò rọ̀, bí àgbàdo ò gbó, kí ni ọmọ aráyé ó jẹ?
Target_Text_En: If rain does not fall, and corn does not mature, what will humans eat?
Cultural_Context: If the powers people rely on do not fulfill their obligations, the masses face peril.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí òru bí òru ní ńṣe aláṣọ dúdú.
Target_Text_En: Eager anticipation of nightfall is the mind set of the person wearing black-colored garments. On human vulnerability 365
Cultural_Context: One always seeks operating con ditions conducive to one’s circumstances.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọmọdé bá lówó, ìgbéraga ní ńdà lójú àgbà.
Target_Text_En: If a youth is wealthy, his actions seem like pride in the eyes of the elders.
Cultural_Context: Older people are not beyond being jealous of youthful success.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọ̀pọ̀lọ̀ bá fẹ̀hìn lélẹ̀, nǹkan ló ńṣe é.
Target_Text_En: If a toad lies on its back, something is the matter with it.
Cultural_Context: If a person does the unex pected, there must be a reason.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí pẹ́pẹ́yẹẹ́ bá jẹ òkúta, omi ni yó fi ṣu.
Target_Text_En: If a duck eats stones, it evacuates them in the form of water. E
Cultural_Context: No matter what the cir cumstances, some people cannot change their nature or habits.

Source_Text_Yo: Ebi ò mọ̀ pé oókan ò sí nílé; bí ojú bá mọ̀, ebi a máa pani.
Target_Text_En: Hunger does not care that there is not one single cowrie shell in the home; when morn ing breaks, hunger assails one.
Cultural_Context: Hunger does not leave one alone simply because one is poor.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèmọ̀ ní Ìmọ̀: Onímọ̀-ọ́ sòpá, ayaa rẹ̀-ẹ́ dégbò
Target_Text_En: Unspeakable abomination: the ruler of Imọ contracts hydroceles, and his wife develops a sore.
Cultural_Context: Even those people to whom one would look up are blighted.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèyàn gígùn ò ṣé-é bọ òrìṣà méjì.
Target_Text_En: A tall person is not enough sacrifice for two gods.
Cultural_Context: The mightiest person is still one person.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèyàn kan ní ńrọ kangara mọ́ni lọ́wọ́.
Target_Text_En: It is a person who fashions a billhook and thrusts it into one’s hand.
Cultural_Context: Impositions do not materialize by themselves; there is always human agency behind them.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèyàn ní ńkọ́ni ká gùn; èèyàn ní ńkọ́ni ká kúrú.
Target_Text_En: People teach one to be tall [or long]; people teach one to be short.
Cultural_Context: One soon learns from experience how to cope with the devious ways of humans.

Source_Text_Yo: Egbinrin ọ̀tẹ̀: à ńpàkan, ọ̀kan ńhù.
Target_Text_En: Plots like wild vegetables: one eliminates one, and another sprouts.
Cultural_Context: Some problems are so resistant that they are virtually impossible to resolve.

Source_Text_Yo: Eji wẹ́rẹ́-wẹ́rẹ́ ní ńlé ọmọ wọlé; àgbàrá òjò ńlá ní ńmi ọ̀gọ̀rọ̀ tìtì lẹ́sẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is a light rain that chases a child indoors; it is a raging torrent that shakes the raffia palm to its roots.
Cultural_Context: Every person, however lowly or mighty, has his or her nemesis.

Source_Text_Yo: Ejò ò kó ọmọ lẹ́hìn jẹ yọọ-yọ kánú igbó
Target_Text_En: A snake does not wander in the bush with all its young in train.
Cultural_Context: Each person pursues his or her destiny singly.

Source_Text_Yo: Èké ní ńrojọ́; ìkà ní ńdá a.
Target_Text_En: The person stating a case is devious; the person judging it is evil.
Cultural_Context: One’s adversary and the person one looks to for justice are in league together.

Source_Text_Yo: Èlùbọ́ ṣègbodò rí; ẹrú ṣọmọ rí nílé-e bàbá ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Yam flour was once fresh yam; a slave was once a child in his father’s house.
Cultural_Context: No one is immune to a change in fortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Etí kì í tóbi kó gb r méje lọkan ṣoṣo.
Target_Text_En: Ears are never so large that they can hear [decipher] seven messages all at once.
Cultural_Context: There is an existential limit to human capabilities.

Source_Text_Yo: Etí lobìnrín fi ńgbóhùn Orò
Target_Text_En: Only with her ears does a woman hear the voice of Orò.
Cultural_Context: The sight of Orò is forbidden to a certain class of people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀bìtì ò peèrà; ará ilé ẹni ní ńpani
Target_Text_En: Atrap does not kill an ant; people of one’s household engineer one’s death.
Cultural_Context: The enemy within is the one to fear.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀bùn Ọlọ́run ò kan ọgbọ́n.
Target_Text_En: God’s gift has nothing to do with wisdom.
Cultural_Context: Natural gifts are nothing to take credit for.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀hìnkùlé lọ̀tá wà; ilé laṣeni ńgbé.
Target_Text_En: One’s back yard is where one’s enemy is to be found; it is in one’s home that the per son who means one harm lives.
Cultural_Context: One’s most dangerous enemies are those closest to one.

Source_Text_Yo: Èjọ́ bá ọ, bí ọ̀ràn ikúnlẹ̀-ẹ́ bá arọ.
Target_Text_En: Trouble has found you, just as the compulsion to kneel has found the cripple
Cultural_Context: You have just as much chance of escaping trouble as the cripple has of avoiding crawling.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹjọ́ ní ḿbá mo-kó-mo-rò wa
Target_Text_En: ‘I will tell all I know’’ results from a dispute.
Cultural_Context: If there were no dispute, one would not be required to explain; when one lands in an unfortunate situation, inconveniences are piled on.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹlẹ́dẹ̀-ẹ́ pàfọ̀ tán, ó ńwá ẹni rere tí òun ó fara yí.
Target_Text_En: The pig, after wallowing in the mud, goes looking for a decent person to rub bodies with.
Cultural_Context: Evil people are always on the prowl for decent people to corrupt.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni à bá fẹ̀hìntìí jẹ́ ẹlẹ́gùn-ún; ẹni à bá finú hàn-án jẹ́ aláròkiri.
Target_Text_En: The person one would lean on turns out to be thorny; the person one would confide in turns out to be a blabbermouth. On human vulnerability 367
Cultural_Context: There are few people one can really trust.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni a gbójú olókùn lé kì í ṣẹni ẹgba.
Target_Text_En: The person for whom one has readied a rope is not one for whom a whip is appro priate.
Cultural_Context: The person one has been spoiling to destroy turns out to be beyond one’s reach.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni à ńpète pèrò ká sọwọ́-ọ rẹ̀ dilẹ̀, pípele ní ńpele sí i.
Target_Text_En: The person we keep plotting to bring to de struction nevertheless continues to grow in prosperity.
Cultural_Context: The machinations of enemies have no effect on the fortunes of a certain person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni a rí la mọ̀; ẹni a mọ̀ rí a gbàgbé.
Target_Text_En: We know only those whom we see; those we saw in the past we forget.
Cultural_Context: Only those who are present command people’s attention.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni a rí ṣígun: ó ní fèrè lòun ó fọn.
Target_Text_En: The person on whose arrival one advances against the enemy: he says all he will do is blow the bugle.
Cultural_Context: The person one reposed all one’s hopes in turns out to be a disappoint ment.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni ẹni ní ńṣeni; bìtì ò peèrà.
Target_Text_En: One’s own relatives constitute one’s bane; the ant does not fall victim to a snare.
Cultural_Context: Those closest to one are best placed to cause one injury.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni gígùn kì í kú lẹ́ẹ̀mejì..
Target_Text_En: A tall person does not die twice.
Cultural_Context: However great a person can be, he or she remains yet only one person; however great a person is, he or she shares the same destiny with all human beings.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni ìjà ò bá ní ńpe ara lọ́kùnrin.
Target_Text_En: It is the person not faced with a fight who boasts about his manliness.
Cultural_Context: One can always boast when one is certain there will be no need for proof.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni mọ́tò-ó pa-á re run ìyà; ẹni rélùwéè-é pa-á re ọ̀run ẹ̀sín.
Target_Text_En: Whoever is killed by a motor vehicle dies a miserable death; whoever is killed by a train dies a disgraceful death.
Cultural_Context: It is better to be killed by a motor vehicle than by a train, but neither way of death is becoming

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni ọká bá ṣán: bí kò kú, a di ẹlẹgùn ejò.
Target_Text_En: When a person is bitten by a cobra and he does not die, he becomes a devotee of the snake’s cult.
Cultural_Context: Whoever survives a great calamity has no further reason to fear its like.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní ra fìlà fún akàn-án fowó ṣòfùn; níbo ni yó de sí?
Target_Text_En: Whoever buys a cap for a crab wastes money; where will it place the cap?
Cultural_Context: One should not waste one’s resources on foolish ventures.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí à bá finú hàn ní ńṣe elénìní ẹni.
Target_Text_En: The person in whom one would confide is the author of one’s ruin.
Cultural_Context: There is hardly anyone a person can confidently trust.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a bá ní ní ńgbani.
Target_Text_En: The champion one has is the one who comes to one’s aid.
Cultural_Context: A champion should not default just when his or her aid is needed.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a kọ́ níkà tó gbà, ó ti ní tirẹ̀ nínú tẹ́lẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: A person who is receptive to the advice to do evil was predisposed to evil.
Cultural_Context: Only those willing to be corrupted can be corrupted.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a sọ òkò lùú ní kí á sọ ìdàrọ.
Target_Text_En: The person at whom one throws stones urges one to throw iron dross.
Cultural_Context: The tar get of one’s punishment, rather than being impressed, urges one to do one’s worst.

Source_Text_Yo: Èyí tí ebi ńpa ò gbọ́ íwàásù.
Target_Text_En: A starving person hears no preaching.
Cultural_Context: A starving person hears no preaching.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ò mú nǹkan wá sáyé ò lè mú nǹkan lọ sọ́run.
Target_Text_En: People who brought nothing into this world cannot expect to depart from it with some thing.
Cultural_Context: We came into this world naked, and we shall depart naked.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ò rí ehín fi jẹ ẹja tútù ò lè jẹ gúgúrú.
Target_Text_En: Whoever lacks teeth to eat fresh fish cannot eat popcorn.
Cultural_Context: A person who fails at an easy task will not succeed at a difficult venture.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí òjò-ó pa, tí Ṣàngó ò pa, kó máa dúpẹ.
Target_Text_En: The person who is caught in the rain but is not struck by Ṣango, god of lightning, should be thankful.
Cultural_Context: If one suffers a small misfortune, one should remember that it could have been much worse.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó bá ogun níbodè-é bá iṣẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Whoever walks in on a battle at the town gate walks in on a tough assignment.
Cultural_Context: If one walks in on trouble, one’s task is cut out.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó gba ọmọ ẹni ò ní òun ò níí gba aya.
Target_Text_En: The person who makes off with one’s daugh ter will think nothing of making off with one’s wife.
Cultural_Context: One should expect no quarter from an adversary who has proved himself or herself ruthless and unscrupulous.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó kàn ló mọ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is the person a calamity has befallen who knows how it feels.
Cultural_Context: No amount of sympathy can give one firsthand experience of other people’s woes.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó láyà ní ńṣòwò ọ̀tẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Only a person who is bold makes conspiracy his trade.
Cultural_Context: Those who conspire must have the spine to take on the consequences.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó mọ ìhín ò mọ ọ̀hún; alágbẹ̀dẹ ò roko.
Target_Text_En: The person who is familiar with this place is not familiar with the other place; the black smith does not till a farm.
Cultural_Context: No one person can know it all, or do it all.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó mọ̀ ọ́ kò kò ó; ẹni tó kò ó kò mọ̀ ọ́.
Target_Text_En: Those who know him do not meet him; those who meet him do not know him.
Cultural_Context: People often fail to appreciate the qualities of those they encounter.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó mọ ọ̀ràn tán di Olódùmarè.
Target_Text_En: The person who knows everything has be come God Almighty.
Cultural_Context: No human being can know everything.

Source_Text_Yo: Èni tó sọ pé láti ìgbà tí òun-ún ti dáyé ìyà ò jẹ òun rí, ohun tí ìyà ńjẹ lẹ́nu ni kòì tíì kúnná.
Target_Text_En: The person who says since he came to this world he or she has never been in the teeth of suffering: it is simply because suffering has not yet chewed up what it already has in its teeth.
Cultural_Context: Everybody comes to know suffering in time.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó tàkìtì lÉkòó, tó bal nÍbàdàn: wọ́n ní Abẹ́kùúta ńkọ́? Ó ní káfò ó
Target_Text_En: The person who somersaulted from Lagos and landed in Ibadan is asked, ‘‘What about Abòkúta?’’ He responds, ‘‘Let us skip that.’
Cultural_Context: When earthshaking problems arise, it is no time to dwell on trifles.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó tẹjúmọ́lẹ̀-ẹ́ mọ ohun tí òun ńwa.
Target_Text_En: The person who fixes his eyes on the ground knows what he is looking for.
Cultural_Context: No one does anything without a good reason, even if it is not readily apparent to others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnìkan kì í gbọ́n tán.
Target_Text_En: Nobody is all wise.
Cultural_Context: Everybody can learn something from others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu ẹyẹ ò lè yán òkúta
Target_Text_En: A bird’s beak cannot snap up a rock.
Cultural_Context: There are certain tasks that are beyond a person’s capabilities.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu kò gb ‘‘Mo jẹ rí.’’
Target_Text_En: The mouth does not say, ‘‘I ate once before.’’
Cultural_Context: Hunger is not something one assuages once and for all.

Source_Text_Yo: A Yoruba form of lamentation that a despair ing sick person might resort to is Mo kú o! (‘‘ Oh, I am dead!’’).
Target_Text_En: A Yoruba form of lamentation that a despair ing sick person might resort to is Mo kú o! (‘‘
Cultural_Context: The Yoruba believe that such talk invites its own fulfillment.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀pa ò bá oró mọ́.
Target_Text_En: The antidote can no longer catch up with the poison.
Cultural_Context: Matters have gone past the possibility of redress.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀rú gba ẹdùn, ominú ńkọ igi.
Target_Text_En: The axe is slipped onto the haft; the tree be come anxious.
Cultural_Context: When danger threatens, the vulnerable become apprehensive.

Source_Text_Yo: Èrù kì í pa òṣùká; ẹlẹ́rù lẹrù ńpa.
Target_Text_En: The load does not weigh down the carrying pad; it is the owner [carrier] of the load that the load weighs down.
Cultural_Context: Much as one may give aid to a person in trouble, one cannot assume the trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹsẹ̀ ńtẹlẹ̀, inú ḿbí aráyé.
Target_Text_En: The feet tread the ground, and people are angry.
Cultural_Context: Some people will begrudge others simply for living.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹṣín dára ó ku aré; èèyán dára ó ku ìwà; ajá òyìnbó dára ó ku àtidẹ.
Target_Text_En: The horse looks great but lacks speed; the man is handsome but lacks character; the European dog is good-looking but can not hunt.
Cultural_Context: Looks are nothing compared to substance or utility.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹṣin ẹni kì í ga lójú tá ẹni.
Target_Text_En: One’s horse is never tall in the eyes of one’s enemy.
Cultural_Context: Not Provided

Source_Text_Yo: Whatever one does, one cannot impress an enemy.
Target_Text_En: r p ṣ -p ṣ , meaning ‘‘exceeding softness’’ or ‘‘exceeding ease,’’ is a charm for which the juice obtained by cracking a snail shell is an essential ingre dient.[?]enemy. (
Cultural_Context: Whatever one does, one cannot impress an enemy.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹṣin tá ẹni kì í ga lójú ẹni; à ní bíi kẹ́tẹ́kẹ́ ló rí.
Target_Text_En: One’s enemy’s horse is never tall in one’s sight; one says it is just like an ass.
Cultural_Context: One always minimizes an enemy’s accomplish ments. Compare the preceding entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀tù ò sí ìbọ́n dọ̀pá; baba ọmọ́ kú ọmọ́ dẹyọ.
Target_Text_En: Without gunpowder the gun becomes a stick; the father dies, and his children be come disconnected individuals.
Cultural_Context: When the main support is removed, the greatest edifice collapses.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹyẹ ńwú bà-ǹ-kù ba-kù, ìyẹ́ làṣírí ẹ̀
Target_Text_En: The bird swells to a huge dimension, but the secret is in its feathers. G
Cultural_Context: A person’s impressive appearance is not always backed by substance.

Source_Text_Yo: Gagalo-ó ṣubú, ọwọ́ tẹ apákó.
Target_Text_En: The stilt walker falls; planks become avail able.
Cultural_Context: When a person loses control, his or her belongings become fair game.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkákùre beans have curly pods.
Target_Text_En: Ìkákùre beans have curly pods
Cultural_Context: On human vulnerability

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Gbà kún tìrẹ’’ ò bí ọmọ aráyé nínú. ‘‘
Target_Text_En: Take this and add it to yours’’ does not offend humankind.
Cultural_Context: People are ever recep tive to aggrandizement.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Gbà pamọ́’’ fún olè ní ḿmú olè jà. ‘‘
Target_Text_En: Take this for safekeeping’’ addressed to a thief encourages thievery.
Cultural_Context: The person who places temptations in another’s path is partly responsible for whatever goes amiss.

Source_Text_Yo: "Gbà ràn mí" di ẹlẹ́rù; ajínifẹ́ di ọkọ ẹni.
Target_Text_En: Help me with this load’’ becomes the owner of the load; the cuckolder becomes the hus band.
Cultural_Context: Temporary expedients sometimes become permanent conditions.

Source_Text_Yo: "Gbà tọ́wò-ó" gbé ipọn mì; Gbà ràn mí lẹ́rù-ú di ẹlẹ́rù; Bá mi gún èlùbó fi ẹ̀gbé gún èèkàn
Target_Text_En: Taste this’’ swallows the spoon; ‘‘Help me with this load’’ becomes the owner of the load; ‘‘Help me pound these dried yams’’ impales herself on a wooden peg.
Cultural_Context: One should not be more zealous as a helper than the person one is helping.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbànújẹ́ sọ orí àgbà kodò.
Target_Text_En: Sadness bows the head of the most venerable elder.
Cultural_Context: No one outgrows sadness.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi iṣẹ́ la ti ḿmọ ọ̀lẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is at his or her trade or occupation that one knows the shirker.
Cultural_Context: To really know the hard worker or the shirker, one must see him or her at work.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó gbọdọ̀n ọrọ ọkàn, ó gbọdọ̀n ọrọ ọjọ.
Target_Text_En: To really know the hard worker or the shirker, one must see him or her at work.)
Cultural_Context: Not Provided

Source_Text_Yo: Igí gbun nígbó à ńsọ̀; ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ èèyàn ló gbun láàrin ìlú.
Target_Text_En: We complain that a tree grows crooked in the forest, yet a great many people are crooked in the town.
Cultural_Context: When one has skele tons in one’s own closet, one should not find fault with others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbàgbé ò lóògùn.
Target_Text_En: Forgetting knows no antidote.
Cultural_Context: Anyone is likely to forget something sometime.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbòó wá ilé ẹyẹkẹ́yẹ tú
Target_Text_En: Àgbìgbò takes delight in raiding the nests of other birds.
Cultural_Context: Said of a person who enjoys introducing disharmony into other people’s affairs.

Source_Text_Yo: Ijó ḿbẹ nínú arọ, ẹsẹ̀ ni ò sí.
Target_Text_En: There is a lot of dance in the cripple; what he or she lacks are legs.
Cultural_Context: If one had the wherewithal, one would perform wonders.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikán ńjẹ orù; kèrègbè paramọ́.
Target_Text_En: Termites are consuming the small earthen pot; gourds had better beware.
Cultural_Context: If an evil fate befalls those who are more formidable than you are, look out.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikùn baba òrìṣà.
Target_Text_En: The stomach [is the] father of all gods.
Cultural_Context: One can less afford to neglect one’s stomach than one’s gods.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikún ní bí òun-ún bá p nílé, ràn ilé á bá òun; bí òun-ún bá sì pẹ́ lóde, ọ̀ràn òde a bá òun.
Target_Text_En: The squirrel says if it stays too long at home, it is beset by the problems of home; if it stays long outside instead, it is plagued by problems of the outside.
Cultural_Context: No matter where one turns, there is trouble aplenty.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilẹ̀ kì í gba ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ kó so ìdì méjì.
Target_Text_En: The soil is never so nourishing for the banana plant that it brings forth two bunches at once.
Cultural_Context: Nature places limits on everyone and everything.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilẹ̀ tí kò ti ojú ẹni ṣú, a kì í mọ òkùnkùn un rẹ̀ẹ́ rìn.
Target_Text_En: One never knows how to negotiate the dark ness of a night that did not fall in one’s presence.
Cultural_Context: One cannot know all the intrica cies of a matter that developed outside one’s knowledge.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìlérí ilé ò mọ ti à ńjagun; kùfẹ̀-kùfẹ̀ ò mọ ìjà; ọj táa rógun là ḿmojo.
Target_Text_En: Boasting within the house is no proof of bravery in battle; rearing in anticipation is no proof of prowess in a fight; the day that war breaks out is when one knows who is a coward.
Cultural_Context: Valor is a matter not of speech but of deed.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìlú kì í kéré kó má nìí ààtàn
Target_Text_En: A town is never so small that it does not have a dung hill.
Cultural_Context: Everybody has his or her flaws, or skeletons in the closet.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìnùkínù ní ḿmú ìwákúwàá wá; ẹṣín sọnù à ńwá a nínú igbá Ifá
Target_Text_En: Inexplicable loss occasions senseless search ing; a horse is lost and one searches for it in an Ifá divining bowl.
Cultural_Context: Baffling occurrences lead one to strange behavior.

Source_Text_Yo: Inúnibíni ò kan àì-mọ̀wà-rere-éhù.
Target_Text_En: Malice toward others does not result from not knowing how to be good.
Cultural_Context: Evil behavior is a matter of will, not of nature.

Source_Text_Yo: Irọ́ ní njẹ "Mo kú tán."
Target_Text_En: The exclamation ‘‘I am dead!’’ is a lie.
Cultural_Context: A person who can still lament has not reached the height of suffering.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣẹ́ ní ḿmú ahùn jẹ eèrí; eèrí kì í ṣe oúnjẹ ahun.
Target_Text_En: It is destitution that brought the tortoise to eating corn bran; bran is no food for the tortoise.
Cultural_Context: Misfortune reduces one to doing things one would rather not do.

Source_Text_Yo: Iṣé tán, òwó pin, òwú ó kún kẹ́kẹ́; ara gbogbó le bí ìtì ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The work is done, the trading is over, the cotton does not fill the barrow; the body remains as firm as a banana trunk.
Cultural_Context: One has done what one is called upon to do, but the desired goal is not yet achieved, and one would rather continue to work if one only could.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣeǹṣe tó ṣe dé ìhín kì í tán lọ́rọ̀-ọ panṣágà.
Target_Text_En: The sort of behavior that brought her to her present condition never leaves the prosti tute.
Cultural_Context: One cannot change one’s nature.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyà mẹ́ta a-fàdá-pa-ikún: ikún lọ, àdá nù, aládàá ní òun ó gba àdá òun.
Target_Text_En: Three misfortunes that befell the person who would kill a squirrel with a cutlass: the squirrel escaped, the cutlass was lost, and the owner of the cutlass demanded its return.
Cultural_Context: Said when problems climb on problems.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyà mẹ́ta ọ̀gànjọ́: bi a fésẹ̀ kó imí, à fọwọ́ bà á, à fi runmú.
Target_Text_En: Three outrages of a dark night: if one steps into excrement, one feels it with one’s hand, and then one takes a sniff at it.
Cultural_Context: One who is not careful about what he or she does or the company he or she keeps will endure unpleasant consequences.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyàn ní ḿmúni jẹ èso igi-kígi.
Target_Text_En: It is famine that brings one to eating the fruits of all sorts of trees.
Cultural_Context: Hard times force one to unbecoming behavior.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyàwó tí a gbé lójú ijó, onílù ni yó bàá lọ.
Target_Text_En: The wife one met at a dance will eventually elope with a drummer. K
Cultural_Context: People cannot shed their innate habits.

Source_Text_Yo: Ká rí owó ra elééyọ́ ò dàbí-i kó yẹni
Target_Text_En: Having the means to buy the cloth elééy is nothing like having it look good on one.
Cultural_Context: Having money is nothing like knowing how to use it well.

Source_Text_Yo: Kì í ṣe ẹjọ́ ajá: ẹni tó so ó ni ò só ore; ẹni tó só só ore: okùn ni ò yi; okùn-ún yi: orúkọ ajá ló ro ajá tó fi ńjá.
Target_Text_En: The dog is not to blame: it was the person who tied it up that did a poor job; the person who tied it up did a good job: it was the rope that was brittle; the rope was not brittle: the dog was simply acting according to its name when it broke loose.
Cultural_Context: In spite of any preemptive efforts, a person will eventually show his or her true colors.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí ni a fi ńpa lára ìka tí à ńwí pé ó tó màyànkàn-mayankan?
Target_Text_En: What wound would one sustain on one’s f inger that one would say was huge and gaping?
Cultural_Context: There is a limit to which anyone or anything can be at risk.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí ni a ó ti ṣe Ẹrú tí kò ní hùwà ẹrú?
Target_Text_En: What could one do to Ẹrú [Slave] to keep him or her from behaving like a slave
Cultural_Context: Nothing one does will ever keep a person from acting according to his or her nature.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí ni òkóbó ńwò tí kò gbé nǹkan mì?
Target_Text_En: What is the eunuch considering that keeps him from swallowing poison?
Cultural_Context: A worthless person has little cause to cling tenaciously to life.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí ọmọdé tó gbọn, ìwà-a ẹ̀ á bájẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Before a child learns wisdom, he or she will have earned a bad reputation.
Cultural_Context: One seldom learns wisdom before one has made some blunders.

Source_Text_Yo: Kiní kan-án ba àjàò jẹ́: apá ẹ̀-ẹ́ pọ̀ ju itan ẹ̀ lọ
Target_Text_En: Àjàò [a nocturnal bird] has one blemish: its wing is heftier than its thigh.
Cultural_Context: Said of an essentially good person who, however, has an unfortunate serious flaw.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Kiní yìí, ng kò lè jẹ ẹ’’: kí Ọlọ́run má dà à sí agbada ẹni.
Target_Text_En: This thing is something I cannot eat: may God not pour it into my vat.
Cultural_Context: May God keep away from me the problems I cannot handle.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Kò mọ̀ọ́ tà kò mọ̀ọ́ rà’’ tí ńgun ẹṣin lórí àpáta.
Target_Text_En: He-knows-not-how-to-sell-and-he-knows not-how-to-buy who rides a horse on the rock.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who misuse valuable things which other people must pay for and care for—vandals, in one word.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò pa ẹtu kò jọkí ẹtu jẹ̀, tí ńfaṣọ funfun sọdẹ.
Target_Text_En: He-will-not-kill-antelopes-and-he-will-not let-antelopes-forage who hunts in white attire.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who will neither do something nor get out of the way of others willing to do it: dogs in the manger. See 3837.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò run ẹni, kò run ẹni, ó wa ńdòyì ka ẹni.
Target_Text_En: It does not destroy one, it does not destroy one, yet it persists in circling one.
Cultural_Context: Said of needling problems that persist despite one’s efforts to get rid of them.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí bí a ti lè ṣe ebòlò tí kò níí rùngbẹ́.
Target_Text_En: There is nothing one can do to the vegetable ebòlò that will make it not smell of the wild.
Cultural_Context: There is nothing one can do to the vegetable ebòlò that will make it not smell of the wild.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí bí a ti lè ṣe ẹlẹdẹ̀ tí kò níí pàfọ̀.
Target_Text_En: There is nothing one can do to the pig to keep it from wallowing in the mud.
Cultural_Context: People cannot be cured of their natures.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí bí a ti lè ṣe Ifá kó má hùwà èkùrọ́
Target_Text_En: There is nothing one can do to Ifá that will keep him from behavior suggestive of palm kernels.
Cultural_Context: There is no curing people of their natures.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò ṣe, kò jólúrè ṣe.
Target_Text_En: He or she will not act, and he or she will not permit others to act.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who will neither do something nor get out of the way of others willing to do it: dogs in the manger

Source_Text_Yo: Kó wó, kó wó lojú aṣeni.
Target_Text_En: That things would collapse, that things would collapse is the expectation of the ill wisher.
Cultural_Context: One’s enemies always wish for one to fail.

Source_Text_Yo: Èkùr (palm kernels) are used in consulting Ifá, the Yoruba oracle divinity.
Target_Text_En: Èkùr (palm kernels) are used in consulting Ifá, the
Cultural_Context: On human vulnerability 375

Source_Text_Yo: Kòkòrò jewé-jewé, kòkòrò jobì-jobì: kò kòrò tí ńjewé ara ewé ní ńgbé; kòkòrò tí ńjobì ara obì ní ńwà.
Target_Text_En: Leaf-eating insect, kola-nut-eating insect: the insect that eats leaves lives on leaves; the insect that feeds on kola nuts sticks to the kola nut.
Cultural_Context: One should remain where one is supposed to be, or where one’s living is.

Source_Text_Yo: Kòtò ayé, kòtò obìnrin, àti kòtò ikú, kan ò yàtọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The pit dug by the world, the one dug by a woman, and the one dug by death: they are all the same.
Cultural_Context: The world, women, and death are equal in their portent.

Source_Text_Yo: Kúkúrú yẹ ijó.
Target_Text_En: Shortness is an asset in dancing.
Cultural_Context: Being short is not all bad.

Source_Text_Yo: Kùkùté àgbọn ò lè sọrú.
Target_Text_En: The stump of a coconut palm cannot sprout leaves. L
Cultural_Context: A person down and out cannot excel.

Source_Text_Yo: Lílọ-ọ́ yá fún oníbodè tí wọ́n kó nÍfá lọ
Target_Text_En: It is quitting time for the gatekeeper whose divining tray has been stolen.
Cultural_Context: When one’s surest weapon has been neutralized, one had better make one’s escape

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Lọ fún mi nílé yìí’’ kọ́ ni ‘‘Lọ fún mi níbòmíràn.’’
Target_Text_En: ‘‘Get out of my sight in this house’’ is not ‘‘Get out of my sight elsewhere.’’
Cultural_Context: If one is shut out of one opportunity, one can usually f ind another elsewhere.40 The following entry is a variant.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Lọ kúrò nílé mi’’ kì í ṣe ‘‘Kúrò láyé.’’
Target_Text_En: Get away from my home’’ is not the same as ‘‘Get out of this life.’’
Cultural_Context: Divorce is not a death sentence. Compare the preceding entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Lójú àwòdì òkè, bí-i kádìẹ lọ sórí àpáta.
Target_Text_En: In the eyes of a kite aloft, the wish is that the chicken would venture onto a rock.
Cultural_Context: One always wishes that one’s intended victims would render themselves more vulnerable.

Source_Text_Yo: Má rìí igbo loògùn-un wèrè; bó bá rígbó á kó wọ̀ ọ́.
Target_Text_En: Not seeing a bush is the only remedy for a madman; if he sees a bush, he will head for it.
Cultural_Context: The best remedy for a weak-willed person is not to bring temptation his or her way.

Source_Text_Yo: Mò ḿbọ̀! Máa bọ̀! Àwọn méjèèjì lẹ̀rù bá.
Target_Text_En: Here I come!’’ ‘‘Come on already!’’ Both of them are afraid.
Cultural_Context: Both the person bluffing and the person calling the bluff are secretly apprehensive.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Mo ròkè ọgbà mo tètè bọ̀’’: a lè fi wé tẹni tí ò lọ? ‘‘Àkèekèé ta mí kò tù mí’’: a lè fi wé ẹni tí sèbé bùjẹ?
Target_Text_En: ‘‘I went to my nearby farm and returned early’’: can one compare such a person to a person who went nowhere? ‘‘A scorpion stung me and the pain is unrelenting’’: can onecomparesuchapersontoapersonbitten by a viper?
Cultural_Context: Misfortunes vary in their severity.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Mo yó lánàá’’ ò kan tebi
Target_Text_En: ‘‘I ate my fill yesterday’’ does not relieve hunger.
Cultural_Context: Each day brings its own cares.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Ng óò gúnyán, ng óò bùn ọ́ jẹ’’; ibi ẹ̀sun la ti ḿmọ̀ ọ́
Target_Text_En: ‘I will prepare pounded yam and share it with you’’; one will see the signs of its like lihood in connection with roasted yams.
Cultural_Context: People’s behavior in circumstances of no consequence is a good indication of how they will behave in circumstances that mat ter.

Source_Text_Yo: Ní ọj tí ọ̀bùn-ún bá wẹ̀ lara ńyún un.
Target_Text_En: It is on the day that the filthy person takes a bath that his or her whole body itches.
Cultural_Context: Evil people never feel comfortable with virtuous things.

Source_Text_Yo: Ní ọjọ́-ọ ṣíṣu ni fùrọ̀ ńlà.
Target_Text_En: It is on the day one must defecate that the anus must open. O
Cultural_Context: Some obligations permit no options.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó di ọjọ́ tí aláró bá kú ká tó mọ oye aṣọ tó gbà rẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is on the day of the dyer’s death that one knows how many pieces of cloth she had taken in to dye.
Cultural_Context: When one dies, one’s every secret becomes public knowledge.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó wuni ká jẹran pẹ́ lẹnu, olóǹfà ni ó jẹ.
Target_Text_En: One would like to chew a piece of meat for a long time, but a downward pulling force will not allow.
Cultural_Context: Contingencies often limit how long one can relish a boon.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó yé ọmọ tí ńsunkún, ó sì yé ìyá tí mbẹ̀ ẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The crying child knows why it is crying, and the mother consoling it knows why she is doing so.
Cultural_Context: Each person is privy to the motivation for his or her actions.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrin kì í ròhìn àjò tán
Target_Text_En: A woman is never done telling about the trip she took.
Cultural_Context: Some people never cease talking about an experience.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrin kì í tóbi kÓrò má gbèe e
Target_Text_En: A woman is never so large that Orò cannot carry her off.
Cultural_Context: There are certain offenses a woman cannot get away with.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrin ò ṣéé finú hàn
Target_Text_En: A woman is not suitable to expose one’s secrets to.
Cultural_Context: Women cannot be relied on.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrin-ín tẹ ìlú, ó tú
Target_Text_En: A woman founds a town, and it scatters.
Cultural_Context: A woman is not a fit mainstay of a commu nity.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrin tí a fi ijó fẹ́, ìran ni yó wò lọ.
Target_Text_En: The woman one marries on account of her dancing will leave one by losing herself On human vulnerability watching [dancers].
Cultural_Context: People’s habits seldom leave them.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrín torí ọ̀rọ̀ rodò.
Target_Text_En: Women go to the stream only in search of gossip.
Cultural_Context: Women will do anything for the opportunity to gossip.

Source_Text_Yo: Òbò kò jọba, ilú kò darú.
Target_Text_En: [If] the vagina does not become king, the town does not descend into chaos.
Cultural_Context: Affairs in the hands of women inevitably become chaotic.

Source_Text_Yo: Òbúkọ-ọ́ ní àìsàn àgbẹ̀ olówó òun yìí ḿba òun lẹ́rù; bí àìsàn náà-á bá pọ̀ si, babaláwo a ní kí wọ́n lọ mú òbúkọ wá láti fi ṣe ètùtù fún un; bó bá sàn, àwọn ọmọ ẹ̀ a ní wọn ó mùú òbúkọ fi wewu àmódi.
Target_Text_En: The he-goat says the illness of his owner, the farmer, frightens him: if the illness wors ens, the diviners will ask that a he-goat be brought and offered as a propitiatory sac rifice on the farmer’s behalf; if the illness lessens, the children will vow to sacrifice a he-goat as a thank offering.
Cultural_Context: One is in a pre dicament whose every possible outcome is disastrous.

Source_Text_Yo: Ògúnná gbòǹgbò tí ńdátọ́ lẹ́nu ìgbín!
Target_Text_En: Mighty faggot that dries up the dribble in the snail’s mouth!
Cultural_Context: An exclamation on being confronted with an overwhelming problem or stupefying situation.

Source_Text_Yo: The name Láwálé (Ọláwálé) means ‘‘The illus trious one comes home,’’ whereas Láb lùú (Ọláb lùú) means ‘‘ The illustrious one has plunged into it.’’ Names are believed to influence their bearers’ fates. nature confronted with an overwhelming problem or stupefying situation.)
Target_Text_En: The name Láwálé (Ọláwálé) means ‘‘The illus trious one comes home,’’ whereas Láb lùú (Ọláb lùú) means ‘‘
Cultural_Context: Not Provided

Source_Text_Yo: Ògbójú ò tẹ ara nÍfá; ọ̀mọ̀ràn ò fara ẹ̀ joyè; ọ̀bẹ tó mú ò gbẹ́ ẹ̀kù ara ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The intrepid person does not consult the Ifá oracle on his own behalf; the sagacious per son does not enthrone himself; the sharpest knife does not carve its own hilt.
Cultural_Context: No matter how powerful and accomplished one might be, one will need other people for some things.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun mẹ́ta ní ńfi ara wọn rẹ́rìn-ín: aṣọ tó ya ńfi abẹ́rẹ́ rẹ́rìn-ín; àbíkú tí yó kùú ńfi oníṣègùn rẹ́rìn-ín; obìnrin tí yó kọ ọkọ ńfi onípẹ̀ rẹ́rìn-ín.
Target_Text_En: There are three things that laugh at their mates: a torn piece of cloth laughs at the needle; an ábíkú bound to die laughs at a[?]medicine man; a woman intent on leaving her husband laughs at a conciliator.
Cultural_Context: Some problems mock any person who attempts to solve them.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí a bá ńwá ní ńgbọ́n juni lọ.
Target_Text_En: Whatever one is searching for always seems wiser than the searcher.
Cultural_Context: Nothing is ever more difficult to find than whatever one is searching for.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí afọ́jú fojú ẹ̀ rí kó tó fọ́ ló rí mọ; kò tún rí òmíràn mọ́.
Target_Text_En: Whatever the blind person sees before going blind is all he or she will ever see; he or she will never see another thing.
Cultural_Context: One should seize all opportunities before it is too late.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí ó tánni ní ìdùn ní ńtánni lówó.
Target_Text_En: Whatever exceeds the limits of one’s ca pacity to endure is the same thing that will exhaust one’s supply of money.
Cultural_Context: Serious problems wreak havoc on one’s resources.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò ńlá ní ńtẹrí ikin balẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is a heavy rain that beats the lemon grass to the earth.
Cultural_Context: It is a mighty misfortune that can prostrate even the most resilient person.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjó ńrọ̀ sí kòtò, gegele ḿbínú.
Target_Text_En: The rain fills up the gully, and the hill be comes envious.
Cultural_Context: When fortune smiles on some, others become envious.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò ò dá, ìrì ò da; eji wẹ́rẹ́ gba ọjọ́ aláṣọ.
Target_Text_En: The rain does not stop, and the drizzle does not stop; the gentle precipitation takes the day away from the cloth seller.
Cultural_Context: A succession of inconsiderable but persistent problems keeps one from attending to important matters.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò tó rọ̀ ló  mú pẹ̀tẹ̀-pẹ́tẹ̀ wá.
Target_Text_En: The rain that fell is what brought about much mud.
Cultural_Context: Some unfortunate incident has resulted in an unpleasant situation.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò-ó pa alágundi, iyán domi; ìyàwó ńretí agundi, ọkọ́ sùn sóko.
Target_Text_En: The agundi purveyor is caught in the rain, and the pounded yam becomes like water; the wife awaits agundi, but the husband spends the night on the farm.
Cultural_Context: Adverse circumstances will cause the best-laid schemes to go awry.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò-ó pa wèrèpè ó dẹni à ńkọlù.
Target_Text_En: Rain beats the cow-itch and renders it something one can walk into.
Cultural_Context: Misfortune renders one vulnerable to abuse from people who otherwise would not dare displease one

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú aboyún ò tó fùrọ̀; ojù òṣìkà ò tó la.
Target_Text_En: The eyes of a pregnant woman cannot see her genitals; the eyes of the wicked cannot see the future.
Cultural_Context: The wicked do not know when they will reap what they have sown.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú elégbò legbò-ó ti ńkẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is to the knowledge of the person with a sore that the sore festers.
Cultural_Context: Some reverses one can do nothing to prevent.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú layé ńjẹ; bí a yísẹ̀ padà wọn a pẹ̀gàn.
Target_Text_En: Humans serve only the eyes; when one is absent, they ridicule one.
Cultural_Context: It is human nature to love you in your presence and smear you in your absence.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú mọ́n a ò gb poro-poro odó; ọ̀gànjọ́ gàn a ò gbọ́ wọ̀ṣọ̀-wọ̀ṣọ̀ -ọ kọ̀ǹkọ̀ṣọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The day dawns and we fail to hear the sound of the mortar; noontime came and we heard no sound of sifting.
Cultural_Context: One sees and hears no sign of life where one had expected it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú olóbì ni kòkòró ti ńwọ̀ ọ́ lọ.
Target_Text_En: It is in the presence of the kola-nut seller that worms enter the kola nut.
Cultural_Context: Some developments one can in no way prevent.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú olójú là ńrí; ẹni ẹlóri ní ńrí tẹni.
Target_Text_En: One can see only other people’s eyes; only other people can see one’s eyes.
Cultural_Context: You can always see other people’s flaws, but only other people see your flaws.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú ọ̀run ò hu koóko, ilẹ̀pa ò jẹ́ kókù-ú bẹ ọ̀nà wò.
Target_Text_En: The sky does not grow grass; the soil of the graveyard does not afford the dead an op portunity to read trails.
Cultural_Context: Some phenomena offer people no helpful clues to understand them.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú-u baba àtọmọ ni làpálàpá ti ńmú ọmọ lórí.
Target_Text_En: It is with the knowledge of both father and child that ringworm attacks the child’s head.
