Cultural_Context: There are some vicissitudes nothing one can do will avert.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojúgun-ún dé ojú eékún pàrò; ná dé orí àpata pòrúrù.
Target_Text_En: The shin arrives at the knee and disappears; the path arrives at the rock and becomes confused.
Cultural_Context: The problem one faces is most intractable.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojúgun-ún mú odò fọhùn.
Target_Text_En: The shin forces the stream to speak out. 380 human nature
Cultural_Context: A matter one cannot ignore forces one to take action.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkè ìhín ò jìyà rí tọ̀ún.
Target_Text_En: The nearer hill prevents one from seeing the farther one.
Cultural_Context: Urgent obligations keep one from attending to less urgent ones.

Source_Text_Yo: Ókété fẹ́ẹ́ jẹyán, ilé ò gbodó.
Target_Text_En: The giant bush rat wishes to eat pounded yams, but its home is not large enough for the mortar.
Cultural_Context: One’s capacity does not match the feats one would wish to perform.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkú àfín ba àkàlà lẹ́rù.
Target_Text_En: The albino’s corpse strikes terror into the vulture.
Cultural_Context: Response to an affair that stupefies even the most unflappable person.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkú ajá kì í gbó; òkú àgbò kì í kàn
Target_Text_En: A dead dog does not bark; a dead ram does not butt.
Cultural_Context: Once a person is dead, he or she can do nothing.

Source_Text_Yo: Olórí lorí ńsán; kì í sán akàn lókè odò.
Target_Text_En: Only a person who has a head suffers from headaches, not a crab on the bank of the river.
Cultural_Context: If one does not have the amenities, one will not suffer the inconveniences that go with them.

Source_Text_Yo: Òmùwẹ̀ lodò ńgbé lọ.
Target_Text_En: It is the expert swimmer that is carried off by the river.
Cultural_Context: Whatever one is addicted to doing is likely to be one’s death.

Source_Text_Yo: Oníkálukú, a-bèèmọ̀ -nílé.
Target_Text_En: Everybody [is] someone who has something unmentionable at home.
Cultural_Context: Everyone is hiding some secret.

Source_Text_Yo: Oníkálukú a-bi-tiẹ̀ -lára.
Target_Text_En: Everybody [is] someone with his or her own flaw.
Cultural_Context: No one is without some flaw.

Source_Text_Yo: Oník ò sá pamọ́.
Target_Text_En: A person with a cough does not hide.
Cultural_Context: People too much in the public eye cannot be incognito.

Source_Text_Yo: OníṢàngó ò mọ ẹni ọba; òjò ò mẹni ọ̀wọ̀; òjò ìbá mẹni ọ̀wọ̀ kò pa oníṢàngó àtọlỌ́ya.
Target_Text_En: The Ṣango worshiper does not countenance the king’s man; the rain does not know who deserves deference; had the rain any idea who deserved respect, it would not have beaten the Ṣango worshiper or the Ọya wor shiper.
Cultural_Context: Nobody gets any special treatment.

Source_Text_Yo: Ooru-ú gba aṣọ lọ́wọ́ onílé; ó fi abẹ̀bẹ̀ lé àlejò lọ́wọ́.
Target_Text_En: Heat takes the garment off the host and hands a fan to the guest.
Cultural_Context: Excessive heat forces people out of ceremonious pretenses.

Source_Text_Yo: Oówo ńlá sọ ọ̀mọ̀ràn lẹ́nu.
Target_Text_En: An almighty boil has attacked the mouth of the sage.
Cultural_Context: An unheard-of situation has preempted action by even the most capable.

Source_Text_Yo: Òpò fùú, ìyà Ọ̀yọ́; ọ̀pọ̀ ò tajà láwìn; àwìn ò tajà lọ́pọ́.
Target_Text_En: Unrequited effort, the misfortune one finds in y town: the person who sells her wares cheap does not sell on credit; the person who sells on credit does not sell cheap.
Cultural_Context: Two people must deal with each other but cannot see eye to eye.

Source_Text_Yo: Òpó tí à bá fẹ̀hìn tì-í fi gbogbo ara ṣẹ̀gún; ẹni tí à bá finú hàn-án jẹ́ aláròkíri ẹni.
Target_Text_En: The post one would lean on is completely covered with spikes; the person one would confide in turns out to be a talkative back biter.
Cultural_Context: One has no one to look to for help or counsel.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí àgbò ó sunwọ̀n; àgbò ni yó ba orí ara ẹ̀ jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The ram has a good head; it is the ram itself that will ruin its head.
Cultural_Context: People are often responsible for their own misfortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí Olúkànḿbí kì í gẹṣin; ìpín àjàpá kì í ṣọ̀ṣọ́; a sòlẹ̀kẹ̀ máhun lọ́rùn, ahun-ún wọgbó.
Target_Text_En: Olúkànḿbí’s destiny does not include riding a horse; the tortoise’s fate is never to know splendor; people adorn the tortoise’s neck with beads, and it heads for the bush.
Cultural_Context: If one gives something of value to people incapable of recognizing value, they will instantly ruin it.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí pọ̀ ní Mògún; ìpín àìṣẹ̀ ló pó níbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: There are heads aplenty in the grove where Ògún receives sacrifice; most numerous are those of innocent people.
Cultural_Context: Even innocence does not always guarantee safety or justice.

Source_Text_Yo: Orin kan tí adití bá gbọ́ kó tó dití ní ńtẹnu mọ́ láé-láé.
Target_Text_En: The one song the deaf person heard before going deaf is the one he will sing repeatedly forever.
Cultural_Context: It is difficult to move people fixated on one thing to something else.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrìṣà bí fun ò sí; ojoojúm ní ńgbẹbọ.
Target_Text_En: There is no god like the gullet; it received sacrifices daily.
Cultural_Context: No one can be anything without food.

Source_Text_Yo: Òtom̀pòrò-ó jókòó gaga-gúgú; alára ló mọ̀ pé kò le
Target_Text_En: Òtòm̀pòrò sits upright and in splendor; only the owner of the body knows it is un well.
Cultural_Context: A person’s outward appearance is not always a good indication of his or her true condition.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí ẹ bàj (‘‘Your head is ruined’’), Orí ẹ ò sunw n, and Orí ẹ ò dára (‘‘ Your head is no good’’) are all insults.
Target_Text_En: Orí ẹ bàj (‘‘Your head is ruined’’), Orí ẹ ò sunw n, and Orí ẹ ò dára (‘‘
Cultural_Context: The proverb refers to the ram’s habit of butting against hard objects, such as other rams’ heads.

Source_Text_Yo: On human vulnerability 381
Target_Text_En: Olúkànḿbí was apparently a real person, one who did not appreciate good things.
Cultural_Context: Not Provided

Source_Text_Yo: Òtòṣì-í rìn tolè tolè.
Target_Text_En: The poor person walks with the mien of a thief.
Cultural_Context: A poor person is ever under suspicion of being susceptible to stealing.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó tí àpọ́n fi ra iyọ̀, ó tó-ó ra ẹṣin.
Target_Text_En: The money the bachelor paid for salt is enough to buy a horse.
Cultural_Context: A novice in a venture is bound to commit huge blunders.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀bẹ kì í mú títí kó gbẹ́ ẹ̀kù ara ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: A knife is never so sharp that it carves its own handle.
Cultural_Context: Everybody needs other people sometime.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọdún mẹ́fà-a jàbú, bí ọgọ́rùn-ún ọdún ni.
Target_Text_En: Six years of wading in the river is like a hundred years.
Cultural_Context: Hardship that actually lasts a brief time seems to the sufferer to last forever.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ́fíìsì ní ńrẹ́hìn akọ̀wé.
Target_Text_En: The office will be the death of the clerk.
Cultural_Context: Each occupation has its peculiar hazard.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀gá ḿbọ̀, ọ̀gá ḿbọ̀! ni yó pa ọmọsẹ́
Target_Text_En: Here comes the boss, here comes the boss!’’ will be the death of the apprentice.
Cultural_Context: Fear of discovery, not diligent working, will be the nemesis of the shirker.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ gbé odò sọ sín-ṣín; ẹja gbé inú omi dára.
Target_Text_En: The banana plant grows by the river and prospers; the fish live in the water and look beautiful.
Cultural_Context: One prospers only to the extent that one’s living situation is hospitable.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọkọkíkú lòṣì obìnrin.
Target_Text_En: The husband’s death is the bane of a woman.
Cultural_Context: Nothing is worse for a woman than to be widowed.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlọ́run ìbá dá kan-in-kan-in tóbi tó eṣinṣin, àtapa ni ì bá ta èèyàn.
Target_Text_En: Had God made the black ant as large as a fly, it would have stung humans to death.
Cultural_Context: It is by the grace of God that the wicked lack the power to do as they otherwise would. See the following variant.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlọ́run ò dá kan-in-kan-in kó lẹ́sẹ̀ ńlá bí ẹṣin; àtapa ni ì bá máa ta èèyàn; ẹni tí yó fi èèyàn ṣẹ̀sín, Ọlọ́run kì í jẹ́ kó níláárí.
Target_Text_En: God did not create the black ant to have limbs as big as horses’; otherwise, it would have kicked humans to death; the person who would ridicule people has been denied prosperity by God.
Cultural_Context: By the grace of God one’s adversaries are powerless to injure one. Compare the preceding entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ ẹkùn laja ńpa.
Target_Text_En: It is the young of a leopard that a dog kills.
Cultural_Context: It is only while one is still vulnerable that one’s enemies can get the better of one.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ tí ò lẹ́wà, ọ̀dẹ̀dẹ̀ ìyá ẹ̀ ní ńpẹ́ sí.
Target_Text_En: A woman without beauty lasts long on her mother’s porch.
Cultural_Context: Plain women are not soon married.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ́ kú lọ́wọ́ adití; ọ̀rọ́ di káti-kàti
Target_Text_En: A child dies in the care of a deaf person; matters become a muddle.
Cultural_Context: Coming to an understanding with a person beyond com munication is a formidable task.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀nà ọ̀fun ò gba kòkò òdù; nà ọ̀fun ì bá gba kòkò òdù, òmìrán ì bá ti gbé ọ̀kan mì, ara ọlọ́tí a dá.
Target_Text_En: The throat cannot accommodate a large pot; were the throat able to accommodate such a pot, the giant would have swallowed one, causing the wine seller to wallow in her loss.
Cultural_Context: Only the limits Nature places on the greedy person limit the damage he can do to others’ property.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ọ̀rọ̀gọ̀jìmọ̀ ẹkùn, tí ńkọ ọdẹ lóminú
Target_Text_En: A frightfully huge leopard: it paralyzes the hunter with fear and anxiety.
Cultural_Context: A huge problem stumps even the most resourceful of people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pá ìbúm̀bú sẹ́ àgbò níwo
Target_Text_En: A horizontal stick knocks off the ram’s horns.
Cultural_Context: An unexpected problem has got the better of a person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pálábá, imú ẹ-ẹ́ ṣe báyìí? Ò ní sùù-u lòun ńwò.
Target_Text_En: Broken bottle, why is your nose the way it is? It responds that it is itself contemplating the matter.
Cultural_Context: Said when one cannot explain a situation that people assume one would be able to explain.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọpẹ́ lọpẹ́ àtàrí tí ò jẹ́ kí oòrùn ó pa àgbọ̀n ìsàlẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Much gratitude is due the skull that kept the sun from beating down on the chin below.
Cultural_Context: Even as one laments one’s fate when con fronted by adversity, one should be grateful for little mercies. The following is a vari ant.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọpẹ́ lọpẹ́  èjìká tí ò jẹ́ kí ẹ̀wù ó bọ́
Target_Text_En: Much gratitude is due the shoulders that kept the garment from falling off.
Cultural_Context: Said when one has experienced extreme adversity and has come through by the grace of God. See the previous entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ní bí a bá sọ̀rọ̀ débi ìrù, ká fò ó.
Target_Text_En: The toad says when conversation turns to the matter of tails, let’s skip it.
Cultural_Context: A person with a blemish is always uncomfortable when such blemishes become the subject of conversation.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn burúkú tòun tẹ̀rín
Target_Text_En: A terrible disaster is always confronted with laughter.
Cultural_Context: The laughter that greets a disaster is not one of merriment.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ran kan ẹnìkan kínnìkan má yọ̀; bó ṣe ogún ọdún, ti olúwarẹ̀ ḿbọ̀ wá bá a.
Target_Text_En: When trouble befalls someone, let at an other person not rejoice; it may take twenty years, but that other person will experience his or her own trouble.
Cultural_Context: It does not pay to rejoice at other people’s misfortune, for we are all subject to misfortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn kì í báni ju bí a ti mọ lọ.
Target_Text_En: No problem affects one beyond one’s ca pacity to be affected.
Cultural_Context: One is liable only to the extent that one is vulnerable.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn ò bá ojúgun, ó ní òun ò lẹ́ràn.
Target_Text_En: The shin has not yet got into trouble, and therefore it says it has no flesh.
Cultural_Context: Until one On human vulnerability gets into trouble, one always thinks one is invulnerable.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn tí ńdunni làròkàn ẹni.
Target_Text_En: Whatever problem troubles one is what one talks to other people about.
Cultural_Context: One’s pressing problems always preoccupy one’s conscious ness.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn tí olóko-ó fi ńṣe ẹkún sun ni àpárò-ó fi ńṣe rín rín.
Target_Text_En: The matter that causes the owner of the farm to burst into tears is the same that causes the partridge to burst into laughter.
Cultural_Context: Some people’s disasters are other people’s good fortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ràn-an hùn-hùn ò tán nínú ẹlẹdẹ.
Target_Text_En: The compulsion to grunt is never ended where the pig is concerned.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who are irrevocably wedded to some ten dency.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rẹ́ burú ju ọ̀tá, Olùwa ló lè yọni.
Target_Text_En: Friends are more terrible than enemies; only God can protect one.
Cultural_Context: Friends can be more dangerous than enemies.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rọ̀ àtọjọ́mọ́jọ́ ò lè ṣí ni létí bí ọ̀rọ̀ titun.
Target_Text_En: Stale news cannot pique one’s attention as new news can.
Cultural_Context: People are ever more inter ested in something new than in familiar things.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí akúwárápá bá sọ, ará ọ̀run ló sọ .
Target_Text_En: Whatever an epileptic says is said by some one bound for heaven.
Cultural_Context: An observation that what a certain person is saying is not worth listening to.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rọ̀-ọ́ pọ̀ nínú ìwé-e kọ́bọ̀, epo-o tọ́rọ́ la fi ńkà á
Target_Text_En: The one-penny newspaper is chock-full of words, so much so that one needs three human nature pence oil to read it all.
Cultural_Context: There is a great deal to be said on the matter under discussion, and there may not be enough time to say it all.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀run àkùrọ̀ làparò ńkú sí.
Target_Text_En: The partridge meets its death on the dry season-marsh farm.
Cultural_Context: Danger often finds one while one fulfills unavoidable obligations.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ṣọ́ ilé ò jọ obìnrin lójú.
Target_Text_En: Preening that is confined to the home does not appeal to a woman.
Cultural_Context: Women always wish to go outside the home in order to advertise their beauty.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀tá ọ̀run ò gba ẹbọ.
Target_Text_En: An implacable enemy does not respond to sacrifices.
Cultural_Context: There is nothing one can do to win over a sworn enemy.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀tẹ̀ ní ńdààmú Ọlọ́run-ún-tó-ó-wò; Ọlọ́runúntóówò kì í ṣe ajákájá
Target_Text_En: It is the season that has taken its toll on Ọlọ́runúntóówò; Ọlọ́runúntóówò is not really a worthless dog.
Cultural_Context: Adverse circum stances sometimes make people do unbecoming things they would not normally do.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀tọ̀ọ̀tọ̀ là ńwògbẹ́ íṣe.
Target_Text_En: People enter the jungle of misery in different ways.
Cultural_Context: People take different paths toward ruination.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀wá ò ní pàlàkà.
Target_Text_En: The palm-leaf midrib does not have nodes from which branches may emerge.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who cannot conceivably be of any use to others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀wàrà òjò ní ḿba oníléọgbà lẹ́rù
Target_Text_En: A torrential deluge is what strikes terror into the heart of a person who lives in a house made of thatch.
Cultural_Context: People who are vulnerable to any sort of danger have reason to tremble if it should threaten.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọwọ́ adẹ́tẹ̀-ẹ́ kó òjì ọ̀wọ̀wọ̀, kò tún gba èkùrọ́.
Target_Text_En: The leper’s hands scoop up forty grains of boiled dry corn; there is no room left for palm kernels.
Cultural_Context: People with disadvantages are limited in their capabilities.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọw ahọ́n kì í tó imú.
Target_Text_En: The reach of the tongue is never as far as the nose.
Cultural_Context: There is a limit to what a person can accomplish.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀wọ́n owó là ńro owó níní; ọ̀wọ́n omi là ńde ìsun; ọ̀wọ́n oúnjẹ là ńpé jẹ yànmù.
Target_Text_En: It is when money is scarce that one is pre occupied with the thought of money; it is when water is scarce that one keeps watch by the spring; it is when food is scarce that one joins a crowd to scramble for food.
Cultural_Context: Scarcity reduces people to unseemly behavior.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọyẹ́ ńfẹ́ o ò funfun, ìrì ńsẹ̀ o ò jọ̀lọ̀, oníṣègùn ni yó fi owó ẹ po ori mu.
Target_Text_En: The harmattan rages, and your skin does not go white; the drizzle falls, and your skin does not soften; your money will end up paying for the medicine man’s meal.
Cultural_Context: A per son affected by natural phenomena in a way different from others will enrich doctors.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọyọ sán àrá, kùru-kùru ò tán mọ̀nà mọ̀ná; akọ àparò, abo àparò lágbe lórí sán-sán-sán.
Target_Text_En: The harmattan does not come with thunder; haze does not come with lightning; neither the male nor the female partridge has a prominent comb on its head. P
Cultural_Context: Everybody has some deficiency.

Source_Text_Yo: Pátákò ẹfọ̀n, kaka ní ńti ajá lẹ́nu.
Target_Text_En: The hoof of the buffalo is a tough thing in a horse’s mouth.
Cultural_Context: Said of problems that are difficult to tackle.

Source_Text_Yo: Pípá tórí igún pá, kì í ṣe ti ẹrù rírù.
Target_Text_En: The baldness that afflicts the vulture did not result from its carrying heavy loads. R
Cultural_Context: One cannot presume to know the reasons for other people’s conditions.

Source_Text_Yo: Rẹ́dẹ-rẹ̀dẹ lára alámọ̀ọ́di tó ní omi ẹjá kọrọ.
Target_Text_En: Matters have gone rather badly for the sick person who says fish broth is bitter.
Cultural_Context: When a person sees only putrefaction in priceless things, he or she is really far gone.

Source_Text_Yo: Rírò ni tèèyàn, ṣíṣe ni tỌlọ́run.
Target_Text_En: It is people’s province to propose; it is God’s fiat to dispose.
Cultural_Context: Man proposes, but God disposes.

Source_Text_Yo: Rógódó ìdí igbá ó jọkó jókòó-o re.
Target_Text_En: The protrusion at the base of the calabash keeps it from sitting straight.
Cultural_Context: An obstacle prevents one from acting as one might wish.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣakatá ní ńdá wọ̀n-wọ̀n ni Bèse
Target_Text_En: The bog represents a troublesome obstacle for the people of Bèse.
Cultural_Context: A stubborn and in evitable problem is an impediment one must learn to live with.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣẹgẹ ò mọ ẹni ọba, òjò ò mẹni ọ̀wọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The tall prickly grass does not care who is a royal personage; rain does not care who is a venerable person.
Cultural_Context: Natural phenomena do not distinguish among human ranks.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣíṣán ló dá ẹ̀kọ lára.
Target_Text_En: Being eaten without any condiments is the misfortune of the corn meal.
Cultural_Context: It is a misfortune to have to do without what is needed for comfortable living.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣó-ń-ṣó méjì kì í forí kan orí.
Target_Text_En: Two pinnacles can never touch heads. T
Cultural_Context: Two irreconcilables can never be brought together.

Source_Text_Yo: Ta ní tó Ọlọ́run? Ẹdá tó mọ̀la ò sí.
Target_Text_En: Who is as great as God? No human being knows tomorrow.
Cultural_Context: No one is as great or knowledgeable as God.

Source_Text_Yo: Tìmùtìmù-ú kó ẹ̀gbin dà sínú.
Target_Text_En: The footstool-cushion fills itself with rub bish.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who must put up with a lot of rubbish or annoyance.

Source_Text_Yo: Túlàsì kaya-n-doro, tíná fi ḿb bàtà lẹ́sẹ̀ adìẹ.
Target_Text_En: Irresistible compulsion, with which fire strips the scaly skin off a chicken’s legs.
Cultural_Context: When the problem is unmanageable, even the toughest person hasn’t a prayer.

Source_Text_Yo: Wón ní, Adétì, o ò gbénì àkàrà. Ó ní wọn ò gbàdúrà pé kí tọwọ́ òun ba òun délé ná.
Target_Text_En: They said, ‘‘Leper, won’t you stop and re ceive your extra [gratuity of ] fried bean fritters?’’ He responded by asking if they should not rather pray that what he already has in his hands will go home safely with him.
Cultural_Context: Covetousness can turn out to be a drain on one’s resources.

Source_Text_Yo: Wón ní, "Amúkùnún, ru mà wọ́ọ̀.’’ Ó ní ‘‘Ìsàlẹ̀ ló ti w wá.’’
Target_Text_En: People said, ‘‘Cripple, your load is crooked.’’ He responded that the crookedness was from the ground up.
Cultural_Context: In considering a prob lem, one must look at the root causes, not only the manifestations.

Source_Text_Yo: Wọ́n ní ká faró palé, a faró palé, ìtalẹ̀-ẹ́ àwòtún ńjẹni; wọ́n ní ká fìt pajà a fìtọ̀ pajà, jẹsẹ̀jẹsẹ̀-ẹ̀ tún ńjẹ èèyàn.
Target_Text_En: One is told to scrub one’s floor with indigo dye; one scrubs the floor with indigo dye, yet mud-floor worms persist in biting one. One is told to wash the market stall with urine, and one washes the stall with urine, yet foot-eating worms continue to eat one.
Cultural_Context: All one’s efforts to master a problem have proved futile.

Source_Text_Yo: Wọ́n ní kí ni wọ́n sọnù, wọ́n ní ẹran; wọ́n ní kí ni wọ́n ńjẹ, wọ́n ní eegun.
Target_Text_En: When asked what they lost, they said meat; when asked what they were eating, they said bones. Y
Cultural_Context: In the face of misfortune, one makes do with what one has.

Source_Text_Yo: Yọyọ lẹnu ayé ńdà.
Target_Text_En: The world runs endlessly at the mouth.
Cultural_Context: People can be relied upon to spread tales irresponsibly about others.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í pẹ́ láyé ká má fi ilẹ̀ bora.
Target_Text_En: One does not live so long on this earth that one does not eventually cover oneself with earth.
Cultural_Context: Everybody dies in the end.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í sunkún a-nìkàn-para-ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not weep for a person who took his or her own life.
Cultural_Context: Do not pity anyone who invites disaster on his or her own head.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìdé ikú là ḿbọ Ògún; àìdé ikú là ḿbọ òrìṣà; bíkú bá dé ikú ò gbẹ́bọ.
Target_Text_En: It is when death has not called that one sacrifices to Ògún; it is when death has not called that one sacrifices to gods; when death comes calling, death does not heed sacrifices.
Cultural_Context: There is no medicine or sacrifice to stop death when its time comes.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìsàn kan ò lè kó ọgb n ikú lọ.
Target_Text_En: One illness cannot bear thirty deaths away.
Cultural_Context: One person’s illness or death will not indemnify others against death.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá kú ó feegun sílé ayé; adìẹ funfun-ún kú ó tu ìhùùhù gbugbu; ìgbín kú ó gbàgbé ìkaraun.
Target_Text_En: The dog dies and leaves bones on earth; the white chicken dies and loses its down; the snail dies and forgets about its shell.
Cultural_Context: One cannot take anything with one to heaven.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajogún-Ifá ní kí òun má kù-ú; ẹni tó kọ́ tẹ̀ ẹ́ dà?
Target_Text_En: He who inherited the Ifá priesthood prays that he not die; where is his predecessor as priest?
Cultural_Context: Everyone dies, willy-nilly.

Source_Text_Yo: Akọ ajá lọ́lá; àgùàlà niyì oṣù.
Target_Text_En: The male dog is glorious; the planet Venus is the glory of the moon.
Cultural_Context: One can tell who is illustrious from mere appearance.

Source_Text_Yo: Aláwo á kú; oníṣègùn á rọ̀run; adáhunṣe ò níí gbélẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The diviner will die; the medicine man will go to heaven; the sorcerer will not re main forever on earth.
Cultural_Context: Death is the lot of everyone.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtàrí wo ọ̀run mọmọ bí ẹnipé kò ní ibẹ́-ẹ̀ rẹ; oye ojú tó wo ayé ni yó wo ọ̀run.
Target_Text_En: The skull stares at the sky as though it would not wind up there; every eye that looks upon the earth will also see heaven.
Cultural_Context: One cannot avoid one’s destiny.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtẹ̀mákùú ò sí nÍfá
Target_Text_En: Consulting-without-ever-dying is not a fea ture of Ifá oracle.
Cultural_Context: Even the priest of Ifá is not immune from dying.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtiwáyé ò dàbí àtirọ̀run.
Target_Text_En: Coming-to-earth is nothing like going-to heaven.
Cultural_Context: Life is a pleasurable experience until one thinks of dying.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwáyé-àìkú ò sí; ẹ̀rù lásán la fi ńdá ba ara-a wa.
Target_Text_En: There is no living without dying; we only scare ourselves [with death].
Cultural_Context: Death is inevitable, and there is no point in dreading it.

Source_Text_Yo: Babaaláwo á ku; oníṣègùn á rọ̀run; adáunṣe ò níí gbélẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The diviner will die; the medicine man will go to heaven; the sorcerer will not remain forever on earth.
Cultural_Context: Death comes to all in the end.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá dàgbà, tí a gbó, bó pẹ́ títí ojú á kájọ́.
Target_Text_En: If one lives long and grows old, in time one’s eyes will encompass all.
Cultural_Context: Age is experience.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá forí sọlẹ̀ tí a kò kú, ohun tí a ó ṣe-é kù.
Target_Text_En: If one dives headfirst onto the ground and does not die, one must still have things to accomplish in life.
Cultural_Context: Providence has plans for one who fails in a suicide attempt.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ikú bá dé, kò sí l yà tó lè ṣojú ẹni.
Target_Text_En: When death comes, no lawyer can repre sent us.
Cultural_Context: We cannot hide from death behind well-wishers.

Source_Text_Yo: Ènì fẹ́ẹ́ rí òkú kó sùn; àtúnrarí dòjú àlá.
Target_Text_En: Whoever wants to see the dead should go to sleep; such encounters happen only in the realm of dreams.
Cultural_Context: Once people die, they cannot be seen again in this life.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó kú àti ẹni tó sọnù: wọ́n lè pàdé.
Target_Text_En: The dead person and the lost person: both could meet.
Cultural_Context: A person lost to his commu nity is no different from a dead person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó ó sùn-ún sàn ju ẹni tó kú lọ.
Target_Text_En: The sleeping person is better off than the dead person.
Cultural_Context: Conditions that superficially seem the same may in fact be very different; sleep is preferable to death.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹrú kú ìyá ò gbọ́; ọmọ́ kú ariwó ta
Target_Text_En: A slave dies, and the mother does not learn of the death; a freeborn dies, and lamenta tions erupt.
Cultural_Context: People are not all equal, nor are they valued equally.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹṣín ta ta ta ó kú; èèyán rìn rìn rìn ó sọnù
Target_Text_En: A horse kicks and kicks and kicks and dies; a person walks and walks and walks and gets lost.
Cultural_Context: The fate of humans, as of animals, is to keep striving until death.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbèsè nikú; kò sẹ́un tí kò níí pa.
Target_Text_En: Death is a debt; there is no one it will not kill. I
Cultural_Context: Death is a debt everyone owes and everyone must repay.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbí ò ju ìbí; bí a ti bí ẹru la ti bí ọmọ.
Target_Text_En: No birth is worthier than another; just as the slave was born, so was the scion born.
Cultural_Context: All humans start out equal.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbà mélòó làá fi ńkú? Àfi àìráyè ṣàìsàn.
Target_Text_En: How long does it take to die? The problem is not having the time to be sick.
Cultural_Context: The good thing about sudden disasters is that they are not preceded by protracted anxieties.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikán ńjẹlé àgbà ńsọ̀; àgbà náà oúnjẹ ikán.
Target_Text_En: Termites eat up the house, and the old per son complains; but the old man or woman himself or herself is food for termites.
Cultural_Context: If a certain fate awaits one, one should not make futile efforts to protect others from it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú lorúkọ àjẹ́pẹ̀kun.
Target_Text_En: Death is the name one bears at the last.
Cultural_Context: Death is everybody’s ultimate fate.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú ńpa aláwọ ẹkùn, káláwọ agílíńtí ó múra.
Target_Text_En: Death kills the person clothed in leopard skin; the person clothed in lizard skin had better prepare himself or herself.
Cultural_Context: When the mighty fall, lesser people should take heed.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú tí ńpa ojúgbà ẹni ńpòwe fúnni.
Target_Text_En: The death that kills one’s age mate is send ing one a message in proverbs.
Cultural_Context: One should learn from others’ fate.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú tó pa òwè ńpòwe fún ẹdun.
Target_Text_En: The death that killed the black monkey sends a proverbial message to the colobus monkey.
Cultural_Context: What happened to a person in a position similar to yours may well happen to you.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú tóbi lọ́ba; àrà tó wu ikú nikú ńda.
Target_Text_En: Death is a mighty king indeed; whatever it chooses to do, that it does.
Cultural_Context: There is no force that can stop death.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé ayé, à-fọwọ́-bà-fi-sílẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: This world [is] something to be handled momentarily and then let go of.
Cultural_Context: All life is ephemeral.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilẹ̀-ẹ́ mọ́, ilẹ̀-ẹ́ ṣú, ọlọjú ńkà á.
Target_Text_En: The day dawns, the day ends, and the owner of days keeps count.
Cultural_Context: Time passes relent lessly on.

Source_Text_Yo: Irun dúdú ní ńṣíwájú ewú.
Target_Text_En: Black hair is the forerunner of white hair.
Cultural_Context: Old age comes inexorably after youth.

Source_Text_Yo: Má fọ̀run yọ̀ mí; gbogbo wa la jọ ńlọ.
Target_Text_En: Do not taunt me with heading for heaven; we will all end up there eventually. O
Cultural_Context: The living should remember that they will follow the dead to heaven in the end.

Source_Text_Yo: Ogbó ò lóògùn.
Target_Text_En: Aging has no antidote.
Cultural_Context: We all grow old, willy-nilly.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjòjò kan ò lè ju tẹni tó kú.
Target_Text_En: No illness can be more grave than that of the person who died.
Cultural_Context: Some problems have no equal.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojúm mọ́ à ńyọ̀; ọjọ́ ikú ńdínkù.
Target_Text_En: The day dawns and we rejoice; one’s dying day approaches closer.
Cultural_Context: Every new day brings death closer.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkú ńsunkún òkú; akáṣọlérí ńsunkún ara-a wọn
Target_Text_En: The dead are weeping for the dead; carriers of cloth bundles are weeping for themselves [and for one another]
Cultural_Context: The survivor weeping for the dead soon dies himself or herself; death takes everybody in the end.

Source_Text_Yo: Olè ké-kè-ké ni wọ́n ńpè kúnlẹ̀; ta ní jẹ́ wí pé kí ọmọ Aríọrí ó wá sí gba-n-gba kó wá wí tirẹ̀?
Target_Text_En: Only small-time thieves are called to account on their knees; who dares summon the son of Aríọrí to come out in the open and render an account?
Cultural_Context: Small-time criminals alone are brought to book; the really big criminals go scot-free.

Source_Text_Yo: Òwú là bá gbìn, a ò gbin idẹ; òwú là bá gbìn,a ò gbìnlẹ̀kẹ̀; àtidẹ àtìlẹ̀kẹ̀, ọ̀kan kì í báni dé hòrò òkú; ọjọ́ a bá kú aṣọ ní ḿbani lọ
Target_Text_En: Cotton is what one should plant, not brass; cotton is what one should plant, not beads; as for brass and beads, neither goes with one to the grave; on the day one dies, only cloth accompanies one. Ọ
Cultural_Context: When we die, our jewelry is of no use to us.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ a bá kú là ńdère, èèyàn ò sunwọ̀n láàyè.
Target_Text_En: It is on the day one dies that one becomes an idol; no one is appreciated when alive.
Cultural_Context: People are often more glorious in death than in life.

Source_Text_Yo: The name Mákùú means ‘‘ Do not die.’’
Target_Text_En: The name Mákùú means ‘‘
Cultural_Context: Not Provided

Source_Text_Yo: The term y kú, which heads a subchapter of the Ifá divination corpus, means, roughly, ‘‘a means of deflecting death.’’ The ending bàrà expresses a mode of dodging.
Target_Text_En: The term y kú, which heads a subchapter of the Ifá divination corpus, means, roughly, ‘‘a means of deflecting death.’’ The ending bàrà expresses a mode of dodging
Cultural_Context: People are often more glorious in death than in life.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀run ò dùn; ẹni tó kú ò padà wáyé.
Target_Text_En: Heaven may turn out not to be a pleasant place, but the dead cannot come back to earth. P
Cultural_Context: Once one is dead, one is done.

Source_Text_Yo: Pá-ń-sá ilẹ̀-ẹ́ láriwo nínú; àjà-il-ẹ̀-ẹ́ ba àgbà lẹ́rù.
Target_Text_En: A tomb is attended by crying; a grave strikes human nature terror into elderly people.
Cultural_Context: People are always sobered by reminders of their mortality.

Source_Text_Yo: Tikú tikú là ńro àgbà; àgbà ní ńpète àìkú.
Target_Text_En: People always look at aged people with death in their eyes; the aged are the ones who strive to stay alive. On inscrutability A
Cultural_Context: Each person is the most reliable guardian of his or her own well-being.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í kọ́ni níkà bí a ò bá níká nínú; ta ní ńkọ́ni ká ṣe rere?
Target_Text_En: Nobody teaches one to be wicked if one does not have wickedness in one; whoever teaches one to be good?
Cultural_Context: Goodness and wickedness are not learned but are part of one’s nature.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í mọ̀ràn mọ̀ràn ká mọ oyún ìgbín nínu ìkaraun.
Target_Text_En: One is never so knowledgeable that one can detect the pregnancy of a snail in its shell.
Cultural_Context: Certain things are beyond the ken of even the wisest of people.

Source_Text_Yo: A mọ aláré, a mọ eléki; aláṣìsọ ló kù.
Target_Text_En: The entertainer we know; the praise singer we know; the misspeaker is all that is left.
Cultural_Context: There is no doubt about the intentions of the entertainer and the praise singer, but there may be doubt about the intentions of a person whose utterances are offensive.

Source_Text_Yo: À ńjọ- rìn, a kò mọ orí olówó.
Target_Text_En: Though we might travel as a group, we do not know who is destined to prosper.
Cultural_Context: No one can tell who among a company is most likely to succeed.

Source_Text_Yo: A ò mọ ẹsẹ̀ òṣìkà lọ́nà.
Target_Text_En: One cannot tell who is wicked by his or her footprint.
Cultural_Context: By their deeds they shall be known.

Source_Text_Yo: Abínú ẹní foore ṣegi nígbó; ó ní kẹ́ranko mu jẹ.
Target_Text_En: He who wants no good for one does a favor for trees in the forest; he invites animals to share the favor.
Cultural_Context: Expect no favors from an enemy.

Source_Text_Yo: Afiniṣe kì í jẹ́ ká fòun ṣe.
Target_Text_En: He-who-exploits-others never permits him self to be exploited.
Cultural_Context: The evil person is always on his guard.

Source_Text_Yo: Ahun ḿmí; igbá ẹ̀hín-in rẹ̀ ni ó jẹ kà mọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The tortoise breathes; only its shell con ceals the fact.
Cultural_Context: Whatever appearances might be, no human is essentially different from another.

Source_Text_Yo: Ahùwà-ìbàjẹ́ sẹ bí tòun là ńwí; aṣe burúkú o kú ara fífun.
Target_Text_En: The person of evil character thinks he is the subject of discussion; the evildoer is plagued by suspiciousness.
Cultural_Context: Evil acts breed uneasy consciences.

Source_Text_Yo: Ara la mọ̀, a ò mọ inú.
Target_Text_En: It is the body that one knows; one does not know what lies inside.
Cultural_Context: No one can see into the mind of another.

Source_Text_Yo: A-sáré-ṣá-ṣá-nínú- gún ò sá lásán; bí kò lé nǹkan, nǹkan ńlé e.
Target_Text_En: One-who-runs-wildly-through-a-thorn-bush does not run for no reason; if he or she is not after something, something is after him or her.
Cultural_Context: A person who behaves in an unusual manner must have some reason.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣọ̀ràn ní ńṣe aájò.
Target_Text_En: The guilty person is the one who commis erates.
Cultural_Context: The guilty person often tries to conceal his or her culpability by being the most solicitous.

Source_Text_Yo: A-ṣọ̀ràn-ìbàjẹ́ ṣe bí tòun là ńwí; a-ṣe búburú o kú ara fífun.
Target_Text_En: The-person-who-has-done-something-bad thinks people are discussing him or her; evildoer, we acknowledge your guilty con science.
Cultural_Context: A guilty conscience is an uneasy conscience.

Source_Text_Yo: Awọ fẹ́ẹ́rẹ́ bo inú, kò jẹ́ ká rí ikùn aṣẹni
Target_Text_En: A thin skin covers the stomach and prevents one from seeing inside the evildoer.
Cultural_Context: One cannot tell friends from enemies simply by looking at them.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayé lòkun, èèyàn l sà; a kì í m - w ká káyéjá.
Target_Text_En: The world is a sea, and the people in it are a lagoon; no matter how well one knows how to swim, one cannot swim the world. B
Cultural_Context: The world and the people in it are as dangerous as the sea; no matter what one does, one cannot be entirely safe from them.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá gúnyán fún Kòníífẹ́, kò níí fẹ́; bí a bá rokà fún Kòníífẹ́, kò níí fẹ́.
Target_Text_En: If one makes pounded yams for Kònííf [meaning ‘‘He-will-not-like-it’’], he will not like it; if one cooks yam-powder meal for Kònííf , he will not like it.
Cultural_Context: There is no pleasing a grouch.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá tẹ̀lé wèrè, a kì í mọ ilé tí yó wọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Unless one follows an imbecile, one does not know which house he will enter.
Cultural_Context: There is no anticipating an unpredictable person.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí àlẹ́ yó ṣe rí, ówọ ẹlẹdàá ló wà.
Target_Text_En: What the evening of life will be like is in the hands of the Creator.
Cultural_Context: Only God knows how one’s life will end.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí aráyé bá ṣìkà tán, wọn a tún báni dárò.
Target_Text_En: After people have acted wickedly, they then sympathize with their victims.
Cultural_Context: People are not to be trusted.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí inú kò bá ní odì, odì a nínú.
Target_Text_En: Even if one’s mind harbors no enmity, one’s enemy keeps one in mind.
Cultural_Context: You may harbor no ill will toward others, but others may harbor ill will toward you.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí o ní iyùn, ní èjìgbà, tí o ní sẹ̀gi pẹ̀lú, ata wẹ́ẹ́rẹ́ ni lójú abúni
Target_Text_En: If you have iyùn beads and have èjìgbà beads, even iyùn beads also, they are all like small peppers to the detractor.[?]D
Cultural_Context: Nothing one has or does impresses one’s detractor.

Source_Text_Yo: Dẹ̀ǹgẹ́ tutù lẹ́hìn, ó gbóná nínú
Target_Text_En: Maize porridge is cool on top but steaming hot inside.
Cultural_Context: A person who appears docile may be a firebrand underneath.

Source_Text_Yo: Dùlúmọ̀ ẹ̀pà lọ́rùn-un sèsé: ajẹ̀bi-ọ̀ràn-wò tiiri.
Target_Text_En: Sèsé beans cause trouble for peanuts: the-guilty-one-that-wears-an-innocent-look
Cultural_Context: The person who drags others into trouble is often adept at escaping the responsibility.

Source_Text_Yo: Èéfín nìwà; kò ṣé-é bò mọ́ra.
Target_Text_En: Character is smoke; one cannot conceal it under one’s clothing.
Cultural_Context: Character will show.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèyàn ìbá ṣe bí Ọl run kò bunni lómi mu.
Target_Text_En: Were man in the same position as God, he would not provide humans with water to drink.
Cultural_Context: Trust placed in human goodness is trust misplaced.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèyàn ńwojú; Ọlọ́run ńwọkàn.
Target_Text_En: Human beings keep their gaze on the face; God looks into the heart.
Cultural_Context: Human beings can see only what a face reveals; only God know what is in the heart.

Source_Text_Yo: Èké ò pe ara-a r lórúkọ; ìkà ò pe ara-a rẹ̀ níkà.
Target_Text_En: The devious person does not call himself or herself devious; the wicked person does not call himself or herself wicked.
Cultural_Context: Evil people do not admit being evil.

Source_Text_Yo: Èkúté ilé ò fibi àjà han ara wọn.
Target_Text_En: House mice do not point the way to the rafters to one another.
Cultural_Context: Each person for himself or herself.

Source_Text_Yo: Eléte ò pá a lójú ẹni; ẹ̀hìn ẹni là ńgbìmọ̀ràn ìkà.
Target_Text_En: Plotters do not hatch their plots in one’s presence; evil plots are hatched when the victim is not about. Ẹ
Cultural_Context: One is always in the dark about one’s enemies’ machinations.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni à bá ní kó kínni lẹ́hìn-ín fẹ̀gún sọ́wọ́; ẹni à bá ní kó fẹ́ni lójú fata sẹ́nu
Target_Text_En: The person one would ask to scratch one’s back fills his hand with thorns; the person one would ask to blow into one’s eyes fills his mouth with pepper.
Cultural_Context: Those in whom one would wish to place one’s trust are not to be trusted.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni a fẹ́ ila mọ̀; a ò mọ ẹni ó fẹ́nì.
Target_Text_En: We know only those we love; we know not who loves us.
Cultural_Context: We know our disposition toward others, not their disposition toward us.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni a ní ká fẹ̀hìntì ká mú dídùn ọsàn, kí kan ní ńka fúnni mú.
Target_Text_En: The person one hoped to lean upon to eat the sweetest of oranges plucks only sour oranges for one to eat.
Cultural_Context: It is courting disappointment to place one’s hope in other people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní réjò ńsá; ejò ńsá.
Target_Text_En: The person who sees a snake flees; the snake also flees.
Cultural_Context: Two adversaries confront each other, but neither has the will to make a move.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a bá pète àti ra ẹṣin ní ńfọsọni di olóko ẹṣin.
Target_Text_En: The person with whom one plans to buy a horse is the same person scheming to trade one for a horse.
Cultural_Context: Presumed friends may turn out to be deadly enemies.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó rí ojú ikún m pé yó jẹ oko.
Target_Text_En: Whoever looks at the face of the squirrel will know that it will eat farm crops.
Cultural_Context: If one studies people well, one can predict what they are capable of.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tobìnrin ò kí lọ̀rẹ́-ẹ rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is the person a woman does not greet that is her lover.
Cultural_Context: A woman’s behavior toward a man often belies her true feelings for him.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu èèyàn lẹbọ.
Target_Text_En: People’s mouths are the things to offer sacri fices to.
Cultural_Context: One need fear nothing as much as what people say.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu kò jẹun kan mọ, tí yó sọ ọ̀rọ̀ kan mọ.
Target_Text_En: The mouth is not limited to one type of food or one type of speech.
Cultural_Context: One cannot be certain of what the mouth will say; a tool may be used for more than one task.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹsẹ̀ gìrì-gìrì nílé àńjọ̀fẹ́; ọ̀fẹ́ tán, ẹsẹ̀-ẹ́ sì dá.
Target_Text_En: Thundering footsteps in the home of free gifts: the free gifts are all gone, and the foot steps cease.
Cultural_Context: People will congregate around a person who has a lot to give but only as long as he or she has something left to give.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbogbo lodì; bóo lówó odì, gbogbo lodì; bóò lówó odì.
Target_Text_En: Everything can incite enmity: if you have money, you incite enmity; all things can in cite enmity: if you lack money, you incite enmity.
Cultural_Context: There is no pleasing people; whatever one is or does can earn one enemies.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi ajá la ti ḿmọ oǹrorò àpọ́n.
Target_Text_En: It is from his treatment of his dog that one can tell which unmarried man will be a terror to live with.
Cultural_Context: One can tell much about a person’s character from how he or she acts with regard to seemingly inconsequential matters.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi tí Ng-ó-pa-á-gbé ḿbẹ, ibẹ̀ ni Ng-ó gbà-á sì wà.
Target_Text_En: Where one finds I-will-kill-him-for-sure, even there too will one find I-will-save-him.
Cultural_Context: Just as there are people who bear one ill will, so there are those who have good will toward one.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé bo ilé lójú; òrùlé bo àjà mò; awọ fífiróbo inú kò jẹ́ ríkùn aṣẹni.
Target_Text_En: One house obscures another; the roof con ceals the ceiling; a thin layer of skin covers the stomach, making it impossible to see inside the evildoer.
Cultural_Context: One cannot discern a person’s character by simply looking.

Source_Text_Yo: Inú ìkòkò dúdú lẹ̀kọ funfún ti ńjáde.
Target_Text_En: It is from the black pot that the white corn meal comes.
Cultural_Context: An evil person may sire a good person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣọ̀ràn ni ìṣe aájò.
Target_Text_En: The extent of one’s culpability is the ex tent of one’s commiseration. N
Cultural_Context: The person secretly responsible for a disaster is often the one who shows the greatest sympathy and concern.

Source_Text_Yo: Ní ọj eré là ńjiyàn ohun.
Target_Text_En: It is at play that one argues about weighty issues.
Cultural_Context: Playful arguments sometimes hide deadly serious disagreements.

Source_Text_Yo: Òbírípo layé; ìmùlẹ̀ ọ̀rẹ́ máa dà.
Target_Text_En: Life is something that goes in cycles; sworn friends do become enemies.
Cultural_Context: There is no condition that cannot change.

Source_Text_Yo: Odídẹrẹ́ kì í rí ojú atùkó.
Target_Text_En: The parrot never sees the face of the per son who plucks its tail feather.
Cultural_Context: One seldom knows the identity of one’s enemies and detractors.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojúbánirẹ́ ò dékùn ẹni; aṣhìndeni ò wọ́pọ̀; ṣàṣà èèyàn ní ńfẹ́ni lẹ́hìn bí a ò sí nílé; tajá tẹran ní ńfẹ́ni lójú ẹni.
Target_Text_En: Outward expression of love does not come from within; people who will look after others’ interests in their absence are few; only a few people love one when one is absent, though every dog and goat loves a person in his presence.
Cultural_Context: One cannot trust that those who love one in one’s presence will love one when one is absent.

Source_Text_Yo: Omi inú-u kàn-ǹ-ga: kò ṣéé dúró mu, kò ṣéé bẹ̀rẹ̀ mu.
Target_Text_En: The water in a well: one cannot stand and reach it to drink, neither can one stoop to reach it.
Cultural_Context: Some problems are so difficult as almost to defy solution.

Source_Text_Yo: Oníkùn ló mkà; oníbàǹtẹ́ ló moye òun-ún dì sí i.
Target_Text_En: The owner of the stomach alone knows what wickedness lurks inside; the owner of the loin money pouch alone knows how much money she has tied up in it.
Cultural_Context: No one knows what secret lies buried inside other people.

Source_Text_Yo: Oníkùn ló mọ̀kà; jẹun ló mọwọ́-ọ́ lá.
Target_Text_En: Only the owner of the stomach knows how he will practice wickedness; only the person eating knows how to lick his fingers.
Cultural_Context: One should not from a position of ignorance at tempt to second-guess a person who has all the information and the initiative.

Source_Text_Yo: Onítìjú ẹni lobìnrin ẹni.
Target_Text_En: The woman who is coy in one’s presence is the one destined to be one’s wife.
Cultural_Context: People’s interractions in public often give away their private relationships.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí aṣẹgítà-á lè yí bìrí kó di ọlórọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The fortune of the seller of firewood might suddenly change, and he or she might be come prosperous.
Cultural_Context: Fortune is likely to change unexpectedly.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí ò mọ ibùsùn; ì-bá mọ̀ ọ́ a tún ilẹ̀ ibẹ̀ ṣe.
Target_Text_En: The head does not know where it will even tually rest in sleep; had it known, it would have tidied up the place.
Cultural_Context: If one knew where one’s destiny would lead, one would do whatever one could to cultivate the place.

Source_Text_Yo: Orúkọ mẹ́ta là ńpèyàwó: Ọlọ́rùn-lẹ́lẹ́; Ọlá-yọ́kọ-sílẹ̀; Ọlá-bọ́kọ-lọ.
Target_Text_En: Anewwife has three names: Ọlọ́rùnlẹ́lẹ́ [She of the slender neck]; Ọláyọ́kọsílẹ̀ [She who sneaks off, leaving the husband behind]; Ọlábọ́kọlọ [She who goes with her husband].
Cultural_Context: One cannot predict the actions of a beautiful wife; she may sneak off with other men, but, again, she may remain faithful to her husband.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrùlé bo àjà mọ́lẹ̀; aṣọ́ bo ẹsẹ ìdí; awọ fẹ́ẹ́rẹ́ bonú kò jẹ́ ríkùn aṣeni.
Target_Text_En: The roof covers the ceiling; the cloth covers the buttocks; a thin layer of skin covers the stomach and prevents one from seeing in side a wicked person. Ọ
Cultural_Context: Nobody knows what wickedness lurks inside others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀làjà ò pọ̀ bí amújàwú.
Target_Text_En: Quarrel settlers are not as plentiful as quarrel aggravators.
Cultural_Context: People are more likely to add to your troubles than help you end them.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pẹ̀ òyìnbó fi dídùn ṣẹwà, ó fẹ̀gún bora, oró inú egbèje.
Target_Text_En: The pineapple derives its beauty from sweetness; the wickednesses [dangerous spines on the leaves] it harbors
Cultural_Context: What is beautiful may be deadly also

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀ṣọ̀ọ̀rọ̀ tó mú ajá: owó ẹ̀kọ olúwa ẹ̀ ló dínkù.
Target_Text_En: The dysentry that attacks a dog saves its owner the cost of providing corn meal for it.
Cultural_Context: Every misfortune has its positive aspect.

Source_Text_Yo: "Pẹ̀lẹ́", lákọ, ó lábo.
Target_Text_En: "Take it easy’’ can be either masculine or feminine.
Cultural_Context: Even a greeting or word of cau tion can be said in either an aggressive or a placatory manner.

Source_Text_Yo: Pọ̀ọ̀kọ́ nídìí, ó fìhà jókòó.
Target_Text_En: The coconut shell has a bottom but rests on its side.
Cultural_Context: Unconventional people will always do things differently.

Source_Text_Yo: A gb pé ẹj ọmọdé jàre ná; ó ku ẹni ti yó bàá a wí i.
Target_Text_En: Let us grant that the youth has a just claim, but who will press it for him?
Cultural_Context: The culture favors age over youth, even when youth is in the right.

Source_Text_Yo: A gbọ́ tajá, a gbọ́ tẹran; èwo ni tàgùntàn lórí àga?
Target_Text_En: A dog, yes, even a goat, yes; but who ever heard of a sheep sitting on a chair?
Cultural_Context: One can be flexible and grant exceptions to certain individuals from a prohibition, but there is a point beyond which one refuses to go.

Source_Text_Yo: À ńjọ- rìn, a kò jọ ara wa.
Target_Text_En: Though we travel in the same group, we are not therefore alike.
Cultural_Context: Everybody in a group is unique.

Source_Text_Yo: À ńjù wò nò ṣéé wí lójè ; ìjà ìlara ò tán bọ̀rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: We are driven by envy of them’’ is not a good case to make; a quarrel born of jealousy does not end easily
Cultural_Context: Jealousy is a difficult motive to acknowledge.

Source_Text_Yo: Ààfáà bọ̀rọ̀kìnní: bí Ọlọ́run ò bá ṣeni lágbà, a kì í fìyànjú ṣe bí àgbà.
Target_Text_En: Wealthy, famous Muslim priest: if God has not made one an elder, one does not become one simply by striving.
Cultural_Context: The achievement of status is a gift from God. Certain things are out of human hands.

Source_Text_Yo: Ààfáà-á jóná, ẹ̀ ḿbèrè irùgbọ̀n; kí ló fa sábàbí?
Target_Text_En: The Muslim priest is consumed in a fire, and you ask about his beard; what do you think was the cause of the problem?
Cultural_Context: When the mighty fall, it is idle to wonder what hap pened to lesser beings.

Source_Text_Yo: Àáké wọ igbo, a gbọ́ òkìkí.
Target_Text_En: The axe enters into a forest, and we hear reports of its doings.
Cultural_Context: When an illustrious person acts, his deeds are noised about.

Source_Text_Yo: Áásìkí tí a fún ẹyẹ sìn a ò fún igún; áásìkí ẹrú ò sí lọ́dọ̀ ọmọ.
Target_Text_En: The regard that a domestic bird enjoys is de nied the vulture; the regard a slave receives is not the same as a freeborn enjoys.
Cultural_Context: People are not uniformly fortunate.

Source_Text_Yo: Àáyá ní ohun tí a bá mọ̀-ọ́ ṣe, bí ẹní ńṣeré ni; ó ni bí òún bá ńlọ lóko ẹ̀pà, ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan a máa b sí òun lẹ́nu.
Target_Text_En: The colobus monkey says that one’s spe cialty is like child’s play; it says that when it walks through a peanut farm, peanuts con tinually pop into its mouth.
Cultural_Context: Some chores are ridiculously easy, sometimes even suspi ciously easy, especially for the expert.

Source_Text_Yo: Àdá lẹnu tálákà; igbó la ó fi ṣán.
Target_Text_En: The poor person’s mouth is a machete; its use is to clear the bush.
Cultural_Context: A poor person’s voice carries no weight.

Source_Text_Yo: Àdàbà ò jẹ̀pà; kanna-kánná ò jẹ sèsé.
Target_Text_En: The dove does not eat peanuts; the crow does not eat yam beans.
Cultural_Context: To each its dis likes.

Source_Text_Yo: Afínjú ò dóko; òjòwú ò dígbèsè; òmúmurà ni yó bọ́kọ-ọ rẹ̀ dálè.
Target_Text_En: The preener does not go to the farm; the jealous woman does not get into debt; it is a woman with forbearance that finds a concu bine for her husband.
Cultural_Context: Different people have different habits and qualities.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgún-ì-jẹ ní ńpa ẹrú.
Target_Text_En: Pounding-[food]-without-partaking-of-it is the death of the slave.
Cultural_Context: The slave’s labor is not unheard of, but he derives no benefit from it.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà lẹ́tù; àlàárì lọba aṣọ
Target_Text_En: The ẹtù cloth is the elder; the reddish dyed cloth is the king of cloths.
Cultural_Context: There is a hierarchy even in the textile realm.

Source_Text_Yo: Agbára odó kò jọ agbára ìkòkò; bí a gbé odó kaná a jó; bí a sì gúnyán nínú ìkòkò a lu.
Target_Text_En: The strength of the mortar is not similar to the strength of the pot; if one places a mortar on the fire, it burns; if one pounds yams in a pot, it breaks.
Cultural_Context: To each his or her particular qualities.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbò méjì kì í mumi nínú-u koto kan.
Target_Text_En: Two rams cannot drink [at the same time] from the same water pot.
Cultural_Context: Two masters can not coexist in the same household.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbò méjì kì í pàdé lórí afárá.
Target_Text_En: Two rams will not meet on a narrow bridge.
Cultural_Context: Two contrary and uncompromising forces will never come to an accommodation.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìjẹunsùn àkàlàmàgbò, a ò lè fi wé ti àtíòro
Target_Text_En: Àkàlàmàgbò’s lack of supper is not comparable to that of àtíòro
Cultural_Context: A noble person’s poverty is not the same as an ordinary person’s.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìjẹunsùn ẹkùn, a ò lè fi wé ti ajá.
Target_Text_En: The leopard’s lack of supper is not compa rable to that of the dog.
Cultural_Context: A powerful person’s setback does not make him the equal of a nobody.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìlọ́ràá àkàlàmàgbò, a ò lè fi wé ti àtíòro.
Target_Text_En: The ground hornbill’s lack of fat is not to be compared with that of the allied hornbill.
Cultural_Context: A renowned person’s inconvenience does not make him the equal of a peon.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìlọ́ràá ògòǹgò, a ò lè fi wé ti agílítí.
Target_Text_En: The ostrich’s lack of fat is not to be com pared with that of the lizard.
Cultural_Context: A rich person’s lack of ready cash does not make him the equal of a poverty-stricken person.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìmọ̀ọ́jó là ńtàkìtì; ijó-ò mí ju àńtọ bọ́.
Target_Text_En: It is deficiency as a dancer that induces one to somersault; my dancing goes beyond cartwheeling.
Cultural_Context: Overexertion betrays a lack of competence.

Source_Text_Yo: Àì-rí-ońjẹ-jẹ ológbò kọ́ ni kò fi tó ajá.
Target_Text_En: It is not the cat’s failure to find food that makes it smaller than a dog.
Cultural_Context: Great size is not a measure of one’s striving.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjà ló lẹrù irọ́ ni pẹpẹ ńpa.
Target_Text_En: To the rafter belongs the load; the shelf is a mere pretender.
Cultural_Context: Others may strive, but only certain special people have the means to carry out a task.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjànàkú kúrò lẹ́ran à ńfajá dẹ.
Target_Text_En: The elephant is beyond the sort of animal one hunts with a dog.
Cultural_Context: One should not approach formidable tasks with levity.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjànàkú ló nìgbọẹ́; irọ́ ni gbogbo ẹranko ńpa.
Target_Text_En: To the elephant belongs the forest; all other animals are mere pretenders.
Cultural_Context: There is no disputing a person’s preeminence. .

Source_Text_Yo: Àjẹkùlóko àgb lọba ńjẹ lórí itẹ́.
Target_Text_En: It is the leavings from the farmer’s farm table that the king eats on his throne.
Cultural_Context: Each profession fills a unique need.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjùlọ ò pin s d ẹnìkan.
Target_Text_En: Preeminence does not end with any one person.
Cultural_Context: No one has a corner on excellence.

Source_Text_Yo: Akàn-án ní òún dúpẹ́ àìlórí; gbogbo ẹní lórí lorí ńfọ́.
Target_Text_En: The crab says it gives thanks that it lacks a head, for whoever has a head also suffers headaches.
Cultural_Context: There is no adversity without its positive aspect.

Source_Text_Yo: Akíkanjú wọgbó, o ṣòwò igba èèyàn.
Target_Text_En: An illustrious person enters the forest and does enough trade for two hundred people.
Cultural_Context: One illustrious person accomplishes enough for many ordinary people.

Source_Text_Yo: Akíni-kúuṣẹ́ ńjiyán yó; apòyì-kábà ńyá ìwọ̀fà; olóko ńpa ẹgbàa-gbẹdógún kó tó jẹun.
Target_Text_En: The person who greets one while one is working eats pounded yams to his fill; the person who perambulates around the hut employs a pawn; the farmer himself must earn 15,000 cowries before he can eat.
Cultural_Context: Idlers and hangers-on have the easiest of times, whereas a person working for his living must eat of his sweat.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkókó kun osùn ó kun orí; arèré kun osùn ó kun àyà; olóbùró kun osùn ó kun ọ̀fun
Target_Text_En: The woodpecker takes camwood and stains its head; the custard-apple tree takes cam wood and stains its breast; olóbùró takes camwood and stains its throat.
Cultural_Context: Each has a different notion of self-adornment.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkùkọ ńlá ó jọkí kékeré ó kọ.
Target_Text_En: The big rooster prevents the small rooster from crowing.
Cultural_Context: Those in authority prevent their subordinates from asserting them selves.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkùkọ́ tó lógbe ò ní ìreré; èyí tó ní ìreré ò ní ọ̀gàn.
Target_Text_En: The cock that has a comb lacks tail plumes; the one that has tail plumes lacks spurs.
Cultural_Context: Every person has his or her failings.

Source_Text_Yo: Aláǹgbá ọ̀jọ nì, agbára wọn ló yàtọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The lizard resembles the crocodile; it is their strength that is different.
Cultural_Context: Look-alikes are not necessarily equals.

Source_Text_Yo: Àlùkéḿbù, baba asa.
Target_Text_En: Stirrup, father of the saddle.
Cultural_Context: The stirrup is more important than the saddle.

Source_Text_Yo: Àlùmọ́nì méjì kì í gbé ọwọ́ ẹnìkan.
Target_Text_En: Two treasures will not reside with one per son.
Cultural_Context: A person cannot have everything.

Source_Text_Yo: Àpọ́n sàn ju okóbó pàtítí àpọ́n yó fẹ̀ẹ́ ọbìnrin.
Target_Text_En: A bachelor is better off than a eunuch; sooner or later a bachelor will take a wife.
Cultural_Context: Some ills are better than others.

Source_Text_Yo: Àrùn mìíràn-án kù lẹ́hìn-in wárápá; wárápá nìkan kọ́ ní ńgbéni ṣánl.
Target_Text_En: There are other diseases besides epilepsy; it is not only epilepsy that knocks people to the floor.
Cultural_Context: Nothing and no one can claim to be the ultimate in any regard.

Source_Text_Yo: Àrùn òtòṣì ní ńsàn lóòjọ́; tolówó a máa sàn díẹ̀-díẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is a poor person’s disease that is cured in a day; a rich person’s disease mends only gradually.
Cultural_Context: Protracted illness is too great a luxury for a poor person to afford.

Source_Text_Yo: This is a response to the proverb Ibi tí lékèélékèé ti ńfọṣọ, Ọl run ò fi ib han ọmọ àparò (‘‘ The place where the egret washes its clothes, God has kept hidden from the clan of partridges’’). nature
Target_Text_En: This is a response to the proverb Ibi tí lékèélékèé ti ńfọṣọ, Ọl run ò fi ib han ọmọ àparò (‘‘
Cultural_Context: Not Provided

Source_Text_Yo: Àrùn tí ńṣe aláárùn-únò ṣe ẹlẹ́ẹ́ta.
Target_Text_En: The disease that attacks the person with five does not attack the person with three.
Cultural_Context: Each person with his or her own prob lems.

Source_Text_Yo: Àrùn tí ńṣọ̀bọ ò ṣegún: igún pá lórí; ọ̀bọ́ hùrù.
Target_Text_En: The disease that afflicts the monkey does not afflict the vulture: the vulture is bald on its head; the monkey grows a tail.
Cultural_Context: Different people, different aches.

Source_Text_Yo: Àrùn tí ńṣọ̀bọ ò ṣegún: igún pá lórí; ọ̀bọ́ pá nídìí.
Target_Text_En: The disease that afflicts the monkey does not afflict the vulture: the vulture is bald on its head; the monkey is bald on its buttocks.
Cultural_Context: Different problems for different people.

Source_Text_Yo: Àsísorí ò ní ikùn bí àgbá; òtòṣì ò lówó bí ọlọ́rọ̀
Target_Text_En: A pistol does not have a bore like a cannon’s; a poor person does not have the money of a wealthy person.
Cultural_Context: There is no equality in people’s fortunes.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣọ abilà gbogbo ló lórúkọ.
Target_Text_En: Every striped cloth has a name.
Cultural_Context: Every person has a name; an offender has a name to be mentioned.

Source_Text_Yo: Àti kékeré àjànàkú leerin-ín ti pọ̀ ju ẹfọ̀n lọ.
Target_Text_En: It is from childhood that the elephant was greater than the buffalo.
Cultural_Context: Regardless of age, an elephant is greater than a buffalo.

Source_Text_Yo: Àti ogún ọdún tí ẹ̀kọ́ ti ńlo aṣọ, ìhòòhò làkàrà-á wà.
Target_Text_En: In the twenty years that the corn meal has been wearing clothes, the bean fritters have always been naked.
Cultural_Context: One’s better standing than one’s rival’s is not a recent development.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwa ara wa la ríra-a wa: ológìnní rí ọmọ ẹkùn.
Target_Text_En: All of us assembled here are of a type; the cat comes face to face with the offspring of the leopard.
Cultural_Context: When equals come together, none has anything to fear from any other.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwòròṣàṣà ní ńjẹ ajá Ògún
Target_Text_En: Only the most powerful of priests eats dogs sacrificed to Ògún.[?]B
Cultural_Context: Only a select few can perform formidable tasks.

Source_Text_Yo: Bákan-náà lọmọ ńṣorí lẹ́hìn ìyá-a rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Babies’ heads lie the same way on their mothers’ backs.
Cultural_Context: Natural habits die hard. Also, one baby is no different from another baby.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá bi àgbà tó kúrú mọ́lẹ̀, yóò rí wí.
Target_Text_En: If one asks the elder that is short and close to the ground, he will have something to say.
Cultural_Context: There is always an explanation for a person’s condition, if we will only ask.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí alákẹdun-ún bá rá; tó fọwọ́ ṣẹ́; agbọ̀n la ó fi kó ọmọ òwè níbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: If the colobus monkey breaks its arm while suspended from a tree, it is by the basket ful that black monkeys will be scooped off the place.
Cultural_Context: When an expert comes to grief doing something, novices will fail at it in their hundreds.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ehoro ò lè sáré bí ìgalà, bíi ká fi wé ti ìjàpá kọ́.
Target_Text_En: If a rabbit cannot run as fast as the deer, that does not make it comparable to a tortoise.
Cultural_Context: One’s worth depends on the standard by which one is judged.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí igbá bá wọ odò a lé té-ń-té.
Target_Text_En: If a calabash falls into the stream, it floats on top.
Cultural_Context: Nothing can prevent the illustrious person from shining.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí inú ti ḿbí àjànàkú, bẹ́ẹ̀ ti ḿbí eèrà.
Target_Text_En: Just as the elephant may be angered, so an ant may be angered.
Cultural_Context: Even the least of people has feelings.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí iyán ti ńfún lóko ẹgàn, bẹ́ẹ̀ náà ní ńfún ní ti etílé.
Target_Text_En: As pounded yam is white on a farm deep in the forest, so it is white on the farm near the town.
Cultural_Context: A commodity does not change its nature according to its location.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí lékèélékèé ò bá rómi wẹ̀, a dégbẹ́ àparò.
Target_Text_En: If the egret cannot find water to bathe in, it becomes like the partridge.
Cultural_Context: When a great person loses his resources, he becomes like ordinary people.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí Olúgbọ́n ti gbọ́n, bẹ́ẹ̀ ni Arẹsà-á gbọ́n pèlú
Target_Text_En: As the Olúgbọ́n is clever, so also is the Arẹsà clever.
Cultural_Context: Each person is wise in his or her own way.

Source_Text_Yo: Bó ti ḿbẹ lára adẹ́bọ, bẹ́ẹ̀ ní ḿbẹ lára a-dá-má-rùú.
Target_Text_En: As it is with the person who offers a sacrifice, so it is with the person who refuses to make a sacrifice.
Cultural_Context: Each person makes his or her own choice and also bears the consequences.

Source_Text_Yo: Bó ti wà ní Líkí, b ní ḿbẹ ní Gbà-ǹ- ja
Target_Text_En: As it is in Líkí, so it is in Gbàǹja.
Cultural_Context: Matters are fundamentally the same everywhere.

Source_Text_Yo: Bó ti wá ni yó lọ; ọ̀gbẹ̀rì ò jẹ iyán odù
Target_Text_En: As he came, so will he depart; the uninitiated person will not eat the pounded yams of Ifá.
Cultural_Context: An outsider will not be included in the benefits of exclusive groups.

Source_Text_Yo: Bọ́mọdé bá ní okun tó ọ̀bọ, kò lè ní gèlètè àyà-a rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Even though a youth has as much strength as a monkey, he cannot have a chest as huge as the monkey’s.
Cultural_Context: A person who is a match for another in one regard may be deficient in others.

Source_Text_Yo: Bọ̀rọ̀kìnní ba ọlọrí nínú jẹ.
Target_Text_En: The person of exemplary character angers the rich person.
Cultural_Context: People do not admire those who steal the show from them.

Source_Text_Yo: Bọ̀rọ̀kìnní ìletò ni akéde ìlú ńlá.
Target_Text_En: The celebrated dandy in the village is a street crier in a large town.
Cultural_Context: When people are few, anybody may be important.

Source_Text_Yo: Dúdú lẹ̀gbọ́n, pupa làbúrò.
Target_Text_En: Black is the elder; light brown is the younger. E
Cultural_Context: A dark complexion is more desirable than a light one.

Source_Text_Yo: Erèé òtòṣì lọlọ́rọ̀- fi ńṣe èkuru jẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is of the poor person’s beans that the rich man makes bean meal to eat.
Cultural_Context: The rich will take from the poor the little they have.

Source_Text_Yo: Erin ibòmín-ìn, ẹ̀lírí ibomín-ìn.
Target_Text_En: An elephant in one place; a tiny mouse in another.
Cultural_Context: What people make much of in one place is of no account in another.

Source_Text_Yo: Erín ńtú eruku; ẹfọ̀n ńtú eruku; títú eruku àjànàkú bo tẹfọ̀n mọ́lẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The elephant raises a cloud of dust; the buf falo raises a cloud of dust; the elephant’s ability to raise dust far surpasses the buf falo’s.
Cultural_Context: Certain people or things are beyond all competition.

Source_Text_Yo: Ogbè lèyí ló gbogbo ènìyàn.
Target_Text_En: Some people are more fortunate than others.)
Cultural_Context: Not Provided

Source_Text_Yo: Eṣinṣín kọ ikú àpàbẹrí; yànmù-yánmú kọ ikú àpàlàdọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The fly is immune to death by beheading; the mosquito is immune to death caused by the splitting of the liver.
Cultural_Context: Some fates are impossible for some people or things.

Source_Text_Yo: Èsúó ti ńlògbà kéwúrẹ́ tó dáyé.
Target_Text_En: The red-flanked ducker was already enjoying life before the goat came into being.
Cultural_Context: A person or thing was already long established before the upstart came about.

Source_Text_Yo: Ewé ńlá kì í rú wẹ́wẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Large leaves do not sprout small.
Cultural_Context: A person destined to be great will not fail to be great.

Source_Text_Yo: Èwo ni kò tó ‘‘Hì hì’’ lára ìnàkí?
Target_Text_En: What baboon is incapable of sounding ‘‘Hee hee’’?
Cultural_Context: Certain things are within the capability of everyone.

Source_Text_Yo: Ewúrẹ́ ilé ò mọdẹ; ìbá ṣàgbọ̀nrín a gbọfà lẹ́hìn ṣan-ṣan.
Target_Text_En: The domesticated goat has no regard for the hunter; were it a deer it would sport arrows prominently on its back. Ẹ
Cultural_Context: As the domestic goat’s protected status makes it misbehave when a hunter is around, so a sheltered per son gets away with much that less fortunate people dare not attempt.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀fúùfù gbé ológì lọ; oníyẹ̀fun ni ègbè yàn yàn.
Target_Text_En: The wind blows away the corn-gruel seller; the seller of corn powder is hopelessly doomed.
Cultural_Context: When illustrious ones fall, lesser people have no hope.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀gún ò gún ọmọ lẹ́sẹ̀ ká yọ lọjú ẹrú.
Target_Text_En: When a thorn lodges in the foot of a child, one does not remove it from a slave’s foot.
Cultural_Context: However privileged one might be, there are certain things one must do oneself.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̄gbẹ́ erín ò wón lálọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The equal of an elephant is not difficult to find in Álọ̀.
Cultural_Context: There is little difficulty in finding a substitute for a common thing or an ordinary person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ègbẹ́ ìṣu kọ́ niyán.
Target_Text_En: The pounded yam is not the equal of the yam.
Cultural_Context: A refined product is superior to the raw version.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹgbrún ibalùwẹ̀ ò lè tó sánmà.
Target_Text_En: A thousand bath enclosures are no equal for the sky.
Cultural_Context: Possession of a tiny amount of a substance does not make one an equal of the person who controls its supply.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹlésin-ín sè oògùn ejò tán: ẹlésin-ín wà lókè, ejò-ó wà nílẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The horse rider has the surest antidote for snakebite: the rider is up above; the snake is on the ground.
Cultural_Context: A person beyond the reach of his or her adversary need not fear the adversary.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní Abá ò tọ́ bí ẹní òré; ẹní abá ò ṣéé ká; rírún ní ńrún wómú-wómu
Target_Text_En: Abá mat does not last as long as òré mat; the former cannot be folded, as it disintegrates completely in the attempt.
Cultural_Context: Some things are better and more desirable than others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá pa àfè ìmòjò kó mú-u re Ọ̀yọ́; ẹdá lará oko ńjẹ.
Target_Text_En: Whoever kills a spotted grass mouse should take it to Ọ̀yọ́; the brown bush rat is good enough food for a bush person.
Cultural_Context: Only certain people can appreciate, and therefore deserve, the choicest prizes.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní jẹ Olúwo, ká yìn ín; ṣàṣà èèyàn ló lè jẹ Bara.
Target_Text_En: Whoever takes the title Olùwo deserves commendation; few people can take the Bara title.
Cultural_Context: Whoever has performed an extraordinary feat deserves people’s recognition and praise.)

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní jù ló máa gbéra mì nínú ajá àti òkẹ́rẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The more formidable will triumph over the other in a contest between the dog and the squirrel.
Cultural_Context: The weakling will not triumph over the powerful person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní lágbára juni ní ńfi ọwọ́ ẹni gbáni lẹ́nu.
Target_Text_En: Only a stronger person can use one’s own hand to slap one in the mouth.
Cultural_Context: Only those who have authority over you can make you act against your own interest, or injure you and add insult to the injury.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ ńlá ní ńṣe ohun ńlá, baál Jìnìbà: ó gbé àká mì, ó fọmọrí odó tàyín.
Target_Text_En: From an eccentric person one can expect anything.
Cultural_Context: This is a variant of the pre ceding proverb, with the exception that in this case the application is ironic. The deed referenced is not to be admired but perhaps to be amazed by. Compare the preceding entry.)

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a ò tó là ńgàn; agánrán ńgan ọdẹ.
Target_Text_En: People disparage only those worthier than themselves; the parrot disparages the hunter.
Cultural_Context: Disparagement is an indication of helpless envy; the parrot’s only weapon against the hunter is ineffectual disparagement.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí ńkun osùn ò dàbí ẹni tí ńkun ata.
Target_Text_En: The person rubbing himself or herself with camwood does not compare with the person rubbing himself or herself with hot pepper.
Cultural_Context: Things may look alike without being the same.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó gbọ́ Ifá ò mọ Ọ̀fà; ẹni tó mọ Ọ̀fà ò gbọ́Fá, bẹ́ẹ̀ ni Ifá tà lỌ́fà
Target_Text_En: The person versed in Ifá does not know the way to Ọ̀fà; the person who knows the way to Ọfà is ignorant of Ifá; and yet knowledge of Ifá is lucrative at Ọfà.
Cultural_Context: The talent and the opportunity are available, but they are mismatched; nobody has everything.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó ní àgbàdo ò léhín; ẹni tó léhín ò lágbàdo
Target_Text_En: The person who has corn has no teeth; the person who has teeth has no corn.
Cultural_Context: Need and supply are often mismatched.

Source_Text_Yo: Èni tó ní èjìká ó lẹ́wù; èni tó lẹ́wù ó léjìká.
Target_Text_En: The person who has a shoulder has no gar ment; the one who has a garment has no shoulder.
Cultural_Context: Need and supply are often mismatched.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó ní orí ò ní fìlà; ẹni tó ní fìlà ò lórí.
Target_Text_En: The person who has a head has no hat; the person who has a hat has no head.
Cultural_Context: Need and fortune are often mismatched.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó wà láyé ní inú òun-ún bájì; ẹni tó ti kú ní kú ńkọ́?
Target_Text_En: The person who is alive says he or she is sad; what about the person who is dead?
Cultural_Context: As long as one has life, one should consider oneself fortunate.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó wáyé ò tó asinniwáyé.
Target_Text_En: People who came to the world are far fewer than people who came as companions.
Cultural_Context: There are fewer people with a purpose than people without a purpose.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu àgbà lobì ńgbó.
Target_Text_En: It is only in the mouth of the elder that the kola nut is ripe.
Cultural_Context: The last say in a matter belongs to the elder who is present.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹranko bí ọ̀bọ ò sí lóko, àfi ìjímèrè tí ńpe ara-a rẹ̀ ní olóògùn.
Target_Text_En: There is no animal in the bush like the monkey, except for the brown (Pataguenon) monkey calling itself a medicine man.
Cultural_Context: Nobody can vie with a certain person; those who try deceive themselves.)27

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹranko tó gbọ́n bí ajá ò sí, èyí tó wèrè bí ẹṣin ò wọ́pọ̀; ajá bímọ-ọ rẹ̀ sílẹ̀ ó ńlọ ki ọmọ èkùlù mọ́lẹ̀; ẹṣín bímọ tirẹ̀ sílẹ̀ ó ńfi ẹ̀hìn pọn ọmọ ẹlòmíràn re oko.
Target_Text_En: Animals as wise as the dog are nonexis tent; those as stupid as the horse are rare; the dog gives birth to its children but goes and pounces on the children of the crested duiker; the horse gives birth to its own children but carries others’ children on its back to the farm.
Cultural_Context: The wise put their own interests before all else.

Source_Text_Yo: Èrù tí onígẹ̀gẹ̀ẹ́ rù tí ó ńṣomilójú, abuké kọ́ ni yó pàntéte-e rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The load that draws tears from the eyes of the carrier with a goiter is not one for the humpback to carry nonchalantly, with arms swinging freely.
Cultural_Context: A burden that prostrates a formidable person is not one for a spineless person to tackle lightly.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀rúkọ́ lórí; kò ní mùndùn-múndùn.
Target_Text_En: The hoe shaft has a head but no marrow.
Cultural_Context: One cannot get something from where there is nothing, just as one cannot get marrow from a skull.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹyẹlé kì í ní àgògo, kìkì àrupẹ̀
Target_Text_En: Pigeons never grow to giant size; they are all dwarfish.
Cultural_Context: There is no rank distinction among a certain group of people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìjímèrè, a small brown (
Target_Text_En: Pataguenon) monkey, is considered a clown among the species. nature G
Cultural_Context: Not Provided

Source_Text_Yo: Gagalo-ó ṣísẹ̀ méjì, ó bá ará iwájú.
Target_Text_En: The stilt walker takes only two steps, and he catches up with those who had long gone ahead.
Cultural_Context: The person referred to has extraor dinary capabilities, surpassing all others.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbégẹ́ ṣe gẹ́gẹ́; ónígẹ̀gẹ̀ tó fẹ́ àtìrò.
Target_Text_En: Two well-matched things have come to gether: a person with a goiter has married a cripple.
Cultural_Context: Two or more people are both, or all, all of a kind.

Source_Text_Yo: Gèlè ò dùn bíi ká mọ̀ọ́ wé ò dùn bíi kó yẹni.
Target_Text_En: Head scarf is no good if one does not know how to tie it; knowing how to tie it is no use if it does not look good on one.
Cultural_Context: Having an asset is not as important as knowing how to use it; knowing how to use it is not as important as knowing how to use it profitably.

Source_Text_Yo: Gèlè ò dùn bíi ká mọ̀ọ́ wé; ká rówó ra ẹl yàá ò dàbíi kó yẹni
Target_Text_En: Head scarf is no good unless one knows how to tie it; having money to afford Ẹlẹ́yàá cloth is no good if it does not look good on one.
Cultural_Context: Having an asset is not as important as knowing how to use it; knowing how to use it is not as important as knowing how to use it profitably.

Source_Text_Yo: Gèlè ò dùn bíi ká m wé; oúnjẹ ò dùn bíi ká m jẹ.
Target_Text_En: Head scarf is no good if one does not know how to tie it; food is no good if it is some
Cultural_Context: Having an asset is not as important as knowing how to use it; knowing how to use it is not as important as knowing how to use it profitably.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbajúmọ̀-ọ́ ju owó lọ; àyà níní ju oògùn lọ́tọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Popularity is better than money; bravery is far better than magical charms.
Cultural_Context: Better fame than riches; better fortitude than magic.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbogbo ọdún ni tọba; gbogbo ẹ̀sìn ni tìjòyè.
Target_Text_En: All festivals belongs to the king; all weekly worship belong to the chief.
Cultural_Context: The more important one’s stature, the more important one’s responsibility.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbọ-gbọ-gbọ lọwọ́ ńyọ ju orí.
Target_Text_En: Loftily, loftily, loftily the raised hand reaches above the head.
Cultural_Context: The person blessed with extraordinary qualities will always stand out in a group.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi tí àjànàkú ti fi ẹsẹ̀ tẹlẹ̀ ni gbogbo erankó ti ḿmu.
Target_Text_En: Where the elephant once planted its foot, there the rest of the animals come to drink.
Cultural_Context: The feats of the mighty bestow some boon on the humble.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgún iyán ò jọ ti èlùbọ́; mímú niyán ḿmú, kíki lèlùbọ́ ńki.
Target_Text_En: The consistency of pounded yam is different from that of yam-flower meal; pounded yam is smooth, while yam-flower meal is elastic.
Cultural_Context: Each thing or person is good in a different way.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbà tí ajá ti ńṣe ilé, ọ̀bọ ò ì tíì ti oko bọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The dog was master of the home long before the monkey came from the farm.
Cultural_Context: The upstart or Johnny-just-come must not be garrulous in the presence of well  established old-timers.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbà tí ìkẹ̀tẹ́ òì tíì dáyé, onígbó ti ńjẹ ìkẹ̀tẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Long before the thick sediment of the palm oil came to earth, the lord of the forest had been eating it.
Cultural_Context: Said to claim that one does not need another person’s favors but had always gotten along very well without that person’s help.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbín ò dùn, kò ṣéé fi wé pọ̀nmọ́.
Target_Text_En: The snail is not delicious; it cannot be com pared to boiled cow hide.
Cultural_Context: Some foods are more delicious than others.

Source_Text_Yo: Igbó biribiri, òkùkùn biribiri; òkùkùn ni ó ṣẹ̀tẹ́ igbó.
Target_Text_En: The forest is as dark as ever, and the night is as dark as ever, but the darkness of the night puts that of the forest to shame.
Cultural_Context: Greatness is not without gradation.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìka ò dọ́gba.
Target_Text_En: The fingers are not equal.
Cultural_Context: People are not equally endowed.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé Ifẹ̀ ló ladé; fìlà ni ti baál ibòmíràn.
Target_Text_En: To Ilé If belongs the crown; hats are the lot of the chiefs of other places.
Cultural_Context: The king of Ilé If is preeminent over all other kings.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilẹ̀ tí àjànàkú ńtẹ̀, níbẹ̀ lọmọ ẹrankó ti ńjẹun.
Target_Text_En: The ground the elephant treads is the same place from which the clan of animals eat.
Cultural_Context: Lesser people can benefit from the actions and leavings of great people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìrèké lẹ́wà ju eèsún; igikígi kì í ṣomi síni lẹ́nu.
Target_Text_En: The sugarcane has more appeal than the ele phant grass; no other tree fills one’s mouth with juice.
Cultural_Context: Some things are of surpassing merit and are incomparable to others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìrìn ò papọ̀; ẹni tó ru ọ̀ọ́dúnrún èbù àtẹni tó gun ẹṣin
Target_Text_En: The paths being taken are not the same; one person is carrying three hundred yam seedlings, and the other is mounted on a horse.
Cultural_Context: The expectations and experiences of the servant and the master are never the same.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìrònú ò papọ̀; ebi ló jọ ńpani.
Target_Text_En: Different people have different minds, even though all are hungry.
Cultural_Context: All people may be hungry alike, but each person will have a different approach to solving the problem.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìrù ẹṣin ò ṣe déédé; bákannáà kọ́ la mórí wáyé.
Target_Text_En: Horses’ tails are not of equal length; we did not all come to earth with identical heads.
Cultural_Context: Different people have different destinies.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣe tí igbà ńṣe pẹ, ìbá ṣe àgbọn kò léwé lórí.
Target_Text_En: What the climbing rope does to the palm tree, had it done the same to the coconut tree it would have no leaves left.
Cultural_Context: Some people are better able to withstand vicissi tudes than others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣòwò-ó wà lóòrùn; náwónáwó wà níbòji.
Target_Text_En: The trader [who makes the money] is in the sun; the person who spends the money is in the shade.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who lift not a finger to help the worker but yet get the best of the benefits of his or her efforts.

Source_Text_Yo: Iwájú lojúgun ńgbé.
