Target_Text_En: The front part is where the shinbone lives.
Cultural_Context: The person with leadership qualities will always shine above the rest.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyà àdá pọ̀ ju ti àkọ̀; nígbàtí àdá ńṣẹ, àkọ́ sùnlọ.
Target_Text_En: The suffering the cutlass endures is greater than that of the sheath; while the cutlass works, the sheath sleeps.
Cultural_Context: Some people have to bear burdens greater than others’.

Source_Text_Yo: Iyán ni oúnjẹ, ọkà loògùn, àìkórira là ńjẹ̀kọ, kẹ́nu má dilẹ̀ ni tẹ̀wà, kọmìí ó má baà bọ ni tẹ̀bà.
Target_Text_En: It is pounded yam that is food; corn-flour meal is medicine; corn loaf one eats to prove absence of ill will; black-eyed peas are for snacking; and cassava meal is simply for keeping life going. J
Cultural_Context: People or friends, like food, are not of equal value or appeal.

Source_Text_Yo: Jíjọ ló jọ ; òṣùpá ò lè rí bí ọ̀sán.
Target_Text_En: It is only resemblance; moonlight cannot be like noontime.
Cultural_Context: Some phenomena are without equal.

Source_Text_Yo: Ká tó rí erin ó digbó; ká tó rẹ́fọ̀n ó dọ̀dàn; ká tó rí ẹyẹ bí kín ó di kése.
Target_Text_En: Before one can see the elephant, one must go to the bush; before one can see the buf falo, one must go to the wilderness; before one can see another bird like the egret, one must await the end of time.
Cultural_Context: Comment that the likes of a given person are rare indeed

Source_Text_Yo: Kí eṣú yin ẹyẹ; eṣu fò lọ́jọ́ kan ṣoṣo, ìyẹ́ẹ̀-ẹ́ re.
Target_Text_En: The locust should praise the bird; the locust flew only one day and lost its wings.
Cultural_Context: One should credit those who perform feats that others cannot approach.

Source_Text_Yo: Kì í ṣe gbogbo aṣọ là ńsá lóòrùn.
Target_Text_En: It is not all cloths that one dries in the sun.
Cultural_Context: Some matters require more delicate han dling than others.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí ni ìyẹ́ etutu-ú jámọ́ nínú ìyẹ́ ọ̀sìn?
Target_Text_En: What value has the wing of the tiny flying ant compared to that of the vulturine fish eagle?
Cultural_Context: One should not assign in ordinate value to worthless things, especially in comparison with much more valuable things.

Source_Text_Yo: Kìnìún fìtọ̀ gba ijù; kìnìún gba ijù láìlápó.
Target_Text_En: The lion claims the forest; the lion claims the forest without a quiver of arrows.
Cultural_Context: The mighty do not always need to put them selves out or acquire weapons in order to secure advantages.

Source_Text_Yo: Kìnìún kì í ṣẹgbẹ́ ẹran kọran nínú igbó.
Target_Text_En: The lion is more than the equal of any other sort of animal in the bush.
Cultural_Context: There is a hierarchy among animals and humans.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ẹyẹ méjì tí ńjẹ́ àkùkọ.
Target_Text_En: There are not two birds known as the cock.
Cultural_Context: The likes of some persons are rare.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ìlù tó lè borí-i bẹ̀mbẹ́
Target_Text_En: There is no drum that can surpass the b b .
Cultural_Context: The greatest entity will not lose its preeminence to minor ones.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí òrìṣà tó lè ṣe bí Ògún lágbẹ̀dẹ
Target_Text_En: There is no òrìṣà that can do as Ògún, [god of metals and the forge], can do at the smithy.
Cultural_Context: No one else can attempt the feats that the person referred to can accomplish.

Source_Text_Yo: Láká-ǹ-láká tòyìnbó; làkúrègbé tòyìnbó.
Target_Text_En: Limping is the white man’s habit; rheuma tism is the white man’s ailment.
Cultural_Context: Different people have their peculiar traits.

Source_Text_Yo: Mímú aró ò tó ti abẹ, ìkà ẹṣin ò tó tèèyàn; ẹṣín fọmọ ẹ̀ sílẹ̀ ó ńfẹ̀hìn gbé ọmọ ọlọ́mọ kiri.
Target_Text_En: The keenness of a dye is not comparable to that of a knife, and a horse’s cruelty is nothing compared with a human’s; the horse neglects its own children and carries other people about on its back.
Cultural_Context: There are significant differences among people and their behavior.

Source_Text_Yo: Mímú oòrùn ò jọ mímú abẹ.
Target_Text_En: The sun’s sharpness is not comparable to a knife’s.
Cultural_Context: Even things or people described with the same words are not necessarily alike.

Source_Text_Yo: Mo dáṣáṣá àgbẹ̀, bí bọ ìlú ló rí.
Target_Text_En: The smartest of farmers seems like the idiot of the city.
Cultural_Context: Farm-smartness does not trans late into city [or street] smarts.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó wu ìràwọ̀ kó mọ́lẹ̀ tó òṣùpá, Ọlọ́run ni ó jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The star would wish to be as bright as the moon; it is God that would not permit.
Cultural_Context: God determined individual possibilities, and it is futile to attempt to transcend them.

Source_Text_Yo: Òbu ò tó iyọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Saltpeter does not equal salt.
Cultural_Context: An inferior substitute is never like the real thing.

Source_Text_Yo: Ògìdán kì í ṣẹgbẹ́-ẹ ajá.
Target_Text_En: The leopard is not the equal of the dog.
Cultural_Context: Some powers are superior to others. See the preceding and following entries.

Source_Text_Yo: Ogbe tákùkọ́ fi ńṣakọ ni kọ̀lọ̀kọ̀lọ̀-ọ́ fi ńpanu.
Target_Text_En: The cock’s comb, which the cock flaunts, is the same thing the fox eats as a snack.
Cultural_Context: One person’s prized possession is another person’s trash.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohùn là ńta ọ̀fàfà; ìdí igi là ḿbá a
Target_Text_En: It is in the direction of the tree bear’s voice that one shoots; it is at the bottom of a tree that one finds it.
Cultural_Context: No matter how they might try, some people, because of their greatness, cannot conceal the fact of their presence.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí ojú àgbà-á rí tó fi jìn; bí tọmọdé bá rí i á fọ́.
Target_Text_En: That which the elder’s eyes saw and became sunken, if a youth’s eyes see it, they will go blind.
Cultural_Context: What an elder can easily endure will destroy a youth.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó ṣe àgùntàn tó fi kó òtútù; bó ṣe ewúrẹ́ á ṣe aláìsí.
Target_Text_En: The condition that gave a sheep a cold, if it befell a goat, would result in its death.
Cultural_Context: Some people are more resilient than others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó ṣe àgbìgbò tó fi dẹ́kun ẹ́rín, bó ṣe igúnnugún a wankoko sórí ẹyin
Target_Text_En: The affliction that caused the àgbìgbò bird to stop laughing would have paralyzed the vulture while brooding on her eggs.
Cultural_Context: Some people are more resilient than others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó ṣe igún tó fi pá lórí ló ṣe àkàlà tó fi di alákìísà.
Target_Text_En: The disaster that befell the vulture and made it bald is the same that befell the ground hornbill and reduced its covering to tatters.
Cultural_Context: Some are better able to withstand adversity than others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó ṣe ilá tó ṣe kó, bó bá ṣe ikàn á wẹ̀wù ẹjẹ̀; ohun tó ṣe olówó tó fi ńrojú, bó bá ṣe tálákà wọ́n á ti gbàgbé ẹ; ohun tó ṣe igún tó fi pá lórí, bó bá ṣe àgbò w n a ti yọ̀wo ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The disaster that befell okro and caused it to become wooden, if it had befallen ikàn, it would have taken on a hue of blood; the woe that befell the rich person and caused him or her to scowl, if it had befallen a poor person, he or she would have been long forgotten; the problem that came upon the vulture and made it bald, if it had come upon the ram, he would long ago have lost his horns.
Cultural_Context: The reverses that illustrious people can endure and weather will easily destroy people of little substance.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohùn-un kéjiró ò dé ọ̀run
Target_Text_En: The voice of the kéjiró bird does not rise to reach the sky.
Cultural_Context: A sentiment that a person’s voice carries no weight.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò ńrọ̀, ìwọ̀fà ńyọ̀; ojú olówó kan ó ju ìbó.
Target_Text_En: It is raining, and the pawned laborer is re joicing, but the look on the creditor’s face is as sour as can be.
Cultural_Context: Some people’s fortune is other people’s misfortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò òwúrọ̀ tí ḿbí olówó nínú: olówó gẹlẹtẹ, ìwọ̀fà gẹlẹtẹ.
Target_Text_En: The morning rain angers the creditor: the creditor lolls about, and his pawn lolls about.
Cultural_Context: It is an annoying situation that pre vents one from enjoying what is due one.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjòjò ńṣe ìwọ̀fà wọ́n ní ó kó ìṣe ẹ̀ dé; bó bá ṣe ọmọ-ọ wọn, wọ-n a máa náwó, wọn a máa nára
Target_Text_En: An illness takes hold of the pawned ser vant, and they say he has resorted to his habitual tricks; if it were their own son, they would commit their money and their effort human nature [to healing him].
Cultural_Context: One is always indulgent toward one’s own children while having no patience with others’ children.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú abẹ́rẹ̀ nípin; ibalùwẹ̀-ẹ́ gbòrò kò gba ọkọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The eye of a needle does not ooze matter; the bath place is broad but not enough for a boat.
Cultural_Context: Comparisons between two different things are valid only up to a point.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkèlè àkọ́bù tí ńre ọ̀gangan ìdí.
Target_Text_En: The first morsel of food sinks down to the base of the backbone.
Cultural_Context: Said of a thing that makes an incomparable impression, just as the first morsel makes a powerful impression on a starving person.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkò ńlá ṣe aláǹgbá pìnṣín; ẹni tó juni lọ ní ńṣekú pani
Target_Text_En: A huge stone missile flattens the lizard; a person with more power will be the death of you.
Cultural_Context: Those who are in positions of power are likely to use their power to crush the less powerful.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkun lọba omi.
Target_Text_En: The ocean is the king of all waters.
Cultural_Context: A certain thing or person is without rivals.

Source_Text_Yo: Ológìnní tó fẹ́ẹ́ ṣe bí ẹkùn, ó najú ni.
Target_Text_En: The cat that attempts to emulate the leopard merely fools itself.
Cultural_Context: One should know one’s limits.

Source_Text_Yo: Olóko lẹ̀gbọ́n alágbàro.
Target_Text_En: The owner of the farm is the master of the hired tiller.
Cultural_Context: The employee is subservient to the employer.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó dénú ẹ̀gún kò roko; ìwọ̀fà-á tinú ẹ̀gún bẹ̀rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The rich man gets to the thorn patch and stops hoeing; the pawned servant starts his hoeing from the thorn patch.
Cultural_Context: The rich can afford to leave the worst assignments for those beholden to them.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó fẹ́ẹ̀ sin odò; tálákà ńgbọn orí.
Target_Text_En: The rich man wishes to sacrifice to the river, and the poor man shakes his head in refusal.
Cultural_Context: If one has no standing, one might as well keep one’s opinion to oneself.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó ìlú kan, tálákà ìlú mìíràn.
Target_Text_En: The rich man of one town is the pauper of another.
Cultural_Context: Everything is relative.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó làgbà; olówó sọ̀rọ̀ ẹnu ẹ̀ ńyọná.
Target_Text_En: The rich person is the eldest of all; the rich person speaks, and fire shoots out of his mouth.
Cultural_Context: No one compares with a rich per son; nothing is beyond a rich person.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó lọ̀gá-a tálákà; Ọlọ́run lọ̀gá-a gbogbo-o wa.
Target_Text_En: The rich person is the master of the poor; God is the master of all.
Cultural_Context: The rich may lord it over the poor, but even they must answer to God.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó ńsọ̀rọ̀ ẹnu ẹ̀ ńdùn; òtòṣì ńsọ̀rọ̀ ẹnu ẹ̀ ńró ṣáka-ṣàka.
Target_Text_En: The rich person speaks, and his mouth sounds sweet; the lazy person speaks, and his mouth sounds like unbearable noise.
Cultural_Context: The sound of a rich man’s voice is music to the ears; that of a poor person is merely grating noise.

Source_Text_Yo: Omi ni yó paná.
Target_Text_En: Water is the thing that will quench fire.
Cultural_Context: Each person has his particular nemesis.

Source_Text_Yo: Òní lẹ̀gbọ́n ọ̀la; ìrìwọ̀wọ̀ lẹ̀gbọ́n òjò.
Target_Text_En: Today precedes tomorrow in age; the drizzle precedes the rain in age.
Cultural_Context: There is order in Nature, such that certain things always precede others, never the reverse.

Source_Text_Yo: Oníyàwó ńgbéyàwó, Abídogun ńkó eèp
Target_Text_En: The groom is welcoming his new bride; Abí dogun is carrying sand.
Cultural_Context: Some suffer while others enjoy life.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí ajá lẹkùn ó fàbọ̀ sí.
Target_Text_En: It is to the matter of the dog that the leopard will finally turn.
Cultural_Context: The weakling may tease the bully with impunity for a while, but the bully will find time for him in the end.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí ẹṣin ò ṣee fi wé tọ̀kẹ́rẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The horse’s head is not comparable to that On inequality of the squirrel.
Cultural_Context: Some people are more fortunate than others.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí lẹ̀gbọ́n ara.
Target_Text_En: The head is an elder sibling to the body.
Cultural_Context: Certain entities are unquestionably su perior to their associates.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrìṣà bí Ògún ò sí; ojú lásán ni gbogbo wọn ńyá
Target_Text_En: A god to rival Ògún does not exist; all the others are only being impudent.
Cultural_Context: A certain person is without peer among humans, just as Ògún is without equal among the gods.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrìṣà ní ńṣọlà; ọba ní ńṣọlá.
Target_Text_En: It is for the gods to confer greatness; it is for the king to enjoy greatness.
Cultural_Context: The king’s greatness is at the behest of the gods.

Source_Text_Yo: Oró mú ju oró lọ; ọká gbé paramọ́lẹ̀ mì.
Target_Text_En: Some venoms are more deadly than others; the viper swallows the adder.
Cultural_Context: Some people or things are more formidable than others.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrùlé fara wé ẹṣin; a gùn ún, kò lè rìn
Target_Text_En: A roof looks like a horse; one mounts it, but it cannot walk.
Cultural_Context: Things that may look similar will prove themselves quite different.

Source_Text_Yo: Oyin ò nífiwé nínú adùn.
Target_Text_En: There is nothing that compares with honey in sweetness. Ọ
Cultural_Context: Some things are simply in comparable.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọba kì í dọ̀bálẹ̀ fólórí abúlé.
Target_Text_En: The king does not prostrate before the head of a village.
Cultural_Context: The person of superior rank does not pay obeisance to a person in an inferior position.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọba ò ní fìlà, adé ló ní.
Target_Text_En: The king has no hat; he has only crowns.
Cultural_Context: The king is not to be compared with ordi nary people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀bùn-ún ṣubú lọ́jà a fẹ̀rín si; bí afínjú ṣubú àá gbọ́ ariwo.
Target_Text_En: The filthy person falls in the market, and we burst into laughter; if a fashionable person falls, there will be loud exclamations.
Cultural_Context: Few people care what misfortune befalls a lousy person; everybody cares about the welfare of a fashionable person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀gá ni ìgbò tí ńṣe sójà nínú ẹyẹ
Target_Text_En: The ìgbò bird is a boss, a soldier among birds.
Cultural_Context: Said of a person whose notable deeds have earned him or her renown among the people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀gán ńṣe nǹkan díẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The great one is showing off.
Cultural_Context: Said of a person doing impressive things to show his or her prowess.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọgọ́rùn-ún eṣinṣin ò dá màlúù dúró.
Target_Text_En: One hundred flies will not stop an elephant.
Cultural_Context: A multitude of little people will not prevent a great man from doing what he wishes.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀já kan ò dàbí já òróòro; òkè kan ò dàbí Òkèe Gbadi; Òkèe Gbadií sunwọ̀n sunwọ̀n, o fi ibi ṣóńṣó ṣe àrà; nà kan ò dàbí nà-a sàréè.
Target_Text_En: No sash compares with the red sash; no hill compares with Gbadi Hill; Gbadi Hill is so beautiful that it adorns itself with a tall peak; no path compares with the path to the grave.
Cultural_Context: Some things are incomparable in their quality.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀já kan ò dàbí já òróòro; òkè kan ò dàbí Òkèe Gbadi; ọmú kan ò dùn bí ọmú ìyá ẹni.
Target_Text_En: No sash compares with the red sash; no hill compares with Gbadi Hill; no breast milk is as delicious as one’s mother’s breast milk.
Cultural_Context: Certain things have no rivals in value.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọká ojú nà tí ńlé guuru kó-kó-kó.
Target_Text_En: The pathway gaboon viper defiantly occu pies the whole path.
Cultural_Context: Said of a tough person who defies all would-be opponents.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kín ọba ẹyẹ; kín ẹlẹ́wà àlà.
Target_Text_En: Egret, king of birds; egret whose beauty is in whiteness.
Cultural_Context: Praise for people of exemplary qualities.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlọ́mkọṣíkàtà baba àgbàdo.
Target_Text_En: The corncob with irregular rows of grains on it is the father of all corn.
Cultural_Context: The unconventional person is a person to be reckoned with among people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlọ́run ò pín in dọ́gba; sajiméjọ̀ọ́ ju kòròfo.
Target_Text_En: God did not distribute things equally; the seargeant major is more important than the plain soldier.
Cultural_Context: God did not create people equal in importance.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọlọ̀tọ̀ kékeré là ńfọwọ́ tẹ̀ níkùn
Target_Text_En: It is an insignificant wealthy person whose stomach one pokes with one’s finger.
Cultural_Context: One can take liberties with people of sudden wealth

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ òtòṣì-í ṣubú lọ́jà a fẹ̀rín sí i; ọmọ olówó ṣubú ariwó ta: ‘‘Yéè! Pẹ̀lẹ́!  Pẹ̀lẹ́! Pẹ̀lẹ́!’’
Target_Text_En: The child of a poor man falls in the market, and people burst into laughter; the child of  a rich man falls, and there is a huge outcry: ‘‘Great heavens! Easy does it! Easy does it! Easy does it!’’
Cultural_Context: If you are poor, you are on your own; if you are rich, the whole world is in your corner

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ ọlọ́rọ́ ní ńjẹ ẹyin awó.
Target_Text_En: It is the child of a wealthy person that eats guinea-fowl eggs.
Cultural_Context: Only the wealthy enjoy rare things.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ò ga ju ara wọn lọ, àfi èyí tó bá gun ebè.
Target_Text_En: No one toad is taller than another, except one that climbs a heap.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who, despite the affectations of some of them, are indistinguishable in stature and worth.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ò jẹ gbèsè ju ara wọn lọ; tìẹ okòó, tèmi okòó, tàwa okòó, t yin okòó, okokòó.
Target_Text_En: Toads are not in greater debt than one an other: yours 20 cowries, mine 20 cowries, ours 20 cowries, theirs 20 cowries, 20 cow ries all around.
Cultural_Context: None of us is better off than the others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ò jẹ kí kọ̀-ǹ-kọ̀-ọ́ dún; ẹni tó júni kò jẹ kà sọ̀rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The toad will not let the frog make a sound;  a mightier person prevents one from speak ing.
Cultural_Context: One often must hold one’s tongue for fear of mightier people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rán sàn ju ọ̀ràn; adẹ́tẹ̀-ẹ́ rí wèrè, ó kán lùgbó, ó ní Ng ò níí jẹkí kiní yìí bùmíjẹ ojàre
Target_Text_En: Some misfortunes are worse than others; the leper sees the mad person and dashes into the bush, saying, ‘‘I’ll be hanged if I will let that creature take a bite out of me!’’
Cultural_Context: Even the afflicted know that some people have even worse afflictions.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rán sàn ju ọ̀ràn; ti àpọ́n sàn díẹ̀ ju ti òkóbó.
Target_Text_En: Some problems are better than others; a bachelor’s plight is somewhat better than a eunuch’s.
Cultural_Context: Misfortunes come in different degrees of seriousness.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀wọ́nrín, baba Ifá
Target_Text_En: The Ọ̀wọ́nrín chapter is the father of Ifá.
Cultural_Context: Said of a thing or person preeminent among all others.

Source_Text_Yo: Pàtàkì orò ò ju ilé Àjànà
Target_Text_En: The greatest authority within the Orò cult is not to be sought beyond the Àjànà’s home.
Cultural_Context: Said of a person or thing that is not surpassed in importance. The following entry is a variant

Source_Text_Yo: Pé-ń-pé làṣá wà tó fi ńṣe ọkọ adìẹ.
Target_Text_En: The kite is modest in size, and yet it is the terror of chickens.
Cultural_Context: A person’s importance is not a matter of his or her size.

Source_Text_Yo: Tijó tayọ̀ ní ńṣe ìdin; wùyẹ̀-wùyẹ̀ ní ńṣe ìgòǹgò; à ńjó, à ńyọ̀, ọmọ bọna-b ná ńre oko igi.
Target_Text_En: The maggot is addicted to dancing and re joicing; the worm is addicted to wriggling; we dance, we rejoice, and the wood-boring insect goes in search of wood.
Cultural_Context: The laboring poor person must keep working even while others are relaxing and rejoicing.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í sùn sílé ẹni ká fọrùn ṣẹ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not sleep in one’s own home and break one’s neck.
Cultural_Context: A person does not get into trouble while minding his or her own business.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò bá kú lógún ọdún, baba ẹnìkan o lè gbéni sin.
Target_Text_En: If one does not die in twenty years, nobody’s father can bury one.
Cultural_Context: If one does not die, nobody can stop one from living.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ẹtu ò bá kú, ta ni yó fi awọ-ọ rẹ̀ tọ́ ọsán? Bí ẹ̀kìrì ò bá kú, ta ni yó fi awọ ọ rẹ̀ dá bàtà? Bí olórìṣà ò bá kú, ta ni yó gba ìbò-o rẹ̀ bò?
Target_Text_En: If the antelope does not die, who would make bowstrings of its hide? If the wild goat does not die, who would make shoes from its skin? If the priest does not die, who would usurp his casting of lots?
Cultural_Context: As long as one lives, no one may alienate one’s rights

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ kì í pa ọmọ jayé
Target_Text_En: A child does not kill another child as a means to prosper.
Cultural_Context: There are certain things that one simply may not do to other people, however great one might be.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í kí ayaba kó dòyín; ẹ̀rẹ̀kẹ́ kọ́ lòkó wà.
Target_Text_En: One does not greet a queen and thereby impregnate her; the cheek is not the place where the penis is located.
Cultural_Context: Innocent actions should not get one in trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í torí-i gbígbó pa ajá; a kì í toríi kíkàn pa àgbò; a kì í torí-i wérewère pa òbúkọ.
Target_Text_En: One does not kill a dog for barking; one does not kill a ram for butting; one does not kill a he-goat because of randiness.
Cultural_Context: Do not punish people for doing what they cannot help doing.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣọ tí a bá lára eégún, ti eégún ni.
Target_Text_En: Whatever costume one finds on the mas querader belongs to him.
Cultural_Context: No one can or should begrudge a person what rightfully belongs to him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: Ekòló ḿmì gbàgọ̀, inú ḿbí adìẹ sùú-sùú.
Target_Text_En: The worm crawls nonchalantly, and the chicken is consumed with anger.
Cultural_Context: One’s ene mies are never pleased by one’s prosperity.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu kì í rírí kí ẹlẹ́nu má lè fi jẹun.
Target_Text_En: The mouth is never so filthy that its owner cannot eat with it.
Cultural_Context: A person is always com fortable with his or her own bad habits and shortcomings. See the following variant.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu kò súnwọ̀n, ẹlẹnu pọ́n-ọn lá.
Target_Text_En: The mouth is not appealing; the owner licks it. G
Cultural_Context: One is not put off by one’s own blemish. See the foregoing entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Gegele ló bí gegele; kòtò ló bí kòtò; òjò-ó r sí kòtò gegele ḿbínú.
Target_Text_En: The mound was sired by a mound; the pit was sired by a pit; rain falls into a pit, and the mound becomes angry.
Cultural_Context: Each person is different; one should not envy what others have.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbáà ṣorí pàlàbà kó ṣorí pàbó, tẹni ní ńjẹ́ tẹni.
Target_Text_En: Be his or her head oversized or deformed, one’s own thing is one’s own.
Cultural_Context: One treasures what one has, however defective it might be.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé ẹni la ti ńjẹ òkété onídodo.
Target_Text_En: It is within one’s home that one eats a field rat with a tumor. K
Cultural_Context: One may do what one pleases in the fastness of one’s home.

Source_Text_Yo: Kán-ún ni ọmọ Hausa; asárá ni ọmọ òyìnbó; gọ̀bm̀bọ́ lọmọ Onírè
Target_Text_En: Potash seasoning is the fetish of the Hausa; snuff is the fetish of the white man; facial marks are the fetish of the Ìrè person.
Cultural_Context: Dif ferent peoples have their different habits.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí Lámọnrín ṣe bí ẹni, ìjà ní ńdà.
Target_Text_En: Demanding that such and such a person emulate one exactly leads to a fight.
Cultural_Context: One should not expect others to be just like oneself.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò-jí-kò-wí kò wí pé kí olóhun má lọ ohun ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: He-did-not-steal-and-he-will-not-tell can not tell the person not to broadcast his or her stolen thing
Cultural_Context: One must not be impatient with people agitated by some loss they have sustained.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Ò báà rí, o ò gbọd wí’’ ní ńpa akọni. ‘‘
Target_Text_En: Even though you see it you must not make a sound’’ is what kills the intrepid man.
Cultural_Context: Vain people go to their death even when judiciously calling for help in the face of danger would have saved them.

Source_Text_Yo: Odò kì í kọ ìwẹ̀, kó kọ ìtù, kó tún kọ à-padà-relé
Target_Text_En: A river does not prevent one from swim ming across it, prevent one from rowing across it, and yet prevent one from returning home.
Cultural_Context: If a goal proves unattainable, one can always let go of it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó wu bùn ló ńfowó rà; bí ẹrú bá tagi tán a fowó bu iṣu jẹ.
Target_Text_En: Whatever pleases the bumpkin is what he spends his money on; when the slave sells his load of firewood, he uses the money to buy yams to eat.
Cultural_Context: What one spends one’s money on is what one pleases to spend it on. Compare the following variant.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó wu bùn ló ńfowó rà; ohun tó wu afínjú ló ńfowó ẹ̀ ṣe.
Target_Text_En: The bumpkin spends his money on what ever he pleases; the fop likewise spends his money on whatever he pleases.
Cultural_Context: One does what one pleases with one’s possessions. Compare the preceding proverb.

Source_Text_Yo: Oko ni tàgbẹ̀; gègé ni talákọ̀wé.
Target_Text_En: To the farmer belongs the farm; to the book ish person belongs the pen. On freedom to be oneself 425
Cultural_Context: Each person or profession has its proper preserves.

Source_Text_Yo: Onímàle Ìbàdàn, bí oníṢàngó Ìlọrin.
Target_Text_En: The Muslim from Ibadan is like a Ṣango worshiper from Ìlorin.
Cultural_Context: Different people practice their religion differently.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọbá lè ṣòfin olè kí adìẹ má jẹ̀ lóṣùpá?
Target_Text_En: Can the king interdict stealing and thus stop a chicken from scratching for food in the moonlight?
Cultural_Context: No law or authority has the right to stop people from conducting their normal lives.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọbá tàkìtì ọ̀bọ ò ró, ìnàkí ṣe ‘‘Ha!’’ ní igọ̀ igi; ọ̀bọ́ ní, ‘‘A kì í bánijà ti n kan ẹni.’’
Target_Text_En: The monkey somersaulted and failed to land erect, and the gorilla resting among the roots of a large tree exclaimed, ‘‘Ha!’’ The monkey responded, ‘‘Nobody has a right to fault one over how one performs one’s sig nature stunt.’’
Cultural_Context: One is free to do one’s thing as one wishes.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọká bímọ-ọ rẹ̀ ó mọ rébété; òjòlá bí tirẹ̀ ó gùn gbàlàjà.
Target_Text_En: The gaboon viper has its child, and it is of moderate length; the python has its child, and it is very long indeed.
Cultural_Context: Children take after their parents.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọká ló bí paramọ́lẹ̀; ìkà ló bí ìkà sílẹ̀; ẹni tó bíni là ńjọ.
Target_Text_En: The gaboon viper sired the serpent; the wicked person is born of a wicked person; one takes after one’s parent.
Cultural_Context: Wickedness is an inherited trait.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀mùtí ò ṣe wèrè, owó ẹ̀ ní ńná.
Target_Text_En: The drunkard is not an imbecile; it is his money he is spending. 426 rights and responsibilities
Cultural_Context: The drunk has a right to spend his money as he pleases. The following entry is a variant.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀mùtí ò yan àpà; owó ní ńná.
Target_Text_En: The drunkard is no spendthrift; he is spend ing his own money.
Cultural_Context: One may do as one pleases with one’s property. See the previous entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀nà kan ò wọ ọjà.
Target_Text_En: It is not one road only that leads to the market. S
Cultural_Context: There are many different ways to approach a problem.

Source_Text_Yo: Sèsé ò lè so bí ẹ̀wà.
Target_Text_En: The yam bean cannot produce fruits like the black-eyed peas. Ṣ
Cultural_Context: One can only act accord ing to one’s nature.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Ṣe é báyìí’’ ní ńk aya lọ́bùn. ‘‘
Target_Text_En: Do it this way’’ is the one who teaches filthy habits to his wife.
Cultural_Context: Do not impose your own instructions on people who know better than you do what they are doing.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣòkòtò òyìnbó ò lókùn; apá ni wọ́n fi ńkọ́.
Target_Text_En: The white man’s trousers have no strings; they are suspended from the shoulders.
Cultural_Context: Different people, different fashions.

Source_Text_Yo: Ta ní ḿbá adéléb ṣe ẹj oyún?
Target_Text_En: Who would take a married woman to task for being pregnant?
Cultural_Context: One should not fault people for doing what is expected of them.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Tèmí yémi,’’ tí ńfi inú iṣu ẹ̀ gbin ọkà
Target_Text_En: ‘I know what I am doing’’ plants corn among his yams.
Cultural_Context: Said of a person who thinks he knows it all but who will learn only from the consequences of his folly.

Source_Text_Yo: Tèfètèfèé yọ owó ọjà.
Target_Text_En: Permanent loss patronized the merchant.
Cultural_Context: All one’s labor has gone for nought.

Source_Text_Yo: Wàrà ní ḿmú ọmọ Fúlàní dàgbà; iyán ní ḿmú ọmọ oko sanra.
Target_Text_En: It is cottage cheese that nurtures the Fulbe child to adulthood; it is pounded yams that make the farm dweller fat.
Cultural_Context: Different people depend on different things for nurturing.

Source_Text_Yo: Wọnsàn-wọnsàn ò mú ehín gbórín; bí kò jù síkí, a ó máa fi rún àgbàdo.
Target_Text_En: Loud chewing does not increase the size of one’s teeth; if one’s teeth are short, one can at least chew corn with them.
Cultural_Context: One does not need to prove that one is great; no matter how lowly one might be, there is much one can accomplish.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi àìlẹ́pà n di ẹrù asòpá.
Target_Text_En: One does not become afflicted with ele phantiasis of the scrotum despite having no testicles.
Cultural_Context: One cannot be deprived of an amenity and yet be subjected to the cares of enjoying it. Compare 4521.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í kó owó ra ẹṣin, ká kówó ra yàgòlọ́nà.
Target_Text_En: One does not spend one’s money purchasing a horse and then spend more money purchasing ‘‘Get out of the way.’’
Cultural_Context: Once one has done one’s part, one is entitled to expect others to do theirs.

Source_Text_Yo: Àáyá ò g bíi ká fà á nírù.
Target_Text_En: The colobus monkey is not so stupid as to permit its tail to be pulled.
Cultural_Context: Even the most foolish people are wise to certain things.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjànàkú fojú ọwọ ọ̀bọ,ò tọrọ jẹ.
Target_Text_En: The elephant looks at the monkey with the eyes of disdain, but the monkey does not beg food to eat.
Cultural_Context: Each person has his or her worth; even the lowly monkey has its dignity, since it is not beholden to the elephant

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò fi ẹni nílùú, a kì í tó abẹ́rẹ́.
Target_Text_En: If one is not wanted in a town, one is worth less than a needle.
Cultural_Context: An unwanted person enjoys no regard.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ikú yó pani á gb tẹnu ẹni; òpìtàn ní ńfi ìtàn gba ara-a r kalẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: If death will kill one, it should listen to what one has to say; he who tells tales may by that means deliver himself.
Cultural_Context: One should not im pose punishment before hearing from the offender.

Source_Text_Yo: Eégún ni baba l run; Pààká ni baba nígbàlẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The masquerader is the father figure in heaven; Pààká is the father figure in the masquerader’s secret grove.
Cultural_Context: There is no disputing the preeminence of a person among his or her peers.

Source_Text_Yo: Ejò-ó kéré kò kéré, kò ṣéé dì ní ìgbànú.
Target_Text_En: However small a snake may be, it cannot be used as a belt. Ẹ
Cultural_Context: However mean or weak a person may be, there is a limit to what one can do to him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a tìràn mò lè dákán; ẹni tí a pè lólè ò lè fojú rere wóni
Target_Text_En: A person one has falsely accused will not remain quiet; a person one has called a thief will not look kindly on one.
Cultural_Context: One who causes others injury should not expect them to be indifferent.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí kò kú yó họra
Target_Text_En: A person who is not dead will be able to scratch where he itches.
Cultural_Context: So long as one has life, one can act in one’s own interest.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹrú kì í ṣe ọmọ igi; èèyàn ló bí ìyá-a rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: A slave is not born of a tree; his or her mother was the offspring of a human being.
Cultural_Context: Even a slave deserves the consideration due every human being; misfortune does not rob people of their humanity.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹrú ṣe ọmọ nílé ìyá-a rẹ̀ rí
Target_Text_En: A slave was once a freeborn person in his or her mother’s house.
Cultural_Context: A person who is down on his or her luck was once in better circumstances; people’s circumstances do change.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé ahun là ńpa ahun sí.
Target_Text_En: It is inside the tortoise’s own house that one kills it.
Cultural_Context: One should make a stand in defense of one’s rights and property, even to the death.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé là ḿbá onímọ́tò gbé; oní-báísíkùlù, má tẹ̀ wá mọ́lẹ̀ pa.
Target_Text_En: One is able to share a home with the owner of a motor vehicle; owner of a bicycle, do not crush us to death.
Cultural_Context: People with little advantages should not throw their weight around, especially when truly great people are considerate of others. Compare the next entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìlú là ḿbá ọba gbé, kí ìjòyè má t wá mọ́lẹ̀ pa.
Target_Text_En: One is able to live in the same town with the king; the chief should not stomp us to death.
Cultural_Context: The minor official should not impose on people more than the important officials do.

Source_Text_Yo: Kì í burú fún èèyàn ká lọ fi ajá wa
Target_Text_En: A person is never so down on his or her luck that one sends a dog to seek him or her out.
Cultural_Context: A person, however disgraced, still deserves to be treated like a human being.

Source_Text_Yo: Kíkéré labẹ́rẹ́ kéré, kì í ṣe mímì adìẹ.
Target_Text_En: A needle may be small, but that does not make it something a chicken can swallow. On the right to human dignity 429 M
Cultural_Context: One should not underestimate people simply because they seem unimpressive.

Source_Text_Yo: Má fi òdù fọ́ mi ní àdó; má fi ẹṣin t mí lágùntàn pa.
Target_Text_En: Do not break my tiny gourdlet with your large pot; do not use your horse to trample my sheep to death. O
Cultural_Context: Do not take advantage of me, even though you are wealthier and more powerful than I.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó di hìn ìgbín ká tó fìkaraun ẹ̀ họ igbá.
Target_Text_En: Not until the demise of the snail can one use its shell to scoop out the inside of a calabash.
Cultural_Context: As long as one is still around, one does not permit one’s interests to be assaulted without making a scene. Compare 4348.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú ẹrú ò gbé ìpàkọ́; a-bojú-níwájú bí ọmọ.
Target_Text_En: The slave’s eyes are not at the back of his head; his eyes are in front just like a free born child’s.
Cultural_Context: A slave is just as human as the freeborn child.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í pọ́n òkú kó má nas tọ́tọ́
Target_Text_En: A corpse is never so benighted that it can not stretch its legs.
Cultural_Context: Even in the worst of circumstances, one can still count some blessings.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í pọ́nni ká má nìí aṣọ kan.
Target_Text_En: One is never so poor that one does not own one single item of clothing.
Cultural_Context: Suffering is never absolute.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó ẹni kì í rorò kó ní ká má ṣu.
Target_Text_En: One’s master cannot be so tyrannical that he orders one not to shit. 430 rights and responsibilities
Cultural_Context: Even servants have some rights.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó tí kò sí, ọba ò lè gbà á.
Target_Text_En: Money that does not exist, no king can take from you.
Cultural_Context: One cannot be at risk for what one does not own.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọba kì í kọ obìnrin síl kí tálákà lọ gbé e sílé
Target_Text_En: A king does not divorce a woman, only for her to be married then by a pauper.
Cultural_Context: A dis graced person is not necessarily without some residual dignity and standing.

Source_Text_Yo: Pàṣípààrọ̀ obìnrin ò ṣeé ṣe.
Target_Text_En: One cannot take a woman back for an ex change.
Cultural_Context: Wives are not like commodities purchased at the market.

Source_Text_Yo: Pátá-pátá k nìjàpá ò níru.
Target_Text_En: It is not completely that a tortoise lacks a tail.
Cultural_Context: A poor person is not absolutely bereft of means.

Source_Text_Yo: Tolè tolè ni mẹ̀kúnnùú fi ńrìn lójú olówó.
Target_Text_En: Ever with a propensity to steal is the appear ance of a simple person’s movement in the eyes of the wealthy. W
Cultural_Context: The well-off are ever suspicious that the worse-off are after their wealth.

Source_Text_Yo: Wọ́n so ajá mọ́lẹ̀, wọ́n so ẹkùn mọ́lẹ̀, wọ́n fìrù ẹkùn lé ajá lọ́wọ́
Target_Text_En: They tied down the dog; they tied down the leopard; and then they delivered the leop ard’s tail into the dog’s paws. On the right to human dignity 431 On the right to one’s patrimony and to property A
Cultural_Context: One’s enemies have conspired to make one vulnerable to people who otherwise would not have dared to confront one.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í bá eku du igbó, a kì í ba ẹfọ̀n du ọ̀dàn, a kì í bá Olúkóre du ipò-o baba-a rẹ̀
Target_Text_En: One does not dispute the bush with the rodent; one does not dispute the grassland with the buffalo; one does not dispute Olúkóre’s patrimony with him.
Cultural_Context: One should not seek to deny people their God-given rights.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbé ọmọ Ọbà fún Ọ́ṣun
Target_Text_En: One does not give the child of the Ọbà river to the ṣun river.
Cultural_Context: Do not rob Peter to pay Paul.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í lé ẹlènu rírùn níbi àmù ìyá ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not chase a smelly-mouthed person away from his or her mother’s water pot.
Cultural_Context: Even problem people have their rights.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í pa igún jẹ ká sòrò; kì í ṣe ẹyẹ baba ẹnìkan.
Target_Text_En: One does not kill a vulture for food and deny doing so; it is not a bird that belongs to anybody’s father.
Cultural_Context: Never be afraid to own up to taking advantage of something or someone nobody favors.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ṣúpó alààyè.
Target_Text_En: One does not inherit the wife of a living man.
Cultural_Context: Do not attempt to wrest property or a right from its owner while the owner is still around.

Source_Text_Yo: A sebẹ̀ fún Fádípẹ̀, Fájẹbẹ̀-ẹ́ fá a lá; ọlọ́bẹ̀ ló lábẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: We prepared stew for Fádípẹ̀, and Fájẹbẹ̀ ate it; the person who deserved the stew got it.
Cultural_Context: If the legitimate owner snatches an article from the illegitimate owner, no crime has been committed

Source_Text_Yo: Àkọ́bí ni ti ẹlẹ́ran
Target_Text_En: The firstborn belongs to the owner of the animal
Cultural_Context: To the owner of an object belongs the largest right to it. This is a variant of the preceding entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣọ tá a bá rí lára igún, ti igún ni.
Target_Text_En: Whatever cloth one finds on the vulture be longs to it.
Cultural_Context: The vulture may lack feathers, but it does not borrow from other birds.

Source_Text_Yo: Aya ọ̀lẹ là ńgbà, a kì í gbọmọ ọ̀lẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is a lazy person’s wife that one may take; one may not take a lazy person’s child.
Cultural_Context: Even the lazy person has some rights.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí oògùn ò bá jẹ́, owó á jísẹ́.
Target_Text_En: If the medicine does not work, the money expended on it must explain why.
Cultural_Context: One has a right to the service one has paid for or an explanation for the withholding of it.

Source_Text_Yo: Eégún mọ̀ọ́ jó kò mọ̀ọ́ jó; yó gba owó ọjà-a rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Whether the masquerader knows how to dance or does not, he will receive his market fee.
Cultural_Context: People in authority will receive their reward whether they perform well or ill.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèyàn lásán ò ní gọ̀bì; olówó ò ní ìlàrí.
Target_Text_En: An ordinary person does not have a throne room; a wealthy man does not have royal courtiers.
Cultural_Context: Each position has its proper privileges.

Source_Text_Yo: Èkúté ilé ó lènu bá alákàá wíjọ́.
Target_Text_En: The house mouse has no mouth to dispute a case with the owner of the granary.
Cultural_Context: A known culprit cannot successfully plead innocence.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹja ló nibú.
Target_Text_En: To the fish belongs the deep.
Cultural_Context: People should not be begrudged what is rightfully theirs.

Source_Text_Yo: Èlenu là ḿbi ká tó gbá a.
Target_Text_En: It is from the owner of the mouth that one asks leave before one slaps it.
Cultural_Context: One should not take liberties with a thing without the permission of its owner.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó gba nà ẹ̀bùrú wá ta ojì: wọ́n ní a kì í gba nà ẹ̀bùrú wá ta ojì; ó ní ṣé a lè gba ọ̀nà ojúlé? Wọ́n ní bẹ́ẹ̀ ni.
Target_Text_En: A man who came on the sly to confront his cuckolder was told one does not confront one’s cuckolder on the sly; he asked if one could do so frontally and was told, yes. F
Cultural_Context: If one’s cause is just, one should press it boldly and openly.

Source_Text_Yo: Fúlàní ló ni pàpá-a daran-daran.
Target_Text_En: To the Fulbe man belongs the cattle-herding staff.
Cultural_Context: The objects people favor are good indicators of their occupations.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣe kí mú ọkọ mú aya kó má ran ọmọ.
Target_Text_En: Suffering does not grip the husband and grip the wife but spare the child.
Cultural_Context: The dependent cannot escape the hardship that befalls his or her benefactors.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìwọ̀fà àjọyá, orí ẹ̀ ní ńkún
Target_Text_En: A person pawned to several creditors is the one whose hair overgrows.
Cultural_Context: Everybody’s responsibility is nobody’s responsibility.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyàwó ọ̀lẹ là ńgbà, a kì í gba ọmọ ọ̀lẹ.
Target_Text_En: The shiftless man’s wife one may take from him, but one may not take his children.
Cultural_Context: Everybody has some inalienable rights.

Source_Text_Yo: Kàkà kí eku má jẹ sèsé, a fi ṣe à-wà dànù.
Target_Text_En: Rather than leave the yam beans uneaten, the rat will scatter them.
Cultural_Context: If one cannot have access to one’s property, one would rather destroy it than permit others to have access.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ohun tí Alágbaà ò l ṣe nígbàlẹ̀ eégún
Target_Text_En: There is nothing the Alágbaà cannot do in the eégun grove.
Cultural_Context: The person invested with absolute authority can do as he or she wishes.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó wu olówó ní ńfi owó rà.
Target_Text_En: It is whatever the wealthy person wishes that he or she does with his or her money.
Cultural_Context: One can do as one wishes with one’s property.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í pọ́n ààfáà kó má nìí tẹ̀sùbáà kan ṣoṣo.
Target_Text_En: Muslim priest is never so hard up that he does not have a solitary string of telling beads [prayer beads].
Cultural_Context: Whatever condition one may be in, one will always have something to fall back on.

Source_Text_Yo: Oko ti ikún, ilẹ̀ ti ẹ̀pà; a kì í bá àlùkẹrẹsẹ du ilé-e baba-a rẹ̀
Target_Text_En: The farm is the domain of the squirrel; the ground is the domain of the groundnut; one does not dispute its father’s house with the plant àlùkẹrẹsẹ.
Cultural_Context: Each person has the right to enjoy his or her patrimony in peace.

Source_Text_Yo: Olórùká gbòrùka, ọwọ́ àwé dòfo.
Target_Text_En: The owner of the ring has taken back his ring; the fingers of the friend are now empty.
Cultural_Context: When the owner takes his property back, the flaunting of it by the borrower comes to an end.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó ṣe bí tòun là ńná.
Target_Text_En: The rich person thinks it is his money other people are spending.
Cultural_Context: The rich would be grudge others any money of their own.

Source_Text_Yo: Olówó ṣe bí tòun là ńwí; òtòṣì ò jẹ iyanrìn.
Target_Text_En: The rich person believes that it is he every body thinks and talks about, [but] the poor person does not eat sand.
Cultural_Context: There are other people in the world besides the rich, even if the rich do not think so.

Source_Text_Yo: Òṣùpá ò mòde òtòṣì; bó bá délé ọlọ́rọ̀ á dé tèmi.
Target_Text_En: The moon does not know which yard be longs to a poor man; if it reaches a wealthy man’s abode, it will reach mine also.
Cultural_Context: With regard to Nature, all people are equal.

Source_Text_Yo: Oye tó bá wuni là ńta Ifá ẹni pa
Target_Text_En: Whatever amount one pleases is what one demands for one’s Ifá paraphernalia.
Cultural_Context: One is at liberty to do as one pleases with what one owns.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ àjànàkú kì í ya aràrá; ọmọ erín bí erin ní ńjọ.
Target_Text_En: An elephant’s baby will not turn out to be dwarfish; the baby sired by an elephant resembles nothing but an elephant.
Cultural_Context: People take after their parents.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ alápatà-á jogún bẹ.
Target_Text_En: The son of the butcher inherits a knife.
Cultural_Context: One takes after one’s parent’s trade.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ erin-ín jogún ọlá.
Target_Text_En: An elephant’s child inherits greatness.
Cultural_Context: One takes after one’s parents.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ ẹni ì ba jọni à bá yọ̀; ọmọ tí Gàm̀- bàrí bí okùn ni yó ran.
Target_Text_En: Were one’s child to resemble one, one would rejoice; the child of a Hausa man takes up the rope-weaving trade.
Cultural_Context: One always hopes that one’s offspring will take after one.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ lẹ ní ńlágbára; ọmọ alágbára ní ńlẹ.
Target_Text_En: The child of a lazy person is usually strong; the child of a strong person is usually lazy.
Cultural_Context: Children often turn out as opposites to their parents.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ tí a jí adìẹ bí, yó jìí adìẹ ju ìyá ẹ̀ lo.
Target_Text_En: A child born while the mother is a habitual chicken stealer will steal chickens even more compulsively than its mother.
Cultural_Context: Children take after their parents.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ tí a pọ̀n lọ yọ ọ̀mùnù-un koóko, yó yọ ọ̀mùnù-un koóko ju ìyá ẹ̀ lọ.
Target_Text_En: The child carried on the mother’s back while the mother plucks young grass proposes to pluck more young grass than its mother.
Cultural_Context: This is a slam at anyone who presumes to do better than those who enable him or her to do anything at all. See the previous entry for comparison.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ tí àgbẹ̀-ẹ́ bí, oko ni yó ro; ọmọ tí Gàm̀bàrí bí, okùn ni yó ran.
Target_Text_En: The child sired by a farmer will engage in farming; the child sired by a Hausa man will engage in rope weaving.
Cultural_Context: People usually take up their lineage profession

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ tí ẹjá bí ẹja ní ńjọ; ọmọ tí ẹkùn ún bí ẹkùn ni yó yà; ọmọ tí Fúlàní bí okùn ni yó ran.
Target_Text_En: The child spawned by a fish resembles a fish; the child sired by a leopard resembles a leopard; the child born to a Fulbe per son will weave ropes.
Cultural_Context: One takes after one’s parents.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀tá elésùúsú yó kòó tiẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The enemy of the person in charge of the saving scheme will collect when his or her turn arrives.
Cultural_Context: People’s rights do not depend on whether one likes them or not.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣòkòtò ní ńjogún ìdí; ọmọ ní ńjogún-un baba.
Target_Text_En: To the trousers belong the heritage of the buttocks; to the child belongs the patrimony of the father. 436 rights and responsibilities T
Cultural_Context: Children survive and inherit from their father, just as the trousers survive and inherit from the buttocks.

Source_Text_Yo: Ta ní mbá adẹ́tẹ̀ du ońjẹ jẹ.
Target_Text_En: Who would scramble for food in the same plate with a leper?
Cultural_Context: People are unlikely to expose themselves voluntarily to abominations.

Source_Text_Yo: Ta ní ḿbá kọ̀-ǹ-kọ̀ṣọ̀ du èlùbọ́ kù?
Target_Text_En: Who would dispute with the sieve the func tion of sifting yam flour?
Cultural_Context: No one can or should deprive people of what is rightfully theirs.

Source_Text_Yo: Ta ní ḿbá yímí-yímí du ìyípo?
Target_Text_En: Who would ever wish to take over the dung beetle’s habit of rolling dung?
Cultural_Context: There are certain things one should have no aspiration whatsoever of achieving.

Source_Text_Yo: Tẹni ntẹni, ààtàn ló làkísà.
Target_Text_En: One’s property belongs to one; to the dung heap belongs the rag. On subservience to authority
Cultural_Context: No one should be grudge a person what is rightfully his or hers.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbèjà èèwọ̀; èèwọ̀ ní yó gbèjà ara ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not fight on behalf of a taboo; the taboo will fight its own fight.
Cultural_Context: It is unnecessary to try to keep people from committing crimes; the system will seek out offenders.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayé lòyìnbó ńjẹ kú.
Target_Text_En: Lifelong luxury is the lot of the white man.
Cultural_Context: The white man enjoys nothing but the best all his life long.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó bá bú ọba lẹ́hin, tó dójú ọba tó sé, ẹ̀rù ọba ló ba.
Target_Text_En: The person who insults the king in the king’s absence and denies doing so in the king’s presence shows his fear of the king.
Cultural_Context: People’s behavior in one’s presence counts more than their behavior in one’s absence, at least as an index of their fear. Compare 1378 and 1379.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó gba ọtí fún eégún, òun náà ní ńgba obì fún ọ̀gbẹ̀rì
Target_Text_En: The person whose office is to bring wine to the masquerader is the same who will bring kola nuts to the novices.
Cultural_Context: The servant cannot choose whom he or she will serve and whom he or she will not.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó ránni níṣẹlà ṣe, a kì í b ẹni tí a ó jẹ fún.
Target_Text_En: One fears the person who sent one with a message; one does not fear the person to whom one will deliver it.
Cultural_Context: The messenger need not fear the recipient of his or her message, since he or she is not responsible for its content; one’s duty is to one’s mas ter, not to those one serves on his or her behalf.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi tó wu ẹ̀fúùfù lẹ̀lẹ̀ ní ńdarí ìgbẹ́ sí; ibi tó wu olówó ẹni ní ńranni lọ.
Target_Text_En: The stiff breeze bends the bush in whichever direction it pleases; the person in control may send one wherever he or she wishes.
Cultural_Context: A person under authority has no choice but to obey the orders of the powers over him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọba ló nilẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The king is the owner of the land.
Cultural_Context: There is no higher authority on earth than the king.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọba ní ńgba owó ibodè.
Target_Text_En: It is the king who receives customs dues.
Cultural_Context: The wealth of the community belongs to the king.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọba ní ńjẹ ọrọ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is the king who enjoys all prosperity. 438 rights and responsibilities
Cultural_Context: It is the king’s lot to prosper.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọba tó ni apá tún ló ni apá òsì.
Target_Text_En: The king who owns the area to the right also owns the area to the left. On just deserts A
Cultural_Context: The lord of all has authority over all.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í sinni ká má nìí àpèjúwe.
Target_Text_En: One does not escort a traveler and lack a description.
Cultural_Context: The helper must be acknowl edged and rewarded.

Source_Text_Yo: Ààbà ò ṣéé kàn mọ́ ẹni lọjẹ, àfi ẹni tí ńṣe búburú.
Target_Text_En: Stakes are not meant for people’s legs, only for the legs of evildoers.
Cultural_Context: One who has not committed an offense does not deserve punishment.

Source_Text_Yo: Agídí páálí òun ìyọnu; akùrẹtẹ̀ òun ìyà.
Target_Text_En: Unalloyed obstinacy with its attendant troubles; lowly birth with its attendant suf fering.
Cultural_Context: Each condition imposes its woes.

Source_Text_Yo: A-gúnyán-sanyán kì í bẹ̀rù òkèlè.
Target_Text_En: He-who-will-pound-yam-to-repay pounded-yam is not bashful about morsels.
Cultural_Context: One can be as free as one chooses with a loan one will repay.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà tí kò bá dáwó, omitooro ọbẹ̀ ni yó jẹ.
Target_Text_En: An elder who does not contribute money will eat the watery remnants of the stew.
Cultural_Context: Nothing goes for nothing.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà tí kò mú iṣu wá sábà ó ní jẹ iyán alẹ́.
Target_Text_En: An elder who does not bring yams to the hut will not eat pounded yams at supper time.
Cultural_Context: One may not reap where one has not sown.

Source_Text_Yo: Agbèfọ́ba kì í j bi fún un.
Target_Text_En: The king’s spokesman does not bear the king’s guilt.
Cultural_Context: The servant is not liable for the master’s misdeeds.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá kì í kọsẹ̀ ibi sí ààtàn; bí kò bá tútù a bá gbígbẹ
Target_Text_En: A dog never encounters an ill omen
Cultural_Context: like stubbing its toe) on its way to the dung heap; if it does not find fresh dung there, it will find dry. ( Whatever the circumstance, one cannot be left entirely without some asset.

Source_Text_Yo: Ajá tó lọ sílé ẹkùn tó bọ̀, ká kí i kú ewu
Target_Text_En: A dog that goes to a leopard’s home and returns: one should congratulate it on sur viving the ordeal.
Cultural_Context: One should acknowledge and praise unusual feats.

Source_Text_Yo: A-jí-ṣeṣe-ló-ṣe-d dín ńjẹun ju a-jí-gbọn enini.
Target_Text_En: He-who-wakes-in-the-morning-and-works on-the-porch usually eats more than He-who-wakes-in-the-morning-and-brushes-against-morning-dew.
Cultural_Context: Those who have it easier often also receive the larger rewards.

Source_Text_Yo: Akátá jẹyìn ó ṣu ihá; ohun a bá jẹ là ńṣu.
Target_Text_En: The civet cat ate palm fruits and excreted palm-fruit pericarp; one excretes what one eats.
Cultural_Context: One should not be surprised at the logical consequences of one’s actions.

Source_Text_Yo: Akéde ò jẹ iyán gbígbóná.
Target_Text_En: The town crier does not eat steaming pounded yam.
Cultural_Context: Every obligation has its toll.

Source_Text_Yo: Akẹ̀sán lòpin Ọ̀yọ́; ilé ọkọ nibìsinmi obìnrin
Target_Text_En: Akẹ̀sán is the frontier of Ọ̀yọ́; a spouse’s home is a woman’s place of rest.
Cultural_Context: Just as Akẹsan is yọ’s city limit, so a spouse’s home is a woman’s final destination.

Source_Text_Yo: Aláàárù tí ńjẹran ńjẹ awọ orí-i rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: A hired carrier who eats meat eats skin off his skull.
Cultural_Context: The laborer eats of his sweat; the laborer with a luxurious taste pays for it with his sweat.

Source_Text_Yo: Alákatam̀pò-ó bojú wòkè.
Target_Text_En: The user of a crossbow casts his eyes upward.
Cultural_Context: One’s trade imposes certain behaviors.

Source_Text_Yo: Alápatà tí ńjẹran, ẹran orí-i r ló ńjẹ.
Target_Text_En: The butcher who eats meat eats the skin off his skull.
Cultural_Context: One eats of one’s labor.

Source_Text_Yo: Àpáàdì-í bá wọn dín àgbàdo kò rí rún; ọkọ́ tó bá wọn ṣá oko-ó sùn lébi.
Target_Text_En: The potsherd makes itself available for pop ping corn but gets no share of it; the hoe that helped to clear the farm sleeps in hun ger. 440 rights and responsibilities
Cultural_Context: The fate of some is to work so that others might thrive.

Source_Text_Yo: À-pa-ì-délé ò jìká mọ̀ pé ológbò ńṣọdẹ.
Target_Text_En: Failure to bring home its kill denies the cat recognition as a hunter.
Cultural_Context: Secret accomplish ments are like no accomplishments at all.

Source_Text_Yo: Baálẹ̀ Ìròkò-ó yan tiẹ̀ tẹ́lẹ̀; ó ní bí ẹ rọ́kùnrin ẹ ṣá a; bí ẹ róbìnrin ẹ ṣá a
Target_Text_En: The chief of Ìròkò made his pronouncement beforehand; he said, ‘‘If you come upon a man, slash him, and if you come upon a woman, slash her.’’
Cultural_Context: The law does not distinguish between man and woman, or between one offender and another.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá bu omi sórí, ó ńwá ẹsẹ̀ bọ̀.
Target_Text_En: If one pours water on one’s head, it comes looking for the legs.
Cultural_Context: Actions have their inevitable consequences; matters will not be resolved until they have reached their conclusions.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá pẹja tán, lébé ẹja la fi ńhá ẹja lẹ́nu.
Target_Text_En: After killing a fish, one stuffs its tail fin into its mouth.
Cultural_Context: An offender furnishes the means of his or her own punishment.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a ó lọ nílùú, a ó mọ ohun tí ńléni.
Target_Text_En: If one must flee a town, one should know what is chasing one off.
Cultural_Context: One must know the cause of one’s suffering or punishment.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí àrígiṣẹ́í bá ṣí, orí ara-a rín ńfí rù ú.
Target_Text_En: After the twig-cutting insect cuts twigs, it carries them on its own head.
Cultural_Context: The disaster a person causes descends on his own head.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí egbò ò bá pa elégbò, kì í pa ẹni tí ńwẹ̀ ẹ́.
Target_Text_En: If an ulcer does not kill the person who has it, it will not kill the person who treats it.
Cultural_Context: Each person suffers his or her own woes.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ẹkọ́ bá ní kókó, kì í ṣẹj alágbàdo.
Target_Text_En: If the corn meal is lumpy, the fault does not lie with the corn seller.
Cultural_Context: The person who furnished the raw material is not responsible for the flaws of the finished product.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ìyàwó bá ṣojú ẹni, tó tún ṣẹ̀hìn ẹni, ó ní láti ní èrè tí yó jẹ níbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: If a wife honors one’s wishes in one’s pres ence and also honors one’s wishes in one’s absence, some reward is certainly due her.
Cultural_Context: The ever-faithful mate deserves some rich reward.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí owó bá ti mọ ni oògùn ńmọ.
Target_Text_En: The limit of the money is the limit of the medicine.
Cultural_Context: One gets only as much as one’s money can buy.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọmọ́ bá ti rí là ńṣe àna-a rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The considerations one offers to the par ents and relatives of one’s fiancée are always commensurate with the quality of the fian cée.[?]Ẹ
Cultural_Context: One offers equal value in exchange for whatever one procures.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀fọ́ kì í sún ẹ̀fọ́ sọ́hùn-ún.
Target_Text_En: Vegetables do not push vegetables out of the way.
Cultural_Context: One must respects others’ claims as one asserts one’s own.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀gàn ni ‘‘Hẹ̀".
Target_Text_En: A sneer is a mere indication of jealousy.
Cultural_Context: Let us acknowledge achievements when we see them and not sneer in envy.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀gàn ò pé kóyin má dùn.
Target_Text_En: Detraction does not rob honey of its sweet ness.
Cultural_Context: People’s failure to acknowledge one’s achievements does not detract from their value; one’s ability to thrive does not depend on other people’s approval.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní da eérú leérú ńtọ̀; eléte lète ńyé; oun a bá ṣe ní ńyéni.
Target_Text_En: Ashes blow toward the thrower; the plotter alone knows what he or she is plotting; one is privy only to that which one is involved in.
Cultural_Context: Evil recoils on those who plot evil, and those who are visited with evil must know what actions of theirs caused it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní fúnni lẹ́gbàá ò ṣeun bí ẹni a fún.
Target_Text_En: The person who gives six pence deserves less praise than the person to whom it is given.
Cultural_Context: Whoever gives a trifle as a gift is less to be valued than the person who accepts such a gift.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a bá ṣe lóore tí kò dúpẹ́, bí a bá ṣe é níkà kò níí dùn ún.
Target_Text_En: The person who shows no gratitude when he or she is done a favor will feel no hurt when he or she is done an injury.
Cultural_Context: Ungrateful people deserve to be deliberately hurt.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí a kò fókèlà ńgàn.
Target_Text_En: People we do not like are the ones we sneer at.
Cultural_Context: One can always find fault with people one does not like.

Source_Text_Yo: Èyí tí kò kíni "kú àbọ̀" pàdánùú kúulẹ.
Target_Text_En: The person who does not give one ‘‘Welcome’’ forfeits the arriving person’s salutation to those already there
Cultural_Context: Courtesies and discourtesies are repaid in kind.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí kò níyàwó kì í bí àbíkú.
Target_Text_En: A man who has no wife does not father born-to-die children.
Cultural_Context: Misfortunes have their fortunate aspects.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó bá dẹ bìtì kágbó ní ńpa orí kágbó.
Target_Text_En: The person who sets traps all over the for est is the one who has to wander all over the forest.
Cultural_Context: One will have to live with the consequences of one’s actions.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó fọni ní àfẹlówó, iwọ ní ńfúnni jẹ.
Target_Text_En: A woman who marries one even though one paid no dowry feeds one nothing but gall.
Cultural_Context: One cannot expect much from something one acquires free or too cheaply.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó lẹrú ló lẹrù.
Target_Text_En: The owner of the slave also owns the luggage [he carries].
Cultural_Context: Appendages go with the main item.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó mọ iyì-i wúrà là ńtà á fún.
Target_Text_En: One sells gold only to those who appreci ate its value.
Cultural_Context: Do not squander treasure on those incapable of appreciating it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó pa èèyàn ni yó ru òkú; ẹni tó f koto ejò ni yó gbèé e.
Target_Text_En: It is the person who kills another person who will carry the corpse; it is the person who breaks the gourd housing a snake who will carry the snake.
Cultural_Context: Each person is re sponsible for the consequences of his or her actions.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó se ọbẹ̀ tí kò dùn, a ní kí òrìṣá pa á; ẹni tí kò sè ńkọ́?
Target_Text_En: The person who makes a stew that is not delicious, we ask the gods to kill; what about the person who did not cook anything?
Cultural_Context: We should not overreact to other people’s minor flaws.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó ṣe ọ̀ràn òtùfù ní ńkíyè sí ẹ̀hìnkùlé.
Target_Text_En: It is a person who has done something that calls for the torch [light] who must keep a close watch on his back yard.
Cultural_Context: If one has done something underhanded, one has good reason to be apprehensive.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu asoṣọkọ́ kì í tó ọ̀rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The mouth of the person whose garment is a loincloth is never welcome in a discussion.
Cultural_Context: A shiftless person has no privileges in the community.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀pà pẹ̀lú olúwa-a rẹ̀ ní ńfojú winá.
Target_Text_En: Both the peanut and its owner will feel the effects of the fire.
Cultural_Context: The person belaboring others will also suffer from the exertion.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹran tó jẹ èbù ló ní ká gbé olówó-o rẹ̀ yílẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The goat that ate the yam cut for planting caused its owner to be flung to the ground.
Cultural_Context: One may be blameless and yet be dragged into trouble by the actions of those one is responsible for.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹṣin pòpóòrò kì í sáré ju ẹni tó gùn ún lọ
Target_Text_En: A cornstalk horse does not gallop faster than its rider. I
Cultural_Context: The limit of one’s effort is the limit of one’s reward.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbẹ́ lẹtu ḿbá erin gbé.
Target_Text_En: The antelope shares the forest with the ele phant as its home.
Cultural_Context: The lowliest creature has a claim to some space just as the mightiest has.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkà a máa gbó; ìkà a máa tọ́; àtisùn ìkà ni kò sunwọ̀n.
Target_Text_En: The wicked may live long, and the wicked may survive long, but the end of the wicked is never pleasant.
Cultural_Context: However long the wicked succeeds, he or she comes to grief in the end.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkàtè-é forí gbùsì; oun tí ńpẹja-á wà nísàlẹ̀ omi.
Target_Text_En: The stick to which the fishhook line is tied receives the curses on its head, but what kills the fish is under the surface of the water.
Cultural_Context: Sometimes one’s position makes one bear the blame for others’ misdeeds.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkòkò tí ńse ẹyìn, ẹyìn ni yó fọ̀ọ́ ọ.
Target_Text_En: The pot used for cooking palm fruits will be broken by palm fruits in the end.
Cultural_Context: Those who live dangerously die dangerously.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú ogun ní ńpa akíkanjú; ikú odò ní ńpa òmùwẹ̀; ikú ara-ríré ní ńpa arẹwà, màjà màsá ní ńpa onítìjú; òwò tádàá bá m ní ńká àdá léhín
Target_Text_En: It is death related to warfare that kills the warrior; it is the death associated with the river that kills the swimmer; it is the death attendant on preening that kills the beautiful person; wondering whether to stand and fight or run kills the easily embarrassed per son; the trade that the cutlass knows knocks out its teeth.
Cultural_Context: Each person’s bane is closely connected to his or her calling.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú ọmọ ní ńpa ayíntalẹ̀
Target_Text_En: It is death that comes of having children that kills the grub.
Cultural_Context: Some obligations carry deadly risks with them.

Source_Text_Yo: Imú kì í tóbi kó gba r ẹnu sọ.
Target_Text_En: The nose cannot get so big that it takes the speech out of the mouth.
Cultural_Context: No one, however mighty, may usurp tthe rights of others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìpín àìṣẹ̀ ni yó pa aláròká.
Target_Text_En: The protective mystical force of the innocent will kill whoever speaks ill about him or her.
Cultural_Context: Whoever spreads scandal about an inno cent person will answer to the powers of the universe.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣẹ́ ibi, èrè ibi á tálẹ.
Target_Text_En: The suffering that results from doing evil, the rewards for doing evil, will last until nighttime [i.e., until old age].
Cultural_Context: The reward for wickedness is not fleeting

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kéré lóòrúnmàgbà.
Target_Text_En: The reward for wickedness is not fleeting.)
Cultural_Context: Not Provided

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣòkú ni ìjogún.
Target_Text_En: One’s manner of performing the burial de termines how one inherits.
Cultural_Context: One’s claim to inheritance is dependent on how worthy a survivor one proves oneself.

Source_Text_Yo: Iṣu ẹni ní ńki ọwọ́ ẹni bọ epo.
Target_Text_En: It is on account of one’s yams that one’s fingers come to be soiled by palm oil.
Cultural_Context: Said when one is forced to endure some indignity because of the behavior of others close to one.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìtà a ta olè là ńta adóhunmọ́.
Target_Text_En: The terms with which one sells the thief are the same as those one applies to the false accuser.
Cultural_Context: The thief and the perjurer deserve the same fate.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìwà adìẹ ní ńwípé ká tu ìyẹ́ ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is the chicken’s behavior that caused its wing feathers to be plucked.
Cultural_Context: People by their own habits suggest what restrictions should be placed on them.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìwà awó ní ńpe awó lẹ́tù
Target_Text_En: It is the guinea fowl’s behavior that makes one know it as a guinea fowl.
Cultural_Context: By their habits shall people be known.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìwọ̀fà ẹgbàá àtolúwa-a rẹ̀ ní ńsin ẹrú.
Target_Text_En: The person pawned for 2,000 cowries [six pence in old British currency] will share the slave labor with the creditor.
Cultural_Context: One cannot expect a great deal of service from something acquired on the cheap.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìwọ̀fà tí kò wá ní ńjókú-ùgbó lójú olówó.
Target_Text_En: The pawn who does not come to work is the one the creditor regards as a deadbeat.
Cultural_Context: A person who does what is expected of him or her avoids criticism.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyá kà, ọmọ́ kà ni òwò.
Target_Text_En: Mother counts and then the child [or daughter] counts; such is the practice in trading.
Cultural_Context: In a joint venture each person involved must do his or her share.

Source_Text_Yo: Iyán díkókó, kì í ṣẹjọ́ oníṣu; ọkàá mẹrẹ, kì í ṣẹjọ́ elélùbọ́.
Target_Text_En: If the pounded yam is lumpy, the fault does not belong to the seller of the yams; if the yam-flour meal is ill cooked, the fault does not belong to the seller of the yam flour.
Cultural_Context: One should not blame those from whom one obtained materials if in the end one botched their use.

Source_Text_Yo: Iye ajá bí lajá ńṣọ́.
Target_Text_En: The dog looks after whatever the number of pups in its litter.
Cultural_Context: One is entitled only to what one owns.

Source_Text_Yo: Jagun-jagun ní ńjẹ obì; àgbẹ̀ jẹ awùsá ṣẹnu yángí-yángí
Target_Text_En: It is the warrior that eats kola nuts; the farmer eats only awùsá nuts, which make the mouth bitter.[?]K
Cultural_Context: To the valiant belong the best of the spoils; the rest get only the leavings.

Source_Text_Yo: Ká fi inú ṣèkà, ká fòde ṣòótọ́, kan-kan lara ńnini; ohun tí ḿbini kò níí ṣàì bini wò.
Target_Text_En: If one is kind outwardly but secretly wicked, one is beset by unease; whatever is supposed to call one to account will not fail to do so.
Cultural_Context: Wickedness, however well concealed, will not go unpunished.

Source_Text_Yo: Kàkà ká fi ọmọ oyè joyè, wọ́n ńwá ọmọ aṣẹwé.
Target_Text_En: Instead of placing the legitimate heir on the throne, they go in search of the son of a seller of leaves.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who bypass gems in preference for pebbles.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí ikú má pa ẹni tí ńdáni lóro; kí òrìṣà má jẹ̀ẹ́ kí ǹkan ṣe ẹni tí ńṣe èèyàn níkà; bó pẹ́ títí orí ẹni a dáni
Target_Text_En: May death not take the person who deprives one of the things one needs; may the gods not permit anything to happen to the person who does wicked things to one; sooner or later one’s head will vindicate one
Cultural_Context: One should let evil people do their evil without seeking revenge; eventually they will reap what they have sown.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò tètè dé ò níí tètè lọ; ẹni ò tètè dáyé ò níí tètè lọ sọ́run.
Target_Text_En: The person who was not early in arriving will not be early in departing; the person who did not come into this world early will not go early to heaven. L
Cultural_Context: Older people should die before younger ones.

Source_Text_Yo: Má sọ lófin, òfin ní ńsọ ara ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Do not lay down the law; the law will lay itself down.
Cultural_Context: One does not need to be a vigi lante for the wrongdoer to come to grief.

Source_Text_Yo: Méjì kì í ko ọ̀bẹ́mu; bí kò bá rí mu yó rìí tà; bí kò bá rí tà yó rìí mu.
Target_Text_En: Two misfortunes will not befall a palm-wine tapster; if there is not enough to drink, there will be enough to sell; if there is not enough to sell, there will be enough to drink.
Cultural_Context: Every misfortune has its consolation

Source_Text_Yo: Egbejila
Target_Text_En: Compare the next entry.)
Cultural_Context: Not Provided

Source_Text_Yo: Méjì ni ìlẹ̀kùn; bí kò ṣí sínú a ṣí sóde; bí kò tì sínú a tì sóde.
Target_Text_En: Doors come in two different dispositions; if they do not open inward, they will open out ward; if they do not shut inward, they will shut outward.
Cultural_Context: One always has an option in the face of any difficulty. Compare the preceding entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Mọ̀ọ́ gún, mọ̀ọ́ tẹ̀, oníṣu ló niyán.
Target_Text_En: One may be an expert at pounding and mashing, but the pounded yam belongs to the owner of the yams. N
Cultural_Context: The owner’s claim is always superior to the helper’s.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrin kì í gba owó àlè tán kó ní gìnìsà ńṣe òun
Target_Text_En: A woman does not take a lover’s money and then complain of menorrhagia.
Cultural_Context: One should perform obligations for which one has received payment.

Source_Text_Yo: Ogun ní ńṣi ẹni mú; èpè kì í ṣi ẹni jà
Target_Text_En: A war might capture a person by mistake; a curse never affects one by mistake.
Cultural_Context: More often than not one’s misfortunes are the clear results of curses, not simply happen stance.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun ìdí là ńtà ra ìdí; bóbìnrín bá gba owó àlè a fi ràlẹ̀kẹ̀ sídìí.
Target_Text_En: It is something that pertains to the buttocks that one sells to buy buttocks; if a woman receives money from her paramour, she uses it to buy beads for her waist.
Cultural_Context: The profit from a venture should go to promoting that venture.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí a sọ síwájú là ḿbá; ohun tí a gbìn là ńwà; nígbàtí a ò sọ síwájú, tí a ò gbìn sẹ́hìn, kí la ó bàá?
Target_Text_En: Whatever one throws ahead is what one comes upon; whatever one plants is what one reaps; when one does not throw any thing ahead and does not plant anything, what can one expect to find later?
Cultural_Context: One can expect no profit without investment.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí a wá là ńrí.
Target_Text_En: One finds what one seeks.
Cultural_Context: Whatever befalls, it has most likely been invited.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó dé ló ní ká wáá wo òun.
Target_Text_En: It is the phenomenon that occurred which summoned people to come witness it.
Cultural_Context: If something did not attract people’s attention, they would not assemble to watch it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú àánú ti fọ́ tìkà ló kù.
Target_Text_En: Merciful eyes have gone blind; only wicked ones remain.
Cultural_Context: The time for mercy is past; now is the time for hardheartedness.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í rí arẹwà kó má kìí i.
Target_Text_En: The eyes never see a beautiful person with out acknowledging him or her.
Cultural_Context: Things that deserve one’s attention should receive it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í ti ọkọ kó má bàá ìyàwó ẹ̀ sọ̀rọ̀
Target_Text_En: A husband can never be so bashful that he cannot speak to his wife.
Cultural_Context: However reti cent one might be, some duties one must perform.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú ní ńyin-ni kòyè ó ṣèmín-ìn.
Target_Text_En: It is the eyes that praise one and cause one to do even better.
Cultural_Context: Approving eyes are an encouragement to do even better.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú olóko làgbàdó ṣe ńgbó.
Target_Text_En: The corn matures in the presence of the farmer.
Cultural_Context: An incantation or a prayer that the fruition of one’s efforts will happen in one’s lifetime.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú oníkàn nikàn-án ṣe ńwẹ̀wù ẹ̀jẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is in the presence of the locust-bean planter that the locust bean puts on a cloth of blood [or ripens]. On just deserts 447
Cultural_Context: One will know of the consequences of one’s actions.

Source_Text_Yo: Okùn-ún mú ẹlẹdà.
Target_Text_En: The noose has caught a trickster.
Cultural_Context: A person is hoist with his own petard.

Source_Text_Yo: Olókùnrùn tó jẹ iyán ogójì, tòun tiwọn ní ńre ogun.
Target_Text_En: The invalid who eats pounded yams worth 40 cowries: both he and the warriors will head for the war.
Cultural_Context: One cannot have a healthy appetite and also complain of ill health.

Source_Text_Yo: Omi kì í wọ́n ká má fi fún òde mu.
Target_Text_En: Water is never so scarce that one does not give some to the outdoor earth to drink.
Cultural_Context: However hard up one is, one will do those things that are essential.

Source_Text_Yo: Onídìí gègèrè ni yó gba ẹgbàá; ohun ẹ bá rí ẹ féléegun.
Target_Text_En: The person with a hefty backside is the one who deserves 2,000 cowries [six pence]; whatever else you can afford, give it to the bony person.
Cultural_Context: The better-endowed woman is the one to spend money on.

Source_Text_Yo: Oníyà ni yó jẹ èyí tó jù.
Target_Text_En: The person who earned the punishment will bear most of it.
Cultural_Context: The person respon sible for a problem will suffer most of its consequences.

Source_Text_Yo: Òòjọ́ là ńṣu imí àgbagbà.
Target_Text_En: The shit from a plantain meal comes on the same day. 448 rights and responsibilities
Cultural_Context: The consequences for certain actions are virtually immediate.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí ẹ̀ ló kún tí à ḿbá a fá a.
Target_Text_En: It is his head that has grown bushy and that we are helping him to groom.
Cultural_Context: It is because a person has erred that he is being lectured for his own good.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí òpómù: ó k ajá l dẹ; ajá mọdẹ tán ó pa orí bọ jẹ.
Target_Text_En: The monkey’s fortune: he taught the dog hunting; the dog became adept at hunting and killed the monkey for food.
Cultural_Context: A person one has helped may turn around to plot one’s destruction.

Source_Text_Yo: Òròmọ-adìẹ ò lè nù kí eégún gba òbúkọ
Target_Text_En: A young chick that goes missing cannot thereby justify the presentation of a he-goat to the masquerader as replacement. Ọ
Cultural_Context: The re placement or compensation for a thing must be commensurate with that thing.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀gá ni oníjó, gá ni arìnnà, gá ni àtè tó mú ẹyẹ lóòsì tí kò lè lọ.
Target_Text_En: The dancer is honorable; the wayfarer is honorable; also honorable is the birdlime that catches a bird and prevents it from flying off.
Cultural_Context: Anybody who performs a com mendable feat deserves honor.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀gá tà, gá ò tà, owó aláàárù á pé.
Target_Text_En: Whether the master’s wares sell or not, the porter’s fees must be paid in full.
Cultural_Context: Whether you use the services well or not, the pro vider’s fee must be paid.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀gọ́ tà, ọ̀gọ̀ ò tà, owó aláàárù á pé.
Target_Text_En: Whether the foolish trader profits or not, the porter’s fees must be paid in full.
Cultural_Context: One’s folly will not absolve one of obligations.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ gbogbo ni tolè, ọj kan ni tolóhun.
Target_Text_En: Every day belongs to the thief; one day be longs to the owner.
Cultural_Context: The evildoer may enjoy prolonged success, but the day he is exposed is the one that matters.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kọ̀ṣẹ́ ò mọ ìpè búburú, kí ńṣò mọ ìpè rere
Target_Text_En: A shirker does not know which summons will be taxing and which will be reward ing.
Cultural_Context: People who will answer no call cannot know which is profitable.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ kì í forí pẹkàn kó mú bàbá dání; iye ọmọ lọmọ ḿmú lọ
Target_Text_En: A child does not emerge from a womb with its father in tow; the child emerges all by itself.
Cultural_Context: A child who gets in trouble cannot depend on his father to bear the conse quences.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọdé kì í wọ oko èèsì kó má jo
Target_Text_En: A child does not venture into a bush of stinging nettles and escape being stung.
Cultural_Context: One cannot escape the consequences of one’s actions.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọwọ́ kékeré la fi ńgba ńlá.
Target_Text_En: It is with a small hand that one provokes a big one.
Cultural_Context: A weakling should take care not to attract the attention of a bully through provocative behavior.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọwọ́ kì í pẹ́ nihò àkèekèe, àfi bí a ò bá bá a nílé
Target_Text_En: The hand does not stay long in a scorpion’s hole unless the scorpion is not at home.
Cultural_Context: Unless he is somehow incapacitated, a vindictive person does not delay before ex tracting vengeance; unless the world has turned upside down, retribution for certain offenses is swift.

Source_Text_Yo: Tàkúté Ọlọrun, kò sẹ́ni tí kò lè mú; bó májá, a mẹ́ran, a sì mú adìẹ òkókó.
Target_Text_En: No one is beyond being caught in God’s mousetrap; it catches the dog, catches the goat, and catches even the strapping chicken.
Cultural_Context: No one is beyond God’s judgment.

Source_Text_Yo: À bá m a kò ṣe é; a ṣé tán ó di aápọn.
Target_Text_En: Had one known, one would not have done it; having been done, it becomes a bother.
Cultural_Context: If one knew what the consequences of cer tain actions would be, one would avoid them, but hindsight does not diminish the consequences.

Source_Text_Yo: À bá sọ pé omi ni yó se ẹja jinná, à pé irọ́.
Target_Text_En: Had anyone said that water would cook fish, one would have argued the opposite.
Cultural_Context: Water is the natural medium for fish; who would have thought that it could also be the death of fish?

Source_Text_Yo: A bọ́ ike lọ́wọ́ ọ̀tún, a fi bọ ọwọ́ òsì; lọ́wọ́ lọ́wọ́ niké wà.
Target_Text_En: One removes an ivory bangle from one’s right wrist and slips it onto the left wrist; for all that, the bangle remains on one’s wrist.
Cultural_Context: The gesture or effort has not significantly altered the status quo ante.

Source_Text_Yo: A bú ológbò ní a-bẹ̀rẹ̀kẹ́ kókangiri; a ha púrọ́ mọ́ ọ.
Target_Text_En: We insult the cat as being bulge-cheeked; do we misspeak?
Cultural_Context: The insult is a justified description of a cat.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dé ìgbàro èṣí ká fòhun okòó kù.
Target_Text_En: One does not get to last year’s farm and not find things worth 20 cowries.
Cultural_Context: One cannot become so destitute that one is left with absolutely nothing.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dé ilé arúgbó lọ́fẹ̀ẹ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not go to an old person’s home for nothing.
Cultural_Context: Nothing in life is free.
