Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dé ilé ikú ká fóhórí kù; bí a ò bá tútù, a ó bàá gbígbẹ.
Target_Text_En: One does not get to Death’s home and fail to find heads; if one does not find fresh ones, one will find dry ones.
Cultural_Context: The sole custodian of a commodity is unlikely to experience a lack of it.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dẹ igbó ká pẹja; a kì í gbọ́n odò ká pa àfè.
Target_Text_En: One does not hunt in the bush and kill fish; one does not drain a river and kill a grass mouse.
Cultural_Context: Some occurrences would be impos sible and unexpected in certain places.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dó ọkọ dá gbèsè; ọmọ la fi ḿbí.
Target_Text_En: One does not make love to a person and get into debt; it is childbirth that results.
Cultural_Context: A routine and pleasurable activity should not lead to disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í dùn yùngbà ká fi wé ìbòsí ìgárá
Target_Text_En: One does not make a joyful noise that can be compared to the alarm that announces a theft.
Cultural_Context: Joyousness should express itself differently from disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í fi ojoojúmọ́ rọ́kọ ẹni; ọmọ ẹni kì í ní ọbàkan.
Target_Text_En: One does not see one’s husband every day; one’s child does not have a half-brother.
Cultural_Context: Never expect the impossible.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbélé mọ ẹni ogún pa.
Target_Text_En: One cannot remain at home and know who has been killed in battle.
Cultural_Context: There is no knowledge like firsthand knowledge.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbélé mọ ogun tí ò níí dùn.
Target_Text_En: One does not stay at home and know which battle will be unpleasant.
Cultural_Context: Only an eye witness knows the truth of an affair.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í gbin àlùbọ́sà kó hu ẹ̀fọ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not plant onions and have [the ground] yield spinach.
Cultural_Context: What one plants is what one reaps.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í há ẹran kí òróòro má gba tiẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not butcher and share out an ani mal’s meat without the gallbladder taking its share.
Cultural_Context: Never seek to do rightful claimants out of what they deserve.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í já lórí pẹ ká tún jọba nísàlẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not fall from atop a palm tree and then become a king below.
Cultural_Context: One does not reap glory from disgrace

Source_Text_Yo: Oṣogbo ko gba agba.
Target_Text_En: One does not reap glory from disgrace.)
Cultural_Context: Not Provided

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í jà nígbó ráhùn ọpa.
Target_Text_En: One does not fight in the bush and lament a lack of sticks.
Cultural_Context: There can be no drought in a deluge.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í jẹ aládùn méjì pọ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not enjoy two pleasures at the same time.
Cultural_Context: One cannot have everything at once.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í jẹ ejò ká jẹ ogún inú ẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not eat a snake and eat the un born snakes inside it.
Cultural_Context: It is not done to have an affair with a mother and also with her daughter.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í jẹ aládùn méjì pọ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not enjoy two pleasures at the same time.
Cultural_Context: One cannot have everything at once.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í jẹ òkèlè lérí òkèlè.
Target_Text_En: One does not eat one morsel [or mouthful] atop another.
Cultural_Context: Do things at a seemly pace, not in a rushed manner.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í kó imí tán kó tún máa rùn.
Target_Text_En: One does not remove excrement and yet en dure its stink.
Cultural_Context: Once a problem is resolved, there should be an end to its attendant bad blood.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í lápá-a bàbá ká má nìí ti ìyá.
Target_Text_En: One does not have relatives on the father’s side and not have relatives on the mother’s.
Cultural_Context: There is complementarity in all things.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í rí ewú lọ́sàn-án.
Target_Text_En: One does not see the nocturnal bush rat at high noon.
Cultural_Context: Everything at its proper time.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í rí idà lọ́rùn eṣinṣin.
Target_Text_En: One does not see a sword at the neck of a fly.
Cultural_Context: It is unnecessary to use a sledge ham mer to kill a fly. Also, some approaches are improper in tackling certain problems.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í rí kékeré ẹkùn.
Target_Text_En: One never sees an insignificant leopard.
Cultural_Context: Never minimize any danger.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ro rere ká má ro búburú.
Target_Text_En: One does not think of the good without thinking also of the bad.
Cultural_Context: There is not good without evil.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í ṣe méjì ní Mèkà: a kì í kírun ní Mèkà, ká tún nájà ní Mèkà.
Target_Text_En: One does not do two things in Mecca: one does not worship in Mecca [performing the hadj] and also trade in Mecca.
Cultural_Context: Always concentrate on one major project at a time.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í tẹ̀hìn akiṣalẹ wúre
Target_Text_En: One cannot make good-luck charms without the akiṣalẹ plant.
Cultural_Context: No venture can succeed in the absence of the condition most essential for its success.

Source_Text_Yo: A kì í wáyé ká má da nǹkan; oun a ó dà la ò mọ̀.
Target_Text_En: One does not come into this world without becoming something; what one does not know is what one will become.
Cultural_Context: Everybody has a future, but no one knows what it is ahead of time.

Source_Text_Yo: À ńdín i, kò dùn ni à ńwí pé adìẹ́ itan mẹ́ta.
Target_Text_En: It is when one fries a chicken but it does not taste good that one says it had three thighs.
Cultural_Context: A bad cook quarrels with his ingre dients.

Source_Text_Yo: A ò mọ ibi orí ḿbá ẹsẹ̀-ẹ́ rè.
Target_Text_En: No one knows where the head will accompany the feet.
Cultural_Context: The future is hidden from us.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí in this instance is again not the physiologi cal head but the repository of a person’s destiny The proverb, despite its wording, actually means that no one knows where orí will guide or conduct the feet.
Target_Text_En: Orí in this instance is again not the physiologi cal head but the repository of a person’s destiny
Cultural_Context: It can, of course, also be used to suggest that although orí directs one’s destiny, it is the feet that do the walking, and they may conduct orí wherever it suits them.

Source_Text_Yo: A tẹ́ní bẹẹrẹ kò sí oǹdá; a pàjùbà bẹẹrẹ kò sí oǹkọ.
Target_Text_En: We spread the divination mat wide, but there is no client; we clear the field for plant ing, but there is no tiller.
Cultural_Context: Some human aspirations come to nought.

Source_Text_Yo: A ti oko ìroko de oko ìrokòtò.
Target_Text_En: We have gone from hoeing a farm to hoe ing a gully.
Cultural_Context: Matters have gone from bad to worse.

Source_Text_Yo: Abẹ́rẹ́ bọ́ lọ́wọ́ adẹ́tẹ̀ ó dète; ọ̀rán balẹ̀ ó dèrò.
Target_Text_En: A needle drops from a leper’s hand and presents an impossible problem; a grievous matter hits the ground and imposes deep contemplation.
Cultural_Context: Certain problems defy easy solution.

Source_Text_Yo: Abiyamọ ló mọwọ́ ọ̀já.
Target_Text_En: It is a nursing mother that is adept at tying the child-support strip.
Cultural_Context: One cannot beat an expert at his or her trade.

Source_Text_Yo: Adùn-únṣe bí àlejò omi.
Target_Text_En: Painless hospitality, like one requiring only the offering of water.
Cultural_Context: A good deed that en tails hardly any cost is easily and cheerfully performed.

Source_Text_Yo: Àfẹ́dànù ni tìyàngbò.
Target_Text_En: To-be-blown-away-in-the-wind is the fate of fallen leaves.
Cultural_Context: The person this incantational proverb is directed at will not escape an evil fate, just as fallen leaves cannot avoid being blown about by the wind.

Source_Text_Yo: Afẹ́fẹ́ lẹlẹ ò jẹ́ kà gbé orí igi; àgbàrá òjò ò jọkà gbé ilẹ̀-ẹ́lẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Turbulent winds dissuade one from living atop a tree; flash floods dissuade one from living on the ground. means ‘‘fan’’ but also ‘‘one who pleads’’ or ‘‘intercessor.’’ The second meaning comes from the formation of the word as a b b .
Cultural_Context: Life offers no risk-free options. one who begs, a peculiar rendition of ‘‘makes’’ plea

Source_Text_Yo: Àfowórọ́wó laláròóbọ̀-ọ́ fi là; àfowórọ́wó sì laláròóbọ̀-ọ́ fi dígbèsè.
Target_Text_En: It is by reinvesting his profits that the retailer makes his fortune; it is also by reinvesting his profits that the retailer gets into debt.
Cultural_Context: Commerce is subject to uncertainty and luck.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgùntàn kì í yọ̀wo.
Target_Text_En: Sheep never sprout horns.
Cultural_Context: Certain things can, and should, never be.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbà-ì-kà lolè ńgbowó.
Target_Text_En: Snatching-without-counting is the way a thief takes money.
Cultural_Context: The evildoer seldom has peace of mind.

Source_Text_Yo: Agbárí ò ní mùdùn-múdùn.
Target_Text_En: The skull has no marrow.
Cultural_Context: One cannot get blood out of a turnip.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbásí mú ààtàn gélé.
Target_Text_En: Constant addition of garbage makes a mountain of the garbage dump.
Cultural_Context: Little things add up.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbélémọ̀ kan ò sí; awo ní ńsọ fúnni.
Target_Text_En: There is no medicine that enables one to know, without leaving home, what is taking place abroad; only compacts [with those who know] enlighten one.
Cultural_Context: There is no substitute for being there.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbẹ̀ gbin ohun gbogbo má gbin iyọ̀
Target_Text_En: A farmer plants everything but not salt.
Cultural_Context: Desirable as salt is, one cannot grow it.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbẹ̀ ni baba oníṣòwò.
Target_Text_En: The farmer is the father of the trader.
Cultural_Context: No profession is as venerable as farming.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbẹ̀ ò moko àrolà; oníṣòwò ò mọ ọjà ànápẹ̀kún
Target_Text_En: A farmer does not know which planting will bring prosperity; a trader does not know which transaction will be his last.
Cultural_Context: No one knows the future.

Source_Text_Yo: Àgbìgbò lọba ẹyẹ.
Target_Text_En: The hornbill is the king of birds.
Cultural_Context: Some people are superior to others.

Source_Text_Yo: Agbọ́n ńsẹ́; oyin ńsọ; ojú ọmọ olóko ló wú yìí.
Target_Text_En: The wasp denies responsibility; the bee de nies responsibility; yet here is the farmer’s son with his eyes all swollen.
Cultural_Context: A crime has obviously been committed, yet all possible culprits deny responsibility.

Source_Text_Yo: Ahéré ní ńkẹ́hìn oko; ààtàn ní ńkẹ́hìn ilé.
Target_Text_En: At the demise of the farm the hut survives; at the demise of the house the garbage dump survives.
Cultural_Context: When the ephemeral is gone, the permanent remains.

Source_Text_Yo: Àìfárí kì í ṣe ọ̀bọ ní túúlu; àìjẹun lèèwọ̀-ọ rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Want of a shave is no headache to the mon key; it is want of food that it cannot abide.
Cultural_Context: Certain things are luxuries; certain things are essentials.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjànàkú kì í sòpá kínú bí ọlọ́dẹ.
Target_Text_En: The elephant’s development of hydrocele does not anger the hunter.
Cultural_Context: One cannot be dismayed because one’s enemy has been visited by disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjànàkú ò lókàn; ọba tí yó mùú erin so ò tìjẹ.
Target_Text_En: The elephant tolerates no stakes; the king that will tether the elephant has not been crowned.
Cultural_Context: Some people are beyond any body’s control.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjẹ́ ké lánàá, ọmọ́ kú lónìí; ta ni ò mọ̀ pé àjẹ́ àná ló pọmọ jẹ?
Target_Text_En: A witch announced her presence yester day, and a child dies today; who does not know that yesterday’s witch killed the child?
Cultural_Context: When the evidence suggests an obvious conclusion, one should not shy away from it

Source_Text_Yo: Yoruba town.
Target_Text_En: Ìlọrin is a northern
Cultural_Context: As the proverb indicates, other branches of the Yoruba family have a low opinion of Ìlọrin people.

Source_Text_Yo: Kà rí ọ rán is a way of saying in Ìjèṣà, ‘‘ Come here a minute.’’
Target_Text_En: Kà rí ọ rán is a way of saying in Ìjèṣà, ‘‘
Cultural_Context: Not Provided

Source_Text_Yo: Àjẹ́ lápo, ojúu rẹ̀-ẹ́ rọ̀
Target_Text_En: The witch licks palm oil and becomes calm.
Cultural_Context: A balm masters wild dispositions.

Source_Text_Yo: Àjẹ-i-padà-wálé ó jẹ ká mọ ọdẹ adìẹ.
Target_Text_En: Its foraging-without-returning-home prevents people from knowing what a hunter the chicken is
Cultural_Context: Without seeing the kill, people will not credit the hunter

Source_Text_Yo: Àkàṣù ò níbií rè lágbọ̀n.
Target_Text_En: The corn meal has nowhere to go in the basket.
Cultural_Context: A treasure is not lost in a safe.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkéte kékeré ò gba èèyàn méjì
Target_Text_En: A tiny bed will not accommodate two people.
Cultural_Context: Some deficiencies cannot be fi nessed.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkẹ̀hìnsí onígbé, bí ẹni tí ńkébòsí.
Target_Text_En: The back view of a person with goiter gives the impression that he or she is hailing someone.
Cultural_Context: Seeing something from a disadvantageous perspective is likely to mislead.

Source_Text_Yo: Akọ ikú tí ńpa ojú àrùn mọ́.
Target_Text_En: Masculine death, that which closes the eyes of a disease.
Cultural_Context: It is a determined death that sees the end of an illness.

Source_Text_Yo: Akọ ológbò-ó mú owó rá
Target_Text_En: A male cat renders the money invested on it unprofitable.
Cultural_Context: One cannot expect kittens of tomcats.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkọsẹ̀bá, èyí tí ńjẹ́ ìfà.
Target_Text_En: An unexpected find: free booty.
Cultural_Context: Unanticipated good fortune is free for the taking.

Source_Text_Yo: Àkúdin ò kọminú àáké.
Target_Text_En: The heartwood fears no axe.
Cultural_Context: Hardy souls need fear no adversaries.

Source_Text_Yo: A-kú-mā-tóó-élèjì rù, ó dàrù pa ẹnìkan.
Target_Text_En: He-who-dies-but-is-too-small-for-two people-to-carry constitutes a load that weighs down one person.
Cultural_Context: A matter that falls in the crack between two categories is a troublesome thing.

Source_Text_Yo: Àlà funfun, ọ̀rẹ́ òrìṣà.
Target_Text_En: White cloth, friend of the gods.
Cultural_Context: Each occasion has its special requirements.

Source_Text_Yo: Aláàfáà, ìmàlé adodo; ó ní bí òun ò bá dé ibú òun ò mu.
Target_Text_En: Muslim priest, inhabitant of the conical house, vows that until he reaches the deep, he will not drink.
Cultural_Context: It is a choosy priest who will drink nothing but water from the deep est part of the sea.

Source_Text_Yo: Àlàárì, baba aṣọ.
Target_Text_En: Reddish hand-woven cloth, father of all cloths.
Cultural_Context: No cloth is more glorious than àlàárì.

Source_Text_Yo: Alágbàtà ní ńsọ ọjà-á dọ̀wọ́n.
Target_Text_En: It is the retail merchant who makes mer chandise dear.
Cultural_Context: Caretakers are often more punctilious and stingy than owners.

Source_Text_Yo: Alágbe ò kú lỌ́yọ̀ọ́.
Target_Text_En: A beggar does not die in y .
Cultural_Context: Other people’s generosity will save the destitute from starvation.

Source_Text_Yo: Alájàpá ò lẹ́ran láyà.
Target_Text_En: The tortoise has no flesh on its chest.
Cultural_Context: It is futile to seek meat on a turtle’s chest.

Source_Text_Yo: Alápámálèṣí, baba lẹ.
Target_Text_En: A person with sturdy arms but no will to work is the laziest of creatures.
Cultural_Context: Strong arms that will not work are lazy arms.

Source_Text_Yo: Aláròyé, olókotoro, onítìjú àwòko tí ńgbónu nínú oko; ó délé tán ó ṣẹnu mẹ́rẹ́n.
Target_Text_En: Loquacious, forward person, bashful bird that boasts on the farm; on reaching home it keeps its peace.
Cultural_Context: Boasting is easy where no one will dare one to prove oneself.

Source_Text_Yo: Alásẹ mọ̀ pé ó ńjò kó tó rà á; ẹní hún mọ̀ pé ó ńjò kó tó tà á; iṣẹ́-ẹ jíjò ni wọ́ fi ńṣe.
Target_Text_En: The owner of the sieve knew that it leaked before buying it; the weaver of the sieve knew that it leaked before selling it; after all, it is used for tasks that call for leaking.
Cultural_Context: If the particulars of a transaction are not kept secret, no party involved has grounds for complaint. And, differences are proper, for circumstances and needs are not the same.

Source_Text_Yo: Aláyìn-ínsí ò lódó; ẹnu gbó-ń-gbó lodó o wọn.
Target_Text_En: The interfering person owns no mortar; his mortar is his overactive mouth.
Cultural_Context: The interfering person’s only asset is his mouth.

Source_Text_Yo: Àlejò tí kò wá là ńpa àgbà àgùntàn dè
Target_Text_En: It is a visitor who fails to show up in whose truisms honor one killed a large sheep.
Cultural_Context: A safe lie is one no one can disprove.

Source_Text_Yo: A-le-koko-bí-ọsán: egbòó jinná, ohùn ò jinná
Target_Text_En: A thing as resistant as bowstring: the ulcer heals, but a spoken word does not heal.
Cultural_Context: Words are as tough as bowstrings; while wounds may heal, the marks words leave do not heal.

Source_Text_Yo: Alẹ́ tí kò ti ojú ẹni lẹ́, a kì í mọ òkùnkùn-un rẹ̀ẹ́ rìn.
Target_Text_En: A night that does not fall in one’s pres ence, one never knows how to walk in its darkness.
Cultural_Context: A person who does not know the origin of an affair will surely err if he attempts to intervene in it.

Source_Text_Yo: Àlòkùàdá ò jọ obìnrin lójú
Target_Text_En: A secondhand machete does not impress a woman.
Cultural_Context: Newness is all-important to a woman, even when the newness does not mean greater efficiency.

Source_Text_Yo: Àlọ la rí; a ò rábọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The departure is all we saw; we did not see the return.
Cultural_Context: Much was made of the be ginning of a project, but that was the last anyone heard of it. This is an abbreviated version of 66.

Source_Text_Yo: Àlùkò-ó fínní; ìbọn rẹ̀-ẹ́ fínní
Target_Text_En: Àlùkò is well groomed, and his gun is well groomed.
Cultural_Context: The person concerned is pains taking and particular about his affairs.

Source_Text_Yo: A-mòòkùn-ṣolè, bí ọba ayé ò rí ọ, tọ̀run ńwò ọ́.
Target_Text_En: Person-who-lies-low-to-do-evil: if the king on earth does not see you, the king of heaven is looking at you.
Cultural_Context: Nothing one does is hidden from God.

Source_Text_Yo: Àmọ́dún ò rííriì; ká múra ká síṣẹ.
Target_Text_En: One year hence is not unforeseeable; let us gird ourselves and set to work.
Cultural_Context: A year of grace is soon over; one should conscien tiously do what is expected of one.

Source_Text_Yo: Amọ́nilójú ò bániwí; kọ̀bì-kọ̀bì ló ńwò
Target_Text_En: A-person-who-looks-disdainfully-at-one but says nothing: it is simply that there is something the matter with his or her sight.
Cultural_Context: Disdainful looks cannot kill; what is more, they do not become the looker.

Source_Text_Yo: A-mọ̀ràn-mòwe ní ńlàdí ọ̀rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: It is a-sage-who-knows-proverbs that re solves disputes.
Cultural_Context: Proverbs are a means of settling differences.

Source_Text_Yo: Àmù tí a fi ńse iṣu ò lè mọ̀ọ́ w bí èyí tí a fi ńpọnmi.
Target_Text_En: The pot used for cooking yams cannot know swimming as well as the pot used for draw ing water.
Cultural_Context: In one’s métier one is master.

Source_Text_Yo: Amúniṣẹ̀sín ẹ̀tẹ̀ tí ńmúni lọ́gangan imú
Target_Text_En: A-thing-that-exposes-one-to-ridicule, lep rosy that attacks one on the tip of one’s nose.
Cultural_Context: A disfigurement that afflicts one in the most conspicuous place will surely be laughed at.

Source_Text_Yo: Àpáàdì ní ńṣíwájú ọ̀fọ̀nná.
Target_Text_En: It is the potsherd that precedes the live coal gatherer
Cultural_Context: Events should take their proper order, and people should observe the proper order of precedence.

Source_Text_Yo: Àparò, aṣọ-ọ̀ rẹ́ ṣe pọ́n báyìí? O ní ìgbà wo ni aṣọ òun ò níí pọ́n?  Ọ̀sán jíjẹ, òru sísùn, oúnjẹ̀ ò ṣéé fi sílẹ̀ lọ́sàn-án; orun ò ṣéé fi sílẹ̀ lóru.
Target_Text_En: Partridge, how come your dress is so red [dirty]? He said, how would his dress not be red [dirty]? In the afternoon grubbing for food, at night sleeping: one cannot leave off food in the afternoon, and one cannot leave off sleep at night.
Cultural_Context: The priorities of the self-indulgent are always inverted.

Source_Text_Yo: Àparò ńgba ikú oníkú kú, áḿbǹtorí ikú ara-a rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The partridge falls prey to the death meant for others, let alone a death meant for it.
Cultural_Context: A person whose destiny is to be a habitual victim will not escape his or her fate.

Source_Text_Yo: Àparò ò ga ju ara-a wọn lọ, àfi èyí tó gun ebè.
Target_Text_En: No partridge is taller than another except for those [standing] on earth mounds.
Cultural_Context: Said of people among whom there is nothing to choose.

Source_Text_Yo: Apata-á ríkú kẹ̀hìn si í; apata ní ńgbani lógun.
Target_Text_En: The shield sees death and presents its back to it; it is the shield that saves one in battle.
Cultural_Context: There is nothing like the shield when it comes to defying death.

Source_Text_Yo: Àrán nìparí ọ̀ṣọ́.
Target_Text_En: Velvet is the ultimate in finery.
Cultural_Context: There is no cloth more resplendent than velvet.

Source_Text_Yo: A-rí-erin-látẹ ò mọyì erin.
Target_Text_En: One-who-sees-an-elephant-on-a-tray does not appreciate an elephant.
Cultural_Context: Those who have not seen you on your home ground cannot appreciate you.

Source_Text_Yo: A-rí-jẹ-níjà ò níṣe mìíràn àfi ìjà.
Target_Text_En: The person who profits from quarrels has no other pursuit than quarreling. The cooking hearth does not stay hot until nighttime.
Cultural_Context: It is most difficult to wean people from their bad habits. There is no difficulty that does not have its moments of release. There is no difficulty without an end. Compare 4734.

Source_Text_Yo: Àrò kì í jóni lọjá lásán; ọmọ aráyé ní ńfanná sí i
Target_Text_En: A cooking hearth does not burn one’s feet on its own; it is people who stoke fire in it.
Cultural_Context: There is no misfortune behind which one will not find other people’s machination.

Source_Text_Yo: Àrò kì í rẹrù kó má só.
Target_Text_En: A cooking hearth does not bear a load without eventually setting it down
Cultural_Context: There is no problem that does not come to an end.

Source_Text_Yo: Àròyé ò kún àjọ
Target_Text_En: A lengthy explanation will not fill the till.
Cultural_Context: Excuses are a poor substitute for fulfilling one’s obligations.

Source_Text_Yo: Arọ tí ḿbú ogun, orí ẹlésú méjì ló bú u lé.
Target_Text_En: The cripple who incites war incites it on those who have two legs.
Cultural_Context: A person of no means who incurs obligations for the whole community causes problems for the people with means.

Source_Text_Yo: A-rọ́ba má sàá pàdé ara ba má yà; pakí ko pakí.
Target_Text_En: He-who-never-runs-from-the-king meets him-who-never-makes-way-for-the-king; trouble comes face to face with trouble.
Cultural_Context: When two obstinate people meet, trouble is in the offing.

Source_Text_Yo: Arugudu òjò tí ńṣú laàrin òru.
Target_Text_En: The problematic rain: its clouds gather in the middle of the night.
Cultural_Context: It is a formidable visitation that descends when one is least prepared.

Source_Text_Yo: Arúgbó ẹrú ò jẹ́ ọ̀fẹ́; òtòṣì ọba ò singbà; ìwọ̀fà kan ò dàgbà dàgbà kó ní  òun ò sin olówó mọ́
Target_Text_En: An old slave does not go for nothing; a poor king does not pawn himself; however old a pawn may be, he may not refuse to serve the creditor.
Cultural_Context: Every station has its obligations and its limits; prosperity, poverty, and duties are relative to one’s position.

Source_Text_Yo: Àrùn ní ńmúni jẹun ọ̀tá.
Target_Text_En: It is disease that makes one eat food offered by one’s enemy.
Cultural_Context: When one is prostrated by a formidable misfortune, one is forced to do many things one would rather not do.

Source_Text_Yo: Àsárébá ní ḿmú ìrìn yá.
Target_Text_En: It is running-to-overtake-those-ahead that speeds a journey.
Cultural_Context: One should strive to match those ahead of one, not behind.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣọ̀rọ̀kẹ́lẹ́ bojú wògbẹ́; ìgbẹ́ ò délé sọ fẹ́nìkan; ẹni a ḿbá wí ní ńwíni kiri.
Target_Text_En: The whisperer glances at the bush; the bush does not go home to expose one’s secret; it is the person one talks to who spreads one’s secret about.
Cultural_Context: Secrets do not expose them selves; those who know about them reveal them.

Source_Text_Yo: Àsúnmò dẹ̀tẹ́; èèyàn gbókèèrè níyì.
Target_Text_En: Closeness breeds contempt; the person who lives afar is made much of.
Cultural_Context: To be close by is to be unappreciated; to be far away is to be valued. See the next two entries also.

Source_Text_Yo: Àsúnmò dẹ̀tẹ́; òkèèrè ní ńdùn.
Target_Text_En: Closeness breeds contempt; distance is best.
Cultural_Context: Distance is a good cloak for a person’s flaws.

Source_Text_Yo: Àsúnmọ́ là ḿmọ ìṣe ẹni; èèyàn gbókèèrè níyì.
Target_Text_En: Only by living close does one know an other’s nature; the person who lives far away enjoys much respect.
Cultural_Context: Distance is a good cloak for a person’s flaws.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣá gbé mi ládìẹ kò dúró, nítorí ó mọ ohun tó ṣe.
Target_Text_En: The kite snatched my chicken and did not tarry, because it knew what it had done.
Cultural_Context: The guilty person has his or her conscience to contend with.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣá ni baba ẹyẹ.
Target_Text_En: The kite is the father of birds.
Cultural_Context: There is no bird to match the kite.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣá ńtà, àwòdì ńrà; àwòdì tí ńgbé adìẹ l sàn-án ò sanra to igún; b l run ò pa igún, ohun tí igún bá rí a máa jẹ.
Target_Text_En: The kite sells and the eagle buys; the eagle that snatches chicks in broad daylight is no fatter than the vulture; if God spares the vulture, it will feed on whatever it can find.
Cultural_Context: The powerful may live luxuriously; the weak, by the grace of providence, will find something to live on.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣá tó gbé adìẹ òtòṣì-í gbé ti aláròyé.
Target_Text_En: The kite that snatches a poor person’s chick provokes endless complaint.
Cultural_Context: A poor person never ceases bewailing a small loss.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣápẹ́ fún wèrè jó, òun àti wèrè ẹgbẹ́nra.
Target_Text_En: The person who claps for an imbecile to dance and the imbecile are no different.
Cultural_Context: Any person who has time for unworthy people is himself or herself unworthy.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣàwí ẹjọ́ ẹnìkan-án ṣàre.
Target_Text_En: The doctored case of the only side heard in a dispute is always just.
Cultural_Context: If one’s opponent has no say, one’s case is just by default.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣẹ́ ni ik oyún; àtọ̀ ni ikọ̀ ọmọ; rírà lódọ̀ẹ̀dẹ̀ ni ik àwòdì tí ńjá ọmọ lẹ́hìn adìẹ.
Target_Text_En: Menstruation heralds pregnancy; sperm heralds children; hovering in the yard sig nals the presence of the kite that snatches chicks from their mothers.
Cultural_Context: Momentous events send their omens before them.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀jáde akàn, a ò mọ ibi tí ó ńlọ.
Target_Text_En: The newly emerged crab gives no indication of where it is headed.
Cultural_Context: It is futile to attempt to predict the unpredictable.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀wọ̀lú àlejò, jolojolo lojú ńṣeni.
Target_Text_En: On first entering a town, the stranger’s eyes are restless.
Cultural_Context: The eyes of a stranger do not rest on anything for long.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣetán ló níyì; a kì í dúpẹ́ alàṣekù.
Target_Text_En: Completing-a-job is what is appreciated; one does not express gratitude for something half done.
Cultural_Context: What is worth doing is worth finishing.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣìṣe ò kan ọgbọ́n.
Target_Text_En: Mistakes have nothing to do with wisdom.
Cultural_Context: To be mistaken is not necessarily to be unwise.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣiwèrè-é yẹ ìlú, kò yẹ ẹni ẹni.
Target_Text_En: An imbecile is acceptable in a town but not among one’s kin.
Cultural_Context: No one wants an imbecile for a relative.

Source_Text_Yo: Àṣìwí ò tó àṣìṣe; àṣìṣe ò tó ká múra ọ̀run.
Target_Text_En: To misspeak is not as bad as to commit a blunder; to commit a blunder is not as bad as making ready to go to heaven.
Cultural_Context: Errors are not all equally grave.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣooregbèṣù: baba àdánù.
Target_Text_En: Doing-a-favor-and-receiving-wickedness in-return: father of losses.
Cultural_Context: Receiving evil in return for good is the worst sort of loss.

Source_Text_Yo: A-ṣoore-má-ṣìkà; ẹní ṣooré ṣe é fúnra-a rẹ̀; ẹní ṣìkàá ṣe é fúnra-a rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Doer-of-good-who-does-no-evil; who does good does it for himself or herself; who does evil does it for himself or herself.
Cultural_Context: Good deeds and evil deeds will come home to roost.

Source_Text_Yo: A-ṣòro-ó-bini, ìjà àná.
Target_Text_En: Difficult-to-ask-about, yesterday’s quarrel.
Cultural_Context: A festering quarrel is a difficult issue to broach.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣòroófinúhàn bí èké.
Target_Text_En: Difficult-to-confide-in like an unreliable person.
Cultural_Context: An untrue friend is not one to confide in.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣòroógbé bi agọ̀-ọ Masiada; báa bá gbe níwájú a balẹ̀ lẹ́hìn; báa bá gbe lẹhìn a balẹ̀ níwájú.
Target_Text_En: Difficult-to-wear like the costume of the Masiada masquerade; if one lifts it in front, it drags at the back; if one lifts it at the back, it drags in front.
Cultural_Context: In certain circumstances, nothing one does turns out right.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣòroóṣe bí ohun tỌ́lọ́run ò fẹ́; adùnúnṣe bí ohun tỌ́lọ́run-ún ṣe tán.
Target_Text_En: Difficult-to-accomplish like something God disapproves of; easy-to-accomplish like something God is ready to do.
Cultural_Context: What does not please God is difficult to do; what pleases God is easily accomplished.

Source_Text_Yo: Aṣòroówí bí àrùn ìdílé.
Target_Text_En: Difficult-to-discuss like a hereditary dis ease.
Cultural_Context: Discussing the congenital disease of a family is a delicate matter.

Source_Text_Yo: Ata loògùn ẹ̀mí; ẹ̀mí tí kò jata, ẹ̀mí yẹpẹrẹ.
Target_Text_En: Pepper is the medicine for life; a soul that does not eat pepper is an insignificant soul.
Cultural_Context: The benefits of pepper cannot be overesti mated.

Source_Text_Yo: Ata ò m pé òun ó dèélé.
Target_Text_En: Pepper had no idea it would end up in the house.
Cultural_Context: One cannot foretell what lies in one’s future.

Source_Text_Yo: Ataepo àti araepo ló mọ ohun tí wọ́n fi ńnuwọ́
Target_Text_En: The seller of palm oil and the buyer of palm oil both know what they use to wipe their hands.
Cultural_Context: People who share the same trade or secrets understand one another.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtàm̀pàkò baba ìka.
Target_Text_En: Thumb, father of fingers.
Cultural_Context: The thumb is the chief among the fingers.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtàm̀pàkò ò ṣéé júwe kánkán.
Target_Text_En: The thumb is useless for pointing straight ahead.
Cultural_Context: Even an important tool is not proper for every task.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtàrí àjànàkú kì í ṣẹrù ọmọdé.
Target_Text_En: An elephant’s head is no load for a child.
Cultural_Context: There is a limit to what youth can accom plish.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtàtàkurá: ẹnu ẹyẹ ò ran òkúta.
Target_Text_En: An impossible task: the bird’s beak avails nothing against a rock.
Cultural_Context: The rock has noth ing to fear from the bird.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtè pẹyẹ mọyẹ kú.
Target_Text_En: Birdlime kills birds and causes the death of birds.
Cultural_Context: Birdlime is the nemesis of birds.

Source_Text_Yo: Atètèdélé ní ńjoyè ẹrú.
Target_Text_En: The-first-to-arrive-home assumes the ownership of slaves.
Cultural_Context: The race is to the swift.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtètègbà làtètèsan.
Target_Text_En: Early-arrival-at-terms means early payment.
Cultural_Context: Too-long haggling defers the enjoyment of the acquisition.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtètèlóbìnrin ò kan ọmọ bíbí.
Target_Text_En: Taking-a-wife-early has nothing to do with having children.
Cultural_Context: Marrying early does not guarantee having children early.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtètèsùn làtètèjí; ẹní tètè kú ló múlẹ̀ lọ́run
Target_Text_En: Going-to-sleep-early is rising early; the first Miscellany 465 to die is the homesteader in heaven.
Cultural_Context: The first arrival has the richest choice.

Source_Text_Yo: Atètèṣágba kì í mọ ọgbẹ́-ẹ́ ṣá bí aṣánisan.
Target_Text_En: The-first-to-wound-with-a-machete does not know how to wound like the-person who-wounds-in-retaliation.
Cultural_Context: Retaliation is usually more severe than the provocation.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtẹ̀gbé lẹsẹ̀ ńtẹ ọ̀nà.
Target_Text_En: Stepping-upon-without-repercussion is the way the foot steps on the path.
Cultural_Context: The path has no recourse against the foot that steps on it.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtẹ́lẹsẹ̀ àwẹ̀nù tó dojú ara-a rẹ̀ dẹ́lẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The washed-in-vain sole sets its face down on the ground.
Cultural_Context: Avoid inconsistencies or senseless efforts.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtòlèsẹ̀ ní ńjẹ̀gbin nà.
Target_Text_En: It is the sole that eats the filth on the path.
Cultural_Context: One’s responsibilities often expose one to unwarranted abuse.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtẹ̀yún àtẹ̀wá là ńtẹ èkùrọ́ ojú nà.
Target_Text_En: Stepping-on-while-going, stepping-on while-returning is the way one steps on the kernel in the path.
Cultural_Context: The ill-fated person can hope for no respite.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtidé onígbàjámọ̀ là ḿmọ̀, a kì í mọ àtilọ.
Target_Text_En: One knows only of the arrival of the barber, not of his departure.
Cultural_Context: Once one has served one’s purpose, one is soon forgotten.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtijẹun, ọ̀tọ̀tọ̀ ọ̀ràn.
Target_Text_En: Finding a means of livelihood, a formi dable problem.
Cultural_Context: Earning a living is no mean matter.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtìkà àtoore, ọ̀kan kì í gbé.
Target_Text_En: Be it good or evil, neither goes for nought.
Cultural_Context: Good as well as evil will be requited.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtilọ-ọ lámi-lámi là ńrí, a kì í rí àtibọ̀.
Target_Text_En: One sees only the departure of the dragon fly, never its return.
Cultural_Context: The boastful person proclaims his accomplishments beforehand, but is usually silent when he falls short.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtíòro-ó jẹ̀gbá jẹlá, ó ní òun ò kú; ó ní bí gbogbo ẹyẹ ayé ti ńfò náà ni òun ńfò yí.
Target_Text_En: The allied hornbill eats garden eggs and eats okro and proclaims that it has not died; it says that just as other birds on earth fly around, so it also does.
Cultural_Context: However tough the times, whoever will survive will sur vive.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtípìjí, a-wúwo-bí-àtẹ-ìbànùjẹ́;ìbànùjẹ́ dorí àgbà kodò
Target_Text_En: A mighty problem, heavy-as-a-tray-of sadness; sadness causes an elder to hang his head.
Cultural_Context: Heavy sadness prostrates even an elder.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtiràbọn ò tó àtirẹ̀tù; ọjọ́ kan là ńra ìbọn; ojoojúm là ńrẹ̀tù.
Target_Text_En: Buying-a-gun is nothing like buying gun powder; one buys a gun only on one day, but one buys powder every day.
Cultural_Context: Making an impressive purchase is one thing; being able to maintain the thing purchased is quite another.

Source_Text_Yo: Àtiwáyé ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ alágídígba ò ṣẹhìn èkùrọ́
Target_Text_En: The incarnation of the lágídígba bead will not be in the absence of the palm kernel.
Cultural_Context: Nothing can be done in the absence of a person whose consent is all-important, o

Source_Text_Yo: Atúmálọ̀ọ́yún, aràmáṣèdin, agbẹmánìí sẹ̀ẹ́pẹ́.
Target_Text_En: It-bursts-without-pus, it-rots-without maggots, it-dries-without-scales.
Cultural_Context: It is never as one would expect but stops halfway.

Source_Text_Yo: Atúnniṣe ò pọ̀ bí abanijẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Those-who-groom-people are not as many as those-who-soil-people.
Cultural_Context: There are far more detractors than praisers.

Source_Text_Yo: Awo kan ò sí nínú awo ẹ̀wà.
Target_Text_En: There is nothing inscrutable about beans.
Cultural_Context: Common knowledge is nobody’s mo nopoly.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwo ò m pé òun ó jata.
Target_Text_En: The plate did not know that it would eat pepper.
Cultural_Context: Some boons one does not work for or anticipate.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwòdì jẹun èpè sanra
Target_Text_En: The hawk feeds fat on accursed food.
Cultural_Context: One cannot worry too much about offending people

Source_Text_Yo: Àwòdì ńrà, inú aládìẹ́ bàjẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The hawk hovers, and the owner of chickens becomes unhappy.
Cultural_Context: The appearance of one’s enemy never fails to displease.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwòdì ò náání à ńkùngbẹ́; igí wó ẹyẹ́ fò lọ.
Target_Text_En: The hawk is not bothered that the forest is being burned; the tree crashes, and the bird flies away.
Cultural_Context: Some people are immune to certain perils.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwòdì ò sí ńlé, kan-na-kán-ná ńṣe bí ọba lóko.
Target_Text_En: The hawk is away, and the crow behaves like a king on the farm.
Cultural_Context: In the absence of the hawk, the crow is king.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwòdì tó bà lé òrùlé; ojú tólé, ojú tóko.
Target_Text_En: The hawk that alights on a roof: the eyes see the home and the eyes see the farm.
Cultural_Context: One perched on high can see near and far.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwòdì-í lọ re ìyà, wón ní ẹyẹ́ sà lọ.
Target_Text_En: The hawk goes to molt, and they say the bird has fled.
Cultural_Context: Those who do not know why one does what one does choose the explanation they prefer.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwòdì-í sọ olówó adìẹ di wèrè.
Target_Text_En: The hawk makes a maniac of the owner of chicks
Cultural_Context: The imperative of protecting one’s property sometimes makes one do strange things.

Source_Text_Yo: Miscellany 467 chicks.
Target_Text_En: A reference to the curses that attend the hawk’s snatching of chicks
Cultural_Context: The imperative of protecting one’s property sometimes makes one do strange things.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwòkó, wọ́n ní o bú ọba; ó ní ìgbà wo lòún ráyè bú ọba, kí òun tó kọ igba láàárọ̀, igba lọ́sànán; igba lálẹ́?
Target_Text_En: Àwòko, they say you insulted the king; it replies, when would I have the time to insult the king, given the task of singing two hun dred songs in the morning, two hundred in the afternoon, and two hundred at night?
Cultural_Context: Too elaborate alibis call for a close look.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwòmọ́jú kì í pọ̀tá; mọ́jú-mọ́jú lọrùn ńdùn.
Target_Text_En: Disdainful looks do not kill an enemy; it is the looker who suffers neck strain.
Cultural_Context: If there is nothing one can do to one’s enemy, looking at him disdainfully is no substitute.

Source_Text_Yo: Awoníní kọjá àlùkùráni.
Target_Text_En: Possession of charms is more efficacious than carrying a Koran.
Cultural_Context: A sure medicine is preferable to faith in religion.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwòrán ṣètè kólóbó, igi tá-a bá gbọléhín ò lè bunijẹ.
Target_Text_En: An image with its small lips, a piece of wood whose teeth one carved cannot bite one.
Cultural_Context: A sculpture one carves with one’s hands cannot do harm.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwòsùn-ùn, àwònù lẹkùn ńwẹyẹ òkè.
Target_Text_En: It is a frustrated stare and pointless watching that the leopard directs at the bird flying high above.
Cultural_Context: When a person is beyond one’s control or discipline, all one can do is stare at him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: Awọ nídìí àdá ò wí pé kí àdá má kàn án.
Target_Text_En: Wrapping the hilt in leather will not keep a machete from breaking. 468 truisms
Cultural_Context: There is a limit to what one can do to prevent occupational disasters.

Source_Text_Yo: Awọ́ni ní ńfìdí ara-a rẹ̀ lànà fún ẹni tí ńwọ́ lọ.
Target_Text_En: He who drags a person uses his buttocks to clear the bush for the person he is dragging.
Cultural_Context: Victimizing another person does not leave oneself unscathed.

Source_Text_Yo: Àwúyẹ́wúyẹ́, àròyé ọ̀tẹ̀ wọ́n ní kí wọ́n tún ìlú sẹ, wọ́n fẹ́ẹ́ tú ìlú.
Target_Text_En: Clandestine whispering, the devious con versation of plotting; they were urged to improve conditions in the town, but they would rather destroy it.
Cultural_Context: Clandestine plot ters would rather engage in secret designs to ruin the community than work for its improvement.

Source_Text_Yo: Àyà ọmọdé ni wèré dì sí; ọrẹ́ la fi ńjá a.
Target_Text_En: Insanity is bunched on the chest of the child; it is a whip that one uses to dislodge it.
Cultural_Context: A whip is the surest cure for a child’s misbehavior.

Source_Text_Yo: Aya-méè-rọ́mọ-rí ní ńtanna wo oyún ọ̀gànjọ́.
Target_Text_En: Wife-I-have-never-seen-a-child-before is the one who lights a lamp in the middle of the night to look at a pregnancy.
Cultural_Context: A person new to a privilege is usually not noted for moderation in its exercise.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayé àgbẹ̀ bí àjẹrọ̀run
Target_Text_En: A farmer’s lifestyle is like something out of this world.
Cultural_Context: Farm dwellers know no social constraints.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayé àkámarà! Ayé lè pa ìràwọ̀ dà.
Target_Text_En: Untrustworthy humankind! Humankind can alter people’s destiny.
Cultural_Context: People are not to be trusted.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayé di lẹhẹ-n-hẹ: ẹyin adìẹ́ tókè wá fìpón.
Target_Text_En: The world has turned awry: a chicken egg drops from above and breaks a wooden spoon below.
Cultural_Context: When a raw egg breaks a spoon, the world has turned upside down.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayé jìn, kò lópin; ibi tí ẹsẹ̀ ò dé lógún ọdún ò ló-ǹ-kà.
Target_Text_En: The world is so vast that there is no end to it; the places a person’s feet cannot reach in twenty years are uncountable.
Cultural_Context: No one can claim to know all there is of the world.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayé kì í di pọlọru ká fẹs rọrí sùn.
Target_Text_En: The world is never so disrupted that one rests one’s head on one’s legs to sleep.
Cultural_Context: How ever the world turns, a person does not suffer the same fate as a chicken.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayé le; bí o bá a o pa á; bí o ò bá a o bù ú lẹ́kẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Humankind is awesome: if you catch up with him, kill him; if you are unable to, put a hex on his footprint.
Cultural_Context: Humans’ evil machi nations are formidable; people will explore all means to injure others.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayé le, èèyàn-án burú ju ẹkùn.
Target_Text_En: The world is tough; people are more evil than the leopard.
Cultural_Context: Living among people is full of peril.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayé ńretí ẹlẹ́yà; níbo ni wọ́n fi ti Olúwa sí?
Target_Text_En: The world waits expectantly for one’s dis grace; to what place have they relegated God’s purpose?
Cultural_Context: People hope for a person’s disgrace without considering what God might wish.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayé ó fẹ́ kà ru ẹrù ká sọ̀; orí ẹni ní ńsọni.
Target_Text_En: The world does not wish that one rid oneself of the burden one carries; it is one’s head that relieves one.
Cultural_Context: Other people do not wish one good fortune; each person’s guardian spirit ensures his or her good fortune. See also the next entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayé ó fẹ́ni fòrọ̀ àfi orí ẹni.
Target_Text_En: The world does not wish one to prosper; only one’s own head does.
Cultural_Context: Only one’s guardian spirit, not other people, wishes one to prosper.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayé ò lọ́ràá: ọjọ́ a rí kéré ká jẹ kéré; ọjọ́ a rí wọ̀mù ká jẹ wọ̀mù; àgbà kì í ṣubú yẹ̀gẹ̀ kó da ti ikùn sílẹ̀; oun a bá jẹ ní ḿbani lọ.
Target_Text_En: There is no fat to this world: when one has only a little, one should eat only a little; when one has a great deal, one should eat a great deal; an elder does not fall and spill what is in his stomach; it is what one has eaten that goes with one.
Cultural_Context: The future is uncertain; one should therefore live ac cording to one’s present circumstances; the only thing that can go with one in death is what one has already enjoyed. Compare 3981.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayé ò ríni nígbà tí a sun ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ jẹ; ìgbà tí a fi gúsí seb tó pọ́n bí edé layé ríni.
Target_Text_En: The world pays no attention when one has to roast plantains for food; it is only when one cooks melon-seed stew that is as pink as shrimps that the world pays attention.
Cultural_Context: People have time only for those whose stars are ascending.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayò kì í jẹ ká yẹ̀ ẹ́.
Target_Text_En: One does not hit the jackpot in the game of ayò and refuse to collect.
Cultural_Context: One does not turn one’s back on good fortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayo òtòṣì lọl r ńfọwọ́ tẹ̀ níkùn.
Target_Text_En: It is a satiated poor person that a rich person may poke in the stomach with a finger.
Cultural_Context: The poor person’s abundance does not impress a wealthy person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ayọ̀ abaratíńtín.
Target_Text_En: Happiness, a thing with a frail constitution.
Cultural_Context: Happiness is fickle.

Source_Text_Yo: Àyọ̀ká, ọmọ ẹnìkan ló kù.
Target_Text_En: Universal happiness: only a certain person is left out.
Cultural_Context: The happiness in question is all-embracing, leaving out only the unfortu nate.

Source_Text_Yo: Àyúnbọ̀ lọwọ́ ńyún ẹnu.
Target_Text_En: Going-and-returning is the manner of the hand’s journey to the mouth. B
Cultural_Context: The hand that lifts food to the mouth always returns safely.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Bá mi na ọmọ- mi’’ ò dénú ọlọ́mọ.
Target_Text_En: Whip my child for me’’ does not come from deep inside the mother.
Cultural_Context: No mother is en thusiastic in delivering her child to deserved punishment.

Source_Text_Yo: Baál tó sọ ọmọ ajá di ẹgbàá, ọmọ tir á wọ́n níbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The chief who raised the price of a puppy to 200 cowries, his own child will pay the price.
Cultural_Context: The child will reap some of what the father sowed.

Source_Text_Yo: Baba ẹnìkan ò gbin yánrin; baba ẹnìkan ò gbin tẹ̀tẹ̀; fúnra-a rẹ̀ ní ńhù
Target_Text_En: Nobody’s father plants yánrin [a wild vege table], and nobody’s father plants wild spinach; they grow by themselves.
Cultural_Context: No one may lay an exclusive claim to public prop erty.

Source_Text_Yo: Ba-owò-jẹ, obì tí ńso larùn.
Target_Text_En: Ruiner-of-trade, kola nut that fruits in the dry season.
Cultural_Context: Plants that yield out of their season undermine the market.

Source_Text_Yo: Báríkà lónìí; Báríkà lọla; Ẹ kú ìrọ́jú; Ò jìnnà síbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Congratulations on surviving a disaster’’ today; ‘‘Congratulations on surviving a disaster’’ the next day; ‘‘Accept my con dolences’’ is not far away.
Cultural_Context: Persistent close shaves sooner or later become real disasters.

Source_Text_Yo: Bàtá dún kò dún, á tan ilẹ̀kú kanlẹ̀ kanlẹ̀
Target_Text_En: Whether or not the bàtá drum sounds well, it will do its part in the funeral obsequies.
Cultural_Context: What matters is that a thing serve its purpose, not that one like it

Source_Text_Yo: Bàtà la fi ńṣagbára láàrin ẹ̀gún.
Target_Text_En: Shoes make for fearlessness amid thorns.
Cultural_Context: Who has shoes may strut even over danger ous ground.

Source_Text_Yo: Bàtà ò jẹ́ mọ agésẹ̀ òyìnbó; a ṣẹ́ aṣọ létí kò jẹ́ mọ ẹni tí ńfàṣọ ìyà bora
Target_Text_En: Shoes keep one from knowing which white man has lost his toes; hemming dresses keeps people from knowing who is clothed in wretchedness.
Cultural_Context: Outward appearances often belie private woes.

Source_Text_Yo: Bàtáakoto, atiro àrìnjó, ṣaworo g d , gbogbo wọn bákan-náà bákan-náà
Target_Text_En: The bàtáakoto drum, a lame itinerant dancer, a rattle made of bananas, all are the same.
Cultural_Context: The enumerated things are three of a kind, all defective.

Source_Text_Yo: Bẹ́ màrìwò, bẹgòdà, ọj kan-náà ni wón ńyọ.
Target_Text_En: Cut off palm fronds and cut down a banana tree; they sprout anew the same day.
Cultural_Context: Said of things that share the same characteristics.

Source_Text_Yo: Bèbè ìdí ni yó lo kíjìpá gbó.
Target_Text_En: The large beads adorning the waist will wear out the durable home-woven cloth in the end.
Cultural_Context: One always pays somehow for one’s pleasures and vanities.

Source_Text_Yo: Bẹ̀wẹ̀ kó ó rọ́kọ̀ṣẹ́, ṣagbe kó ó ráhùn.
Target_Text_En: Seek help and find out who is recalcitrant; beg for alms and find out who is a miser.
Cultural_Context: The accomplishment of one feat does not prevent the accomplishment of another

Source_Text_Yo: Ó gbọrọ ẹni tó gbọrọ, ó gbọrọ ẹni tó gbọrọ.
Target_Text_En: One does not know one’s friends until one needs help.)
Cultural_Context: One does not know one’s friends until one needs help

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá bọ́jú tí a bọ́nu; ìsàlẹ̀ àgbọ̀n là ńparí-i rẹ̀ sí.
Target_Text_En: After one has washed one’s face and one’s mouth, the ablution concludes at the under side of the chin.
Cultural_Context: After discussing a mat ter back and forth, one rests it with the proper person to decide on it.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá gé igi nígbó, gbohùn-gbohùn á gbà á.
Target_Text_En: If one fells a tree in the forest, the echo carries the sound.
Cultural_Context: Not even things done in secret can be long concealed.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá máa jẹun dun ọmọdé, híhàn la fi ńhàn án.
Target_Text_En: If one wishes to hurt a child by eating some thing he wants, one shows it to him first.
Cultural_Context: If one intends to hurt a person, one should be sure the person knows of one’s actions.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá ńfẹ́ràn ọmọdé ní ilẹkú, à mọ̀ pé a fẹ́ẹ́ fi sọfà ni.
Target_Text_En: If a child is being made much of at a funeral (presumably of his father), it is obvious that he is about to be pawned.
Cultural_Context: Favors done for an orphan have ulterior motives.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá ńjiyàn sípàá, à ṣí aṣọ kúrò.
Target_Text_En: If there is any dispute about hydrocele, let us strip away all clothing.
Cultural_Context: There is no point in carrying on protracted arguments when a simple and incontrovertible means of resolving the issue is available.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá ńrẹ́rín-ín hẹ̀n-hẹ̀n, tí à ńgúnni l bẹ, kò ní kó má wónú.
Target_Text_En: If one laughs while stabbing another, that does not keep the dagger from piercing the Miscellany 471 skin.
Cultural_Context: A person killed with kindness is just as dead.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá ńṣẹ́ gègé ìjà, ká mú ti ológbò kúrò; ọba lọba ńjẹ.
Target_Text_En: If people cast lots to determine the best fighter, a cat should be set aside; a king is a king.
Cultural_Context: The cat is undisputed king where wrestling is concerned.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá pọn omi, tó dànù, tí agbè ò fọ́, à tún òmíràn pọn.
Target_Text_En: If one draws water and it is spilled but the gourd is unbroken, one refills the gourd.
Cultural_Context: As long as one has a capacity to act, temporary setbacks are of little consequence.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá sọ idà sílẹ̀ mẹwàá, ibi pẹlẹbẹ ni yó dà dél.
Target_Text_En: If one throws a sword down ten times, it will come to rest on its side.
Cultural_Context: However long one worries a case, the facts will not change.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a bá yọ ipin lójú, ojú la fi ńhàn.
Target_Text_En: If one removes secreted matter from the eye, one shows it to the eye.
Cultural_Context: One discusses an offense with the offender, not other people.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí a kò ṣe àṣenù, a ò lè ṣe àṣejẹ.
Target_Text_En: If one has never labored for nought, one does not gain from one’s labor.
Cultural_Context: Disappoint ment comes before fulfillment.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí àfẹ́fẹ́ bá ńfẹ́, koríko a máa jó.
Target_Text_En: If the wind blows, the grass dances.
Cultural_Context: Certain orders cannot be ignored.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí àgbàlagbà-á bá ńti orí jẹ àkèré, kọ́mọdé má nìírètí ati jẹ níbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: If an elder begins eating a frog from its head, a youth should not hope to have any share of it.
Cultural_Context: One can expect no help from a per son whose actions reveal his or her own desperation.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí agbọ́n bá máa ṣorò, a kìdí bọlẹ̀; bí idà-á bá máa ṣorò, a ki kù bọ àkọ̀.
Target_Text_En: When the wasp is about to fight, it dips its tail in the ground; when a sword is about to fight, it dips its hilt into the scabbard.
Cultural_Context: Before engaging in a demanding task, one makes the proper preparations. Also, mo mentous events are presaged by warning signs.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ajá bá ńwọ agbádá iná, tí àmọ̀tẹ́kùn ńwẹ̀wù ẹ̀jẹ̀, tí ológìnní ńsán àkísà jìnnì mọ́dìí, ẹgbẹ́ apẹranjẹ ní ńṣe
Target_Text_En: If the dog wears a garment of fire, and the leopard wears a dress of blood, while the cat ties a tattered rag around its waist, it is nevertheless a member of the clan of carni vores.
Cultural_Context: Innate quality, not clothing, is what matters.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí àjànàkú jẹ tí kò yó, ìgbẹ́ lójú ó tì.
Target_Text_En: If the elephant eats and is not full, the shame belongs to the forest.
Cultural_Context: To the person unable to fulfill his or her obligations belongs the shame, not to the disappointed person.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí alágbẹ̀dẹ-ẹ́ bá ńlurin lójú kan, ojú àmì ló wà níb.
Target_Text_En: If a blacksmith keeps hitting the iron on the same spot, it is because there is a mark or blemish there.
Cultural_Context: There is a reason for every action.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí alápatà-á bá pa ẹran, alágbàtà a bù ú ní àjàn.
Target_Text_En: When a butcher kills an animal, meat hawkers cut it up for sale.
Cultural_Context: Each person does his or her bit when it is his or her turn.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí asé bá pẹ́ làpò, á bu.
Target_Text_En: If a cloth remains too long in the sack, it goes moldy.
Cultural_Context: If a person stays long enough in one place, he or she acquires the traits of that place.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ayé bá já, kò ṣéé so.
Target_Text_En: Once life has snapped, it cannot be mended.
Cultural_Context: A lost life is irretrievable.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí eégún ò bá ṣe ohun tó tóbi, atọ́kùnun rẹ̀ kì í tú u wò.
Target_Text_En: If a masquerader has not done something unprecedented, his attendant does not open his mask for inspection.
Cultural_Context: Only extraordinary actions call for extraordinary reactions.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ẹrán bá balẹ̀, ojú a yán ọdẹ.
Target_Text_En: When an animal falls to the ground, the hunter’s eyes lose their wildness.
Cultural_Context: At the end of the chase, ennui sets in.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí igí bá dá, igi a yẹrí; bí èèyán bá kú, a ku èèyàn sàà-sàà níl; bí ẹni orí ẹní bá kú, ẹni ilẹ̀ẹ́lẹ̀ a di ẹni orí ẹní.
Target_Text_En: If a tree breaks, other trees make way; if a person dies, other people will remain; if the person on the mat dies, the person on the bare floor becomes the person on the mat.
Cultural_Context: As one generation passes, another genera tion succeeds it; life goes on regardless.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ilẹ̀-ẹ́gbe òṣìkà, tí kò gbe olóòtò, oore a súni se.
Target_Text_En: If the earth succors the wicked but not the good person, one tires of good deeds.
Cultural_Context: If the wicked prosper while good people flounder, one is discouraged about doing good.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí iná bá jó lóko, màjàlà a fò wá sílé.
Target_Text_En: When there is a fire in the forest, the soot flies home.
Cultural_Context: Events that happen afar send their news back home.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí iná kò bá láwo nínú, kì í gun òkè odò.
Target_Text_En: If a fire is not endowed with mysterious powers, it does not jump rivers.
Cultural_Context: When matters take unprecedented turns, they are driven by unusual forces.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí inú ẹnìkan ó bájà, inú ẹnìkan kì í dún.
Target_Text_En: If one person does not become sad, another person does not become happy.
Cultural_Context: One per son’s sadness is another person’s happiness.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí kò bá sí lójú, kì í kàn sáyà.
Target_Text_En: If it is not visible to the eyes, it does not weigh on the mind.
Cultural_Context: What the eyes do not see does not cause terror.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí kò bá sí ohun tó ṣe ẹ̀ṣẹ́, ẹ̀ṣẹ́ kì í ṣẹ́.
Target_Text_En: If the fist is not provoked, the fist does not fight.
Cultural_Context: For every quarrel there must be some reason.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí kò sí bó ti rí, ìr kì í ṣẹ́ nítàn.
Target_Text_En: Were things not as they were, the cricket’s thigh would not have snapped.
Cultural_Context: Unavoid able adversity caused a calamity.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí kúkúrú ò gbọ́n, èyí gbọgbọrọ ńkọ́?
Target_Text_En: If the short person is unwise, how about the tall person?
Cultural_Context: A group cannot be uniformly stupid.

Source_Text_Yo: Miscellany 473
Target_Text_En: K nn n gó drums are part of the dùndún drum ensemble.
Cultural_Context: Not Provided

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ogún bá lọ, ogún á bọ̀; bí kò ṣe bó, ìbòsí ìgárá là ńké.
Target_Text_En: If twenty go, twenty should return; other wise, one raises an alarm that one has been defrauded.
Cultural_Context: Welching is not a good practice in dealing with others.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ojú bá ṣọ̀bùn ojú là á fi í hàn; bí a bá yọpin lójú, à fi han ojú.
Target_Text_En: If the eyes produce filth, one shows it to the eyes; if one takes secreted matter out of the eyes, one shows it to the eyes.
Cultural_Context: It is with the perpetrator of an offense that one discusses it.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí òkú bá kú láyé, àkàlà a mọ̀ lọ́run.
Target_Text_En: When the dead dies on earth, the ground hornbill knows in heaven.
Cultural_Context: A momentous event cannot be kept quiet.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ológìnní bá lọ sájò tó bọ̀, inú èkúté a bájẹ́.
Target_Text_En: If the cat goes on a journey and returns, the mouse becomes sad.
Cultural_Context: The oppressed always bemoan their oppressor’s good fortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí olÓrò-ó májá, owó oúnjẹ olówó-o rẹ̀ ló dínkù.
Target_Text_En: If the secret cult impounds a dog, it is the owner’s food expense that is lessened.
Cultural_Context: There is a bright side to every misfortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí Onírese ò fíngbá mọ́, èyí tó ti fín ò lè parun
Target_Text_En: If Onírese stops carving calabashes, those he has carved will not perish.
Cultural_Context: Whatever one has accomplished cannot be undone, even after one has lost the capacity to accomplish more.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí oṣù-ú bá lé, gbogbo ojú ní ńrí i.
Target_Text_En: When the moon appears, all eyes see it. 474 truisms
Cultural_Context: A public event cannot be hidden from people.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí òyìnbó bá máa lọ l gbà, a ba ọgbà jọjọ.
Target_Text_En: When a white man prepares to take his leave from a yard, he ruins it.
Cultural_Context: The white man on taking his leave from a place creates a shambles. See the following entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí òyìnbó bá máa lọ nílùú, a ṣu sága.
Target_Text_En: When a white man prepares to leave a town, he defecates in the chair.
Cultural_Context: The white man on departing a place creates a mess to leave behind. See the previous entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọba ò kú, ọba ò jẹ.
Target_Text_En: If a king does not die, a king is not crowned.
Cultural_Context: There is a certain order to events, and every event has its purpose.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọ̀bẹ ò bá mú, òun ìpọ́nrin ni yó mọ̀.
Target_Text_En: If a knife is not sharp, both it and the honing stone will know.
Cultural_Context: The solution of a prob lem is between the person involved and the person who will help to solve it.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọdún bá burú, èṣí làgbẹ̀ ńyìn.
Target_Text_En: If a year is bad, the farmer speaks well of the previous year.
Cultural_Context: Present hardships make one appreciate past comforts.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí ọkọ̀-ọ́ re òkun, bó re sà, a forílé èbúté.
Target_Text_En: After a boat has plied the oceans and plied the lagoon, it returns to harbor.
Cultural_Context: After much traveling, one returns home in the end.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí olẹ́ bá lẹ, ìgbòrò-o rẹ̀ á gbójú.
Target_Text_En: If a lazy person engages in his lazy ways, his farm will be neglected.
Cultural_Context: The affairs of a lazy person will not prosper.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí Ọl rún bá páni lórí, a fi irùngb n dípò-o r .
Target_Text_En: If God makes one bald, he gives one a beard as compensation.
Cultural_Context: There is a bright side to every misfortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí p èèyàn-án bá kúrò ló gbogbo, pà dáni lára yá.
Target_Text_En: If many people leave a company, many people cheer one up.
Cultural_Context: The departure of many people from a company should not stop the rest from pursuing their aims.

Source_Text_Yo: Bí yó ti rí ni yó rìí; alágb dẹ ò lè gbé ọmọ owú mì.
Target_Text_En: Whatever threatens to happen will have to happen; the blacksmith cannot swallow his hammer.
Cultural_Context: Come what may, one will not do what one has no intention of doing.

Source_Text_Yo: Bìrí bìrí layé ńyí; ìgbà kan ò lo ilé ayé gbó.
Target_Text_En: Round and round the earth turns; one sea son does not mark the end of the world.
Cultural_Context: The times are always changing.

Source_Text_Yo: Bọ̀rọ̀kìnní òun ọlọ́rọ̀ ẹgbẹ́ra; ọ̀bùn òun aṣiwèrè ọ̀kan-ùn; ọ̀kánjúà òun olè déédé ni wọ́n já sí.
Target_Text_En: The dandy and the wealthy person are equal; the filthy person and the imbecile are alike; the covetous person and the thief amount to the same thing.
Cultural_Context: Being fashionable is as desirable as being wealthy; filthiness is com parable to imbecility; covetousness is kin to thievery.

Source_Text_Yo: Bùtù-bútú nà Ìjèṣà lọmọdé fi ńṣeré; bí kò kọ́mọ ní rírìn ẹsẹ̀, a kọ́mọ ní yíyan
Target_Text_En: It is in the fine sand on the road to Iléṣà that the child is playing; if it does not teach the child how to walk, it will teach him how to stride.
Cultural_Context: Nobody comes out of an encounte

Source_Text_Yo: Dà bí mo ti dà layé nfẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Become-as-I-am is what the world wants.
Cultural_Context: People always want others to share their misfortunes. Compare 3318.

Source_Text_Yo: Dan-dan kì í sélẹ̀
Target_Text_En: A necessity cannot be ignored.
Cultural_Context: Whatever must be done cannot be left undone.

Source_Text_Yo: Dìdì lópin-in sinimá.
Target_Text_En: The end’’ marks the end of a film show.
Cultural_Context: When a thing or a relationship is over, it is over.

Source_Text_Yo: Dídùn là ḿbá láfárá oyin.
Target_Text_En: One finds only sweetness in a honeycomb.
Cultural_Context: A certain person’s affairs will always be characterized by pleasantness.

Source_Text_Yo: Díẹ̀-díẹ̀ là ḿmọ àpẹrẹ.
Target_Text_En: Portents make themselves known only gradually.
Cultural_Context: From little things one learns the true nature of someone or something.

Source_Text_Yo: Ebi kì í wọnú koro míràn-án wo o.
Target_Text_En: Hunger does not enter into a person and leave room for other matters.
Cultural_Context: A hungry person is a distracted person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ebi ní ńpani bákan-náà; oràn kì í dunni bákan-náà.
Target_Text_En: Hunger affects people the same way, but disasters do not hurt people the same way.
Cultural_Context: Different people have different vulnerabili ties.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèmọ̀ lukutupebẹ́; ìyàwó lóyún ó bí ajá.
Target_Text_En: Unspeakable abomination: the bride be comes pregnant and gives birth to a puppy.
Cultural_Context: The occurrence under reference is such as the world has never seen before. The following entry is a variant.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèmọ̀ lukutupebẹ́, sòbìyà Àjàyí, èyí tó dá a lese tó ńro ó léhín
Target_Text_En: Unspeakable abomination: Àjàyí’s guinea worm, which attacks his foot and causes his teeth to ache.
Cultural_Context: It is a strange affliction whose effects are wholly at variance with experience.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèmo-ọ kí lèyí? Ẹni a be lórí géni jẹ.
Target_Text_En: What sort of abomination is this? The person one has beheaded bites one.
Cultural_Context: Unnatural events defy explanation.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèyàn bí ahun ní ńhe ahun; èèyàn bí aṣọ kì í je kó kùtà.
Target_Text_En: Only tortoiselike people find tortoises; it is people who are attracted to particular cloths that save them from being unsalable.
Cultural_Context: Everything has its champions.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèyàn bí ìgbín ní ńhe ìgbín; èèyán bí ahun ní ńhe ahun.
Target_Text_En: Only tortoiselike people find tortoises; only snaillike people find snails.
Cultural_Context: People with like temperaments are inevitably drawn together.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèyàn búburú po ó jùgbe; ẹni reré won ju ojú lọ.
Target_Text_En: Evil people are as common as feces; good people are dearer than eyes.
Cultural_Context: Evil people are a dime a dozen; good people are a rarity.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèyàn yin-ni yin-ni keni ó ṣe òmíràn.
Target_Text_En: People’s unstinted praise encourages one to perform further feats.
Cultural_Context: To be praised is to be urged on to further accomplishments.

Source_Text_Yo: Ehoro tó jẹṣu, tó dùn mọ, a tún padà wá.
Target_Text_En: The rabbit that eats yams and enjoys them will return for more.
Cultural_Context: People remember good experiences and seek their repetition.

Source_Text_Yo: Eku-kéku kì í rùn borí asín
Target_Text_En: No rat surpasses asín [a vicious rat with a pointed snout and strong smell] in stink.
Cultural_Context: Certain people are unique, or unsurpassable, in certain ways.

Source_Text_Yo: Èpè ńrò kó tó jà.
Target_Text_En: Curses delay a while before taking effect.
Cultural_Context: Retribution may not be swift, but that does not mean that it will never come.

Source_Text_Yo: Erín wó sílù-ú àìlobẹ.
Target_Text_En: An elephant collapses in a town without knives.
Cultural_Context: An unmanageable problem has arisen.

Source_Text_Yo: Eruku gbágbá ọmọ ìyá odá; ìrì wọ̀wọ̀ ọmọ ìyá òda; iri wọ̀wọ̀ omo iya ojo
Target_Text_En: Billowing dust, sibling of drought; showering sprinkle, sibling of rain.
Cultural_Context: Certain phenomena are symbols of other realities; cer tain people have qualities that recall those of legendary people.

Source_Text_Yo: Èwo ló sàn nínúu ‘‘Ó di ìjẹsàn-án tí ọmo ti ńṣu,’’ àti ‘‘Ó di ìjẹsàn-án tí ọmọ ò ti lè ṣu’’?
Target_Text_En: Which can one say is the better statement: It has been nine days now that the child has been having the runs’’ or ‘‘It has been nine days now that the child has been unable to shit’’?
Cultural_Context: An indication that one has been presented with a form of Hobson’s choice.

Source_Text_Yo: Ewúre wo alápatà bíi kó kú.
Target_Text_En: The goat eyes the butcher as though it would kill him with looks.
Cultural_Context: If one’s adversary is too formidable, one is reduced to ineffectual gestures.

Source_Text_Yo: Ebẹ̀ là ḿbẹ Ṣàngó; obìnrin kì í wọ ṣòkòtò.
Target_Text_En: One’s only option before Ṣango is to plead; it is taboo for a woman to wear trousers. .
Cultural_Context: Certain things are irrevocable and must be accommodated, like the prohibition of trousers for women

Source_Text_Yo: Edá ní kó má torí òun dá; ológùn-ṣẹṣee ní kó má torí òun ṣe; ọkàa bàbàá ní kó má torí òun bàje
Target_Text_En: Edá says that it must not break in his time; ológùn-ṣẹṣe says it must not occur in its time; guinea corn says it must not spoil in its time.
Cultural_Context: Evil will not occur during a certain person’s watch

Source_Text_Yo: Edá ò làròpin
Target_Text_En: A human being does not have a write-off point.
Cultural_Context: Never write anyone off.

Source_Text_Yo: Egún ò bẹ́sẹ̀ rẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Thorns do not make friends with the soles of the feet.
Cultural_Context: Certain people are by constitu tion incompatible with others, just as certain actions are unsuitable for certain situations.

Source_Text_Yo: Egbìn kì í jọ elo; opó kì í jọ àtọwọ́fẹ́.
Target_Text_En: What one plants is not like what one grafts; an inherited wife is not like one married by choice.
Cultural_Context: Something thrust on one is never the same as something acquired of one’s free will.

Source_Text_Yo: Ejá kì í já kó pé
Target_Text_En: A fragment, after being broken off, cannot be reattached perfectly.
Cultural_Context: Once something has been damaged, it can no longer return to its pristine state.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹjọ́ ni àlè ḿbáni rò bí yó kani.
Target_Text_En: When a concubine begins to argue with one, it is a sure sign that she intends to expose one
Cultural_Context: When one’s accomplice in a crime begins to be unfriendly and contentious, one should look out.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá rí ṣe lọ̀tá ayé.
Target_Text_En: Whoever finds success is the enemy of humankind.
Cultural_Context: People always begrudge suc cessful people their good fortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá rìn jìnnà á fi odó ìbúle jẹun.
Target_Text_En: Whoever travels far will eat food pounded in a horizontal mortar.
Cultural_Context: Whoever looks well beyond his or her immediate environment will be exposed to unusual habits; the more one travels, the more one learns.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá bá Ìjebú ṣorò-ó bá Ọlorun ṣe.
Target_Text_En: Whoever makes a pact with an Ìjebú person makes a pact with God.
Cultural_Context: No relationship is more auspicious than one with an Ìjebú person.

Source_Text_Yo: Emú (ni) baál àgbedẹ.
Target_Text_En: Pliers [are] chief of the smithy.
Cultural_Context: A certain object or person is more to be reckoned with than others in a certain context.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní bá tàjò wá ní ńpurọ́ fárá ilé.
Target_Text_En: It is the person who has just returned from a journey that tells tall tales to those who stayed at home.
Cultural_Context: A person with wide ex periences has the advantage of those with narrow ones.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní fi ewù fábuké wọ̀ ló ní kó ròde kó má tètè dé.
Target_Text_En: Whoever gave the humpback a garment to wear is to blame for his going on an outing from which he will be long in returning.
Cultural_Context: The person who suddenly comes into the sort of fortune he or she never dreamed of is sure to be ostentatious in showing it off.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní fúnni lomọ-ọ́ parí oore.
Target_Text_En: Whoever gives one a child [to marry] has gone the limit in conferring favors.
Cultural_Context: There is no greater favor a person can do than to give another his daughter in marriage. One should acknowledge extraordinary gestures.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹní ṣu-ú lè gbàgbé; ẹni tó kó o ò níí gbàgbé.
Target_Text_En: The person who defecates may forget; the person who cleans the feces off will not forget.
Cultural_Context: A person who offends may soon for get, but the person wronged will not soon forget.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí kò gbọ́ tẹnu ẹ̀gà ló ńní egà ńpàtótó.
Target_Text_En: It is a person who does not understand what the weaver bird is saying who says it is chattering.
Cultural_Context: Unless one is privy to people’s thoughts, one does not know why they do what they do.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí oràn-án dùn, a kì í fi oràn lọ̀ ọ́.
Target_Text_En: The person most aggrieved is not the one to ask for mediation in the case.
Cultural_Context: A partisan is not a good judge.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí Ṣàngó bá ti ojú-u re wọle ò níí bú Ọya lékèé mọ́.
Target_Text_En: Whoever witnesses Ṣango enter the ground [i.e., sees lightning strike] will never again say that Ọya lies.
Cultural_Context: Once one has seen the feat a person can perform, one stops being a skeptic.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí yó kọ igba lóko, ìrìn ẹsẹ́-ẹ rẹ̀ là ńwò.
Target_Text_En: The person who vows to make two hundred heaps on the farm: one should pay attention to how he walks.
Cultural_Context: How a person behaves re veals more about his or her capabilities than what the person says.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó bí arẹwà-á bí ìyọnu.
Target_Text_En: Whoever gives birth to a beautiful girl gives birth to trouble.
Cultural_Context: A beautiful girl will even tually cause her parents a great deal of unease or disturbance. This is a variant of the next entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tí yó pegàn òrìṣà ni yó pèé àfín kò fín tó; ó fe kó bó lára ni?
Target_Text_En: It is a person who wishes to scorn the gods who will say that the albino is not bleached enough; would the person prefer that the albino have no skin?
Cultural_Context: It is silly to find fault with perfection.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó fe arẹwà-á fe ìyọnu; gbogbo ayé ní ḿbá wọn tan.
Target_Text_En: Whoever marries a beautiful woman marries trouble; the whole wide world [of men] claims kinship with him.
Cultural_Context: Whoever marries a beautiful woman will have the whole world of scheming men to fend off. See the preceding entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó mọ èyí tí yó gbẹ̀hìn ọ̀rọ̀ là ńpè lágbà.
Target_Text_En: Only the person who knows the last word in a matter deserves the title of elder.
Cultural_Context: An elder earns his status by his effectiveness in settling disputes.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó wáyé dáràn.
Target_Text_En: Whoever comes into the world comes into trouble.
Cultural_Context: Life is a pain.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó yínbọn sí ahoro, ó ti mo pé alámù lòun óò rí pa níbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The person who shoots a gun into a de serted house knows that he will kill only lizards therein.
Cultural_Context: A person who engages in a pointless gesture is reconciled to emptiness.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu ni Ifá wà
Target_Text_En: The Ifá oracle is in the mouth.
Cultural_Context: There is no oracle as powerful as the word the mouth pronounces.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹnu oníhìn ni ìhìn-ín ti ńdùn.
Target_Text_En: It is in the mouth of the person who has the news that the news is interesting.
Cultural_Context: One should not take the news out of the mouth of the bearer.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹran ọba ló fiṣu ọba jẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is the king’s goat that has eaten the king’s yams.
Cultural_Context: The offender and the offended are virtually one and the same; there is no need for punishment. Compare 3187.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹrán kú, ereke yo.
Target_Text_En: An animal dies; the cheeks rejoice.
Cultural_Context: A person’s misfortune is another person’s for tune.

Source_Text_Yo: Erín mú erẹ̀kẹ̀ dùn; ẹkún ba ẹnu jẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Laughter sweetens the cheeks; crying dis figures the mouth.
Cultural_Context: Laughter is more agree able than crying.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹrù àgbà kì í ní òṣùká; baba, ẹ kú ẹrù àgbà.
Target_Text_En: An elder’s load is without the luxury of a carrying pad; elders, we acknowledge the load you bear.
Cultural_Context: Elders bear a great many difficult and thankless responsibilities.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹṣin kì í kọ eré àsárelé
Target_Text_En: A horse never refuses a homeward gallop.
Cultural_Context: Nobody refuses an exertion that has a great reward at its conclusion.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹṣín rí ogun jó; okọ̀-ọ́ rí ogun yọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The horse sees war and dances; the spear sees war and rejoices.
Cultural_Context: The most distasteful of tasks have their enthusiasts.

Source_Text_Yo: Etẹ́ awo ni ete ọ̀gberì.
Target_Text_En: The disgrace of the initiated is the disgrace of the novice.
Cultural_Context: When one member of the group is disgraced, every member is dis graced.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹwìrì ní ńfẹ́ná lágbẹ̀dẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is the bellows that fans the furnace at the smithy.
Cultural_Context: Difficult tasks demand the proper tools.

Source_Text_Yo: Ewọ̀n kì í já kó pé
Target_Text_En: A chain once broken is no longer whole.
Cultural_Context: Lost innocence can never be retrieved.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹyẹ kì í fò kó forí sọ igi
Target_Text_En: A bird in its flight does not collide with a tree.
Cultural_Context: One does not blunder while doing what is second nature.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹyin ní ńdi àkùkọ.
Target_Text_En: It is an egg that becomes a cock.
Cultural_Context: Great things and great people start small.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Fi ojú kàn mí’’ àna kì í ṣe lásán; bí kò fẹ́ẹ́ gba owó, ó fẹ́ẹ́ sọ nǹkan.
Target_Text_En: A parent-in-law’s ‘‘Come see me briefly’’ is not for nothing; if he or she is not after money, there must be something to discuss.
Cultural_Context: People seldom do things for others without having ulterior motives.

Source_Text_Yo: Fi òní kú, fi ola jí, ọjọ́ kan ní ńkú tán.
Target_Text_En: Die one day, return to life the next; one day the dying will be for good.
Cultural_Context: Intermittent maladies eventually become permanent.

Source_Text_Yo: Fi oore lọ osìn, fi ibi lọ osìn; àti oore àti ìkà kan kì í gbé
Target_Text_En: Show kindness to a ward, show wickedness to a ward; kindness or wickedness, neither goes unrewarded.
Cultural_Context: One is eventually re warded in kind for the way one treats one’s dependents.

Source_Text_Yo: Fi ọmú fomọ, fi ọmọ fomú; bí ọmọ́ bá ti mu ọmú, kò bùṣe?
Target_Text_En: Take the breast to the child, take the child to the breast; as long as the child is nursed, is that not all that matters?
Cultural_Context: There is no point in arguing over trifles.

Source_Text_Yo: Fífe ni yiyìn oṣù; méjì-i rẹ̀ kì í lé lójú ọ̀run.
Target_Text_En: Adulation for the moon is a mark of admi ration for it; there are never two of them in the sky.
Cultural_Context: People or things that are peerless deserve to be so acknowledged.

Source_Text_Yo: Fìlà ò dùn bí-i ká mọ̀ọ́ dé; ṣòkòtò ò dùn bí-i kà mọ̀ọ́ wọ̀.
Target_Text_En: A hat is of little use if one does not know how to wear it well; pants are of little use if one does not know how to wear them well.
Cultural_Context: Having assets is one thing; knowing how to use them effectively is another.

Source_Text_Yo: Fìrífìrí ò jọ kolombo; ìhòòhò ò jọ awọ.
Target_Text_En: Vaguely is not like clearly; nakedness is not like leather.
Cultural_Context: It is better to be clear about something than to be vague, better to be clothed in leather than to be naked.

Source_Text_Yo: Erìndínlógún àgbọn ò ṣeé dá nÍfá.
Target_Text_En: Sixteen coconuts are useless for casting [consulting] Ifá.
Cultural_Context: Everything has its limitations as well as its uses.

Source_Text_Yo: Funfun lẹyẹ ńṣu, kì í ṣu dúdú.
Target_Text_En: White is the color of bird’s droppings, never black.
Cultural_Context: Certain things one can rely on to happen in certain set ways.

Source_Text_Yo: Funfun ni iyì eyín; ó gún régé ni iyì ọrùn; ọmú ṣìkí-ṣìkí ni iyì obìnrin.
Target_Text_En: Whiteness is the pride of the teeth; straight ness is the pride of the neck; firm, pointed breasts are the pride of a woman.
Cultural_Context: There is a proper and ideal form for everything. Compare 2723.

Source_Text_Yo: Gààrí olóóyo; ó ti ládùn tele, àgbéré ni ṣúgà ńgbé.
Target_Text_En: Sifted cassava grits are sweet by them selves; sugar is simply strutting for nothing.
Cultural_Context: Natural endowments need no validation or acknowledgment by detractors; and, the self-sufficient person needs no help from others.

Source_Text_Yo: Gùdù-gudu ò ṣéé be èlùbo.
Target_Text_En: Poisonous yam is nothing to make yam flour with.
Cultural_Context: A certain object or person is of no use to anyone.

Source_Text_Yo: Gùdù-gudu ò ṣéé sè; ó kọ àwàsunjẹ.
Target_Text_En: Poisonous yam cannot be cooked for food; it defies being roasted to eat.
Cultural_Context: A certain thing or person is of no use to anyone.

Source_Text_Yo: ‘‘Gba akọṣu’’ ni ‘‘Gba ewùrà’’; gbà lẹ́nu ọ̀fọ́n-ọ̀n ni gbà lenu agánrán.
Target_Text_En: ‘‘Have a prime-quality yam’’ equals ‘‘Have a water yam’’;60 snatching something out of a rat’s mouth is no different from snatching something from the mouth of a green parrot.
Cultural_Context: All gift giving is of a kind; all property husbanding is of a kind.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbà lẹ́nu asín ni gbà lenu èkúté.
Target_Text_En: Taking something from a malodorous rat’s mouth is the same as taking something from a mouse’s mouth.
Cultural_Context: All inappropriate behavior is of a kind.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbogbo ohun tí a bá ńṣe lónìí, ìtàn ni lola.
Target_Text_En: Whatever one does today is a story tomorrow
Cultural_Context: Whatever the event, however grandiose or earthshaking, it eventually passes into memory.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbogbo ohun tí okó bá ńṣe, òbò ní ńgbà á.
Target_Text_En: Whatever effort the penis might put forth, it is the vagina that reaps the reward.
Cultural_Context: A prayer or incantation that a person be the benefi ciary of his her efforts, and even of those of others.

Source_Text_Yo: Há-ń-há lopolo fi ga ju alámù lọ.
Target_Text_En: Only by bloating itself does the toad come to be taller than the lizard.
Cultural_Context: There is really nothing to choose among certain rivals.

Source_Text_Yo: Híhó là ńhó tọ olè lẹ́hìn.
Target_Text_En: It is with clamorous insults that a crowd pursues a thief.
Cultural_Context: A person who disgraces himself or herself deserves public humiliation.

Source_Text_Yo: Hùn hùn hùn inú ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ inú ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ ní ńgbé.
Target_Text_En: The [meaning of the] grunting of a pig does not go beyond the pig.
Cultural_Context: The ranting and raving of a worthless person are not worth one’s attention.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbàje ìkọ̀kọ̀, gba-n-gba ni lójú Olúwa.
Target_Text_En: Wickedness perpetrated in secret is open knowledge to God.
Cultural_Context: No secret wickedness can be hidden from God.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi a bá pè lórí ní ńhurun.
Target_Text_En: It is the place named the head that grows hair.
Cultural_Context: People and objects should live up to expectations.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi tí Gàmbàrí ti ńjẹ obì bọ̀ kó tó pọn léhín, oná jìn.
