Target_Text_En: The time the Hausa person began chewing kola such that all his or her teeth are now red is far in the past.
Cultural_Context: Present conditions had their origins long ago.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi tí ó tòrò ò mu agbè; ibi tó mu agbè-é léwu.
Target_Text_En: The place where the water is clear is not deep enough for the gourd; the place where the water is deep enough, though, is dangerous.
Cultural_Context: There is no boon without its dangers.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi tí ọká pẹbu sí lońjẹ e ḿbo wá bá a.
Target_Text_En: Wherever the viper makes its lair, there its food will come to find it.
Cultural_Context: Whatever is des tined to come one’s way will do so without one’s lifting a finger.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibi tí ọmọ ńrè lọmọ ò mọ̀, ọmọ́ mọ ibi tó ti wá
Target_Text_En: What the child does not know is where he or she is headed; the child knows where he or she came from.
Cultural_Context: The future may be a mystery, but the past is not.

Source_Text_Yo: Ibìkan ṣoṣo ko la ti ńrí orun.
Target_Text_En: It is not only at one location that one can see the sky.
Cultural_Context: There are few opportunities that do not have alternatives.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbọkúbọ lọmọdé ḿbọ kórikóto; ìgbàkúgbà ní ńgbà á.
Target_Text_En: Children’s manner of sacrificing to their guardian spirit is nonchalant, and its way of heeding their worship is also nonchalant.
Cultural_Context: How one approaches others determines how they respond.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìbù-ùbú là ńtu òkun; odò-odò là ńtu osà; ibi tí a bá fe là ńtu Ọ̀yán
Target_Text_En: One rows in the ocean along the shore; in the [Lagos] lagoon one rows down the channel; as for the yán river, one rows as one pleases.
Cultural_Context: Each situation has its peculiar difficulties and demands, which must be accommodated.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìdálùú ni ìṣe ìlú; eégún ní ḿgba owó òde lÓṣogbo
Target_Text_En: The customs of a town are established on the establishment of the town; at Òṣogbo, tax collecting is the duty of masqueraders.
Cultural_Context: Different people have different responsibili ties.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìdí nikú ìgbín; orí nikú ahun.
Target_Text_En: The rear end is the death of the snail; the front end is the death of the tortoise.
Cultural_Context: Each person is vulnerable in a different way.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìdìkudì là ńdi ẹrù ikùn.
Target_Text_En: Indifferently is one’s manner of tying the load destined for the belly.
Cultural_Context: One does not need to worry overmuch about details where matters never exposed to public scrutiny are concerned.

Source_Text_Yo: Ifá ńlá ní ńya olúwa ẹ̀ lápò
Target_Text_En: It is an extraordinary [useless] Ifá that rips the owner’s sack.
Cultural_Context: It is a strange charm that ruins the owner instead of benefiting him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbà iyán ò jọ ìgbà ìyàn; yíyó là ńyó nígbà iyán, rírù là ńrù nígbà ìyàn.
Target_Text_En: The days of pounded yam are different from the days of famine; one enjoys a full stom ach on the days of pounded yam, while one grows lean during the days of famine.
Cultural_Context: Life is made up of different seasons.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbà kì í yí padà kéwúre bí màlúù.
Target_Text_En: Times cannot so change that a goat will give birth to a calf
Cultural_Context: Certain things in life are immutable.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìdtí ò mátà; woléwolé lẹj bá wí.
Target_Text_En: Dirt does not matter; only the sanitary inspector fusses.
Cultural_Context: The subject under discussion is not of great import.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbà ò lọ bí òréré.
Target_Text_En: Time does not go on endlessly.
Cultural_Context: Life is short.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbà tí ìlú bá ńdùn jù, à mọ̀ pé yó tùú
Target_Text_En: When a town becomes too happy a place, one should know that it is on the verge of breaking up.
Cultural_Context: Excess of even good things brings disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbẹ̀hìn laláyò ńta.
Target_Text_En: It is at the end of the game that the real champion shines.
Cultural_Context: Early advantages do not ensure final victory.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbẹ̀hìnwá ayé ò ní ìmo; ó dá fún ẹni tí òì tii kú.
Target_Text_En: The manner of life’s end is unknown; the oracle is directed at those who have not died.
Cultural_Context: Said as consolation to people suffer ing misfortune or reverses; it says fortunes may change for the better.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbẹ́kẹ̀lé èèyàn, asán ni.
Target_Text_En: Trust placed in humans is misplaced.
Cultural_Context: One should be wary about trusting people.

Source_Text_Yo: Igi ìbàjẹ́ layé ńsáré gùn
Target_Text_En: It is the tree of defamation that the world hurries to climb.
Cultural_Context: People are ever more eager to seek the ruination of others than to seek their elevation.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìgbà laṣọ, ìgbà lẹ̀wù, ìgbà lòdèrée-kókò nÍlọrin.
Target_Text_En: The season prescribes cloth; the season prescribes clothes; the season determines the presence of the Senegal dove in Ìlọrin.
Cultural_Context: Everything in its proper time or season.

Source_Text_Yo: Igi tí a bá torí ẹ̀ gbodì, ó yẹ kó ṣená fúnni yá.
Target_Text_En: The tree on account of which one makes enemies should at least kindle fire for one to warm oneself.
Cultural_Context: One deserves some recom pense for one’s sacrifices.

Source_Text_Yo: Igi tí a fehìntì tí ò gbani dúró, bó wó luni kò lè pani
Target_Text_En: A tree that one leans on but that cannot support one’s weight, if it falls on you it will not crush you.
Cultural_Context: A person whose support is ineffectual cannot do one any ill by his or her opposition.

Source_Text_Yo: Igi tó hù lójú ẹni kì í dá pani
Target_Text_En: A tree that sprouts while one is alive can not fall and crush one.
Cultural_Context: Upstarts whose beginnings one knows cannot have supreme power over one.

Source_Text_Yo: Igúnnugún kì í kú séwe.
Target_Text_En: The vulture never dies young.
Cultural_Context: A wish or prayer that a person may live long.

Source_Text_Yo: Igbó ńla la ti nrí ẹyẹ-keyẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is in a huge forest that one finds all sorts of birds.
Cultural_Context: Multitude offers variety.

Source_Text_Yo: Igbó ńla ní ḿmu ẹni mu orí.
Target_Text_En: It is a huge forest that swallows a person, in cluding the person’s head.
Cultural_Context: It is a great task that makes great demands on one.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìháhá tó há sọ́rùn opẹ, orí araa ẹ̀ ló fi ńrù ú.
Target_Text_En: The pericarp of the palm fruit that is wedged atop the palm tree is a burden that the palm tree itself must bear.
Cultural_Context: Whatever ill will one wishes others recoils on oneself.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìhìn ọjà là ḿgbo nájà.
Target_Text_En: It is the report one hears about a market that induces one to trade in it.
Cultural_Context: A person’s or a thing’s reputation determines how people will act toward it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìhó odòó bo ìhó igba èèyàn mọ́lẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The roar of a river drowns the roar of two hundred people.
Cultural_Context: One illustrious person makes a greater impression than a multitude of worthless people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìjà kì í lọ lásán kóníjà má fara pa
Target_Text_En: A fight does not end without those involved showing some mark from it.
Cultural_Context: The aftermath of a fight or quarrel is never like the time before the fight or quarrel.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìjà ní ńje ‘‘Ìlú ḿpè ọ́’’; gbogbo wọn ló lórúkọ.
Target_Text_En: It is when there is a quarrel that the message says, ‘‘The town demands your presence’’; everybody [in the town] has a name.
Cultural_Context: When communication with acquaintances becomes cryptic, something is amiss.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìjà ò bímọ kó rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: A fight or quarrel never fathers a child that is docile.
Cultural_Context: The aftermath of a fight or quarrel is always troublesome.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìjá tán lóko àropọ̀; egbọ́n tẹ Ifá, àbúrò-ó gbéyàwó
Target_Text_En: There is no more cause for a fight on the communal farm; the elder brother has taken up Ifá divination, and the younger has gone to get married.
Cultural_Context: The principals in a feud are too preoccupied with other pressing problems to carry on the feud.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìjàgbon lẹ́hìn ẹni tí ò kú; ẹní kú bo lọ́wọ́ aápọn.
Target_Text_En: Constant worries are the lot of the person who has not died; only those who have died are free from worries.
Cultural_Context: Only death saves humans from the need to worry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìjàmbá ṣolè, onílé tají
Target_Text_En: A great disaster befalls the burglar: the homeowner wakes up unexpectedly.
Cultural_Context: Said of an evildoer who is beset with his or her comeuppance.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìjẹ̀bú kì í jẹ́ Òjó
Target_Text_En: The Ìjebú never bear the name Òjó.
Cultural_Context: Certain things one must never do.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkà ìbá là a bàlúje; ẹrú ìbá jọba èèyàn ìbá kùkan.
Target_Text_En: Were the wicked to prosper, they would ruin the town; were a slave to be made king, there would be no one left in the town.
Cultural_Context: To put the affairs of a community in the hands of wicked or careless people is to destroy the community.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkaakà là ḿbá ọmọrí igbá.
Target_Text_En: Face up is the way one always finds the cala bash lid.
Cultural_Context: Some things are ordained to be certain ways always.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkórítamẹ́ta tí ńdààmú àlejò.
Target_Text_En: The fork in the road throws a stranger into a quandary.
Cultural_Context: Those who know not the se crets of a process have no way to solve its puzzles.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkótí ò jẹ́ nnkan lẹ́rù ìyàwó
Target_Text_En: A hairpin does not add much to the luggage of a bride.
Cultural_Context: A little chore is of no conse quence in addition to an immense task.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkokọ̀ ayé yá ju ìkọ̀kọ̀ ọ̀run lọ.
Target_Text_En: The obscurity of this earth is far better than the obscurity of heaven.
Cultural_Context: Not knowing what is what in this life is better than not knowing what is in store for one in heaven.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú ẹgbẹ̀rún kan ò payé rẹ́; bí èèyán ṣe ńkú làwọn mìíràn ńwá sáyé.
Target_Text_En: The death of any one thousand people will not obliterate the world; as some people die, so others come to life.
Cultural_Context: Humankind will survive the most deadly disasters.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú kì í jẹun ẹni kó pani; àrùn kì í jẹun ẹni kó ṣeni.
Target_Text_En: Death does not eat one’s food and then kill one; disease does not eat one’s food and then afflict one.
Cultural_Context: Those who enter into cove nants are obliged to fulfill their part of the bargain.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú ò je kẹ́ni ó lọ sógun; ìfà ò je kẹ́ni ó foyè sílẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Death keeps one from going to war; spoils keep one from giving up one’s chieftaincy.
Cultural_Context: Thoughts of the advantages of a position make one reluctant to contemplate giving it up.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú pa olówó; odò-ó gbé ìwọ̀fà; ṣọ̀npọ̀nọ́n pa onígbọ̀wọ́; ẹni tó mọ oye owó ṣẹ̀ ḿbùṣe.
Target_Text_En: Death killed the lender; a river carried off the pawn; the guarantor died of smallpox; there is hardly anyone left who knows the amount of the debt.
Cultural_Context: Said of a matter that occurred so long ago that hardly anyone remains who remembers the circumstances.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú tí yó pani kì í peni lórúkọ.
Target_Text_En: The death that will kill a person does not call the person by name.
Cultural_Context: Disasters do not announce their approach.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú wọnú ahoro ṣákálá.
Target_Text_En: Death enters an abandoned home in vain.
Cultural_Context: A person who has lost everything has noth ing else to lose.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikun ní ḿbá ẹkún wá; kẹ̀lẹ̀bẹ̀ ní ḿbá ‘‘tùẹ̀’’ wá.
Target_Text_En: Mucus is what accompanies crying; phlegm is what accompanies a cough.
Cultural_Context: Each afflic tion has its particular misery.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikún ńwá onà àtilọ, won ní ẹrú àna ee sá; àwòdì re Ìbarà efúùfù-ú ta á nídìí pá; ó ní iṣẹ́ kúkú yá
Target_Text_En: The squirrel is waiting for an excuse to get away and is told that its parents-in-law’s slave has escaped; the eagle prepares to depart for Ìbarà, and the breeze lifts its tail feathers; time, it says, to get going.
Cultural_Context: A person straining to do a certain thing is grateful for any excuse offered him or her.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé tí a fi itọ́ mọ, ìrì ni yó wo
Target_Text_En: A house built with saliva will be demolished by the dew.
Cultural_Context: Ventures based on shaky foun dations will not withstand even the flimsiest of tests.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé tí a gbá èèyàn létí wọ̀, bó pe títí a ó gbàá èèyàn létí jáde níbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: A home one is able to enter only after one has slapped someone in the ears: sooner or later one will have to slap someone in the ears in order to get out of it.
Cultural_Context: A transaction that has a fractious beginning will end in a fractious way.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilẹ̀ ìjàmbá kì í ṣu.
Target_Text_En: The day of disaster is never done.
Cultural_Context: Disaster can befall anyone anytime.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìlú tí a ò ti rímú rí ní ḿmú imú ẹni tó àká.
Target_Text_En: It is in a town where no one has ever seen a nose that one’s nose seems as capacious as a granary.
Cultural_Context: A person seeing an ordinary thing for the first time always overestimates its importance or significance.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìmàdò ìbá ṣe bí ẹlẹ́de a bàlúje; ẹrú ìbá jọba èèyàn kì bá kùkan.
Target_Text_En: Were the warthog to enter the town, it would ruin the town; were a slave to become king, there would be no citizens left.
Cultural_Context: Trust ing matters to the hands of an unfit person guarantees disaster.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìmàdò kì í dé odò kó tòrò
Target_Text_En: A warthog does not arrive at the stream and leave it unmuddied.
Cultural_Context: A boorish person’s intervention in a matter always muddies the water.

Source_Text_Yo: Iná dile lehìn asunṣujẹ.
Target_Text_En: The fire earns some rest after the person roasting yams to eat is done.
Cultural_Context: Peace descends after the departure of a troublemaker.

Source_Text_Yo: Iná jí ó gbé aṣọ epo mú; oòrún jí ó gbewù oṣẹ̀rìṣẹ̀rì bọrùn; òṣùpá jí ó gbáwo-ọ yìnyín.
Target_Text_En: Fire wakes up and takes up a cloth of palm oil; the sun rises and puts on a dazzling dress; the moon rises and dons a skin of hailstones.
Cultural_Context: Each phenomenon has its spe cial qualities. Or, comment in praise of an exceptional person.

Source_Text_Yo: Iná jó lóko kò jó erùpẹ̀ ilẹ̀; ọ̀ràn tí ńṣeni ò ṣolùkù ẹni.
Target_Text_En: Fire consumes the forest but not the earth; what plagues one does not plague one’s friends.
Cultural_Context: Nobody shares one’s fate.

Source_Text_Yo: Iná orí ò jó aṣọ; àbàtà rẹẹrẹ ò gbọko.
Target_Text_En: Fire-of-the-head [head lice] cannot burn one’s clothing; floating mud will not accom modate [or support] a boat.
Cultural_Context: Each task or occasion has its specific requirements.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìpọn-ọ́n ríkú ki orí bọ̀ ọ́.
Target_Text_En: The wooden spoon sees death and plunges into it.
Cultural_Context: Comment on the death-defying behavior of an intrepid person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìrì kékeré ní ńdi odò; ìrì wàwà ní ńdi òjò; bọ́mọdé méje-é bá kọ oúnjẹ ale, a dìjà àgbàlagbà.
Target_Text_En: Tiny dewdrops soon become a river, and heavy dews soon become rain; if seven children refuse their dinner, a fight ensues among adults.
Cultural_Context: Seemingly unimportant matters soon mushroom into unmanageable problems.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìrírí ní ḿmúni gbọ́n.
Target_Text_En: It is experience that makes one wise.
Cultural_Context: Ex perience is the best teacher.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìsọ̀rọ̀ nìgbèsì.
Target_Text_En: How one speaks is how one receives a re sponse.
Cultural_Context: People respond in kind to the way one addresses or behaves toward them.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣe èèyàn nìṣe ẹranko.
Target_Text_En: As animals behave, so do humans.
Cultural_Context: One may learn much about humans by watching animals.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣe tí a fi he àdá lóko igbó ni yó ṣe sọnù lóko ẹgàn.
Target_Text_En: What caused one to find a cutlass in the forest will cause one to misplace it in the wilderness.
Cultural_Context: Easy come, easy go.

Source_Text_Yo: Iṣe ḿbẹ nílé, iṣẹ́ ḿbẹ lóko: ìwọ̀fà ọ̀pọ̀lọ́.
Target_Text_En: There is work at home, and there is work on the farm,’’ said the frog that was pawned.
Cultural_Context: No matter where one goes, there is work to be done.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìṣe ò dún, ìyà ò fọhùn ká mọ ẹni tí ìyà ńdùn lára.
Target_Text_En: Destitution does not make a sound, and suffering does not speak to let people know who is plagued by suffering.
Cultural_Context: One cannot tell from just looking who is in the grip of suffering.

Source_Text_Yo: Isú paradà ó diyán, àgbàdó paradà ó dẹ̀kọ.
Target_Text_En: Yam changes its state and becomes pounded yam; corn changes its state and becomes steamed corn meal.
Cultural_Context: People and things can change for the better.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìtì ogẹ̀dẹ̀ẹ́ bo lọ́wọ́-ọ gbẹ́nagbẹ́nà
Target_Text_En: The banana trunk is safe from the carpenter.
Cultural_Context: One is safe from those who have no use for whatever one has.

Source_Text_Yo: Iwájú iwájú là ḿbá ọ̀nà.
Target_Text_En: One always finds that the road is ahead of one [one can never walk past it].
Cultural_Context: Said as a prayer that a person may never fall behind his or her peers, or as a boast that one will ever be ahead of one’s peers.

Source_Text_Yo: Iwájú iwáju lọ̀pá ẹ̀bìtì ńré sí.
Target_Text_En: The ẹ̀bìtì snare always springs forward when tripped.
Cultural_Context: Used in the context of a prayer to wish someone continuous progress.

Source_Text_Yo: Iwájú lalákàn ńfà sí.
Target_Text_En: Forward is the direction in which the crab crawls.
Cultural_Context: A wish that a person’s fortunes will always improve.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìwofà tó gun ẹṣin lọ sódò, owó ní ńgun owó.
Target_Text_En: The pawn who rides the horse to the stream: money is riding on money.
Cultural_Context: Said to indicate that the people referred to, though seem ingly different, are really indistinguishable.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìwọ̀sí loko etílé; ìyà loko ẹgàn ńjẹ
Target_Text_En: A farm hard by the town brings insults; a farm far away in the wilds suffers neglect.
Cultural_Context: Every pursuit has its drawbacks.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyà méjì kì í jẹ òkú; bí kò bá ráṣọ bora, a rílẹ̀ bora.
Target_Text_En: Two misfortunes will not befall a corpse; if it lacks a shroud, it will not lack earth to cover itself.
Cultural_Context: If one’s first option fails, there will always be a fall-back alternative.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyá tó bí aṣọ ló bí ẹ̀wù.
Target_Text_En: The mother who gave birth to the cloth also gave birth to the shirt.
Cultural_Context: Two or more seemingly different things are essentially the same.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyáa ṣòkòtò ló bí bàntẹ́.
Target_Text_En: The mother of the trousers also gave birth to the loincloth.
Cultural_Context: Though apparently different, the two entities are virtually indistinguish able.

Source_Text_Yo: Iyán ogún ọdún a máa jóni lọ́wọ́.
Target_Text_En: Twenty-year-old pounded yams can still scald one’s fingers.
Cultural_Context: One can still remember favors or injuries twenty years after they were done.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyàwó fi àparò dá ilá; ọkọ́ jẹ iyán àìjẹkù.
Target_Text_En: The wife cooks a partridge stew, and the husband eats the pounded yam without leaving a morsel.
Cultural_Context: It is difficult to restrain oneself in the face of something powerfully appealing.

Source_Text_Yo: Iyì lọbá fi orí bíbe ṣe; ọba kì í mu ẹ̀je.
Target_Text_En: A king derives only awe from beheading people; the king does not drink blood.
Cultural_Context: One does certain things out of duty and not from desire.

Source_Text_Yo: Jẹ kí njẹ kì í pa ayò.
Target_Text_En: You win and I win does not make for de feat in a game.
Cultural_Context: When both sides are evenly matched, there will be no winner; coopera tion makes for harmony.

Source_Text_Yo: Jẹ kí njẹ ní ḿmú ayò dùn.
Target_Text_En: You win and I win is what makes a game exciting.
Cultural_Context: Sharing alike makes for a harmo nious relationship.

Source_Text_Yo: Jìgìjìgì ò ṣéé fà tu
Target_Text_En: A firmly rooted plant cannot be uprooted.
Cultural_Context: Whatever is based on a sound foundation will not be easily dismantled.

Source_Text_Yo: Ká kú ní kékeré ká fẹṣin ṣe ìrẹ̀lẹ̀ ẹni, ó sàn ju ká dàgbà kú láìní adìẹ ìrènà.
Target_Text_En: To die young and have a horse sacrificed to ease one’s passage to the beyond is better than to reach old age before dying but with not even a chicken sacrificed to ease one’s passage.
Cultural_Context: Better to die young and prosperous than to die old and destitute.

Source_Text_Yo: Ká ọwọ́ fún mi kí nká ẹse fún ẹ.
Target_Text_En: Move your hands out of the way for me, and I will move my legs out of the way for you.
Cultural_Context: Consideration earns consideration in return.

Source_Text_Yo: Kàkà kí ewé àgbọn rọ̀, pípele ní ńpele sí i.
Target_Text_En: The coconut palm’s leaves instead of wilting only become even stiffer.
Cultural_Context: The opposite of what one has been hoping for is what keeps happening.

Source_Text_Yo: Kán-un-kàn-un ìlù ìgbàgbọ́.
Target_Text_En: Bereft of rhythm and bereft of coherence is the sound of Christians drumming.
Cultural_Context: The matter or person referred to lacks any sense of coherence.

Source_Text_Yo: Keese-keese lẹ rí, kààsà-kààsà ḿbo lehìn; kààsà-kààsà baba keese-keese
Target_Text_En: Something evil is all you have seen, but be hind it comes something extremely evil; Kààsà-kààsà is the father of all keese-keese.
Cultural_Context: What people are complaining about does not compare in terror to what is in the offing.

Source_Text_Yo: Kì í pẹ́ títí kí eji ọdún má rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: No matter how long it takes, the annual rain will eventually fall.
Cultural_Context: What is ordained to happen eventually will, however long it might take.

Source_Text_Yo: Kì í ṣe títí ayé ni Ọ̀rúnmìlà ò níí jẹ àgbàdo mọ́.
Target_Text_En: It is not forever that rúnmìlà will abstain from eating corn.
Cultural_Context: Even though one is en joying plenty, lean times may come around.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí ni à ńjẹ tí kì í tan? Kí ni ó ńkù sílẹ̀ tí kì í dọ̀la?
Target_Text_En: What does one eat that one does not even tually finish? What does one leave aside that does not keep until the morrow?
Cultural_Context: A per son who knows no thrift deprives himself or herself of a future; the person who puts something aside today will have something to use in the future.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí oràn ó lè sú ọlọ́ràn la fi ńsọ pé a ò rí irú èyí rí; kò sí irú ohun tí ojú ò rí rí.
Target_Text_En: It is only so that the offender might know the enormity of the offense that one says one has never seen the likes of it before; there is nothing the likes of which the eyes have never seen.
Cultural_Context: There is nothing a person does that others have not done before, even though one might say the contrary in order to regulate people’s behavior.

Source_Text_Yo: Kíjìpá kì í ṣe awọ.
Target_Text_En: Durable hand-woven cloth is not leather.
Cultural_Context: One should not overestimate the quality of one’s possessions or make too much of one’s position.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ẹni tó mọ bí omí ṣe ńdénú àgbọn.
Target_Text_En: Nobody knows how water gets into the coconut
Cultural_Context: No one knows the mystyery of nature

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ‘‘Fi síle’’ mo; gbogbo ayé di ‘‘Mú u re!’’
Target_Text_En: There is no more ‘‘Let him or her be’’; all of life is now ‘‘Hold him or her tight!’’
Cultural_Context: The world no longer knows mercy.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí obìnrin ọ̀fẹ́; bó ṣe akúwárápá, owó ni.
Target_Text_En: No woman is available free; even if she has epilepsy, she costs money.
Cultural_Context: One must have the means if one means to take a wife.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ohun tí a ńjẹ tí kò tán, àfi ọlá Ọlorun.
Target_Text_En: There is nothing one eats that is never fin ished except the grace of God.
Cultural_Context: One should never forget that whatever material things one has will eventually be gone.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ohun tí ò nítàn.
Target_Text_En: There is nothing without a history.
Cultural_Context: Every phenomenon, as well as every condition, has its explanation.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí ohun tí owó pa tí kò kú.
Target_Text_En: There is nothing money kills that does not die.
Cultural_Context: Money accomplishes all.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò sí orin kan tó borí aráyé.
Target_Text_En: There is no song that surpasses ‘‘People of this world.’’
Cultural_Context: Said when all that needs to be said has been said. Also, there is nothing one needs to be more wary of than people.

Source_Text_Yo: Kò tó iṣẹ́ ikú; arẹwà ló ńpa.
Target_Text_En: One cannot put it [anything] past death; it kills beautiful people.
Cultural_Context: Even beautiful people are not beyond the notice of death.

Source_Text_Yo: Kòkòrò ní ńdi labalábá.
Target_Text_En: It is an insect that becomes the butterfly.
Cultural_Context: The youth of today will be the elders of tomorrow. Compare 4981.

Source_Text_Yo: Kòsíǹkan òun nǹkan ní ńjọ ńrìn.
Target_Text_En: There-is-no-problem always travels in the company of problem.
Cultural_Context: Even when there is no problem, problems are never far away.

Source_Text_Yo: Kòtónilẹ́rù tí ńtani lórí
Target_Text_En: A-thing-that-is-not-a-big-enough-load-for-one hurts one’s head nevertheless.
Cultural_Context: Said of an insignificant thing that nevertheless constitutes a persistent nuisance.

Source_Text_Yo: Kọ̀lọ̀kọ̀lọ̀ tí ńgbé adìẹ ò jẹ́ ká mọ olè.
Target_Text_En: The fox that steals chickens prevents one from knowing about the thief.
Cultural_Context: Said of cir cumstances in which offenders are able to hide behind fortuitous occurrences.

Source_Text_Yo: Kọ̀lọ̀kọ̀lọ̀ tí ńgbe adìẹ ò sanra bí igún.
Target_Text_En: The fox that steals chickens is not as fat as the vulture.
Cultural_Context: A criminal has not profited visibly from his or her crimes.

Source_Text_Yo: Lójú ọ̀tá, bí kí ìdálẹ̀ di ọ̀run ni.
Target_Text_En: For one’s enemy, the wish is that one’s jour ney would lead to heaven.
Cultural_Context: One’s enemies never wish one well.

Source_Text_Yo: Mo gbójú wo ewé ìgbá, ng ò rí èyí tó gba àkàṣù níbẹ̀
Target_Text_En: I looked up at the leaves of the acacia tree, but I did not see any that would do for wrapping corn meal.
Cultural_Context: However precious a thing might be, if it will not serve one’s end, it is of little value.

Source_Text_Yo: Nǹkan kì í dùn ko tún pọ̀
Target_Text_En: A thing is never both pleasant and plentiful.
Cultural_Context: One cannot have things all ways.

Source_Text_Yo: Ò báà sín iyùn ẹgbàá, kóo sín sẹ̀gi pelú, ata wẹẹrẹ ni lójú abúni.
Target_Text_En: Even if you wore coral beads and tubular beads in addition, to a detractor they are just like red peppers.
Cultural_Context: Nothing one does impresses detractors.

Source_Text_Yo: Ó kù dẹ̀dẹ̀ ká kó iwì wọ Akẹ̀sán, ọba tí à ó yìn-ín tẹ́rí gbaṣọ
Target_Text_En: We were just about to enter Ak sán market with our praise-singing performance when the king we would honor gave up the ghost.
Cultural_Context: One’s gifts or services may be too late to be of any use to the recipient.

Source_Text_Yo: Obínrin kì í ní iná kí torogún ẹ̀ má jòó
Target_Text_En: A woman’s having fire does not stop her co wife’s from burning.
Cultural_Context: One’s fierceness does not stop one’s rivals from being fierce also.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrín pọ̀ lọ́jà, gbogbo wọn ló lọ́kọ.
Target_Text_En: Women are plentiful at the market, but all of them have husbands.
Cultural_Context: There are few things out there that have not been spoken for.

Source_Text_Yo: Òbírí lọkọ̀ ńdà; yíyí layé ńyí.
Target_Text_En: It is all of a sudden that a boat capsizes; turning is what the world does.
Cultural_Context: Nobody can predict the future.

Source_Text_Yo: Obìnrin kì í je Òjó.
Target_Text_En: No woman ever bears the name Òjó.
Cultural_Context: There are certain things a person may not do, simply because of who he or she is.

Source_Text_Yo: Ogún ọdún kì í ṣe títí láé.
Target_Text_En: Twenty years hence is not the same as the infinite future.
Cultural_Context: The furthest day arrives in time. Compare the entry that follows.

Source_Text_Yo: Ogún ọdún ḿbọ̀ wá kọ̀la.
Target_Text_En: Twenty years hence will soon become tomorrow.
Cultural_Context: No matter how distant, the future sooner or later arrives. Compare the preceding entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun ẹlẹgẹ́ kì í gbè é bàjẹ́.
Target_Text_En: An excessively delicate thing is easy to ruin.
Cultural_Context: One cannot be too careful with delicate matters.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun ẹye ńjẹ lóko lẹyẹ ńgbé fò.
Target_Text_En: Whatever the bird eats on the farm is what it takes with it in flight.
Cultural_Context: One always devotes great attention to protecting what is dear to one.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun ńlá-ńlá tó ròkè, ìlẹ̀ ní ḿbo.
Target_Text_En: The mighty thing that rose into the heavens will wind up back on earth.
Cultural_Context: However long the diversion, a matter eventually winds up before the tribunal charged with adjudicat ing it.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí a bá ní là ńnáání; ọmọ àgbẹ̀ ńnáání ewùrà; ọmọ aṣegità ńnáání èpo igi; ọmọ alápatà ńnáání ẹ̀do ẹran; ọmọ ọdẹ ńnáání ẹran gbígbẹ.
Target_Text_En: Whatever one has [in abundance] is what one disparages; the child of the farmer dis parages the water yam; the firewood seller attaches little value to the bark of firewood; the child of the butcher belittles cow liver; the son of the hunter disdains dried bush meat.
Cultural_Context: One never attaches much value to articles one has in plenty.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tí kòì délẹ̀ yó tàn-án; èyí tó ti dé tán nìyẹn
Target_Text_En: Whatever is in the offing will end in time; that applies only to what has already arrived.
Cultural_Context: One can know the nature of only those things one has experienced.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó bá dunni là ńjagun mú lógun.
Target_Text_En: Whatever one craves most painfully is what one takes as booty in a war.
Cultural_Context: One’s greatest need is always uppermost in one’s preoccu pation.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó bá wuni ní ńpo lorọ̀ ẹni; ológún ẹrú kú, aṣọ ee ku ọ̀kan ṣoṣo.
Target_Text_En: Whatever one most values will be the most abundant component of one’s wealth; the owner of twelve slaves dies and leaves only one garment.
Cultural_Context: One spends one’s wealth on whatever one most likes.

Source_Text_Yo: Ohun tó wà lẹ́hìn ẹ̀fà-á ju èje lọ.
Target_Text_En: What comes after six is a lot more than seven.
Cultural_Context: People seldom realize how serious the consequences of their actions could be.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò àkọ́rọ̀ kì í ro lọ́sàn-án; ejidún kì í palẹ̀ lóru.
Target_Text_En: The first rain never falls in the afternoon; the annual downpour does not soak the soil in the middle of the night.
Cultural_Context: There is a proper time for everything.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò iwájú kì í pa ahun; òjò ẹ̀hìn kì í pa ìgbín; lẹ́hìn lẹ́hìn lọlọ́bẹ ńso.
Target_Text_En: The rain ahead does not beat the tortoise; the rain behind does not soak the snail; ever to the rear does the olobe grow its fruits.
Cultural_Context: Incantation to ward off evil.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò lọkọ àgbàdo.
Target_Text_En: Rain is the lord of the corn.
Cultural_Context: Without one’s source of sustenance one is nothing.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò ò bẹ́nìkan ṣọ̀rẹ́, ẹni ejí rí leji ńpa.
Target_Text_En: The rain plays favorites with no one; whomever the rain finds, it drenches.
Cultural_Context: Misfortune is not selective.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò tó rọ̀ lásìkò ní ńjẹ́ ejidún.
Target_Text_En: It is rain that falls at its proper time that is known as the annual heavy rain.
Cultural_Context: Windfalls that come when one cannot take advantage of them are of no value.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojoojúmo ko lobìnrin ńrí ń kan oṣù.
Target_Text_En: It is not every day that a woman sees her monthly thing [i.e., menstruation].
Cultural_Context: Not every day is Christmas.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í mo kéji òwúrọ̀ má rọ̀.
Target_Text_En: A day does not dawn without formation of the morning dew.
Cultural_Context: A prayer that one might always find blessing, just as the morning is always blessed with the dew.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kì í pa ojú jẹ.
Target_Text_En: An eye does not kill an[other] eye for food.
Cultural_Context: Staring eyes pose no danger.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú kòkòrò kì í pa ojú kòkòrò jẹ.
Target_Text_En: An envious eye cannot kill an envious eye for food.
Cultural_Context: One person’s envy can’t stare down another person’s.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú ò lẹ́jẹ̀, omi ní ńsun.
Target_Text_En: The eyes have no blood; they only ooze tears.
Cultural_Context: One can seldom tell from mere appearance what another person’s inner state is.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú tí a fi ata bo; màjò-màjò-ó tán níbẹ̀
Target_Text_En: The eyes into which pepper has been thrown: there one finds the ultimate in frantic jumping about.
Cultural_Context: Where one finds the greatest disaster, one will also find the greatest lamentation.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkìtì bààbà ní ńpẹ̀kun òpópó.
Target_Text_En: It is usually a large hill that marks the end of a straight avenue.
Cultural_Context: Nothing goes on forever.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkò tí a bá sọ ságbọn làgbọn ńsọ síni.
Target_Text_En: The stone one throws at a coconut palm is the same as the coconut palm throws back.
Cultural_Context: One’s evil deeds are likely to recoil on one.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkú ẹjọ́ lọlọ́jà ńdá.
Target_Text_En: It is a dead case that the ruler adjudicates.
Cultural_Context: A matter that has come before a conciliatory body is no longer urgent.

Source_Text_Yo: Òkú ò lè sin baba
Target_Text_En: A dead person cannot serve the patriarch.
Cultural_Context: One cannot expect service from a corpse.

Source_Text_Yo: Olè lọmọ olè ńfìwà jọ
Target_Text_En: A thief ’s child takes after him.
Cultural_Context: One takes after one’s parents.

Source_Text_Yo: Olè ní ḿmọ ẹsẹ̀ olè-é to lórí àpáta.
Target_Text_En: Only a thief can find the tracks of a thief on a rock.
Cultural_Context: It takes a thief to catch a thief.

Source_Text_Yo: Olè ńpolè lólè; ìkà ńpèkà níkà.
Target_Text_En: The thief calls another thief a thief; a wicked person calls another wicked person wicked.
Cultural_Context: The pot is calling the kettle black.

Source_Text_Yo: Olóòlà kì í wolú kó má fọwọ́ kan ẹ̀jẹ̀
Target_Text_En: A circumciser does not enter a town and not get his fingers bloody.
Cultural_Context: One cannot avoid the fallout of one’s profession.

Source_Text_Yo: Omi, baálé àlejò.
Target_Text_En: Water: the lord and master of the visitor.
Cultural_Context: Water is the ultimate thing with which one welcomes a visitor.

Source_Text_Yo: Omi titún dé, ẹja titún wọ̀ ọ́
Target_Text_En: A new stream arrives, and new fish enter into it.
Cultural_Context: Each era brings its own fashion.

Source_Text_Yo: Òní ló bo ọ̀la lójú.
Target_Text_En: It is today that obscures tomorrow.
Cultural_Context: Tomorrow arrives before one knows it.

Source_Text_Yo: Oníbàje ò wọ́n; awọ́ngógó bí atúnniṣe; atúnniṣe ò po bí abanijẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Detractors are not scarce; nothing is more difficult to find than reputation menders; reputation menders are far fewer than de tractors.
Cultural_Context: Most people are more interested in running others down than in building them up.

Source_Text_Yo: Onígbàjámọ̀-ọ́ fe kiri tẹ́lẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: The itinerant barber always intended to get on the road.
Cultural_Context: One needs little goading to do what one wanted to do anyway.

Source_Text_Yo: Oògùn tí a ò bá fowó ṣe, ẹ̀hìn àdìrò ní ńgbé.
Target_Text_En: Medicine on which one spent no money usually winds up behind the cooking hearth.
Cultural_Context: One seldom places any value on things that come easy and cheap.

Source_Text_Yo: Oorun ò mọ ikú.
Target_Text_En: Sleep does not know death.
Cultural_Context: A sleeping person does not know when death comes.

Source_Text_Yo: Òrìṣà kì í gba méjì lọ́wọ́ imẹ́lẹ́; bó bá gba apá a fún un lẹ́nu
Target_Text_En: The gods do not deprive the shirker of two gifts; if they take his arms, they endow him with a mouth.
Cultural_Context: People whose arms are feeble always have overactive mouths.

Source_Text_Yo: Oríṣìírísìí ọ̀bẹ là ńrí níjọ́ ikú erin.
Target_Text_En: One sees all sorts of knives on the day an elephant dies.
Cultural_Context: Extraordinary events prompt extraordinary behavior.

Source_Text_Yo: Orúkọ ẹni ni ìjánu ẹni.
Target_Text_En: One’s name is one’s bridle.
Cultural_Context: The means of controlling people, or getting their attention, is their names.

Source_Text_Yo: Òtìpí ìjí, a-wúwo-bí-àtẹ-ìbànújẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Huge baboon, as heavy as a tray of sadness.
Cultural_Context: Sadness is a heavy burden to bear.

Source_Text_Yo: Òwe lẹṣin ọ̀rọ̀; bí ọ̀rọ̀-ọ́ bá sọnù, òwe la fi ńwá a.
Target_Text_En: Proverbs are the horses of communication; if communication is lost, proverbs are what one uses to find it.
Cultural_Context: Effective discourse is impossible without resort to proverbs.

Source_Text_Yo: Òwò tí àdá bá mọ̀ ní ńká àdá léhín.
Target_Text_En: The trade the cutlass knows is the one that knocks out its teeth.
Cultural_Context: The dangers to which one is most vulnerable are those attached to one’s profession.

Source_Text_Yo: Owó tí ò lè dáni ní gbèsè ò lè lani
Target_Text_En: Money that is not enough to make one a debtor is not enough to make one prosper either.
Cultural_Context: Insignificant amounts of money, or of anything cannot affect one, one way or another

Source_Text_Yo: Òwúro la ti ḿmọ bí alẹ́ yó ti sanni sí.
Target_Text_En: It is from the morning that one knows how good one’s night will be.
Cultural_Context: From youth one can tell how pleasant one’s old age will be.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọba mewàá, ìgbà mẹ́wàá.
Target_Text_En: Ten kings, ten eras.
Cultural_Context: Each generation has its peculiar fashions and tastes.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọbẹ tó dùn kì í pe níṣasùn
Target_Text_En: A delicious stew does not last long in the pot.
Cultural_Context: Desirable commodities are soon used up.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọdọọdún lẹ̀wà ńwà.
Target_Text_En: It is annually that black-eyed beans are available.
Cultural_Context: May good fortune be ours each year.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọdọọdún ni ṣákúwé ńrúwe; ọdọọdún lewúro ńyọ ewé
Target_Text_En: It is every year that the sákúwé plant sprouts leaves; it is yearly that the bitterleaf plant sprouts leaves.
Cultural_Context: A wish that a desired annual event will never fail to occur.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọdọọdún nìrèké ńso
Target_Text_En: The sugarcane flourishes annually.
Cultural_Context: Prayer for perennial good fortune

Source_Text_Yo: Owo obi; obi owo
Target_Text_En: Money, kola nut; kola nut, money
Cultural_Context: Money and kola nuts are equal in importance

Source_Text_Yo: Ogá ńtà, Ogá ńrà.
Target_Text_En: The master is selling; the master is buying.
Cultural_Context: It takes a buyer and a seller to make a deal.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjà ojú-u sánmà lókè, àwọn ẹyẹ ni yó na.
Target_Text_En: The market holding in the sky aloft is for the birds alone to ply.
Cultural_Context: Only people with the requisite qualifications can engage in certain trades.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojá osùn ní ńfi-í hàn pé a bí ọmọ titun.
Target_Text_En: It is a camwood-stained baby strap that announces that one has a newborn baby.
Cultural_Context: Some events are announced by their ac companying behavior.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjà ọba ò mọ̀ pé ẹnìkan ò wá.
Target_Text_En: The king’s market does not know that a person is absent.
Cultural_Context: An individual’s input, if withheld, will not disrupt the project of the community.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ kan òjò-ó borí ọ̀dá.
Target_Text_En: The rain of one day conquers the drought.
Cultural_Context: However long the deprivation, relief is welcome when it comes.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjọ́ kì í pẹ títí kó má pèé; ọj kì í jìnnà jìnnà kó má kò.
Target_Text_En: The day is never so distant that it does not arrive; the future is never so far that it does not arrive
Cultural_Context: A thousand days are soon over.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọdọọdún là ńrí yemẹtì.
Target_Text_En: It is annually that one sees yemẹtì.
Cultural_Context: A prayer that good fortune will annually be a person’s lot, just as the yemẹtì insect is seen annually.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjo kì í rííriì kó má pèé.
Target_Text_En: A day is never so distant that it does not arrive.
Cultural_Context: The furthest future soon becomes the present.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjo kì í to lọ bi òréré.
Target_Text_En: Days do not go on straight like an avenue.
Cultural_Context: Life is not without curves.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjo tí atá bá bo sójú ní ḿba ẹwà ojú jẹ́; ọjọ́ tína bá fojú ba ẹ̀tù ni ẹ̀tù ńgbà.
Target_Text_En: The day pepper enters the eye is the day it ruins the beauty of the eye; the day fire catches a glimpse of gunpowder is the day the gunpowder does its bidding.
Cultural_Context: ‘‘No’’ is not an option as a response to the inevitable.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọjo tí ọmo bá fi ojú kan ayé lojú ẹ̀ ńlà.
Target_Text_En: The day a child first glimpses [comes into] the world is the day its eyes open.
Cultural_Context: The business of living begins on the day one is born.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kákárá re ilé òkokoro.
Target_Text_En: Destitution goes to the home of distress.
Cultural_Context: Troubles pile on trouble.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kan ṣoṣo ẹkùn, ó ba igba ọdẹ jẹ́
Target_Text_En: One single leopard sows confusion among two hundred hunters.
Cultural_Context: A formidable problem defies the efforts of many experts.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀kolé ò mú u ràjò.
Target_Text_En: The person who builds a house does not travel with it.
Cultural_Context: Even though one owns a house, one will still have to be a lodger if one travels.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmoge ńrelé ọkọ pelú-u májèlé, alárẹnà a re-e mú apó dání, ọkọ ìyàwó di ẹ́bìtì sílẹ́; ká wá wo irú ọmọ tí wọn ó bìí
Target_Text_En: A young woman leaves for her groom’s home carrying poisons; her intermediary carries a quiver, and the husband awaits them with a snare; let us see what sort of children they will produce.
Cultural_Context: One can predict the outcome of a collaborative venture from the nature of those involved.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ ẹja lẹjá ńjẹ sanra.
Target_Text_En: It is the children of fishes that fishes eat and grow fat upon.
Cultural_Context: It is the nature of things that people who prosper do so at the expense of other people.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ kékeré la fi ńṣe oògun ògbójú.
Target_Text_En: It is a small child that serves as an ingredient for a charm for bravery.
Cultural_Context: Even small things can effect large consequences.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọdé kékeré kì í ṣe àkopa ikú
Target_Text_En: A small child is not death’s first victim.
Cultural_Context: Children have been dying since the beginning of time.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ òjò ló ti ro tílẹ̀-ẹ́ ti fimu
Target_Text_En: A great deal of rain has fallen, which the earth has soaked up
Cultural_Context: Much more has hap pened than one could ever recount.

Source_Text_Yo: Opẹ Ìjàyè là bá bi ní ìhìn ogun Ògúnmola
Target_Text_En: It is the palm tree of ijaye that one should ask about the battle with Ogunmola
Cultural_Context: Said of a disaster that leaves no survivors

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rán dé; otá yọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Problems arrive; enemies rejoice.
Cultural_Context: One’s enemies rejoice at one’s misfortune.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọ̀rẹ́ ẹni ní ńbáni pile ọro; ará ilé ẹni ní ńkófà-a rẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Friends help one lay the foundation for wealth; one’s relatives reap the benefit.
Cultural_Context: Friends are in some regards more valuable than kin.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọwọ́ kì í ṣìnà ẹnu.
Target_Text_En: The hand never misses the way to the mouth.
Cultural_Context: Actions that are second nature will not go awry.

Source_Text_Yo: Palaku-n-gọ palaku-n-gọ: ìpàkọ́ igún bí erú àáké; bẹ́ẹ̀ni kò ṣéé lagi
Target_Text_En: Protruding, protruding: the occiput of the vulture seems like an axe’s handle, yet one cannot split wood with it.
Cultural_Context: Said of a thing that may look impressive but is really useless

Source_Text_Yo: Pani-pani kì í je ká mú idà kọjá nípàko òun.
Target_Text_En: The murderer would never let people carrying swords pass behind him.
Cultural_Context: The evildoer is always afraid of his shadow.

Source_Text_Yo: Pẹ́tẹ-pẹ̀tẹ là ḿbá ibalùwẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: Ever in a muddy state is how one finds the bath place.
Cultural_Context: Said to invoke a filthy fate on a person.

Source_Text_Yo: Ṣàn-n-gbá tú sépo.
Target_Text_En: The bean cake has disintegrated in the oil.
Cultural_Context: A misfortune has occurred.

Source_Text_Yo: Ta ló gbọ́ ikú ẹbọra? Ẹnìkan kì í gbo ikú Olódùmarè.
Target_Text_En: Whoever heard of the death of a spirit? No one ever hears of the death of the Almighty.
Cultural_Context: God endures forever; this is also a wish for longevity.

Source_Text_Yo: Tibi tire làfon ńrọ̀.
Target_Text_En: The fruit of the baobab tree drops with out regard for good or foul weather.
Cultural_Context: A prayer that a pregnant woman might deliver without hardship.

Source_Text_Yo: Tòjò tẹ̀rùn, omi kì í gbẹ níhò akàn.
Target_Text_En: Be it the rainy season or the dry, the crab’s hole is never short of water.
Cultural_Context: A wish that one may never be short of the good things of life, whatever the season. The following is a variant.

Source_Text_Yo: Tòjò tẹ̀rùn, omi kì í won ọmọ oníròjoròjo.
Target_Text_En: Whether in the rainy season or in the dry, the oníròjoròjo child never lacks water.
Cultural_Context: A prayer for unceasing blessings. Compare the foregoing entry.

Source_Text_Yo: Wúńdíá: abọkọjọjọ.
Target_Text_En: The unmarried woman: one whose husbands are legion.
Cultural_Context: The potential husbands of an unmarried woman are uncountable.

Source_Text_Yo: Tàlùbo ni iyèkan afjú.
Target_Text_En: Tàlùb is the blood sibling of the blind.
Cultural_Context: Said of things that are always to be found in the company of one another.

Source_Text_Yo: Ọwọ́ tó we, ilẹ̀ ló fi nù.
Target_Text_En: The hand that he washed, he had to wipe on the ground.
Cultural_Context: Said of people frustrated in their expectations.

Source_Text_Yo: Orán ìhùùhù ní ńdun aládìẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is the matter of the down feathers that troubles the owner of the fowl
Cultural_Context: Delicate tasks are far more taxing than routine ones

Source_Text_Yo: Ọmọ́yẹ-ẹ́ ti rìnhòòhò dọ́ja; aṣọ ò bá Ọmọ́yẹ.
Target_Text_En: Ọmọ́yẹ has arrived at the market naked; clothes are too late for Ọmọ́yẹ
Cultural_Context: Matters are past remedy

Source_Text_Yo: Orí-i Táyé yàto sí ti Kẹ́hìndé.
Target_Text_En: Táyé’s destiny is different from Khìndé’s.
Cultural_Context: No two people, however close or similar, have identical destinies.

Source_Text_Yo: Orí kì í burú kó má lọ̀ọ́rùn.
Target_Text_En: A head is never so unfortunate that it does not have a neck.
Cultural_Context: No matter how bad one’s situation, there will be some redeeming factor.

Source_Text_Yo: Olè-é ta ohun lọ́pọ̀; ewúrẹ́ meta ẹgbẹ̀ta; àgùntàn mẹ́fà ẹgbẹ̀fà.
Target_Text_En: A thief sells everything cheap: three goats for 600 cowries; six sheep for 1,200 cowries.
Cultural_Context: A person who did not work for something is never reluctant to discard it for little or nothing.

Source_Text_Yo: Ojú ológbò òun gún; àmtẹ́kùn òun ẹkùn; ọ̀kánjúwà òun olè; déédé ni wọ́n.
Target_Text_En: The scarlet love-bean plant and thorns, the àmtekùn big cat and the leopard, greed and thievery: they are equivalents.
Cultural_Context: A greedy person is no different from a thief.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò-ó kọ̀ òjò ò rọ̀ mo; Ọlorun-ún fi tẹ̀ẹ̀so lé àgbàdo lóko.
Target_Text_En: The rains become adamant and stop falling; God has inflicted ts on the corn in the fields.
Cultural_Context: Adverse conditions make it impossible for people to thrive.

Source_Text_Yo: Òjò pa gbòdògì ró wọ̀rọ̀-wọ̀rọ̀
Target_Text_En: The rain pounds the gbòdògì, producing a loud noise.
Cultural_Context: Certain behaviors by others force comments out of the mouths of even normally recalcitrant people.

Source_Text_Yo: Kí ni àfàní orógbó? A pa á kò láwẹ́; a jẹ ẹ́ ó ńkorò; a ní ká figi e dáná, Ṣàngó ní ọmọ ìyá òun ní ńṣe.
Target_Text_En: Of what use is the bitter kola? One splits it, but it lacks naturally separated lobes; one eats it and it is bitter; one attempts to use its wood for fire, and Ṣàngo says both [he and the tree] were born of the same mother.
Cultural_Context: Why should one put oneself out for something or someone from which or whom one can expect no appreciation or reward?

Source_Text_Yo: Kí ilẹ̀ tó pa òṣìkà, ohun rere gbogbo á ti bàjẹ́.
Target_Text_En: Before Earth kills the wicked, a great many good things will have been ruined.
Cultural_Context: God’s justice may eventually prevail, but by then a lot of evil will have been done.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìyá tó bí Alárá ló bí Ajerò, ló sì bí Ọ̀ràngún Ìlá.
Target_Text_En: The mother who gave birth to the Alárá [king of Ará] gave birth to the Ajerò [king of Ìjerò] and the ràngún of Ìlà.
Cultural_Context: All referents are of a kind.

Source_Text_Yo: Irúkan-ùn, ọbẹ̀ iwọ.
Target_Text_En: All of a kind, stews made with brimstone tree leaves.
Cultural_Context: Said of people who have no real individual identities outside of the group.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìpín àìṣẹ̀, ìpín àìrò ní ńpa aláròká.
Target_Text_En: The destiny of the innocent, the destiny of the person who thought no ill, will be the death of the person who spreads evil reports about another person.
Cultural_Context: (The evil that one does to innocent people will rebound on one.

Source_Text_Yo: Ilé ni adìẹ ńya òpìpì; ìbá ṣe àparò, ọmọ aráyé a mú u jẹ.
Target_Text_En: It is in the household that a featherless chicken is shunned; were it a partridge, humans would have killed it for food.
Cultural_Context: One very often does not appreciate the value of what one has.

Source_Text_Yo: Ikú ẹja ní ḿmú ẹja mlú; ẹja Ògùn ìbá ṣe dé Akẹ̀sán?
Target_Text_En: It is the death of the fish that makes it know the town; what else would have brought a fish from the Ògùn river to Aksán market?
Cultural_Context: A mishap is likely to bring other mishaps in its wake.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìkórítamẹ́ta ọ̀nà Èṣù.
Target_Text_En: The point where three roads meet: Èṣù’s pathway.
Cultural_Context: Evil colonizes the place it finds hospitable.

Source_Text_Yo: Igúnnugún kì í ṣe ẹyẹ ‘‘Gbà jẹ.’’
Target_Text_En: The vulture is not a fowl in reference to which one says, ‘‘Take and eat this.’’
Cultural_Context: Not all things are available for exploitation.

Source_Text_Yo: Igi tí yó pani ldúnnìí, kì í ṣe bòtujẹ̀ ẹ̀hìnkùlé ẹni.
Target_Text_En: The tree that will kill one this year will not be the Jatropha plant in one’s back yard.
Cultural_Context: A person of absolute insignificance in relation to one cannot be one’s effective adversary.

Source_Text_Yo: Igi tí baba ẹní bá lo, a kì í fà á tu, bíi tẹ̀gẹ́ kọ́.
Target_Text_En: A tree that one’s father plants one does not uproot, but that does not apply to cassava.
Cultural_Context: One must treat tradition and patrimony with reverence, but one should know when exceptions are called for.

Source_Text_Yo: Ìdí funfun ò níran, àfi bí àgbẹ̀ tó bá fi tiẹ̀ yí eèpẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: A white buttock is not a natural condition; for a farmer it happens when he rubs his buttocks in the dirt.
Cultural_Context: One should not mistake temporary setbacks or afflictions for permanent conditions.

Source_Text_Yo: Gba-n-gba-á dẹkùn, kedereé bẹ̀ ẹ́ wò: ọ̀rọ̀ ìkọ̀kọ̀ ò sí níbẹ̀.
Target_Text_En: A leopard is trapped in open space; clear sight gets a good look at it; the matter does not admit of secrets.
Cultural_Context: Once a secret is leaked, it can no longer be hidden.

Source_Text_Yo: Gbé oyún lọ kó o gbọ́mọ bọ̀.
Target_Text_En: Leave with a pregnancy and return with a baby.
Cultural_Context: However long the journey, the traveler eventually returns home.

Source_Text_Yo: Gùdù-gudu-ú fi ojú jọ èṣúrú, bẹ́ẹ̀ni kò ṣéé jẹ.
Target_Text_En: Poisonous yam looks like èṣúrú yam, yet it is not edible.
Cultural_Context: What looks inviting is often quite deadly.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹni tó sọ pé òkúta a máa dàgbà ò purọ́; ẹni tó sọ pé òkúta kì í dàgbà ò purọ́.
Target_Text_En: The person who says that rocks age does not lie; the person who says that rocks do not age does not lie.
Cultural_Context: Two people can see the same situation in different but equally valid ways.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ̀jẹ̀ ahun ò kúnni lọ́wọ́.
Target_Text_En: The blood of the tortoise does not fill one’s palm.
Cultural_Context: There is very little one can expect from a miser.

Source_Text_Yo: Ebìtì tí yó pa erè, ojú-u rẹ̀ á pọ́n.
Target_Text_En: The trap that will kill a python will grow red in the eyes.
Cultural_Context: Whoever attempts the near-impossible will labor greatly.

Source_Text_Yo: Ẹ ti pé yó rìí, nígbàtí ọmọ olè ńgun ìbaka?
Target_Text_En: What do you expect, when the scion of a thief rides a camel?
Cultural_Context: If a person lives conspicuously beyond his or her means, one may legitimately suspect some hanky-panky.

Source_Text_Yo: Èésú ò lérè; oye a dá là ńkó.
Target_Text_En: Pooled contributions earn no profit; one winds up with only how much one contributed.
Cultural_Context: Certain pursuits or obligations are necessary or expedient but thankless.

Source_Text_Yo: Èèmo lukutupẹ́bẹ́; ìyàwó lóyún tán ọ̀na ò gba ọkọ.
Target_Text_En: Unspeakable abomination: the wife becomes pregnant, and the doorway cannot accommodate the husband.
Cultural_Context: The person with a problem shows no adverse effects, but the bystander does.

Source_Text_Yo: Eégún ní òún fẹ́ẹ́ jó; òjò-ó ní òún fẹ́ẹ́ rọ̀; ọmọ-ọ́ ní òún fee ṣe bẹbẹ.
Target_Text_En: The masquerader says he wants to dance; the rain says it wants to fall; and the child says he wants to perform wonders.
Cultural_Context: Conflicting desires pose a difficult problem.

Source_Text_Yo: Eégún tí ḿbe ọmọ lórí kì í dẹ́rù ba ọmo-ọ tire.
Target_Text_En: The masquerader that beheads people does not pose a threat to his own child.
Cultural_Context: People who are uncompromisingly strict with the children of others are usually permissive with their own.
